items.statement: Expects FY26 EBITDA to grow ~30% YoY in absolute terms
items.quote: Overall 30% increase in the EBITDA. If you see as an absolute number, last year, we did around INR257 crores. So 30% around over and above that, we should do a year as a whole in this year.

items.statement: Expects FY27 EBITDA to grow ~30% YoY over FY26, potentially more
items.quote: Because we are adding capacity, we are also -- will be having power also, all these projects, which we are doing will be on stream. So we could have much better than 30%.

items.statement: Q1 FY26 margins expected to be much better than Q1 FY25, with some inventory loss from crude price drop
items.quote: Q1 margins are good, but there was some reduction in the raw material drastic when the crude has fell from $75 to $65. So there could be some inventory loss. But overall, we should be better than Q1 of last year, much better than Q1 of last year.

items.quote: additional yarn capacities at Dahej plant, POY capacity of 19,800 metric tons per annum, DTY capacity of 14,400 metric tons per annum. FDY capacity has been doubled from what was initially planned. FDY capacity addition will be now 28,800 metric tons per annum instead of 14,400. FDY market is gaining ground in domestic market. The capacity addition envisages a capital expenditure of around INR235

items.statement: Recycling plant: INR200 cr term loan + INR100 cr equity from parent; Yarn expansion: INR125-126 cr ECB + internal accruals; Steam & green power: internal accruals
items.value: INR200 cr term loan, INR100 cr equity, INR125-126 cr ECB

And the INR235 crores, we will be taking a ECB of around INR125 crores, INR126 crores. Balance will be internal accrual. And rest of the other 2, it will be all under internal accruals.

items.statement: Working capital cycle increased marginally: debtors +1 day, inventory +1-2 days in March due to market situation
items.quote: I think debtors have gone up by 1 day and inventory also, you will see maybe 1 or 2 days. So it depends on the market situation in March, that could make a slight difference. It's not a very major shift in the cycle.

items.quote: then only people will be interested to license. They would like to see it first, then we will see. We are open to that. Rishi Solanki: Okay. Loop Industries is doing, but I don't think they are coming with any plans of putting up a big plant. It's still

Madhu Sudhan Bhageria: Some interest provision we had made in earlier year that was written back. There was some interest to be paid to customs and all, so that we were not able to win the case and not need to pay. So that's why we have written back

items.statement: Recycling plant in 100% subsidiary; new venture separate from main Filatex operations
items.quote: And the new, which we said recycling, which we are doing, that's a new venture. That's a 100% subsidiary of Filatex. That is the new thing which we'll be doing.

items.statement: In talks with brands for recycled yarn supply; brands would nominate Filatex as supplier to their fabric/garment vendors
items.quote: We are talking to some buyers. Directly, they will not buy, but they make us like a nominated supplier to the people who are making fabrics and garments for them. So we are in talks with some brands.

items.statement: Management stops guidance for FY26 to build strength, predictability and stability; will reassess and bring focus.
items.quote: We will be stopping guidance for now. Given the current macro environment, we believe it is prudent to utilize FY26 to build strength, predictability and stability across our portfolio.

items.statement: Margin target recalibrated to stabilizing at 15% over next 24 months from earlier 16% in 12 months.
items.quote: But we may have to recalibrate this to touching and even staying steady at 15% over the next 24 months.

items.statement: March was softer than anticipated due to global uncertainties; Q1 FY26 will see some impact but not significant or sustained.
items.quote: March was softer than what we anticipated, given some of the global uncertainties that are going on. We do not see any significant challenge because of this.

items.statement: Pipeline unchanged but decision-making has paused due to macro uncertainty.
items.quote: Because stress also creates an opportunity to create a pipeline of a different nature. But has it caused or created a pause in decision making? The answer is yes.

items.statement: DET EBIT margin 13% in Q4 FY25, down 48 bps QoQ; FY25 margin 13.5%, down 261 bps YoY.
items.quote: The DET EBIT margin for Q4 FY25 stood at 13% down by 48 bps quarter-on-quarter.

items.statement: Cost optimization phase two started end of Q3 FY25 helped mitigate margin impact.
items.quote: And in part due to the early benefits from the second phase of the cost optimization exercise, which we have embarked already at the end of Q3 of FY25.

items.statement: Six large deals won in Q4 FY25; two from aerospace, two from communications, three from top 10 clients.
items.quote: Of the 6 large deals we won in Q4, two were from aerospace and two were in communications.

items.statement: Green hydrogen project win in Norway for marine transportation; meaningful for energy vertical, ramp-up in progress.
items.quote: We're very proud to have received a very large order for the engineering and of the first-of-its-kind green hydrogen production project, which will be used for Marine Transportation.

items.statement: Top 5 clients grew 4.5% YoY, top 10 grew ~9% YoY in FY25; no structural client issues seen.
items.quote: Actually, if any, -- the top 5 customers grew by 4.5% year-on-year for us, and the top 10 clients grew by about 9% year-on-year for us.

items.statement: Alliance with Micware Navigations in intelligent mobility for sustainable smart transportation.
items.quote: I also want to highlight the alliance with Micware Navigations in the mobility space. This partnership will deliver some very interesting solutions for intelligent mobility focused on same sustainable smart transportation system.

items.statement: Capex reduced from ~3% of revenue; will continue to generate strong cash.
items.quote: We also did a lot of work in terms of reducing our capex spend, which at one point is almost 3% of our revenue.

items.statement: DET became long-term debt-free in FY25; cash position highest ever at $157 million.
items.quote: At the end of FY25, our cash position is the highest ever we've had at $157 million for DET and the FCF for DET was INR800 crores, up by INR45 crores year-on-year. At the same time, we've also cleared all our long-term debt within the year, essentially meaning that DET is now a long-term debt-free business.

items.statement: DET free cash flow INR 800 cr in FY25, up INR 45 cr YoY; Q4 FCF INR 215 cr, 132% PAT conversion.
items.quote: The DET FY25 free cash flow stood at INR800 crores, our best ever with an improvement of INR45 crores year-on-year, resulting from our continued focus on cash generation.

items.statement: Final dividend INR 14 per share; full year dividend INR 26 per share; Board to review dividend policy during the year.
items.quote: We're also very happy to announce a final dividend of INR14 per share, which translates into a full year dividend of INR26 per share.

items.statement: Sukamal Banerjee joined as CEO 6 weeks ago; Prabhakaran (KAP) hired as SVP & CTO for DET from Honeywell; Beatrice Lippus rehired to lead energy business in Germany.
items.quote: We welcome Prabhakaran to the Cyient family. He joins us as the Senior Vice President and Chief Technology Officer for our DET business.

items.statement: Sustainability vertical split into utilities, energy, and mining & minerals for agile leadership; reporting change from Q1 FY26.
items.quote: We also took a decision to break up sustainability vertical into its constituents, which are utilities, energy and mining and minerals.

items.statement: GCC-focused BU created with dedicated leader; accounts aligned; EBIT not to be diluted.
items.quote: We have also started working on, as I said, building back our talent. And one of the key areas of focus that we have done from that perspective is to bring back successful tenured employees of Cyient, who had left us in the near past.

items.statement: Cash to be used for semiconductor business and M&A to plug technology gaps; no specific deals yet.
items.quote: So we will continue to look at ways to enhance our portfolio using M&A and the use of the cash will also be for that.

items.statement: Group revenue INR 7,360 cr in FY25, up 3% YoY, highest ever; DET revenue $687.7M, down 3% YoY CC.
items.quote: In rupee terms, the revenue per group stands at INR7,360 crores at a growth of 3% year-on-year. This is the highest ever revenue for the group.

items.statement: DLM business grew ~27% YoY in FY25.
items.quote: And the third axis of course, is the DLM business or the Design-Led Manufacturing business, which continues to do well. And you may have seen that business grew about 27% year-on-year last year.

items.statement: Macro uncertainty causing softer demand, delayed decisions, and forecasting challenges; guidance paused temporarily.
items.quote: Given the current macro environment, we believe it is prudent to utilize FY26 to build strength, predictability and stability across our portfolio.

items.statement: Cyient Semiconductor Private Limited (CSPL) carved out; financials to be reported as separate segment from Q1 FY26.
items.quote: As previously communicated, CSPL financials will be reported as a separate segment starting Q1 FY26 onwards.

items.statement: No significant aerospace MRO impact yet; flying hours stable; tariff impact may appear later.
items.quote: I think right now, we're not seeing any significant impact on the aerospace side. I think we will start to see some of that as we go forward.

items.statement: Wage hikes planned for FY26; investments to be more prudent and outcome-focused.
items.quote: The second thing I'll say is that we intend to continue with wage hikes to our colleagues and associates, which is what we will do in F Y26. The third thing I'll say is that we'll be a lot more prudent and focused on investments we will make in the current year towards

items.statement: Connectivity contract renewal with major customer completed in April; some slowdown in new awards during renewal.
items.quote: And during that process, there was definitely some slowdown of business award -- new business being awarded. And I think we are over that now with the contract being signed in April.

items.statement: Healthcare, automotive segments showed healthy growth momentum entering FY26.
items.quote: We definitely have some of the areas which has grown healthily in th e last year. I'll call out health care as one of them. So definitely, it's an area where we have seen momentum. We have seen growth in some of the other segments as well like automotive

items.statement: Target cost to average assets of 2.5% for the year; fee to average assets higher than predicted; provision cost lower than projected for 1% ROA
items.quote: The go-to which we have spoken about albeit in a yearly sense is about 2.5%. So these are within touching distance of where we want to be. Fee to average asset is higher than what we had predicted. Provision cost to average assets, we are lower than what w e had projected ourselves to be to reach a 1% ROA

items.statement: NIM stabilized at 3.28% in Q4 FY25 vs 3.29% previous quarter; one basis point decline despite 25 bps repo cut
items.quote: From a NIM perspective, the NIM is stabilizing at 3.28% from 3.29% in the previous quarter.

items.statement: NIM trend over last five quarters: 3.62%, 3.39%, 3.27%, 3.30%, 3.29% showing stabilization after downward trend
items.quote: Let me tell you what the NIMs were looking like in the last five quarters. 362, 339, 327, all down. Then 330 and 329. So that's why I said there is a stabilization happening.

items.statement: Further repo rate cuts will hurt margins; limited ability to reduce savings account rates further; later rate cuts better for bank
items.quote: Any further repo rate cuts will hurt the bank. What we have, we have managed, but the later the repo rate cut happens, the better it will be for the bank.

items.statement: Loan book grew 25% YoY in FY25; deposit growth 22%; savings account growth 19%
items.quote: In continuation of the trend of growth momentum, we have seen a balance sheet growth of 22% for the year. Deposit growth was a healthy 22 % and the loans growth was 25%.

items.statement: Co-lending book ~Rs 7,000 crore, grew ~100% in FY25; future co-lending growth to match balance sheet growth rate (~20-25%) not exceed it
items.quote: If you were to see the last year, we've got almost a Rs.7,000 crores co-lending book. We built up a Rs.7,000 crores co-lending book, roughly about 100% growth in co-lending for the matter.

items.statement: Shift from home loans to LAP in mortgage portfolio; LAP yields 150-250 bps higher; incremental disbursements skewed to business loans
items.quote: Business loans will give you anywhere between 150 to 250 basis points higher yield. So that's a journey we started about five quarters back. We're seeing the results of it now.

items.statement: PMAY 2.0 loans at max 11.5% rate (near current 11.54% yield), 5-year subsidy, max Rs 25 lakh size; bank comfortable with new-to-credit customers; will be integral to growth plan
items.quote: We're very happy with it for multiple reasons. One is that the max interest rate on that is 11.5%, which if you were to look at it is almost on par with the yield and advances that we're currently getting at 11.54%.

items.statement: MFI portfolio small, no improvement seen, accelerated provisions taken; gold loan organic book unchanged despite RBI circular
items.quote: Honestly, I don't see any improvement. At least our portfolio, there is no improvement. It's a small portfolio, so we are okay with it. We have taken accelerated provisions on it.

items.statement: Upgraded core banking (Finacle), instalment lending (FinOne), treasury management (TCS); 3 of 4 core systems upgraded; significant cybersecurity (SIEM) and DR investment
items.quote: have upgraded our core banking system, Finacle a year before last. Last year, we upgraded our instalment letting program FinOne. It's the state-of-the-art, one which we have implemented now. Third item is our treasury management system. TCS, we upgraded it in June of last

items.statement: Tier 1 capital 14.30% (down 23 bps YoY); Total CRAR 16.77%; RWA <50%; 24.7% advance growth with only 23 bps capital consumption; capital raise planned Q2 FY26 at better valuation
items.quote: Tier 1 has moved from 14.53 to 14.30, 23 bps utilization for a 25% advances growth. And even now, obviously, if you were to look at 14.3, it is well above what we believe is a go to capital kind of mark.

items.statement: Savings account rate spectrum 1.5% to 7.98%; transactional users price inelastic; surplus parkers rate sensitive; UPI driving transaction volumes
items.quote: By having a spectrum of rates, which is as low as 1.5 currently, and perhaps even as high as 7.98. So, basically, what does the customer want? We are catering to that customer's need.

items.statement: Core fee income Rs 161 crore in Q4 (record high); 5-quarter trend: 118, 114, 139, 141, 161; fee to avg assets 1.18% quarter, 1.09% full year
items.quote: let me take you thro ugh the last five quarters of core fee income growth, starting from March ’ 24. Rs.118 crores, Rs.114 crores, Rs.139 crores, Rs.141 crores, Rs.161 crores

items.statement: Non-interest income 5-quarter trend: 136, 143, 205, 184, 219; treasury gains favorable in rate cut environment but focus on core fee consistency
items.quote: Similarly, on non-interest income, 136, 143, 205, 184, 219. To my mind, that is some level of consistency.

items.statement: Co-lending draft guidelines (15-18 points) awaited; personal view: blended rate benefits customers and expands market; will assess final guidelines
items.quote: There is a draft guideline which has come in with about 15-18 points. Jai, I would suggest let's wait for the final guidelines to come in to see what changes have to be made.

items.statement: Gold loan organic book unchanged despite RBI circular; co-lending guidelines separate
items.quote: Absolutely no change. Whatever was mentioned in some form or the other or perhaps even higher, we are - for organic book, okay, I'm not talking about co-lending at all.

items.statement: Penal interest replaced by penal charges: 5 bps NIM reduction offset by 5 bps fee income improvement; collection now required for recognition
items.quote: There is a 5 bps reduction of NIM and a similar 5 bps improvement in the fee to average earnings, which has happened.

items.statement: NLD SMS volumes grew double-digit at 15-20% YoY despite pricing pressure.
items.quote: From a volume perspective, I think industry would have only grown or at least between 15% to 20% double-digit growth.

items.statement: Enterprise gross margin target band is 25-27%; pricing pressure has bottomed out and solution-led efficiency gains are helping.
items.quote: I think between 25% to 27% gross margin is a narrow band that we have been operating in the last couple of quarters. While we do not guide, but I would say those are the range or range that we want to operate at.

items.statement: SMS pricing pressure has bottomed out; any price increase will benefit top line and gross margins.
items.quote: I believe that hopefully, have bottom ed out from a pricing perspective and any upside that we get from a price increase would only help both to p line and gross

items.statement: Meta raised WhatsApp marketing message prices and cut utility prices to SMS levels; impact already baked into Q3-Q4.
items.quote: Meta has increased the prices for marketing messages, okay? And so, by doing that, the customers have reduced the volumes on marketing. And on the other side, they reduced the prices for utility messages, which we call it, let us say, for example, transaction message where you're sending information messages or transaction messages and all of that.

items.statement: Signed RCS MaaP platform deal with two large telcos outside India; revenue share subscription model, contribution expected from end of Q1 FY26.
items.quote: I'm sure you would have gone through our announcement a couple of days that we have done that we have signed a deal to deploy RCS platform with two of the large telcos outside India. So, it's the first large win for us, which is in outside India. So, you should start seeing the contribution of that by end of Q1 onwards as the things ramps up.

items.statement: ATP platform has two large telco wins and one small OTT deal in India; contracts renewed, pipeline growing.
items.quote: We have done two success stories in India, have been with the client for almost a year now, and we are very happy, and we have renewed with them as well.

items.statement: Won largest NBFC, largest gaming company, largest bank, and second-largest PSU bank on WhatsApp/RCS; cross-selling OTT and RCS to existing NLD base.
items.quote: We have signed and gone live with one of the largest NBFC in the country. We have gone live with the largest gaming company in the country on WhatsApp as well as on RCS. We have signed the largest bank on WhatsApp and currently the integration is going on and we are building a lot of use cases. We have also signed with number two largest PSU bank and have gone live with them.

items.statement: Gaining market share on OTT channels each quarter; customers shifting from competitors to Tanla for omnichannel solutions.
items.quote: I strongly believe uh that we have gained the market share every quarter that has been gone by in last say couple of quarters right so. Our belief is that we have moved the market share for now.

items.statement: Investing in talent, technology, GTM and innovation; cash balance ₹1,009 crore, free cash flow 101% of PAT for FY25.
items.quote: Our bank balance at the exit of this year is ₹1,009 crores. Our free cash flow for the full year was 101% of the PAT and last Q3, Q4 has been on an average more than 150% of the PAT.

items.statement: Board approved second interim dividend of ₹6 per share in Q4 FY25.
items.quote: And hence, we have given an interim dividend and then the next interim dividend of ₹6 and Board has approved it this quarter.

items.statement: Actively evaluating strategic M&A for assets that accelerate growth and fit culturally; will not rush.
items.quote: And the third M&A, as we said, we continue to look out for the assets. We do not want to rush. But whenever we believe that there are the right assets, which will help grow us faster, which will fit with us from a cultural perspective, I think we will not shy away from making those investments.

items.statement: Tanla profitable while most competitors are bleeding; profit share >70% vs revenue share 40-45%.
items.quote: Most of them are bleeding. So, if we really see ourselves vis-a-vis our competition, we really did very, very well. And we generated profits. I can very safely say that we would be, though our revenue market share may be 40%, 45%. But in terms of our profits, our share would be more than 70% of the industry.

items.statement: Platform ambition: each platform to reach ₹100 crore ARR over 4-8 quarters; Trubloq mature, ATP and RCS MaaP scaling.
items.quote: Our aspiration is that each of the platform that we work on over four to six quarters or eight quarters, depending on the life cycle and the use case goes to ₹100 CR ARR is the wish list of the ambition that we have put for ourselves.

items.statement: International enterprise business growing, offsetting ILD weakness; Middle East presence expanding.
items.quote: If you see ILD, which has significantly impacted has got offset by go od growth that we have seen from an international business perspective

items.statement: No forward guidance given; FY26 growth depends on pricing recovery, OTT scaling, and platform ramp-up.
items.quote: See, it would be difficult for me to make a forward-looking statement. I can only tell you that we are exiting the year with a very good note, right? If you see from last number of four, five quarters, we have not grown. In Q4, we have grown 2% plus.

items.statement: Q4 FY25 revenue grew ~2% QoQ, exiting year on positive note after flat prior quarters.
items.quote: If you see from last number of four, five quarters, we have not grown. In Q4, we have grown 2% plus. So, we will have a tailwind from a Q4 growth perspective, right? Q4 Into four itself will lead to growth.

items.statement: Omnichannel solution capability (WhatsApp, RCS, Truecaller, SMS) drives stickiness and cross-sell; charging for services on OTT channels starting this year.
items.quote: We are providing options for customers on WhatsApp, RCS and Truecaller as well. As far as prices are concerned customers have also realized the kind of work we are doing. So, In nutshell we are going to start charging for our services as well to these customers this year and we would see that our OTT revenues would definitely go up and our number of customers will go up on these channels and our m

items.statement: Heavy investment in hiring and talent retention across enterprise and platform teams.
items.quote: Our HR team is working day in, day out to ensure that the talent is critical, and we have the right hiring and right team in place.

items.statement: ATP anti-phishing platform addresses regulatory and enterprise pain points; adoption cycle longer than expected but use case proven.
items.quote: The way to see about this product, it's solving the problem of today and it's a very, very promising technology. And I believe both the regulatory authorities, telcos, enterprises, all are cognizant of the fact.

items.statement: Revenue growth guidance for FY26 is 11-12%
items.quote: next year I think we should be better than that, maybe between 11% - 12%.

items.statement: EBITDA margin guidance for FY26 is around 27%
items.quote: Going forward, I think, since we have to make a lot of investment in newer geography, newer talent and some digital initiatives and so on and so forth , so around 27% kind of margins we are looking or we are confident to maintain.

items.statement: Maintenance capex for FY26 expected at Rs 60-70 crore including 15-20 new labs and IT investments
items.quote: Normally our maintenance CAPEX is about Rs. 60 – Rs. 70 crore a year. And I believe in next year, FY26, similar kind of CAPEX will be there.

items.statement: Added 18 new labs in FY25, plan to add 15-20 labs in FY26 and next year to catch up on pre-COVID pace
items.quote: We have added 18 new testing labs last financial year. And for this financial year and maybe one more, we definitely would like to keep up the tempo at this pace.

items.statement: Added ~845 patient service centers in FY25 (14-15% YoY growth); will continue adding PSCs alongside labs
items.quote: Yes, collection center s, so lab and collection centers or PSCs as we call them, go hand in hand. It is the whole hub and spoke and the whole network approach that we have in every geography.

items.statement: Sample volumes grew 9.5% to 20.9 million in Q4 FY25; patient volumes grew 3.8% to 6.8 million
items.quote: Sample volumes grew by 9.5% to 20.9 million, while patient volumes increased by 3.8% to 6.8 million.

items.statement: SwasthFit bundled test program grew 22% in FY25; extending into illness segment and Tier-3/4 towns
items.quote: Our bundle d test program, SwasthFit, also delivered robust growth of 22%, contributing meaningfully to the overall performance.

items.statement: Q4 FY25 EBITDA margin 28.1%; full year FY25 EBITDA margin 28.3%
items.quote: For the full year, EBITDA stands at Rs. 696 crore compared to Rs. 609 crore in FY24, registering a growth of 14.2% with a margin of 28.3%.

items.statement: No price hikes taken in FY25; pricing is a strategic choice, not driven by lack of pricing power
items.quote: Price increase is something which for us will be a very strategic decision. I think in some previous call also we had discussed that if there is, you know, if we see the need, whether it is in terms of costs or whether it is in terms of the whole pricing table in the industry moving in a certain direction where we are left behind, if any of those things happen, then we may consider, but it is not

items.statement: Pricing in Tier-3/4 towns similar to Tier-1/2; no differential pricing on MRP basis
items.quote: So, our pricing approach in Tier-3, Tier-4 is not really different compared to whatever are the contiguous Tier-2 or Tier-1 markets. Our pricing is similar, it's not essentially lower pricing on an MRP basis.

items.statement: Specialized tests ~20% of portfolio; launched advanced Amyloid Typing Test, first in South Asia
items.quote: the specialized portfolio is something which each company would be defining differently. But the way we define our specialized portfolio; it is about one -fifth of our portfolio comes from the specialized test.

items.statement: Radiology revenue less than 5% of total; focused on pathology, radiology option remains on table
items.quote: Our revenue from radiology is actually miniscule. It is very low single digits. I mean, it is all pathology revenue only.

items.statement: West region revenue grew mid-single digits in FY25; Suburban impacted by IT stack changeover and liquidation in Q4, recovering in 1-2 quarters
items.quote: We did the whole IT stack changeover in Suburban in Q4 and also the voluntary liquidation process was carried out in Q4. So, because of that, there has been a bit of an impact in terms of the revenue for Suburban in Q4. And we have already started recovering and we believe that we should be able to recover quickly in the next 1-2 quarters.

items.statement: Competition from pharma players like Lupin entering diagnostics seen as positive for industry organization; market large enough for all
items.quote: And I think as long as more and more organized players come into the industry, it is good. Because the overall industry benefits from more organized players. It becomes more level playing field.

items.statement: Pathology reagents: virtually zero sourcing from China (<1%); no supply chain risk from China export restrictions
items.quote: In pathology diagnostics, no reagent in our case comes from China. None.

items.statement: Collection center fees grew only 3% YoY in Q4 due to test/geography mix, not channel margin changes
items.quote: There is no change in the margins. Deven, it's purely on the mix.

items.statement: Net cash and equivalents Rs 1,229 crore as of March 31, 2025; kept for organic growth and inorganic opportunities in South/West
items.quote: Net cash and equivalents as on 31st March 2025 is Rs. 1,229 crore.

items.statement: No fund raise planned; using internal cash for organic expansion and potential inorganic opportunities in South/West
items.quote: Again as a stated strategy , we are keeping this cash with us for any opportunity which will emerge and as earlier mentioned , I mean, obviously we are growing organically and we have started our own efforts in South, particularly South and West, but if there is any opportunity there, definitely we will be keen to do that opportunity.

items.statement: Final dividend of 60% (Rs 6/share) approved; total FY25 dividend 240% (Rs 24/share)
items.quote: I am pleased to share that the Board of Directors of the Company have approved a final dividend of 60%, that is Rs. 6 per share, taking the total dividend for the year to 240%, that is Rs. 24 per share.

items.statement: Revenue per patient Q4 FY25 Rs 887 (+6.4% YoY); tests per patient 3.07 vs 2.91 YoY
items.quote: Revenue per patient for Q4 FY25 is Rs. 887, up by 6.4%, compared to Rs. 833 in Q4 FY24. This is mainly due to improvement in test and geographic mix.

items.statement: Tier-3 revenue grew mid-teens in FY25; trend continues from previous years
items.quote: We have had a good growth in our Tier-3 revenues even in this year. We had a healthy, mid-teens kind of growth. So, it is definitely in the similar trajectory as what we would have seen earlier.

items.statement: Suburban Diagnostics voluntarily liquidated in Q4 FY25; business transferred to parent on going concern basis
items.quote: pursuant to the approved scheme of liquidation of Suburban, the entire business undertaking of Suburban has been transferred to Dr. Lal PathLabs Limited on a going concern basis in Q4 FY25.

items.statement: Open to inorganic opportunities in South/West; dual-brand strategy in Mumbai/Pune/Goa for Suburban
items.quote: There could be a possibility that if there are inorganic acids which are coming with the radiology business attached to it, then that becomes a part and parcel of our business also going forward.

items.statement: Investing in frontline sales teams for newer geographies and marketing/advertising spend
items.quote: And also there is more frontline sales teams to work on in the newer geographies that we are going and intensifying our approach in the markets that we are already there and also advertising costs.

items.statement: New lab/collection center network takes 18-36 months to mature; ongoing investment may pressure near-term margins
items.quote: It could be anything between 18-36 months that would take for the collection network or a new collection center and a lab network to really start maturing and contributing significantly to the volume and the revenue numbers.

items.statement: Implemented Microsoft D365, Starlims and full IT stack in Suburban in Q4 FY25; unified digital infrastructure across brands

items.statement: Cost of borrowing flat QoQ at 8.07% despite increase in long-term borrowings share
items.quote: Cost of borrowing remained flat QoQ at 8.07% despite an increase in share of long-term borrowings.

items.statement: GNPA at 1.84% and NNPA at 0.85% for Q4 FY25; PCR at 54.47%
items.quote: The asset quality remains stable with GNPA at 1.84% and NNPA of 0.85% for the Q4FY25. The provisioning coverage ratio stood at 54.47%.

items.statement: No accelerated write-off in Q4 FY25; policy write-off only ₹141 crores vs ₹520 crores last quarter (incl. ₹163 crores accelerated)
items.quote: Last quarter, we had ₹520 crores of write-off in the erstwhile STPL, which included ₹163 crores of accelerated write-off. I would like you all to take the note that there is no accelerated write -off in Q4FY25, and the policy write-off is only ₹141 crores.

items.statement: Erstwhile STPL credit cost down 33% QoQ to ₹137 crores from ₹200 crores; residual book under control
items.quote: Our overall credit cost for erstwhile STPL has come down to ₹137 crores in Q4FY25 as compared to ₹200 crores in Q3FY25. That is a reduction of 33% over the previous quarter. This makes it quite clear that the erstwhile STPL issue has been addressed and with significant improvement in collection efficiency, we are in control of the residual book.

items.statement: Full year write-offs at ₹1,548 crores; Q4 write-offs significantly lower than Q2/Q3 FY25
items.quote: So, our full year write -off numbers are ₹1,548 crores, and however, if you look at the Q4, the write-offs have significantly come down as compared to the write -offs which we have done in

items.quote: We have recently raised ₹1,525 crores through NCDs in April-2025, which is in public domain. This issue was a fantastic success with competing pricing and participation from top 5 mutual funds and a bank. With this, NCD contribution increased now to 12% of the total borrowings as against the 6% as of March-2025.

items.statement: Variable rate borrowings at 70% of total liability, advantageous in declining rate environment
items.quote: The share of variable rate borrowings in our total liability stood at 70%, which puts us in the advantageous position with the declining interest rate environment envisaged.

items.statement: Debt-to-equity at 3.2x providing headroom for growth; capital adequacy at 22.94% (Tier 1: 21.67%)
items.quote: Our debt-to-equity ratio stood at 3.2x. This gives us enough headroom for our growth. Our capital adequacy continues to be healthy and comfortably above the regulatory requirement at 22.94%, of which the Tier 1 Capital is 21.67%.

items.statement: LCR at 126% as of Mar 31, 2025; surplus liquidity of ₹4,686 crores with positive cumulative mismatch across all buckets
items.quote: The LCR, the liquidity coverage ratio stood at 126% as of March 31, 2025. On the liquidity front, we remain comfortable with positive cumulative mismatch across all buckets and a surplus liquidity of ₹4,686 crores as of March 31, 2025.

items.statement: Plan to launch 400 new branches in next 4 quarters for gold loan business
items.quote: We have successfully launched 6 businesses till date with plans to launch another 400 branches in the next 4 quarters.

items.statement: AI-driven credit underwriting tools deployed, delivering 35%-40% increase in credit managers' efficiency
items.quote: We have already shared that this is leading to 35%-40% increase in credit managers' efficiency, and we've already launched the first phase of this.

items.statement: Debt management AI capabilities delivering 2x-3x sharper risk assessments and 2x faster customer reach
items.quote: In debt management , with the aim of enhancing efficiency, we now have capability to have micro strategies along with customer profiles, communication channel and engagement timings on a unified platform. This transform s the collection journey while reducing manual effort and enhancing efficiency through predictive models, delivering around 2 x to 3x sharper risk assessments, and we're able to hi

items.statement: HR AI tools reduced time to hire to 1/10th and increased offer capacity by 10x
items.quote: We have reduced our time to 1/10 and increased our offer capacity by 10x.

items.statement: 17-18 incremental AI projects identified across departments with specific launch timelines through Q4 FY25-26
items.quote: We've also done a fair work to identify 18 further incremental projects across departments, Credit, Internal Audit, HR, Admin, Infra, Analytics, IT, Customer service, Operations and other departments. They're based on the feedback received from the ground, which will improve productivity, bring in efficiency over a period of time.

items.statement: Forward collection efficiency improved 9%-10% in 6 months in toughest product line; early bucket flows moderated >40%
items.quote: In the last 6 months, we've improved forward collection efficiency by 9% to 10% in one of the toughest product lines and early bucket flows have moderated by more than 40%.

items.statement: On-book secured to unsecured mix improved to 57:43 from 54:46 previous quarter and 49:51 year ago
items.quote: Our on-book secured to unsecured mix was 57:43 compared to 54:46 in previous quarter and 49:51 in the same quarter last year.

items.statement: AUM mix: MSME 36%, personal & consumer finance 23%, LAP 24%, pre-owned cars 14%
items.quote: In terms of our AUM mix, contribution from MSME was 36%, followed by personal and consumer finance at 23%, loan against property and pre -owned cars at 24% and 14%, respectively.

items.statement: PL Prime: 75% customers at Category A companies, 72% with take-home salary above ₹75,000
items.quote: But I also want to assure you that 75% of customers work at Category A companies, 72%, that we do have take-home salaries above ₹75,000.

items.statement: Regulatory guidelines aim for enhanced transparency, consumer protection, harmonized lending norms; 50 bps repo cut in last 2 quarters
items.quote: The lending landscape has witnessed recent changes via regulatory guidelines aiming enhanced transparency, protecting consumers and harmonizing lending norms across financial institutions. This, coupled with a steep repo cut of 50 basis points in the last 2 quarters, intends to boost our country's economic growth.

items.statement: All incremental businesses post risk recalibration showing better than industry trends; need 3-6 months seasoning before regular disclosure
items.quote: So, see, in the last 10 months, all our credit underwriting for incremental businesses, which we have risk recalibrated, every signs are showing better than industry trend. However, I would like to see the seasoning it out in the next 3 to 6 months before we put it out as a regular information to all of you.

items.statement: FY26 consolidated double-digit revenue growth; Plywood EBITDA margin 10%+, MDF EBITDA margin 16%+
items.quote: In FY '26, we aim to achieve a double -digit revenue growth on a consolidated basis, contributed equally by both the businesses and EBITDA margin of 10% plus in Plywood business and 16% plus in MDF business.

items.quote: In FY '26, we are looking at a total capex again of around INR60 crores, INR65 crores, which will be very similar to our depreciation, consol depreciation. items.quote: Construction of our HDF flooring line is likely to be completed in this quarter, and the equipment is already in transit. Construction of glue plant is completed.

items.quote: Our consolidated core EBITDA for the quarter was at INR68 crores, a growth of 18.1% on a Y-o-Y basis. The core EBITDA margin for the quarter was at 10.5% as compared to 9.6% in quarter 4 FY '24.

items.statement: MDF Q4 EBITDA margin 15% vs 10.4% QoQ; FY26 target 16%+
items.quote: Our EBITDA margins improved to 15% as against 10.4% in the previous quarter.

items.statement: MDF inventory build for capacity expansion; plywood raw material inventory up INR70-80 crore to liquidate in 6 months
items.quote: INR70 crores to INR80 crores of additional inventory is there on the raw material front, which will come down in the next 6 months

items.quote: In the Plywood business, our volume growth for the quarter was 4.9% Y-o-Y and value growth for the quarter was around 9.8%.

items.quote: Market in the commodity segment post 15th April has done a 5% scheme increase or a price cut, whatever you want to call it. But Greenply is operating within the 1.5%, 2% range. We are not operating in the full 5%.

items.quote: Imports in any case at this point of time has almost become zilch. items.quote: Looking at the cash flows and the growth, what we are looking at, for sure, by the end of this year, the debt will get reduced by around INR100 crores, INR120-odd crores. And the year subsequent also for sure, the debt can reduce by INR100 crores to INR150-odd crores.

items.quote: I think the major bit is kind of done. Obviously, people were promised ESOP over a period. So some people are yet to vest what they've already been given. So because of that, a small cost will continue, but there's no major new plan coming in with some major new quantity.

items.quote: Our own expectation is that in year 1 itself, we should be doing anything around INR70 crores to INR80 crores first year. items.statement: Plywood Q4 core EBITDA margin 9.2% vs 8.7% YoY (+50 bps); FY25 8.5%
items.quote: the margin front, our core EBITDA margin for quarter 4 FY '25 was 9.2% as against 8.7% in quarter 4 of FY '24. The margin improved on a Y-o-Y basis by 50 basis points

items.statement: MDF double-digit volume growth FY26; dependent on capacity extension completion

items.statement: Annual debt repayments INR50-55 crore for next 2 years
items.quote: On the debt repayment side, every year, I think next 2 years, our repayments will be in the range of INR50 crores to INR55 crores each year.

items.statement: Expect double-digit volume growth in FY26 on organic capacity
items.quote: Prateek, we expect to grow double digit this year on a higher base.

items.statement: Target clinker-to-cement ratio of 1.54 by end of FY27

items.statement: India Cements EBITDA per ton target INR500 in FY26, INR800 in FY27, four-digit thereafter
items.quote: During this year, we target to cross an EBITDA per metric ton of INR500. FY '27 should be crossing INR800 and thereafter, a 4-digit mark.

items.statement: Building Products revenue target INR3,000 crores in 3 years
items.quote: This should go up to INR3,000 crores to INR 4,000 crores in -- INR3,000 crores not INR4,000 crores, sorry, INR3,000 crores in 3-year time window.

items.statement: Building Products ROCE upwards of 30% to 40%
items.quote: The ROCEs are upwards of 30% to 40%.

items.statement: FY26 organic capex INR9,000-10,000 crores, INR7,000 crores for strategic expansion to 212 mtpa
items.quote: FY '26 also would amount to about INR9,000 crores to INR10,000 crores of capex, out of which INR7,000 crores is towards strategic investments, the ongoing expansion program, which will take us from the current capacity of 184 million tons , 184 million includes India Cements and Kesoram capacities also from 184 million to take us to close to 212 million tons of capacity in India.

items.quote: The team has chalked out a capex plan of about INR1,500 crores for India Cements, out of which INR1,000 crores is towards WHRS and other profit improvement opportunities with a payback period of less than 3 years. This will be spent in fiscal '26 and '27

items.statement: FY27 capex expected to come down as expansion plan nears completion
items.quote: '27. We'll talk about it next year. But it should come down because most of our -- the expansion plan will start coming to a close. So it will not be as high.

items.quote: this year cement industry has ended with a capacity of about 655 million tons, up from 625 million tons . And at UltraTech, out of this 30 million tons of new capacity addition, almost 57% has been added by UltraTech.

items.statement: Effective capacity utilization 79% on 150 mtpa available capacity for FY25
items.quote: The capacity utilization that we achieved was 79% on an effective capacity available for the year of 150 million tons .

items.statement: Kesoram and India Cements add 25 mtpa to available capacity

items.statement: Industry demand grew ~4% in FY25, UltraTech volume growth ~10%
items.quote: We believe that this quarter, cement demand overall for the country would have grown around 4%. And in that backdrop, UltraTech has done close to 10% volume growth.

items.statement: Cost improvement program targeting upwards of INR300 per ton by FY27, INR86 achieved in FY25
items.quote: We will deliver upwards of INR300 per ton in efficiency improvement. As for demand, we are seeing positive movement in government spending.

items.statement: Kesoram FY25 EBITDA per ton INR112, Q4 FY25 INR399
items.quote: INR112 per ton, okay. Atul Daga: I think somewhere around INR 112 or INR115 per ton . Previous periods, I really don't have a handle. I'm just doing a console

items.quote: Second, from here onwards, where this quarter, their operating EBITDA or total EBITDA was INR40 a ton , improvement in volumes, which is capacity utilization at India Cements

items.statement: Kesoram full year volume 6.87 mt, Q4 volume 1.53 mt
items.quote: Full year Kesoram volume is 6.86 million tons or 6.87 million tons.

items.statement: India Cements sold >1 million tons in March 2025, first time in history
items.quote: Second case of sweet success was sales of more than 1 million metric tons in the month of March by India Cements.

items.statement: Prices improving in South markets from April, general improving trend seen
items.quote: With prices improving in the South markets from April, this will only reflect in further improvement in the company's performance.

items.statement: Fuel prices increased early in quarter but stabilizing with US crude output and softening global prices
items.quote: As for costs, fuel prices, as you're all aware, increased during the early days of the quarter. items.statement: India Cements working capital cycle improvement driving cost reduction
items.quote: Difficult to break up, a lot of efficiency improvement, which is being driven by working capital, improving the working capital cycle, which means cost of purchase is coming down, production efficiency is being improved.

items.statement: Net debt-to-EBITDA 1.16x at March 2025, expected to decline rapidly with volume and EBITDA growth
items.quote: Net debt-to-EBITDA is what we ended with 1.16x at the end of March '25. With the sales volumes continuously increasing, performance of the company continuously improving, EBITDA profile improving, the debt will start receding rapidly.

items.quote: With effect from 1st of March 2025, we have fully taken charge of these units. After obtaining an unconditional CCI approval, we had started working with these units earlier on, helping them improve their performance.

items.quote: We grabbed a small opportunity to strengthen our position in the white cement business with the acquisition of cement putty manufacturing facility. This is a small transaction, which should get concluded in the next few days.

items.statement: Kesoram rebranding to UltraTech over time
items.quote: Over a period of time, yes, it will get rebranded.

items.statement: Tamil Nadu mine auction technical bid deadline May 4-5, UltraTech interested
items.quote: We will be interested, but there is no date yet. As of now, I think May 4. We are in April. May 4 or 5 is a technical bid submission, the last date, which I remember. No extensions have been announced as yet.

items.statement: Building Products segment revenue INR921 crores in FY25, 21% growth
items.quote: First, on the Building Products segment. So revenue is at INR 921 crores, impressive growth of 21%.

items.statement: Northeast expansion challenging due to infrastructure and access issues, holding Star Cement stake
items.quote: It's not an easy terrain to operate because even if you find mines and plant land, the access roads are not really there and the economics of operating the plant go for a toss depending because of the various issues that are existing. items.statement: CW business critical positions hired, long lead items ordered, revenue start targeted December 2026
items.quote: Critical positions, 1 or 2 critical people have been hired or sorry, offers have been made. Orders have been placed for long lead item, drawings work has been completed, and we are committed to start revenues as planned by December '26.

items.statement: Targets 30% top-line and bottom-line growth for FY26
items.quote: And as our commitment, we will definitely expect we will achieve 30%as that we have achieved inlast few years.

items.quote: For financial year 2026, we plan to invest in the range of 25% to 28% of our revenue in new content acquisition.

items.statement: Content acquisition budget targeted at INR95-120 crores for FY26
items.quote: Yes, we are targeting that.

items.statement: Operating margin guidance of 64% to 67% for FY26
items.quote: So next year also, , it could be in that range of, , 64% to 67% depending on how the content gets released,.

items.statement: Warner deal renewed with deal size 4x bigger; second tranche due October 2025

items.quote: But going forward, we are targeting to release 100 -125 songs but we'll invest 25% to 28% of our top line.

items.statement: Warner Music contributes 20-25% of full year revenue
items.quote: And Warner deal, as you are aware, we booked the revenue basis the consumption report. And what Kumarji has said that it is in the range of around 20-25% of the overall revenue.

items.statement: Warner advance tranches: one received March 2024, second split between April 2025 and October 2025
items.quote: The second tranche was divided into two parts. So, one came in, , April '25, right And the second tranche will come in October 2025

items.quote: There were certain old content advances, which were more than 3 years. So we had done a provision on a conservative basis. And second, there was a loan given also to one of our erstwhile landlord, which was outstanding for more than 3 years.

items.quote: During FY '25, the company has declared a cumulative interim dividend of INR7 per share and a buyback for non-promoter shareholders amounting to INR46.6 crores, which brings the payout ratio for FY '25 to around 82%.

items.quote: I think if you see the overall industry, our total industry is around INR3,500 crores, INR4,000 crores in that range. And we have a potential to grow around INR10,000 crores in the next 4 to 5 years.

items.quote: In India, we need 2 or , 3 companies in the content business, particularly I'm talking about Hindi Music. And we are already now 5 people fighting for the content.

items.quote: And yes, IPRS and other societies are continuously growing in India, thanks to the consumption that happens in India.

items.statement: Content investment recovery target: 4-5 years; company has historically recovered content cost in same quarter
items.quote: Our target is to recover whatever we invest in the next 4 years to 5 years' time. So that will continue. And you know, we are the only company which rise of the content cost in the same quarter.

items.statement: Expect double-digit volume growth in FY26 on organic capacity
items.quote: Prateek, we expect to grow double digit this year on a higher base.

items.statement: Target EBITDA per ton of INR 500 for India Cements in FY26, INR 800 in FY27, and 4-digit thereafter
items.quote: During this year, we target to cross an EBITDA per metric ton of INR500. FY '27 should be crossing INR800 and thereafter, a 4-digit mark.

items.statement: Target clinker-to-cement ratio of 1.54 by end of FY27
items.quote: By the end of fiscal '27, we are targeting to reach 1.54.

items.statement: FY26 organic capex guided at INR 9,000-10,000 crores, including INR 7,000 crores for strategic expansion to reach ~212 mtpa capacity
items.quote: FY '26 also would amount to about INR9,000 crores to INR10,000 crores of capex, out of which INR7,000 crores is towards strategic investments, the ongoing expansion program, which will take us from the current capacity of 184 million tons , 184 million includes India Cements and Kesoram capacities also from 184 million to take us to close to 212 million tons of capacity in India.

items.statement: India Cements capex plan of INR 1,500 crores over FY26-27, INR 1,000 crores for WHRS and profit improvement with <3 year payback
items.quote: The team has chalked out a capex plan of about INR1,500 crores for India Cements, out of which INR1,000 crores is towards WHRS and other profit improvement opportunities with a payback period of less than 3 years. This will be spent in fiscal '26 and '27 and the benefits will start reflecting in the performance of the company in the quarter of Jan, March '27.

items.statement: Current effective capacity 150 mtpa, rising to 158 mtpa with new additions; year-end capacity 184 mtpa including acquisitions
items.quote: The capacity utilization that we achieved was 79% on an effective capacity available for the year of 150 million tons . Mind you, the effective capacity is important to know, whilst our year -ending capacity was significantly higher, the effective available capacity weeds out the impact of non-availability of capacity through the 12 months.

items.statement: Target to expand capacity from 184 mtpa to ~212 mtpa via ongoing expansion program
items.quote: the ongoing expansion program, which will take us from the current capacity of 184 million tons , 184 million includes India Cements and Kesoram capacities also from 184 million to take us to close to 212 million tons of capacity in India.

items.statement: Kesoram full-year volume 6.86-6.87 mt; Q4 volume 1.53 mt at INR 399 EBITDA/ton
items.quote: Full year Kesoram volume is 6.86 million tons or 6.87 million tons.

items.statement: India Cements achieved EBITDA breakeven in first quarter post-takeover; sold >1 mt in March 2025
items.quote: I'm delighted to inform you that the company has achieved an EBITDA breakeven in the first quarter after the takeover. Second case of sweet success was sales of more than 1 million metric tons in the month of March by India Cements.

items.statement: Q4 FY25 organic EBITDA/ton INR 1,270; consolidated with Kesoram INR 1,238/ton
items.quote: this quarter, our organic capacities, if I were to measure like-for-like, we did an EBITDA per ton of INR1,270 per ton. With the performance of Kesoram added for full quarter January, February, March '25, this INR1,270 drops down to INR1,238 per metric ton.

items.statement: Cost improvement program targeting upwards of INR 300/ton efficiency gain by FY27; INR 86/ton delivered in FY25
items.quote: We will deliver upwards of INR300 per ton in efficiency improvement.

items.statement: Kesoram FY25 EBITDA/ton INR 112-115; Q4 FY25 INR 399/ton
items.quote: INR112 per ton, okay. Atul Daga: I think somewhere around INR 112 or INR115 per ton . Previous periods, I really don't have a handle. I'm just doing a console

items.statement: Industry demand grew ~4% in FY25; UltraTech organic volume growth 6-7% in Q4, ~6% for full year
items.quote: We believe that this quarter, cement demand overall for the country would have grown around 4%. And in that backdrop, UltraTech has done close to 10% volume growth.

items.statement: Short-term demand impacted by heat wave; expect improvement once temperatures subside, especially in Bihar and Andhra
items.quote: The beginning of the year is slightly weak because of very heavy heat or high heat that is prevailing, the heat wave that is prevailing in the country, which slows down the construction activity in a bit.

items.statement: Prices improving in South markets from April; general improving trend seen in current month vs last quarter
items.quote: With prices improving in the South markets from April, this will only reflect in further improvement in the company's performance.

items.statement: India Cements improvement driven by working capital cycle improvement, reducing purchase costs
items.quote: a lot of efficiency improvement, which is being driven by working capital, improving the working capital cycle, which means cost of purchase is coming down

items.statement: Net debt-to-EBITDA at 1.16x end March 2025; expect rapid deleveraging with volume and EBITDA growth
items.quote: Net debt-to-EBITDA is what we ended with 1.16x at the end of March '25. With the sales volumes continuously increasing, performance of the company continuously improving, EBITDA profile improving, the debt will start receding rapidly.

items.statement: Kesoram mines transferred and registered in Telangana and Karnataka; full operating control from March 1, 2025
items.quote: After a tedious long -drawn process, we successfully completed the transfer and registration of mines in Telangana and Karnataka for the cement units that we acquired from Kesoram.

items.statement: India Cements takeover from Dec 2024; tolling arrangement and gradual rebranding to UltraTech by end FY27
items.quote: We will -- same thing, we will enter into a tolling arrangement and gradually convert India Cements brand also into UltraTech.

items.statement: White cement putty manufacturing facility acquisition to conclude in few days
items.quote: We grabbed a small opportunity to strengthen our position in the white cement business with the acquisition of cement putty manufacturing facility. This is a small transaction, which should get concluded in the next few days.

items.statement: No plan to acquire remaining 18.51% of India Cements; will do MPS to reduce to 75%
items.quote: We are holding 81.49% 81.49% of India Cements. The first requirement will be to do an MPS to bring it down to 75%.

items.statement: Building Products segment ROCE 30-40%; revenue target INR 3,000 crores in 3 years from INR ~1,000 crores
items.quote: The ROCEs are upwards of 30% to 40%. Growth trajectory, we have achieved, let's say, INR1,000 crores of revenues. This should go up to INR3,000 crores to INR 4,000 crores in -- INR3,000 crores not INR4,000 crores, sorry, INR3,000 crores in 3-year time window.

items.statement: WHRS capacity addition: 44 MW for UltraTech, 24 MW for Kesoram, 22 MW for India Cements by FY27
items.quote: I have given you specifically the numbers on Kesoram assets, 24 megawatts. And ICL is about 22 megawatts. That's about -- 22 and 24, 46 megawatts of additional which will get added into our network.

items.statement: Tamil Nadu mine auction technical bid deadline May 4-5; UltraTech interested but no date extensions announced
items.quote: We will be interested, but there is no date yet. As of now, I think May 4. We are in April. May 4 or 5 is a technical bid submission, the last date, which I remember. No extensions have been announced as yet.

items.statement: JP asset arbitration award still awaited; no timeline visibility
items.quote: No, it's still -- award is still awaited.

items.statement: Royalty imposed in Tamil Nadu at ~INR 150/ton could impact cost improvement translation to EBITDA
items.quote: Take the case of the royalty, which was imposed in the state of Tamil Nadu, which is INR 150 a ton or something else that happens. So those factors have to be taken into account as well

items.statement: FY26 revenue growth guidance of 12% to 15% in constant currency and EBIT margin guidance of 11.25% to 12%
items.quote: We expect our revenue to grow in the range of 12% to 15% in constant currency terms and our EBIT margin to be in 11.25% to 12% band in FY26.

items.statement: FY25 constant currency revenue growth of 22.6% exceeded guided band of 21.8% to 22.3%
items.quote: Our constant currency revenue growth was 22.6%, above the higher end of our guided band of 21.8% to 22.3% that we have provided in Q3FY25.

items.statement: 14 large deals won in FY25 including 4 over $10M ACV; total ACV intake highest ever; exit pipeline up over 30% YoY
items.quote: Overall, we won 14 large deals in FY25, including four deals that are over US$10 million of ACV, this is the highest we have had in the history of the company.

items.statement: Largest healthcare deal won in Q4 from new logo mid-market health plan in North America with ACV well over $50M steady state
items.quote: We won our largest deal in healthcare this quarter from one of the mid-market health plans in North America. This happens to be a new logo for us as well. This is a five-year business process as a service or BPaaS deal for us with an ACV well over $50 million in steady state.

items.statement: FY25 EBIT margin excluding one-offs at 11.1% within guided 11-11.5% range; Q4 EBIT margin 11.2% up 10bps QoQ and 20bps YoY
items.quote: Our EBIT margin for FY25 excluding one-offs was 11.1% within our guided range of 11 % to 11.5%.

items.statement: 37 margin levers under 9 buckets identified to achieve FY26 margin expansion of 50-75bps per year
items.quote: We have got roughly about 37 margin levers which sit under these nine broad buckets that I called out. That essentially is the margin walk, if you will, that we are working on as a company to try and get to be in the 11.25% to 12% range.

items.statement: Healthcare vertical grew 30% YoY in FY25 despite H2 softness; Q4 record ACV won; momentum expected to carry into FY26
items.quote: As you will note, even with some softness in the second half, this vertical grew 30% YoY in FY25. We expect that momentum to carry forward into FY26 as well.

items.statement: Diverse portfolio declined 9% QoQ due to retail seasonality; healthy pipeline in retail and utilities for coming quarters
items.quote: Lastly, coming to our Diverse Portfolio, which comprises of our Retail and Utilities business. We saw a 9% QoQ decline in constant currency terms, primarily due to seasonal softness in the retail business.

items.statement: Top 5 client concentration down to 29.4% from 36.4%; Top 10 down to 43.7% from 52.6% YoY; 13 clients added with >$1M revenue, 5 with >$5M, 2 with >$10M in last 4 quarters
items.quote: The share of revenues from our Top 5 clients has come down to 29.4% versus 36.4% and Top 10 clients to 43.7% from 52.6% in Q4 of last year.

items.statement: 43 new logos added in FY25 including 12 strategic logos; 7 new logos in Q4 including 2 strategic
items.quote: In FY25, we added 43 new logos, which include d 12 logos that we consider as strategic

items.statement: Capex in FY25 more than double FY24; added over 7,000 seats vs 2,000+ in FY24; will continue investing in FY26 given order book strength
items.quote: Our capex in FY25 was more than double that of FY24, as we prepared the execution infrastructure to fulfil the order wins. To give a perspective, we added over 7,000 seats in FY25, versus 2,000 plus we added in FY24.

items.statement: DSO 70 days in Q4; normalized for collection delays would be 67 days; delays subsequently collected in first two weeks of April
items.quote: DSOs stood at 70 days in Q4. There were some delays in collections in a couple of accounts all of these were subsequently collected in the first two weeks of April. Normalized for that, our DSO would be 67 days.

items.statement: Hedge book: GBP 74.6M at avg Rs 110.3/GBP and USD 167.1M at avg Rs 86.1/USD for next 12 months
items.quote: Our hedge book as of 31st March 2025 was as follows: we had coverage of GBP 74.6 million for the next 12 months with an average rate of Rs 110.3 per Pound and coverage of US D 167.1 million with an average rate of Rs 86.1 per US$.

items.statement: BPaaS deal uses non-linear Per-Member Per-Month (PMPM) pricing model; revenue flow-through staggered over 24-month transition
items.quote: The contract has a non-linear construct in the form of a Per-Member Per-Month (PMPM) model. So you will see the revenue flow-through also happen accordingly in this fashion.

items.statement: Revenue per employee declining due to conscious shift to 80% offshore/nearshore hiring at lower revenue realization by design
items.quote: We have consciously increased the percentage of workforce that we have in offshore and near-shore locations, which come at a lower revenue realization than what you'd see typically in-country in the U.S. or U.K. or Australia itself. So that's by design more than anything else.

items.statement: Gained almost half a percent market share over last 4 quarters vs basket of 15 global publicly traded peers based on trailing 4-quarter revenues
items.quote: Our improved growth momentum has helped us gain almost half a percent of market share over the last four quarters against the basket of fifteen of our closest global publicly traded peers, based on trailing 4 quarters reported revenues.

items.statement: Dividend payout of Rs 2.8 billion during Q4; cash balance including investments at Rs 2.2 billion end of Q4
items.quote: Our cash balance, including investments, stood at Rs 2.2 billion at the end of Q4. This is after the dividend payout of Rs 2.8 billion during the quarter.

items.statement: Included in S&P Global Sustainability Yearbook second consecutive year; Industry Mover recognition; Top 5% S&P Global CSA Score among 7,690 companies; EcoVadis Silver Medal 71/100, 91st percentile
items.quote: Firstsource was included in the prestigious S&P Global Sustainability Yearbook for the second consecutive year, this time with an even greater impact, earning recognition as an Industry Mover and achieving a Top 5% S&P Global CSA Score amongst the 7,690 companies assessed during 2024-25.

items.statement: Targeting 15% revenue growth for FY26, up from 8-9% in recent years
items.quote: We have -- last 2 years have been almost stable at around 8%, 9% I'm hoping t o break that barrier this year a nd we are targeting for 15%, but let's see how it goes

items.statement: Aiming to reach INR500 crores revenue in 1-2 years and INR1,000 crores longer term
items.quote: Once again, like I said that the first target is INR500 crores. The next as a target will be obviously 1,000 fine.

items.statement: Expect gross contribution margin to maintain 52-54% for at least next year
items.quote: We expect it to maintain between 52% to 54% for over at least next year, then we will see about the balance subsequently.

items.statement: Targeting 2-3 percentage point improvement in EBITDA and net profit margins
items.quote: So let us say the aim should be to increase about 2 to 3 basis points on both these issues.

items.statement: Advanced bookings jumped 63% to INR151.21 crores from INR92.59 crores last year
items.quote: Last year our advanced bookings were INR92.59 crores. This year it is INR151.21 crores, INR150 crores of advanced booking gentlemen. It shows that the company is accepted into the market. It is a 63% jump over the last year.

items.statement: Gross margins remained strong at 52% plus with exceptional jump in FY25
items.quote: Gross margins remained strong at 52% plus with an exceptional jump in the current year, underscoring the resilience of our product mix and the pricing discipline we have maintained throughout the year.

items.statement: EBITDA grew 4% to INR52 crores while revenue grew ~9%
items.quote: EBITDA for the year was INR52 crores, up by almost 4% year-on-year and PAT rose by 13.3% to INR41.6 crores.

items.statement: Non-cotton non-paddy segment contribution increased to 48% from 43%, revenue grew 38% to INR171 crores
items.quote: I'm happy to share that this year, the contribution of the NCP segment increased to 48% compared to 43% last year. Revenue from this segment grew up by 38%, reaching to INR171 crores, up from INR140 crores in FY '24.

items.statement: Vegetable seed segment value growth 60.45% and volume growth 76.71%
items.quote: The vegetable segment, not to be left behind, it had value growth of (corrected from 16.45%) 60.45% and volume growth of 76.71%.

items.statement: Maize business registered 47% year-on-year value growth
items.quote: Our maize business also showed good momentum, registering year-on-year value growth of 47%.

items.statement: Bajra segment recorded 8.77% growth driven by Super 27
items.quote: Bajra continues to be a standout performer for us, supported by strong traction of Super 27. The segment recorded 8.77% growth over last year.

items.statement: Cotton sales 11.35 lakh packets in FY25, expecting 60-70% more supply this year
items.quote: And this year, again, it will be strengthened because this year, we are expecting to supply more than, let's say, 60% to 70% what we have sold this year.

items.statement: Added cold storage, warehouses and conditioning godowns with cumulative capacity of 25,000 metric tons
items.quote: Our infrastructure backbone has also been significantly strengthened with state-of-the-art cold storage units, warehouses and conditioning godowns with a cumulative capacity of 25,000 metric tons.

items.statement: Uzbekistan JV with 90% shareholding, 600 hectares for cotton production, broke even at contribution level
items.quote: We have set up a JV company there with 90% of shareholding, 10% being mandatory given to the people in Uzbekistan, which is okay. Nath Bio-Genes ( We have the full control on that. And this was the first full year of operation wherein we took on around 600 hectares of land for cotton production

items.statement: Philippines cotton in advanced stage, optimistic about government commercial sales next season
items.quote: In the Philippines, we are in an advanced stage with our cotton and we are optimistic about commercial sales to the government in the coming season.

items.statement: Regular exports only INR4-5 crores, may reach INR10 crores; Uzbekistan could add INR100 crores in 2 years
items.quote: Regular exports are always like INR5 crores to INR6 crores only. It may go up to INR10 crores. That's it, which will not be making a net debt to my top line. But yes, if Uzbekistan comes through 2 years down the line, we'll be able to give you the quantum jump.

items.statement: Debtor days reduced to 89 from 103; inventory days increased due to planned quantum jump in FY26
items.quote: On the working capital front, we made good progress, especially receivables management improved noticeably with debtor days reducing to 89 days from 103 days. The inventory days have increased due to the quantum jump planned in year '26.

items.statement: Positive operating cash flow INR26.8 crores; bank balance INR87.6 crores as of March 31
items.quote: The company had achieved positive cash flow from its operations to the tune of INR26.8 crores, and we had a bank balance of INR87.6 crores as on 31st March.

items.statement: Credit rating upgraded 2 notches to BBB+
items.quote: I'm also pleased to share that our credit rating was upgraded by 2 notch to BBB+, which is a clear endorsement of our financial prudence and healthy outlook.

items.statement: Cash balance of INR87 crores is operational money from advance bookings, not available for buyback/dividend
items.quote: We do have a fixed deposit of around INR87 crores as on 31st March 2025. But that money is currently are operational monies, which we are having pursuant to the advanced booking, which came to us for the current year sales.

items.statement: Buyback under consideration for past year, may announce if conditions permit
items.quote: Secondly, your question regarding buyback. I'm not able to answer it straightforward as of now, but we do have been thinking on it over the last one year. Maybe if the things permit, God willing, we'll come back to you.

items.statement: Hybrid paddy share 38% in value and 19% in volume; strategy shifting from RS to hybrid paddy
items.quote: The share of hybrid paddy in our portfolio was 38% in value and 19% in volume. This aligns with our broader goal of driving margin accretive growth through higher value hybrid products.

items.statement: Launched WINPro GOLii and WINall Granules biotonic products for plant nutrition
items.quote: We Nath Bio-Genes ( further expanded our portfolio with two new biotonic products, WINPro GOLii and [WINall Granules offering farmers more comprehensive solutions to boost crop growth and yield

items.statement: Consolidated three product verticals under unified marketing leadership for sharper execution
items.quote: In a move to drive better synergy, we consolidated all three product verticals under a unified marketing leadership, ensuring sharper execution and stronger customer connect.

items.statement: Claim superior product performance vs Kaveri in cotton, maize, bajra; expect to match or exceed in hybrid paddy in 3-4 years
items.quote: And if you see in other crops, right, our product performance is coming better than Kaveri, either it's a note down. There are 2, 3 products which have performed outstandingly well in the market in quarter, corn, which is 11, 33 and Dominator 401, which is performing outstanding ly well

items.quote: I'd just like to add for the industry the outlook for cotton is naturally because there is an increase in cotton MRP by the government by INR37 per packet this year. items.statement: Expect slight price increases in other crops due to rising commodity prices
items.quote: Number two is other crops. Other crops, there will definitely be a little bit of increase in the prices realization because the commodity prices themselves are going up.

items.statement: R&D spend INR10-12 crores annually (4-5% of revenue), decreasing as percentage due to revenue growth
items.quote: We -- every year, we spend around INR10 crores to INR12 crores increasing every year, if you 16:59 go through our schedules again. And it comes to around 4% to 5% of the top line.

items.quote: Retail loan growth 18%, Affordable loan book on 31st March 2026 will be Rs. 9,500 crores.

items.statement: Affordable loan book target of Rs 9,500 crores by March 2026
items.quote: Affordable loan book on 31st March 2026 will be Rs. 9,500 crores.

items.statement: Corporate disbursement guided at Rs 1,500-2,000 crores for FY26
items.quote: Corporate disbursement will be in the range of Rs. 1,500 crores to Rs. 2,000 crores.

items.quote: NIMs should be stable. When I say stable, if I have to give you a range, it will be between 3.6 to 3.65.

items.statement: ROA guided at 2.5-2.6% for FY26
items.quote: ROA would be in the range of 2.5% to 2.6%.

items.statement: Credit cost to remain negative for whole of FY26 due to write-off recoveries
items.quote: Yes. Whole of FY26 will be write back and credit cost will be negative.

items.statement: Affordable loan book target of Rs 15,000 crores by March 2027
items.quote: By March 27, our Affordable books will be Rs. 15,000 crores.

items.statement: Retail loan book target of Rs 1,00,000 crores by March 2027
items.quote: March 27 , I reiterate , our retail loan book is going to be Rs. 1,00,000 crore.

items.quote: Emerging will be Rs. 25,000 crores and the balance Rs. 60,000 crore will be a Prime book.

items.statement: Affordable and Emerging mix target of 40% by FY27
items.quote: So on a long -term basis, we have guided that this mix should touch by 40% by FY '27.

items.statement: Steady state ROA target of 2.5-2.6% by FY27 excluding write-off recoveries
items.quote: So by FY '27 on a steady state, we want to reach to around 2.5-2.6 without the support of the recovery.

items.statement: NIM target of 4.0-4.1% by FY27
items.quote: By FY'27, NIM will go to 4.0-4.1.

items.quote: Our idea is to take a yield to about 12.65% in FY'26.

items.statement: Prime incremental yield target of 9.5-9.6% for FY26

items.quote: The plan is to take to 500 by March '27. So Affordable, which is now 200 we will take it to about 300 branches and the rest would be largely in Emerging.

items.quote: We closed the year with an order backlog of INR1,019 crores, where INR900 crores plus of that was from India and INR100 crores plus from International.

items.quote: The domestic opportunity pipeline that we have includes large projects in the government sector, which we have discussed before. Many of them are in a very advanced stage of negotiations and hope to continue for the next one or two quarters.

items.quote: Well, yes, I think their capex spend has a direct relation to us. items.quote: The profitability for the quarter and to that ex tent the full year is partly impacted because of the provisions for inventory obsolescence and write-down of about INR117 crores that we did in this quarter, Q4. The number for the full year was INR181 crores

items.quote: the Board has recommended a dividend of 25%, which turns out to be INR2.5 per share, subject to the approval of the shareholders.

items.quote: In wireless, there are Nokia, Ericsson, and others. In optical, these are Ciena, Nokia, and so on. And in routing and switching for the service providers, Nokia and Cisco, and so on. items.quote: Since we develop a significant amount of hardware as part of our products, there will always be some amount of inventory which goes obsolete or which becomes unus able in terms of business because of products that we couldn't take to production and so on

items.statement: No cost of funds reduction penciled in for FY26

items.statement: Co-origination to remain at 20% of incremental origination
items.quote: Six, co-origination will remain at 20% of our incremental origination, nothing changes there.

items.statement: Gold loan book to remain 15-17% of total AUM
items.quote: Gold will remain 15% to 17% of our book, no change.

items.statement: Credit cost guidance of 1% plus/minus 10 bps for FY26
