items.statement: AUM reached INR 8,747 crores with 28% YoY and 7% QoQ growth as of March 2025
items.quote: Our AUM for March 2025 is INR 8,747 crores with a growth of 28% on a Y-o-Y basis and 7% on a Q-o-Q basis, with 100% of our AUM now secured by properties and gold.

items.statement: MSME AUM grew 27% YoY and 7% QoQ to INR 7,249 crores (83% of total AUM)
items.quote: Our MSME AUM, which is 83% of our AUM grew by 27% Y-o-Y and 7% Q-o-Q to INR 7,249 crores.

items.statement: Added 22 branches in FY25, 8 in Q4; total branch count 205 as of March 2025
items.quote: We added 22 branch during the year, 8 branch during the last quarter. The total branch count now stands at 205, as of 31st March '25.

items.statement: Yields stable at 17.88%, spreads at 8.53% for Q4 FY25
items.quote: In terms of yield, spreads and opex, the yields and spreads continue to remain stable at 17.88% and 8.53%, respectively, for the quarter.

items.statement: Borrowing cost reduced 5 bps YoY to 9.33% for full year FY25
items.quote: Our borrowing cost has reduced 5 basis points Y-o-Y and is at 9.33% for the full year in spite of continuous increase in MCLR during the year.

items.statement: Opex flat QoQ at 4.62% but improved 39 bps YoY due to operating leverage
items.quote: Our opex is flat compared to previous quarter and is at 4.62% for the quarter, but improved by 39 basis points from Q4 of previous year due to operating leverage increase in the organization.

items.statement: GNPA at 2.74% in Q4 FY25 with PCR improving to 45.69%
items.quote: In terms of asset quality, our GNPA is range bound in Q4 to 2.74% with PCR increasing to 45.69%.

items.statement: Credit cost at 1% for Q4 FY25, within guidance range
items.quote: Our credit cost is 1% for the quarter, which is in the range of our guidance.

items.statement: Karnataka portfolio impact caused 50 bps increase in 0+ DPD
items.quote: Basically 50 basis points is due to that thing.

items.statement: Month-on-month improvement in Karnataka collections since January 2025
items.quote: So obviously, this started somewhere at the beginning of the last quarter. And all I can mention is that sequentially, we're seeing improvement month-on-month. So Feb was better than Jan and March was obviously better than Feb.

items.statement: PAT of INR 94 crores for Q4 FY25, up 29% YoY and 7% QoQ; full year PAT INR 345 crores, up 46% YoY
items.quote: We made PAT of INR 94 crores for the quarter, thereby reporting a growth of 29% on a Y-o-Y basis and 7% on a Q-o-Q basis. And the PAT for the full year is at INR 345 crores, which has grown at 46% on a Y-o-Y basis.

items.statement: Return on average AUM at 4.52% and ROE at 13.14% for Q4 FY25
items.quote: Our return on average AUM for the quarter is 4.52%, with return on average tangible equity further improving to 13.14% for the quarter.

items.statement: Capital adequacy ratio at 36.1% with tangible net worth of INR 2,900 crores as of March 2025
items.quote: In terms of capital and return ratios, our capital adequacy ratio is 36.1% with tangible net worth of INR2,900 crores, as of March '25.

items.statement: Rate cut transmission to customers unlikely in FY26 due to lag in MCLR repricing
items.quote: I don't see any rate reduction possibility for customers this financial year at least.

items.statement: RBI draft gold loan circular provides clarity; regulatory risk off the table for SBFC
items.quote: On product design of gold loans, there was ambiguity and interpretation issues. The new draft circular provides immense clarity and the regulatory risk on the business continuity, which was a concern all of last year, is now off the table.

items.statement: Tamil Nadu exposure at 3% of AUM; will monitor before ramping up
items.quote: Answering your second question in terms of the Tamil Nadu exposure, we have a 3% overall exposure. We'll be a little watchful as to how the situation unfolds in this particular quarter before deciding to significantly ramp-up.

items.statement: Gold loan volume grew 15% YoY; price appreciation contributed ~25% to 40% total growth
items.quote: So in terms of the tonnage, we saw -- so in terms of volume growth, the split is 15% is largely driven because of volume and 25% is the benefit that we got in terms of the price increase -- average price increase. And that's how it sums up your 40% growth in the gold business.

items.statement: Western region growth muted at ~12% due to deliberate slowdown; accelerated ramp-up planned
items.quote: It is a soft pocket for us and some part of it is by design. Some of the states we had last year consciously had slowed down because we weren't very comfortable on the numbers that were coming up from the industry perspective.

items.statement: Management expects continued volatility; maintains watchful stance on credit quality
items.quote: So one needs to be careful, and one needs to be watchful. We don't know what the future entails. And the fact is that when we are lending to a customer segment, which is a higher risk segment, and therefore, we have to be a lot more watchful always.

items.statement: Steady-state ROA target of 4-4.5% for next year as leverage increases
items.quote: ROA has been ranging around 4.5% from the last 6-odd quarters. And as we lever up, there will be some compression on the ROA, but we would want to hold it on for the next 1 year between 4% to 4.5%.

items.statement: Technology investments include paperless gold loan via iris scan, account aggregator, and generative AI credit assessment with AWS
items.quote: We have just gone live with a paperless gold loan. When a customer visits our branch today, just with their iris scan, we have e-KYC, e-signed done and money is in the customer's account and agreement on their WhatsApp.

items.statement: Management not providing FY26 revenue guidance

items.statement: Near-term slowdown in decision-making for large transformational deals due to macro uncertainty

items.statement: FDA staff cuts may delay submission reviews and increase quality expectations, creating medium-term opportunity for AI solutions

items.statement: Q4 FY25 EBITDA margin 20.2%, down 60 bps QoQ due to higher wage bill from vacation accrual, US payroll taxes, and off-cycle increments
items.quote: EBITDA margins for the quarter stood at 20.2%, a drop of 60 basis points sequentially. The drop off in margins is due to a higher wage bill consisting of seasonal trends in vacation accrual and payroll taxes in the US and also midyear & off-cycle increments applicable to a subset of employees.

items.statement: FY25 EBITDA margin 19.8%, down 90 bps YoY due to higher on-site mix and technology non-employee expenses
items.quote: EBITDA margin on a full year basis reduced by 90 bps to 19.8%, mainly due to a higher on-site employee mix and certain increases in the non-employee expenses related to technology, both having almost an equal impact on the margin rate drop.

items.statement: Margin outlook for FY26 fairly stable with operating leverage upside, no material customer pricing pressure
items.quote: I would say that the margin outlook would be fairly stable even in the coming periods, and we will continue to strive to improve this, as we grow because we would get more operating leverage, which should add to the margins.

items.statement: Q4 wins: one $5M+ ACV deal with Top 10 EU pharma, three deals of $1.5M-$3M ACV with mid-tier pharma, pipeline of large engagements with Top 10 accounts
items.quote: We had some good wins in Q4 . One USD 5 million plus ACV deal with a Top 10 EU headquartered company. This customer and the deal hold potential for us. And three deals of 1.5 million to 3 million ACV with mid-tier pharma. These should start contributing to revenues later in the year. We have a pipeline of interesting potentially large engagements with a few of our Top 10 accounts as well.

items.statement: Top 20 customers grew 2% YoY; two top-5 accounts faced headwinds in FY25, one stabilized, other to see further volume reductions (~INR1M revenue impact each starting late Q1)
items.quote: We faced headwinds in 2 of our top 5 customers in 2024 or FY '25. We've been speaking about it through the last year. One of them has stabilized, and we believe will start growing this year. The other one, which we believe had stabilized, will see some further reductions in volumes.

items.statement: Active clients decreased from 75 to 73 in Q4 due to one-time project completions; $1M+ clients grew from 38 to 41
items.quote: The total number of active clients for us decreased slightly from 75 to 73, mainly due to some one-time revenue project completions. On the other hand, USD1 million clients grew from 38 to 41 in Q4.

items.statement: FY25 growth driven by customers outside Top 20; active accounts grew from 63 to 73, $1M+ clients from 35 to 41, mostly mid-sized pharma
items.quote: The growth was driven mainly by customers outside of the Top 20. This was a result of growth in existing customers and also new account additions. We grew our active accounts from 63 from last year to 73 this year and grew our USD1 million customers from 35 to 41.

items.statement: Enterprise commercial and medical segments are recurring (75% recurring, 11-12% reoccurring); omnichannel activation has more project-based work
items.quote: Typically, in the enterprise businesses, and this would be consistent across both enterprise commercial and enterprise medical, about 75% of our business would be recurring, about another 11%, 12% would be what we would call reoccurring, right? It may not be the same kind of business, but coming from the same customer under the same master service agreement year-on-year.

items.quote: Current quarter saw margin improvement of 40 bps. Q1 margin at 16.7 percentage. The 40 bps improvement was driven by operational benefit of 50 bps, which was partially offset with currency headwind of 10 bps.

items.statement: Declared dividend of $5.75 per share post quarter close, total payout $40M
items.quote: We declared dividend post-a quarter close of $5.75 per share leading to a total payout of $40 million.

items.quote: We continue to make progress on our operational metrics and the offshore mix has improved by 200 bps sequentially. You heard Keech state that we had two clients move some of their work offshore, plus the ramp up in the new deals helped with the better offshore mix.

items.quote: Early this year we got results for 24 and as always, we scored very well. On NPS 67, 27 points higher than industry median.

items.quote: The currency headwind for us is a combination of two factors. The underlying benefit that we get with respect to rupee depreciating, but at the same point of time how the hedges play out because we start taking hedges as per our hedge policies two years in advance.

items.statement: Facing continued price pressure from new labs; prices remain competitive in the market

items.statement: Inorganic growth is a strategy but nothing concrete currently

items.statement: Foray into biologics CDMO services: clone development, process development, biosimilarity assessment, preclinical scale-up for novel biologics, biosimilars, peptides

items.quote: We had successful GCP regulatory audit by the Ministry of Health of the Republic of Kazakhstan and cGMP audit by EMA, European Medicines Agency for human health products.

items.quote: For us, we look at a 1:1 return when we are investing in capex. And more or less, our investments have yielded this average.

items.statement: FY25 operating cash flow Rs. 7,484 crores, 73% YoY growth
