items.statement: Q4 FY25 operating cash flow Rs. 4,047 crores, 559% QoQ and 55% YoY growth
items.quote: Operating cash flow in the 4th Quarter stood at Rs. 4,047 crores representing a quarter-on-quarter growth of 559% and a year-on-year growth of 55%.

items.statement: FY25 business development added 14 projects with Rs. 26,450 crores expected booking value, 132% of guidance
items.quote: We added 14 new projects with an estimated saleable area of approximately 19 million square feet and expected booking value of Rs. 26,450 crores. This includes two new projects with an expected booking value of Rs. 3,000 crores added in the 4th Quarter. GPL has achieved 132% of its annual guidance for business development in Financial Year '25.

items.statement: Unsold inventory from recent acquisitions Rs. 50,000-55,000 crores, total inventory over Rs. 1,10,000 crores
items.quote: So, between Rs. 50,000 to 55,000 crores worth of inventory we have from just fresh inventory of acquisitions which are largely outright in nature and then a total inventory of, even we have some township project like Panvel and all, total inventory would be in excess of about Rs. 1,10,000 crores.

items.statement: Unsold inventory on books around Rs. 20,000 crores
items.quote: Around Rs. 20,000 crores.

items.statement: FY25 imputed EBITDA margin 26.2%, flat vs 26.8% in FY24
items.quote: I think the imputed EBITDA margins are essentially flat, 26.8% and 26.2%.

items.statement: FY25 PAT margin slightly above 10-15% guidance range
items.quote: We are actually slightly above that this year. So, I think reasonably happy with the margins achieved during the year and again don't really see them as very different than the previous year.

items.statement: Target 14-15% PAT margin at portfolio level for new business development
items.quote: Give or take 14% to 15% PAT margins what we are looking at, of course there are plotted development where this goes up to between 20% and 25%, even 30% of PAT margin. But at a portfolio level, 15% is what we want to consistently do.

items.statement: Absolute construction spends will increase in line with sales uptick
items.quote: I think the overall construction activity will of course be increasing in line with the sales uptick we have seen. So absolute spends will certainly increase but of course so will absolute collection.

items.statement: Cost inflation benign; steel prices dropped, cement flat to down, aluminum up in some markets
items.quote: I would say if I were to give you a sense of what we are seeing cost inflation in the last, say 2 to 3 years, I think this has been a very stable period of time where most of the cost inflation indices have been in control. Yes, in some markets aluminum costs have increased, but steel prices have also dropped, some markets cement have been flattish to

items.statement: Global macro uncertainty and low oil prices indicate relatively low commodity inflation period
items.quote: But I think some of the global macroeconomic uncertainty due to tariffs, etc. depending how that plays out, it could lead to a further benign cycle. On the cost side we are already seeing economies from China, US all underperforming so of course the situation is not stable and could change. But oil prices are at a low, these are all indicative of a relatively low commodity inflation period which w

items.statement: Strong demand across markets; no signs of concern; Q4 best ever quarter for sales and collections
items.quote: We just came off our best ever quarter from both the sales and cash collections perspective in Q4. This quarter is off to a good start with a strong launch underway already for us in Bangalore. So, we are not seeing any signs of concern at the moment and we will certainly be looking to another strong year ahead.

items.statement: Demand driven by wealth creation, aspiration, GDP growth, government policies, interest rate cuts
items.quote: I think it's simple wealth creation and aspiration in India. If you just look at some data points, depending on which report you refer, give or take India's GDP is going to get doubled into next 5 to 7 years. We would get into a sort of

items.statement: Conversion rates divergent 7-25% depending on project value proposition; rule of thumb 10-15%
items.quote: It's very divergent to be very frank. It can go as low as say 7-8% and can go high as 22% to 23% and sometimes even 25%. It depends upon very frankly the value proposition that the person coming into the site sees from price, product and payment plan. So generally, as a rule of thumb when you see anything which is slightly lower in APR, generally as a rule of thumb like plotted and all the convers

items.statement: Subvention limited to negative units, low single digits of sales
items.quote: See we don't tend to push much of subvention other than say negative units as in the units that don't have great views and the likes of it and they hover in typically low single digits at any point of time.

items.statement: Market share ~4.3% in top 7 cities; aim for double digits over medium term
items.quote: We have looked at the data that suggests that basis prop equity data for the top seven markets, our current market share would be about 4.3%. I think over the medium term we would like to take that to double digits.

items.statement: Ranked #1 in Pune, #2 in Mumbai, NCR, Bangalore by sales value despite single-digit market share
items.quote: For the first time we would be either #1, which we were in Pune, or #2 which we were in Mumbai, NCR and Bangalore by sales value. And in all of those, despite being one of the leaders, we would have a single digit market share implying to us that there is opportunity for significant growth in each of those markets.

items.statement: Net debt cap set at Rs. 10,000 crores; QIP proceeds of Rs. 6,000 crores to be deployed for growth
items.quote: The constraint we have set ourselves now is that we would like to keep net debt below Rs. 10,000 crores. Instead of looking at a net gearing target, we are looking at an absolute net debt cap. So, I think we can use that for the maximum that we will go to.

items.statement: Raised Rs. 6,000 crores equity via QIP in December 2024
items.quote: The record operating cash flow of nearly Rs. 7,500 crores we generated in Financial Year '25 combined with the equity capital of Rs. 6,000 crores we raised through a QIP in December 2024 will enable us to continue to invest for growth.

items.statement: FY25 volume growth 29% to 25.73 million sq ft; highest ever by any listed developer
items.quote: This was achieved through the sale of 25.73 million square feet of area, a volume growth of 29%. This is the highest ever booking value and volume achieved by any listed developer in India in a financial year.

items.statement: FY25 deliveries 18.4 million sq ft across 5 cities, 47% YoY growth
items.quote: We delivered projects aggregating to 18.4 million square feet across five cities in the year representing a year-on-year growth of 47%.

items.statement: FY26 revenue growth target of around 15%
items.quote: on an annualized basis, we would stick to that 15%-odd top line and growth. So that's what we are looking at today.

items.statement: FY27 expected to be a much better year with CAPEX on stream and EO availability resolved
items.quote: FY27 should be a much better year, because by then, the CAPEXs will be on stream. Hopefully, the EO availability issues will also get resolved.

items.statement: Board approved total CAPEX of Rs. 192 crore for expansions at subsidiaries and Rossari Biotech, phased commissioning by Q4 FY26
items.quote: The Board has approved a total CAPEX of approximately Rs. 192 crore, covering expansions at our sites. These projects, expected to be commissioned in a phased manner by Q4 of FY26

items.statement: Additional CAPEX of Rs. 97 crore for Unitop Chemicals and Tristar Intermediates, and Rs. 95 crore at Rossari Biotech, commissioning by Q4 FY26
items.quote: we are pleased to announce further investments with an additional CAPEX of Rs. 97 crore for expansion at our subsidiaries, Unitop Chemicals and Tristar Intermediates, and Rs. 95 crore at Rossari Biotech. These projects, which are expected to be commissioned in a phased manner by Q4 FY26

items.statement: Ethoxylation capacity expansion at Unitop and Tristar expected to commission by Q2 FY26; new non-EO backward integration projects by Q4 FY26
items.quote: the current CAPEX that is going on, that's more on the Ethoxylation capacity expansion that we are doing, that is expected to come on stream by Q2 FY26. These CAPEXs, the current CAPEXs, which we have announced, they are a mix of new initiatives and some new products

items.statement: Current Ethoxylation utilization at peak; formulation side at 50-55% utilization
items.quote: Currently on the Ethoxylation side, we are completely utilized in Unitop, Tristar. Overall, our capacity utilization apart from that would be in that range of 50% - 55% on the formulation side.

items.statement: Core business adjusted EBITDA margin at ~15% for FY25; consolidated margin 12.7% due to new vertical investments
items.quote: our core business continues to deliver healthy profitability with an adjusted EBITDA range of approximately 15% for FY25

items.statement: Institutional and B2C business to show low single-digit EBITDA in FY26, targeting positive annualized EBITDA
items.quote: FY26, we hope that this business on an overall basis, the Institutional and the Consumer business will start showing some positive EBITDA on an annualized basis. We should see some low single-digit EBITDA number for FY26.

items.statement: HPPC business expected low double-digit to mid-teens growth in FY26 driven by improved EO availability and non-EO products
items.quote: We are optimistic that some of these new non-EO products that our R&D has worked out, we should see traction of that in the current year. We should see overall, a low double-digit to a mid-teens growth in the HPPC business.

items.statement: Institutional and B2C vertical grew 67% YoY to Rs. 299 crore in FY25, now reported separately
items.quote: Our Institutional and B2C business delivered strong momentum, growing by 67% YoY to reach Rs. 299 crore in FY25.

items.statement: Exports grew 27% YoY in FY25, presence in over 70 countries; Q4 FY25 exports Rs. 162 crore vs Rs. 127 crore YoY
items.quote: Our global business also recorded a strong year with exports growing by 27% and our presence expanding to over 70 countries.

items.statement: Q4 FY25 exports were Rs. 162 crore compared to Rs. 127 crore in Q4 FY24
items.quote: Q4 exports was about Rs. 162 crore. And last year, it was about Rs. 127 crore.

items.statement: Working capital improved by 2 days YoY; inventory up for Agro season and supplier shutdown, receivables down 2 days, targeting further improvement in FY26
items.quote: On the working capital front, we have improved slightly by 2 days compared to last year. Inventory levels increased. This is in line with our strategy to build stocks in March 2025 ahead of the upcoming Agro season, and a planned supplier shutdown. Receivables have come down by 2 days

items.statement: Net debt of Rs. 70 crore in FY25; expected to at least double after new CAPEX; cost of debt ~8%
items.quote: FY25, we were at about net debt of Rs. 70 crore. Some of the new CAPEXs will come up during the year. I think we should be at a level of at least twice of what we currently are.

items.statement: Average cost of debt at about 8%
items.quote: We are at about 8% of cost.

items.statement: Board recommended dividend of Rs. 0.50 per share for FY25
items.quote: Additionally, the Board has recommended a dividend of Rs. 0.50 per share for FY25.

items.statement: Renewa biosurfactant platform (Sophorolipids) commercialized successfully, expanding capacity for cross-industry applications
items.quote: A key highlight is Renewa, our in-house biosurfactant platform. Designed with sustainability at its core, Renewa offers health, safety and environmental benefits while enhancing application efficiency.

items.statement: New CAPEX includes backward integration for Esters, Monomers, Trimellitic Anhydride; new chemistries in home/personal care, oil & gas, pharma, agro, paints, textiles
items.quote: the new expansion is for non-EO products, which are already raw materials, which we procure from outside, which includes Esters and a lot of Monomers, which we buy from outside, we would like to backward integrate. There are a couple of new chemistries which we are trying to explore in the Mellitic space.

items.statement: Ethylene Oxide (EO) availability from Reliance expansion delayed; expecting higher allocation in FY26; will prioritize high-margin EO products if supply constrained
items.quote: For this year, the Reliance expansion is delayed a little, and we are expecting confirmation from Reliance for the new EO supply. But at the moment, if there is a constraint on EO supply, we will give the EO to the maximum margin products rather than working on lower margins.

items.statement: Acrylic acid now a very small input cost; locally available from BPCL Kochi refinery, reducing import dependence
items.quote: Acrylic acid is a very small item. Ethylene oxide is our major item. But now we have a huge number of raw materials, which includes vegetable oil. So, it will be a very, very small percentage now. And now acrylic acid is available locally from Bharat Petroleum Corporation Limited from the Kochi refinery.

items.statement: Headcount increased by ~140-145 people over 2 years; significant additions in R&D (3x increase), sales, and consumer business
items.quote: if you see our overall terms in terms of number of people, the headcount has gone up roughly between the 2 years by about 140-145 people. There have been increases in the consumer business. The major increases have happened there. But even in the core businesses, we have added lot of people on the sales side as well as in the R&D

items.statement: Asset turnover for new backward integration CAPEX expected at 2x-3x vs 3.5x-4x for Ethoxylation
items.quote: Around 2x – 3x should be, because the backward integration, so around 2x – 3x should not be an issue.

items.statement: Geopolitical uncertainty (tariffs, wars) clouds visibility beyond FY27; management unable to provide 3-year outlook
items.quote: At the moment, we have done some expansion last year, and we are planning some expansions this year. Now looking at the global scenario with the geographical war situations in the Indian subcontinent, but also China, Taiwan, and the Iran and the Ukraine, all these issues, we are still not certain with the tariffs. So, at the moment, we are not clear on what the future is. The skies are not clear.

items.statement: Textile exports to Bangladesh cautious due to forex issues; diversifying to Southeast Asia, Egypt, Turkey to offset risk
items.quote: We have strong demand requirements, but we are being a little careful on what customers to work with, keeping in mind that they have issues on the foreign currency, et cetera. So, we are going a little slow in Bangladesh. But seeing that the current issues in Bangladesh, we have also started looking at other geographies to grow our textile exports. Some of the countries in Southeast, also looking

items.statement: Employee cost run rate Rs. 30-35 crore/quarter; other expenses Rs. 65 crore/quarter expected for FY26; costs front-loaded for growth initiatives
items.quote: my expectation is that we will be at that Rs. 30- Rs. 35 crore run rate. And the other expenses should be around Rs. 65 crore plus-minus per quarter.

items.statement: Gross margins for Buzil business in 26-27% range for FY25 and expected same for FY26
items.quote: Gross margins overall have been in the range of 26% -27%. It will be in the same range for this year as well as the last year.

items.statement: Board approved initial borrowing sanction of INR60,000 crores for FY26
items.quote: my Board has given me the initial sanction of INR60,000 crores of borrowing for this year. And that is a very conservative number that we have started.

items.statement: Conservative disbursement target of INR30,000 crores from railway-linked ecosystem
items.quote: if we do, say, typically even INR30,000 crores out of INR2.5 lakh crores, it will be akin to INR90,000 crores of what I'm giving to the Indian railways.

items.statement: INR14,000 crores of loans sanctioned or won as bids in calendar year 2025 including April
items.quote: In this calendar year, including the month of April, we have already done more than INR14,000 crores of loans.

items.statement: INR5,000 crore loan L1 with NTPC in April FY26
items.quote: In the first 4 months of this FY or if you take only this month, April, we have already done INR5,000 crores loan L1 with NTPC.

items.statement: Total addressable market of INR2.5 lakh crores including metro railways within MOA mandate
items.quote: the whole business is around INR2.5 lakh crores, including the metro railway.

items.statement: New business margins 2x to 3x higher than Indian Railways lending
items.quote: We are becoming lowest in this beating all banks and NBFCs and still making margins of 2x to 3x to what we used to get from Indian Railways.

items.statement: Operating cost less than 0.1% and lowest cost of funds enabling L1 bids
items.quote: You must have seen our operating cost is one of the lowest in the industry, about 0.1 -- we don't have 0.1%, even less than 0.1%.

items.statement: Diversifying from single client Indian Railways to entities with backward or forward railway linkages
items.quote: We are only limiting ourselves to the MOA, which gives me the legroom for giving loans to anything which is having backward or forward linkages to the railways.

items.statement: Expecting PPP projects from Indian Railways budget to create SPV financing opportunities
items.quote: We are also very excited to look at the PPP projects in the Indian Railways. If you look a t the budget of this FY, there is announcement that there will be PPP projects coming forward from the railway, and once it materializes, we'll be very happy to look at the requirements by the SPVs

items.statement: Refinancing opportunities actively in pipeline with instant disbursement upon bid win
items.quote: Refinancing is -- we are looking forward to very excitedly for the fact that the moment I win a bid for refinancing, the disbursement is done instantly. So yes, there are many things in pipelines.

items.statement: AUM rundown of ~INR10,000 crores per annum from 15-year Indian Railways loans
items.quote: Rundown of AUM is very steady. If you know, we have financed to the Indian Railways where it is repayment period is 15 years, okay? So the 15th year, to be precise, if it is 2025, then 2010 loan will come out to be going out of my books, which is in terms of INR10,000 crores per annum.

items.statement: Most of INR14,000 crores sanctioned loans expected to be disbursed in FY26 despite 2-year period
items.quote: what we expect that although there are 2-year period for this disbursement, we expect that most of the disbursement will be done in this FY itself.

items.statement: Targeting A-plus rated assets with negligible NPA chance in new railway ecosystem lending
items.quote: We are looking for good quality A -plus assets as our space where we do not find much competition as of now. And these are the space where we are looking forward to having a negligible chance of NPA.

items.statement: AUM steady at INR4.6 lakh crores as of FY25
items.quote: Our Asset Under Management is also very steady at INR4.6 lakh crores.

items.statement: Debt-to-equity ratio was touching near 10 before diversification strategy
items.quote: as the loan book with Indian Railways is very high and debt-to-equity ratio also were touching near to 10.

items.statement: Company conferred Navratna status in FY24-25, targeting Maharatna status
items.quote: Company was conferred Navratna status also in FY '24-'25, and we are working forward, cementing our position to be just Maharatna sooner

items.statement: Aim to improve SSSG and SCSG and achieve positive SSSG in FY26
items.quote: For FY26, our aim is to improve our SSSG and SCSG (1:50) and achieve positive SSSG in FY26.

items.statement: Target net addition of 120 stores annually starting FY26
items.quote: With these closures done, we aspire to do an addition on a net basis 120 stores annually, starting FY26.

items.statement: Expect first Middle East store to open by May end or June end in Dubai
items.quote: We expect our first store to open either by May end or by the June end marking an exciting milestone in our international expansion. This store is going to be planned to open in Silicon Central Mall in Dubai.

items.statement: Pilot 15 stores in first six months and 10 stores in second six months for new categories
items.quote: We would be looking to have 15-stores of this new concept in the first six months phase and 10 stores in the second six months' phase.

items.statement: Conservative estimate of 100 gross LFS additions in FY26
items.quote: I think about 100 additions in the coming FY26 on a conservative basis, because I have visibility for 100, it might be more as well.

items.statement: Target inventory days between 90 and 95 days through the year
items.quote: Usually our inventory spikes a little bit in March because of summer season, but through the year, we target inventory days between 90 days and 95 days.

items.statement: Expect gross margins in range of 62% to 63% or slightly higher in FY26
items.quote: From a gross margin perspective, I see our gross margins maybe in the range of 62% to 63% or maybe a little higher, but. I think maintaining gross margins and maintaining P&L margins will be our endeavor in FY26.

items.statement: Advertising and promotional spend to remain at 2% of revenue
items.quote: I think we will be at 2% and I think through the 2% we will be able to do justice for a bottom-wear and for the new pilot as well. So I don't see our AMP increasing in any way.

items.statement: Capex for new concept stores at Rs.2,000 to Rs.2,500 per square feet for additional space
items.value: Rs.2,000 to Rs.2,500 per square feet
items.quote: when we are going to be doing the additional space, CAPEX, I think to the extent of Rs.2,000 to Rs.2,500 per square feet we would Go Fashion (India) Limited April 30, 2025 be incurring of that additional

items.statement: Q4 FY25 SSSG at 2.1%, early signs of gradual demand improvement; April SSSG flattish, expecting May-June improvement
items.quote: During Q4 FY25, we achieved a low single digit SSSG of 2.1% while the broader environment remains somewhat challenging. We're beginning to see some early signs of gradual improvement in demand at the ground level.

items.statement: April SSSG flattish, expecting May and June to be good
items.quote: From what I see April SSSG has been flattish. So, we are expecting May and June to be good, but April has been a little slow.

items.statement: Average selling price Rs.769 driven by product mix shift; full price ratio maintained at 95.4%
items.quote: This transformation is reflected in the growth of our average selling price, which stood at Rs.769, mainly driven by the shift in our product mix. We have maintained a strong full price ratio at 95.4%, highlighting both the strength of our pricing strategy and continued acceptance of our products in the market.

items.statement: Expanding into women's topwear (kurtis, shirts, dresses) and select menswear (polos, chinos, lounge pants, casual shirts) as pilot in 25 stores
items.quote: These will include products like basic kurtis, shirts, dresses, and all day everyday casual clothing of women as well as selected men's apparel such as Polo Shirts, Chinos, Lounge Pants and Casual Shirts.

items.statement: Inventory days maintained at 102 days; target to optimize further by few days; achieved 50% pre-IndAS EBITDA to operating cash flow conversion in FY25
items.quote: A disciplined inventory management has resulted in maintaining our inventory days at 102 days. We believe that there is room to optimize this further by a few days, which will contribute to a stronger balance sheet and support long-term sustainable growth. I am pleased to share that we successfully achieved our target of converting 50% of our pre IndAS EBITDA into operating cash flows during FY25.

items.statement: Trade receivables up 6-7 days due to 70-80 store additions in Q4 and LFS expansion; expected to stabilize by Q1-Q2
items.quote: The debtors have actually gone up by about 6-7 days. Nikhil, which I think will stabilize in Q1 because we have added about 70,80 stores in Q4 also and through the year we have expanded into Shoppers Shop and Lifestyle.

items.statement: No standout bottom-wear only brands emerging; competition from top-wear players adding bottom-wear; Aditya Birla Retail stores consolidated in North
items.quote: So from a bottom-wear competition perspective, we don't really see any standout bottom-wear only brands, but yes as bottom-wear as the category has expanded, we have seen other players in top-wear also add bottom-wear to their existing portfolio of top-wear products.

items.statement: New category pilot risks: uncertain full price ratio, inventory turns, customer acceptance of menswear; will evaluate after 7-8 months
items.quote: Right now based on the research what I have done, I know it is a very high full price sales percentage category, but whether it is going to be 80%, whether it is going to be 85% or whether it is going to be close to 90%, that is something we will know only after the pilot.

items.statement: Separate product and design team built for new categories; bottom-wear team remains separate to avoid dilution
items.quote: We have strengthened our product and developed a design development team. So we have a separate team within our product and design team which is working only on this. The bottom-wear team still continues to be separate because at the end of the day when we are doing this pilot, we cannot dilute our main business which is a fast growing business.

items.statement: Reliance credit note Rs.11 crores in Q4 FY25 vs Rs.8 crores in Q4 FY24; delta Rs.3 crores contributed to LFS revenue growth
items.quote: See, last year during the same quarter, we had received a credit note of about Rs.8 crores and this year for Q4 same quarter, we have received Rs.11 crores. So the delta difference between this quarter and that quarter would be about Rs.3 crores.

items.statement: Combined ratio on NEP basis improved 1.4% YoY to 110.8% for FY25
items.quote: When we see this for '24-'25, this combined ratio would be 110.8. So basically, you can see, there is an improvement of 1.4% on the combined ratio.

items.statement: Q4 FY25 combined ratio on NEP basis improved 0.9% YoY to 110%
items.quote: On a quarter-by-quarter basis, the combined ratio in Q4 F '24 on a NEP basis would be 110.9%, while in Q4 FY '25 the combined ratio is 110 %, an improvement of 0.9%.

items.statement: Full year FY25 combined ratio on IRDA basis was 109.3% vs 108.7% in FY24
items.quote: Combined ratio, including 1/n is 109.3% for the year and Q4 is 111.3%. And compared to the full Financial Year last year it was 108.7%.

items.statement: Q4 FY25 combined ratio on IRDA basis was 111.3%
items.quote: Combined ratio, including 1/n is 109.3% for the year and Q4 is 111.3%.

items.statement: PAT more than doubled to Rs 425 crore in FY25 from Rs 182 crore in FY24
items.quote: PAT for the year has more than doubled from Rs. 182 crores to Rs. 425 crores.

items.statement: Q4 FY25 PAT was Rs 116 crore, more than 2x YoY
items.quote: For Quarter 4 our profit is Rs. 116 crores, which is more than 2x the profit.

items.statement: FY25 profit had no capital gains, in fact a capital loss of Rs 3.4 crore
items.quote: In fact, we have a capital loss of Rs. 3.4 crores.

items.statement: ROE for Q4 FY25 was 3.5%, full year FY25 ROE was about 13%
items.quote: ROE in the 4th Quarter is 3.5%, for the entire year it is about 13%.

items.statement: Health loss ratio improved to 83.8% in FY25
items.quote: In Health, I think we have seen a good development in growth as well as on the loss ratio, which is 83.8%.

items.statement: Fire gross loss ratio improved to 56.8% in FY25 from 84% in FY24
items.quote: This year, the loss ratio , on a gross basis , is only 56.8%.

items.statement: Marine loss ratio continuously improving
items.quote: When we look at marine, I would say , loss ratio is continuously improving.

items.statement: Engineering loss ratio volatile, FY25 at 103% vs 130% in FY24
items.quote: Engineering, again, on that basis, as for fire as I said , in engineering when you write a project which takes three or four years to complete, if losses come in between the premium has not come in. So engineering has that peculiar situation , and the loss ratios can be very volatile . And you can actually see in Quarter 4 the loss ratio is only 40.3%, but overall for the year it was 103%, but on

items.statement: Three-year average loss ratio around 70%
items.quote: So on the loss ratio, again, if you look at total, our loss ratio, I would say , on a three-years is around 70%.

items.statement: GWP without 1/n grew 15.6% YoY in FY25 to Rs 10,419 crore
items.quote: If you look at GWP for the entire year, without 1/n, our growth rate would be 15.6%.

items.statement: GWP with 1/n grew 14% YoY in FY25 to Rs 10,282 crore
items.quote: With 1/n growth rate for the year is 14%.

items.statement: Q4 FY25 GWP growth was 13.5% YoY
items.quote: And for the quarter, the growth rate is 13.5%.

items.statement: Industry GWP growth with 1/n was 6% in FY25, Digit grew ~14%
items.quote: For the Financial Year, the overall growth rate for the industry with 1/n is 6%, and in the case of Digit this growth rate is about 14%.

items.statement: Motor TP market share stable at 5.92% in FY25 vs 5.96% in FY24
items.quote: In TP, as I already mentioned, the market share last year for the whole year was 5.96%. This year, the market share is 5.92%.

items.statement: Expect industry growth rate 3-4% higher in FY26 vs FY25
items.quote: I would still expect the growth rate of the industry to be about 3 % to 4% higher compared to last year.

items.statement: Expect TP premium rate increase in FY26, timing uncertain
items.quote: We would also expect some increase in the third-party premium rates. We would not hazard a guess whether this would happen from July or September, but there should be some increase in the third-party rates.

items.statement: Fire premium rates increased from January 2025, real impact from July 2025
items.quote: In fire premium rates have increased especially from January, but from February we have seen the impact. The real impact of this will start coming in more from July onwards.

items.statement: April 2025 group Health renewals saw high competition on April 1, improvement in pricing for smaller policies later in month
items.quote: What I am hearing is that on April 1 when the big renewals were due, we have actually seen, I would say, that we have seen very high competition on April 1. But I think the smaller policies which were due now, say, during the month, not exactly on 1st of April, there I would say we have seen some improvement in the pricing.

items.statement: Motor growth in Jan-Mar 2025 gives indication, April first fortnight okay
items.quote: I think it will give you a bit of an idea as to what's happening on Motor growth. Supratim, since we do not give a guidance, so I do not want to exactly speak as to what we are looking at . But if you look at February and March, it should give you some indication on the Motor. I think our sense in April , in whatever days we have seen, and I would say this is too early to see this as a trend. But

items.statement: Equity allocation increased from 2.9% to 6.4% of AUM in Q4 FY25
items.quote: As of December 31st, if you see the note below, the bottom most line, our equity allocation was only 2.9% , and as of 31st March equity allocation has actually now moved to 6.4%.

items.statement: Target equity allocation up to 10% of assets
items.quote: We have been saying that we have now sufficient solvency margin. And given the market opportunities, we would actually like to increase our equity allocation up to 10% of our assets.

items.statement: AUM grew by Rs 2,850 crore in FY25, similar to Rs 2,750 crore in FY24
items.quote: We have generated close to about Rs. 2,850 crores, which is similar to Rs. 2,750 crores of AUM generated in the previous year.

items.statement: Investment yield 7.2% annualized in Q4 FY25 from fixed income only, no capital gains
items.quote: Our yield in Quarter 4 purely is coming in from fixed income without any capital gains is about 1.8 %, annualized basis you get at 7.2%.

items.statement: Reinsurance accepted grew ~70% YoY in FY25, now ~80% of portfolio
items.quote: The insurance acceptance for, obviously, the year '25 grew by almost 70% year-on-year. If you look at GDP growth, it is 7%, and the reinsurance accepted led to that growth of 14%. So, now the base is very big, so just wanted to check that on such a big base, which is 80% of your total portfolio.

items.statement: Reinsurance treaty capacities increased across almost all lines, especially property, terms slightly better
items.quote: We have been able to increase our capacities in our reinsurance treaties , in general, across almost all kinds of treaty, but especially in property and our terms have also become slightly better.

items.statement: Expect more inward facultative business industry-wide in FY26 due to reinsurance guideline changes
items.quote: our sense is that for the entire industry we should actually see more premium being written in inward fact this year, because dealing with cross -border reinsurers has become more tedious and it is also difficult for the cross -border reinsurers

items.statement: Expense ratio (EOM) reduced 2.9% YoY to 33.4% without 1/n in FY25, 33.9% with 1/n
items.quote: Last year, as per EOM, our expense ratio was 36.3%. This year, on the same basis, that is without 1/n, our expense ratio is reduced to 33.4 %. So there is a reduction of 2.9% on the overall expenses for the whole year. If we do this '24-'25 with 1/n, then this 33.4% will become 33.9%.

items.statement: Commission to GWP reduced in Q4 FY25
items.quote: Overall, there has been a reduction in the overall OPEX expansion. Towards commission to GWP, once the full results get published, you will be able to see that the commission to gross written premium would have reduced in Quarter 4.

items.statement: Expect IRDA to take corrective action on EOM to reduce commissions
items.quote: I would expect IRDA to take some corrective actions on EOM so that they can actually achi eve the objective of lower commissions.

items.statement: IRDA clarified TP obligation quota requires 30-day gap, reducing aggressive TP writing in FY25
items.quote: Where a lot of companies assumed that if you pick up renewals of other companies, it will actually go towards meeting the third-party obligation quota, and this got clarified by IRDA sometime in February that you only will get credit for your quota if there is a gap of 30 days.

items.statement: Reinsurance guidelines changed in FY25 due to collateral requirements
items.quote: Reinsurance guidelines have also undergone changes this year because of the requirement of collateral, etc.

items.statement: TP reserve release proportion normalized to ~25% per quarter in FY25 vs outlier 37% in Q2 FY24
items.quote: This year our reserve release in terms of proportion has been around 25% for all the four quarters. Quarter 4 is 21%, all the other three quarters were 26%, 25%, 28%.

items.statement: ESOP costs allocated to shareholder account, vesting over 4 years
items.quote: Second is , it also includes some cost relating to ESOPs where when you award ESOPs, it has a certain cost . And then, again, that is seen from a long term perspective , because in our case ESOPs also get vested after four years.

items.statement: Brand investment costs allocated to shareholder account, not policyholders
items.quote: One is that we as a company have now decided to spend a bit of money on the brand, and that is in general on the brand. It is not from a perspective of one line of business and things like that. So the idea is that the company wants to invest in the brand and the board felt that we can continue to spend this money without allocating it to the policyholders.

items.statement: Market volatility and tariff/geopolitical situation delayed full equity allocation to 10%
items.quote: Our thought process, why we did not move to 10% was, we felt that the market was very volatile , especially due to this tariff and geopolitical situation. So we felt that if the market drops, comes to another level, we will actually then go for the balance 3 .5% to go totally up to 10%.

items.statement: Fire net loss ratio volatile due to small net premium base (18-19%), one or two large losses can move ratio significantly
items.quote: In fire, last year, our net premium was only about 18%, 19%. So the net is relatively small. The combined ratio, everything will still be very, very good , highly profitable. And if we just see it from a perspective of loss ratios of our reinsurers, we should look at loss ratio on a gross basis, in previous year '23-'24 gross loss ratio in fire was 84% due to various five nat cat events which we h

items.statement: Engineering loss ratios volatile due to project duration mismatch
items.quote: Engineering, again, on that basis, as for fire as I said , in engineering when you write a project which takes three or four years to complete, if losses come in between the premium has not come in. So engineering has that peculiar situation , and the loss ratios can be very volatile .

items.statement: FY26 store openings expected in same ballpark as FY25 (90 stores)
items.quote: In FY '26, I would not give any specific guidance, Vivek, if you can understand that. But we will be in the same ballpark.

items.statement: No specific SSSG guidance given; management remains optimistic based on historical trends
items.quote: I would not give any specific guidance on SSSG, same store sales growth or any numbers specifically. But I can only say that we generally remain optimistic about our same store sales growth into the future as well.

items.statement: Store size fine-tuned smaller in Tier-3 towns to maintain revenue per sq ft viability
items.quote: As we are going deeper and deeper into the country, we are fine tuning our store size to ensure the viability of the stores.

items.statement: Opened 90 new stores in FY25; now present in 458 cities with 12.2 million sq ft trading area
items.quote: Over the year, we accelerated our new store opening plan and we opened 90 new stores. Now we are present in 458 cities in India and we occupy a trading area of 12.2 million square feet.

items.statement: Average bill value ~Rs875; same-store bill count growing ~10% YoY
items.quote: our aver age bill value is , I am being quite specific, around Rs. 875 per bill, and our number of bills is growing Y-o-Y at about 10% on a same store basis

items.statement: Will react on pricing if competitors undercut opening price points; committed to owning entry price in every category
items.quote: When I say that we will own the opening price point, it obviously means that we will be very price competitive, depending on what the other players in the market are doing. So, it obviously means that if somebody is owning the opening price point or has an opening price point which is lower than ours, we will react in terms of pricing.

items.statement: Trained retail manpower availability limited; company owns continuous recruitment and training
items.quote: The availability, as you know, of trained manpower in India is very limited in retail, because it is a very nascent industry. Therefore, for players like us who are rolling out rapidly across the country, you have to own the task of recruiting, training people on a continuous basis.

items.statement: Store payback ~18 months even in Tier-2/3 towns; 70% of 450+ stores already in smaller towns
items.quote: Our typical breakeven in 18 months, and even in the smaller towns it is in the same range. Do recognize that 70% of our stores even today, which is let's say more than 450 stores are in Tier-2 and Tier-3 towns.

items.statement: Quick commerce near cash break-even; potential not yet established as business keeps growing
items.quote: this business is close to a cash break even. W e have not really established the potential , because as I mentioned earlier, the business continues to grow

items.statement: Kumbh Mela gave temporary boost in Allahabad/Varanasi/Lucknow; no adverse impact anywhere; double-digit SSSG sustained post-Kumbh
items.quote: inevitably, there was some positive impact in Allahabad, Varanasi, even Lucknow, etc., all the towns which are in the neighborhood of Allahabad. But it was temporary and , obviously, it's gone now. But they do not see any negative impact in any which way any where in the country

items.statement: Management targets double-digit year-on-year revenue growth for the full year.
items.quote: our focus has always been to try and deliver a double-digit growth year-on-year, which we have continued to sustain for the fourth succeeding quarter, delivering a double-digit growth rate.

items.statement: Capex for Q1 CY25 was INR 82.5 crores; full year capex expected to be slightly above the Q1 run rate.
items.quote: for the quarter, we have just invested INR 82.5 crores, which is almost at half the level when compared to the same period last year.

items.statement: Fifth plant in Shoolagiri to be operational in second half of CY25.
items.quote: our fifth plant in Shoolagiri will be up and running in the second half of this year.

items.statement: Standalone EBITDA margin reached 19.3% in Q1 CY25, the highest ever, up from 18.8% in Q4 CY24.
items.quote: this has resulted in a strong EBITDA, as you can see, 19.3%. And I guess, this is the highest EBITDA that we have registered so far, bringing in an EBITDA of INR 407 crores into the system.

items.statement: Consolidated EBITDA margin was 18.3% in Q1 CY25, down 1% due to KRSV losses.
items.quote: at a consolidated level, Schaeffler India, both the companies put together, our revenue stands at INR 2,174 crores with an EBITDA of 18.3%, which is a dip of 1 % because of the impact of KRSV.

items.statement: Exports grew 20% QoQ and 23.2% YoY in Q1 CY25, driven by Asia Pacific and industrial bearings.
items.quote: Our star performer in the business has been the exports in this quarter, which grew 20% over the preceding quarter. And if one were to compare it with year-on-year quarter also grew at 23.2%.

items.statement: Industrial demand strong in wind energy, construction equipment, and raw material sectors.
items.quote: we saw a pretty strong demand coming in, in the first quarter as well, particularly -- in line with the gearbox manufacturers who cater to the wind equipment manufacturers. We have seen a strong uptick.

items.statement: Export order book viewed cautiously for short term due to geopolitical uncertainty, but performance expected to sustain.
items.quote: as of now, the order book is for the short term, we are very cautiously looking at the developments that are happening around the world, but we expect to sustain this level of performance.

items.statement: E-axle series production started in Q1 CY25; volumes lower than anticipated but expected to improve.
items.quote: we have started our series production and supplies for the e-axles. As you all know, the delay was because the customer was -- they deferred the launch of the product, which finally has happened.

items.statement: Hybrid vehicle components already in series production at Hosur plant for Japanese OEMs.
items.quote: We are definitely strongly engaged with the Japanese customers who patronize the hybrid technology, yes. And we already are in series production of some products and components for the hybrid applications in our plant in Hosur.

items.statement: Customer survey score improved to 8.62 from 8.41 in previous survey.
items.quote: our rating has improved to 8.62 from the previous survey, which was at 8.41 and that too adds credibility to the efforts that we are making towards our customers.

items.statement: Free cash flow improved to INR 237 crores in Q1 CY25 from INR 163 crores in Q4 CY24 due to working capital management and capex optimization.
items.quote: our free cash flow also registered a strong numbers at INR 237 crores compared to the preceding quarter, which was INR 163 crores.

items.statement: Working capital as percentage of sales improved marginally but remains above Q1 CY24 levels; target is to reduce to last year's level.
items.quote: However, we still are some way on the numbers that we have delivered. If you look at the Q1 of last year, our working capital was at much lower, and we have now kind of gone up there, and we still have to bring in a lot more focus here.

items.statement: Localization ratio increased to 76% of revenue from own production in India across four plants.
items.quote: our localization ratio has gone up to 76% now. So, whatever we are selling, 76% is manufactured in our 4 plants in India.

items.statement: Focus shifting to capacity utilization of existing assets after aggressive capex of INR 1,700-1,800 crores over last three years.
items.quote: in last 3 years, we have invested aggressively close to INR 1,700 crores - 1,800 crores. And it is time that we focus on capital efficiency.

items.statement: Auto bearing share within Bearings & Industrial Solutions segment is approximately 17%.
items.quote: if we talk about the segmental mix on bearings, within that, auto bearing is close to 17%.

items.statement: Group task force monitoring geopolitical impacts on raw materials and trade; no major concern seen currently.
items.quote: At the group level, we have a task force who is closely monitoring different impacts, which can have on Schaeffler worl dwide, whether it is about raw material, whether it is about our own finished product import export

items.statement: No impact seen in India from European restructuring or Vitesco merger synergies so far.
items.quote: in India, so far, we have not seen any impact due to what is happening in Europe coming in India.

items.statement: Vitesco India remains a separate legal entity; arm's-length transactions maintained, but combined customer-facing approach leveraged.
items.quote: Vitesco in India still remains a different company altogether, although it is under the Schaeffler umbrella as such within the country. Now that said, are we leveraging when we go to in front of the customer? Of course, we are leveraging.

items.statement: Gross margin improvement of INR 115 crores drove EBITDA growth, attributed to higher sales and favorable vertical mix.
items.quote: clearly, the maximum contribution of INR115 crores out of the INR407 crores did come in, obviously, at the gross margin improvement, which is attributed to higher sales and the mix of the verticals.

items.statement: Export growth driven by Asia Pacific (Southeast Asia, Japan, Korea) and EU; US exposure remains insignificant.
items.quote: the export business increase is mainly attributed to Asia Pacific. As we have said in past few calls that, we are finding new geographies and within Asia Pacific, Southeast Asia, Japan, Korea, we are focusing on those markets as well now.

items.statement: No job cuts or restructuring in India despite European group actions; focus on operational efficiency continues.
items.quote: in India, so far, we have not seen any impact due to what is happening in Europe coming in India. As you can see, our numbers are proving it that we continue to deliver the double-digit growth.

items.statement: KRSV Innovative Auto Solutions revenue INR 64.6 crores in Q1 CY25; EBITDA still negative but order inflows and customer stickiness improving.
items.quote: KRSV Innovative Auto Solutions Private Limited too in the first quarter has delivered a strong performance by bringing in a revenue of INR 64.6 crores in the quarter, which is clearly an improvement over the preceding quarter. And the EBITDA definitely still is in the negative region.

items.statement: Vehicle Lifetime Solutions (aftermarket) revenue dipped QoQ due to seasonality; steering kit sales reached INR 1-1.5 crores in Q1.
items.quote: we have started to regi ster a sale of almost INR 1 - 1.5 crores registered in the first quarter itself

items.statement: Relocating used machinery from underutilized European plants to India to optimize capex for localization.
items.quote: we have PUBLIC the option in front of us to look at brand-new machines or look at machines that can be utilized from the older plants lying there. Obviously, they would come as a lower investment for us

items.statement: Housing Finance AUM expected to grow at 20% in FY25, achieved
items.quote: And we had already guided that our AUM is expected to grow at 20% in FY25, and that's what we have achieved in FY25.

items.statement: AMC market share in net sales expected to continue improving in FY26
items.quote: We are confident that with the current run rate of flows that we've seen in the months of February, March and the early trends in the month of April, our AUM market share could continue to rise in FY26 over the exiting FY25 numbers.

items.statement: Private Equity Fund V targeting to raise at least $900 million
items.quote: We have recently received the SEBI approval to launch our fifth private equity fund, wherein we are targeting to raise at least $900 million, which is 2x the size of our Fund IV.

items.statement: Wealth Management net flows grew 3x to Rs 10,279 crores in FY25
items.quote: This is reflected in our FY25 growth wherein our net flows grew 3x to over Rs. 10,279 crores in FY25 on a YoY basis.

items.statement: AMC gross flows grew 290% YoY to Rs 68,007 crores in FY25
items.quote: Coupled with expansion in our distribution presence, our gross flows grew by 290% YoY in FY25 to Rs. 68,007 crores.

items.statement: AMC net flows grew 10x to Rs 48,450 crores in FY25
items.quote: In terms of net flows of the asset management business, it grew multi-fold from Rs. 5,191 crores FY24 to Rs. 48,450 crores, increased by 10x in FY25.

items.statement: Housing Finance disbursements grew 78% to Rs 1,794 crores in FY25
items.quote: Our disbursements grew by 78% to Rs. 1,794 crores.

items.statement: Private Wealth relationships grew 25% in FY25 over FY24
items.quote: We've grown the total relationships by 25% in FY25 over FY24.

items.statement: Net interest income spread improved from 5.9% to 6.5% in FY25
items.quote: Net interest income, which grew by 37% YoY due to higher lending book, as well as improvement in spreads from 5.9% in FY24 to 6.5% in FY25.

items.statement: Incremental cost of funds 50 bps lower than overall cost, spreads improving
items.quote: Our incremental cost of funds is now 50 b ps lower than the overall cost currently. We are already seeing the positive impact of favourable rate cycle coming to us on both of the lending business

items.statement: Wealth Management distribution book grew 33% to Rs 31,551 crores
items.quote: Consequently, the book grew from Rs. 23,715 crores as of Mar '24 to over Rs. 31,551 crores in Mar'25, up by 33% YoY.

items.statement: Alternates AUM grew 23% to Rs 28,285 crores
items.quote: Our alternates AUM grew by 23% to Rs. 28,285 crores as of Mar'25.

items.statement: Housing Finance AUM grew 20% to Rs 4,878 crores
items.quote: This resulted in the business achieving an AUM of Rs. 4,878 crores, which is up by 20%.

items.statement: Lending book (MTF + LAS) at Rs 7,257 crores, MTF at Rs 5,000 crores
items.quote: The book size total on the lending, on both MTF and loan against securities is Rs. 7,257 crores, o f which, MTF is around Rs. 5,000 crores and rest is loan against securities

items.statement: Technology spend at 4.5-5% of net revenues, up 100 bps YoY
items.quote: In terms of our tech spends also, we spend almost about 4.5% to 5% of our net revenues on technology, and this number is growing. Over last year, this number is up almost 100

items.statement: Wealth Management RM strength increased, Housing Finance Sales RM up 40% to 1,329
items.quote: Our Sales RM force increased to 1,329, up by nearly 40% YoY.

items.statement: Private Wealth RM strength at 595, only 33% with 3+ years vintage
items.quote: Our current RM strength is 595, and we expect improvement in RM productivity as only 33% of this RM base has a vintage of over 3-plus years.

items.statement: Distribution yields at 110 bps on ARR assets, transaction yields higher on flows
items.quote: In distribution, our overall yields are 110 basis points for the year on ARR assets. If you're looking at the transaction revenues, the yield is to be looked at on the flows.

items.statement: Fee-based revenue contribution increased from 31% to 37% of total revenues
items.quote: Our fee-based revenue contribution to our total revenues increased from 31% same time last year to 37% now.

items.statement: Annual recurring revenue at 56% of total net revenue
items.quote: Our annual recurring revenue as a percentage of total net revenue grew to 56% at the end of FY25.

items.statement: Servicing 12+ million customers: 7.8M mutual fund folios, 4.8M broking accounts
items.quote: We've crossed a major milestone by servicing more than 12 million customers, comprising of 7.8 million unique mutual fund folios and over 4.8 million unique broking accounts.

items.statement: Investment Banking ranked #1 in QIP league tables, #3 in IPOs filed
items.quote: We successfully completed 39 deals, with a cumulative issuance of Rs. 51,000 crores last year. We were ranked #1 in QIP league tables and ranked #3 in terms of the total number of IPOs filed last year.

items.statement: New F&O regulations implemented, expected to strengthen competitive position
items.quote: We also saw implementation of new F&O regulations, which we believe will only strengthen the competitive position of Motilal Oswal as a full-service broker in the marketplace.

items.statement: Housing Finance GNPA 0.8%, NNPA 0.4% as of Mar'25
items.quote: Our GNPAs and NNPAs are at 0.8% and 0.4% respectively as of Mar'25.

items.statement: Gearing (ex-Home Finance) at 1x
items.quote: Our gearing (ex of Motilal Home Finance) stands at 1x.

items.statement: Leadership strengthening across businesses and support functions, new Group Head AI hired
items.quote: We also have created few new positions in the technology as part of Pankaj's team. We have Group Head AI who has joined from a global firm. We also have a technology research team created separately for the first time

items.statement: No formal FY26 revenue or EBITDA guidance given; management will provide outlook once tariff uncertainty settles in a quarter or two
items.quote: We believe it is a question of a quarter or 2 at the most. And that is the one reason why we do not know how the conversion of orders into revenue will happen.

items.statement: Q4 FY25 deal closures (TCV) reached $280 million, up sequentially from $236 million in Q3
items.quote: We had during this quarter total closures of $280 million.

items.statement: Deal closures have risen each quarter in FY25: Q1 $202M, Q2 $207M, Q3 $236M, Q4 $280M
items.quote: If you recollect, in the first quarter, we had a deal closure of USD 202 million. The second quarter, it went to 207. The third quarter, it went to 236. And the fourth quarter, it went to 280.

items.statement: FY25 EBITDA margin 21%, meeting the raised guidance of 21% (previously 20.5%)
items.quote: We had also given some EBITDA guidance in the first place, which was 20.5%, which we later on increase d to 21%, and we have kind of met

items.statement: Management aims to maintain FY26 margins while investing in AI, platforms and automation; no specific margin number given
items.quote: We believe that many of these things will help us not only that we want to continue having the margins, same margins, but we would like to invest in terms of many areas for future and really making a transition to the new models, business models.

items.statement: European OEMs are consolidating vendors and accelerating SDV programs; KPIT sees strong pipeline and pole position in Europe
items.quote: Many European OEMs are absolutely looking at how they can very quickly catch up. Naturally, we are in a specific situation where specifically in SDV or some of these areas, we are very well entrenched.

items.statement: US growth expected across passenger cars, trucks and off-highway; new passenger car OEM engagement started
items.quote: We've started an engagement with the new OEM in U.S., which is a good thing for us. And we believe that we'll grow, we'll have substantial growth from that particular pass car OEM in the US.

items.statement: Asia growth to be broad-based: India and Japan positive, Korea flattish, China small but improving
items.quote: India will be a growth market. We see a reasonable growth in India. , China has been a small part. So we will see at least something positive there than what it was last year. Japan will be also positive. And Korea is probably flattish as of now.

items.statement: Three growth offerings: cost reduction, cybersecurity, end-to-end validation; building automotive-specific AI agents and platform tools
items.quote: We believe our 3 major offerings, namely the cost reduction, cybersecurity, and end-to-end validation will be of relevance in the current period.

items.statement: Vertical adjacency expansion: started work with 4 of 8 new clients (2 truck OEMs, 1 off-highway, 1 passenger car)
items.quote: Out of those 8, we have started working already on 4. And out of them, 2 are commercial vehicles and 1 is off highway. And the last one is, of course, passenger cars.

items.statement: Mercedes-Benz SDV deal is multi-year (3-4 years), similar scope to Honda/Renault deals, not included in Q4 $280M TCV
items.quote: It's a multiyear deal, which we are looking at 3 to 4 years deal. this engagement is there. And naturally, it's like being a strategic partner for them in these areas.

items.statement: No significant ramp-downs or cancellations post April 2 tariff announcement; only small project closures
items.quote: We have seen certain projects which we are expecting not coming up and some small way where the projects got closed, we did not continue with some of these. So that has happened, but nothing on a significant scale.

items.statement: Investing meaningfully in AI transformation: hiring team, building automotive-specific AI agents, platform tools and accelerators
items.quote: We are also making a meaningful investment into AI transformation. It is in terms of hiring the team, then we are also building solutions as I said, AI is not just AI because that any company can come up with.

items.statement: Building China organization: hiring local talent, establishing partnerships, moving Chinese-speaking staff to engage global OEMs
items.quote: We are in that process where we have hired people from the technology side who can bring our learning from China to here. We are building a local stronger presence which can meaningfully engage with China in China.

items.statement: Acquisition discussions in advanced stages for strategic adjacency (vertical or offering); not for pure growth; financing undecided
items.quote: we are looking at certain acquisitions also in advanced stages of discussion, but till it doesn't happen, it doesn't happen. So those opportunities are there. The idea is not really for a growth, as we always say. It is about more a strategic intention

items.statement: Proposed final dividend INR 6 per share; if approved, total FY25 dividend INR 8.5 per share, up 27% YoY
items.quote: We are proposing a dividend for the AGM at INR6 per share. And if that gets approved, then the final dividend will be INR8.5 per share, which would be a 27% growth over the last year.

items.statement: QORIX JV contributed INR 14 crore profit in Q4 (also N-Dream profit); quarterly volatility expected, medium-term positive outlook
items.quote: Yes. Absolutely, it is from QORIX. And actually, it is from both. I think we also had a profit in N-Dream also. So it is a profit from both.

items.statement: Tariff and trade agreement uncertainty may delay order-to-revenue conversion for 1-2 quarters; clients cautious on scaling
items.quote: many of these larger deals, which we have got, many of them are already in the transition phase. Many of them have started scaling up, but slowly than what we would have lik ed from the client perspective

items.statement: Discretionary R&D and proof-of-concept programs being deferred by OEMs; urgent production programs remain on track
items.quote: Some of these further in the timeline activities start falling into discretionary activities and they start getting tuned. They're not necessarily cancelled, but they start getting tuned in terms of deferment, what to do now, what to do later, 2 quarters later, etcetera.

items.statement: Some clients giving rate increases; others demanding cost-effective solutions; KPIT shifting to productivity-based fixed-price models with offshoring and PTAs
items.quote: In some customers, we have got the increment that is increased rates in some customers. And of course, there are clients which are coming back for a better cost-effective solution.

items.statement: Offshoring continues: large programs move 6-8 months from onsite to offshore; model based on productivity, PTAs and offshoring
items.quote: If we take a very large program, initially, still you will have to deliver at least have some people on site, but in 6 to 8 months, we can move them offshore.

items.statement: Expect trade agreements to settle in 3-4 months; daily improvement in environment
items.quote: All our discussions with the clients tell us that the governments and the industry that the trade agreements will get settled in the next 3 to 4 months. And every day, you see a better environment.

items.statement: China strategy has four avenues: take China learnings to global OEMs, help global OEMs stay relevant in China, take Chinese OEM offerings global, serve Chinese OEMs in China with tools/PTAs
items.quote: We see 4 buckets of opportunities for us. And we have been doing extensive work in China now really understanding the market very well. And therefore, we have come to a conclusion that we can possibly look at 4 ways in which we can use China for our growth.

items.statement: FY25 ended with healthy cash conversion; cash on hand INR 15.8 billion
items.quote: We ended the year with a healthy cash conversion with a cash on hand of INR 15.8 billion.

items.statement: Q1 FY26 growth expected to be positive QoQ; no negative growth anticipated
items.quote: We don't talk about quarter-to-quarter growth, but it would be positive.

items.statement: Management expects adjusted EBITDA margin to be between 24-25% in FY26 due to railway business dilution, down from 27% in FY25.
items.quote: So end of next quarter we will give you a range, but if you just do the ma th that you take 27% is what we did 27 %x80 and do 18 x20, you will come to somewhere closer to between 24 to 25.

items.statement: Net order book reached a record high of Rs 24,200 crore ($2.8 billion) at end of FY25, with 77% EV contribution.
items.quote: Which brings me neatly to a net order book which at the end of FY25 stands at 24.2 thousand crore rupees or $2.8 billion. The EV contribution to this order book remains high. It's at 77%.

items.statement: Added Rs 47 billion of new orders from 37 programs and 7 new customers in FY25; net addition Rs 16 billion after consuming Rs 31 billion.
items.quote: Our next KRA, business development, we added 47 billion rupees worth of new orders during the year. This came from 37 new programs, which were won and 7 new customers , which were added.

items.statement: BEV revenue grew 38% to Rs 1,224 crore in FY25, reaching 36% revenue share; Q4 BEV revenue grew 8% to Rs 294 crore (34% share).
items.quote: Our BEV revenue for the full year grew by 38% to ₹1,224 crore and BEV share of revenue increased to 36%.

items.statement: FY25 adjusted EBITDA margin declined 60 bps to 28.2% due to adverse product mix, offsetting benefits from lower input prices and operating leverage.
items.quote: Our adjusted EBITDA margin was 28.2%, which is 60 basis points lower than the last year. While we had positive impact on the margin from the lower input prices and operating leverage, this was more than offset by a change in the product mix.

items.statement: Deployed Rs 415 crore in capex in FY25; high capitalization of ~Rs 400 crore led to fixed asset turnover decline to 3.4x.
items.quote: We've deployed about Rs. 415 crores in Capex that has left us with Rs. 360 crores of free cash flows.

items.statement: Mexico plant phase one investment below $10 million; first customers are Mexico-based companies producing heavy trucks and off-highway vehicles.
items.quote: At this moment, we are looking to invest a number which is below $10 million. That's the first stage.

items.statement: 31 EV programs in production at end of FY25 (15 mature, 16 ramping); 27 programs not yet in production, starting in FY26 or later.
items.quote: At the end of FY25, we have 31 EV programs in production, of which 15 are mature and completely ramped up, while 16 are in the ramp- up phase. The remaining 27 programs are not yet in production and will start during this or the following years.

items.statement: ICE-dependent revenue share shrank to 9% in FY25; commercial vehicle share declined from 14% to 11%; auto to non-auto 90:10 (pro forma 70:30 with railway).
items.quote: The trend of increasing electrification and decreasing ICE dependence continues unabated. And this year, we've seen the ICE-dependent revenue share shrink to only 9% of our revenue.

items.statement: Received large EV order from North American OEM in last week of March (after US tariff announcement) for rotor-embedded differential sub-assembly and epicyclic gear train; supplies start Q4 FY26.
items.quote: We got a new EV order from an existing customer, like I mentioned. It's a North American OEM of EVs. We will supply the rotor-embedded differential sub-assembly as well as the epicyclic gear train for an upcoming electric SUV.

items.statement: US auto tariffs (25%) expected to adversely impact demand; 3% of total revenue at medium risk of revenue loss in next 12-18 months; USMCA exemptions apply.
items.quote: Net net we have 40% of our total revenue to US, in which we have identified 3% where there could be some risk of either revenue loss where they could look to somebody local, which somebody can come at a better price than us.

items.statement: China rare earth magnet export restrictions being managed via inventory, export license applications, alternate materials (ferrite, different grades), and non-China suppliers; no production impact yet.
items.quote: We have inventory right now, so nothing yet. We are working with our suppliers to do get them the export licenses. Sat you can give more details on other efforts also we are trying to make.

items.statement: Working capital turnover improved to 5x in FY25; net debt/EBITDA remains negative; cash and investments Rs 2,673 crore at year-end.
items.quote: Working capital turnover ratio has further improved to 5 times. On the other hand, fixed asset turnover ratio has declined to 3.4 times because we had a very high capitalization this year of around 40 0 crores.

items.statement: Reduced borrowings by Rs 220 crore in FY25; net debt/EBITDA negative; cash balance Rs 2,673 crore including QIP proceeds of Rs 2,370 crore (net).
items.quote: There was a reduction in the borrowings by 220 crores, and we invested about 60 crores in NOVELIC and Clear Motion Inc. At the end of the year, we had cash and investments balance of about 2,673 crores.

items.statement: Raised Rs 2,370 crore (net) via QIP in September 2024; part to fund railway business acquisition from EKL.
items.quote: We also raised QIP funds in September of 2024, so net off expenses, that amount is 2,370 crores. Besides this, the bigger items were dividend distribution of 190 crores, which is a cash outflow.

items.statement: Invested Rs 60 crore in NOVELIC and Clear Motion Inc. in FY25; railway business acquisition from EKL pending, to be funded from cash.
items.quote: There was a reduction in the borrowings by 220 crores, and we invested about 60 crores in NOVELIC and Clear Motion Inc. At the end of the year, we had cash and investments balance of about 2,673 crores. Part of these funds, as you may know, would be used for the acquisition of railway business from EKL.

items.statement: Distributed Rs 190 crore as dividend in FY25.
items.quote: Besides this, the bigger items were dividend distribution of 190 crores, which is a cash outflow.

items.statement: Vivek Vikram Singh completed 10 years as MD & Group CEO; company grew 10x revenue and 20x profit in his tenure.
items.quote: When I joined Sona BLW , standalone revenue for FY15 and its net profit were around 346 crores and 29 crores, respectively. So , in my first decade here, we've seen the company grow 10 times in revenue and over 20 times in profit.

items.statement: Tariffs will increase end consumer prices, reduce volumes due to inelastic demand; demand impact unmodelable until tariffs kick in; supply chain disruptions possible.
items.quote: Eventually, the consumer, the end consumer pays for it in the form of higher end product prices is what eventually happens. And again, there is no such thing as like 5% you take 5% I take.

items.statement: Rare earth supply dependency is a geo-strategic risk; accelerating magnetless and rare-earth-free motor development; customer approval needed for heavier ferrite-based motors.
items.quote: If any material's supply can be used as a geo-strategic negotiating tool, we must find ways to counter that threat in the future. So it's a good wake up call that anything from anyone that you depend on totally, you should not.

items.statement: Entering humanoid robot components market (actuators, motors, reducers >50% of BoM); at technology readiness level but commercial success binary; no orders yet.
items.quote: We are at a certain technology readiness level, but success, as you know, in these things is binary. When we get an order, we will make that white circle blue , and we will tell you what we have won, but till you win, it means nothing.

items.statement: Commercialized steering bevel box for commercial vehicle steering systems (global OEM); supplies start FY26; leverages forging and precision machining strengths.
items.quote: We also commercialized a new product, which was in white in our tech road map, it has come into blue now, the steering bevel box which has applications in commercial vehicle steering systems.

items.statement: Clear Motion suspension motor launched on Nio ET9 in Q4 FY25; good reviews; discussing other vehicle applications with customer.
items.quote: CMI launch or the Nio launch happened, in the last quarter. The vehicle which is ET9 is doing pretty good. We are getting a good reviews from our customers as well as from CMI.

items.statement: Seeing renewed starter motor RFQs from US customers due to ICE refocus; won large starter motor orders last quarter; second-order effect of tariffs.
items.quote: Strangely, yes, so that's been one of the I'd say weird second order impact of all of this which is going on, that we are now suddenly getting starter motor RFQs which had kind of dried up, pretty much completely.

items.statement: Chinese competitors face higher tariffs, widening Sona's relative pricing advantage; 2018 tariff cycle gave market share gains in US; current cycle larger.
items.quote: Our competitors in both our major product categories tend to be from China. And in an event in which tariffs are imposed on every Sona Comstar – Q4 FY25 Earnings Call country, it is basically then your relative pricing that comes into place. And then the gap has actually widened much more

items.statement: Will wait for tariff clarity before committing to new US assembly plant (12-18 months lead time); have existing US and Mexico plants; zero customer requests for localization.
items.quote: We will wait for the dust to settle before we make any committed investments anywhere, but as you well know, we have a plant in Mexico. We have a plant in the US. We are actually in the process of another plant in Mexico.

items.statement: PLI income for full FY25 recognized in Q4 (Rs 19 crore for first 3 quarters net of expenses); will accrue quarterly from FY26; 8 motors certified.
items.quote: So if, let's say if we have to take out the first 3 quarters impact, that would be about 19 crores.

items.statement: ROCE and ROE ~18% in FY25, lower due to QIP capital raise; revenue/EBITDA/PAT grew 12%/8%/16% YoY.
items.quote: ROCE and ROE were around 18%, which is obviously lower than last year, but this is due to the capital raise or QIP that we did in September-24.

items.statement: Industrial demand strong in wind energy, construction equipment, raw material and power transmission sectors.

items.statement: Group task force monitoring geopolitical/tariff impacts on raw materials and finished goods; no major concern seen currently.

items.statement: No expectation of excess Chinese capacity flowing into India; Schaeffler China serves large local market.

items.statement: Average daily turnover Q4 FY25: Rs. 1,92,871 crores (cash Rs. 2,535 crores, derivatives Rs. 1,90,336 crores); down ~36% YoY from ~Rs. 3 lakh crores due to derivative expiry norm tightening.
