And this was almost Rs. 3 lakh crores in the Q4 of FY '24. And as I explained earlier, this was because of the tightening of derivative norms, particularly related to expiry of indices.

items.statement: NIM guidance for FY26 between 3.75% and 4.00%, likely close to 4%
items.quote: Our NIM for this quarter is 3.75%, and for the full next year, the guidance will be somewhere in between 3.75% and 4.00% and probably somewhere close to 4% is what will be there.

items.statement: Credit cost guidance for FY26 kept below 30 basis points
items.quote: We are keeping our credit cost guidance below 30 basis points for next year. We sh ould be able to comfortably achieve this - is our

items.statement: ROA guidance 1.5% to 1.8%, ROE guidance 15% to 17% for medium term
items.quote: On return on assets, our guidance is between 1.5% to 1.8% and return on equity between 15% to 17%.

items.statement: Asset growth anticipated between 20% to 25% for FY26, constrained by liability growth
items.quote: Overall, I think anything between 20% to 25% growth is anticipated as of now. But of course, we have to see.

items.statement: NIM bottomed out at 3.75% in Q4 FY25; FY25 full year NIM at 4.13%
items.quote: I think from a NIM perspective, we have definitely hit the bottom. We will not go below where we are right now. But on a year-on-year, the NIM is 4.13% and we need to see. Our NIM for this quarter is 3.75

items.statement: NIM compression driven by excess liquidity, higher FCY hedging costs, business mix shift, and interest reversals from slippages
items.quote: The fourth point is the higher cost of funds which went up prima rily because of liquidity issue s. Some of the FD costs were slightly high and also as I just mentioned a bout FCY borrowing cost and the hedging cost

items.statement: Net advances grew 29% YoY; gold portfolio up 35%, retail ex-gold up 24%, SME up 33%, wholesale up 22%, corporate loans up 44%
items.quote: On the asset growth, net advance grew by 29% Y-o-Y- which is higher than 2x times over industry growth of 12%. All the verticals have started contributing towards the asset growth, and this is the highlight of this quarter and hopefully going ahead.

items.statement: Long-term portfolio mix target by FY30: wholesale 30%, SME 20%, retail 30%, gold 20%
items.quote: our long-t erm philosophical thinking is wholesale will be 30%, SME will be 20%, retail will be 30% and gold will be 20%. That's our FY 2030 journey

items.statement: GNPA 1.57%, NNPA 0.52%, PCR 83.71% with PWO, 67.19% without PWO; provisioning buffer INR 185 cr above regulatory requirement
items.quote: Asset quality ratios are stable. GNPA and NNPA ratios for the quarter was 1.57% and 0.52% as against 1.58% and 0.64% respectively with a mild improvement on a Q-on-Q basis. PCR now stands at 83.71% with PWO and 67.19% without PWO.

items.statement: Slippages at 1.19% in Q4 FY25; driven by migration provisions, unsecured book slippages, and prudent provisions for security deterioration
items.quote: Overall slippages were around 1.19% in Q4. But if you look at it previously, our slippages in March quarter last year were 2.16%. June quarter was 1.64%. September was 0.93%, December 0.85%. Despite what we have done, it has come to 1.19% in this quarter.

items.statement: Retail unsecured book below 3.5% of total book; expected to become negligible in 2 quarters
items.quote: The retail unsecured book share is less than 3.5% for us right now. We also took some prudent provisions over and above the internal accelerated /RBI policy prescription s since our overall business has been reasonably good

items.statement: Major tech transformation underway: migrating CBS to Oracle, implementing OGL, OFSAA, OBDX, new CMS, LOS, supply chain platforms; datacentre migration done; go-live expected in May
items.quote: We are migrating our CBS to Oracle system along with the implementation of various surr ound systems. Everything in the bank is changing as it comes to the tech stack, and this will help us in targeting new segments, new businesses, transaction banking, wholesale banking, retail assets scale up etc

items.statement: IT capex and opex rising due to tech migration; opex up 17% QoQ, other opex up 35% YoY; staff costs to rise from H2 FY26
items.quote: Other opex has gone up by around 35% primarily because of some of these technology-related expenses, there's a capex and opex there. For example, to give you a data, on IT capex, we hav e not fully utilized last year

items.statement: Branch network expanded to 829 branches, 791 ATMs; added 56 branches, merged 6 in FY25; similar pace in FY26, significant expansion from FY27
items.quote: We expanded our distribution network to 829 branches and 791 ATMs as of March end. We have added 56 new branches during the FY and merged 6 branches as a part of branch rationalization.

items.statement: CD ratio at 86%, average LCR 124%, NSFR 121%; surplus liquidity managed via deposits, CDs, FCY borrowings, SIDBI refinance
items.quote: CD ratio stood at 86%. Average LCR for the quarter is 124% and NSFR ratio was at 121%.

items.statement: Borrowings 13% of funding mix, 8-9% FCY borrowings; hedging costs spiked due to global uncertainty but now normalizing
items.quote: We have a funding mix comprising of 13% of borrowings. Out of that, almost 8 to 9 % is FCY borrowing. Because of the global uncertainty, tariff war and all of that happened, the hedging costs went up.

items.statement: Branch distribution shifting: Kerala share down from 52% to 33-34%; new branches in North, West, South for granular liability franchise and cross-sell
items.quote: If you look at our branch distribution, currently, we have around 33-34% in Kerala. It was 52%, I think few years back. What it means is that more and more branches we are building fo r the future

items.statement: Gold loan draft circular impact uncertain; operational and system changes needed; no major business impact expected; compliance to be built into new core system
items.quote: Actually, it's too early to comment, because it has not been fo rmally circularised. It is a draft discussion paper and various representations are going on through IBA and other similar bodies

items.statement: Key risks: tech migration execution (biggest risk and opportunity), residual global/tariff uncertainty; unsecured book and liquidity risks largely mitigated
items.quote: If you ask me, the biggest risk for us is this migration and the entire tran sformation and biggest opportunity is also that and we are waiting for that. Otherwise, I don't see any major risks

items.statement: Senior management team fully in place, no attrition at CXO/regional/product heads; wholesale, SME, transaction banking teams built; entry-level attrition normal
items.quote: On the management, we have no major gaps as of now. Every senior position starting from CXO level to CXO plus 1 to regional head to distribution head to product heads is in place.

items.statement: CASA grew 10% YoY, CASA ratio 24.19%; deposit growth 24% YoY vs industry ~10%
items.quote: On the liability side, we had a robust deposit growth of 24% year -on-year; amid a slow-paced industry growth of around 10%. CASA grew by 10% Y-o-Y and CASA ratio sta nds now at 24.19

items.statement: CRAR 22.46%, Tier 1 20.59%; book value per share INR 249, EPS INR 34.23, ROE 15.44% for FY25
items.quote: On the capital adequacy front, our CRAR ratio was 22.46% with a Tier 1 ratio of 20.59%. We have a low proportion of risk-weighted assets compared to the industry.

items.statement: SBS 2030 vision: build phase ending, scale journey starts FY27; FY27-30 execution and scaling
items.quote: In short, our SBS journey, which we started in FY 22, is in the last phase of build journey, and our scale journey will start from FY '27. From FY '27 to '30, it is mostly execution and scaling.

items.statement: Management expects overall book yield to dilute by 1-2 bps due to higher ETF/index fund inflows
items.quote: Going forward, we expect maybe a dilution of max to max 1 or 2 basis points in yield, mainly because of the higher proportion of ETF AUM that we have.

items.statement: Book tax rate expected at 23-24% from FY26 onwards
items.quote: Yes, on a book rate, we see in the range of around 23% to 24%.

items.statement: Other expenses expected to grow 7-8% over FY25 base
items.quote: No, I think, 7% to 8% inflation increase on these numbers, you can assume.

items.statement: Capex expected to decrease in FY26 as branch expansion slows; some capex for pension fund POP business
items.quote: Yes, the Capex amount should go down. I don't think we will be opening such high number of offices in FY '26. But on the Pension Fund, since we are expanding POP business, there might be some Capex cost on the pension fund business.

items.statement: UTI Group total AUM at ₹21.05 lakh crore as of March 31, 2025, up 14% YoY
items.quote: The UTI Group's total assets under management stood at ₹ 21.05 lakh crore as of March 31, 2025, reflecting a growth of 14% compared to ₹ 18.48 lakh crores at the end of the previous year.

items.statement: Mutual fund quarterly average AUM at ₹3.4 lakh crore in Q4 FY25, up 16.8% YoY
items.quote: The quarterly average AUM as of March '25 was ₹ 3.4 lakh crores, a 16.8% growth year -on-year.

items.statement: Equity and hybrid net sales turned positive ₹1,178 crore in FY25 from negative ₹4,230 crore in FY24
items.quote: We have moved from a negative of ₹ 4,230 crores of net sales for the last financial year to a positive net sales of ₹ 1,178 crores during this financial year.

items.statement: ETF and Index fund net inflow ₹19,605 crore in Q4 FY25; quarterly average AUM ₹1,41,492 crore, up 23% YoY
items.quote: Our quarterly average AUM for the index and ETF funds stood at ₹ 1,41,492 crores, up by 23% in the 4th Quarter. ETFs and Index fund net inflow stood at ₹ 19,605 crores.

items.statement: UTI Pension Fund AUM ₹3.59 lakh crore, up 19% YoY; manages 24.86% of NPS industry AUM; PAT ₹57 crore, up 5% YoY
items.quote: UTI PFL has recorded a growth of 19% year -on-year in its AUM, reaching approximately ₹ 3.59 lakh crores as of March '25 and currently manages 24.86% of the NPS Industries' AUM. The profit after tax of UTI PFL for FY '25 is at ₹ 57 crores, an increase of 5% year -on-year.

items.statement: UTI International AUM ₹25,383 crore; IDEF fund $805M, J Safra Sarasin Responsible India $65.4M, UTI India Innovation Fund $47M
items.quote: UTI International, which represents our international business has an AUM of ₹ 25,383 crores as of March '25. One of our flagship funds, India Dynamic Equity Fund (IDEF) domiciled in Ireland has an AUM of $805 million.

items.statement: Consolidated core revenue ₹1,445 crore, up 22% YoY; core PAT ₹492 crore, up 43% YoY; overall net profit ₹731 crore, down 5% YoY
items.value: ₹1,445 crore revenue; ₹492 crore core PAT; ₹731 crore net profit
items.quote: On a consolidated basis, for the full Financial Year ‘2 4-'25, core revenue from operations was ₹ 1,445 crores, up by 22% year-on-year. The core profit after tax for FY '24-'25 was ₹ 492 crores, up by 43% year-on-year and overall consolidated net profit was ₹ 731 crores, down by 5% year - on-year

items.statement: Standalone core revenue ₹1,180 crore, up 24% YoY; core PAT ₹447 crore, up 52% YoY; net profit ₹653 crore, up 9% YoY
items.value: ₹1,180 crore revenue; ₹447 crore core PAT; ₹653 crore net profit
items.quote: On a stand-alone basis, for the full year FY '24-'25, the core revenue from operations was ₹ 1,180 crores, up by 24% year -on-year. The core profit after tax for FY '24 -'25 was ₹ 447 crores, up by 52% year -on-year. The overall net profit was ₹ 653 crores, up by 9% year -on-year.

items.statement: Book yields: equity/hybrid ~75 bps, equity/index ~5-6 bps, cash ~9-10 bps, income ~22-23 bps; weighted average ~34 bps
items.quote: So as far as the book yield is concerned, equity and hybrid fund, our book yield is close to around 75 basis points. Equity and Index fund is around 5 to 6 basis points. Cash around 9 to 10, and income fund for around 22 to 23 basis points. So the weighted average yield is around 34 basis points.

items.statement: Commission rationalization on older AUM implemented in Q4 FY25; will cushion equity yield dilution going forward
items.quote: We have also rationalized some of the distributor commissions, older AUM, which had been impacting our margin over the last 4 to 5 years and market has corrected. So that rationalization we have already carried out. We believe that rationalization will cushion some of the decline in the yield that may happen because of fresh inflows under equity and hybrid fund.

items.statement: Capex of ~₹50 crore in FY25 mainly for 91 new branches opened over 15 months and IT infrastructure upgrades
items.quote: Major part of these Capex relates to those offices. Plus , in FY24 we have upgraded our IT infrastructure. There are some Capex costs relating to IT infrastructure as well.

items.statement: Opened 68 new branches in Tier-2/3 cities in FY25 with net zero cost addition; total branches increased from 164 to 255
items.quote: We inaugurated 68 new branches in Tier-2 and Tier-3 cities in financial year 2025 and this physical expansion has been carried out with net zero cost addition to UTI AMC by rationalizing space, reallocating people and modifying branch organization al structure.

items.statement: Launched Quant Fund (Feb 2025), three smart beta, two thematic, one market cap-based index fund in FY25; multi-cap fund NFO open Apr 29-May 13, 2025
items.quote: Amongst the NFOs we launched in FY 2025, UTI Quant Fund, which opened in February '25, saw good traction from our investors and partners alike. We also launched three smart beta, two thematic and one market cap-based index fund, further augmenting our offerings in passively managed space.

items.statement: Regulatory approval received for multi-cap fund; no further diversified equity NFOs planned; ETF/index launches based on appetite
items.quote: We have recently got a regulatory approval to launch a multi-cap fund, and that fund is already open for subscription from 29th of April till 13th of May. Apart from multi-cap fund, we don't see any pipeline as far as the diversified equity is concerned. There will be some launches on the ETF and the index fund, depending on the appetite.

items.statement: MFD channel contributes ~51% of SIP flows; direct/RIA channels 15-20%; direct channel steady at 17-18% over 4 quarters
items.quote: If you look at the share by the channel, the highest share in SIP flows was from the MFD chan nel, which is about 51%, followed by direct and RIA channels, which are in the range of 15% to 20%. If you look at the 4 quarters, the contribution of the direct channel to SIP flows remained at around 17% to 18

items.statement: Added ~8,500 new MFD partners in FY25 through empanelment drive
items.quote: To augment our distribution network, we conducted an empanelment drive, which helped us in extending our MFD network with around 8,500 new partners in FY '25.

items.statement: Declared dividend of ₹48 per share including ₹22 special dividend for FY25; ~94% of standalone profit of ₹653 crore
items.quote: UTI AMC has declared a dividend of ₹ 48 per share, including ₹ 22 as a special dividend for the Financial Year '24-'25. This is almost 94% of the stand-alone profit of the company, which is at ₹ 653 crores.

items.statement: Adjusted EBITDA margin expected to be 24-25% in FY26 due to railway business dilution
items.quote: if you just do the ma th that you take 27% is what we did 27 %x80 and do 18 x20, you will come to somewhere closer to between 24 to 25.

items.statement: Net order book at Rs 24,200 crore ($2.8 billion) with 77% EV contribution
items.quote: Which brings me neatly to a net order book which at the end of FY25 stands at 24.2 thousand crore rupees or $2.8 billion. The EV contribution to this order book remains high. It's at 77%.

items.statement: US tariffs expected to adversely impact auto demand but improve competitive positioning
items.quote: In our opinion, they will adversely impact the demand for cars and light trucks. Although we believe our competitive positioning will improve further if tariffs persist

items.statement: Q4 FY25 adjusted EBITDA margin 27.6%, down 130 bps YoY due to product mix change
items.quote: Adjusted EBITDA margin was 27.6%, which is a drop of 1.3% compared to fourth quarter of last year, and it's primarily on account of change in the product mix.

items.statement: FY25 capex Rs 415 crore; Mexico plant phase 1 investment below $10 million
items.quote: we've deployed about Rs. 415 crores in Capex that has left us with Rs. 360 crores of free cash flows

items.statement: Mexico plant phase 1 in progress for heavy truck/off-highway customers; US final assembly possible in 12-18 months if needed
items.quote: We are actually in the process of another plant in Mexico. And yeah, if really required, we can put up a final assembly plant in the US. It's not like it's something we can't do.

items.statement: BEV revenue share 36% in FY25 (up from 29%), ICE share down to 9%, commercial vehicle share 11%
items.quote: Our BEV revenue for the full year grew by 38% to ₹1,224 crore and BEV share of revenue increased to 36%.

items.statement: Added 7 new customers and 37 new programs in FY25; large US EV order received post-tariff announcement
items.quote: This came from 37 new programs, which were won and 7 new customers, which were added.

items.statement: Chinese competitors face higher tariffs, widening Sona's competitive gap; starter motor RFQs returning
items.quote: Our competitors in both our major product categories tend to be from China. And in an event in which tariffs are imposed on every Sona Comstar – Q4 FY25 Earnings Call country, it is basically then your relative pricing that comes into place

items.statement: Working with government and Chinese Embassy to speed up rare earth magnet imports; evaluating ferrite and alternate grades
items.quote: In India, while we are working with the industry and the government and the Chinese Embassy to speed up the process of importing magnets from China, we're also evaluating alternate materials

items.statement: North America 41% of revenue; India 43% pro-forma with railway business; Europe 19%
items.quote: Geographically, pretty much similar to last year, North America was our largest end market, contributing 41%. However, if we factored in the railway business that we announced the signing off on a pro forma basis, India is now the largest market with a revenue share of about 43%.

items.statement: Working capital turnover improved to 5x; fixed asset turnover declined to 3.4x due to high capitalization
items.quote: Working capital turnover ratio has further improved to 5 times. On the other hand, fixed asset turnover ratio has declined to 3.4 times because we had a very high capitalization this year of around 40 0 crores.

items.statement: QIP of Rs 2,370 crore (net) raised in September 2024
items.quote: We also raised QIP funds in September of 2024, so net off expenses, that amount is 2,370 crores.

items.statement: Invested Rs 60 crore in NOVELIC and Clear Motion Inc; railway business acquisition from EKL pending
items.quote: we invested about 60 crores in NOVELIC and Clear Motion Inc. At the end of the year, we had cash and investments balance of about 2,673 crores. Part of these funds, as you may know, would be used for the acquisition of railway business from EKL.

items.statement: Dividend distribution of Rs 190 crore in FY25
items.quote: Besides this, the bigger items were dividend distribution of 190 crores, which is a cash outflow.

items.statement: Vivek Vikram Singh completed 10 years as MD & Group CEO; company grew 10x revenue and 20x profit
items.quote: When I joined Sona BLW, standalone revenue for FY15 and its net profit were around 346 crores and 29 crores, respectively. So, in my first decade here, we've seen the company grow 10 times in revenue and over 20 times in profit

items.statement: 3% of total revenue at medium risk from US tariffs in next 12-18 months; rare earth supply disruption risk
items.quote: Net net we have 40% of our total revenue to US, in which we have identified 3% where there could be some risk of either revenue loss where they could look to somebody local

items.statement: Tariffs ultimately passed to end consumer; no margin absorption possible at 25% tariff level
items.quote: 25% tariff is not something that can be absorbed by anyone because nobody makes 25% net margin. Which is why eventually the consumer, the end consumer pays for it in the form of higher end product prices

items.statement: Entering humanoid robot components market leveraging motor, gear, actuator capabilities; 10M humanoids estimated by 2035
items.quote: One estimate puts the total of 10 million humanoids by 2035. It's a very important megatrend not to be missed. Sona Comstar, with its strong capabilities in gears, sensors, motors, controllers, embedded hardware and software, is uniquely positioned to ride this wave.

items.statement: Edible oil EBITDA per ton guidance of INR 3,500-3,600 for full business including other income
items.quote: I think we should be able to deliver the margin structure in per ton terms, which we have been delivering earlier, except for the last year. I think last year, we have to take out because it was an exceptional year. So just to spell out very clearly, INR 3,500 to INR3,600 a ton of EBITDA for edible oil should be -- should be -- on an overall basis

items.statement: Food & FMCG revenue target of INR 10,000 crores by end of FY27
items.quote: And with a INR 6,000 crores plus of revenue this year, I think we have taken internal target that by end of FY '27, that is after 2 years, we should be able to clock INR10,000 crores of revenue for the food.

items.statement: Edible oil volume growth target of 7-8% for FY26
items.quote: See, on growth front, e dible oil consumption we are hopeful of anything between 7% to 8% growth, although the country consumption is growing by only 3%, but we expect to do better than average industry, and we will continue to do, one

items.statement: Capex guidance of INR 500-600 crores per year for next couple of years
items.quote: So maybe for a purpose of taking any number, I think for next couple of years, I don't think we would be spending more than INR500 crores, INR600 crores of capex for a year.

items.statement: Gohana food complex to be commissioned by August 2025
items.quote: Our Gohana food complex, which is one of the big capex that we spent out of IPO funding is now more or less ready. We are hopeful that we should be able to commission the entire food park sometime in August '25.

items.statement: Castor derivative plant to be completed by end of FY26
items.quote: the locations. The c astor derivative plant is right now ongoing and should be completed by end of this financial year

items.statement: Ongoing capex of INR 1,000 crores includes Krishnapatnam complex and small facilities
items.quote: We are already building 1 -- we are already running 1 capex of INR1,000 crores which includes the wholly-owned complex in Krishnapatnam down South and a couple of small facilities for the

items.statement: Edible oil capacity utilization at 60%+ with room for growth
items.quote: Capacity utilization for all our edible oil capacities is decently placed, plus of 60%. So, we still have a lot of capacities with us to absorb any kind of growth that we will see in coming years.

items.statement: Gohana plant wheat flour capacity of 15,000 tons per month (180,000 tons annually)
items.quote: It is 15,000 tons per month. 180,000 tons on the lower side, higher side [inaudible 59:51].

items.statement: Gohana plant paddy processing capacity of 150,000 tons annually
items.quote: See, this plant can process roughly around 150,000 tons of paddy annually and roughly around over 150,000 tons, 200,000 tons of rice

items.statement: Food & FMCG revenue crossed INR 6,000 crores in FY25, grew 26% YoY
items.quote: For the full year, it crossed INR6,000 crores mark for the first time. Profitability of the food as we are suggesting earlier also remain at a breakeven or EBITDA neutral by design.

items.statement: Alternate channel revenue at INR 3,600 crores, quick commerce grew 113% YoY in Q4
items.quote: Now the alternate channel is reasonably big in our overall scheme of the things, contributing close to INR3,600 crores of revenue to our portfolio. Within this alternate channel, we are quite happy to see that quick commerce actually increased by 113% year-on-year in quarter 4.

items.statement: Overall ROCE improved to 15% in FY25 from 12% in FY22
items.quote: FY '22, we had an overall ROCE of 12%, whereas now we are sitting at 15%. And once the food starts delivering on the bottom line, this 15% should improve from here.

items.statement: Edible oil ROCE at 23%, Industry Essentials at 17% in FY25
items.quote: Edible oil continued to give better numbers in terms of volume as well as return on capital employed at 23%. Industry e ssentials delivered an ROCE of 17% and at an overall company level, we delivered an ROCE of 15

items.statement: Food & FMCG to remain EBITDA neutral for next 2-3 years by design
items.quote: On margin front, I think we have been saying this for quite some time that food will remain into an investment phase or a growth phase for next 2 years to 3 years and we'll continue to operate at an EBITDA neutral.

items.statement: Edible oil industry flat in Q4, wheat flour grew 12% in rural but flat in urban, Basmati rice full-year growth tepid at 5.5%
items.quote: In the Q4, the edible oil was -- the industry didn't grow actually. Industry was flattish without any growth. Similarly, when we look at wheat flour, which is one of the significant contributor to our food business also had got a mixed growth where it didn't grow in urban, but we did saw 12% growth in rural areas. When we look at the Basmati rice, again it's a significant contributor to our food b

items.statement: Palm oil prices high vs soya/sunflower impacted palm volumes, prices stabilizing entering Q1 FY26
items.quote: The prices of palm remained high as compared to soya and sunflower, impacting, of course, the demand on palm and that's where also company had some bit of i ssues in terms of palm volumes, b ut this proposition as we go forward should change as we enter into quarter 1 of FY '26. The prices have already started stabilizing and we are hopeful that the palm prices should cool down as we go forward fr

items.statement: Differential duty between CPO and refined palmolein at 7.5%, industry requesting 15% for Make in India
items.quote: Now it is cheaper to import olein and sell rather than to buy CPO process and sell. Now the industry has put in a lot of capex and most of the players are running at around 40%, 45% capacity utilization. Now, we have been requesting the government that Make in India is something that is being talked about, but it needs a differential duty of at least 15%.

items.statement: Soya nuggets and poha are star products with 30%+ gross margin and 15%+ EBITDA margin
items.quote: Soya nuggets and poha are the two categories with a very high-margin profile with a gross margin of plus of 30% and EBITDA of plus of 15% kind of numbers, which we have been able to clock. And this is one of the star product in our food segment and continue to grow.

items.statement: GD Foods acquired at EV of INR 603 crores (1.5x revenue), INR 400 crores topline with 50%+ gross margin
items.quote: We acquired this company at an enterprise value of INR 603 crores, which is close to 1.5x of their revenue. And we are hopeful that basis our distribution strength, we should be able to multiply the business model of this company.

items.statement: Direct retail reach expanded to 860,000 outlets (up 20%), reached 50,000+ rural towns target
items.quote: End of March '25, we are now 8.6 million retail outlets where we reach directly, up by close to 20% from last year. Last year, March '24 we were at 7.2 million outlets – 7,20,000 outlets, sorry to 860,000 outlets now. On the rural side, we have -- as we were saying in quite a few calls earlier that we would want to reach target 50,000 rural towns by March '25 and we are happy to announce that we h

items.statement: Branded share: edible oil 60%+, food 70-75%, overall 70% branded
items.quote: Edible oil, we do have a good chunk of institutional clients also. But in edible oil, it's close to plus of 60% is brand. In food, it is more than 70%, 75%. when you look at the overall scheme of the things, we have good 70% of business coming from the brand.

items.statement: Lost 1.3% market share in palm oil due to high prices, overall share down 30 bps; plan to regain via flanker brands and rural expansion
items.quote: We lost almost 1.3% market share in palm oil. We are number 2 player. And obviously, we have big share in olein and that we dropped because the high prices, obviously, consumption dropped. We got incremental 10 bps in soybean oil. Sunflower oil grew by 20 basis points and mustard oil grew by 30 basis points. Overall, overall, our market share dropped by 30 basis points only because of olein.

items.statement: Government accepted industry request for higher differential duty on refined palm oil, expected to happen soon
items.quote: Government has accepted it as a positive sign. And I think things will happen sooner or later because government has understood that helping the Indonesian industry is of no use. And I hope it happens fast.

items.statement: Gohana plant delayed 3 months due to new NCR pollution control norms requiring Central Pollution Control Board clearance
items.quote: But what happened was that new norm of getting pollution control came up for units located in NCR. And our Gohana unit is located in NCR. So one, it has to work on biofuel. So, that is not an issue. Issue was that the government said that as per the law, the unit can only start after the Central Pollution Control Board gives us clearance certificate.

items.statement: GD Foods acquisition closed in Q1 FY26, targeting 2x revenue growth in couple of years via distribution and sourcing synergies
items.period: Q1 FY26 and next couple of years

items.quote: On people cost, there are two reasons. items.statement: Edible oil volume CAGR of 7% over full year, reached 4+ million tons in FY25
items.quote: Edible o il quarterly sales trend is healthy, 6% growing in volume terms. We did 1.04 million tons in Q4 '25. Full year, the CAGR of 7%. We closed at a little over 4 million tons for the edible oil in FY '25

items.statement: Wheat flour market share near 6%, distant number two player
items.quote: Wheat flour business continues very well to grow and gain market share. We are now close to 6% of market share and distant number two player in the country.

items.statement: Palm oil price uncertainty due to potential Indonesia/Malaysia B40 blending mandates
items.quote: But one doesn't know about any policy that Indonesia or Malaysia will bring on B40. Now, these are some things where things always remain uncertain. But going ahead, we feel that palm oil will not be as pricely as it used to be in the past, at least last 6 months and it's going to be reasonable.

items.statement: Company renamed from Adani Wilmar Limited to AWL Agri Business Limited with new logo
items.quote: On business update, happy to inform everyone that we got renamed from Adani Wilmar Limited to AWL Agri Business Limited. And the logic of our new logo, of course, is like river that nurtures the land and carry stories across the generation.

items.statement: Management expects continued growth momentum and margin improvement but does not provide specific FY26 revenue or profit targets.
items.quote: If you look at the last three, four quarters, we are inching towards better revenue numbers as well as better margins. So, clearly there are some things that are working in our favor.

items.statement: EBITDA margin improved from 17% to 20% annually in FY25; PAT margin improved from 6% to 9%.
items.quote: On the annual side, you know, the demand has improved, the expenses are tightly controlled and therefore, the EBITDA margin has jumped from 17 to 20 on an annual basis. And if you look at the PAT margins, it has jumped from 6 to 9%.

items.statement: Demand has improved and the company is seeing positive traction in large enterprise accounts.
items.quote: On the annual side, you know, the demand has improved, the expenses are tightly controlled and therefore, the EBITDA margin has jumped from 17 to 20 on an annual basis.

items.statement: Enterprise customers increased from 15 to 18; clients with >$1M revenue increased to 12; revenue from existing clients rose to 95%.
items.quote: Enterprise customers have increased from 15 to 18. Clients which have built more than a million dollars is now 12. And clients which have built more than a crore at least is 70 now. Our share of revenue from existing clients has increased to 95% because our clients are also

items.statement: IT park project in Indore: 3 acres leased at Rs 9 lakh/year for 50 years; InfoBeans holds 51% in consortium; capital burden ~Rs 30 crore; rest funded via debt against land collateral.
items.quote: The capital burden for InfoBeans is going to be about 30 crores which is not a signiﬁcant capital infusion looking at the size of our balance sheet and rest will be through debt because the land can be put as collateral for generating about 150 crores of debt to build this building

items.statement: Utilization crossing 82% monthly; yearly average under 80% but improving.
items.quote: Utilization is increasing. I think we are crossing 82 percent right now. So that is on a monthly basis. But on a yearly, obviously it will be under 80 right now because the earlier ones were not as, but as optimized.

items.statement: Revenue split: 52% product engineering, 48% digital transformation; InfoBeans Cloud Tech share decreasing in parent revenue.
items.quote: Revenue breakup for segment, digital transformation, product engineering, more or less similar, 52 percent product engineering, 48 percent digital transformation. And InfoBeans cloud tech revenue is decreasing in the parent organization in the total pie.

items.statement: Significant growth in Europe and UAE markets; US share reduced in revenue mix as part of geographic de-risking.
items.quote: A signiﬁcant growth in the European market and also decent growth in UAE market for us and thus this has reﬂected in reduction, increase in share of Europe and UAE and reduction of USA in the total pie when I break up the revenue by

items.quote: Eternus Solutions 22.6 crores towards the impairment of intangible assets and reduction in contingent liability of about 22 crores because the founders were not eligible for the earnout due on March 2025.

items.statement: Board recommended annual dividend of Rs 1 per share (face value Rs 10), subject to AGM approval; payout ~6.3% of FY25 PAT.
items.quote: Annual dividend of 1 rupee is announced by the board today and it will be up for the shareholder approval in the AGM, it comes to about 6.3 percent of PAT for this

items.statement: US market uncertainty and potential recession noted; company de-risking via Europe, UAE, Canada, Nordics expansion.
items.quote: US seems to be running in certain chaos and might be headed towards a recession but with the de-risking that we have been able to achieve in the last couple of years, we are in a good position.

items.statement: Ascent acquisition expected to be EPS neutral in FY26 and value-accretive from FY27
items.quote: We have seen a healthy increase in EPS, about 34% increase versus last year and we believe that in times to come with the acquisition of Ascent at least for FY'26 it will be neutral and from FY'27 we believe it will be value-accretive.

items.statement: Signed definitive agreement to acquire 51% controlling stake in Ascent Fund Services, Singapore
items.quote: the biggest highlight KFintech has had to offer, which many of you might have already heard in the earlier analyst meetings was about K Fintech signing a definitive agreement to acquire a controlling stake of 51% in the As cent Fund Services , Singapore-based

items.statement: Large M&A ambitions closed for foreseeable future; only minor plug-ins may be evaluated
items.quote: With this, we would have summarily close our large M&A ambitions for the foreseeable future . There will be minor plug-ins which may still continue to evaluate.

items.statement: IT spend at 19% of revenue in FY25 vs 21% in FY24; expected to continue declining
items.quote: overall we believe that 19% of the total revenue that we have spent on IT in the current year vis-à-vis 21% last year, will continue to come down in the coming years.

items.statement: International business at 100 contracts; large trustee win in Malaysia (full fund admin + DTA) and full-service tier deal in Philippines AMC
items.quote: I am happy to also tell you that we have now reached 100 contracts in our international business. And if you recollect one of the points that I had made in the initial days was , the contracts that we had been signing initially were obviously the smaller and the medium-tiered AMCs and it's a matter of time the larger contracts tend to come in.

items.statement: International AUM grew ~33% YoY in FY25 with both mark-to-market gains and net inflows for first time in 4 years
items.quote: But this year, FY25 , saw the first year in the last four years both mark-to-market gain as well as net inflows, which means that the revenue hopefully from now on will be on account of both new wins and more importantly on the back of the expansion of the AUM of the current clients. So, the AUM grew nearly about 33% year-on-year into the previous year.

items.statement: GIFT City funds at ~30, ~50% market share; target 75% combined with Ascent
items.quote: we have onboarded three new funds and GIFT City taking our total funds to close to 30, making our market share close to about 50% of the GIFT City funds and with Ascent Fund Services should we include that obviously our market share will be far superior KFin Technologies Limited April 29, 2025 to that. We intend to get to three-fourths of the total market share in the GIFT City with the combined s

items.statement: AIF count nearing 600, market share ~37%, AUM ~Rs.1.5 trillion, up ~50% YoY
items.quote: In terms of the alternates, a quick milestone , we are reaching nearly 600 alternate investment funds as we speak today and market share has increased close to 37%. That overall AUM is at about Rs.1.5 trillion and it's grown nearly about 50% year-on-year as we stand today.

items.statement: Issuer Solutions: ~8,000 corporates, ~50% of NSE 500; managed top 3 IPOs (Bajaj Housing, Hyundai, etc.)
items.quote: We have added nearly 1 ,000-plus corporates into our roster, getting the number closer to 8,000. In terms of market share, we now are the service provider for nearly 50% of all NSE 500 listed companies. We have done the top three of the biggest IPOs that have happened in this country this year whether it is Bajaj Housing Finance or Hyundai, so on and so forth.

items.statement: Wealth platform mPowerWealth signed 5 large wealth managers (added Thrive Wealth, Northern Arc in Q4)
items.quote: within a matter of few months very happy to inform you that we have signed up with five large wealth managers . Some of this was already announced in the previous quarter, but in this quarter into the previous three months we have signed two more wealth management companies called Thrive Wealth and N orthern Arc Capital.

items.statement: Revenue mix FY25: MF fee-based ~64%, Issuer Solutions ~15%, International & Investor Solutions ~14% (International ~5-6%)
items.quote: The breakup of revenue is more like mutual fund , fee-based revenue continues to be in the range of about 64%, the Issuer Solutions revenue is 15% of total revenue, the international and other investor solutions revenue is about 14% of total revenue. Within that, now international business continues to be about in the range of about 5% to 6%.

items.statement: International revenue contribution expected to move from 5-6% to 13-15% with Ascent acquisition
items.quote: And we believe that the trajectory in terms of international KFin Technologies Limited April 29, 2025 business contribution will change with the acquisition of Ascent, which currently is about 5-6%, will move towards 13% to 15% in future with the acquisition of

items.statement: FY25 EBITDA margin 43.9% (would be ~45% ex Rs.12 cr M&A due diligence); Q4 margin 43.2% (would be ~46% ex due diligence)
items.quote: EBITDA margins which are 43.9% for the year would have been about 45% for the year but for this Rs.12 crores that we had to incur to do a due diligence , and for the quarter, which is 43.2% would have been about 46%.

items.statement: Cloud/license expansion added ~Rs.12-13 cr extra IT cost in FY25; optimizing cloud vs on-prem strategy
items.quote: There are expenses related to cloud expenses and licenses that we have incurred in terms of expansion and balancing strategy between on-prem to cloud, which is a similar increase about Rs.12, 13 crores extra that we have incurred to ramp up in terms of IT strategy.

items.statement: Dividend declared Rs.7.5 per share for FY25, subject to shareholder approval
items.quote: dividend of Rs.7.5 per share has been declared by the board and subject to shareholders’ approval shall be disseminated so.

items.statement: Cash & equivalents Rs.660 cr (Mar 31); to fund Rs.7.5/share dividend and Rs.305 cr for 51% Ascent acquisition
items.quote: We remain healthy in terms of cash and cash equivalents. That's 660 crores of cash, which will be utilized towards payout of dividend that the board has recommended subject to shareholders’ approval of Rs.7.50 per share and the acquisition of initial 51%, about Rs.305 crores will also be funded out of it

items.statement: EBITDA-to-free cash flow conversion ~60% while investing in new products
items.quote: We continue to convert EBITDA-to-free cash flow at about 60%, while we continue to invest for future and capital expenditure to develop new products.

items.statement: KRA in-principle SEBI approval received; platform built; awaiting final approval; launch expected this quarter
items.quote: we received in-principle approval from SEBI for the KRA business. We have completed our platform build at this point in time. We are awaiting SEBI's final approval. Our readiness at this very moment is we are literally a minute away from launching our KRA Solutions the moment we get approval from the regulator. So, our preparedness is absolutely done and we believe it's a matter of time and hopefu

items.statement: Thailand services fully live with organic pipeline growth; Malaysia MF market share ~55%
items.quote: We have initiated starting of our services into Thailand last year. The contract has gone fully live into this year and with resounding success. items.statement: ESOP grants expected to continue in FY26 for talent attraction/retention in knowledge business
items.quote: ESOPs were given in the previous year; I would expect KFin Technologies Limited April 29, 2025 some ESOPs to be given this year as well. To a certain extent, it is probably wise to factor in certain amount of ESOPs to be given. We are in a knowledge industry . As you all know, it's an asset light model. We don't have plants and machinery. Our assets are our people

items.statement: Non-current asset held-for-sale relates to asset to be transferred to MFCentral JV upon EOP license
items.quote: it is basically the asset which has been generated which will be transferred to the MFCentral JV as we have formed. So, as and when they get the EOP license, the asset needs to be transferred to them. That is why it is shown in the balance sheet as asset held-for-sale.

items.statement: Management maintains FY26 guidance of 18-20% top-line growth and 40-45% EBITDA margin; Ascent integration neutral to EBITDA margin in FY26, accretive in FY27
items.quote: We continue to maintain guidance of 18% to 20% top line growth and 40 % to 45% of EBITDA margin. While we will see the integration of Ascent in the coming three, four months we believe that it will be neutral in terms of EBITDA margin impact, and it will become accretive in FY27

items.statement: KFintech international deal pipeline in Southeast Asia (ex-Thailand) is ~$25M revenue potential, growing with 7 large deals signed in last 6 months
items.quote: Our KFintech deal pipeline in Southeast Asia is close to about $25 million at this point in time. And the conversion rate if you saw in the last six months had been pretty solid with nearly seven large deals to have been signed

items.statement: Ascent deal pipeline larger than KFintech's international pipeline across 18 countries, expanding faster; details to be shared after integration
items.quote: Ascent, their pipeline is larger in the context of multiple geographies that they are present in 18 different count ries and of course we are still in the early stages of integration

items.statement: Ascent integration mathematically dilutes consolidated EBITDA margin below 44% initially, but impact marginal at percentage level and not dilutive at absolute level
items.quote: Mathematically, absolutely, yes, it will. But again, keep in context, the total revenue profile is roughly $18 million and KFintech's total revenue into the coming year obviously is going to be much, much higher. So, the impact will be marginal at a percentage level, but at an absolute number level, it won't be dilutive.

items.statement: MF contract renegotiation may cause some yield compression but not materially high given only 2 of 27 AMCs up for renewal
items.quote: There can be some compression, but I wouldn't anticipate it to be materially high.

items.statement: MF contract losses due to severe price undercutting; management prioritizes profitable deals over volume
items.quote: We did not find some of those deals accretive in terms of business. At the end of the day I have responsibility to my shareholder to drive a profitable and a meaningful business. So, it is sometimes important to lose the trees for the woods.

items.statement: Issuer Solutions added 9M folios in FY25, nearly all organic from existing clients; full annuity revenue impact from FY26
items.quote: On the Issuer Solutions, the total folio addition in the previous year was 9 million folios, which is pretty robust. And I think with the exception of one specific transition, nearly all of it is organic

items.statement: AIF revenue purely annuity with 1-3 month lag from fund launch to revenue recognition; no one-time revenue
items.quote: In AIF usually there is no episodical one-time revenue at all. So, this is purely annuity. In fact, you will always see a lag of revenue because it usually takes a month to t wo to t hree months where a fund house when it launches and onwards and RTA for us to set ourselves keep ourselves operationally ready for them to go live and then they get the

items.statement: Tech spend as % of revenue rose from 7-8% five years ago to 23-24% in FY25 (on revenue growing from ~Rs350Cr to ~Rs1,200Cr); focused on modernization, cloud, cyber security, AI
items.quote: If you see our spend of tech as a percentage of revenue, which is a parameter we track to , five years back, it used to be about 7 % to 8%, the year that had gone by, it has risen to almost 23 % to 24%.

items.statement: Completed migration to AWS cloud by 2019-20; leveraging data engineering (DIGIX, PARAS) for client solutions; drafting corporate AI policy with real use cases like AI-generated status reports
items.quote: We have successfully completed our migration into AWS . And it is not just about for the sake of migrating data, but it's about your ability to create business solutions and value based on that ability to crunch peta bytes of data in a few seconds and help our clients grow.

items.statement: Employee cost increase driven by volume growth (transactions +33% YoY) with headcount up only 5-7%; ESOP cost Rs11.3Cr added in FY25, expected Rs18-20Cr in FY26
items.quote: We also have ESOP cost of about Rs.11.3 crores, which was incurred as an addition to what was incurred last year and next year again, you will see an increase in the ESOP cost because more employees will get covered in a new scheme which new brands will come in and we do expect anywhere around 18 to 20 crores of ESOP expenses to come in the next year.

items.statement: International competition varies by geography: captives in Malaysia/Philippines; global fund administrators (Apex, SS&C, IQEQ) in Singapore/Hong Kong/West; differentiation via service standards, speed, advisory in private mandates
items.quote: in a private mandate space, unlike in the case of a public mandate space transitions are possible because the lineage of the funds won't be very large, the number of investors won't be very large, the history isn't as significant as in the case of mutual funds. Given the transitions are possible , a good number of the cases it happens is largely because of the service standards , go-to-market

items.statement: BlackRock Aladdin partnership: KFintech 1 of <10 preferred partners; integrating mPower with Aladdin; revenue expected in 1-2 quarters; differentiation via integrated tech stack, pricing, analytics
items.quote: We by virtue of being a preferred partner for BlackRock to implement Aladdin and Aladdin as things stack today has roughly about $20 trillion of global funds which means that we as one of the preferred partner, has access to compete and win any of the fund managers who have currently onboarded Aladdin platform.

items.statement: Revenue per folio in Issuer Solutions fell to Rs9.4 from Rs10-10.3 due to high IPO activity (folios counted full year, revenue partial); not structural; contract prices actually revised upward for select clients
items.quote: Definitely , your observation about a lot of IPOs happening in the year, which means the folio is counted, but the revenue is not counted for the full year. Obviously, mathematically it will look and it will appear to dilute the revenue p er folio. That is definitely the first of it.

items.statement: Hexagram/mPower platform strategic for global ambitions; revenue not fully captured in Hexagram books (e.g., mPower Wealth ~Rs20Cr, AIF fund accounting on mPower booked in AIF line)
items.quote: We created an entire m Power Wealth as a business line. Within a matter of a few months it's already about Rs.20 crores business for us, right. And the alternate investment funds, for example, the revenue that you see there, unlike in the case of mutual funds, we do both transfer agency and fund accounting for AIF s. The fund accounting as a solution is rendered on top of mPower, which is a Hexagr

items.statement: Asset held for sale classification due to pending EOP license transfer to JV partner
items.quote: So, as and when they get the EOP license, the asset needs to be transferred to them. That is why it is shown in the balance sheet as asset held-for-sale.

items.statement: One MF shifted to CAMS due to key management personnel's prior affiliation with CAMS; 10 MFs shifted from CAMS to KFin over 15 years
items.quote: The fundhouse that has shifted from K Fin to CAMS, is a fun dhouse which has an AUM less than a few hundreds of crores. And I think the affiliation was largely in the context of some of the key management personnel who joined that entity belonged to CAMS back in the day.

items.statement: VAS revenue sequential decline not a trend; project-based with spillover; maintenance annuity ~20-25% of contract value
items.quote: I wouldn't read too much into the sequential component of it given it is not annualized or an annuity revenue as against contracts that we win and deliver and then obviously we get on to the maintenance mode for us to have annuity revenue, but that would be at a smaller clip of about 20% or 25% of the total value so to speak.

items.statement: Management focused on asset/wealth management depth and geographic breadth; no plans to diversify into banking, payments, insurance aggregation
items.quote: We believe that our 100% of our time, effort and focus will be needed for us to achieve these goals and ambitions and we don't believe digressing into say, banking industry for example, payment aggregation, some of our competitors get into that space or account aggregation and bunch of others or insurance for that matter.

items.statement: Expects EBITDA growth of close to 25% with at least 100 bps margin expansion in FY26; aims for 20-25% minimum bottom-line growth
items.quote: And for the financial year FY '26 also, our focus remains on increasing the profitability, and we expect that the growth in our profitability in terms of EBITDA would be close to 25%, with at least a 100 basis point increase in the margin.

items.statement: No specific top-line guidance given due to geopolitical and tariff uncertainties
items.quote: We'll not be able to give a specific guidance on the top line, but our aim is that on the bottom line, we expect at least 20% to 25% minimum growth for the next financial year.

items.statement: FY25 capacity expansion completed ahead of schedule and below budgeted capex
items.quote: The planned capacity expansion that we had planned for the last financial year, which is FY '25, was completed seamlessly and fully integrated with our existing operations and executed ahead of the schedule and also below the originally budgeted capex.

items.statement: Flexible hose capacity expanded from 16.5 million to 20 million meters; 16.5M commissioned end of Q3 FY25, targeting full utilization in FY26
items.quote: And also with that, we are expanding from 16.5 million to about 20 million.

items.statement: Metal bellows Phase 1 capacity 120,000 pieces/year (10,000/month) started production in Q4 FY25; miniature metal bellows project to be commissioned by March 2026
items.quote: The total capacity in Phase 1 is 120,000 pieces per annum, which is about 10,000 pieces a month. So far, obviously, the revenue that has come in is close to about INR1.5 crores in the last financial year.

items.statement: Order book from U.S. remains strong; some shipment delays due to longer transit routes and customer requests to delay in Feb-Mar
items.quote: Our order book is quite strong from America. The one thing that has happened is because of the longer delays or the delays in the shipping, that's why the transit time has increased.

items.statement: FY25 EBITDA margin 21.5% (up from ~17.5% FY24); Q4 FY25 EBITDA margin 20.71%; PAT margin ~14%
items.quote: Our EBITDA for the entire year stood at INR82 crores, which is a growth of 24% on a year-on-year basis and with an EBITDA margin of 21.5%.

items.statement: 10% U.S. tariff (up from ~3.5-4%) has minor margin impact; no major demand destruction seen
items.quote: So the reduction in margin is there, but it's minor, not much.

items.statement: Assemblies share reached 52-53% of FY25 sales (Q4: 60%); target 65-70% over next 3-4 years
items.quote: Overall, if you see for the entire year, we have more than 50% of our sales coming in from assemblies, I think about 52% to 53% to be exact, coming in from the assembly business.

items.statement: Healthy sustained demand across energy, oil & gas, chemicals, metals, railways and new-age sectors; domestic growth outpacing exports
items.quote: From an end user perspective, we are witnessing healthy and sustained demand across the key sectors, which includes energy, oil and gas, chemicals, metals, railways and other new age sectors.

items.statement: Collaborating with a multi-billion dollar U.S. company for liquid cooling flow solutions for AI data centers at bellows plant
items.quote: I'm happy to share that we are collaborating with a multibillion-dollar global company, which is headquartered in the U.S.A. for providing flow solutions for liquid-based cooling for AI data centers.

items.statement: U.S. tariffs rose from ~3.5% to 10%; 90-day pause on higher reciprocal tariffs (~27-30%); EU tariff differential ~4-5% if implemented
items.quote: So in terms of tariffs, so obviously, as we all are aware, there is a 90-day pause on the tariff. But the tariffs on our products earlier was around 3.5%, which has now increased to 10%.

items.statement: Export sales grew minimally in FY25; domestic sales grew much faster; export working capital cycle ~120 days vs domestic ~75 days
items.quote: Definitely, our domestic sales has increased at a much, much faster pace as compared to our export sales. That doesn't mean that our export sales have not increased.

items.statement: Domestic working capital cycle ~75 days vs export ~120 days due to container filling and transit time
items.quote: For example, if an overall working capital days, say, for example, for an export is just assuming, say, for example, 120 days overall working capital cycle. In India, that comes down to about 75 days.

items.statement: Company remains debt-free
items.quote: And we continue to remain a debt-free company, and we remain focused on effectively utilizing our working capital.

items.statement: Shareholder-approved QIP (~INR400 cr) documentation under process; proceeds mainly for inorganic acquisitions, small part for working capital; no specific timeline
items.quote: Yes. So most of the proceeds of the QIP will be used for inorganic acquisitions and a small part of it would be used for working capital.

items.statement: Actively exploring U.S. acquisition for local presence; part of manufacturing in India, last-mile assembly in U.S.; early stage, nothing finalized
items.quote: Yes, we are planning and nothing is finalized as yet. So we will not be able to comment on that.

items.statement: Metal bellows revenue potential INR85-90 cr at peak; miniature metal bellows INR25-30 cr; combined hose+bellows peak revenue ~INR650-750 cr at 20M meters and 70% assembly mix
items.quote: So at a 20 million meter annual capacity and say, I just assume that, say, if 70% of the business comes from the assemblies, right? So we can see a revenue potential of about INR650 crores.

items.statement: Metal bellows to contribute 25-30% of revenue in 4-5 years; currently loss-making at start-up phase
items.quote: I would say, 25% to 30% of our business, if not more, would come from metal bellows 4, 5 years from now.

items.statement: Board recommended final dividend of 15% (INR0.30 per equity share) for FY25
items.quote: I'm also happy to share that the Board of Directors have recommended a final dividend of 15%, that is INR0.30 per equity share.

items.statement: MD completed Harvard Business School course on digitalization and AI in manufacturing; aim to become digitally dextrous organization
items.quote: Last month, I did a course from Howard Business School on how to implement digitalization and usage of AI tools in manufacturing businesses. And our aim in the future is to become a digitally dextrous organization.

items.statement: Short-term tariff pain possible (1-2 months); longer shipping routes via Cape of Good Hope increasing transit time; customers delaying procurement but not cancelling
items.quote: So like I mentioned that there might be like short-term pain with regards to maybe a month or so. But I think long term, I think we expect that the demand for Indian manufacturers and the demand for actually -- demand for India-made products will actually increase in the U.S.

items.statement: Competition from U.S. and European manufacturers; strengthened domestic market share (80/20 to 75/25 export/domestic mix); aim to be global #1
items.quote: We are the number one player in India, and we would want to continue to remain number one for the foreseeable future. And also our plan is not only for India, but we ultimately aim to become the number one player in our business worldwide.

items.statement: Steel prices currently 20-25% below peak of 1.5-2 years ago
items.quote: I think a couple of years back, steel prices right now, I think, would be at least, I would say, 20% to 25% lower as compared to the peak prices.

items.statement: Metal bellows require extensive certifications; some received, some pending; longer sales cycle than hoses
items.quote: Also, as I mentioned earlier that this product requires a lot of certification. So our products are already under certifications. Some of the certifications we have received, some of the other certifications are still pending.

items.statement: AUM growth target 12-15% including business loans; 25-30% excluding business loans for FY26
items.quote: If you take that in the base, then you will see around 12 % to 15% growth. If you remove that from the base, you will see about 25% to 30% AUM growth is what we are targeting.

items.statement: Credit cost expected to stay around 1% plus or minus 10 bps in FY26
items.quote: I am expecting it to stay around 1 % plus or minus 10 bps. So I am seeing the credit cost hovering around that range.

items.statement: Net interest margin expected to remain stable
items.quote: Ajit, we expect the net interest margin to be stable.

items.statement: Doorstep gold loan share target 18-22% in next 1-2 years from current 15%
items.quote: In the next one year to two years, we want to take it up by 3% or 4% points. That means you will see that 15% number going to about 18% to 22% in the next one year to two years.

items.statement: Cost to average assets may dip 5-10 bps; cost-to-income guidance deferred due to investments
items.quote: On the average assets basis, you can look at a 5 to 10 basis points there.

items.statement: Gold loan AUM grew 48% YoY driven by 18% tonnage growth and price appreciation; added 35,000 new customers in Q4
items.quote: In the gold business, we had a fantastic year and quarter with our AUM growing 48% YOY aided by tonnage growth 18 % YOY.

items.statement: Small ticket LAP disbursals grew 58% QoQ to Rs 270 crore in Q4 after migration to Salesforce and new BRE
items.quote: With the new processes in BRE, our small ticket LAP disbursals for Q4 touched Rs. 270 crores, a growth of about 58% quarter-on-quarter.

items.statement: Yields up 43 bps, cost of borrowings up 30 bps, pure spread expansion 13 bps in FY25
items.quote: On a daily average basis, our yields have increased by 43 bps over the fiscal. While on an average, our cost of borrowings have gone up by 30 bps. Consequently, we have seen a pure spread expansion during the year of 13 bps.

items.statement: Total AUM Rs 15,812 crore, up 30% YoY; Gold AUM Rs 5,880 crore (37% of AUM), MT LAP Rs 4,394 crore (28%), ST LAP Rs 3,668 crore (23%), Unsecured BL Rs 1,656 crore (<10%)
items.quote: Overall AUM was Rs. 15,812 crores as of March 31, 2025. This is up from Rs. 12,191 crores as of April 1. So AUM has grown 30% in this fiscal.

items.statement: Off-balance sheet book Rs 3,973 crore, up 75% YoY; includes gold CLM Rs 1,131 crore, unsecured BL securitized Rs 440 crore, mortgage DA Rs 2,408 crore
items.quote: Our off balance sheet book as of March 31, 25 stands at Rs. 3,973 crores, up 75% year-on-year from Rs. 2,276 crores in the previous year.

items.statement: Gross Stage 3 at 2% vs 1.8% QoQ; credit cost 1% in Q4 vs 0.7% YoY; full year credit cost 1.8% of average assets
items.quote: Our gross stage 3 stands at 2% versus 1.8 quarter-on-quarter. A credit cost for the quarter stood at 1% versus 0.7% last year.

items.statement: Expect near-term flows in ST LAP over next two quarters, then plateau and normalization by year-end
items.quote: There are likely to be flows in the quarters coming and we see those flows coming in the next two quarters. And thereafter I am seeing a plateau and then by year end we will normalize.

items.statement: PCR to stabilize between previous high and low levels after one-time provision jump
items.quote: So it will stabilize somewhere in between, depending because, see, the incremental flows will happen at a incremental different PCR, like whatever the model suggests.

items.statement: Investing in collection infrastructure: verticalized structure, middle layer and field hiring to complete by Q1, added call center and litigation resources
items.quote: We have verticalized the collection structure to bring focus at product level. The middle layer and field level hiring is in progress and we expect to complete it by Q1.

items.statement: Strengthening ST LAP middle management and frontline team; substantial completion expected by Q1
items.quote: We are in the process of strengthening the middle management as well as the frontline team. We expect to complete substantial part of the exercise by Q1.

items.statement: Branch expansion plans under review; update expected by Q1; focus on co-locating MSE and gold branches
items.quote: On the branch expansion side, we will look at the opportunities going in quarter one, and we should be able to update by quarter one.

items.statement: Gold loan portfolio yield 19.7% (not comparable to origination yield); tenure premium drives difference; penal charges excluded from yield
items.quote: When we say 19.7, that is the weighted average rate of the portfolio.

items.statement: Confident of maintaining gold loan yields despite competition; focus on retail book with less competitive pressure
items.quote: we co ncentrate on the retail book and we do not see much of a competition coming there from the customer's requirement or need. We are, are confident to maintain these yields

items.statement: Gold loan LTV: portfolio average 66%, origination LTV 72%; stress testing and margin call mechanism in place at 75% regulatory cap
items.quote: Our overall LTV at the top level is at 66%. It is not 71.7%, 71.7% is our origination LTV.

items.statement: RBI draft gold loan guidelines seen as healthy clarification on LTV; level playing field; short-term transition blip expected
items.quote: These particular guidelines, I think, are very, healthy in terms of the clarifying on the LTV side. Earlier there was a lot of confusion on the interpretation of LTV. Now these draft guidelines are clarifying it and making it a level playing field for everyone.

items.statement: RBI guidelines on bank investment in NBFCs: status quo; representations submitted by company and parent; awaiting regulator response
items.quote: There is no change between Q3 and Q4. Our representation which we had sent in Q3 still remains the same and we are hoping that the regulator looks at it with a different eye because we are a listed entity.

items.statement: Weighted average cost of borrowings 8.72% (up 3 bps QoQ); 89% floating rate (47% MCLR, rest external benchmark); added one foreign lender, total relationships 42
items.quote: On a quarter-on-quarter basis, our weighted average cost of borrowings has marginally gone up by three basis points from 8.69% to 8.72%.

items.statement: Debt-equity ratio 4.03 (up from 3.98); capital adequacy improved 30 bps to 21.9% via DA/CLM of Rs 787 crore in Q4
items.quote: Our debt equity ratio has marginally increased from 3.98 in December to 4.03 as of March. On the capital conservation strategy, the Company continues to move forward in its policy of deleveraging the balance sheet through co-lending and direct assignment of installment loans.

items.statement: Strategy unchanged: twin-engine focus on ST LAP and Gold; MT LAP provides low-risk complement; BL slowed for 100% secured construct
items.quote: The strategy remains same. The strategy is to focus on the ST LAP business and the gold business together. We have always articulated our twin-engine strategy.

items.statement: Gold loan added 35,000 new customers in Q4; doorstep gold now 15% of gold AUM, more than doubled in FY25
items.quote: We have added 35,000 new customers in Gold loans during the quarter.

items.statement: Moved Rs 787 crore off-book in Q4 (DA Rs 531 crore mortgage, CLM Rs 256 crore gold) to improve capital adequacy
items.quote: During the quarter, our AUM grew by Rs. 900 crores. We moved Rs. 787 crores of loans off book which constituted a DA of Rs. 531 crore across the mortgage book and a CLM of Rs. 256 crores on the gold loan book.

items.statement: No write-offs in Q4; elevated Stage 2 in ST LAP indicates near-term flows; BL rundown managed within 1% credit cost guidance
items.quote: We have not done any write-off in Q4.

items.statement: Employee count reduced; OPEX optimization planned across manpower, technology, premises; investing in collections and growth
items.quote: There will be work which we will be doing on the manpower side, on the technology side, and on the premises side, trying to optimize and see what is the trajectory we can take there.

items.statement: Filed universal bank application within 30 days after meeting RBI norms of GNPA <3% and NNPA <1% for two consecutive years
items.quote: With that, we would like to file in our application for the universal Bank within the next 30 days.

items.statement: Accelerated provisions of Rs 305 cr taken in FY25 to keep net NPA below 1%; worst of credit costs behind us
items.quote: The Rs. 305 crores obviously is to make sure that net NPA remains below 1 %, and Rs. 305 crores obviously have come from increased MFI stress leading to obviously most slippages and then our need to provision.

items.statement: Expect some accelerated provisioning in FY26 but much lower than FY25; will maintain net NPA <1% and gross NPA <3% for universal bank application
items.quote: So yes, I will tell you that we will have some accelerated provision this year also. But again, why the acceleration on Rs. 300 crores and not Rs. 200 crores? Because of MFI stress. If there is no stress, acceleration would have been lower here. So I expect it to be much lower this year but would not be zero because we would like to keep net NPA below 1% and gross NPA below 3%.

items.statement: NIMs expected to improve in FY26 driven by lower interest suspense, unsecured growth, deposit cost reduction, and stable secured NIMs despite higher funding costs
items.quote: So yes, Manish, we should expect NIMs to improve as we go into this financial year, and I mentioned all the right reasons for that.

items.statement: Secured product NIMs held steady from March 2024 to March 2025 despite deposit cost increases
items.quote: And the good news is, my NIMs of secured are identical between March '24 and March '25 in spite of cost of deposit going up.

items.statement: Secured assets grew 40% YoY in FY25 (3-year CAGR 40%); unsecured de-grew 11% but turned slightly positive (+0.2%) in Q4
items.quote: Overall growth in secured assets is 40%. And where we sit, we would like to continue the same growth rate and there is no reason why we should not continue the same growth rate of secured asset growth.

items.statement: MFI book down from 40% to 30% of assets; 28% now under guarantee programs (CGFMU/CGTMSE), targeting 90% by September
items.quote: The MFI book, 28% of which is now under the guarantee program. As we all know that this guarantee program takes in new disbursements, so we will complete the balance 70 %-odd through this year. So by September, we will mostly be 90%-odd under the guarantee program.

items.statement: Gold loans grew 237.6%, two-wheeler loans 105%, affordable housing 37.8%, micro-LAP 21.6%, MSME 29.1%, NBFC lending 50% in Q4
items.quote: Gold loans at 237.6%. Kindly ignore the gross NPA of 2.7% on gold loans because that is technical in nature.

items.statement: Invested heavily in secured business headcount: affordable housing/micro-LAP sales staff doubled from 1,800 to 3,300 in FY25; investment already baked into cost base
items.quote: When we began March '24, the number of people who were in business, that is in sales, in affordable housing and micro-LAP was 1,800 people. I am finishing March '25 with 3,300 people in affordable housing and micro-LAP.

items.statement: Cost-to-income ratio worsened to 61.3% in FY25 from 57.4% due to unsecured revenue drop; target to return to 5x% in FY26 via digital productivity and no major headcount additions
items.quote: We have unfortunately this year have gone the wrong way; we have become 61.3%. The single biggest reason is, drop in revenue from unsecured. And that has really caused the income to compress from an unsecured perspective, so we really cannot address costs so quickly in the short-term. But let me assure you, we will come back to first-digit being 5 this financial year.

items.statement: Deposits grew 29% to Rs 29,120 cr; CD ratio 93.3% (82.9% with refinance); CASA grew 18% to Rs 5,235 cr with cost down to 4.36%; retail deposits grew 19%, bulk 48%
items.quote: 29% has been the deposit growth this year against the industry growth of 11%. Our deposits now stand at Rs. 29,120 crores and you will see our CD ratio is now down to 93.3%. If you add in the refinance, it is only 82.9%.

items.statement: Expect retail+CASA share to rise into 60s% in FY26 as liquidity improves and bulk deposit need diminishes; LCR to decline from 253% but remain healthy under new April 2026 norms
items.quote: But yes, should retail grow harder than bulk? Ideally, yes. And maybe this is the year we would say that because liquidity has become much better. Our segments, which we launched last year, are showing good results. CASA is showing it, retail is showing it. But because we did get a good opportunity on bulk growth, it does look like the retail number has gone down. But retail by itself has grown 19

items.statement: Refinance tenor extended to 5.6 years (from 4.7 years) via NABARD, NHB, SIDBI; surplus liquidity Rs 2,816 cr as of March 31
items.quote: Importantly, our refinance which we availed this year has increased our tenor of refinance to 5.6 years, roughly about 4.7 years last year.

items.statement: Capital adequacy improved to 20.7% (from 20.3%) without raising capital; driven by PAT, 28% guarantee coverage, and gold loan book; expect further strengthening without capital raise
items.quote: Our capital adequacy has moved upto 20.7%. It was 20.3% last year and we have not raised capital. It only tells you that we do not need to raise any more capital.

items.statement: RBI gold loan circular (75% LTV including interest) creates level playing field; converting part-time valuers to full-time and adding karatometers to expand gold business
items.quote: So, I think the impact is very positive because it says that all regulated entities, which includes NBFCs and banks, should have 75% loan to value, including the interest. And as you know, that was the difference between banks and NBFCs where NBFCs were able to do 75% without the interest, so I think there is a level playing field.

items.statement: BC book GNPA 12.7% and Agri GNPA 7.5% elevated due to shrinking denominators; BC book may surprise positively in FY26; MFI growth expected 3-5% conservatively
items.quote: So in that page, next to the GNPA is quarter-on-quarter growth, year-on-year growth. And you will see that both the BC book is in a decline and agri book is in a decline. So a lot of the gross NPA percentages you are referring to is because the denominator is also going down.

items.statement: Unsecured flow rate (gross slippages) Rs 309 cr in Q4 vs Rs 277 cr in Q3, driven by Karnataka; secured flow rate flat at ~Rs 150 cr
items.quote: Nidhesh, the unsecured flow rate was gross loan, not net, it's Rs. 309 crores, up from Rs. 277 crores in Quarter 3. And that was primarily to do with the Karnataka thing. And on secured, it remained very flat between Q3 and Q4 at around Rs. 150 crores.

items.statement: Regulatory provisions Rs 448 cr: ~Rs 280 cr for unsecured (30% of book), balance for secured; BC book FLDG absorbed ~Rs 120 cr provisioning
items.quote: Out of the Rs. 448 crores, roughly about Rs. 280 crores is for unsecured and the balance is for secured, so 280 is for 30% of the book and the balance is secured portion

items.statement: ARC sales done in FY25 on both secured and unsecured (mainly unsecured); provisioning identical for ARC and on-book; will use judiciously based on NPA flows
items.quote: Yes, we have done ARC sale this year, both on secured and unsecured. And mainly unsecured. As you know, the provisioning for an unsecured book with ARC or within the Bank has to be identical.

items.statement: DTA balance Rs 550 cr at FY25 end; final DTA utilization year FY27; expect Rs 20-40 cr addition in FY26; Rs 50-60 cr DTA lost due to FY25 PAT shortfall vs Rs 650-700 cr target
items.quote: Abhilash Sandur: Rs. 550 crores. Ajay Kanwal: Rs. 550 crores, yes.

items.statement: 98% digital account opening; three AI projects started for productivity, customer service, and front-end co-pilot; not baked into FY26 numbers
items.quote: Because if you are doing 98% account opening with digital, then there is 99% and 100% cannot be so important, right? So one thing I must tell you that we are fully focused on digital. I would like to share with you the progress of our AI projects, which I will do in the next quarter.

items.statement: MFI not fully sorted; staying on high alert; conservative growth 3-5% until environment cleaner; guarantee program cost baked into 30% PAT growth guidance
items.quote: But you and I should know that I do not think the MFI is sorted out as yet. It is still something to be on high alert for. And that is what we will be.

items.statement: Adjusted PAT (ex-accelerated provisions & DTA deferrals) Rs 779 cr in FY25; Q4 PAT Rs 120 cr vs Rs 105 cr YoY; operating margin Rs 293 cr vs Rs 279 cr YoY
items.quote: Now if you back out, more deferred tax asset year-on-year deferrals and the accelerated provision, our adjusted PAT should have been Rs. 779 crores.

items.statement: FY26 EBITDA guidance of INR5,500-6,000 crores
items.quote: We are projecting an EBITDA range of INR5,500 crores to INR6,000 crores, a substantial growth from FY25.

items.statement: Consolidated order book at INR47,000 crores including Waaree RTL
items.quote: Our order book remains robust at INR47,000 crores.

items.statement: INR9,000 crores capex for 6 GW integrated PLI project by 2027
items.quote: The PLI project, which is an integrated 6 gigawatts of ingots and wafers, cells and modules, that's the one which we would be commissioning by 2027. And that is on time. We are on time for that. And that's that, the capex for that, on your question for capex, that's around INR9,000 crores of capex that we'll be spending to get that done.

items.statement: Module capacity 15 GW; 5.4 GW cell factory operational; 1.6 GW US module facility operational; 3.2 GW Chikhli expansion in 3-4 months; 4.8 GW module addition by FY27; 6 GW wafer-cell-module PLI by 2027; 3.5 GW battery storage and 300 MW gre
items.quote: Our module manufacturing capacity now stands at 15 gigawatts, making us the largest in the country. Our 5.4 gigawatt cell factory was inaugurated during the year, also the largest of its kind in India. In the U.S., we operationalized 1.6 gigawatts manufacturing facility.

items.statement: FY25 EBITDA margin 21.04% vs 15.56% FY24; Q4 margin 25.59% up ~900 bps YoY; gross margin improving as raw material costs fall faster than prices
items.quote: EBITDA for the year stood at INR3,123 crores, representing a strong increase of 72.59% year-on-year with margins of 21.04%. Last year, the same margin was at 15.56%.

items.statement: Raw material cost % of revenue fell from ~68% to ~65% QoQ; total COGS margin improved from 29.3% to ~32%; cell cost internally ~7-8 cents vs 11.5-14 cents externally sourced
