items.quote: So, if you see the last quarter, we came in something like around 68% and this quarter we are something around 65%. And on a total COGS basis, if you see the margin has gone up, of course, like from 29.3% to about 32%.

items.statement: India solar demand to rise from ~35 GW/yr to 70 GW/yr by 2030; DCR market 3-4 GW last year, expected 10-15 GW this year; global demand rising from AI/data centers; pipeline ~100 GW modules, ~30 GW EPC
items.quote: In the next few years, the cumulative demand for solar will now will be 35, but by the time we get towards the end of the decade, it will go to 70 gigawatts. So that's a very, very strong demand.

items.statement: US revenue share 17-20% currently, expected to stay in 17-22% range; US module facility provides natural hedge against tariffs
items.quote: In the revenue stack that we have at this point in time, anywhere between 17% to 20% is U.S. bound, directionally. And so, as you can see, there's a very substantial 80% of our revenue coming from India market.

items.statement: Contract liabilities (customer advances) ~INR4,300-4,400 crores on balance sheet
items.quote: So Vishal, if you can just look at the contract liabilities on the balance sheet, that's indicative of the advance that mostly the advance is there sitting there, both in the current and the non-current section. So currently roughly about I can say around INR4,300 crores or INR4,400 crores is what we have as advances.

items.statement: ENEL acquisition equity commitment ~INR790 crores; IPP projects typically 65-70% debt, 25-30% equity
items.quote: We have committed an equity value of around INR790-odd crores of money plus there are other small pricing mechanism which shall uncover by the time we close the transaction which is expected probably within this quarter itself.

items.statement: Retail ~23-25% of revenue; utility ~60%+; DCR share rising with own cell production; TOPCon ramping, HJT niche
items.quote: Like I said directionally we have about 23% to 25% from our retail business.

items.statement: Order book split ~45% India, 55% overseas (mostly US); EPC customers wide basket, large institutional EPCs ~25%+
items.quote: Our order book at this point in time is roughly split about 47% from India or 45% from India and the rest overseas.

items.statement: Cell efficiency: mono PERC 23-23.5%, TOPCon pushing 24%; module capacity utilisation 60-90% across lines
items.quote: The efficiency of the cells for mono PERC, we are getting already in the region of 23%, 23.5%. for the TOPCon modules where the lines have just started, we are already pushing 24%.

items.statement: Benefiting from Make in India, PM Surya Ghar, PM Kusum, PLI; DCR policy driving domestic cell demand
items.quote: All of this has tailwinds of regulatory policies of Make in India, PM Surya Ghar Yojana, PM Kusum, and several other benefits like PLI.

items.statement: Execution risks: supply chain, logistics, power outages, collections, facility timelines/capex; tariff uncertainty managed via dual manufacturing footprint
items.quote: There are risks in terms of, supply chain, making sure that you get your material on time. There are risks associated with logistics. There are risks associated with power outages as you start manufacturing.

items.statement: ENEL acquisition in progress, expected to close this quarter; equity ~INR790 crores; 170 MW power infrastructure in development
items.quote: ENEL acquisition at this point in time is in progress. So the numbers that we have given, consider a very small portion of potential power infrastructure business, as we call it.

items.statement: INR15,550 crores funds available for capital deployment as of March 31
items.quote: And as of March 31, we had INR15,550 crores of funds available for capital deployment, a testament to our strong financial health.

items.statement: PAT target of INR800+ crores by FY27
items.quote: So, by FY '27, we expect a PAT of INR800-plus crores.

items.statement: Cash capex of INR600-700 crores for FY26 funded internally
items.quote: Cash capex will be around INR600 crores to INR700 crores.

items.statement: Specialty carbon black expansion from 60,000 to 130,000 MTPA at Singur operational by Q3 FY26
items.quote: At Singur, our work on brownfield expansion of special ity carbon black line from 60,000 metric ton per an num to 130,000 metric ton per annum is progressing as planned and is expected to be operational by Q3 FY '26

items.statement: Overall carbon black capacity to reach 250,000 MTPA making it world's largest single-site specialty carbon black facility
items.quote: This will take our overall carbon black capacity from 180,000 metric ton per annum to 250,000 metric ton per annum, which will make this the sing le largest site for specialty carbon black facility in the world

items.statement: Anthraquinone and carbazole specialty product line scheduled for Q2 FY27
items.quote: The high value-added specialty product line is scheduled to go live in Q2 FY'27.

items.statement: LFP cathode plant capex of INR1,130 crores with INR300 crores in FY26 and balance in FY27
items.quote: I think INR300 crores will be in FY '26 and balance, most of it will be in FY '27.

items.statement: LFP cathode active material plant first phase 40,000 MTPA operational by Q3 FY27 targeting 200,000 MTPA by 2030
items.quote: Our vision is to build a capacity of 200,000 metric ton per annum of electric cathode active material plant sufficient to power 100 gigawatt per hour of lithium-ion batteries with the first phase of 40,000 metric ton per annum expected to be operational by Q3 FY '27.

items.statement: LFP segment first full year revenue of INR2,200-2,400 crores at full capacity utilization
items.quote: So in first full year of operations, it will have a top line of around INR2,200 crores to INR2,400 crores at full capacity utilization.

items.statement: Strong order book and contractual agreements for carbon black for next 2-3 years
items.quote: With our order book and our contractual agreements, we are placed in a very good situation for next 2 to 3 years, clearly.

items.statement: Specialty carbon black margins range from INR20,000-50,000 per ton depending on grade and application
items.quote: specialty carbon black margin differs from 20,000 to 50,000, depending on what grade you are producing, what application you are selling to.

items.statement: Volume trajectory expected to hold and grow further in FY26
items.quote: Yes, definitely, we expect the volume trajectory to hold on and grow further.

items.statement: Tyre sector concentration less than 25% of carbon black volumes
items.quote: So tyres in our case is less than 25%.

items.statement: Focus shifting to value-added products like high-purity naphthalene and specialty carbon black reducing volumes but increasing profitability
items.quote: So value-added products are naphthalene of high purity that we are making. That is one of the very critical products for us. And other than that, specialty carbon black. So, when you convert from commodity to different grades of specialty, the volume comes down.

items.statement: Cost of goods sold reduced 10% from INR63,820 to INR57,080 per ton in FY25
items.quote: So if you look at FY '24, the cost of goods sold were INR63,820. And this year, it is INR57,080. So it has come down by 10%.

items.statement: Birla Tyres acquisition with Dalmia Bharat Refractories; modernization underway with phased operations from end of Q1 FY26
items.quote: Modernization and revamping efforts are well underway with operations set to begin in phases starting end of Q1 FY'26.

items.statement: Birla Tyres capacity 400 TPD to be ramped over 3-4 years; initial focus on agri, mining, bias commercial tyres
items.quote: total capacity as on date is 400 TPD. Nishant Agarwal: 400. Anurag Choudhary: Different types of tyres. And we expect to ramp this up in the next 3 to 4 years' time

items.statement: Birla Tyres revenue expected from H2 FY26 with major revenue from FY27
items.quote: For second half of this financial year, you'll see some revenue coming in. But I think major revenue will start coming from the next year.

items.statement: ROCE reached 34% in FY25
items.quote: Our return on capital employed has also shown a steady upward trajectory, reaching 34% in FY '25, a testament to our sharp focus on value creation and

items.statement: Net positive cash balance of INR371 crores as of March 31, 2025
items.quote: As of 31 st March 2025, we hold a net positive cash balance of INR371 crores, which gives us ample fle xibilities to pursue growth opportunities while maintaining a prudent approach to capital allocation

items.statement: Dividend of INR0.60 per share (60% of face value) proposed for FY25
items.quote: share of INR1 each, which represents 60% of the face value for the financial year 2024-'25. This is subject to the approval of our shareholders.

items.statement: Business model not dependent on opportunistic China or Russia sanctions-driven markets; focused on sustainable long-term specialty relationships
items.quote: Our business model and business that we have built is not based on opportunities. So unlike other companies, a lot of companies being impacted with what China is doing. And you will be pleased to know that there is no impact of China on Himadri business model.

items.statement: LFP samples approved by OEMs; commercial MOUs to follow after demo plant sample approval
items.quote: No, not yet, but the samples have been approved. So what is the stage? Second, we have to sell -- send the samples to them from demo plant. And once that is approved, then the commerc ial plant, there will not be much time required for approving from commercial plant. So post that, only the MOU will be

items.statement: LFP Phase 1 focus more on exports; Himadri to be only commercial manufacturer outside China
items.quote: More of exports. Domestic, whatever material will be there, requirement will be there, we'll be meeting that. We'll be the only commercial manufacturer. And then we'll be growing our capacity depending on the domestic and international market, which will be huge.

items.statement: Board vision to achieve Rs 15,000 crore topline on group basis by 2030 through organic growth and strategic acquisitions
items.quote: The Greaves Board had set itself a vision to achieve Rs. 15,000 crore topline on a group basis by 2030 through a blend of organic growth and strategic acquisitions and the management of Greaves Cotton and Greaves Electric Mobility remain committed to the same.

items.statement: Parag Satpute appointed as Managing Director & Group CEO with 29 years experience in mobility and manufacturing sectors
items.quote: I wanted to take a moment to welcome Mr. Parag Satpute sitting here with me on the table as our new Managing Director and Group CEO for Greaves Cotton.

items.statement: Consolidated revenue Rs 2,918 crore for FY25 with standalone revenue growing 12% YoY to Rs 1,988 crore
items.quote: Moving to the full Financial Year 2025, consolidated revenues reach ed Rs. 2,918 crore, backed by strong contributions across all our business verticals

items.statement: Standalone EBITDA Rs 260 crore for FY25 with combined GCL and Excel EBITDA at Rs 338 crore and 15% margin
items.quote: The combined EBITDA of GCL and Excel stood at Rs. 338 crore with a margin at a healthy 15%.

items.statement: Engineering and Retail divisions revenue grew 14% and 7% annually respectively in FY25
items.quote: Engineering and Retail divisions continue their growth trajectory with revenues growing annually by 14% and 7%, respectively.

items.statement: Electric Mobility division posted revenues of Rs 659 crore for FY25 driven by new model launches and growing consumer demand
items.quote: Our Electric Mobility division posted revenues of Rs. 659 crore for Financial Year 2025, driven by the launch of new models, improved channel efficiencies and growing consumer demand.

items.statement: Genset market share improved from approximately 2.7% to around 4% over last 6-8 quarters
items.quote: In gensets, our market share had been in the region of approximately 2.7% some time back. And we currently are below 4% or around 4%.

items.statement: Rs 100 crore capex outlay planned for Excel Controlinkage over 3-4 years with ongoing de-bottlenecking initiatives
items.quote: We have outlaid almost Rs. 100 crore capex plan when we invested in this Company and this was something that we were planning to undertake over a 3 to 4-year period.

items.statement: Excel plant overall utilization approximately more than 80% with some pieces at 60-70% and others at 90% plus
items.quote: So, this is an ongoing journey, but we would be approximately at an overall level more than 80% of plant utilization.

items.statement: Consistently deploying Rs 80-100 crore capex annually into standalone business for new production lines, automation and de-bottlenecking
items.quote: We will outlay approximately Rs. 100 crore capex even in the coming year for our internal growth purpose.

items.statement: Near zero debt balance sheet supported by standalone cash reserves of Rs 379 crore
items.quote: We continue to operate with a near zero debt balance sheet supported by standalone cash reserves of Rs. 379 crore.

items.statement: Return on capital employed for FY25 stands at healthy 19%
items.quote: Our return on capital employed for FY25 stands at a healthy 19 % each, underscoring our capital efficient growth approach

items.statement: GEML electric two-wheeler market share increased from 3.4% to 4.3% in Q4 FY25 with Vahan registration growing 15% QoQ
items.quote: Our Vahan registration grew by 15% quarter-on-quarter, resulting in an increase in our electric two-wheeler market share from 3.4% to 4.3% in this quarter.

items.statement: GEML FY25 revenues grew 7.4% YoY driven by e2-wheeler volume growth of 10% and L5 segment growth of 61%
items.quote: In terms of annual update, our revenues in FY25 grew by 7.4% year-on-year, driven by volume growth in the e2-wheeler at 10% and L5 segment at 61% year-on-year.

items.statement: L5 diesel market share increased from 1.2% in FY24 to 3.7% in FY25
items.quote: Also note our market share increased from 1.2% in FY24 to 3.7% in FY25 in the L5 diesel segment.

items.statement: Launched three electric two-wheelers in FY25: Ampere Nexus, Magnus Neo, and Ampere Reo
items.quote: This year, we introduced three electric two-wheelers, new two-wheelers, Ampere Nexus, Magnus Neo, and Ampere R eo, each engineered to be safe, smart, stylish, and affordable

items.statement: Launched Ampere Reo 80 at Rs 59,900 for mass market students and senior citizens
items.quote: Continuing our commitment to affordability and access, this quarter we launched the Ampere Reo 80 at Rs. 59,900, an electric scooter designed for mass market in India - students and senior citizens.

items.statement: Partnership with Indofast Energy for battery swapping for fleet operators and shared mobility platforms
items.quote: This quarter also saw a strategic milestone, our partnership with Indofast Energy to enable battery swapping for fleet operators and shared Mobility platforms.

items.statement: GEML filed DRHP dated December 23, 2024 for proposed IPO subject to SEBI approvals and market conditions
items.quote: As you are aware, we have filed a draft red herring prospectus dated December 23rd, 2024, for a proposed initial public offering, which is subjected to receipt of regulatory approvals from the SEBI, market conditions and other commercial considerations.

items.statement: Subsidy currently at Rs 2,500 per kWh capped at Rs 5,000 per vehicle for two-wheelers and Rs 5,000 per kWh capped at Rs 25,000 for L5 three-wheelers extended for full financial year
items.quote: The subsidy presently is at Rs. 2,500 per kWh on two-wheeler which is capped at Rs. 5,000 per vehicle. And on the L5 three-wheeler it is at Rs. 5,000 per kWh capped at Rs. 25,000 per vehicle.

items.statement: Working towards subsidy-free environment focusing on product value proposition, quality, reliability and after-sales service
items.quote: We are working towards a subsidy-free environment where it is the value proposition of the product and the consumer connect which you build through your quality, reliability and after sales service, where we will be able to compete.

items.statement: New EV products Nexus, Magnus Neo, and Reo are profitable at standalone basis, building volumes to meet fixed and variable expenses
items.quote: the new products we have launched – Nexus, Magnus, Neo, and R eo have been received very well. And they are all profitable at a standalone basis

items.statement: Electric powertrain business manufactures motor and motor controller for L3 and L5 segments at Aurangabad with secured OE clients
items.quote: By electric powertrain, we specifically refer to both the motor and the motor controller. The motor, as you know, is a very critical prime mover, critical component for the entire e-powertrain.

items.statement: GEML has 600+ touchpoints, own EV financing platform evfin, and growing digital infrastructure for consumers and channel partners
items.quote: We have also made meanin gful strides in customer service support with 600 plus touchpoints, our own EV financing platform, evfin, and a growing digital infrastructure that supports both consumers and channel partners

items.statement: GEML holds 15% market share in Tamil Nadu and strong presence in South and East India, focusing on building brand visibility in North and West
items.quote: Our market share in South India and Eastern India are relatively higher than in the North and West. So, that's part of our action plan in terms of developing these markets.

items.statement: Hydrogen technology concept showcased at Bharat Mobility Global Expo in Jan 2025 as incubating project
items.quote: On the hydrogen, that was more a concept which we had launched in the Bharat Mobility and that we will be looking at an incubating project and also will work with other players in the market.

items.statement: Aerospace and defence focus area for Excel with Engineering business certified as tier two supplier for aerospace components
items.quote: Aerospace and defen ce, this is something that we have initiated. Excel does some work in both these areas and that is a focus area for us in the next year to continue

items.statement: DRHP filing constrains forward-looking statements on EV profitability, burn rate, and quarterly guidance
items.quote: Going forward on the profitability part, as you are aware, we are waiting regulatory clearances from SEBI on our DRHP. So, I think I would constrain myself from giving any forward-looking statements as we have already mentioned it in our DRHP in detail.

items.statement: Management confident of strong double-digit growth across retail portfolio in FY26
items.quote: Overall, we remain confident of delivering strong double-digit growth across our retail portfolio in FY26 underpinned by sustained demand, proactive planning and the continuing evolution of our brand and experience proposition.

items.statement: Material office leasing expected in FY26 with 1.2-1.4 million sq ft pipeline
items.quote: I think in terms of leasing, Puneet, you will see material leasing happening in FY26, especially I think if I add the pipeline that are under active discussions between Pune, Bangalore and Chennai, we are talking about 1.2 to 1.4 million sq. ft. of leasing discussions going on across these three new offices and we should see significant conversions during this year.

items.statement: Annual construction CAPEX of Rs 1,000-1,200 crores for next 5 years
items.quote: I think this will be maintained even for next five years for sure. I mean of course this will, I mean any other acquisition or a bigger FSI purchase will be over and above that but on a construction side the number should be restricted to around Rs. 1,200 crores every year for next 5 years.

items.statement: April 2025 retailer sales expected to cross Rs 1,130 crores, up 14% YoY
items.quote: April is typically a lean month, but we have continued to see strong momentum in retail sales, with retailer sales expected to cross Rs. 1,130 crores for this month. This reflects a 14 % year-on-year growth, and to our minds, it confirms the depth and consistency of consumer demand across our portfolio.

items.statement: Like-for-like consumption growth across portfolio exceeded 8% in Q4 FY25
items.quote: Importantly even excluding the newly launched malls in FY24, like -for-like consumption growth across the portfolio stood in excess of 8% underscoring the sustained strength of our discretionary retail ecosystem.

items.statement: Retail EBITDA grew 20% to over Rs 2,000 crores in FY25
items.quote: Reflecting this momentum in consumption, retail income for FY25 rose 18% to Rs. 1,951 crores, and EBITDA grew by 20% to over Rs. 2,000 crores for the year.

items.statement: Hotel portfolio EBITDA grew 11% to Rs 266 crores with 46% margin in FY25
items.quote: The hotel portfolio has delivered a strong performance once again this year with income rising to Rs. 580 crores up 6% year-on-year and EBITDA is growing by 11% to Rs. 266 crores reflecting an overall healthy margin of 46%.

items.statement: Pre-leasing pipeline of over 500,000 sq ft at Millennium Towers Pune
items.quote: Pre-leasing activity is underway with an active pipeline of over 500,000 sq. ft. in discussions at this moment.

items.statement: Pre-leasing conversations for almost 800,000 sq ft across Bangalore and Chennai offices
items.quote: Between Bangalore (Phoenix Asia Towers) and Chennai (One National Park), we have pre-leasing conversations ongoing for almost 800,000 sq. ft.

items.statement: FY25 aggregate CAPEX of Rs 2,600 crores including Rs 1,600 crores for land and FSI
items.quote: Our aggregate CAPEX in FY25 was around Rs. 2,600 crores. Out of this , around Rs. 1,600 crores has been invested in th ree land parcels, namely Coimbatore, Chandigarh, and Bangalore i.e. Mittal Land and the FSI, which we have bought recently in the Lower Parel area and around Rs. 1,000 crores we have incurred toward s the construction at various places across the country and to densify our growth

items.statement: Secured additional FSI of 136,000 sq meters at Lower Parel for Rs 586 crores in Q4 FY25
items.quote: We have secured FSI of approx. 136,000 sq. meters for a premium payment of approx. Rs. 586 crores during Q4 FY25.

items.statement: Target to add 7 million sq ft retail leasable area by 2030, taking portfolio to 18 million sq ft
items.quote: We are looking to add around 7 million sq. ft. of leasable area to our operational retail portfolio by 2030. This will take us from 11.5 million to around over 18 million sq. ft. in the retail side.

items.statement: Phoenix MarketCity Bangalore adding 170,000 sq ft third floor operational by end of FY26
items.quote: We are also adding and operationalizing the 3rd floor in Bangalore during this year, second half of this year which is new retail area of about 170,000 sq. ft.

items.statement: Phoenix Palladium Rise 2 West Zone 250,000 sq ft fully operational by June 2025
items.quote: There is the new zone that we have added which is Rise 2 (Phoenix Palladium West Zone) which is about 250,000 sq. ft. and which should become fully operational by June of this year.

items.statement: Phoenix Palladium Rise 1 and revamp to add 350,000 sq ft over next 2 years
items.quote: So it is, in aggregate, you would have another 350,000 sq. ft. of additional retail area in Phoenix Palladium.

items.statement: Revamping Phoenix MarketCity malls to improve brand mix with premium categories
items.quote: We are prioritizing right -sizing, relocations and churn aimed at bringing in new -age anchors while also creating space for premium categories across jewelry, watches, cosmetics and accessories as well as new fine-dining experiences.

items.statement: Bershka first India store at Phoenix Palladium achieved highest single day sales globally
items.quote: For Quarter 4, a remarkable standout moment was the launch of Bershka's first store in India, which incidentally also achieved the highest sing le day sales globally for this brand on opening day.

items.statement: 70-75% of tenants currently hitting revenue share threshold
items.quote: So, Varun, typically about 70% to 75% of the tenant mix hit the revenue share threshold. Now revenue share is payable when the revenue share component crosses the fixed rent component. So from that perspective, I would say that about 75% of the tenants are right now hitting the revenue share threshold at this point in time.

items.statement: Gross debt stable at Rs 4,400 crores, net debt to EBITDA at 1.2x
items.quote: Importantly, despite these deployments, gross debt at the group level remain s at the same level as compared to last year. So , we are around Rs. 4,400 crores, which is lower than FY20 levels, i.e pre-COVID levels. So, we are still fully in control in terms of debt and our net debt to EBITDA ratio is around 1.2x.

items.statement: Cost of debt reduced from 9.2% to 8.5% over last few years
items.quote: We are putting a lot of efforts to reduce the cost of the debt which has come down from 9.2% to 8.5% in the last few years.

items.statement: Retailer sales across malls reached Rs 13,750 crores, up 21% YoY in FY25
items.quote: Retailer sales across our malls reached Rs. 13,750 crores, which is a 21 % increase over FY24.

items.statement: St Regis Mumbai revenue crossed Rs 500 crores for first time at Rs 523 crores in FY25
items.quote: The St. Regis, Mumbai continues to set the benchmark for experience and luxury in Lower Parel crossing Rs. 500 crores in income to reach Rs. 523 crores overall in revenue.

items.statement: St Regis Mumbai RevPAR up 13% and occupancy at 86% in FY25
items.quote: This was driven by a 13 % increase in revenue per available room and an impressive occupancy rate of 86%, up 3 percentage points over FY24.

items.statement: Indore mall access constrained by highway construction, improvement expected in 12 months
items.quote: There is a bit of a constraint in access to the mall at this point in time, but with the highway activities scheduled to be completed in the next 12 months, we believe that access to the mall will improve multi -fold, and we should see very strong growth in consumption going forward in Indore in FY27 and beyond.

items.statement: Residential launches planned for Tower 8,9 at One Bangalore West and Alipore Kolkata in FY26 Q2-Q3
items.quote: We continue to evaluate the timing and approach for future residential launches, including Tower 8 and 9 at One Bangalore West and our Alip ore project in Kolkata , and both of these projects are scheduled to launch during FY26, maybe in the Q2 and Q3 around that time.

items.statement: FY26 credit growth target 2-3% above industry growth
items.quote: If you see the visibility, we would be 2%-3% more than the credit growth.

items.statement: FY26 NIM guidance 3.5-3.7%
items.quote: Yes, I will confirm we will be around 3.5-3.7. This is what we are looking at and 2%-3% more than the industry growth is what we are looking at if the visibility is good for the current year.

items.statement: FY26 slippages target Rs 650-700 crore with recoveries exceeding slippages
items.quote: So we gave a guidance of Rs. 800 crores for the current year and we closed at Rs. 815 and for the next year, we will be around Rs. 650-Rs. 700 crores. That is the number we are looking at. But in terms of provisions, we will also have, D1, doubtful 1 to doubtful 2 extra provisions we will have for the year which we may have to take. Otherwise, we are quite confident of recovery, will be more than

items.statement: FY26 cost-to-income ratio expected 48-50%
items.quote: We said that we will be around 48-50 this year, number one.

items.statement: FY26 retail portfolio exit target Rs 3,000 crore
items.quote: So to be precise, we are looking to exit this year with Rs. 3,000 crores. Rs. 3,000 crores should be the exit number for retail for this year as we speak.

items.statement: FY26 branch expansion target 50-75 new branches
items.quote: We had been consistently opening about 50-75 every year except during the COVID years. So this year, from 875, probably we will be taking it to about another 50-75 basis points, 75 branches. If let us say, things are favorable, we may also open few more branches.

items.statement: Q4 FY25 NIM 3.60%, full year FY25 NIM 3.60%
items.quote: Our NIM for Q4 FY '25 stood at 3.60% as compared to 3.58% in Q3 FY '25. For the full Financial Year FY '25, NIM is at 3.60%.

items.statement: Yield on advances increased 12 bps sequentially to 9.93% in Q4 FY25
items.quote: Our yield on advance stood at 9.93% for Q4 FY '25 as against 9.81% in Q3 FY '25, which is increase of 12 bps sequentially.

items.statement: Cost of deposits 6.02% in Q4 FY25 vs 5.75% in Q4 FY24; full year FY25 5.85% vs 5.59%
items.quote: The cost of deposit stood at 6.02% for Q4 FY '25 versus 5.75% in Q4 FY '24 and for the full year FY '25, the same was 5.85% compared to 5.59% last year.

items.statement: Gold loans migrated from floating to fixed rate in July 2024 to cushion against rate cuts
items.quote: In addition, with respect to gold loans, we have migrated to fixed rate from floating rate as we envisage decreasing interest cycle rate, and these measures will act as a cushion during decreasing interest rate cycle.

items.statement: Savings bank rate cut 25 bps in February 2025, term deposit rates cut in April 2025
items.quote: During the middle of the quarter, we have also decreased our Savings Bank rate by 25 bps and during the month of April, we have reduced our term deposit rate in line with the reduction in repo rates.

items.statement: FY25 gross advances grew 14% to Rs 53,066 crore from Rs 46,481 crore
items.quote: For FY 2025, we have registered 14% growth on our gross advances. We have increased to Rs. 53,066 crores from Rs. 46,481 crores for the Financial Year '24.

items.statement: FY25 deposits grew 14% to Rs 63,526 crore; CASA grew to Rs 18,119 crore (29% of deposits)
items.quote: Our deposits have also increased by 14% and stood at Rs. 63,526 crores for FY '25 as compared to Rs. 55,657 crores for FY '24. The CASA has increased from Rs. 17,050 crores to Rs. 18,119 crores in FY '25. CASA-to-total-deposit stood at 29%.

items.statement: CD ratio at 84%, targeting 85% LDR for FY26
items.quote: Based on the same, our CD ratio stands at 84%. The cost of deposit stood at 6.02% for Q4 FY '25 versus 5.75% in Q4 FY '24 and for the full year FY '25, the same was 5.85% compared to 5.59% last year.

items.statement: FY25 slippages Rs 815 crore (1.54%) vs Rs 800 crore guidance; Q4 slippages Rs 229 crore, recoveries Rs 291 crore
items.quote: We had said that we are aiming for approximately Rs. 800 crores of slippages for this financial year at the beginning of the year and we have stick to that and we have ended up this financial year with Rs. 815 crores of slippages, which is 1.54% against 2.18% of last year.

items.statement: FY25 gross NPA 3.09% (down 90 bps), net NPA 1.25% (down 72 bps), PCR without technical write-offs 60% (up from 52%)
items.quote: We closed the gross NPA last financial year at 3.99% and now, we have closed at 3.09%, which is 90 bps reduction from the last financial year. Similarly, our net NPA number had reduced to Rs. 653 crores in FY 2025 as against Rs. 899 crores in FY 2024, which is 1.97% in Q4 FY '24 and 1.25% in the current quarter, which is 72 bps reduction for the year.

items.statement: SMA-2 to total advances 1.10% in Q4 FY25 vs 2.08% a year ago
items.quote: Overall SMA-2 to total advance stands at 1.10% in Q4 FY '25 as compared to 2.08% in the similar period last year. We could see substantial improvement in SMA and slippage numbers.

items.statement: FY25 total recoveries Rs 1,042 crore (Rs 834 crore live NPA + Rs 208 crore written-off)
items.quote: The total recovery for FY '25 is Rs. 1,042 crores. splitted into Rs. 834 crores of live NPA and Rs. 208 crores from technically written-off accounts as against Rs. 1,031 crores in FY '24 which is Rs. 816 crores is from live NPA and Rs. 215 crores is from technically written-off accounts.

items.statement: FY25 ROA 1.55% (above long-term 1.5% average), ROE 12.6% in Q4 FY25
items.quote: Our ROA for the year, FY '25 is at 1.55% compared to 1.52% in the last financial year. Our ROA for all the 4 quarters of FY '25 is above 1.5%, which is our long-term average. ROE stood at 12.6% for Q4 FY '25 as compared to 12.39% in Q4 FY '24.

items.statement: FY25 cost-to-income ratio 47.77% (better than 48-50% guidance)
items.quote: Our cost-to-income ratio for FY '25 is at 47.77% as against the expectation of 48%-50%.

items.statement: MSME outstanding growth 23% in FY25; digital lending (Newgen) driving growth with <Rs 7.5 cr decisions largely system-driven
items.quote: Actually speaking, the outstanding MSME growth was 23% for the current Financial Year.

items.statement: Gold loan book growing comfortably; retail secured (home loan, LAP) hitting double-digit blended yields
items.quote: I don't think so. I think we should be comfortable in growing this book at this rate.

items.statement: Personal loans Rs 1,200 crore are secured loans to existing MSME borrowers, not unsecured
items.quote: This is not an unsecured loan. This is a loan given to my existing borrowers or MSME under the personal loan headline, which also collateral with us.

items.statement: Exited Rs 1,250 crore low-yield IBPC (6-6.5%) and NBFC advances (8-8.5%) in FY25, Rs 750 crore in Q4
items.quote: This growth we have achieved after we have decided not to renew IBPC to the tune of Rs. 1,100 crores and we have also let go of low yielding NBFC funding to the tune of Rs. 150 crores which is approximately Rs. 1,250 crores of reduction in advance, of which Rs. 750 crores of reduction has come in Q4 FY 2025.

items.statement: EBLR portfolio 48% of exposure; first 25 bps repo cut passed in February, second 25 bps cut in early May
items.quote: Overall, we have around 48% of total exposure to EBLR. So the first rate cut of 25 bps, we have passed out and the second rate cut of 25, we are going to do it in this week.

items.statement: Retail hiring largely done (Sales Head, Zonal Heads, Credit Risk Heads, feet on street); branch-based affordable home loan strategy, DSA only for LAP in North/West/South
items.quote: Broadly, home loans will be a brand sourcing. Only for LAP, North and West and some part of South where in Tamil Nadu we plan to do a DSA sourcing for loan against property. Otherwise, AHL is broadly a branch-based strategy where the branch will sell the affordable home loans to their customers or new to bank customers with the existing retail set up.

items.statement: Dividend recommended Rs 2 per share (200% of face value Rs 1) for FY25 vs 150% last year
items.quote: The Board of Directors recommended a dividend of Rs. 2 per share on the face value of Rs. 1 per equity share at 200% for the year ended 31st March 2025, subject to the approval by the shareholders in the ensuing Annual General Meeting. Last year, it was 150%.

items.statement: V. Ramesh appointed Executive Director effective Feb 21, 2025 post RBI approval; bank now has two Whole-Time Directors besides MD & CEO
items.quote: We are glad to inform you that based on the approval accorded by RBI on February 14th, 2025, the Board of Directors of the Bank had appointed Shri. V. Ramesh as the Executive Director on the Board of the Bank with effect from February 21st, 2025.

items.statement: Tamil Nadu coercive loan recovery bill not applicable to RBI-regulated entities; no operational impact expected
items.quote: Yes, this law doesn't apply to RBI regulated entities, you are right, particularly for the banks. So we don't anticipate any, let us say, issue because of this law, any new impact because of this.

items.statement: Credit growth outlook assumes stable economic environment without geopolitical turbulence; 2-3% above industry growth on 'as is where is' basis
items.quote: We are making this assumption on 'as is where is basis', subject to current economic environment continues without any turbulence or geopolitical tension we can improve growth by few more points as well.

items.statement: Credit growth target 14-15% for FY26
items.quote: Sir, credit growth for this year also, we would like to grow at around 14% to 15%. That will continue.

items.statement: Deposit growth target 12-13% for FY26
items.quote: We have got our strategy in place and our plan is to grow deposit to the tune of 12% to 13% in this financial year.

items.statement: Cost-to-income ratio target around 42% by end of FY26
items.quote: And going forward, since income is increasing, we are expecting to maintain it at around 44% or maybe 100 or 200 bps lower than that, around 42% by the end of this year.

items.statement: CASA growth target around 10% for FY26
items.quote: The plan which is there for CASA growth is around 10%, that is what we are looking at.

items.statement: NIM target around 3.50% for FY26
items.quote: NIM, we are looking at maintaining at around 3.50%. There will be some pressure. And I think around 3.5% we'll be able to maintain at year-end.

items.statement: CD ratio target around 80-81% for FY26
items.quote: We'll try to maintain it around 80%, 81%, sir.

items.statement: Recovery target INR4,500 crores for FY26
items.quote: For this year, our recovery target is around INR4,500 crores for the entire year.

items.statement: ROA target to maintain 1.12% and improve by few bps by end of FY26
items.quote: We will try to maintain it. And by the end of this financial year, we'll try to improve it by an additional some few basis points.

items.statement: Branch expansion target above 100 new branches for FY26
items.quote: And this year also, the guideline -- the guidance is that we will try to open new branches at new centers, which should be matching to this number above any -- it can be any number above 100.

items.statement: IT budget INR1,700 crores plus for FY26
items.quote: This year, we have got the budget approved from the Board amounting to INR1,700 crores plus.

items.statement: Shift to new tax regime expected in last quarter of FY26
items.quote: We will be maybe last quarter of this financial year. In this year, we will be shifting to new tax regime.

items.statement: MTNL account INR2,332 crores became NPA in Q4 FY25
items.quote: INR2,332 crores of MTNL account became NPA in February this year in Q4.

items.statement: Excluding MTNL, FY25 slippages INR1,200 crores lower than previous year INR1,500 crores
items.quote: If you take that out, then total slippage for the entire year is INR1,200 crores only, which is lower than the previous year slippage of INR1,500 crores.

items.statement: GNPA reduced to INR5,348 crores, NNPA to INR912 crores (0.37%) as of March 2025
items.quote: Gross NPA reduced from INR 6794 Crores to INR 5348 Crores year on year basis. So net NPA reduced from INR 1,217 crores to INR 912 crores. So percentage-wise, it has come to 0.37% this time.

items.statement: PCR improved to 97.30% as of March 2025
items.quote: PCR, provision coverage ratio has increased to 97.30% as on 31st March as compared to 96.85% last year.

items.statement: Total recovery from NPA INR4,014 crores in FY25
items.quote: Total recovery from NPA during the quarter is INR 992.33 crores and the year-on-year, it is INR4,014 crores.

items.statement: No other corporate accounts under stress besides MTNL
items.quote: During the quarter and during the year also, we do not see any other account under stress, corporate.

items.statement: Cost of deposits 5.08% for FY25
items.quote: Cost of deposit increased to 5.08% for this year.

items.statement: Yield on advances improved to 8.82% due to RAM segment margin
items.quote: And yield on advances improved to 8.8 2%, mainly due to the improved margin from the RAM segment.

items.statement: Yield on investments improved to 6.83% due to high yield securities
items.quote: After that this yield on investment improved to 6.83% due to planned investment in high yield security.

items.statement: Business mix crossed INR5,61,000 crores with 11.30% YoY growth
items.quote: Bank has achieved a business mix of INR5,61,000 crores. First time, it has crossed INR5,50,000 crores and recording a year-on-year growth of 11.30%.

items.statement: Gross advances grew 14.15% YoY to INR2,50,019 crores
items.quote: Gross advance grown year-on-year basis by 14.15% is INR2,50,019 crores against the INR2,19,018 crores last year.

items.statement: Total deposits grew 9.11% YoY to INR3,11,939 crores
items.quote: Total deposit growth achieved at INR3,11,939 crores as on 31st March with a growth percentage of 9.11%.

items.statement: CASA grew 8.49% YoY to INR1,36,161 crores
items.quote: Then CASA also grown by INR1,36,161 crores with year-on-year growth of 8.49%.

items.statement: Overseas book growing 12-14% YoY
items.quote: They are growing around 12%, 13%, 14% year-on-year.

items.statement: ROA crossed 1% for first time at 1.12% in Q4 FY25
items.quote: Return on asset of March '25 is 1.12%. So first time we had crossed 1%. Earlier, it was less than 1%.

items.statement: ROE inched up to 16.28% in FY25
items.quote: Return on equity also inched up to 16.28%.

items.statement: Cost-to-income ratio improved to 47.14% in FY25 from 56%
items.quote: Cost-to-income ratio was 47.14% as compared to last year, so that 918 bps.

items.statement: Q4 FY25 cost-to-income ratio 44.35%
items.quote: We are at 44.35% for quarter ended March '25.

items.statement: Net profit grew 25.56% YoY to INR3,335 crores in FY25
items.quote: And net profit of the bank year-on-year basis, it has increased by 25.56% to INR3,335 crores.

items.statement: Operating profit grew 28.44% YoY to INR8,688 crores in FY25
items.quote: Bank has shown an operating profit of INR8,688 crores, registering a growth of 28.44%.

items.statement: Q4 FY25 net profit INR1,051 crores highest in bank's history
items.quote: December quarter's net profit was INR874 crores. That was the highest for the bank in its history. And this quarter, we have gone -- we have done better than that and INR1,051 crores of net profit has happened.

items.statement: CRAR improved to 19.74% after QIP of INR1,437 crores
items.quote: Capital adequacy ratio due to that we had gone for QIP, first we had generated INR1,437 crores. So this has increased to 19.74% as against the 11.50% mandatory requirement from the earlier.

items.statement: CRAR sufficient for 3 years credit growth, further capital raise for MPS compliance
items.quote: Our CRAR is at 19.74%. And this CRAR can take care of our 3 years credit growth comfortably. So for CRAR purpose, we do not need capital that is very true. The fact is that the Government of India shareholding is -- was 96% in the bank. And in the month of February, we raised INR1,400 crores of capital through QIP process, and that reduced Government of India shareholding to 94%. And going forward

items.statement: RBI penalty INR31 lakhs for jewel loan classification error
items.quote: Regarding penalty, I have to convey is that it is jewel loan and the classification of jewel loan was -- there was some, I will say, wrong calculat ion on the part of the bank regarding Indian Overseas Bank May 02, 2025 classification of jewel loan and that was corrected. And because of that technical issue, this penalty of INR31 lakhs has come on the

items.statement: Lakshya project launched for performance management, skill upgradation, leadership development
items.quote: There's a Lakshya project, which has been started, which is revamping the entire performance management system, u pgrading the skills, leadership development

items.statement: RLR cut 25 bps due to RBI repo rate reduction, automatic transmission

items.statement: No long-term debt on books; ample working capital limits; growth financed through internal accruals
items.quote: There is no long -term debt on t he books, and we remain comfortable on the cash front with ample working capital limits available to leverage future growth, which will be financed through internal accruals

items.statement: GST credit accumulation increased by INR 14-20 crores in FY25 due to reverse charge on rentals and capex GST; difficult to utilize for growing business
items.quote: And in fact, in this year, there's been an added complexity being added by the government in terms of the reverse charge on rentals for smaller landlords as well. So that balance continues to grow.

items.statement: ESOP expense INR 16 crores in FY25 (1% of revenue); normalized run-rate INR 8-10 crores annually; performance-linked over 4 years targeting 20% YoY growth
items.quote: ESOP expense for the quarter accounted for almost 1% of revenues and 0.5% of revenues for the full year.

items.statement: Manpower cost up 45% YoY due to ESOP and sales incentives; differentiated service model requires higher staffing vs hypermarket peers
items.quote: The manpower cost for the quarter was up by 45%, mainly due to the increased ESOP expense and increased sales incentives, which were in line with sales growth.

items.statement: Competitors opening stores aggressively in V-Mart markets; organized retail share rising from 15% to 30-35% in Tier 2/3 towns
items.quote: Everybody has some plans to open up some retail stores in the markets where we exist or which are likely market for us to open up new stores. So we are seeing a lot of dynamism.

items.statement: Beauty, artificial jewelry, wearables (smart watches, speakers) launched in some stores showing promising traction; may shift mix 2-3% over time
items.quote: We also launched a wearab le segment, which is the smart watch and there will be the speaker. And they also have shown some promising signs

items.statement: Repeat customers ~70% of V-Mart sales; focus on increasing frequency, bill value, and Gen Z acquisition
items.quote: Our repeat sales or repeat consumer sales is almost -- in V-Mart almost 70% of our total sales.

items.statement: Risk of manufacturer constraint if export opportunities draw capacity away from domestic supply
items.quote: there is one risk that we see that the amount of manufacturers available -- good manufacturers available in the market could be a little constrained going forward if cont inued overexpansion or overinvestment doesn't happen in this particular sector

items.statement: Average bill size flat at ~INR 977; conversion stabilized in Q4 after declining trend; footfalls up as consumers compare across nearby stores
items.quote: The average transaction size as we're going forward and as we see more and more youth coming into the market and into the store. And generally, we have seen that you don't do a bigger size basket.

items.statement: Ind AS 116 lease reassessment yielded one-time INR 24 crore exceptional gain; new store first-half accounting losses ~50% lower going forward
items.quote: During the quarter, we undertook a reassessment of our lease term estimates in accordance with Ind AS 116, which is for leases, reflecting a strategic view of the store portfolio. As a r esult of this exercise, the company recognized a net exceptional gain of INR 24 crores

items.statement: LimeRoad losses to reduce ~50% in FY26 but not breakeven; focus shifting to omnichannel integration
items.quote: We also anticipate for FY '26, while it may not be a breakeven business for the full year, but it will remain in a very comfortable range of definitely less than 50% or roughly around 50% of losses that we did this year.

items.statement: Warehouse expansion from 5 lakh to 8 lakh sq ft planned in 1-1.5 years with automation investments
items.quote: The opportunity to build an area in that particular warehouse land is almost around 8 lakh square feet. So we may build it maybe after one more -- 1, 1.5 years.

items.statement: Monsoon outlook positive; expects farm/rural income growth to support consumption momentum
items.quote: So overall, I think monsoon seems to be looking good till now. We believe the farm income and then the rural income is supposed to grow.

items.statement: Management expects double-digit volume growth for CY2025
items.quote: We have always said that we can grow in double digit, and this is what we are expecting happening this year and we are quite comfortable with that guidance.

items.statement: Capex guidance for CY2025 is ~Rs 3,100 crore with ~Rs 900 crore remaining to be spent
items.quote: We have given the guidance of ~ Rs. 3,100 crore for this year and we are on track and appx. Rs. 900 crore out of which is yet to be spent.

items.statement: Bihar plant commissioning on May 1, 2025; Meghalaya plant by end of May 2025
items.quote: Well, Bihar is getting started tomorrow, May 1, 2025 and Meghalaya will be by the end of May 2025.

items.statement: Greenfield facilities in Kangra and Prayagraj commenced operations; backward integration facilities established in Prayagraj and DRC
items.quote: We recently commenced operations at our new Greenfield production facilities in Kangra, Himachal Pradesh and Pr ayagraj, Uttar Pradesh significantly enhancing

items.statement: South Africa volumes reached 141 million cases over trailing four quarters, up ~13% YoY
items.quote: We achieved 141 million cases in South Africa over the trailing four quarters marking a growth of ~13% over the same period last year.

items.statement: Consolidated gross margin declined 171 bps to 54.6% due to South Africa owned-brand mix and higher CSD share in India
items.quote: Due to relatively lower margin profile of owned brands in the South African market and the higher mix of CSD in India, gross margins stood at 54.6%, a decline of 171 basis points as compared to Q1 CY2024.

items.statement: India EBITDA margin improved 111 bps; consolidated EBITDA margin declined 20 bps due to South Africa at 14.4% margin
items.quote: EBITDA margins in India improved by 111 bps driven by operational efficiencies resulting from strong volume growth at the consolidated level for this year. At the consolidated level, margins declined marginally by 20 bps due to lower profitability in the South Africa market, where margins currently stand at 14.4%.

items.statement: Management expects to maintain South Africa EBITDA margin at ~14.4% for the year
items.quote: No, it used to be ~ 10% odd, and we have reached ~ 14.4% and we expect to maintain 14.4% for the year.

items.statement: Raw material costs stable; packaging slightly lower due to oil prices, sugar slightly higher but balances out
items.quote: We don't see the raw material prices going up significantly. Fortunately for us oil prices are not going up, so our packaging material pricing are quite stable or rather even slightly lower. Sugar slightly has gone up, so it balances out and we are quite comfortable with our production costs.

items.statement: Low/no sugar products increased to ~59% of consolidated sales volumes in Q1 CY2025
items.quote: Aligned with our growing focus on healthier beverages, the mix of the low sugar , no sugar products increased to ~59% on consolidated basis of the total sales volumes in Q1 CY2025.

items.statement: PepsiCo brand salience in South Africa increased from 15% to close to 20%; growing faster than owned brands
items.quote: Our Pepsi brand sales are going up from 15% and it's close to 20% now. All our products are growing including our homegrown brands. PepsiCo product our growing at a faster pace.

items.statement: India organic volume growth of 15.5% in Q1 CY2025; consolidated volume growth 30.1% YoY
items.quote: Consolidated sales volume grew by 30.1% YoY driven by healthy organic volume growth of 15.5% in India.

items.statement: Zimbabwe volumes expected to normalize from Q1 CY2025 after sugar tax impact last year
items.quote: From this quarter onwards we expect the volumes to come back to normal in Zimbabwe.

items.statement: Domino's account loss was less than low single digit of volumes; not material to overall growth
items.quote: It was less than low single digit.

items.statement: Market growing faster due to competition; India underpenetrated with ~12 million FMCG outlets vs ~4 million reached
items.quote: There are ~ 12 million FMCG outlets and we are reaching out to about ~ 4 million only. So there is still so much room for everyone to add new outlets through increased GTM and by putting more chilling equipment.

items.statement: CRISIL upgraded long-term credit rating to CRISIL AAA Stable
items.quote: Lastly, we are pleased to share that CRISIL has upgraded our long-term credit rating to CRISIL AAA Stable.

items.statement: Interim dividend of 25% face value (Rs 0.50 per share) approved; cash outflow ~Rs 1,691 million
items.quote: In line with our dividend policy, the Board of Directors has approved an interim dividend of 25% of face value, i.e., Rs. 0.50 per share, resulting in a total cash outflow of ~Rs. 1,691 million.

items.statement: India realization per case improved 1.8% YoY in Q1 CY2025
items.quote: In India, realization per case improved by 1.8% while it remained stable across international markets excluding South Africa.

items.statement: Consolidated sales volume 312.4 million cases in Q1 CY2025, up 30.1% YoY
items.quote: Consolidated sales volumes increased by 30.1% to the level of 312.4 million cases as compared to 240.2 million cases of the corresponding period i.e., Q1 CY2024.

items.statement: EBITDA increased 27.8% to Rs 12,639.6 million in Q1 CY2025
items.quote: EBITDA increased by 27.8% in Q1 of 2025 to the level of Rs. 12,639.6 million compared to Rs. 9,887.6 million in Q1 of 2024.

items.statement: PAT increased 33.5% to Rs 7,313.6 million in Q1 CY2025
items.quote: PAT for Q1 CY2025 increased by a healthy 33.5% YoY to Rs. 7,313.6 million driven by volume growth and lower finance costs.

items.statement: Ghana and Tanzania deals on hold pending regulatory clearances; will not proceed without full clarity
items.quote: It's just that we have not got the clearances what we were supposed to get. And in the African countries, till we get full clarity, being a listed company, we are not going to take control of the company.

items.statement: South Africa margin improvement to domestic levels is a multi-year process requiring backward integration
items.quote: It's a couple of years process and not going to happen overnight. In the near future we have to make sure that we do complete backward integration in all our plants in the international markets.

items.statement: Realization per case impact from promotions uncertain quarter to quarter but not significant
items.quote: Very difficult to say, it will depend on quarter to quarter. It might have some effect but nothing significant.

items.statement: Sting Gold (malt-based energy drink) launched in March 2025; early reaction good but need 1-2 months to assess
items.quote: The energy drink we have launched in March is a variant of Sting, which is a malt-based energy drink. It's just been put in the market, we have to give it a month or two months before we get really the reaction. But initially the reaction is good.

items.statement: Management does not provide formal guidance but notes historical quarterly revenue and EBITDA CAGR of ~15% over last 7 years
items.quote: I don't think we give any guidance, but your last 7 years of listed performance will tell you that our quarterly CAGR for revenue is close to 15% and our quarterly CAGR for EBITDA also is close to 15%, 16%.

items.statement: Consolidated EBITDA margin reached 4.8% in Q4 FY25, highest ever EBITDA of INR 165 crores
items.quote: On a consolidated level, EBITDA grew by 10.1% year -on-year to INR 165 crores, which is the highest ever reported by SIS and it translates to an EBITDA margin of 4.8%.

items.statement: India Security EBITDA margin 5.6% in Q4 FY25, up from 5.5% in Q4 FY24
items.quote: India Security reported an EBITDA margin of 5.6%, up from 5.5% in Q4 FY '24.

items.statement: FM EBITDA margin 4.7% in Q4 FY25, up 80 bps YoY, highest quarterly EBITDA of INR 27.4 crores
items.quote: FM has reported an EBITDA margin of 4.7%, which is 80 basis points higher on a year -on-year basis. Additionally, the segment also reported its highest-ever quarterly EBITDA of INR 27.4 crores, which is 34% growth on a year-on-year basis.

items.statement: International Security EBITDA margin 4% in Q4 FY25 vs 3.8% in Q3 FY25, driven by AUD 180M new wins in FY25
items.quote: For the International Security business, the EBITDA margin for Q4 FY '25 was 4% compared to 3.8% in Q3 FY '25. This is driven by new wins of AUD 180 million in FY '25.

items.statement: India Security contract churning done, margins expected to gradually return to pre-COVID 6% level
items.quote: I think in Security business in India, I think the contract churning exercise is pretty much done. Therefore, we are reporting 5.5%, 5.6%. And I think gradually, as we gain more operating leverage that will go back to 6% levels, which is the pre - COVID normal level.

items.statement: FM business inching towards 5% EBITDA margin, expected to be out of woods in Q1 FY26
items.quote: In FM, it has taken more time than before, but even FM now is inching towards 5% EBITDA margin. And I think hopefully, in the coming first quarter, you will see that even the FM business is out of the woods as far as the margin is concerned.

items.statement: International Security expected to operate at 4-4.5% EBITDA margin band going forward
items.quote: As far as international is concerned, on the international side, the pre-COVID EBITDA margin level was roughly 4.5%. International is back at close to 4% already, and you can expect it to operate at that 4%, 4.5% band going forward as well.

items.statement: International Security booked AUD 150M permanent revenue new wins in FY25, impacting FY26 and beyond
items.quote: Over the last year, they have booked AU$150 million of permanent revenue, which will obviously impact not just FY '26, but also the subsequent years.

items.statement: International Security won defence and Sydney Trains contracts in Australia after 2-3 years of business development investment
items.quote: And we have landed on some meaty contracts, one being defence and another being Sydney trains locally. So, these kinds of events don't happen every year. It's a mature market, but we are happy that we have been able to gain market share in this business in such a significant manner.

items.statement: Net debt reduced to INR 429 crores from INR 889 crores in March 2024, net debt/EBITDA at 0.7x from 1.5x
items.quote: Overall, very happy to report that net debt is now at INR 429 crores, which is down by INR 460 crores from March '24, which was INR 889 crores a year back. So, INR 889 crores is now down to INR 429 crores. This brings the net debt-to-EBITDA ratio to 0.7, which was 1.5 a year back.

items.statement: OCF to EBITDA at 175%, DSOs improved by 5 days to 65 days from March 2024
items.quote: Now, OCF to EBITDA is also now at 175%. DSOs have improved by 5 days to 65 days from March '24, driven by an improvement in collections.

items.statement: DSOs fixed in security business but headroom for improvement in international and FM
items.quote: Our DSOs are fixed in the security business, but I think there is headroom for improvement in the international side and the FM side.

items.statement: Average cost of gross debt at 7-7.5%, negotiating rates down with banks, no equity dilution needed
items.quote: In fact, even the debt that we have, the gross debt that we have, the average cost of that debt is barely 7%, 7.5%, and we are negotiating our interest rates down with Banks already.

items.statement: Labour codes enacted 2020-22 but state adoption pending; implementation timing uncertain due to national security focus
items.quote: We were informally advised by the department functionaries on a casual chat basis that one can expect that this will be implemented somewhere around this month or two here and there. But I think the whole country's focus now is on different and more pressing national security matters. So, it's very hard to say, when the labour laws will get implemented.

items.statement: 80JJAA provision continues unchanged per budget announcements
items.quote: For now, I don't see any change in the budget announcements as well with regard to 80JJAA. So, I think the 80JJAA provision continues as is with no change.

items.statement: Goodwill impairment of INR 306 crores taken for Henderson, SLV, Uniq, ADIS acquired in 2019; no further significant impairment expected
items.quote: However, as you have all seen, our reported PAT is minus INR 223 crores. This is because of a non-cash goodwill impairment charge of INR 306 crores, which we have taken during this quarter for the investments that we had made in Henderson, SLV , Uniq and ADIS.

items.statement: Remaining INR 700 crores goodwill relates to MSS, DTSS, RHPL; auditors confirm enough headroom, no further impairment indicated
items.quote: The remaining INR 700 crores goodwill which is appearing in the books is mainly related to the past acquisition like MSS, DTSS, RHPL. And during the process of account finalization, the auditor has done the impairment testing of all the entities. And other than these three entities for which we have taken the impairment, there is no indication , there's enough headroom available as per the impairm

items.statement: Cash Logistics DRHP filed with SEBI in Q4 FY25, received first feedback from SEBI yesterday
items.quote: The cash business, DRHP, we received first comments or first feedback from SEBI just yesterday. So, I think that project is coming along well.

items.statement: Cash Logistics listing aims to bring back capital to SIS to further reduce net debt
items.quote: That listing exercise also aims to bring back capital into SIS to further reduce our net debt situation.

items.statement: Actively looking at acquisitions in security, FM, cash logistics but no definitive agreements signed; growth not M&A dependent
items.quote: We are constantly on the lookout, but we won't be making any forward -looking statements for acquisition. As and when we tie up something, definitely, we'll get to know. But we are looking out in all security, FM, cash logistics, all 3 segments.

items.statement: SIS has acquired 15+ companies historically, 5-7 since listing; comfortable not doing M&A
items.quote: First, that SIS has acquired more than 15 companies in the past. Since listing, we would have acquired close to at least five or seven companies. So we have wide experience of M&A and successful M&A. The second point that, SIS growth is not M&A dependent. We are primarily an organic growth entity.

items.statement: Solutions revenue share: India Security sub-10% (5-6%), FM ~30%; solutions defined as outcome-based contracts using man-machine
items.quote: In security business, it is still sub 10%. And in FM business, it is closer to 30%. When I say solution, you must understand there is man and machine. Now that could be machine learning, or it could be equipment of different types from cleaning equipment to various others.

items.statement: FM solutions have higher gross margin but slower growth reduces operating leverage, keeping EBITDA below 5%
items.quote: Higher solutioning means higher gross margin. That is a correct statement. However, when you talk in terms of EBITDA, there is operating leverage that has to play through. So, if you're growing single digit, if you're growing 9%, 10% and the wage cost of your non -billing staff is growing higher, your unit operating costs are growing higher, it doesn't sort of percolate down to EBITDA level as app

items.statement: FM price points per unit lower than security; lower gross margin business growing slower increases SG&A percentage, reducing EBITDA margin
items.quote: The price point for an FM manpower, for example. Per unit is lower for cleaning services or FM services than it is for security. That's the way the industry is structured.

items.statement: International business sitting on large bag of contracts to execute, providing good tailwinds
items.quote: I think what also is very interesting is that the international business is sitting on a large bag of contracts to execute, which should give them good tailwinds.

items.statement: International labour cost pressure driven by manpower availability, not minimum wages; early signs of easing
items.quote: So, what we do is in our business, there is a pressure in the labo ur cost, largely not because of these minimum wage increases, but it's because of non -availability of labour in the market. And that situation, as and when it eases, we are seeing early signs of that easing.

items.statement: Operating PAT INR 83 crores (2.4% margin), up 53% YoY; reported PAT negative INR 223 crores due to impairment
items.quote: Our operating PAT for this quarter is INR 83 crores, resulting in an operating PAT margin of 2.4%, which is 52.9%, almost 53% growth on a year -on-year basis. However, as you have all seen, our reported PAT is minus INR 223 crores.

items.statement: ROCE improved to 14.3% from 12% last quarter after goodwill impairment
items.quote: Now, as a result, after this impairment, our ROCE has now improved to 14.3%, which was 12% in the last quarter.

items.statement: Operating PAT for FY25 INR 318 crores, free cash flow INR 602 crores
items.quote: Number two, as far as accounting is concerned, this is a noncash entry. So operating profit after tax remains at INR 318 crores for the year. And free cash for the year stands at INR 602 crores.

items.statement: Targets 15-17% CAGR advances growth over next 3 years with secured mix >55% by FY27
items.quote: Given the current macro-economic environment, we are targeting an advances growth of 15 – 17% CAGR over the next three years, with a strategic focus on increasing the secured mix. We expect secured advances to constitute over 55%+ of the total advances by FY27.

items.statement: Targets credit cost of 1.5-1.6% over next 2-3 years, elevated in H1FY26
items.quote: While credit costs are expected to remain elevated in H1FY26, we are targeting to reach 1.5–1.6% of credit cost over the next 2-3 years, based on our relentless focus on improving portfolio quality through robust risk management and aided by improving MFI cycle

items.statement: Targets RoA of 1.8-1.9% over next 2-3 years
items.quote: Our focus remains on a steady and sustainable improvement in profitability, with a clear glide path toward improving RoA to 1.8–1.9% over the next 2-3 years, driven by better asset quality, improvement in other income and operating leverage

items.statement: Expects NIM to moderate by 50-60 bps over next 2-3 years as secured mix increases
items.quote: I think as our secured mix increases further, over the next 3 years, we should expect, I think, the NIMs to come down by, say, another 50 to 60 basis points over the next 2-3 years.

items.statement: Expects opex to assets ratio to increase 10-20 bps over next 2 years then improve
items.quote: As a result of these investments, we expect the operating expenses to assets ratio to increase by 10–20 bps from current levels over the next two years. However, as operating leverage begins to take effect thereafter, we anticipate a gradual improvement in this ratio

items.statement: Q4FY25 NIM at 6.7%, down from 6.9% in Q3FY25; full year FY25 NIM at 7.1%
items.quote: Net interest margin for Q4FY25 came in at 6.7%, down from 6.9% in Q3FY25, reflecting similar pressures from the secured loan mix and higher slippages. However, on a full year basis, the NIM remained resilient at 7.1%

items.statement: Yield differential between EEB (~20%) and non-EEB (~10%) portfolios is roughly 10%
items.quote: I think the differential between the two yields is roughly around 10%. So EEB is I think around or upwards of 20%. Partha Pratim Sengupta: Yes, 20% and 10

items.statement: Q4FY25 GNPA 4.7%, NNPA 1.3%, PCR 73.7% (86.5% incl. write-offs)
items.quote: As a result, the gross NPA and the net NP A ratios remained stable on a sequential basis at 4.7% and 1.3%, respectively. The provision coverage ratio increased marginally to 73.7%, excluding the write -offs and including the write -off, as Partha sir talked about earlier, was higher at about 86.5

items.statement: EEB DPD pool (SMA 0,1,2) improved to 3.4% of EEB advances in Q4 from 3.8% in Q3
items.quote: The overall EEB DPD pool, SMA-0, 1, and 2, stood at INR1,895 crores, representing 3.4% of EEB advances in Q4 compared to 3.8% in Q3 FY '25, representing a 40 basis points improvement.

items.statement: Collection efficiency (ex-NPA) improved to 97.9% in Q4FY25 from 97.7% in Q3FY25; EEB collection efficiency 97.8% in Q4 vs 97.4% in Q3
items.quote: The bank's overall collection efficiency, excluding NPA, in Q4FY25 improved slightly to 97.9% compared to 97.7% in Q3FY25, a 20 basis points improvement. For the EEB book, collection efficiency, excluding NPAs in March, improved to 98.2%, up from 97.5% in December 2024. And for the quarter, collection efficiency also showed an improvement, reaching 97.8% compared to 97.4% in Q3FY25

items.statement: Q4FY25 gross slippages INR 1,748 crore (EEB INR 1,349 crore); recoveries/upgrades INR 355 crore; write-offs INR 1,136 crore
items.quote: On asset quality, the gross slippages rose to INR1,748 crores versus INR1,621 crores in Q3, with the primary contributor being the EEB segment. Slippages in the EEB book increased to INR1,349 crores, up from INR1,196 crores in Q3 FY '25. Recoveries and upgrades improved slightly during the quarter, reaching INR355 crores compared to INR282 crores in Q3FY25 at the bank level. Additionally, the bank

items.statement: Credit cost 3.9% in Q4FY25 (down from 4.1% in Q3); FY25 credit cost 2.9% (down ~50 bps YoY)
items.quote: Credit costs, including the standard assets, for the quarter stood at 3.9% of advances, down from 4.1% in the previous quarter. For FY '25, the credit cost declined to 2.9%, representing nearly 50 basis points year-on-year reduction.

items.statement: Advances INR 1.37 lakh crore (10% YoY, 4% QoQ); secured book 32% YoY growth, now 50.5% of total; EEB down 9% YoY, non-EEB up 29% YoY
items.quote: As of March 2025, gross advances stood at INR1.37 lakh crores, reflecting a growth of 10% year-on-year and 4% quarter -on-quarter. In line with our strategic plan of product diversification, we are focused on growing the share of our secured book across housing, wholesale banking and retail assets. Th e secured book grew by 32% year -on-year and now represents 50.5% of the total

items.statement: Retail assets grew 98% YoY, wholesale banking 35% YoY, housing 18% YoY (excl. IBPC)
items.quote: Specifically, retail assets grew by 98% year-on-year, wholesale banking assets saw an increase of 35% year-on-year, and housing loans grew by 18% year-on-year, excluding IBPC.

items.statement: Reduced savings and term deposit rates effective May 1; highest term deposit bracket cut 30 bps from 8.05% to 7.75%
items.quote: So we have also reduced our interest rates on both savings bank and term deposits. So the rationalization has already been taken place. It will come effect from 1st May onwards. So we are expecting that around 30 basis points where we were giving on t he highest term deposit bracket, so 8.05%, it has come down to 7.75

items.statement: ~41% of loan book is EBLR repo-linked (transmission immediate); ~55% fixed rate; ~4-5% MCLR-linked
items.quote: So to give you, 55% is fixed. And of the balance 45%, our EBLR linked Repo is 41% and MCLR linked loans is just 4%-5%.

items.statement: Investing in people, technology, branches; core banking upgrade done, now implementing loan origination system (Salesforce)
items.quote: As you know, last year, we had the core banking system upgrade, and now we are focusing on further systems like loan origination, which is going to -- with the state-of-the-art LOS providers such as Salesforce, and we are going to make sure that it has an enhanced cust omer experience that comes through

items.statement: 1,715 branches and nearly 4,594 Banking Units to deepen reach and mobilize granular deposits
items.quote: Leveraging the capabilities of our 1,715 branches and nearly 4,594 BUs, we aim to deepen our reach and mobilize more granular deposits.

items.statement: Advances mix: EEB group lending 26%, SBAL 15%, wholesale banking 27%, housing 24%, retail loans 8%
items.quote: From a business mix perspective, our advances are well diversified across various segments. EEB group lending represents 26% of the advances, SBAL at 15%, wholesale banking 27%, housing 24%, and retail loans have reached to 8%, respectively.

items.statement: RBI Feb 2025 clarification reduced MFI risk weights to 100%/75% (from 125%), boosting CAR to 18.7%, Tier I to 17.9%
items.quote: In February 2025, the RBI clarified the risk weight norms, reducing them to 100% or 75% for MFI loans based on certain eligibility criterion. This regulatory clarification has had a favourable impact on our capital ratios with CAR at 18.7% and Tier I at 17.9%

items.statement: RBI NBFC lending risk weight change effective April 1 will provide further RWA benefit
items.quote: We are cognizant of the change that is coming from 1st April, which is for lending to NBFCs. And I think that should give some further benefit to the RWA calculation. That's not yet included in the March number, because that's applicable only from 1st of April.

items.statement: Board recommended dividend of INR 1.50 per share for FY25
items.quote: Furthermore, I am pleased to inform you that the Board of Directors has recommended a dividend of INR 1.50 per share, subject to the approval of the shareholders at the forthcoming Annual General Meeting.

items.statement: MFI sector stress elevated; expect continued stress in H1FY26 with turnaround by Q3FY26
items.quote: But I think as we have said, due to the risk which is still there in the EEB segment in the industry, the MFI segment in the industry, and with further tightening of the existing criteria from 4 to 3, I think it's natural to expect the next 2 quarters that there will be some continued stress, albeit we do expect some marginal improvement quarter-on-quarter. But as Vishal earlier mentioned, by Q3 i

items.statement: West Bengal Murshidabad district disturbances: 4% NPA, 88% accounts regular, INR 91 crore NPA out of INR 2,151 crore outstanding
items.quote: Murshidabad District, has 4% NPA. As of April, about 88% of accounts are regular. The SMA-0 accounts make up 6%, while SMA-1 and SMA-2 accounts are 1% each. Currently, the total outstanding is INR 2,151 crores, with only INR 91 crores classified as NPA.

items.statement: Q4FY25 PAT INR 318 crore vs INR 55 crore in Q4FY24 (prior year had one-time write-off)
items.quote: The bank reported a net profit of INR318 crores in the quarter compared to INR55 crores in Q4 FY 2024.

items.statement: Negative tax in Q4 due to INR 61 crore deferred tax asset on ESOP and INR 26 crore old tax provision release (total INR 87 crore)
items.quote: So in total, about INR87 crores between these 2 items.

items.statement: Target net debt of Rs. 3,500-4,000 crore at end of Vadraj CAPEX cycle

items.quote: In Financial Year '2025 our overall GWP has grown by 15% , our fresh GWP grew by 22% , Renewal GWP premium growth was at 12.5% .
