items.quote: ATS/AMC have direct correlation. They're somewhere between 18% to 22% of our revenue when they kick in.

items.statement: Macro uncertainty acknowledged but diversified geography and vertical mix (India, APAC, US, banking, insurance, government) provides resilience; no major project cancellations seen.
items.quote: Having said that, as I said, we are pretty diversified. There's not a single market or a single client segment on which we are dependent. And some of our markets do seem to be less affected initially.

items.statement: GenAI seen as enabler not threat; AI capabilities driving deal wins in content management and low-code platforms.
items.quote: GenAI has actually reinvented all the use cases across industry for kind of things which we sell. In fact, using AI for content ingestion is one of the most hot cases right now in the market by which the last quarter around 6 deals we got in U.S., 3 to 4 are just around the AI capabilities of our product.

items.statement: Large complex project execution timelines extended to 1.5-2 years from 6-7 months previously; most delayed projects nearing completion in next 2-3 quarters.
items.quote: Our typically projects used to be 6, 7 months. Now they are 1.5 years to 2 years. So that's -- it was a part of great wins, and then this is the impact of that.

items.statement: Planning rate revisions and price renegotiations on support contracts to enhance annuity revenue stream over next 1-2 years.
items.quote: We are looking at rate revisions. We are looking at again price renegotiation in certain cases. This should also give a few percentage points going into next 1 or 2 years.

items.statement: Named Leader in Forrester Wave Content Platforms Q1 2025 with highest scores in 10 criteria including AI automation and app design.
items.quote: In Q4, Newgen has been named A Leader in The Forrester Wave Content Platforms report Q1 2025. NewgenONE Contextual Content Services received the highest possible scores in 10 criteria including metadata, search, content migration, life cycle management, intelligent data extraction, document generation and digital process automation.

name: Home First Finance Company India Ltd

items.statement: Raised Rs 1,250 crores via QIP in April 2025, issuing 1.3 crore equity shares to institutional investors
items.quote: In April 2025, we successfully raised Rs. 1,250 crores through a qualified institutional placement, issuing 1.3 crore equity shares to market institutional investors, details of which are available on our website and exchanges.

items.statement: Targeting 20-25% disbursement growth for FY26, with 20-25% from new branches and 75% from existing branches
items.quote: Disbursement growth, we are targeting it on 20% +; somewhere in the range of 20% to 25% is what we are looking at for disbursement growth. And the trend will be similar – about 20% to 25% will come from new locations, branches, expansion, distribution and 75% will continue to come from existing branches.

items.statement: Confident of achieving Rs 20,000 crores AUM by FY27 and Rs 35,000 crores by FY30 with no major hindrances seen
items.quote: No, we are fairly confident of achieving the Rs. 20,000 crores mark in the next 2 years. At this point, we don't see anything which could be a hindrance to achieving the Rs. 20,000 crores.

items.statement: Maintain spread guidance of 5% to 5.25% excluding co-lending, and credit cost guidance of 30-40 bps
items.quote: Our expectation is that we will be able to hold on to the cost of borrowing moving ahead. So, we are comfortable with that 5% plus guidance on the spread, excluding co-lending.

items.statement: Q4 FY25 spread ex-co-lending at 5.1%, cost of borrowing ex-co-lending at 8.4%, NIM at 5.1% expanded 20 bps qoq
items.quote: For Q4 FY25 , our spread, excluding co -lending, is at 5.1% . Our cost of borrowing, excluding co-lending, is maintained at 8.4%. Net interest margin for Q4 was at 5.1%. It expanded by 20 bps on a qoq basis, driven largely by better liquidity management.

items.statement: Margins will expand for next few quarters post equity raise, then compress in 6-8 quarters as leverage picks up; focus on 5%+ spreads
items.quote: Because we have just had an equity raise. The margins will expand for next few quarters. As leverage starts to pick up, 6 - 8 quarters out, we will see compression on margin. So, the right number would be to look at spreads of 5%+.

items.statement: 1+ DPD improved to 4.5% (-30 bps qoq), 30+ DPD improved to 3.3% (-10 bps qoq), Gross Stage 3 stable at 1.7%, credit cost at 30 bps
items.quote: 1+ DPD improved to 4.5%, which is a decline of 30 bps on a qoq basis. o 30+ DPD improved to 3.3%, which is a decline of 10 bps on a qoq basis. o Gross Stage 3 assets remained stable at 1.7%. o Our credit costs continue to be contained at around 30 bps

items.statement: LAP NPA at 1.2-1.3%, home loan NPA at 1.9%; LAP lower due to selective underwriting and no aggressive targets
items.quote: LAP is around 1.2% - 1.3% NPA and home loan is about 1.9%. Actually, the numbers are disclosed in our QIP placement document, and it is already published on the stock exchanges.

items.statement: Added 40 touch points including 22 branches in FY25, total 361 touch points and 155 branches; plan 20-30% branch growth annually (30-40 branches/year)
items.quote: During the fiscal 2025, we further expanded our network, adding 40 touch points, including 22 branches. This added our reach to 10 more districts within our 13 states and emerging territory. As of March 2025, our total touch points stand at 361 with 155 branches.

items.statement: AUM grew to Rs 12,713 crores (31.1% YoY, 6.4% QoQ); disbursements Rs 4,805 crores (21.2% YoY); run-off 17-18%, BT-out 7.5%
items.quote: Our assets under management grew to Rs. 12,713 crores, registering a 31.1% yoy and 6.4% qoq increase while delivering a PAT of Rs 382 crores with an ROE of 16.5% for the full year 2025. We touched an ROE of 17% in Q4 FY25. • Our disbursements for FY25 stood at Rs. 4,805 crores, up 21.2% yoy, in line with our guidance for the

items.statement: LAP mix 15% of AUM, 16-17% of disbursements; expected to move to 15-20% over next 5 years; average ticket size growing 3-5% annually
items.quote: LAP mix broadly will end up in 15% to 20% range . 15% is the current share of AUM while share of disbursal is slightly higher at 16%-17%. That catch-up is something which we have already communicated that over the next 5 years, it can move up from 15% to 20%.

items.statement: Cost of borrowing ex-co-lending held at 8.4% despite MCLR rise; 60% transmission of rate cuts over 12 months; repo-linked borrowings 18-19%
items.quote: Assuming a 100 basis points cumulative rate cut. What we have observed, generally, is that there's a 60% transmission if we take a very long-term 10-year data. But the transmission takes about 12 months to happen.

items.statement: Proforma leverage 3.3x post-QIP, CRAR 51%, net worth Rs 3,751 crores; comfortable up to 5x+ leverage, capital sufficient for ~4 years (until FY30)
items.quote: Given our enlarged equity base post the capital infusion, our proforma leverage has come down to 3.3x. Proforma capital adequacy (CRAR) post capital raise will be 51% and a net worth of Rs. 3,751 crores.

items.statement: RBI draft co-lending guidelines omit Model 2 (currently used); if Model 2 not allowed, Model 1 is more tedious (simultaneous disbursement); but guidelines expand addressable market
items.quote: One thing that we are watching out for is that they have not mentioned the modus operandi of how those assets will get transferred. Till now, we were following the co-lending model 2, but the draft guidelines do not have mention of that co -lending model 2.

items.statement: Active connectors ~3,800; ~1,200 relationship managers; top 10 connectors contribute <4% of disbursements; connector commission 40-50 bps
items.quote: Total connectors active , as of now, is about 3,800. And number of relationship managers that the sales team would be about close to 1,200 sales people. Nutan Gaba Patwari: And disbursement from top 10 connector is below 4

items.statement: Affordable housing market growth expected at 10-15% YoY in FY26; Home First market share ~2%, targeting 4-5% in 3-5 years
items.quote: As far as the overall market is concerned for FY26, we think it should be another year of good or decent demand because affordable housing demand has largely been secular. The growth has been secular in the range of 10% to 15% a year.

items.statement: Direct assignment of Rs 230 crores in Q4 FY25; no annual targets, driven by liquidity needs and bank relationships; DA book ~Rs 1,500 crores
items.quote: As part of our liquidity management strategy, we executed direct assignment transaction worth Rs. 230 crores during the quarter. We continue to focus on co -lending business and are looking to scale with newer partner.

items.statement: No dividend or buyback mentioned; focus on growth and ROE recovery to 15%+ in 6-7 quarters post-QIP
items.quote: Our first milestone is to get to 15%+, which is in about 6 to 7 quarters from now.

items.statement: No specific state or segment stress seen; early delinquencies improved across board; bounce rates behavioural not indicative of stress
items.quote: I would say we are not seeing anything other than what you are seeing on the asset quality. There is nothing which we are reading from the ground level data that we are getting.

items.statement: Private banks less focused on mortgages, selling down secured books; PSU banks and large HFCs more active; competition uniform year-on-year
items.quote: From my conversation with the banks, you're right, private sector banks are not so focused today on mortgage. In fact, there's a significant sell -down of book from their side on the s ecured side

items.statement: Digital adoption: 75% sanctions via account aggregator, 80% loans digitally fulfilled, 96% customers on app, 88% service requests digital
items.quote: Today, 75% of our sanctions are being facilitated by the account aggregator framework. o 80% of our loans are digitally fulfilled through the agreements in E-NACH mandates. o And 96% of our customers are registered on our mobile app with 88% of service requests being raised

items.statement: ESG: 120 Green Homes certified by March 2025; S&P Global score 46 (2024), Morningstar Sustainalytics 16.2 (low risk)
items.quote: We expanded our Green Home initiative during the year with 120 homes certified as of March 2025. ESG efforts are being acknowledged and appreciated by independent global agencies in the form of high ESG scores – 46 by S&P Global for 2024 and 16.2 by Morningstar Sustainalytics indicating “low risk”.

items.statement: FY26 revenue growth guidance of minimum 25-30% YoY and profit growth of 20-30%
items.quote: So our expectations with the kind of order book that we have, we are very, very confident. And on a very conservative side, we expect a minimum growth year -on-year of 25% or maybe even 30%. And our profits would always -- should be in line with what our current numbers are i the same ratios as we go forward to 20% to 30

items.statement: FY25 EBITDA margin at 43%, maintained in 41-44% range
items.quote: For full year EBITDA, it has grown by 35.3% to INR263.8 crores with EBITDA margin of 43%. We have been maintaining EBITDA margins in the range of 41% to 44%.

items.statement: Q4 FY25 EBITDA margin dropped to 34% due to one-time expenses of INR 10-11 crores from newly acquired companies
items.quote: So on a quarterly bas is, as we consolidated newly acquired companies in addition to their exceptional items, there are certain other expenses also which were consolidated under Q4 and that is the reason particularly for a drop in margin in Q4

items.statement: FY26 capex plan of INR 500 crores, including INR 350+ crores for equipment and rigs
items.quote: See primarily, we would be doing capex of INR500 crores, of which more than INR350 crores would be for equipment. We would be adding a few more rigs and other processing equipment in this financial year.

items.statement: Evaluating QIP for funding, comfortable on liquidity
items.quote: But having said so, we are quite comfortable on our liquidity position. So we would definitely look for good time to go ahead with QIP.

items.statement: Acquired Kandla Energy & Chemicals and Dolphin Offshore Shipping for INR 9 crores total; backward integration and fleet expansion rationale
items.quote: See, at the end of day, acquisition cost for acquiring both this com pany put together is just INR9 crores for us. And so against INR9 crores, these two companies with their properties, their receivables and their experiences with their assets is coming

items.statement: Beluga International invested $2.2 million for 37% stake in JV with HF Offshore, acquired one Anchor Handling Tug
items.quote: So that investment is for joint venture with HF Offshore. And under this JV, we have acquired one Anchor Handling Tug. So our stake in that investment would be 37%.

items.statement: Beluga International DMCC signed 3-year lease agreement with Ballast Shipping for deployment of Prabha DP2 accommodation barge in Mexico
items.quote: DMCC, a wholly -owned subsidiary of Dolphin Offshore, has entered into a 3 agreement with Ballast Shipping, a Mexican company for the deployment of accommodation barge

items.statement: Government target to double natural gas production to 60 BCM and expand exploration area to 1 million sq km by 2030
items.quote: Additionally, our proficiency in our value -added services like charter hire of entire gas processing facilities and integrated project managemen t aligns seamlessly with the government's ambition to double natural gas production to 60 billion cubic meters and enhance its share in the energy mix

items.statement: India's energy demand projected to reach 11 million bpd by 2045 and natural gas consumption 550 MMSCMD by 2030
items.quote: With India's energy demand projected to grow faster than any major economy, reaching 11 million barrels per day by 2045 and natural gas consumption forecast to hit 550 million cubic meters per day by 2030, the opportunities are immense.

items.statement: Actively exploring production enhancement contracts and charter hiring of entire gas processing facilities for growth
items.quote: We are actively exploring production enh ancement contracts and charter hiring of entire gas processing facilities , segments poised to drive our growth in the coming

items.statement: Kandla Energy acquisition expected to improve operating margins by 2-3% through backward integration of chemicals and fluids
items.quote: So since many chemicals and fluids would be useful, so we believe in our operating margins, we can have an improvement of more than 2% to 3%, at least on a minimum side.

items.statement: Dolphin Offshore FY26 revenue expected at INR 100 crores minimum, potentially more with added projects
items.quote: FY '26, we are expecting revenue of almost INR100 crores, for sure. we can book more than this if we will add a few more projects in Dolphin.

items.statement: Regular receivables (ex-acquisitions) 70-80% within 90 days, balance over 90 days
items.quote: And majority of them would be 90 days. I would say more than 70% to 80% would be 90 days and balance would be more than 90 days.

items.statement: Consolidated receivables doubled to INR 588 crores from INR 276 crores due to Kandla and Dolphin acquisitions
items.quote: Correct. So we have categorically given note for these receivables. So as you rightly said, the number is primarily because of the receivables of these two targets which we have acquired.

items.statement: Kandla receivables (INR 208 crores) kept outstanding pending evaluation; hopeful of recovery
items.quote: No. So we have kept those receivables outstanding because evaluation is going on. And since we have recently acquired and taken control over the company, so all documents and supporting we are going it through. And we are quite hopeful to recover out of this receivables.

items.statement: Board recommended final dividend of INR 3.05 per share (61% of face value Rs 5) for FY25
items.quote: We are happy to inform that Board of Directors have recommended a final dividend of INR3.05, is 61% on the face value of Rs. 5 per equity share, subject to approval of shareholders of the company at the ensuing annual general meeting

items.statement: Oilfields Amendment Bill passed March 2025 expands mineral oils definition to include shale gas and unconventional hydrocarbons
items.quote: The Oilfields Amendment Bill passed in Lok Sabha in March 2025 has redefined the sector's traject ory. By expanding the definition of mineral oils to include shale gas and unconventional hydrocarbons, streamlining dispute resolution enhanced oil recovery techniques, this legislation is unlocking new opportunities for exploration and production

items.statement: 10th round of OALP launched with AI-driven seismic data; DSF4 round also expected soon
items.quote: We have mentioned that the 10th round of OALP is already there, one more round of already out. So likewise, and many such PECs are also -- are not out, they are supposed to get out very soon

items.statement: Contracts are fixed-price for 3 years, insulated from crude oil price volatility
items.quote: Thirdly, our contracts are of a fixed-price nature assuming that we have a contract for the three years, the prices may go, it does not have any impact on commitments and our services. They are fixed for that period.

items.statement: Competition visible in lack of margin expansion due to more players and category competition
items.quote: The impact of competition is visible in the lack of significant margin expansion that we would have otherwise expected.

items.statement: Competition from existing and new quick commerce players in discounting, marketing, free delivery, store expansion
items.quote: The competition has been in different shapes and forms coming from both players, who are already in the quick commerce space and the new players that are trying to enter the quick commerce space.

items.statement: Significant competition for same real estate in most cities
items.quote: There has been significant competition for the same real estate in most of the cities that we are in.

items.statement: Competition hasn't reduced, price action peaked in Q3FY25, elevated competition continues
items.quote: in the last quarter, competition hasn't reduced in any way. It was definitely way more competitive in terms of price action that we saw in the market in the quarter prior to that (Q3FY25).

items.statement: Competitive intensity remains high, margin pressure stays, no meaningful directional change
items.quote: competitive intensity remains high, and therefore, the pressure on margin, that Albinder alluded to, stays. At least so far, we haven't seen any change.

items.statement: Food delivery 20%+ is long-term 4-5 year CAGR guidance, not immediate yearly target
items.quote: 20%, therefore, is more a long-term 4-5 year CAGR guidance. I'm just clarifying that even in the past, we have stated that it's not an immediate every year growth guidance.

items.statement: No margin guidance for Blinkit due to multiple moving parts and seasonality
items.quote: we don't want to stick our neck out and give any guidance at this point, given the multiple moving parts.

items.statement: Store rollouts elevated at ~300 stores/quarter, larger share in non-top 8 markets
items.quote: broadly, we are going into smaller cities every quarter. And incrementally, a larger portion of our new store expansion is happening in the non-top eight markets.

items.statement: New store ramp-up to breakeven remains consistent with past, no deterioration
items.quote: So far, we're not seeing any deterioration in the time stores are taking to ramp up to breakeven. It remains pretty consistent with the past.

items.statement: Zomato Everyday shut down as it wouldn't move needle for food delivery at scale
items.quote: given the overall size of that business, in our mind, we didn't feel that it would move the needle for the food delivery business on an overall basis.

items.statement: Zomato Bistro is separate early-stage business, unclear if it fills Everyday/Quick gap
items.quote: Bistro, is a separate business. It's very early days. We don't have a point of view on whether that fills the gap for Zomato Quick or Everyday.

items.statement: Ad income north of 4% of GOV, customer fees ~3% of GOV
items.quote: It's north of 4% of GOV today for us.

items.statement: GOV to NOV difference varies widely, up to 70-80% in some unbranded categories
items.quote: There could be categories where it is also 70% - 80%.

items.statement: Inventory days may increase to 20-25 days if expanding into electronics/white goods
items.quote: there's definitely a chance that the number of inventory days on books will go up as a result.

items.statement: Market share maintained in quick commerce despite high competitive intensity
items.quote: even with the new competition, we have more or less maintained our market share over the last few quarters.

items.statement: Good consumer appetite in tier 2/3 cities driving aggressive expansion
items.quote: Yes. That is why we are expanding aggressively.

items.statement: Blinkit Adjusted EBITDA at -2% of NOV, not deep in red
items.quote: We are at -2% margin today in terms of Adjusted EBITDA as a percentage of NOV.

items.statement: Going-out business GOV growing >100% YoY, Adjusted EBITDA -2 to -2.5% of NOV
items.quote: If you look at year-on-year growth, the GOV of going-out is still growing by more than 100%. And on profitability, we are at -2 to -2.5% of Adjusted EBITDA as a percentage of NOV.

items.statement: Going-out investment phase to continue for next year, losses not expected to increase
items.quote: that investment phase will continue for the next year or so. And hence, we are not expecting this business to become profitable in that time frame. But at the same time, we don't expect that losses will go up from here as well.

items.statement: Last mile worker supply temporary mismatch, expected to ease over medium-long term
items.quote: Supply always catches up with some lag, and that's what we expect here as well over time. We will see the supply increase and therefore, this pressure should ease off.

items.statement: Rider availability issue not due to commercial model, compounded by summer season and quick commerce expansion
items.quote: it's just a temporary supply/demand mismatch, because of the rapid expansion of e-commerce in the last three / four months.

items.statement: Q1FY26 food delivery trending as per seasonal expectations, nothing surprising
items.quote: seasonally, this (Q1FY26) is a better quarter. And so far, nothing surprising. We're trending as per the expectations we have from this quarter.

items.statement: No private labels in B2C as brands better equipped, strategic choice to operate as platform
items.quote: We work with a lot of brands, and we feel that they are better equipped to create and sell products that customers need. We would like to be in the business that we do best, which is operating as a platform.

items.statement: Shareholder approval needed for foreign ownership to evaluate inventory model for new categories
items.quote: Once we get the approval, then we'll start evaluating it, whether we want to go down that path at all.

items.statement: Other income increase due to full quarter impact of QIP raised in November
items.quote: We raised money through the QIP in November last quarter. So, the full quarter impact of that is now leading to the higher income.

items.statement: Tax dip in Q4 due to prior quarter over-provision adjustment, not recurring
items.quote: the amount of tax that we provided for, in the previous quarters was a little higher, but the actual tax to be paid, came out a little lower, and therefore, there was that adjustment that was made in Q4.

items.statement: FY26 volume growth guided at 10-15% driven by CPVC, ECH and chlorotoluene ramp-up
items.quote: So considering the CAPEX that we have commissioned this year, we should be seeing a volume growth around 10 % to 15% and that will drive the value growth as well.

items.statement: Long-term EBITDA margin target of around 25% considered sustainable
items.quote: But at the same time, t he Derivatives, there were other products which had compensated for that, and that's when the average EBITDA we have landed up around 28% and considering th e situation, we believe that on a longer-term basis 25% is something which is achievable

items.statement: Revenue CAGR of 15-20% visible for next 4-5 years based on executed CAPEX and demand assumptions
items.quote: So on a CAGR basis, 15% to 20% growth for next five years is something which is visible.

items.statement: FY26 capex planned at Rs 450 crore for CPVC resin expansion to 150kt and ECH expansion to 100kt by H1 FY27
items.quote: So capital expenditure, we have announced to expand CPVC resin by adding another 75,000 so we reach to 1,50,000 tonnes of capacity for CPVC resin. We are adding Epichlorohydrin, we are expanding Epichlorohydrin as well. So we will reach from 50,000 to 1,00,000 tonnes of capacity by the first half of FY'27. So in-line with that, this year we are expecting to spend the CAPEX around Rs.450 crore.

items.statement: Capex financing primarily through internal accruals with debt as backup if needed
items.quote: So, the financing we are going to do it by debt and debt mainly, if required moving forward. But as of now, there is no, we are going to manage from the internal accrual.

items.statement: Chlorotoluene value chain commissioned March 2025; optimal utilization expected by end of FY26
items.quote: We commissioned our chlorotoluene value chain facility in March 2025 and we expect to reach optimal utilization of the plant by the end of this financial year.

items.statement: CPVC resin and ECH expansions to reach optimum utilization by H1 FY27
items.quote: Once we reach optimal utilization, and also as our expansion announcement of doubling capacity of CPVC resin and Epichlorohydrin facility will also reach optimum by that time, we expect the revenue contribution from Derivatives & Specialty business to reach around 70%.

items.statement: Caustic soda plant membrane/electrolysis overhaul completed in May; operating efficiency to improve from next quarter
items.quote: Every eight years you normally do a major change in the caustic soda membrane and electrolysis that we have already done, that is going to be completed in May, so probably from the next quarter onwards, the operation efficiency of the caustic soda plant will also improve.

items.statement: FY25 EBITDA margin 28% vs 25% in FY24; Q4 FY25 EBITDA margin 28% vs 30% in Q4 FY24
items.quote: EBITDA grew by 48% to Rs.711 crores, leading to EBITDA margin of 28% compared to 25% in FY 2024.

items.statement: CPVC pricing trending down next few quarters due to weaker demand from real estate and lower PVC raw material prices
items.quote: The pricing is seen downside because of, there is slightly demand growth is less compared to last year in terms of the CPVC demand. And the second, because of the real estate sector, is little bit lower side right now in terms of the growth. And the second is, the raw material price has also gone down for the CPVC, which is a PVC, so PVC is on the lowest cycle globally right now.

items.statement: ECH pricing slightly higher compared to past quarters
items.quote: and then the ECH is on a slightly higher side compared to the past quarters, so this is what we see in next couple of quarters

items.statement: Q4 FY25 ECU realization ~Rs 33,000; chlorine negative ~Rs 5,000
items.quote: The ECU for the quarter, for the Q4 was around Rs.33,000 and the chlorine was somewhere around negative Rs.5000.

items.statement: Solar/wind generation lower YoY in Q4; coal cost slightly higher YoY
items.quote: So the major point was, compared to last year, the similar quarter what we generate the solar and wind which was this quarter, it was little lesser in terms of the percentage, because it is related to the natural phenomenon. So it was little less unit generation compared to the last year. And the second thing, there is a slightly increase in the coal also compared to last year.

items.statement: 18.34 MW solar plant commissioned ~2 years ago; power cost 25-30% cheaper than grid
items.quote: So we have already commissioned 18.34 megawatt we have already started almost two years before this time. So that has already started contributing to the bottom line, and in terms of cost saving, it is almost you can say 25%, 30% cheaper than grid price.

items.statement: Chemical industry growth product-specific and region-specific; agrochemical revival driving chlorine derivative demand
items.quote: Overall, the chemical industry is witnessing some sort of a growth in a few selected products portfolio and a few products baskets, the growth is still a t a slower pace. So chemical industry movement is product specific and region specific in terms of growth

items.statement: Global caustic soda demand robust from alumina and nickel; chlorine prices expected to improve long-term in India
items.quote: Globally, the caustic soda demand will remain robust in terms of the alumina, in terms of the nickel consumption, nickel mining and in terms of the alumina consumption of the caustic soda globally. So that is remain from globally and the pressure will remain on the chlorine side only because of the caustic soundness, but we are going to be better than in the last quarter going forward.

items.statement: Chlorotoluene derivatives target mix: 70% agrochemical intermediates, 30% pharma intermediates; domestic and export customers
items.quote: It's a mix, definitely export customers are there, which are majorly focused on the agrochemical intermediate manufacturing companies and Indian Specialty chemical companies, who are doing toll manufacturing for on behalf of all multinatio nal they are going to be our customers, along with some of the pharma intermediate companies as well, because the agrochemical and the pharma both having applic

items.statement: Inventory days stable at 47 days in FY25 vs 45 days in FY24; increase in line with sales growth
items.quote: So if you see our inventory days that was around 45 days in FY'24, so in FY'25 it is 47 days. So whatever it has increased, it is in-line with the increase in sales.

items.statement: Net debt/EBITDA improved to 0.7x at March 2025 from 2.0x at March 2024
items.quote: Our net debt-to-EBITDA has remarkably improved to 0.7x at the end of March 2025 against 2.0x at the end of March 2024.

items.statement: CRISIL rating upgraded to AA Stable from AA- Positive
items.quote: Lastly, the rating is also upgraded by CRISIL, rating upgraded to CRISIL AA Stable from CRISIL AA- positive outlook.

items.statement: Captive chlorine consumption 72% in FY25; target 90%+ after new capacities reach optimum
items.quote: In FY'25 our captive chlorine consumption was around 72%, this is in-line with our expansions. Our captive chlorine consumption will also increase and will be optimum, strengthening our integrated complex further.

items.statement: ROCE improved to 25% (28% excl. CWIP) in FY25 from 17% in FY24
items.quote: Thus the return on capital employed improved to 25% for the year ending 31st March, 2025 compared to 17% as on 31st March 2024. This is including the capital work-in-progress. If we exclude capital work-in-progress, the ROCE stands at 28%.

items.statement: New 100-acre land acquired 1 km from existing site for new value chain/chemistry; board approval pending
items.quote: In the new location, which is one kilometer away, we have already taken a land of 100 acres, there we are looking for a new value chain and new chemistry. We are not going to enter in the similar chlor-alkali that.

items.statement: Global caustic soda prices soft due to low downstream chlorine demand (60-65% utilization) and low PVC cycle; but alumina/nickel demand supports prices
items.quote: soda price are remaining soft globally, the reason behind is the downstream chemistry which is used chlorine globally, which is almost 60 % to 65% that is very low. somewhere, even PVC cycle is on the lowest level right now and because of that, caustic is remain firm

items.statement: Cable share increasing in both domestic and export; premium/mid-premium FMEG products now ~20% of FMEG revenue
items.quote: Like earlier, whatever contribution we were getting, now we are getting almost 20% of our revenue from premium and mid-premium category, which gives you brand presence also and improvement in profitability also.

items.statement: Exports 26% of FY25 revenue, grew 11% YoY; strong demand from Europe, US uncertainty but favorable outlook for India
items.quote: Our export business contributed 26% to our total revenue in FY '25, stable compared to FY '24. In absolute terms, exports grew by 11% year-on-year despite global uncertainty.

items.statement: Working capital cycle improved from 88 days (FY22) to 56 days (FY25); normalized level ~60 days; payables stable at INR760 cr (no one-off)
items.quote: The company has also been consistently improving its working capital cycle from 88 days in FY '22 to 56 days in FY '25.

items.statement: Board approved dividend of INR3.5 per share (70% of face value)
items.quote: It pleased me to announce that the Board of Directors of the company has approved a dividend of INR3.5 per share, 70% of face value.

items.statement: Wires & Cables demand robust in domestic and export markets after 2 subdued quarters; industry expected to grow at 15% CAGR to INR2 lakh cr by FY31
items.quote: Wires and cables demand was robust in both domestic and export market after 2 quarters of relatively subdued demand.

items.statement: Copper price uptrend provided marginal margin benefit but majority of margin improvement from volume growth; price actions follow metal prices
items.quote: I will not say inventory gain, but since the copper prices or other metal prices were on upward trends, so always whenever there is upward trend, we get -- like first, it is always good.

items.statement: Industry size INR90,000 cr, growing at ~2x GDP; organized market share expanding
items.quote: Currently valued at INR90,000 crores, the industry is expected to grow at a CAGR of 15% and reach approximately INR2 lakh crores by FY '31.

items.statement: Q1 FY26 demand may remain subdued/stable seasonally; copper prices falling; US market uncertainty but expected to favor India
items.quote: So it seems that this quarter may remain like subdued or stable kind of demand. But it is in routine basis only, nothing abnormal in growth or reduction in growth also.

items.statement: Management reiterated 20-25% growth zone for FY26
items.quote: You can take a similar guidance of 20% to 25% zone as a guidance that we have and we will keep on growing in that zone.

items.statement: Targeting INR1,000 crore order book in wastewater management within 18 months
items.quote: We had already evaluated pipelines. We had already evaluated which tenders or projects that we will go ahead and evaluate, bid for work around. Only after that, we have gone ahead and made the announcement that we will have an order book position of 1,000 crores in the next 18 months.

items.statement: Won INR349 crore facility management contract from Tamil Nadu Medical Services
items.quote: To just name a few recent noteworthy contract wins over the last quarter, we secured a INR349 crores facility management contract from Tamil Nadu Medical Services

items.statement: Won INR84 crore sanitization order from PGIMER
items.quote: INR84 crores worth of sanitization service order from PGIMER, which is one of the very prominent hospitals in

items.quote: Further, we secured the 3-year INR167 crores facility management contract and a 5-year INR134 crores staffing and payroll management contract from the Directorate of Medical Education and Research Center, Maharashtra.

items.statement: Board approved INR300 crore fundraise for various projects
items.quote: We've already taken Board's approval in the last Board meeting for fundraise for INR300 crores for our various projects.

items.statement: Q4 FY25 EBITDA margin improved 4 bps to 6.48%
items.quote: Our EBITDA, excluding the other income for the quarter stands INR26.75 crores, growing 42.28% year-on-year. EBITDA margin improved by 4 basis points to 6.48%.

items.statement: Pricing environment improved on corporate side post-pandemic
items.quote: The pricing environment is in the corporate side it definitely is looking a little better for two reasons whoever listening also. We have been acquiring customers which are very good and who value good quality service. So I will say that the pricing environment is a little better than what we have been seeing post pandemic.

items.statement: Launched wastewater management vertical with 20-member specialized team including ZLD expertise
items.quote: We have already hired a team of 20 talented memb ers who understand the technical - the technology and the engineering part of it. Also, some are specialized into the ZLD process, which is zero liquid discharge

items.statement: Launched Taskmaster B2C subsidiary for residential deep cleaning services in Mumbai, Alibag, Goa
items.quote: Taskmaster is what I just touched upon, it's Taskmaster Private Limited. This is a 100% subsidiary as I explained to you, which is going to provide deep cleaning services and everything and all other services that are required by the residential sector, homes, Bungalows, villas and other residential sectors.

items.statement: Carved out technical facility management as independent vertical covering MEP, HVAC, DG set maintenance
items.quote: Technical facility management used to be one odd service that we used to offer in our integrated facility management portfolio. But because of the demand for the services, because of the market that these services have, we have carved out this vertical as an independent technical facility management vertical.

items.statement: Trade receivables increased due to new contracts in Q3/Q4; streamlines over a quarter
items.quote: Yes, because we've gotten into many new contracts in the last year, also in the last quarter 3 and quarter 4. So while these businesses -- we start this business, the entire process of documentation, billing takes a little time and one has to give that for both parties to understand. So therefore, you are seeing a little variance in these numbers.

items.statement: Negative operating cash flow due to working capital from new businesses
items.quote: We have working capital which we have acquired very new businesses. So, that is pertaining to that, you see that negative cash flow.

items.statement: Board recommended final dividend of INR1.50 per share (face value INR10) for FY25
items.quote: The Board of Directors has recommended a final dividend of INR1.50 per equity share of face value of INR10 for the financial year '25, subject to approval of shareholders.

items.statement: Workforce grew to 43,300+ on-site employees across 26 branches
items.quote: We have 43,300-plus on-site workforce who are our brand ambassadors. Through our pan-India footprint of 26 branches

items.statement: Security services demand unaffected by automation; technology complements manpower
items.quote: We have already made our assessment there and the cameras and the other technologies, they have been there since a couple of decades now. So, which has not stop ped the growth of manpower. It is a good complement, both of the technology and manpower complement each other

items.statement: Wastewater projects are project-based with 8-9 month execution and 2-3 year O&M; no startup losses expected
items.quote: because these are project-based businesses, the break-even there is nothing like breakeven because once the project is over, we've already taken all our build money and revenues and the major chunk -- we've already booked our profit. After that, it is a two-year, three-year O&M, which we are getting paid for on a monthly basis

items.statement: Catering kitchen has spare capacity; can also produce onsite at client locations
items.quote: We still have space for manufacturing food in our current kitchen. We have not reached the optimum level of customers that we are servicing. So, there is, again, the nature of business is twofold. One is the production which happens in the kitchen and one is the production which happens onsite.

items.statement: Strong demand across airports, hospitals, metros, manufacturing; bidding for both government and private airport contracts
items.quote: we are participating. We have the experience of working with GMR, GVK also and now the Adani Airport also. We are anyway offering our services at the Mumbai International Airpor t, the international terminal. But while we are pursuing our business with the private players, we are also not forgetting the Airport Authority of India terminals, because they have more than 100 terminals nationally and

items.statement: Expect double-digit consolidated revenue growth and double-digit operating profit growth in FY26
items.quote: Moving into next year, we expect to sustain double -digit revenue growth and will strive to deliver double -digit operating profit growth.

items.statement: Foods portfolio to grow 25%+ over medium term to reach ~8x FY20 scale
items.quote: The Foods portfolio has reached 5x of the FY20 scale, and we expect 25% + growth over the medium term to reach about 8x of the FY20 scale, while we continue to improve profitability in the category.

items.statement: Digital-first portfolio exit ARR to be 2.5x FY24 ARR by FY27
items.quote: We now expect this exit ARR to be 2.5x of FY24 ARR in FY27, up from the previous target of 2x.

items.statement: Digital-first portfolio to achieve double-digit EBITDA margin by FY27
items.quote: We continue to see marked improvement in profitability in the Digital-first portfolio and maintain our aspiration to achieve double-digit EBITDA margin by FY '27.

items.statement: Foods and Premium Personal Care to expand to ~25% of domestic revenue by FY27
items.quote: We will continue to aggressively diversify the portfolio through these portfolios in line with our medium -term strategic priorities and expect these portfolios to expand to ~25% of domestic revenue by FY 27.

items.statement: India volume growth expected >5% annualized in FY26, with 6-7% as base case
items.quote: We expect the volume growth next year , full year annualized, as more than 5%. 6-7% growth has almost become a base case for us.

items.statement: Gross margin pressure to continue for next 1-2 quarters, easing from end of Q2 FY26
items.quote: While there could be some pressure on margin on account of that in the next one or two quarters, we expect margin pressure to ease out starting end of quarter two.

items.statement: Effective tax rate around 22% for next few years
items.quote: You can take it at around 22%.

items.statement: Consumer sentiment stable with improving rural demand and mixed urban trends
items.quote: During the quarter, consumer sentiment remained largely stable, supported by improving rural demand and mixed trends across mass and affluent urban segments.

items.statement: Core portfolios saw transient sluggishness amid steep inflation; new businesses maintained strong momentum
items.quote: In the demand front, the core portfolios witnessed transient sluggishness amidst steep inflation and key commodities , although we maintain the strong momentum in new businesses, which furthered the diversification agenda.

items.statement: Consolidated operating margin ended just shy of 20% in FY25 despite higher input cost inflation
items.quote: The consolidated operating margin of FY 25 ended just shy of 20%, and we have delivered resilient bottom line performance without any negative surprises despite input cost pressures being significantly higher than for the rest of the sector.

items.statement: A&P spends up 35% in Q4 and 18% in FY25; resisted cutting A&P to protect margins
items.quote: A&P spends were up 35% in Q4 and up 18% in FY25. Now if A&P had grown in line with our top line growth, our EBITDA growth would have moved to 9% on a full year basis and we would have delivered 20.3% EBITDA margin for the period.

items.statement: Foods gross margins structurally expanded ~1,000 bps cumulatively over FY24 and FY25
items.quote: In Foods, we have structurally expanded gross margin s by ~1,000 bps over FY 24 and FY 25, on a cumulative basis, and we expect gradual margin expansion as the business scales in the medium term.

items.statement: Foods annual revenue surpassed ₹900 crore in FY25 with 30%+ growth
items.quote: Foods delivered robust value growth of 44% YoY in Q4 and 30%+ growth in FY25, surpassing the ₹900 crore mark in annual revenues.

items.statement: Digital-first portfolio exited FY25 at ₹750 crore ARR, ahead of aspirations
items.quote: The Digital-first portfolio exited FY25 at ₹750 crores ARR, much ahead of aspirations.

items.statement: Beardo scaled ~4x since FY21, reached near double-digit EBITDA margin
items.quote: Beardo has scaled ~4x since FY21 and has reached near double-digit EBITDA margin.

items.statement: Just Herbs crossed ₹100 crore revenue mark in FY25
items.quote: Just Herbs crossed ₹100 crores revenue mark in FY25.

items.statement: International business sustained double-digit constant currency growth in Q4 and FY25
items.quote: Moving to International business we have sustained a double -digit constant currency growth momentum in Q4 and FY25.

items.statement: Premium business revenue share in international rose from 20% in FY21 to 29% in FY25
items.quote: As a result, the premium business revenue share in the international business rose from 20% in FY 21 to 29% in FY 25.

items.statement: Investing in Project SETU for rural outlet expansion and direct distribution improvement
items.quote: Under SETU , we will focus on rural outlet expansion at a pan-India level, while deploying strong control frameworks to ensure sustainable outlet expansion across markets.

items.statement: Quick commerce scaled to ~3% of India business, building assortment across categories
items.quote: Quick commerce has rapidly scaled up to ~3% of the India business, where we are building assortment across categories to effectively capitalize on the potential of this channel.

items.statement: Copra prices expected to correct towards Q2 FY26; Parachute took 30%+ cumulative price increases
items.quote: Given the extended firmness in copra prices due to lower arrival in the market, the awaited correction is most probably going to happen towards Q2. As prices move from the current hyperinflationary zone to a moderately inflationary zone in Q2, which should be the case for most of the year, we expect volume growth to pick up.

items.statement: Saffola edible oil volumes to be steady if vegetable oil prices remain stable
items.quote: While revenue growth in the coming year will be aided by pricing to some degree, we expect volumes to be steady as long as vegetable oil prices remain stable.

items.statement: Value-added hair oils gained 120 bps value market share, mid/premium segments driving recovery
items.quote: The franchise has gained 120 bps in value market share. We are confident of sustaining the improving growth trajectory through next year, backed by continued innovation, ATL investment s, and focused brand activation.

items.statement: General Trade sluggish; Project SETU progressing well to revive GT through rural outlet expansion
items.quote: While alternate channels gained salience particularly in Tier 1 markets, General Trade remained sluggish. We are making concerted efforts to revive GT through Project SETU, which is progressing well.

items.statement: Local copra players facing supply chain disruption; branded competition taking significant price increases
items.quote: We are already seeing first signs of supply chain disruption among local players, as well as competition taking significant price increases and reducing BTL . All th ese will be a tailwind s for the brand for volume growth to pick up sometime in Q2.

items.statement: Small copra players facing working capital constraints at higher prices, reducing competitive presence
items.quote: Second, availability is also a problem as they have to get working capital to buy copra, at higher prices.

items.statement: Bangladesh declared record high dividend payout in FY25 from surplus cash on balance sheet
items.quote: Surplus cash lying on the balance sheet, and it is only prudent to return it back to the shareholders rather earning interest income on that.

items.statement: Parachute maintained stronghold gaining ~70 bps market share on MAT basis
items.quote: Parachute maintained its stronghold gaining ~70 bps market share on MAT basis.

items.statement: Copra price correction awaited; hyperinflationary cycle impacting Parachute consumption titration
items.quote: Parachute had a muted quarter as a result of consumption titration, which is typical during hyperinflationary cycles like the one we are witnessing currently.

items.statement: FY26 credit growth guidance 12%, deposit growth 10%, CASA target at least 48%, NIM 3.70-3.80%, ROA maintained at 1.32%, ROE 16-17%, GNPA below 3%
items.quote: Now, for March 2025-26 market guidance, we expect the credit growth to be at 12%, deposit growth to be at 10%. We want to improve the CASA to at least 48%. NIM, we will be satisfied with 3.70 to 3.80. ROA, we will try to maintain the ROA at the moment. Return on equity expected in between 16% to 17%, and GNPA below 3%.

items.statement: Cost-to-income ratio target around 50% in a year and a half from current 57.73%
items.quote: Our target is to reach to around 50% in a couple of years, maybe in a year and a half. So, that is the guidance we have.

items.statement: FY25 NIM 3.92%, well above guidance; FY26 guidance 3.70-3.80% factoring rate cuts
items.quote: Withstanding the continuing pricing pressures on liability side, with the cost of deposits at 4.75%, the Bank has been able to maintain its margins with NIM of 3.92 for the financial year, which is well above our guidance and perhaps the only Bank to maintain the NIMs of 2024.

items.statement: 52% of loan book floating rate, 48% fixed; 38% personal loans to govt employees under MoU provide rate protection
items.quote: See, 52% of our loan book is at a floating rate and 48% is in the other category. So, having said that, again, we have the advantage of 38% of personal segment loans that I have already mentioned where the loans are towards the government employees under MoU with the Jammu and Kashmir government.

items.statement: Targeting retail loan growth in rest of India (housing, car loans) to reduce concentration risk; corporate book second line of defense
items.quote: We are now aiming at improving the retail loan book of rest of India. That is something which we are really looking at. The corporate loan book growth will remain as a second line of defense for us.

items.statement: Corporate CAPEX pipeline in J&K/Ladakh tied up around Rs 2,500-3,000 crore; Rs 1,000 crore sanctioned likely to disburse soon, another Rs 500 crore in sanction process
items.quote: I guess if we include these two, I think Rs. 2,500 to Rs. 3,000 crores of projects within this state of UT, this UT of Jammu and Kashmir and Ladakh, which we are already tied up. And there are a couple of others where we are seriously thinking of participating, but with a due diligence and understanding the viability of the project.

items.quote: GNPA at 3.37%, NNPA of 0.79% and provision coverage ratio of above 90%. Excluding the technical write-off of around Rs. 325 crores in Quarter 4, GNPA would have been only 3.67%. There has been a slight slowdown in recoveries which can be attributed to the slowdown in the domestic economy on the back of global trade tensions. However, with a strong credit discipline, we have been able to keep our s

items.quote: we are now digitizing the loan journeys of all products , l iterally all products including agriculture so that there is minimum manual intervention , t he efficiency is improved , t he turnaround time is further improved. items.quote: The record internal accruals have boosted our capital adequacy to 16.29% with CET-1 at 12.95%. Though at present the Bank is placed comfortably, however, the Bank may consider raising both debt and equity capital in this fiscal for funding its growth.

items.statement: ROA 1.32%, ROE 17.37% for FY25; cost-to-income 57.73% (structural shift via digital)

Another significant achievement of this fiscal has been the substantial moderation of our cost-to-income ratio, recorded at 57.73% for the financial year.

items.statement: Personal finance 38% of loan book (+10% YoY); housing +11.5%, car loans +21.5% in rest of India; retail:corporate ~2:1; MSME 18% of book (micro Rs 16,000 cr, small Rs 3,200 cr, medium Rs 1,200 cr)

items.statement: Intense deposit competition from SFBs and FinTechs offering higher rates; household wealth in bank deposits fell from 53% to 42% (2020-24)
items.quote: The numbers for deposits are a reflection of systemic factors like intensive competition from small finance banks and FinTechs offering higher rates, increase in interest rate sensitivity of customers, and movement of funds to equity markets with Bank deposits reducing from 53% to 42% of household wealth between 2020 and 2024.

items.statement: 5-year vision: profit Rs 5,000 cr, business >Rs 5 lakh cr; retail-focused, all-round growth across 20 states beyond J&K; cautious on risk
items.value: Profit Rs 5,000 cr, Business >Rs 5 lakh cr
items.quote: So, we actually see the Bank at a very, very strong position 5 years from now. I don't think that this should be taken as guidance or anything. But we are looking at a profit level of Rs. 5,000 crores, maybe a business level of more than Rs. 5 lakh crores in 5 years' time.

items.statement: Leadership transition: first full year of MD & CEO Amitava Chatterjee; addressing procedural gaps post-transition
items.quote: Also, given that it is my first full year in Jammu and charge at this Bank, we will be making certain changes and addressing any procedural gaps which usually follow a leadership transition to help us drive forward in the coming years.

items.statement: Crisil expects at least two more repo rate cuts of 25 bps each in the rest of fiscal 2026
items.quote: Crisil expects at least two more repo rate cuts of 25 bps each in the rest of fiscal 2026.

items.statement: Bank credit growth expected to grow 12%-13% in Fiscal 2026 vs 11-11.5% estimated for Fiscal 2025
items.quote: Bank credit is likely to grow to 12%-13% just Fiscal, compared with 11-11.5% estimated for Fiscal 2025.

items.statement: Expect slight uptick in bank credit growth by 100 to 200 bps year-on-year in fiscal 2026
items.quote: We expect a slight uptick in the bank credit growth by 100 to 200 bps on -year in fiscal 2026.

items.statement: Global clients maintaining measured stance on discretionary spends but continuing transformation initiatives in cloud, data analytics, AIML, regulatory automation
items.quote: Globally, while the banks are maintaining their measured stance towards discretionary spends, we are seeing clients going ahead with transformation initiatives, with spends continuing in areas such as cloud data analytics, AIML automation requirement on the regulatory side.

items.statement: Asset managers increasing willingness for transformations due to cost-to-income pressure; private markets traction continues
items.quote: Asset managers continue to face pressure on improving cost -to-income ratio and thus have increased willingness towards undertaking transformations. We see continued traction in the private markets due to sustained client activity.

items.statement: Elevated uncertainty may lead to tighter client budgets and delays in discretionary spending by global clients
items.quote: However, elevated uncertainty may lead to tighter client budgets and delays in discretionary spending by global clients.

items.statement: Domestic mutual fund AUM stable compared to last quarter given market volatility; passive and alternate segments progressing well
items.quote: Our AUM has been stable compared to the last quarter, as you can see on the slide, given the volatility in the market in recent months. The move towards passive and the alternate segments continues to progress well.

items.statement: Research, Analytics and Solutions segment margin in 2024 was higher by 2.4% compared to previous year
items.quote: The segment margin in 2024 was higher by 2.4% compared to that of the previous year.

items.statement: Q1 2025 segmental profit grew approximately 16% year-on-year on back of changing product mix and continued focus on margins
items.quote: Segmental profit, on the other hand, witnessed a strong uptick in Q1 2025, growing approximately 16% on year, on the back of changing product mix and continued focus on margins.

items.statement: Rating Services segment grew about 32.5% Y-o-Y in Q1 2025
items.quote: Overall, the Rating Services segment grew by about 32.5% Y-o-Y in Q1 2025.

items.statement: Global Analytical Center saw strong growth from new engagements and robust surveillance work delegation from S&P Global Ratings
items.quote: The Global Analytical Center, GAC, division saw strong growth from new engagements and robust surveillance work delegation from S&P Global Rating Services.

items.statement: Crisil Coalition Greenwich saw good momentum in corporate and investment banking with scaling of product offerings and positive client engagement from large commercial banks
items.quote: Crisil Coalition Greenwich saw good momentum in corporate and investment banking, with scaling of product offerings and positive client engagement from large commercial banks.

items.statement: Crisil Intelligence witnessed momentum in industry research, consulting, credit, and risk offerings; integrated Gen-AI into Credit+ ICON
items.quote: Crisil Intelligence witnessed momentum in industry research, consulting, credit, and risk offerings. We integrated our Gen -AI capabilities into the credit assessment and credit solution, Credit+ ICON, which we offer to our clients.

items.statement: Continue to make significant investments in digital infrastructure, information security, and building a future-ready talent pool
items.quote: We continue to make significant investments in digital infrast ructure, information security, and building a future-ready talent pool.

items.statement: Investing in new-age technologies including Gen-AI; successfully deployed Gen-AI credit assessment solution for global clients in 2024
items.quote: We are investing in new -age technologies, including Gen -AI, and in 2024, we successfully deployed a Gen-AI credit assessment solution for our global clients in one of our businesses.

items.statement: Crisil continues to have a global presence with more than 4,600 employees
items.quote: Crisil continues to have a global presence with more than 4,600 employees.

items.statement: Declining G-sec yields can lead to reduction in AAA and AA-rated corporate bond spreads, thereby reducing overall corporate bond yields
items.quote: Declining G-sec yields can lead to a reduction in AAA and AA -rated corporate bond spreads, thereby reducing the overall corporate bond yields.

items.statement: Continued investor preference for Crisil Ratings aided growth in new rating revenues
items.quote: The growth in new rating revenues is aided by continued investor preference for Crisil Ratings.

items.statement: Strengthening demand from large commercial banks for Crisil Coalition Greenwich products
items.quote: Crisil Coalition Greenwich saw good momentum in corporate and investment banking, with scaling of product offerings and positive client engagement from large commercial banks, strengthening demand for our products.

items.statement: GCCs scaling up but enough demand for both GCCs and third-party players like Crisil; niche solutions remain differentiator
items.quote: I think it is, I would say, it isn't one way solution. I think there is enough demand both for the GCCs as well as third party players like us.

items.statement: RBI cut key policy rates by 25 bps for second consecutive time in April 2025, cumulative 50 bps reduction in 2025; changed stance to accommodative

items.statement: RBI rolled back increase in risk weights for bank loans to NBFCs effective April 1, 2025
items.quote: With effect from April 1, 2025, the RBI has rolled back the increase in the risk weights for bank loans to NBFCs that was announced in November 2023.

items.statement: Global operations generate significant revenue in foreign currencies; Crisil has well-structured hedging policy using forward contracts as buffer against FX volatility
items.quote: Our global operations generate significant revenue in foreign currencies, thus leading to the risk of exchange rate fluctuation, which can negatively impact profitability. items.statement: Declared first interim dividend of INR 8 for Q1 FY25 compared to INR 7 at end of quarter one last year

items.statement: Attrition rate has been stable compared to past trends and is in line with industry trends
items.quote: Having said that, our attrition rate has been stable compared to past trends and is in line with industry trends.

items.statement: Macroeconomic and geopolitical risks kept on active watch; no material direct impact on businesses seen yet
items.quote: Given the current circumstances, we've kept this risk on active watch given global developments. However, at this stage, we have not seen any material direct impact on our businesses on account of geopolitical conditions.

items.statement: India's GDP expected to grow at 6.5% in Fiscal 2026 with downward bias
items.quote: India's GDP is expected to grow at 6.5% in Fiscal 2026, with a downward bias.

items.statement: Bank credit growth declined to 11% as on February 2025 vs 16.6% as on February 2024; wholesale bank credit growth slowed to 9.8% vs 15.2%
items.quote: other hand, the bank credit growth has declined on Y -o-Y basis to 11% as on February 2025 versus 16.6% as on February 2024, due to slowdown in services and retail sector credit growth. items.statement: Gross non-performing assets declined to 2.5%-2.6% of advances driven by lower slippage, steady write-offs, efficient recovery, and shift to retail portfolio

The lower NPAs at 2.5% to 2.6% of advances means that the bank s' balance sheets are adequately healthy to meet the current demand.

items.statement: Mutual fund AUM accounted for all-time high of 18.2% of GDP in fiscal 2024

items.statement: Q1 FY25 revenue grew 10.2% Y-o-Y; PBT and PAT grew approximately 16% Y-o-Y

items.statement: JJM fund release of Rs 70,000 crore puts water infra projects on track; full impact from Q2 FY26
items.quote: This year, the Government has released Rs. 70,000 crores. So , that puts the JJM projects on track. The full impact of that would come in Q2 onwards.

items.statement: Water infrastructure demand strong; HAM model and multilateral funding driving pipe demand

items.statement: Order book at $1.3 billion, down marginally from $1.4 billion as deliberate strategy due to Q4 slowdown
items.quote: Already spoke about the order book. 1.4 billion last year , 1.325, the marginally lower, more of a deliberate strategy because we were seeing some slowdown in Q4.

items.statement: New order received from Saudi Arabia; order book expected to recover
items.quote: So, it will come back because yesterday only we got a very good order from Saudi. So, the order book will come back.

items.statement: Nashik seamless capacity to reach 4.5 lakh tons; Haresamudram DI capacity addition of 1 lakh ton
items.quote: Nashik capacity would go to 4.5 lakh tons, and we would add about 1 lakh ton in Haresamudram.

items.statement: Cost reduction initiatives: PCI, 3rd Coke Oven Battery at Pragpur, waste heat recovery
items.quote: cost reduction initiatives like introduction of PCI 3rd Coke Oven Battery in Pra gpur, subsequent generation of energy from waste to heat.

items.statement: Large diameter pipe headroom allows 10-15% volume growth over next 2-3 years
items.quote: On large Dia, we expect that maybe there is a headroom because as you know in large Dia pipes because of the changeover, the thickness etc., there is a headroom. We can expect 10 % to 15% growth.

items.statement: DI prices stable; no reduction expected; NSR and margins maintained
items.quote: Our DI prices stay stable , and we don't expect any fall in our DI price , and therefore the correction of whatever that you are talking about is not relevant to as far as Jindal Saw is concerned.

items.quote: Luckily, the raw material prices are in a band where the commodity prices seem to be stable and easing out. Going forward , looking at the China scenario , we don't see any disruption in the commodity prices

items.quote: We keep an eye on our rating, which is Double A, and it's significant to mention that even after this JITF Single Bench judgment, we repaid everything, the rating has not changed.

items.statement: JITF cash losses of Rs 345 crore (incl. Rs 146 crore write-off) vs Rs 157 crore prior year; excluding write-off, losses flat
items.quote: Current year numbers which you are seeing is inclusive of this Rs. 146 crore, which we have explained earlier. So, if you exclude that number, then both the numbers are at the same range.

items.statement: Hunting JV contributed Rs 27 crore PAT in consolidated results; first year profit Rs 50 crore+; full order book; first-mover advantage in premium connections

items.statement: Dividend payout maintained at FY24 level to conserve cash for new projects
items.quote: This year also, since the results were similar , we have maintained the same dividend payout. Idea is to conserve cash as we are looking for now getting into some new projects.

items.quote: irrespective of whatever is the outcome of the final judgment, t here cannot be any financial burden on JITF. All the money that was received has been repaid. On the contrary, if the decision goes in favor of JITF, it gets back everything including interest

items.statement: States adopting Hybrid Annuity Model (HAM) for water projects; EPC contractors to participate with equity and O&M
items.quote: many of the states have come up with a new business model, which they call HAM, which is a hybrid annuity model where the EPC contractors are expected to participate in a big way wherein they become a partner with the Government even in putting equity and then they implement the whole project, do the O&M for a period of time and then hand over.

items.statement: Focus on value-added products: coatings, stainless steel, higher grades, threading, premium connections, OCTG
items.quote: Then we would get an incremental margin on account of things like threading, premium connection, OCTG , value added products, stainless steel and all of those.

items.statement: Targeting $2-3 billion valuation each for scalable growth gems by FY30
items.quote: Scalable growth gems have a very clear competitive advantage. They've demonstrated that and therefore, now have a target of $2 to $3 billion of val uation each by F30, in the next five years

items.statement: Targeting $1 billion valuation for emerging growth gems in next five years
items.quote: These are businesses that we want to get to a billion dollars of market valuation in the next five years and then hopefully move them higher.

items.statement: Hospitality business targets 2-3x room inventory growth in next 5 years

items.statement: Real Estate targets Rs 10,000 crore presales in next 5 years with 70-80% land acquired
items.quote: We've taken the liberty of running up to 10,000 crore because the presales that they have committed to for the next 5 years, 70% to 80% of that land has been acquired already.

items.statement: Susten committed to 5x growth plan before FY30

items.statement: Last Mile Mobility targets another 2-3x growth from current 78,000 vehicles
items.quote: Last Mile Mobility, has been a fantastic story from 14,000 vehicles a year, we had 78,000 now, which is 5x already and the plans to get to another 2x to 3x from there.

items.statement: Auto standalone margin 10% without BEVs, 9.2% with contract manufacturing, 9.5% consolidated

items.quote: MEAL as a company was EBITDA positive in its first quarter of operation. It made a INR 10 crore EBITDA profit without accruing any PLI.

items.statement: SUV volumes up 20% in FY25, exceeding mid-to-high teens target

items.quote: While inquiries are good on Pack 1 and Pack 2, they don't get converted right now into bookings because people do want to see the vehicles before they book.

items.statement: Thar capacity 9,000 to 10,500; 3XO capacity +1,500 to ~11,000; 1.2 lakh new capacity at Chakan for new platform; Greenfield plant planned for FY28+
items.quote: The Thar capacity will move from 9,000 to 10,500, that's 1500 addition or 9,500 to 11,000. The 3XO capacity moves up by 1500 to about 11,000, and we are going to create 1.2 lakhs of new capacity in Chakan plant for the platform that I just spoke about.

items.statement: 3 ICE, 2 born-electric, 2 LCV launches planned in CY2026; new platform vision Aug 15 for 2027+ products
items.quote: In the calendar year 2026, we expect 3 ICE products, two born electric products, and two LCV's in calendar year 2026. Out of those 3, two are mid cycle refreshes. items.statement: EV sell prices indexed to global commodity prices with one-quarter lag; no immediate price hike planned
items.quote: The sell prices are indexed, so you know any benefit that is happening out of sell prices being moderated downward around the world, which is what is happening does translate back to us. So, we are indexed on that and that's an important factor from a material cost

items.statement: Cost reduction programs underway on launched EV products like ICE reengineering
items.quote: There are cost reduction programs underway on both the products that we've launched like we do in any ICE products.

items.quote: There is a very large segment of people who will want 79 kWh in lower packs. Now, this has been very different than the assumption in which we went that 79 kWh will give only in the top end and everything else will be 59.

items.quote: We have deliberately had a slowdown in disbursements to focus on asset quality and to focus on controls.

items.quote: At that time, our reported numbers were 4% on ROE and 16.21 EPS, and we had committed to 18% ROE and 15% to 20% EPS growth. items.quote: With Hemant Sikka coming in to lead it now, one of our strongest leaders, we feel that this business will get on a very strong path going forward.

items.statement: Fabric revenue expected to grow 10% in FY26 and ~30% in FY27 on constant prices
items.quote: On fabric side, keeping the prices constant, we can expect the revenue increase in FY26 by 10% and the year after that we can expect about 30%.

items.quote: So absolute number on the fabric side it's about Rs.4,000 crores turnover there, so 10% that is about Rs.500 crores for the year and a year after that maybe about Rs.1,000 crores or so.

items.statement: Synthetic fabric expansion Phase I: 1.5 million meters/month; Phase II timing depends on market acceptance
items.quote: And as for synthetics so we have two phases. So phase-I is 15,00,000 meters per month, that would be coming now and then bases how quickly we are able to establish our product and our brand name in this segment, we will expand according to that.

items.statement: Major margin improvement in Q4 driven by fabric segment; yarn margin improved but fabric contributed substantially
items.quote: For Vardhman, major improvement is coming from the fabric margin, though there is an improvement in the yarn in this quarter, but I think substantial increase is on account of the fabric.

items.quote: So depending upon how much those products we are in a position to sell or that kind of business is set to the India we are all buyers, the advantage would come in, but in any case, whatever expenditure we do, our expectation is always at least 15% EBITDA margin should come over and above the existing costs.

items.statement: Domestic polyester/viscose 18-20% expensive vs Vietnam/Taiwan/Thailand/China due to BIS quality control order blocking imports
items.quote: Our raw material both polyester and viscose are almost as of now expensive by about 18% to 20% compared to the material which is there in Vietnam or Taiwan, Thailand or China.

items.statement: Fabric demand strong in Q4 from US/UK/EU retail; ran at full capacity; best quarter ever
items.quote: There was good demand from the markets all around. There was good retail sales during the festive season of Christmas and New Year. items.statement: US brands view tariffs as short-term pain for long-term gain; Vardhman engaging proactively as strategic partner
items.quote: Some of our US-based customers are referring to this situation as short-term pain for long-term-gain and we share the same optimism. items.statement: Yarn exports: ~50% to Bangladesh, rest to Asia/Central America/Mexico; fabric exports similar
items.quote: I think as a country, whatever yarn we export, 50% goes to Bangladesh and remaining goes to most of the Asian countries or the Central America, maybe some part of this goes to Mexico and so on and so forth. items.statement: Bangladesh land route closed; shipping adds 10-12 days lead time but no material cost difference
items.quote: So the cost is not really very expensive, but more impact is on the serviceability because it takes almost three weeks if we send the material through ship and whereas by road it takes only about 10 days. So there is a gap of about 10 days, 12 days on the delivery side.

items.statement: Other income up due to Rs.25-26 cr land purchase and forex MTM gains
items.quote: The other income increase is due to land purchase for one of our plants, which is about Rs.25 crores, Rs.26 crores. Other than that I think it's all normal and the remaining is we do mark-to-market on the dollar rupee also.

items.statement: Industry consolidation: smaller players exiting due to unsustainable margins

items.statement: Country spinning capacity utilization down 15-18% in last 2 years due to low margins

items.statement: Fertilizer manufactured EBITDA per ton guidance of Rs 4,500-5,000 for FY26 maintained

items.quote: Yes. When the plant gets commissioned, the value addition of the plant flows in, we should see that sort of improvement.

items.statement: Ma'aden long-term contract for 300k tons DAP/NPK annually, potential to scale to 500k tons
items.quote: Right now, the contract is for 300,000 tons and we can potentially go up to 0.5 million tons.

items.statement: Crop protection outlook positive with high double-digit growth expected across domestic formulation, B2B and exports in FY26

items.statement: Crop protection EBIT grew 25% to Rs 365 cr in FY25 on new products and improved demand; specialty nutrients EBITDA margin 18-20%
items.quote: EBIT has grown by 25% to Rs. 365 crores as improved demand for its key molecules in domestic and export markets and performance of new products and captive molecules enhance d the profitability for the business.

items.statement: NPK share rose to 60% of phosphatic sales in FY25 from 51% YoY; unique grades 35% of manufactured volumes

items.statement: Retail footprint expanded by 130+ Mana Gromor centers in FY25; entered Maharashtra and Tamil Nadu; 99% stores profitable

items.statement: NACL debt secured for capex; aim to reduce via working capital control and cash flow from full capacity utilization; no timeline given
