items.statement: Premium business share in international revenue rose from 20% in FY21 to 29% in FY25
items.quote: As a result, the premium business revenue share in the international business rose from 20% in FY 21 to 29% in FY 25.

items.statement: Quick commerce contributes ~7% for Foods category vs ~3% for overall FMCG
items.quote: And if you look at interestingly one piece of data, if quick comm has been contributing to 3% of FMCG and especially in BPC, in Food quick comm contributes nearly 7%.

items.statement: Small copra players facing supply chain disruption and working capital constraints
items.quote: We are already seeing first signs of supply chain disruption among local players, as well as competition taking significant price increases and reducing BTL . All th ese will be a tailwind s for the brand for volume growth to pick up sometime in Q2.

items.statement: Branded competition in coconut oil taking price increases in line with cost, sometimes disproportionate
items.quote: As far as branded competition is concerned, I think last year, we saw a little unreasonable competition but perhaps they are not making margins. They have now taken price increases in line with the cost increase and sometimes disproportionate, which also helps us in a way.

items.statement: Bangladesh declared record high dividend payout in FY25 from surplus cash, not compromising investment
items.quote: Surplus cash lying on the balance sheet, and it is only prudent to return it back to the shareholders rather earning interest income on that. We are not compromising any investment opportunity, the A&P also continues to grow.

items.statement: Copra hyperinflation may persist longer than expected, delaying volume recovery
items.quote: Given the extended firmness in copra prices due to lower arrival in the market, the awaited correction is most probably going to happen towards Q2. As prices move from the current hyperinflationary zone to a moderately inflationary zone in Q2, which should be the case for most of the year, we expect volume growth to pick up.

items.statement: FY26 credit growth target 12%, deposit growth 10%, CASA at least 48%, NIM 3.70-3.80%, ROA maintained at 1.32%, ROE 16-17%, GNPA below 3%
items.quote: Now, for March 2025-26 market guidance, we expect the credit growth to be at 12%, deposit growth to be at 10%. We want to improve the CASA to at least 48%. NIM, we will be satisfied with 3.70 to 3.80. ROA, we will try to maintain the ROA at the moment. Return on equity expected in between 16% to 17%, and GNPA below 3%.

items.statement: Cost-to-income ratio target around 50% in a year and a half from current 57.73%
items.quote: Our target is to reach to around 50% in a couple of years, maybe in a year and a half. So, that is the guidance we have.

items.statement: FY25 NIM 3.92%, well above guidance; FY26 guidance 3.70-3.80% due to rate cuts
items.quote: Withstanding the continuing pricing pressures on liability side, with the cost of deposits at 4.75%, the Bank has been able to maintain its margins with NIM of 3.92 for the financial year, which is well above our guidance and perhaps the only Bank to maintain the NIMs of 2024.

items.statement: 52% of loan book floating rate, 48% fixed; 38% personal loans to govt employees with protected rates
items.quote: See, 52% of our loan book is at a floating rate and 48% is in the other category. So, having said that, again, we have the advantage of 38% of personal segment loans that I have already mentioned where the loans are towards the government employees under MoU with the Jammu and Kashmir government.

items.statement: Personal finance 38% of loan book grew 10% YoY; housing loans 11.5%, car loans 21.5% in rest of India
items.quote: Our biggest sector, that is the personal finance, contributing 38% of our loan book has grown at 10% Y-o-Y, with growth in ROI at 16.2%, again surpassing JKL at 9.3%. Within personal finance, housing loans have grown at 11.5%, whereas in rest of India, they have grown at 16% with car loans also growing at 21.5%.

items.statement: Capex pipeline in J&K/Ladakh tied up Rs 2,500-3,000 cr; Rs 1,000 cr sanctioned, Rs 500 cr in process
items.quote: I guess if we include these two, I think Rs. 2,500 to Rs. 3,000 crores of projects within this state of UT, this UT of Jammu and Kashmir and Ladakh, which we are already tied up.

items.statement: Credit cost increase expected 20-30 bps max in FY26; no significant increase
items.quote: If you consider 20 to 30 bps as an increase in credit cost, I would say that there will be an increase. But it is not likely to be more than 20 bps or 30 bps. So, no significant increase in the credit cost is expected by the Bank going forward.

items.statement: SMA-1 increase technical (>70%); installment dates aligned with salary dates from 3 May; expect substantial SMA drop by 30 May
items.quote: Essentially, what was happening in this Bank was the loan installments were not aligned with the dates of salary payments of the employees. So, we have now aligned the installment date with the salary date. So going forward, you may see a substantial drop in the SM As in the loan book of J&K Bank

items.statement: MSME book: micro Rs 16,000 cr (15%), small Rs 3,200 cr (3%), medium Rs 1,200 cr (1.1%); mostly services
items.quote: Yes, credit to micro enterprises is around 16 ,000 crores, which is 15% of loan book of which manufacturing is 2% and service is 13%. Then, credit to small enterprises is around Rs. 3,200 crores, which is 3% of the loan book.

items.statement: No credit card book, no microfinance book, no personal loans outside government employees
items.quote: No. Personal loan book, we do not have anything outside the government employees , a nd microfinance also. And there is hardly any microfinance institution in this state.

items.statement: FY25 other income +38% YoY crossing Rs 1,000 cr; TWO recoveries Rs 390 cr vs Rs 134 cr FY24; Q4 TWO Rs 168 cr
items.quote: Other income has witnessed a substantial jump of around 38% in Financial Year 2025, crossing Rs. 1,000 crore mark, mainly on the back of total TWO recovery of around Rs. 390 crores during the year, compared to Rs. 134 crores in Financial Year 2024.

items.statement: Employee cost flat after one-off gratuity reversal; no recruitment plans, retirements lined up, salary revision done; no increase expected for 1-2 years
items.quote: And the second is, since immediately we do not have any plans of recruitment , and there are some retirements lined up, and also the salary revision thing is over and out by now, so I do not see any increase in the employee cost going forward at least for a year or two.

items.statement: Digital transactions >90% in FY25; digitising all loan journeys including agriculture; completion expected this quarter
items.quote: We are now digitizing the loan journeys of all products , l iterally all products including agriculture so that there is minimum manual intervention , t he efficiency is improved , t he turnaround time is further improved. So, these are the processes we are likely to complete within this quarter.

items.statement: CRAR 16.29%, CET-1 12.95%; may raise debt and equity in FY26 for growth funding
items.quote: Though at present the Bank is placed comfortably, however, the Bank may consider raising both debt and equity capital in this fiscal for funding its growth.

items.statement: Equity raise options open (QIP, government); timing depends on credit growth needs and opportune moment
items.quote: See, we haven't yet finally decided on that. I said that we may be raising, it depends on the requirement of the credit growth that we may be expecting. At the moment, I said that we are comfortably placed with the CRAR. Going forward, if the credit growth demands a raise, we will look at all the options.

items.statement: Board approved dividend 215% for FY25; third consecutive year
items.quote: Also, I am pleased to share that Board has approved a dividend of 215% for the Financial Year 2025, marking our third consecutive year of rewarding our shareholders and showing our gratitude for their confidence in us.

items.statement: No material impact from Pahalgam terror incident; tourism credit exposure <1% of portfolio
items.quote: I want to assure you all that we do not anticipate any material impact on our business or financial performance as our credit exposure to the tourism sector in Kashmir Division, is not even 1% of our overall credit portfolio.

items.statement: CASA ratio 47.01% vs industry 37.9% (Dec 2024); term deposits +18% YoY, current +9.6%, savings flat
items.quote: Though we have also witnessed a reduction in CASA ratio, yet we remain amongst the best in the industry with 47.01% CASA ratio.

items.statement: ROA 1.32%, ROE 17.37%, cost-to-income 57.73% for FY25
items.quote: Similarly, on the back of another record -breaking year, Bank has been able to deliver on its guidance with return on assets of 1.32% and return on equity of 17.37%. Another significant achievement of this fiscal has been the substantial moderation of our cost -to-income ratio, recorded at 57.73% for the financial year.

items.statement: Leadership transition changes and procedural gap fixes planned in first full year of MD
items.quote: Also, given that it is my first full year in Jammu and charge at this Bank, we will be making certain changes and addressing any procedural gaps which usually follow a leadership transition to help us drive forward in the coming years.

items.statement: Long-term vision: Rs 5,000 cr profit, >Rs 5 lakh cr business in 5 years; retail-focused, all-round growth
items.value: Rs 5,000 cr profit, >Rs 5 lakh cr business
items.quote: I don't think that this should be taken as guidance or anything. But we are looking at a profit level of Rs. 5,000 crores, maybe a business level of more than Rs. 5 lakh crores in 5 years' time.

items.statement: FY26 deposit growth guidance 8-10%, advances growth 10-12%
items.quote: If I talk of the guidance for the FY 2025-26, we are giving guidance for deposit of 8-10% and advances of 10-12%.

items.statement: FY26 CASA ratio guidance around 40%, LDR around 80%
items.quote: We are giving guidance to maintain CASA around 40%. We would like to maintain LDR around 80% range.

items.statement: FY26 Gross NPA guidance <3%, Net NPA maintain current 0.19%
items.quote: Gross NPA , we are giving guidance to maintain less than 3% and we’ll maintain the current levels of n et NPA, because we have already reached 0.19

items.statement: FY26 recovery guidance Rs.5,500-6,500 crore
items.quote: Further, we are giving recovery guidance of Rs.5,500 crores to Rs.6,500 crores.

items.statement: FY26 NIM guidance revised to 3.15-3.30% due to rate cuts
items.quote: we are giving a revised NIM guidance in the range of 3.15% to 3.30%.

items.statement: FY26 RoA guidance 1.20% due to asset growth and profitability moderation
items.quote: we are giving RoA guidance in the range of 1.20%.

items.statement: FY26 cost-to-income ratio guidance around 45%
items.quote: We will be able to maintain cost-to-income ratio around 45%.

items.statement: FY26 credit cost guidance <1%, slippage guidance <1%
items.quote: Credit cost, I am giving guidance of less than 1%, slippage also we are giving guidance of less than 1%.

items.statement: Corporate loan growth target ~9% for FY26
items.quote: Corporate, we have kept a target of around 9% growth.

items.statement: SMA book down from Rs.79,931 crore (Mar'24) to Rs.45,923 crore (Mar'25), 8.06% of advances
items.quote: SMA book has come down significantly from Rs.79,931 crore as on Mar'24 to Rs.45,923 crore as on Mar'25. And SMA 2 book (more than Rs.5 crore) is only Rs.659 crore and there is only one account of Rs.160 crore in SMA 2 book ( more than Rs.25 crore), and we have made 100% provision there.

items.statement: Slippage ratio Q4 FY25 1.09% (QoQ up from 0.78%), FY25 1.11% (YoY down from 1.49%)
items.quote: Slippage ratio was increased for QoQ basis from 0.78% to 1.09%, as I told you on account of some MOC, but on YoY basis it has come down from 1.49% to 1.11%.

items.statement: Credit cost Q4 FY25 0.81% (QoQ up from 0.47%), FY25 0.66% (YoY down from 0.77%)
items.quote: Credit cost for QoQ basis has gone up from 0.47% to 0.81% and on YoY basis it has come down from 0.77% to 0.66%.

items.statement: Recovery FY25 Rs.7,651 crore vs slippage Rs.5,683 crore; recovery <Rs.1 crore Rs.3,396 crore (errata)
items.value: Recovery Rs.7,651 cr, Slippage Rs.5,683 cr
items.quote: recovery is continuously more than the slippage since FY22-23, this year also recovery was Rs.7,651 crores and slippage was Rs.5,683 crores.

items.statement: Written-off book ~Rs.41,000 crore, AUC recovery guidance Rs.2,000 crore (5%) for FY26
items.quote: Okay. Yes. See, my written-off book is around Rs.41,000 crore. So approximately 5% of that.

items.statement: SRs from NARCL: conservative approach, no provision release in FY25, will evaluate in FY26
items.quote: We went with the conservative approach and we have not gone for the restoration or release of the provision in this financial year. Going forward, we will see, if the need arises, we will do it , otherwise we may not opt for that.

Return on assets slightly came down from 1.39% to 1.37%. However, on YoY basis it has grown by 25 basis points from 1.07% to 1.32%. Return on equity for Q4 is almost flat at 21.01% sequentially and for full year, it is 20.76%.

items.statement: CASA ratio (domestic) 40.17%; retail TD <Rs.3 crore Rs.2.79 trillion (YoY +10%)
items.quote: We have been able to maintain CASA ratio (domestic) at 40.17% and one good thing in retail TD (less than Rs.3 crore), we have been able to reach Rs.2.79 trillion with a YoY growth of 10%.

items.statement: RAM advances Rs.3.51 trillion (YoY +13.22%, 64.23% share); Retail +13.71%, Agri +13.68%, MSME ~12%
items.quote: RAM sector, we reached Rs.3.51 trillion with QoQ growth of 4.82% and YoY growth of 13.22%. Retail, we reached Rs.1.19 trillion with QoQ growth of 3.60% and YoY growth of 13.71%. Agri, we reached Rs.1.38 trillion with QoQ growth of 6% and YoY growth of 13.68%. MSME book growth, used to be in the range of 5% to 6%. This year, we have been able to achieve growth of approximately 12% in the MSME. RAM

items.statement: Digital transactions 93% in Q4 FY25 (FY25 92% vs 87% FY24); UPI 2.67 cr/day (Mar'25) vs 1.56 cr/day (Mar'24)
items.quote: If we take the entire year FY'25, the digital transaction has gone up from 87% to 92%. If we take only this quarter, it has gone up from 89% to 93%. So presently, March '25 quarter, the digital transactions are 93%. Even on the UPI side, which used to be 1.56 crore per day transaction in March '24, now it is 2.67 crore per day.

items.statement: Digital business FY25 Rs.2.54 lakh crore (YoY 106%); FY26 target Rs.2.25 lakh crore via digital lending
items.quote: Total overall business, through digital, it is Rs.2,54,000 crore. When we started our digital journey in Apr-22, with the first launch of PAPL, we did business of Rs.5,640 crore, and then March '24, it was Rs.81,250 crore, and March '25, it is Rs.1,67,000 crore. We are projecting Rs.2,25,000 crore for the financial year 2026.

items.statement: Annual digital/IT spend Rs.1,200-1,300 crore; FY26 budget Rs.1,300-1,400 crore
items.quote: Our annual expenditure on digital and IT is in the range of Rs.1,200 crore to Rs.1,300 crore. So, we are maintaining, similar budget of Rs.1,300 crores to Rs.1,400 crores per year going forward.

items.statement: Leadership programs (Rising Star for AGM+), 6-month intensive credit/forex training for middle management
items.quote: Bank has already initiated capacity building for leadership development program s like Rising Star and this is for top management group, like AGM and above. We are also making efforts to provide capacity building for the middle management in a specific area like credit and forex. We are planning to provide an intensive training for six months, 17 weeks

items.statement: Supreme Court adverse judgment on resolved account (Rs.2,600 cr outstanding, 40% recovery); potential reversal but management views net positive if asset value increased
items.quote: We have received a copy of the judgment very recently. And of course, it is a landmark judgment and how it will impact, only time will tell. But one thing I can tell you, if at all, we have to reverse, I think it will be good for the Bank, because if you see, we have got our resolution at 40%, that means 60% haircut was there. Now that the asset is up and running, the enterprise value must have go

items.statement: Psychological impact on NCLT resolution applicants due to Supreme Court judgment after 3-4 year gap
items.quote: I think psychologically there may be some impact for resolution applicants, because it has come after substantial gap of three to four years. S o, psychologically, yes, there may be some impact

items.statement: Co-lending book <Rs.500 crore; cautious NBFC lending (well-rated only); building IT for reconciliation to scale co-lending
items.quote: As for our co-lending exposure, it currently stands at less than Rs.500 crore, which is relatively modest. The limited uptake in co-lending isn't solely due to the primary versus participative model —reconciliation challenges have been a key constraint. In the past, we've faced issues on that front, which hindered our ability to scale co-lending operations. We are in the process of building intern

items.statement: Loan book composition target 65:35 (RAM:Corporate); Q4 sanctions ~Rs.38,000 crore
items.quote: See, endeavor will be to maintain the same, around 65:35, but we are already looking for the opportunity and wherever we are getting good opportunity, we are according sanctions also. And recently, in Q4, we have been able to accord sanction of around Rs.38,000 crores.

items.statement: FY26 AUM target INR1,000 crore plus, disbursement INR400 crore, branches remain at 90
items.quote: Sir, now for FY26, we will do INR1,000 crores plus. I am not saying it will increase from INR1,000 crores to INR1,200 crores. But it will be more than INR1,000 crores. And our disbursement will be around INR400 crores. And our branches, we have 90 branches. We will work on those 90 branches.

items.statement: FY27 AUM target INR1,300-1,350 crore, disbursement INR500 crore, branches increase to 100 after crossing INR1,000 crore AUM
items.quote: And our target for next year will be around INR1,300 INR1,350 crores. And our disbursement will be around INR500 crores, and our branches we will increase above INR1,000 crores, so there the branches will become 100.

items.statement: Medium-term AUM target INR1,500 crore after FY27
items.quote: And after that, if there is next year, then we will reach around INR1,500 crore.

items.statement: FY25 disbursement INR305 crore, up 7.4% YoY
items.quote: In FY25, with the growth of 7.4%, there has been a disbursement of INR305 crores, which was INR284 crores last year.

items.statement: Net interest margin on gross loan book 10.63% in FY25, spread maintained at 10%
items.quote: The company has maintained a healthy spread of 10%. With this, the net interest margin of the gross loan book has been 10.63%.

items.statement: NIM expected to increase next quarter due to repo rate reduction benefit on fixed-rate book
items.quote: Sir, the impact of the repo rate will have its own benefit. NIM will increase. Next quarter will have a good impact. Because we are on a fixed rate. The rate that has come down and the book that has already been made, in the last few years, the loss was also on a fixed rate. Now when it has reduced we will get the benefit.

items.statement: Housing loan portfolio yield maintained at 18%, LAP at 20%; no rate reduction planned despite repo rate cuts
items.quote: No, no. Our average housing loan, that portfolio is maintained at 18% only. And our LAP sits around 20%.

items.statement: Branch expansion paused at 90; will add only 10 more branches (to 100) after crossing INR1,000 crore AUM; no further expansion for 2-3 years
items.quote: No, our target is 100 branches. We have done 90 branches. If our INR1,000 crore loan book target is achieve, then we will only make 10 more branches. Then we will not increase any branch from 100 branches for the next 2 years.

items.statement: Tamil Nadu and Telangana branches to be opened in FY26 after crossing INR1,000 crore AUM
items.quote: Yes, sir. The next 10 branches that we will open in 2026 after crossing INR1,000 crores we will go in Tamil Nadu and Telangana.

items.statement: Monthly disbursement run-rate target INR30-40 crore, implying ~INR500 crore annual disbursement capacity
items.quote: The target was that in the coming time we will do a business of INR30 crore, INR40 crore per month. So you can assume that your disbursement will be around INR500 crore per month.

items.statement: Gross NPA improved to 1.84% from 2.29%, Net NPA improved to 0.61% from 0.69% in FY25
items.quote: Gross NPA was 1.84%, which was 2.29% last year. Net NPA was 0.61%, which was 0.69% last year.

items.statement: FY25 fund raise INR274 crore (INR194 crore debt: 30% banks, 70% FIs; INR80 crore equity); outstanding borrowing INR584 crore (46% banks, 48% FIs, 6% NHB)
items.quote: done a total fund raise of INR274 crores. We have raised INR194 crores from the lender, of SRG Housing Finance Ltd Q4 & FY25 Post Earnings Conference Call May 5, 2025 04:10 PM IST 3 which 30% are from the bank and rest from FI, and INR80 crores have been raised through equity. The outstanding borrowing of the company was INR584 crores, which was INR491 crores last year. Of that 46% the company has

items.statement: Current leverage ~2.2x NOF (INR264 crore net worth); NHB allows up to 12x but industry norm ~5x, so no equity needed up to INR1,500 crore AUM
items.quote: Actually, sir, our guideline of NHB is of 12 times. You can leverage up to 12 times of your NOF. But in the industry, more than 5 times is not possible. In today's date, our 264, if we go to 5 times also, we don't need any equity up to INR250, INR1,500 crores.

items.statement: Credit rating upgraded to BBB+; expected to reach A- at INR1,000 crore AUM, lowering borrowing cost
items.quote: Now our rating has also become BBB plus. And as soon as it comes around INR1,000 crores, then our rating will also come in A minus. If we come in that rating, then it will be a little easier to take money from the bank. And as the rating increases, we will get a little benefit in the borrowing cost.

items.statement: M3 Investment acquired 9.17% stake via preferential allotment; provides equity support and long-term commitment for future capital needs
items.quote: First of all, thank you to them for their trust and hope it will be with us till long term. They have given support and they have also committed that whenever you need equity, you don't need to go anywhere. You just keep working. This is a very good thing. You get help from them.

items.statement: Senior management team of 10-12 HODs hired with 15-18 years experience across credit, recovery, operations, risk, product, HR, compliance; board includes 3 banker independent directors
items.quote: Yes, 100%. As you can see, the team of pan India is already there to grow and is expertized in holding their business smoothly. So, we have already made a team. We have experienced people with us. So, we have a team of 10, 12 people of HOD, from the finance industry.

items.statement: FY25 portfolio: 73% housing loans, 27% LAP; 26% salaried, 74% self-employed; 100% secured against property; avg ticket size INR8 lakh, avg LTV 44%
items.quote: In FY25, housing loan was 73% and loan against property was 27%. Salaried loan was 26% and self-employed loan was 74%. Our 100% loan book is secured against property. The average ticket size of the housing loan book is INR8 lakhs and the average LTV is 44%.

items.statement: Geographic diversification: Q4 FY25 disbursement 26% Maharashtra, 38% Gujarat, 26% Rajasthan, 7.25% Karnataka, 5% Andhra; rural/semi-urban focus with low competition
items.quote: In the quarter 4, the new branches that we have disbursed, we have already disbursed 26% in Maharashtra. 5% in Andhra Pradesh and 7%, 7.25% is in Karnataka. Here, we have 38% Gujarat and 26% Rajasthan. So, diversification has already happened. And as the book increases, diversification will increase.

items.statement: Limited competition in rural/semi-urban areas where SRG operates; large peers focus on urban; comfortable in current geographies
items.quote: In today's housing finance, we can't say that there is no competition, but still, where we are working, today we see that all the companies are working in urban areas. In rural and semi-urban areas, there is still not much competition. We can do comfortable work according to the business there.

items.statement: Liquidity strong with INR55 crore liquid funds; ALM position comfortable
items.quote: The company's liquidity is strong and the liquid funds in the company have been INR55 crores. Our ALM position has also been comfortable.

items.statement: ROA 3.17% in FY25 (down from 3.56%); target to cross 3.5% in FY26 and 4% in medium term as equity base absorbs expansion costs
items.quote: Sir, the ROA has reduced due to the increase in equity, but the expansion plan and the growth of the business and the growth of the PAT, the ROA should cross the 4% which has been taken by the equity, and it will cross 3.5% in the next year.

items.statement: Balance transfer activity 10-11% of book; inflows and outflows roughly offset with 1-2% net difference
items.quote: Sir, balance transfer is 10%, 11%. And the same come back. The same goes and comes back. There is a difference of 1%, 2%.

items.statement: Total confirmed order book stands at INR 1,197 crore as of March 31, 2025, with INR 1,019 crore in water domain and INR 178 crore in geospatial enterprise solutions.
items.quote: As at the March, the total order book confirmed order book stands at around INR 1,197 crores. Of this, projects in the water domain account for INR 1,019 crores and the geospatial enterprise solutions services contribute to around INR 178 crores.

items.statement: Order book increased by around INR 800 crore during FY25, though Q4 saw a decline of INR 190 crore due to execution exceeding new order inflows.
items.quote: I think the order book increase during the year was around INR 800 crores. You are talking of the quarter. You are right that the order book, which has been consumed for the execution was around INR 190 crores. And the new orders, which have been added during the quarter, was less than that.

items.statement: Current bid pipeline is around INR 355 crore, with expectation of winning at least two large projects aggregating over INR 280 crore in the next month.
items.quote: So even as we speak, we have a pipeline for which we have bid in the range of around INR 355 crores. So and that is what we expect something to happen within next one month or so. About these out of INR 355 crores, we expect the disposal of at least two of the large projects, which could be aggregating to more than INR 280 crores in the next one month or

items.statement: Management targets INR 300-400 crore of new order book additions every quarter but refuses to give revenue or margin forecasts for FY26.
items.quote: So typically, our target is to achieve INR 300 crores, INR 400 crores worth of order book every quarter, and it depends on which opportunities are available. So we cannot directly exactly Ceinsys Tech Limited Q4FY25 Results Conference call 07.05.2025 kind of speculate what will be the order book for

items.statement: EBITDA margin was 18.82% in Q4 FY25 and 18.63% for full FY25; management aims to maintain and improve margins but gives no specific target.
items.quote: We have basically said we don't want to give any future projections. What we said consistently over the last year is we do not see any headwinds and we should be able to maintain and improve our margin profile as the quarters and quarters starts unfolding.

items.statement: Technology solutions revenue grew 3.5x to INR 213 crore in FY25, increasing share of total turnover from 24% to 51%.
items.quote: The execution of technology solutions projects witnessed a 3.5-fold increase during the year 2024-2025, rising from INR 60 crores of last year to INR 213 crores of the year 2024-2025, which reflects a strong demand and enhanced delivery capabilities.

items.statement: Invested INR 12 crore in US business development during FY25, expensed in P&L.
items.quote: We have invested around INR 12 crores towards the business development for expansion into U.S. market, and this has been expensed out in the profit loss account for the year 2024-2025.

items.statement: Turnover to net working capital ratio improved from 3.2x to 4.4x in FY25; trade receivables include INR 135 crore unbilled revenue, with INR 88 crore collected in March 2025.
items.quote: A key highlight for the financial year 2024-2025 is a significant improvement in the turnover to net working capital ratio, which increased from 3.2x in the previous year to 4.4x in this year financial year 2024-2025, indicating again enhanced operational efficiency and a better capital utilization.

items.statement: Debtors have decreased year-on-year; unbilled revenue of INR 133-135 crore will be billed as milestones are achieved, majority expected by Q2-Q3 FY26.
items.quote: So when we talk about the total debtors, the trade receivables, which is we are talking of INR 253 crores, this includes the unbilled amount of INR 135 crores, while the debtors have already come down as compared to the previous year.

items.statement: Board appointed Vanish Moorthy as Additional Director and K.P. Surej as CEO Designate and Additional Director on May 3, 2025.
items.quote: One of the significant moves, the Board appointed industry veteran, Mr. Vanish Moorthy, as an Additional Director at his recent meeting on 3rd of May. Mr. Moorthy, with over 25 years of experience has led major outsourcing deals for Fortune 500 companies and currently serves as a strategic consultant through his firm, Prime Enter Incorporated.

items.statement: Prashant Kamat voluntarily surrendered his ESOPs; ESOPs for overseas employees cancelled due to resignation and performance conditions not met; ESOP cost for FY26 not finalized.
items.quote: The third portion which we referred was the ESOPs, which I was supposed to get and these were supposed to be over a period of time. However, as you would see, we have a new CEO coming up by the end of this year and it will be unfair on company and investors that exiting CEO takes all the ESOPs and walks out. items.statement: Two M&A targets under due diligence, expected to conclude in next 1-2 months; strategy focuses on both customer and competence acquisition.

items.statement: Government extended Jal Jeevan Mission to 2028 and announced National Geospatial Mission under PM Gati Shakti; management sees no headwinds from JJM allocation changes.

items.statement: UK FTA signed recently; UK exposure is very small but FTA expected to have positive impact.
items.quote: Our exposure to UK today is very small, and this FDA, if at all, it will help us positively. I don't think there is any negative.

items.statement: Revenue per employee increased to INR 3.34 million in FY25 from INR 2.29 million in FY24; employee cost as % of revenue fell from 35% to 30%.

items.statement: Vidarbha river linking project (INR 381 crore) commenced execution Feb 1, 2025; aerial LiDAR survey of first link to complete by May 31, data processing by June 30; INR 150 crore revenue targeted for Q1 FY26.

items.statement: Board recommended dividend of 35% for FY25, up from 25% in FY24, subject to shareholder approval.
items.quote: Infused with the performance, the Board has recommended a higher dividend of 35% as compared to 25% last year. This will be paid once approved by the members at the ensuing annual meeting.

If we decide to move forward, we will definitely come back and improve. But right now, we are trying planning to put them on back burner because there are more orders and more business being pursued with the existing segments.

items.statement: Intangible assets of INR 8.3 crore capitalized for internally developed technology processes with IPR applications filed; benefits already being realized in projects.

But this is in respect of our technology process, which we have invented. We have applied for that for the IPR, and we are already taking the benefit of that technology innovation in our existing projects.

items.statement: Many competitors in both segments; competitive edge from 26 years experience, technical competencies, project execution capability, and breadth of services.
items.quote: In terms of competition, I think there are many people. So the list will be very long if we want to go through that. But in terms of competitive advantage, you can see it from the numbers. We are definitely doing much better than any other in our competition.

items.statement: Revenue growth target of 40-50% for FY26

items.statement: EBITDA margin guidance of 17-19% for FY26

items.quote: So it goes to roughly about Rs. 450 crores in terms of topline from the SDA plant if it is getting off divided at 100% level.

items.quote: It is our belief about 700,000 tons to 800,000 tons of the sugar that will get exported. We, as a company, decided to sell our export obligation. We've sold pretty much 99% of our export obligation.

items.statement: Board approved dividend of INR 1.25 per share for FY25; buyback to be considered after debt reduction

items.quote: The share of revenue from fabric increased from 6.5% in FY '24, to 7.8% in FY '25. Similarly, the share of exports has also increased from 15% noted in FY '24 to 16% of revenues in FY '25, despite the strategic reduction of exports to Bangladesh.

items.statement: FY25 growth capex INR158 crores mainly on new spindles; working capital released INR54 crores; debt reduced INR8 crores; net debt INR58 crores
items.quote: In the year, we deployed INR158 crores towards growth capex, mainly on the new spindles expansion, while working capital was released by INR54 crores on account of better inventory management and debt was reduced by INR8 crores. We maintained a robust balance sheet, closing the year with a net debt of INR58 crores despite making significant investments.

items.statement: Cotton arrivals 273 lakh bales vs 258 lakh bales last season; CCI procured ~100 lakh bales vs 33 lakh bales; domestic cotton prices stable around INR55,000 per candy; expect range-bound near term
items.quote: Domestic cotton prices are currently stable, averaging around INR55,000 per candy and international prices have also shown steady trends. We expect cotton prices to remain range bound in the near term, though there remains some degree of uncertainty stemming from evolving international trade and tariff dynamics.

items.statement: US tariff adjustments may give India strategic advantage as competitors face higher duties; private sector needs to accelerate capacity investments
items.quote: On the global trade front, recent tariff adjustments by the U.S. have introduced an element of unpredictability. However, this realignment may provide India with a strategic advantage as some of our key competitors face higher duties.

items.statement: Committed INR1,000 crores investment plan on track; INR500 crores deployed; 25,000 new spindles expected to commence operations by June 2025
items.quote: Our committed investment plan of INR1,000 crores remain firmly on track, of w hich INR500 crores have been deployed. The addition of 25,000 new spindles is progressing as scheduled, and we expect operations to commence by June '25

items.statement: New project to install 40 knitting machines at existing location with INR38 crores capex; first phase of 10 machines underway
items.quote: We also initiated a new project to install 40 knitting machines at our existing location with a total capex of INR38 crores. Work on the first phase involving 10 machines is already underway.

items.statement: Target 2x current turnover in 3-4 years with ~30% revenue from value-added knitting, weaving, processed fabric
items.quote: And overall, we have said already that our turnover, we are looking at 2x of what is the turnover today. And out of the total overall, roughly around 30% will be coming from the value added of the knitting and fabric or the weaving product.

items.statement: 25,000 new spindles to add ~INR250 crores incremental revenue at ~1:1 capex-to-revenue
items.quote: Approximately around 1:1. Approximately, it will be roughly INR250 crores kind of a number will be coming.

items.statement: Long-term EBITDA margin target 17-20% (historically achieved 15-16%); vertical integration and market normalization expected to drive improvement
items.quote: We are very confident that you will start seeing these benefit maybe hopefully -- because, we right now, we can't commit on the kind of volatility we have in t he market, you know because of geopolitical, because of US tariff this thing, but once things become normal, definitely, we believe that this 17%, 18%, we will be able to deliver on that

items.statement: Conscious decision to keep lower cotton inventory (90 days) given stable outlook and CCI stock; no major cotton price upside expected
items.quote: So therefore, our view -- we don't see any kind of a big upside into the cotton prices. And therefore we have created -- but still we have a reasonable inventory of 90 days. So it's not that we have become hand-to-mouth because then we have to maintain the consistency, we have to maintain the quality and we are hedged at least for 3 months.

items.statement: FY26 cash capex projected at INR114 crores (mainly leftover spinning and knitting machines); peak debt for FY26 projected at INR128 crores vs INR63 crores in FY25
items.quote: INR114 crores we are projecting to be spent in FY '25, '26. Out of that, major will be these two retail projects the leftover volume amount and second is the knitting machine.

items.statement: Government incentives expected ~INR15-20 crores on INR500 crores invested under Tamil Nadu policy; application filed
items.quote: And approximately, if my memory is correct, we will be getting around INR15 crores to INR20 crores of the benefit out of that this thing.

items.statement: Peak debt projected at ~INR600 crores upon full INR1,000 crore capex completion by FY29; debt-equity ratio to remain 0.35; revenue target ~INR1,700 crores by FY29
items.quote: Approximately around INR600 crores of the overall peak debt once we complete our entire process.

items.statement: FY26 revenue growth projected at 14-15% (skewed to H2); volume growth from 25,000 spindles; margins expected better than FY25 but hard to predict
items.quote: At this point of a time, the way we have projected, this could be around 14% to 15%. I'm giving you a very specific number, which we have projected. This can be more also or this can be slightly less also depending upon how the yarn prices moved.

items.statement: 25,000 spindle ramp-up expected by end July/early August 2025; 70% of new spindle output to feed 40 knitting machines
items.quote: I think I will not take much of the time in terms of the ramping up, probably the activity will start in July, I think by end of July or beginning of August, it should be full on running.

items.statement: No current plans for garmenting; focus on ready-to-cut fabric for garment manufacturers; synthetic/technical textile movement aligned with ready-to-cut vision
items.quote: See, at this point of a time, we don't have any plan to go for garmenting. First, we want to establish. You know that past experience of our home textile. So we want to be firs t establish ourselves as a ready -to-cut fabric to be supplied to the garment manufacturer because that's itself will be a big value creation

items.statement: Imported cotton ~20-25% of procurement (Pima, Giza, Australian long-staple); no duty on these currently; duty removal on other cotton would cool prices and improve availability
items.quote: and overall, out of the total procurement of the cotton, I think maybe approximately around 20%, 25% of the cotton we are procuring, which are all of the value - added like Giza, Pima or Austr alian cotton

items.statement: Current cotton yarn spread INR119; Q3 FY25 spread ~INR109; Q4 FY25 spread ~INR119
items.quote: The cotton spread at this point of time is around INR119.

items.statement: Gross margin improvement driven by better product mix and market; spreads improved from INR109 in Q3 to INR119 in Q4
items.quote: Yes. The cotton yarn spread has improved primarily because of better product and a better market.

items.statement: Open to M&A opportunities (e.g., garmenting business) but cautious; not interested in small/old spinning assets
items.quote: Saket, we are looking at all those possibilities. I would not say that we are not looking at the possibilities. But we are very careful of which kind of assets like suppose we get some garmenting business, probably we may look at it.

items.statement: US tariff uncertainty and 90-day pause delaying order conversion; potential US recession could impact yarn demand; geopolitical volatility makes margin timeline unpredictable
items.quote: But like you know that India looks to be the first mover on to the bilateral trade agreement with the US. And that will definitely bring advantage to India, particularly with the textile industry, I'm very hopeful.

items.statement: No specific FY26 guidance given; will share detailed guidance mid-year
items.quote: As of now, we are not giving any specific guidance for FY '26. We will share detailed guidance in mid of the year as we progress further.

items.statement: Profitability to remain under stress in H1 FY26, material improvement expected post H1
items.quote: Profitability is expected to remain under stress in H1 FY '26, post which we expect material improvement in profitability profile.

items.statement: Deposits grew 23% YoY to INR 21,566 cr; retail term deposits up 33%, CASA up 31%; CASA ratio 21.8%
items.quote: Our deposits grew by around 23% year-on-year to INR21,566 crores. Deposits growth was led by growth in retail term deposits, which grew by 33% year-on-year; and CASA deposits, which grew by 31% year -on-year.

items.statement: Opened 200+ branches in FY25; total branches >1,000; may not need much expansion in FY26
items.quote: We're consistently expanding our franchise and opened more than 200 new branches during FY '25. Our total branch count exceeded 1,000 branches as on March 31, 2025.

items.statement: Added 3,600 staff in FY25; ~2,500 for JLG, 800+ dedicated collection staff; case load reduced significantly
items.quote: Yes. So largely, these people are for JLG business only, almost close to 2,500 out of these people, I mean, 100 plus-minus in the JLG business. And we have created collection team, which has more than 800 people.

items.statement: Reduced savings deposit rates for certain slabs and highest retail term deposit rate by 25 bps; will reduce cost of funds gradually
items.quote: Recently, we have reduced interest rates for savings deposits for certain slabs as well as highest rate for retail term deposits by 25 basis points, which will lead to reduction in cost of funds gradually.

items.statement: Secured loan share increased from 34% to 43% YoY; expected to increase further by 4-5% annually
items.quote: Further in line with our strategy, we have been increasing share of secured loan in our portfolio. It increased further from 34% as on March '24 to 43% as on March '25 and is likely to increase further.

items.statement: No direct JLG exposure in Karnataka and Tamil Nadu; negligible BC presence in Karnataka
items.quote: Furthermore, with respect to state level ordinance and related disruption, we do not have any direct exposure towards JLG lending in Karnataka as well as Tamil Nadu.

items.statement: MFIN guardrail 2.0 (max 3 lenders) fully implemented from April 1, 2025; expected to control leverage and improve portfolio quality
items.quote: MFIN guardrail 2.0 with respect to number of lenders not exceeding three lenders are fully implemented in our system with effect from April 1, 2025.

items.statement: Registered with CGFMU for credit guarantee on unsecured JLG portfolio from Jan 17, 2025; guarantee cost ~1-1.5% annualized
items.quote: We have also registered with CGFMU for credit guarantee for unsecured JLG portfolio and are looking forward for credit guarantee cover for our JLG disbursement post our registration date, that is January 17, 2025.

items.statement: Surplus liquidity INR 3,800 cr as of Mar 31, 2025; LCR 190%; no short-term borrowings
items.quote: As on March 31, 2025, we had surplus liquidity of around INR3,800 crores, which is higher than our usual liquidity requirement and a LCR ratio of 190%.

items.statement: CD ratio declined to 87% (78% net of refinance); no short-term borrowings on balance sheet
items.quote: In line with our strategy, we have been reducing our CD ratio, which declined to 87% as on March '25 versus 94% as on March '24. And if we net off refinance borrowing from advances, CD ratio declines t o 78% as on March '25

items.statement: GNPA rose to 9.43% (from 6.17% Dec'24); SMA book fell from 10% to 5% QoQ; X-bucket collection efficiency 99.1% in Q4
items.quote: On account of challenging operating environment in microfinance lending, our fresh NPA slippages were high in quarter 3 and quarter 4 of FY '25. And as a result, our gross NPAs increased from 6.17% as on December '24 to 9.43% as on March '25.

items.statement: Fresh NPA slippages INR 770 cr in Q4 (INR 665 cr microbanking); unsecured book PCR ~52%; non-microbanking GNPA ~2.4%
items.quote: Overall fresh NPA was about INR 770 crores in quarter 4, out of which about INR 665 crores is microbanking and balance is non -microbanking.

items.statement: Higher stress in Odisha and Rajasthan; other states (Bihar, UP, Jharkhand, Maharashtra) better
items.quote: Out of these states, we see slightly higher stress in the state of Odisha and Rajasthan. Other states are equal, and they are much better than these two states.

items.statement: Expect SMA normalization by Q1 FY26; fresh NPA slippages to decline meaningfully; OD bucket collections to improve in H1 FY26
items.quote: As we highlighted during the last earnings call, we expect SMA book to normalize by quarter 1 FY '26. SMA book in microbanking portfolio reduced from 10% as on December '24 to 5% as on March '25.

items.statement: JLG X-bucket collection efficiency 99.1% in Q4 FY25; center meeting discipline ~65-70%
items.quote: We have seen improvement in X-bucket collection efficiency for quarter 4 FY '25, which was 99.1% for quarter 4 FY '25.

items.statement: Non-microbanking credit cost 1-1.5% (after FLDG); secured portfolio yields improved (MSME +180 bps, Housing +80 bps YoY)
items.quote: Credit costs in these businesses have been in the range of 1% to 1.5%.

items.statement: Expect stress/pain for another 2 quarters (Q1-Q2 FY26); utilized full floating provision (INR 190 cr) in Q4; no buffers remain
items.quote: We expect that this pain, whatever, pain or stress is expected to be there for another 2 quarters, so quarter 1 and quarter 2 of FY '26.

items.statement: Approved up to INR 750 cr Tier 1 capital raise; capital adequacy >20% (RBI min 15%); will raise when market receptive
items.quote: We have taken approval for up to INR 750 crores Tier 1 capital that we can raise for market. So we'll certainly look at market. The moment market is receptive and good, then certainly, we'll go for this.

items.statement: Reverse merger: RBI NOC received, exchange NOCs received, SEBI approval pending; NCLT process 7-9 months post SEBI
items.quote: We have got the NOC from RBI. We also know that the two exchanges through which SEBI ultimately is in okay. So both of them have given their NOC. Currently, we have already responded queries to SEBI.

items.statement: Senior management changes due to natural attrition; strong second line in place; ED Pramod Dubey oversees all businesses
items.quote: These were -- I mean, I can use the word -- of course, timing might be -- you might have seen on April 30, but these were some of the cases where people -- sometimes people want to move on also.

items.statement: Gold loans started in few branches; SuperCard (secured credit card) response very good; fintech BC partnerships to continue
items.quote: Yes. So we have started gold loans, and we intend to increase that, although the numbers at this point of time is a very, very small number.

items.statement: Unexecuted order book of INR 120 crores carried forward to FY26; INR 243 crores L1 positions pending work orders; INR 44 crores tenders awaited; INR 450+ crores bid in April 2025
items.quote: Our order book stands robust as at the end of 31st March 2025 with INR 120 crores worth of orders being carried forward to FY25 and tenders bidded results awaited amounting to INR44 crores. Tenders worth INR 243 crores have already been declared with Solarium being declared as L1 but pending work orders till now.

items.statement: L1 orders of INR 243 crores from NTPC tender (total INR 270 crores); INR 27 crores received by March 2025; expecting INR 54 crores more in next 1.5 months; execution-based LOA
items.quote: Yes, so out of this INR 243 crores, this is part of a larger contract which we have won out of NTPC's tender. This is in total about INR 270 crores worth of orders out of which we have received INR 27 crores by the end of March 2025.

items.statement: Order book split: INR 243 crores L1 all PSU; INR 120 crores unexecuted - INR 98 crores PSU, balance private and residential; INR 17 crores residential orders pushed to Q1 FY26
items.quote: Got it. So, INR 243 crores is all PSUs. Out of 120, almost 98 is PSUs and balance is private and residential. During our speech, as well as in our management commentary, w e have covered orders worth INR 17 crores is being pushed to Q1 for residential rooftop alone

items.statement: No formal guidance given; management foresees continuing growth trajectory similar to past years; expects to maintain INR 10 crores monthly residential rooftop revenue run rate
items.quote: In terms of the future growth, we want to refra in from any sort of guidance. But at the same point in time, we foresee to continue our growth trajectory in a similar fashion as it has happened in the past couple of years

items.statement: EBITDA margin target range of 11% to 13% for overall business
items.quote: 11% to 13% is the range which we want to probably anchor at this point in time.

items.statement: Residential rooftop adoption accelerated: 9 lakh homes installed solar in last one year vs 10 lakh in previous 15 years; multiple states adding extra subsidies
items.quote: Like if I will say, in the last 15 years, there was adoption by 10 lakh homes w ho have gone solar. But in the last only one year, around 9 lakh homes have installed solar at theirs

items.statement: Government mandating net zero by FY2030 for ministries; defense adopting solar; strong sector tailwinds from PM Surya Ghar and 500 GW non-fossil target by 2030
items.quote: The government has taken a target for becoming net zero by FY2030 for all the ministries, which is again becoming more and more prevalent or more and more mandatory for the various ministries itself. Similarly, defense is being asked to kind of use solar as one of our renewable sources of energy.

items.statement: Residential rooftop H2 FY25 gross margins ~20%, EBITDA margins ~10%; margins vary by state maturity - higher in new states (UP, Delhi, Maharashtra, MP), lower in mature states (Gujarat)
items.quote: of gross margins, our gross margins will be in the range of about 20 odd percent. Soham: And EBITDA margins, sir? Himanshu Garg: EBITDA margins will be in the range of 10 odd percent

items.statement: Overall EBITDA margins expected to remain range-bound at 11-13% as new state investments offset mature state margin improvements
items.quote: So, it is because there are older states which are getting matured where gross margins get under pressure, but with our lower manpower or fixed cost, we make higher EBITDA margins but in newer states, we make higher gross margins.

items.statement: Planning more than 15 new warehouses over next 6 months; opened Jodhpur warehouse recently; using Solar Saarthi channel partner model to reduce fixed cost per city
items.quote: Over the next six months, there are very aggressive growth plans across India. When we say across India, largely within these states which we have already opened, going deeper into the same states with a larger number of cities. So, there are more than 15 new warehouses to be opened which are planned.

items.statement: Residential rooftop monthly revenue grew from INR 5 crores to INR 10 crores (2x); H2 FY25 residential revenue INR 45 crores; March 2025 alone INR 56 crores total revenue
items.quote: In terms of numbers, if we talk about, so residential rooftop, we were at INR 5 crores per month revenue at the start of the year, which has been increased to INR 10 crores at the end of the year, which is March 2025 standalone.

items.statement: Employee strength grew from <200 to 309; hired segment heads, experienced CFO, 60 interns from IITs/IIMs; ESOP pool >50% allocated (INR 84 lakh expense)
items.quote: We have hired at the start of the year, the employee strength was less than 200, which has now increased to 309 at the end of March 2025. This has been across the organization, largely towards our residential space, residential rooftop space, where we are opening multiple cities.

items.statement: Receivables jumped due to March revenue skew (INR 56 crores in March alone); residential receivables INR 7.5 crores (secured via advances/PDCs/subsidy funding); bank financing 70% post-installation
items.quote: March 25 alone has contributed INR 56 crores revenue. So if you see, it is largely because of the skewness, which has happened in terms of revenue of March numbers. That is how the receivables have increased.

items.statement: IPO funds to be deployed in working capital; leveraging balance sheet with banks for growth funding
items.quote: Largely, we foresee to deploy those funds within the working capital space at this point in time as our business is growing. So, largely, the fund utilization we foresee in the working capital space.

items.statement: Residential: 37% of revenue, 13,900+ projects executed (Apr 2021-Mar 2025), 905+ ongoing projects, 200 channel partners via Solar Saarthi program (INR 11,000 PE model)
items.quote: Over the past year, we have continued to strengthen our presence across the residential sector, commercial sector, industrial sector, and government segment, driven by disciplined execution and deep industry insight, with executed and ongoing project in nearly 15 states and UTs and a team of over 300 professionals.

items.statement: Institutional: ~50% revenue, 49 projects underway; clients include BARC, BSF, Indian Air Force; L1 in 38 of 45 categories under NTPC distributed rooftop programs
items.quote: On the institutional side, we have successfully executed projects across prestigious public and private sector clients, including Bhabha Atomic Research Centre, multiple projects for BSF, Indian Air Force. These projects not only validate our technical capabilities and delivery excellence, but also position us as a reliable partner for high-impact large-scale solar initiatives.

items.statement: Competes with Solar Square (PE-funded, losses); Solarium profitable since 2017 bootstrap; state-level competition varies - ahead in Gujarat, behind in Maharashtra
items.quote: So, numbers are relatively same. So, month-on-month, sometimes they have more, sometimes we have more. But yes, we compete with each other in terms of numbers. Himanshu Garg: So, it is also at state level, like in Gujarat, we are way ahead of them. In Maharashtra, they are ahead because Maharashtra as a state, we just started very, very recently

items.statement: REC appointed nodal agency for PM Surya Ghar; unified portal for consumers/discoms/vendors; direct benefit transfer of subsidies; ALMM and DCR requirements driving domestic manufacturing
items.quote: Government has appointed REC as a nodal agency for implementation of this program, sir. So REC is a nodal agency. They have created a unified consumer portal, wherein consumers, the discoms, vendors, and state governments, they all work on the same platform.

items.statement: Shifted from trading (INR 70+ crores FY24) to turnkey EPC (INR 200 crores FY25, 100% growth); residential 37%, institutional ~50% of revenue
items.quote: If you see, our turnkey business has increased from INR 100-105 crores to INR 200 crores, which is almost like 100% growth vis-a-vis last year. So till last year, there was a significant amount of trading also, which was about almost like INR 70-plus crores.

items.statement: ESOP expense INR 84 lakh in FY25 (first year, half-year cost); absolute cost to increase in FY26 but decrease as % of revenue; allocated to 50%+ employees including L2/L3 levels
items.quote: ESOP cost is something given this was the first year and that was largely half of the year cost only in this year. But at the same point in time, as a percentage to the overall business, we foresee that to be reduced in terms of percentage as overall business, given the growth we foresee to see the growth trajectory as it is happening. But Yes, in terms of absolute numbers, yes, it will be increas

items.statement: DCR panel availability risk being mitigated via corporate tie-ups; subsidy portal transition (1.0 to 2.0) causing temporary delays (max 45 days vs 15-day target)
items.quote: Currently, there is a total transition of portal which is happening from the MNRE perspective. So, they are transitioning the portal from 1.0 to 2.0 that is also kind of resulting in terms of delay in subsidy but still the subsidy is getting credited to the consumer account within 45 days at max.

items.statement: Part of IPO proceeds used for debt repayment; leveraging balance sheet with banks for working capital funding
items.quote: I see that some part of the debt has been already being paid. So, it is underutilized at this point of time. So, what are the plans for these funds in this financial year? Himanshu Garg: Thanks, Rohit, for the question. Largely, we foresee to deploy those funds within the working capital space at this point in time as our business is growing

items.statement: No plans to enter IPP (capital heavy, higher risk) for next couple of years; focus on distributed solar/rooftop as core forte
items.quote: Not as of now. So, I think if you also see our core forte is residential rooftop or I would rather say rooftop, which is rooftop plus the distributed solar space which is not probably getting into the larger orders which kind of also balances out the risk portion as an organization.

items.statement: FY26 guidance maintained at Rs.7,000 crores revenue, Rs.1,100 crores EBITDA, and Rs.650-700 crores EBIT
items.value: 7000 crores revenue, 1100 crores EBITDA, 650-700 crores EBIT
items.quote: the guidance given during the last quarter earnings call for the first time for FY26, we have given Rs.7,000 crores top line and Rs.1,100 crores EBITDA levels and a wide range of say Rs.500 crores to Rs.700 crores EBIT, we have already reached Rs.512 crores EBIT in the current year itself. So, we are expecting in the region of Rs.650 crores to Rs.700 crores EBIT going forward in the next financial

items.statement: FY26 group capex guided at Rs.750-800 crores
items.quote: Our CAPEX guidance as a whole for a group will be only around Rs.750 crores to Rs.800 crores totally in that region.

items.statement: Standalone capex expected at Rs.550 crores in FY26; Sunbeam and DR Axion capex to be taken as it comes; Fronberg repair & maintenance ~Rs.40-50 crores under evaluation
items.quote: I think Rs.550 crores for Craftsman is what we expect in the current condition. Between Sunbeam and DR Axion, we will take it as it comes. We have just budgeted now and there is some repair and maintenance for a very old equipment at Fronberg, which may be around Rs.40 crores, Rs.50 crores, may be there, we're evaluating that.

items.statement: New powertrain (stationary engine) order book filling up; first revenues in FY27, three-digit revenue from FY27, targeting $100 million peak by 2029-30; Kothavadi Phase-1 operational in Q1
items.quote: the order book is filling up, but the development cycle time is around 18 to 24 months. So, we will not see any three-digit revenue, the three-digit revenue will only come in FY27 on the new powertrain business. But as I mentioned, I think it will peak in 2029, 2030 for $100 million revenue for this business.

items.statement: Sunbeam FY26 blended EBITDA margin expected 8-10%; Q1 weak, Q2 strong, Q3 weak, Q4 strongest due to plant consolidation, cost optimization, manpower rationalization
items.quote: on a blended average we can say between 8% to 10% EBITDA is what we expect for the full financial year, but Q1 will be quite muted.

items.statement: Powertrain margins to creep up with better operating leverage; double-digit revenue growth expected in FY26; Q2 and Q4 strong, Q1 and Q3 challenging
items.quote: Our margins also will start creeping up with better operating leverage but depends on one quarter to another quarter there may be some changes, always Q1 will have some challenges, but we don't see much challenge this year, Q3 will be always a challenge. So, Q2 and Q4, we expect very strong quarters.

items.statement: Storage business FY26 revenue growth expected in high teens (~20%); margins to improve on new orders, product cost rationalization, static racking traction
items.quote: High teens I would say, almost 20% we can expect the growth on the storage business.

items.statement: Conventional powertrain utilization ~70%, headroom to 85-90%; aluminum at 70-75%, targeting 80-85% by Q2, need capex by Q3 for new order pipeline
items.quote: Even in the aluminum side, we are at operating at around 70%, 75%, but the order book is quite strong. So, we need to increase CAPEX. We will quickly touch 80%, 85% by Q2 itself. So, by Q3, we need CAPEX for the new orders which is already there in the pipeline.

items.statement: Deleveraging via high cash generation, potential Sunbeam land sale of ~Rs.300 crores in Q3/Q4 FY26, group EBITDA >Rs.1,100 crores, depreciation ~Rs.450 crores, capex Rs.750-800 crores
items.quote: the cash run rate generation will be quite high even in the next financial year plus aided by possibly the land sale in Q3 or Q4 of Sunbeam, that will add around Rs.300 crores plus depending on that market value at that particular point of time.

items.statement: Exports mainly Ex-Works/FOB; negligible US exposure; Sunbeam ~15-20% revenue from exports (mostly Mexico); no tariff impact, no customer price reduction requests
items.quote: US exports as far as Sunbeam is concerned, it is negligible. It is more towards Mexico there. So, I think around 15%, 20% of Sunbeam's revenue is coming from exports. So, we don't have any impact on the tariff.

items.statement: Consolidated revenue mix: PV 32%, 2W 18%, CV 17%, storage 10%, off-highway 5%, tractor 4%; top 12 customers contribute 60% vs earlier top 6 at 50%
items.quote: the commercial vehicle portion is coming to 17%, two wheeler is coming to 18%, passenger vehicle is 32%, storage is 10%, off-highways is 5% and tractor is 4%. I think overall we have diversified quite well and we have also invested for customers who are export-oriented.

items.statement: Diversification driving growth: OEMs exporting from India to Africa/South America; Maruti targeting 4M cars with new plants; Escorts (Japanese-owned) and Yanmar expanding India footprint for exports; import substitution on alloy wheels from
items.quote: Many of the OEMs from the eastern part of the world like Japan and Korea are also setting their sights on African market for both passenger car, two-wheeler, pickup trucks, tractors and all the products which are going to go into Africa in the future, which is the last market to be developed, the products are similar to India, what India wanted in the last two decades.

items.statement: Consolidated OCF compression due to Sunbeam inclusion (only 6 months); Fronberg working capital infusion not yet deployed, cash lying at holding company
items.quote: Because it's a consolidated basis it's Sunbeam, right. It's not an apple-to-apple comparison because Sunbeam we had it only for six months, that may be the reason maybe not being able to compare.

items.statement: Sunbeam VRS for ~450-500 employees on track; Rs.160 crores fully provisioned at acquisition, no P&L hit in FY26; Gurgaon plant 75% emptied, awaiting Tier-1 OEM validation for full shift
items.quote: It was already provisioned before we took over. There is nothing new. It was Rs.160 crores settlement for 1,000-odd people, 500 people have left, paid and the balance was provisioned in the opening when we took over itself. So, there is no new provisioning will come up.

items.statement: Geopolitical/tariff risk seen as low; products high value-add, competitive; no customer tariff-related price reduction requests except one engineering customer
items.quote: Our products are a high value addition, and they mean a lot to the customer. And I think we are very competitive also. So, even if there is a tariff, they are willing to pay it and take it except one engineering customer, nobody has come and asked us for any price reduction on tariff, nobody has even contacted us on this matter.

items.statement: Alloy wheel operational breakeven at ~Rs.40 crores quarterly revenue; Bhiwadi FY26 target Rs.300+ crores, Hosur Rs.150 crores; Q4 FY25 alloy wheel revenue ~Rs.40 crores, EBITDA-neutral, EBIT -Rs.5 crores
items.quote: Bhiwadi will be around Rs.300 crores plus for FY26 and Hosur will be around Rs.150 crores. This is as per the earlier earnings call.
