items.quote: The company remains focused on a gradual production scale-up, targeting over 700 tons per month by the month of June 2025 and aiming to reach a cumulative capacity of approximately 1,600 tons per month by the end of FY '26.

items.statement: Specialty chem chlorosulfonation scaled to 100 tons/month; targeting 200 tons/month by June quarter
items.quote: We have already scaled up to 100. And in this -- by June quarter, we will be scaling up to 200 tons per month.

items.statement: US-China tariff war may give 10% pricing advantage for spec chem/intermediates exported directly to US
items.quote: So that gives us clearly 10% advantage for the pricing of our products. So we become more competitive by 10%, which is quite a big margin, frankly speaking, for Indian manufacturers.

items.statement: Investing INR8.05 crore for 26.25% stake in 24.4 MWp solar plant for captive power in Maharashtra and Gujarat
items.quote: Through this agreement, the company will acquire 26.25% equity shares and voting rights along with compulsorily convertible debentures in Pro-Zeal Green Power Nine Private Limited and SPV that will develop and operate 24.4 megawatt peak solar power plant.

items.statement: Expect INR10-15 crore power/fuel savings in FY26; INR25-30 crore annually from FY27 via solar and cogen boiler
items.quote: However, for FY '26, we feel around INR10 crores to INR15 crores might -- of benefit might come in this year itself. And from next year onwards, it should be around INR25 crores to INR30 crores.

items.statement: New volume drivers: fluconazole, metformin, metronidazole (245 to 330 tons/month), salicylic acid, monomethylamine; formulations: DPP-4 inhibitors, anticoagulants, 2 oncology drugs
items.quote: The major products where we see that our new volumes will come from, one is antifungal product, fluconazole. Then we foresee volume growth in metformin as well because of the increased production. Plus we see volume expansion in metronidazole because we have increased the production from around 245 tons to 330 tons per month.

items.statement: Gliptins: Teneligliptin sold locally; Vildagliptin DMF in process, improving cost for export competitiveness
items.quote: Teneligliptin, we are selling into local markets. Vildagliptin, we ar e in the process of making DMF. We are further improving the cost, the process of the Vildagliptin

items.statement: Metformin has European CEP; targeting Europe sales and USDMF filing after Tarapur import alert removal
items.quote: Yes. So in metformin, we do have European approval. We have CEP for the product. However, the European sales hasn't picked up much. But there are a few other geographies in the world, which is semi-regulated. There, we just have got into those markets and the sale is improving on a quantity basis for metformin for us in those markets.

items.statement: Debtor days ~90; Q4 spike due to higher quarterly sales; will normalize if run-rate maintained
items.quote: Our debtor cycle is typically around 90 days. So if we sell more in the latest quarter, then -- and if you take the first 4 quarters revenues, then on that number, it looks higher.

items.statement: Revised FY27 revenue target down from INR4,000 crore to INR3,000-3,500 crore due to price variation
items.quote: The only thing is because of the price variation, we have revised down that target. So right now, on a pessimistic level, we are hoping that we will first reach INR3,000 crores plus by FY '27.

items.statement: Fill-finish facility expected to be capitalized by Q2 FY26; BSL-3 facility awaiting BIRAC administrative approval
items.quote: And for fill finish activity, the expected timeline to have a capitalization is by Q2 this year considering the remaining batches to be commercialized and the regulatory approvals in the place.

items.statement: Hester Africa expected to break even in two years; accumulated losses of Rs. 45 crore to be recouped in 1-2 more years
items.quote: We hope that not this year, the next year, we hope two years we should take to breakeven at Hester Africa

items.statement: No concrete new CAPEX plan for current financial year beyond fill-finish and BSL-3; mostly maintenance CAPEX
items.quote: For the CAPEX, right now there is not much plan on it. As mentioned earlier, our fill finish is going to get commercially used now by Q2, latest Q3. And apart from that, we are just planning on our CAPEX plans. It's right now mostly to do with maintenance, etc.

items.statement: New plant utilization expected to progress from 10% to 70% over three years
items.quote: Slowly it will grow utilization from 10 % to 30 % to 60% to 70%. So it's a progression through which we are going. We are reasonably sure that by the time it is 3 years' time, we should be reaching a good level of production from the new plant.

items.statement: Hester Africa has tender for Tanzanian government business and expects 1-2 more country tenders
items.quote: We are already having the tender for Tanzanian government business, we see other 1 or 2 countries also tenders coming up.

items.statement: Standalone gross profit margins stable; EBITDA increased 8% due to better capacity use and expense discipline
items.quote: The standalone gross-profit margins remain stable, supported by a better product mix and cost control. EBITDA has increased by 8%, reflecting better capacity use and expense discipline.

items.statement: Animal Health division grew 6% in FY25 and 8% in Q4; Pet Care saw steady therapeutic demand; Poultry Healthcare benefited from higher vaccine demand
items.quote: The combined division recorded an 8 % growth in Q4 and 6 % in FY'25. Animal Healthcare remained the main contributor with stable demand for our Goat Pox and PPR vaccines under the National Immunization Program

items.statement: Focus on growing health product segment to reduce vaccine dependency; preparing to expand into prescription diet and supplements for Pet Care
items.quote: Our focus remains on growing the health product segment so that we equalize. There is no single dependency on just vaccine heavy product range and grew our pet care as well as animal health care product segment.

items.statement: Appointed two marketing managers in African countries to create demand; exclusive distribution arrangements in Africa and Middle East
items.quote: We have also started appointing our own marketing people in a few countries in Africa. We have started off by appointing two managers in two of the countries.

items.statement: Not losing market share to integrated poultry players; Venky's has in-house consumption, Suguna sold vaccine plant, IB Group has no vaccine plant
items.quote: There is nothing like that we are losing market share. Point number one, Venky's was even before us in business. So there is no question of that way. And they are today the biggest in India in poultry.

items.statement: Avian Influenza vaccine launch expected beginning of Q2 FY26; H9N2 vaccine registration takes 2 years per product per African country
items.quote: We have always maintained Q2. If I have mentioned Q1, I probably don't recollect. But yes, it would be the beginning of Q2 for sure.

items.statement: Hester Nepal supplies PPR vaccines to FAO for global immunization; Hester Africa received marketing authorization for PPR plus sheep and goat pox combined vaccine
items.quote: Hester Nepal has delivered stable profits with the net profit of Rs. 1.2 crore in the Financial Year. It met both domestic demands for the poultry health and export demand for immunization against PPR globally.

items.statement: Reduced consolidated debt by Rs. 32 crore in March 2025 vs March 2024; cash from operations ~Rs. 70 crore sufficient for current debt repayment
items.quote: I think the cash generated from the operations are roughly around Rs. 70 Cr. So I think we are able to manage right now the repayment which is for the current debt from our operations only.

items.statement: No new working capital addition envisaged given current situation
items.quote: I do not envisage, frankly speaking, any new working capital add on looking at the current situation.

items.statement: H9N2 vaccine market estimated at Rs. 80-100 crore in India; world market much larger
items.quote: In India, I think the H9N2 market I am not sure totally but it would definitely be approximately say Rs. 100 crore, around Rs. 80 crores to Rs. 100 crore market and world market is much bigger than that.

items.statement: Africa breakeven delayed by geopolitical slowdowns; Egypt collaboration at status quo due to foreign exchange issues
items.quote: The collaboration activity with Novapharma in Egypt, there is status quo at this point of time because of Egypt having its own reasons as a country in terms of foreign exchange availability, etc., etc.

items.statement: Strengthening marketing activities targeting veterinarians and pet parents for Pet Care division
items.quote: We are also strengthening our marketing activities, focusing on targeted outreach to veterinarians and pet parents to build greater awareness and trust in our product.

items.statement: Management targets minimum 20-25% average revenue growth for FY26 and aims to maintain EBITDA margins north of 20%.
items.quote: We don't want to give a very forward -looking statement, but we will minimum try to maintain our average growth rate of 20% to 25%.

items.statement: Q4 FY25 EBITDA margin hit a record 23.5%; management expects to sustain margins at similar levels in the near future.
items.quote: The EBITDA came in at Rs.147 crores, which is a growth of 50% on a year-on-year basis. EBITDA margins once again is at a record high of 23 .5% for the quarter and we expect to maintain similar EBITDA margins in the near future.

items.statement: Management targets EBITDA margins consistently above 20%, acknowledging potential 1-2% compromise as the company scales.
items.quote: So, Mr. Bheda, I would think that north of 20 % will always be our target. We'll always try to be above 20% for sure. As we grow, we may have to compromise to a certain extent by 1 % or 2%, but we will try to maintain north of 20% for sure.

items.statement: FY26 capex guided at Rs.250-300 crores for debottlenecking and expanding major products, adding 6,000 metric tons capacity by March 2026.
items.quote: You mentioned in the PPT is for FY26, the number is Rs. 250 to Rs. 300 crores. So, is it entirely for debottlenecking or any other plans? Narayan S. Iyer: Yes, it is basically for debottlenecking or expanding on our major products in that.

items.statement: Current capacity utilization at 85-90%; expanding total capacity from 48,000 to 54,000 metric tons by March 2026 through debottlenecking.
items.quote: Our units have all been operating at close to 85% to 90% of our capacities. As has been informed, we are actively working to expand our production capacities for our key products and take it up from 48,000 metric tons to 54,000 metric tons. We expect this expansion to be completed by March 2026.

items.statement: Order book position and customer commitments support confidence in 20-25% growth; customer base expanded from 3 to 6 key customers, now covering most top 10 global players.
items.quote: We are confident of our growth as we see our order books position and we also are working closely with the clients, we have much more clients right now, customers who have given commitments. Earlier, we had only three key customers, now we have six key customers or probably all the top ten companies are our customers.

items.statement: Margin improvement driven by superior product mix including high-value products over $100/kg and value-added products from side streams; shift towards value-added products is steady and evolving.
items.quote: So as I already explained, it is the product mix that now that we now have which includes products which are high value products selling over $100 per kilogram as well as the products that we make from the site streams.

items.statement: Input cost reduction primarily from improved yields and side-stream valorization, not raw material price declines; average product prices at $7-7.5/kg with potential for 5-10% increase.
items.quote: Input cost as in you have to see it in terms of improved yields. It is not that the cost of raw material has substantially gone down. It is improved yields which is resulting into lower material cost.

items.statement: Healthy demand for core products across Asia, Africa, India, and Middle East driven by rising hygiene awareness and per capita GDP growth; US exposure limited to ~7-10%.
items.quote: You see the growth is coming from countries in Asia, India, Africa, where the usage of aroma chemicals has been very significant in the last 10-years and now these people have started using.

items.statement: Working capital cycle improved over last two years; management targets further 15-20 days reduction to boost ROCE/ROE.
items.quote: Working capital cycle, definitely we have been striving hard, and we have been in successful enough in bringing it down and you would have seen that over the last two years, our working capital overall cycle has come down and we still expect there is scope and room for improvement at least by another 15 to 20 days we can bring down the overall working capital cycle.

items.statement: Consolidated gross debt ~Rs.1,100 crores including Rs.232 crores in JV subsidiary; peak debt capped at 3x Debt/EBITDA (currently ~2x).
items.quote: Of the said Rs.1,100 odd crores, there is a loan of about Rs.232 crores lying in one of my JV subsidiary. So as such overall the standalone basis, our debt has come down. And to answer you specifically, what the debt levels will be at peak level requirement? Our overall debt will not be exceeding a Debt-EBITDA of 3x.

items.statement: PRIGIV JV plant commissioned in February 2025; minimal revenue contribution (~Rs.4 crores) in FY25; break-even expected in FY27 with 20%+ margins and potential Rs.300-350 crores top line in 3-4 years.
items.quote: PRIGIV has just started its operation somewhere in February '25. So there's hardly any contribution coming on to the revenue front , about Rs.4 crores or so. And as Mr. Mahesh bhai indicated in his initial opening remarks , PRIGIV will start possibly a breakeven from somewhere around a year from now, maybe '26-27 And then it will start contributing both in revenue and the margins in fact.

items.statement: No significant impact expected from US tariffs due to limited US market presence (~10% of exports) and India's relative tariff advantage versus other supplying countries.
items.quote: We really do not anticipate any significant impact from the ongoing US tariffs as our presence in the US market is limited to around 10%. At the moment, almost all countries supplying to US have to bear higher tariffs than India.

items.statement: Gross fixed asset turnover currently ~1.4x, targeting 1.6-1.8x (up to 2x for some products) through debottlenecking and working capital improvement.
items.quote: As far as the Gross fixed asset turnover that you talked about, it should be in the range of around 1.4 x and we are moving towards going to 1.6 x, 1.7x in the coming few years.

items.statement: Management acknowledges uncertain global environment and adopts slightly conservative margin guidance despite internal optimism for higher profitability.
items.quote: Somebody just a few minutes back mentioned that we live in an uncertain world. Therefore in terms of committing to you, we are being slightly conservative, but obviously internally we are working at the numbers that you will also love to hear in times to come.

items.statement: R&D team of 90 scientists with deep domain expertise in aroma chemistry; long-tenured team leaders enabling sustainable yield improvements and new product development.
items.quote: Privi's capability in terms of R&D, we already have 90 scientists, and most of these guys have been with us for a very long time, including the team leaders.

items.statement: Achieved EcoVadis Gold rating, targeting Platinum; increasing green power share reducing energy costs and supporting sustainability goals.
items.quote: Our current Gold Rating from Eco Vadis further validates our proactive approach in aligning the global best practices , reducing carbon footprint and also sending ESG disclosure. We are now striving for a platinum rating and we are not far from it.

items.statement: Management projects 15-20% top-line growth over the next few years.
items.quote: So like our projection growth outlook for next few years would be in the range of 15% to 20%.

items.statement: EBITDA margin expected to expand ~100 bps for every 10% revenue increase due to operating leverage.
items.quote: I think with every 10% increase in the top line, we will have around 100 bps increase in the EBITDA margin.

items.statement: Modernization of new facility near Kolkata targeting Q2 FY26 completion, Q3 as safe date.
items.period: Q2 FY26 target, Q3 FY26 safe
items.quote: The modernization work which we are doing for a new facility near Kolkata is progressing quite fast. And we expect it to be get it completed by -- we are targeting quarter 2, but I think quarter 3 will be a safe date for the completion, although we are targeting quarter 2.

items.statement: Pentonic revenue share rose from 34.3% to 35.6% in FY25, driving margin improvement.
items.quote: This was enabled by a favorable product mix with the higher-margin Pentonic brand expanding its revenue share from 34.3% to 35.6%.

items.statement: Pentonic range commands 40%+ gross margin.
items.quote: Is about 40% GP. Rohit Jalan: Yes. Management: 40-plus GP in Pentonic range of products. So it continues to be that way

items.statement: Average selling price increased 10% in FY25 (INR5.67 to INR6.21); similar growth expected ahead.
items.quote: We had a 10% increase this year. And going forward, we expect a similar growth in the average ASP.

items.statement: New product pipeline includes premium gel pens, markers, highlighters, sketch pens, brush pens, fine liners, crayons, mechanical pencils, wooden pencils, calculators.
items.quote: Building on our recent launches, including markers, highlighters, mechanical pencils, calculators, and several more, we are excited to launch a new wave of products in the coming quarters. These include premium gel pens, more ranges of markers and highlighters, designed for both school and office use and other essential stationary items such as sketch pens, brush pens, fine liners, crayons and so

items.statement: Exports use exclusive distributors; 90%+ own-branded; key markets Brazil, USA, Myanmar, Africa, Middle East, Southeast Asia.
items.quote: So exports model basically is we appoint or we rather work with exclusive distributors in all the countries we have a presence. And so mostly, I think, almost 90% plus, we are selling our own branded products. And we work with exclusivity, like I mentioned. Some of our key markets would be Brazil, U.S.A., and Myanmar, although it is badly affected, and some countries in Africa, Democratic Republic

items.statement: E-commerce JV approved (65:35 Linc majority) to accelerate quick commerce; small initial equity.
items.quote: So we are close to now finalizing our agreements. However, we are looking at a 65:35 shareholding ratio, majority being with Linc. So it's goi ng to be a small capital equity initially

items.statement: Mitsubishi JV plant on schedule for Q2 FY26 operations and launch; will produce Uni/Signo/Jetstream pens below INR50 MRP.
items.quote: And secondly, our project is on schedule, and it is planned for quarter 2 operations and launch itself.

items.statement: Working capital days expected to improve with scale; inventory and debtor days stable or lower as revenue grows.
items.quote: I think as far as working capital is concerned, we will again enjoy operating leverage. So the larger the top line, we will have lesser number of days as inventory and debtors will be more or less same.

items.statement: Board proposed dividend INR1.5 per share (23.5% payout ratio) for FY25.
items.quote: the Board of Directors has proposed a dividend of INR1.5 per share, implying a payout ratio of 23.5%, subject to shareholder approval.

items.statement: China slipped out of top 10 global pen exporters (UN data), creating white-label opportunities for Linc.
items.quote: So China used to be -- I mean, if you look at the last year, then China was among the top 10, both exporter and importer. But somehow in this financial year, there's a slip out of that. These are government data. So probably the Chinese import has cut down. That also gives a huge opportunity for companies like Linc to aggressively look at white labeling opportunities in these markets.

items.statement: Dedicated brand and channel teams in place; adding headcount to support new projects and opportunities.
items.quote: So we have dedicated brand teams and we have dedicated sales channels. And of course, we are adding a couple of more people to the team as well as we have plenty of opportunities and projects.

items.statement: No legal restriction from Mitsubishi stake to onboard other brands (e.g., Deli since 2019); strategic choice only.
items.quote: No, there is no legal agreement that binds us, and it's our strategic call.

items.statement: New markers/highlighters initially outsourced via OEM job work; molds and designs owned by Linc; in-house when volumes justify.
items.quote: The markers, they are all our capex. So we have invested in designs. The molds are owned by us. And we are initially outsourcing. We are getting job work done through OEM vendors or good factories who supply good quality products to several other brands.

items.statement: New category margins expected in line with current 11-12% EBITDA; no dilution anticipated.
items.quote: So see, the margins would be pretty much in line with our current existing margins.

items.statement: Stationery segment growth expected to outpace overall company 15-20% top-line growth; no formal FY26 guidance yet.
items.quote: We believe that the growth in the stationery segment should be outpacing the growth of the company. At this point in time, this is all that we have.

items.statement: Advertising & promotion budget maintained at 2.5-3% of revenue.
items.quote: So, we approximately budget about 2.5% to 3% of our t op line as the advertisement and promotion budget, which we are continuing to do so and maintaining that

items.statement: Restructuring exercises underway to improve gross margins going forward; FY25 gross margin flat despite ASP rise.
items.quote: The restructuring exercises which we have done will help us in improving the gross margin going forward. And you are right that till this year, we didn't have much of increase in the gross margin, but the restructuring of whatever we are doing is going to come going forward.

items.statement: Target addressing 50%+ of INR38,500 crore stationery TAM in next 2-3 years.
items.quote: I think going forward in next 2 to 3 years, I think about 50% of the TAM is something that we would be definitely addressing. That's the direction.

items.statement: All new projects benchmarked to be ROCE accretive above current returns.
items.quote: All the projects which we have undertaken will be definitely ROC accretive. And the ROC benchmark for us is that whatever we are achieving right now, it has to be in addition to that. So that is our minimum benchmark.

items.statement: Guided for high single-digit to low double-digit revenue growth in FY26
items.quote: We are guiding this year for a high single digit, low double -digit kind of guidance.

items.statement: Expect EBITDA margins to improve by 1-1.5% in FY26
items.quote: EBITDA margins should improve by 1% - 1.5% if that happens.

items.statement: Brand spend to increase to 2.5% of sales in FY26
items.quote: Brand spend will also increase in proportion to about 2.5%.

items.statement: Overall capacity utilization at 81% for FY25, down from 86% in FY24
items.quote: Overall, capacity utilization 81%, down from 86% last year and 81% in Q4, down from 89% last year.

items.statement: Max plant capacity utilization at 55% in Q4 FY25, expected to reach 75-80% within a couple of quarters
items.quote: Max plant, which is getting stabilized, 55% capacity utilization and the minute this ranges betw een 75% to 80% capacity utilization, which is very soon in a couple of quarters, we will have a complete reversal over

items.statement: Only routine capex planned for FY26, no major expansion
items.quote: There will be only routine capex. Of course there is no major capex required.

items.statement: Net dealer addition of 181 and 40 new showrooms in FY25
items.quote: The net dealer addition has been 181 and also 40 new showrooms is the net addition in showrooms.

items.statement: EBITDA at INR221 crores (8.4% margin) for FY25, down from 8.98% in FY24
items.quote: EBITDA, like I mentioned, was under pressure because the entire year, we sold less, expenses have gone up. So therefore, the EBITDA is at INR221 crores, which is 8.4% for the entire year, down from 89.8%.

items.statement: Gross margins decreased by 2.8% in Q4 FY25 due to discounting and lower capacity utilization
items.quote: Gross margins decreased by about 2.8%. So, this was something which has been seen in the last 4 quarters, although we were able to maintain a decent margin overall, but there was a little pressure on the margins considering it was Q4 and a little bit of extra discounting, which happens towards the end of the year.

items.statement: No pricing action taken in Q4 FY25; pricing under pressure due to export material influx
items.quote: So, no we have not – in fact the pricing has been under pressure considering we wanted to sell more. And on top of that, so much of the export material which is coming into India.

items.statement: Gas price at INR47/scm in Q4 FY25 and INR44/scm for full year FY25
items.quote: INR47 is the overall gas pricing. This is purely gas and no other mixed fuel in this. It's just the gas pricing is INR47 per standard cubic meter in Q4 and INR44 in standard cubic meter in the whole year

items.statement: Ceramic PVT+GVT at 33% (Q4) and 34% (FY25); PVT 28%; GVT 39% (Q4) and 38% (FY25)
items.quote: As far as the mix is concerned, ceramic PVT and GVT ceramic stands at 33% for the quarter and 34% for the year. PVT stands at 28% for the quarter and the year and GVT stands at 39% for the quarter and 38% for the year.

items.statement: Bathware sales grew 18% in Q4 and 11% in FY25; expect double-digit growth in FY26
items.quote: Bathware sales is something which we are very bullish about. The sales grew by 18% in quarter 4 and 11% in the whole year of 2025. This is very encouraging, and we hope to do again double-digit growth in Bathware for next year.

items.statement: Channel sales 81% of FY25, projects 18.5%; FY26 target: channel 75%, projects 25%
items.quote: Our entire year, 81% is channel, 10% is private projects and 8.5% in Government. In Q4 which has improved, it 's 9.3% in government and 10.5% in private projects, so this government and the private project next year, we think would go up to about 25% and the channel would remain would go down from 80% to 75%.

items.statement: Working capital days increased by 5 days in FY25, mainly due to 3-day increase in trade receivables
items.quote: Working capital days increased marginally by 5 days. Most of this was on trade receivables, so approximately 3 days on that.

items.statement: Consolidated debt at INR288 crores in FY25, up from INR233 crores; standalone debt-free
items.quote: If you see our debt levels, our total debt levels are INR288 crores, down from last year from INR233 crores. So, we're looking good even on that. Even currently, on the stand -alone basis, we do not have any debt and neither do we consume any working capital.

items.statement: Domestic demand slightly better in Q4 FY25 vs Q2-Q3; April FY26 better than last year; optimism from project completions and deferred demand returning
items.quote: Yes. So, I think my optimism comes from quarter 4. It was slightly better than quarter 2 and 3. And then also April has been slightly better than last year. So that's where the optimism is coming from.

items.statement: Exports down 20% in FY25 from INR20,000 crores to INR16,000-17,000 crores; green shoots visible for FY26
items.quote: From a high of INR20,000 crores, it was down to approximately anywhere between INR16,000 crores and INR17,000 crores is what the number is of exports.

items.statement: Competitor volume growth driven by lower product mix and pricing; Somany avoided lower realization products to protect margins
items.quote: That's because we stayed away from increasing lower quality and lower realization material. And I think if you see their sales, the sales has gone up, but the erosion of EBITDA is far, far, far more than ours

items.statement: Expect 70-80 Morbi plants to shut in FY26 due to financing, land costs, taxation, and quality/pricing discipline issues
items.quote: So, we believe that all of these put together, we think another 70, 80 plants, if not more, will get shut in Morbi again this year.

items.statement: Employee cost as percentage of sales to be lower in FY26 vs FY25
items.quote: We are trying our best to reduce the employee cost. So, if it is as a percentage, it will definitely be lower. So, I can only talk as a percentage. I can't talk in absolute terms. But yes, in percentage terms, it will be lower than FY '25.

items.statement: Sanitary ware plant capacity utilization at 96% in FY25; faucet plant at optimum capacity
items.quote: Capacity utilization in Sanitary Ware. I talked about the capacity utilization in Sanitary Ware is 96% in the Sanitary Ware plant, and we are running at optimum capacity in the fa ucet plant

items.statement: Max plant consolidation loss key risk; profitability expected once utilization reaches 75-80% by H2 FY26
items.quote: This is one piece which we need to solve, and it's already getting better, capacity utilization is higher in this plant and we are on the way to making this profitable very soon.

items.statement: US tariffs seen as positive for Indian tile exports
items.quote: As far as American tariffs are concerned which is a positive for India for the tile market. So overall, I think exports should also grow.

items.statement: Using biofuels to maximum extent alongside natural gas; blended gas cost similar to industry leader
items.quote: If I had to blend the price, it would be more or less the same. So, I'm not at any disadvantage industry leader. So, if that is your question. So, what I am quoting INR47 and INR51, this is purely only the natural gas price, nothing to do with the other biofuels, which we are also adopting and we're using to the

items.statement: Amora and Acer Ceramics plants exited; only Max plant remains loss-making
items.quote: What was not profitable, we have taken out of our kitty, which is Acer Ceramics and also Amora. So, we're looking very good for next year. This is one piece which we need to solve, and it's already getting better, capacity utilization is higher in this plant and we are on the way to making this profitable very soon.

items.statement: Depreciation increased due to reassessment of asset lives; new depreciation level is the new normal
items.quote: On depreciation, we have reassessed life of some of our assets, and that is additional depreciation has come. And the depreciation period, which you are seeing in this further case, is going to be the new normal because there are some assets licenses got reinstated.

items.statement: General trade grew 7% sequentially in Q4 driven by wholesale and rural growth; year-on-year still negative.
items.quote: During the quarter general trade registered a growth of 7% on a sequential basis while on the year-on-year basis it still remained negative.

items.statement: Wholesale channel showed recovery with 15% quarter-on-quarter growth in Q4.
items.quote: The wholesale channel, which had been an area of concern in the past few quarters showed signs of recovery with 15% quarter-on-quarter growth in Q4.

items.statement: Organized trade grew 30% year-on-year in Q4 and 18% for full year; saliency at 30%.
items.quote: The organized trade continued to do well, registering growth of 30% year-on-year in this quarter and 18% in the full year. Saliency of this cha nnel stood at 30

items.statement: International business grew 30% year-on-year in Q4 and 20% for FY25; GCC and Africa grew 25% in Q4.
items.quote: The international business recorded a robust growth of 30% year-on-year in Quarter 4 and 20% for FY'25. GCC and Africa grew by 25% year -on-year in Q4 and 7% in the full year.

items.statement: Rest of world markets posted 107% year-on-year growth in Q4 and 49% for full year led by Canada, Malaysia, USA, Tibet, New Zealand.
items.quote: The rest of the world markets posted excellent performance with 107% growth year -on-year in Q4 and 49% growth in the full year. This strong trajectory was led by key markets Canada, Malaysia, USA, Tibet and New Zealand.

items.statement: ADHO grew 3% year-on-year and 11% sequentially in Q4; Rs.10 SKU grew 16%, Rs.1 sachet declined 10%.
items.quote: ADHO delivered a growth of 3 % in Quarter 4 year-on-year basis and 11% sequentially. The growth was seen across majority packs. The Rs. 10 SKU grew by 16% year -on-year supported by the improved size, perception and value proposition. items.statement: Sequential recovery expected in FY26 with green shoots from moderating food inflation, tax cuts, and positive monsoon forecast
items.quote: We are seeing green shoots in the business. So, I think food inflation is kind of moderating. And we are seeing a 2% to 2.5% of food inflation.

items.statement: Standalone gross margin contracted 247 bps in Q4 due to 4.5-5% input inflation vs 3.5% price increases, competitive intensity limited pass-through
items.quote: We had an inflation of around inflation 4.5%- 5% and price increase was to an extent of 3.5% , and because of competitive intensity, we could not take the full inflation into the price increase. And that is why this GM contraction of 247 basis points that you see.

items.statement: Price increases of 3.5-4% taken in Q4 will flow through in Q1 FY26
items.quote: Yes. So there's already we've increased the prices by around 3.5%, 4%, and that flow-through will happen in quarter 1 also.

items.statement: Premiumization launches will have accretive margins to core products, lifting overall gross margin profile
items.quote: And also, just to add on the premiumization margin, there will be specific guardrails where every new product launch will have to have an accretive margin to the core product of it. And therefore, it will lift the overall gross margin profile.

items.statement: International business grew 19.3% in constant currency in Q4, with strong double-digit growth across MENA, Egypt, UK, USA, Turkey, Bangladesh
items.quote: International business exhibited a strong growth of 19.3% in constant currency and India business declined by around 3.4%.

items.statement: No specific capex numbers disclosed; focus on cost optimization program Samriddhi to fund brand investments
items.quote: And to get cost takeout to invest in our brands, we will be embarking on cost optimization exercise like Samriddhi, which also we did, but there will be a huge focus behind it, pretty much this.

items.quote: See, we mentioned a few examples of the categories, one was tea, other is baby diapers and other is Vita in MFD category. Now these have been margin dilutive for us and tha t's why we are planning to exit with a limited right to win and also breakfast cereals

items.quote: In GT, we are looking at consolidation of stockist in urban India. So reducing cost to serve, increasing span of control, increasing digitization in urban India and rural expand on villages, expand on direct reach, and focusing on the INR10, INR20 bundle pack.

items.statement: Campa Cola disruption in beverages; increased channel margins slightly for out-of-home portfolio to compete
items.quote: We have not changed any channel margins other than out-of-home portfolio where we have kind of increased our channel margins a little bit to compete with this Campa Cola war, which is being played out.

items.quote: As far as recycled plastic is concerned, our use of recycled plastic is fairly limited like all other players in the industry, and therefore, we've represented to the government also on the same because the recycled plastic today is more dearer in the market as compared to the regular plastic.

items.statement: Aggressive two-pronged M&A strategy: revenue-accretive acquisitions and future-fit portfolio in new-age healthcare, wellness foods, premium personal care
items.quote: M&A is what we will aggressively pursue and it will be a two-pronged M&A strategy from our point of view. One will be revenue accretive to us, which will substantially add to the revenue of the company because growth in GT is a little subdued. That is one. And the second will be creating a future fit portfolio which resonates to the new generation.

items.statement: Market share gains across 90% of portfolio; specific gains: Odonil +67bps, Odomos +386bps in MRC, Meswak/Herbal +15bps, Hair Oils +196bps, Chyawanprash +162bps, Honey +75bps, Glucose +112bps, Hajmola +233bps, J&N beverages +261bps

items.quote: Global crude oil demand in Q4 grew by about 1%. Chinese crude oil imports also grew slightly. They have been building stocks as far as we can see.

items.statement: Iron ore trade weak due to seasonal disruptions in Australia and Brazil; global grain trade dropped due to lower Chinese soybean imports and lower Black Sea wheat production

Global grain trade has also dropped off during the quarter.

items.quote: Our target is 35% ROCE, which was around 25% this year. And in next 2-3 years, our target is to increase this ROCE above 50%.

items.statement: Capex of Rs. 1,500 crores approved for 2 million ton capacity expansion over next 3 years
items.quote: We have taken a total of Rs. 1500 crore approval from board. Apart from that , we are doing 4 plants of 2.5 lakhs per ton each in value-addition which will be in 2030

items.statement: Capex phased at Rs. 500 crores per year for FY26-28
items.quote: Rs. 500 crores per year you can factor in.

items.statement: Expanding capacity from 5 million to 7 million tons in next few years, targeting 10 million tons by 2030
items.quote: our total plan for 2030 is 10 million tons minimum. 10 million tons, means that 5 million tons we are already ready for marketing.

items.statement: Adding plants in East India (500k tons), Dubai (200k tons), South India (360k tons), Bhuj Gujarat (300k tons)
items.quote: Expansion in the virgin markets – So virgin market number one is East India, where we are adding two plants with combined capacity of 500,000 tons. The next virgin market is Dubai in the international market, where we are adding an additional 200,000 tons. Then in South India, we are adding up a fourth plant with the capacity of 360,000 tons.

items.statement: Roofing sheet capacity at 100% utilization, expanding by 500k tons; heavy structural at 60% utilization, expanding by 100k tons
items.quote: The roofing sheet is 100% utilized as of now, capacity front and that's why we are expanding. And in heavy structural, the utilization is 60% as of now.

items.statement: General product EBITDA improved to Rs. 2,800/ton, Rs. 1,000/ton higher than 5-year average
items.quote: Now if you look at the margin in our general product category we reported Rs. 2,800 per ton EBITDA. Now that's almost Rs. 1,000 per ton higher than what we have been reporting over the last five years.

items.statement: Blended EBITDA target near Rs. 5,000/ton for FY26, improving beyond over next 3-4 years
items.quote: For FY'26, guidance is near Rs. 5,000 a ton. And over the next few years, EBITDA spreads will continue to improve beyond Rs. 5,000 per ton

items.statement: Dubai export EBITDA at Rs. 7,000-8,000/ton; India export margin currently Rs. 2,000-3,000/ton, targeting Rs. 7,000-9,000/ton from Q2
items.quote: EBITDA per ton for the Dubai export market is close to Rs. 7,000-Rs. 8,000 per ton. And from India, right now the margin is not good, maybe Rs. 2,000-Rs. 2,500 per ton. But there is a reason, the local st eel prices are high than the import price. So now we are importing some quantity for exporting the material. Then we should think our margin is go to 8 to Rs. 10,000 per ton

items.statement: Heavy structural EBITDA sustainable at Rs. 8,000-9,000/ton
items.quote: It should be in the same range Rs. 8,000 to Rs. 9,000 a ton.

items.statement: Employee cost target reduction from Rs. 1,000/ton to Rs. 600/ton over 2 years via automation and scale
items.quote: Now I think this year we will reduce to Rs. 800 per ton this year in FY'25-'26 and in FY'26-'27 we will bring it to Rs. 600 per ton.

items.statement: Power cost target reduction from Rs. 7.6/unit to below Rs. 6.5/unit this year and Rs. 5.5/unit next year via solar contracts
items.quote: Our per unit cost is, last year's cost is Rs. 7.6 per unit cost, electricity cost. We have signed lot of Solar and other contract. So I think this year 7.6 we will bring it down to less than 6.5 and next year we are targeting to bring it down to 5.5.

items.statement: April volume slightly below target by 5-6%, May going well; H1 target 1.7-1.8M tons, H2 over 2M tons
items.quote: Right now, we are right on track. April is just slightly little bit from our target. Like every year the April is on the downside. We are less than our target, volume target by 5% to 6%. And May is going good. So I don't think like first half of the month we can do 17-18 lakh ton, in the second half we crossed 2 million ton.

items.statement: Export share currently 6%, target to exceed 10% in next 2 years
items.quote: As of now we are at 6% and target is to take it beyond 10%.

items.statement: US/Canada market opened after duty equalization for UAE; Europe exports at 5,000-6,000 tons/month
items.quote: Earlier the US and Canada market is catered by the Korean and Japanese mills. But after the Trump government, they equal the duties. The US duty structure which they had, UAE was made equal to Korea and Japan. So all of a sudden US and Canada's market has opened up quite well

items.statement: Net cash position of over Rs. 300 crores as of March 31, 2025
items.quote: It has been a second year that we have closed our balance sheet with net cash. As at 31 st March 2025, we stand with net cash of more than Rs. 300 crores on our balance sheet.

items.statement: Capex to be funded entirely from internal cash flows
items.quote: The CAPEX for this is around INR 15 billion, which will be spread across the next few years and it will be easily funded from the internal cash flows.

items.statement: Incremental growth from new geographies, products, and markets to improve sales mix and EBITDA spreads
items.quote: The incremental growth is coming from new geographies, new products, better sales mix, which will continue to improve our EBITDA spreads going forward.

items.statement: Entering super specialty tubes (SS pipe, API, seamless, automated) with 250k tons each by 2030 for import substitution
items.quote: We are going to come up with very, very small investments, right? 250,000 tons into four different categories, okay? So putting up and investing small amount of Rs. 300 crore-Rs. 400 crore and testing the market into a new product segment

items.statement: Brand premium of 5-6% over nearest competitor in general products sustained via distribution network and product portfolio
items.quote: we can command a 5 %-6% premium over our next competitor. So this gives us confidence that maintaining 20 % volume growth like how we did in last 2 years, my EBITDA spread will continue to improve

items.statement: No hedging instrument available for steel inventory exposure
items.quote: There is no such product to do this. So there is no way, there is no instrument to do this.

items.statement: Chairman surrendered salary and commissions for FY25 and FY26 to lead cost reduction drive
items.quote: Sanjayji just took the lead and he wanted to set by an example and he said okay let me surrender my salary all my commissions for FY'25 and FY'26

items.statement: Steel price crash of 25% in last 18 months depressed margins; no similar sharp decline foreseen
items.quote: Steel prices crashed by 25 % in last 18 months. So that's what depressed the margins. But good part was that we could build the market share at a level, now where we stand, we can command a 5 %-6% premium over our next competitor.

items.statement: Sales volume crossed 3.1 million tons in FY25, making APL Apollo world's largest downstream steel player outside China
items.quote: We crossed 3.1 million tons as sales volume for the full year. This makes APL Apollo as the world's largest downstream steel player outside China.

items.statement: ROCE at 25% in FY25, targeting 35% in FY26 and 50%+ in 2-3 years
items.quote: Our ROCE for FY'25 was 25%. This is slightly off last year, but we shall come back very strongly

items.statement: FY26 standalone revenue expected to decline 5%-7% with operating margin of 10%-11%
items.quote: Assuming some order inflows in the next few months, we expect around 5%-7% decline in stand-alone revenue for this fiscal with an operating margin of around 10% -11%.

items.statement: FY26 consolidated revenue expected to grow 10%-15% with PAT growing further
items.quote: However, at the same time, we are expecting a 10% -15% g rowth in consolidated revenues. And if you look at even this year's consolidated PAT, that consolidated PAT will continue to grow even furthermore next

items.statement: FY26 order inflow target of INR15,000-20,000 crores
items.quote: So, we are looking at about a INR20,000 crores order inflow this year. INR15,000 crores to 20,000 crores at least what we're expecting because last 2 years have been quite muted.

items.statement: FY26 standalone debt reduction of INR500 crores and consolidated debt reduction of over INR2,000 crores
items.value: INR500 crores standalone; INR2,000+ crores consolidated
items.quote: Next year, stand-alone debt will be less by INR500 crores and the consol debt will be at least INR2,000 crores will be reduction in that as well.

items.statement: Net debt-free target at standalone level within next 2 years remains intact
items.quote: That is very much there that we will be a net debt 0 company in the next 2 years.

items.statement: Current order book of INR14,923 crores executable over 2-3 years; INR7,000 crores revenue expected from existing order book in FY26
items.quote: Out of this order book, you can split this into 2 years. So, about INR7,000 crores of revenue should be able to come from this order book alone.

items.statement: Coal MDO orders now included in order book adding 3-year visibility; previously omitted in error
items.quote: Because when you look at last year, till then, we were not adding the coal MDO orders, which should have been rightly done because that is a pure visibility for us.

items.statement: No planned capex for FY26 except minor replacement; coal handling plant capex of INR850 crores starting next quarter over 2 years
items.quote: Now in terms of capex for the company this year, we are not expecting to do any capex in this financial year per se. So, if there is some very small replacement capex that we have to do, that will happen.

items.statement: Coal handling plant construction to start next quarter, complete in 2 years at INR850 crores capex
items.quote: So, the coal handling plant capex is around INR850 crores. And we will start constructing coal handling plant from next quarter, and it will complete in 2 years' time.

items.statement: FY25 standalone EBITDA margin declined to ~10% from ~12.3% YoY; consolidated EBITDA margin improved significantly
items.quote: On full year basis, FY '25 versus FY '24, the revenue decreased by 14.55% from INR10,537 crores to INR9,004 crores in FY '25. The EBITDA decreased by 30% from INR1,299 crores to INR903 crores.

items.statement: Government targeting 10,000 km highway construction in FY26 including 1,100 km in Northeast and 750 km in tribal regions; 50 airport projects over 5 years; 78 tunnel projects worth INR1.1 lakh crores
items.quote: For the next year, the government has set an ambitious target of constructing 10,000 kilometers of highways. It includes the development of 1,100 kilometers in the Northeastern states and 750 kilometers in tribal regions.

items.statement: NHAI ordering expected to pick up significantly from Q2 FY26
items.quote: Sir, we're expecting second quarter onwards, it should pick up significantly.

items.statement: Government tightened EPC qualification criteria to pre-COVID levels; similar steps expected for HAM to reduce unqualified competition
items.quote: EPC project, the government has already taken the steps to increase the qualification criteria pre-COVID level. So, they have increased the performance guarantee requirement, the technical requirement, and they have increased in terms of the technical and financial criteria, EPC is done.

items.statement: Working capital cycle improved at FY25 end after Jal Jeevan Mission payments received; expected to remain in similar range in FY26
items.quote: Luckily, the overall working capital cycle came down by the end of financial year. We are expecting the next year's working capital cycle to also be in a s imilar range only

items.statement: FY26 interest cost estimated at INR400 crores on standalone revenue of INR8,500 crores
items.quote: So basically, for the revenue of INR8,500 crores, we are expecting interest cost around INR400 crores.

items.statement: Siarmal MDO produced 18 MMT in FY25 vs 15 MMT target (original 10 MMT); targeting 25 MMT in FY26 vs 18 MMT target
items.quote: We are well equipped to exceed our targets for next year as well, and we hope to achieve production volume of about 25 million metric ton as compared to the target of 18 million metric ton.

items.statement: Pachhwara MDO at peak production of 6.9 MMT in FY25 (7 MMT capacity); stable for 53 years
items.quote: In our Pachhwara MDO, we have achieved production of 6.9 million metric ton in FY 2025, which is a peak production. This is a 7 million metric ton capacity coal MDO.

items.statement: Alpha InvIT: 8 of 18 assets transferred (7 COD, 1 pre-COD); INR550 crores total consideration with INR360 crores expected in FY26
items.value: INR550 crores total; INR360 crores FY26
items.quote: Total transfer the money is INR550 crores. And out of that, we are expecting INR360 crores we will receive this year. And it is close to 7 assets we are expecting by March, 26% can be transferred.

items.statement: Publicly listed InvIT draft offer document filed March 2025; approvals expected this quarter
items.quote: The formation process of our publicly listed InvIT is progressing well. The InvIT has filed draft offer document in March '25, and we are expecting the approvals within this quarter.

items.statement: Shrem InvIT: sold 1.27 crore units for INR136 crores in FY25; received INR120 crores cash distribution; holding 6 crore units yielding INR70-80 crores annually
items.quote: On an opportunity basis, we have sold 1.27 crores unit and realized around INR136 crores in the last financial year. This is in addition to a cash distribution of INR120 crores received from Shrem InvIT during the last financial year.

items.statement: Evaluating international opportunities including coal block in Mozambique
items.quote: Yes, sir, we were evaluating international markets as well. We were evaluating a coal block in Mozambique as well.

items.statement: 91% of HAM projects won by non-recognized/smaller players in FY25; government tightening criteria to improve quality
items.quote: If you look at the last year's data, in HAM, 91% projects were won by non-recognized or the smaller players, 91%, let that sink in.

items.statement: Government rethinking awarding process after challenges with financial closure and construction quality from low bidders
items.quote: They were facing challenges around financial closure of the HAM projects. They were facing challenges around even once they're getting started, there is because they have been bid at some really ridiculous numbers, they were seeing challenges in progress.

items.statement: Jal Jeevan Mission payments were delayed 9-10 months in FY25 causing elevated working capital; payments realized at year-end
items.quote: While this year, we know that the payments of Jal Jeevan Mission were very, very problematic and slow almost 9-10 months, we didn't see any of that payment coming in, which kept our stand-alone debt levels elevated.

items.statement: 80% of current business is EPC; road segment reduced; diversified across irrigation, water, metro, railways, airports, tunneling, coal mining, optical fiber
items.quote: See the bulk of our business is EPC because the HAM model is only in the road business. Now road itself has become a small part of our overall order book. So, when you look at the company, even if you look at the presentation that we have given, almost 80% of the business that the company is doing right now is EPC.

items.statement: FY27 revenue expected at Rs 22,000-23,000 crore and EBITDA at Rs 2,800-3,200 crore based on current realizations
items.quote: basically if you look at the revenue expectation post-27 based on current realization is about anything between Rs. 22,000 crores to Rs. 23,000 crores and EBITDA we are currently this year at about Rs. 1,866 crores. So it should be anything between Rs. 2,800 crores to Rs. 3200 crores.

items.statement: Minimum 15% annual revenue CAGR targeted
items.quote: we are positioned to achieve a minimum 15% CAGR annually.

items.statement: FY26 capex of Rs 2,010 crore planned across captive power, solar, finished steel, stainless steel and aluminum
items.quote: The remaining CAPEX of around Rs. 3,000 crores, out of the Rs. 3,000 crores, the Rs. 2,000 crores of CAPEX will be incurred during the Financial Year '25-'26 which comprising of captive power, solar, and this combined finished steel Rs. 413 crore, stainless steel Rs. 784 crore, aluminum Rs. 126 crore which all conclude there is a CAPEX of Rs. 2010 crores.

items.statement: Total announced capex of Rs 10,025 crore since IPO, 66% (Rs 6,584 crore) incurred and Rs 4,908 crore capitalized as of FY25
items.quote: Out of the Rs. 10,025 crore of capital announced since IPO, we have already cumulative incurred the amount of Rs. 6,584 crore which is entirely from the internal accrual up to the Financial Year 2025. And capitalized out of this Rs. 6,584 crore, we have capitalized till date Rs. 4,908 crore worth of assets.

items.statement: Remaining Rs 3,904 crore capex to be spent over next two years; carbon steel mostly in FY26, stainless and aluminum in FY27
items.quote: The remaining Rs. 3,904 crore shall be spend over a period of next two financial years with the majority of carbon steel related CAPEX being completed in the current financial year that is '25-'26. The CAPEX related to aluminum and stainless steel to be completed in the Financial Year '26-'27.

items.statement: Blast furnace at Jamuria commissioned in Q3 FY25, achieved 100% capacity in few months, targeting 110% in FY26
items.quote: I am very happy to share that today, in a very few months of operation, we have achieved 100% capacity and we expect that we should be overcoming the 100% into 110% capacity for this year.

items.statement: Color coated plant commissioned last quarter, achieved 90% utilization last month, doubling capacity
items.quote: It is very interesting that we just commissioned the plant in the last quarter of the last year. And last month we achieved almost 90% capacity utilization. Our product is well accepted in the market. And now we are gearing up for high value-added product in the existing product. And also doubling the capacity of the existing HR color coated galvalume business what we have commissioned last year.

items.statement: Stainless steel wire and bright bar division commissioned with 40,000 tons/year capacity, 3-6 months to stabilize
items.quote: comprising of wire and bright bar our total install capacity is close to 40,000 tons per year presently. And on an average I can say that once we establish our product and we are through with all the, overcome all the challenges because we had put up the world class facility so there is no doubt.

items.statement: Launched color-coded roofing sheets under SEL Tiger brand (Royal, Elite, Azure, Alfa variants) and food-grade aluminum foil under SEL Tiger Foil
items.quote: A significant highlight this quarter was launched by our new range of color-coded roofing sheet under SEL Tiger brand introduced in the variant of Royal, Elite, Azure, Alfa, a different brand, a different category and product and price mix.

items.statement: Aluminum foil demand expected to grow 8-10% CAGR by 2030; company well positioned with Jharkhand plant
items.quote: With the demand of aluminum foil in the food business, we expect that we should be growing around 8% to 10% CAGR by 2030 and we will be well positioned to capitalize on the rising demand and emerging opportunity in this sector.

items.statement: Stainless steel flat products being added (tubes, precision steel for railways, defense); focusing on 200/400 series (nickel-free) using captive iron, power, ferroalloys
items.quote: In stainless steel, we are putting up a flat product, mean, we are putting up complete downstream where we can cater to the tube market to the high segment precision steel in the stainless steel sector which is used for the decorative steel in the railways, in lot of other businesses in the defense, lot of requirements are there.

items.statement: Aluminum battery foil approved for EV battery supply; only approved domestic supplier currently
items.quote: In aluminum, as we said, that we have already been approved in the battery foil business. And we expect that once we see any battery plant commission, so we will be, as on date we are only the choice in the country who has been approved and is well established to supply the battery foil in the EV battery space.

items.statement: Q4 FY25 EBITDA margin 12.5%, up 30 bps YoY and 40 bps QoQ; FY25 gross margin 27.7% vs 28.2% FY24
items.quote: Quarter 4 '24-'25 on a consolidated basis, we reported an EBITDA margin of 12.5% which is 30 bps higher on a year-on-year basis and 40 bps higher when compared on a quarter-on-quarter basis.

items.statement: Stainless steel wire/bright bar expected average EBITDA Rs 7,000-12,000/ton, some products >Rs 30,000/ton
items.quote: And on an average I can say that once we establish our product and we are through with all the, overcome all the challenges because we had put up the world class facility so there is no doubt. And since it is a forward and backward integration of our existing stainless steel long product division which we have acquired through the NCLT in Indore. So we expect that close to Rs. 7,000 to Rs. 12,000

items.statement: DI pipe EBITDA currently Rs 7,000-10,000/ton vs Rs 18,000-20,000/ton last year; conservative investment of Rs 350-400 crore for 300k tons
items.quote: DI pipe has been able to gain the EBITDA of close to Rs. 18,000-Rs. 20,000 a ton in last one year and presently I think it is struggling between Rs. 7,000-Rs. 8,000 to Rs. 10,000 a ton.

items.statement: Q1 FY26 expected to show volume and revenue growth QoQ; management optimistic on demand
items.quote: Market is not bad I would say and I expect that there will be a volume growth. The revenue growth will be also there in this Q1 and I am pretty optimistic like everything is looking very positive.

items.statement: OPVC pipes affecting DI pipe industry below 350mm size (40-50% of market); DI still preferred for industrial/open-space applications
items.quote: Below 350, this is close to around 40% to 50%.

items.statement: Steel realizations down 3-5% in FY25 vs FY24; offset by higher aluminum foil and stainless steel realizations and lower raw material costs per ton
items.quote: There has been a decrease in the realization across steel product in the range of 3% to 5% in the Financial Year '24-'25 as compared to Financial Year '23-'24. However, on the back of increased realization in aluminum foil product and stainless steel, we have been able to maintain the gross margin at 27.7% in the Financial Year '24-'25 as against 28.2% in the Financial Year '23-'24.

items.statement: Government imposed safeguard duty on aluminum foil imports from China; positive for domestic manufacturers
items.quote: On the regulatory front, we welcome the government decision to impose a safeguard duty on the aluminum foil import from China. This policy is a very positive step to support the domestic manufacture by mitigating unfair pricing pressure.

items.statement: FY25 working capital days 22 vs 12 in FY24; increase due to new verticals (blast furnace, color coated, stainless steel)
items.quote: In the Financial Year 2025, our working capital days is 22 as against 12 days at the end of the Financial Year 2024. This is against the backdrop of introductions of blast furnace, color coated sheet and stainless steel.

items.statement: Inventory days expected to hover at 90-100 days with new projects
items.quote: The inventory days will be in terms of the new upcoming project, the inventory day will be hovering in between 90 to 100 days.

items.statement: Gross debt/equity 0.07x (FY25) vs 0.06x (FY24); net cash Rs 1,062 crore (cash Rs 1,830 crore vs gross debt Rs 768 crore)
items.quote: The gross debt to equity which was at 0.06x at the end of the Financial Year 2024 is slightly higher at 0.07x at the end of the Financial Year 2024-25. Our net cash positions is Rs. 1,062 crore as on 31 st March 2025 as against the gross debt of Rs. 768 crore as we have cash and cash equivalent along with the long term investments worth Rs. 1,830 crore.

items.statement: Bank limit utilization expected to remain moderate; annual cash accrual sufficient for capex and debt repayment
items.quote: I would like to assure you that the bank limit utilization at the consolidated level is expected to remain moderate going forward too. Also the annual cash accrual should suffice for the capital expenditure requirement and debt repayment.

items.statement: Final dividend Rs 2.25/share declared (subject to AGM approval); total FY25 dividend outflow ~Rs 125 crore including interim
items.quote: declared a final dividend per share of Rs. 2.25 per share, subject to the shareholder approval in the insuring annual general meeting. We shall have a dividend out go of around Rs. 125 crore for the Financial Year 2025 including the dividend of Rs. 2.25 per share which was declared earlier in the form of interim dividend.

items.statement: Capital allocation policy: 70-80% of cash reinvested, 20% retained as liquidity surplus, 10% returned as dividend
items.quote: As you all aware that for many years we have been following a prudent capital allocation policy by which 70% of the cash generated is returned back into the business, 20% is retained as a liquidity surplus and 10% is returned to our esteemed shareholder as a dividend.

items.statement: FY25 ROCE 15%, ROE 14%; target >20% ROCE/ROE for future projects
items.quote: Our ROCE, ROE at the end of the Financial Year 2025 are at 15% and 14% respectively.

items.statement: Management conservative on FY27 EBITDA guidance (Rs 2,800-3,200 crore) due to geopolitical uncertainty; aims to over-deliver on commitments
items.quote: We would love to be conservative because you never know what kind of changes happen in the geopolitical situation. And we want to be pretty sure that our deliverables and our commitment should not disappoint our investors.

items.statement: Import dumping risk marginal for product portfolio; psychological impact possible but limited direct effect
items.quote: Majorly not because you if you see in our business product module, very less percentage of import threat is there. But overall, the psychological scenario do matter.

items.statement: Expect to return to decent retail area growth from Q3 FY26 onwards, focusing on high-quality net area additions
items.quote: However, at maybe 3rd Quarter onwards, I think we are quite sure of getting back on decent retail area growth, and, most importantly, one thing which I want to sort of bring some light on is quality retail area will grow tremendously from a complete financial year perspective.

items.statement: Added ~85,000 sq ft net retail area in FY25, opened 3 Twamev EBOs and 1 Mohey EBO
items.quote: In the Financial Year '25, we have expanded our retail footprint by approximately 85,000 square feet of net retail area. We have also successfully rolled out three EBOs of Twamev in this financial year.

items.statement: EBO network at 1.79 million sq ft across 678 stores in 256 cities globally as of March 2025
items.quote: As of March '25, Vedant Fashions' EBO area stands at 1.79 million square feet, spanning across 678 stores in 256 cities and towns globally.

items.statement: Q1 FY25 severely impacted by negligible wedding dates; 9-month July-March retail sales grew 9.3% with LTL growth of 2.9%
items.quote: However, in the nine-month period from July to March FY '25, retail sales grew by 9.3%, with like-to-like sales growing by about 2.9%.

items.statement: FY25 gross margin 67.2%, EBITDA margin 46.6%, PAT margin 28%
items.quote: The Company continued to report industry-leading gross margin of around 67.2% and a healthy EBITDA margin of around 46.6%.

items.statement: Customer sales (secondary) Rs 18,929 million in FY25, up 2.2% YoY; Q4 customer sales Rs 5,207 million, up 1.9% YoY
items.quote: During Financial Year '25, sales of our customers were Rs. 18,929 million, reflecting a growth of approximately 2.2% over Financial Year '24.

items.statement: Mohey growing ~25% faster than company average; shifted from bridal to wedding wear with lower ASP products (Rs 7-8k vs Rs 22-23k bridal)
items.quote: And when you sort of talked about Mohey, there has been quite a large delta in terms of growth. So, Mohey would have a close to 25% odd delta in terms of the Company from a growth perspective.

items.statement: 40% revenue from grooms/brides, 60% from family/wedding attendees; latter behaves like lifestyle market
items.quote: Now when we say consumer sentiments impact us, it will impact how much 40% is willing to spend, but they will still continue to buy. But the 60% behaves very similar to the other lifestyle markets of India.

items.statement: Competitor store count tripled in 2-3 years but no single player gained share; most new stores financially unsustainable
items.quote: However, has one player taken any market share? That has not been the case, certainly. It's a large number of players opening a few stores, that is what we are seeing on the ground majorly.

items.statement: Receivables up Rs 50 cr due to store additions (50%+) and Mohey/Twamev stock in existing stores; inventory built strategically for Eid timing
items.quote: So, look, our receivables have increased by around Rs. 50 crores, okay. And it is majorly because of the store addition, we had 85,000 - 90,000 square feet net addition during this year.

items.statement: Rent cost up 1.5-2% due to negative operating leverage; renegotiating leases and closing unviable stores to control rent OC
items.quote: And overall, it might have gone up by about 1.5% to 2% this year at the Company's books level, majorly on account of having a negative operating leverage.

items.statement: Launched VFL Parivaar app for daily 1-2 min training of fashion advisors; seeing KPI uptick from daily reinforcement vs quarterly training
items.quote: One of the biggest innovations that was done by us this year, is we created our own app, which we call VFL Parivaar. And every single fashion advisor in our ecosystem is sent a one to two-minute training material every morning.

items.statement: AP-Telangana market dragging performance; macroeconomic slowdown affecting multiple brands equally in region
items.quote: I think the challenges are a lot more macro in nature, that is why a lot more brands are facing the heat in that market. And we see a lot of other challenges with the market as well, reflecting a slower economic sort of slowdown in that entire belt.

items.statement: April showing green shoots due to better wedding dates vs last year, but overall sentiment still weak; expect strategies to fire from Q2/mid-Q2
items.quote: So, overall, we do see green shoots, majorly on account of having wedding dates this year versus negligible wedding dates last year. So, business is better on that account. But overall, in terms of expectations, I w ould say that still overall sentiments we can see from the market are weak and not the best

items.statement: Gross store additions ~1.8 lakh sq ft in FY25; net lower due to aggressive fleet consolidation of unviable stores
items.quote: So, at a gross level we opened about 1.8 lakh square feet this year, which is entering the most important markets of India where we were not present or expanding our presence in our important existing markets.

items.statement: Franchisee acquisition not a challenge; existing partners profitable but ROF down; partners engaged in business reviews to improve performance
items.quote: Rather, even now I would say that has not been a challenge at all and is still one of the easier things to achieve. The second part is regarding existing partners. Now, certainly with lower revenue per square feet, their overall ROF falls, but given how profitable our model has been for them, they continue to make decent money.

items.statement: Launched 2.3-2.4x more new designs in FY25; targeting faster production turnaround and trend responsiveness
items.quote: So, if we used to launch one design, this year we did close to 2.3x, 2.4x of the number of designs. Ensuring if there's any trend in the market, we are able to understand them early and have it available across our fleet.

items.statement: Shifting to digital-first with 12-13 mini-campaigns vs 1-2 big campaigns; rapid speed execution focus
