items.quote: We are not looking for Rs.200 crores, we are not looking for any fundraising and significant CAPEX investment because the infrastructure we have built is poised to achieve that target.

items.statement: Planning to acquire 100-bed hospital outside Dhanbad in current FY; Rs.20 crore revenue factored into FY27 target; due diligence completed, analyzing acquisition mode
items.quote: Sir, we are targeting to add 100 beds, another hospital we want to acquire because when we have fund available, when we have things, it is in the pipeline to acquire 100 bed hospital and bed capacity another 50 beds will be added in the existing both the hospitals.

items.statement: Revenue grew 43% YoY to Rs.120.6 crores in FY25; IPD revenue up 40% to Rs.99.1 crores; OPD revenue up 42% to Rs.19.7 crores
items.quote: Revenue from operations grew 43% on year-on-year basis. Now it is Rs.120.6 crores from Rs.84.4 crores in financial year 2024.

items.statement: EBITDA grew 47% YoY to Rs.223.5 crores with margin improving to 20% from 19%; PAT margin expanded from 5% to 9%
items.quote: EBITDA grew by 47% on year-on-year to Rs.223.5 crores with EBITDA margin improving to 20% up from 19% last year.

items.statement: Debtors increased Rs.15 crores; 92% cancer patients cashless (government schemes); receivables primarily from government; debtor days 3-4 months; reduced existing hospital debtors to 18%
items.quote: Sir, it is all primarily from government. Because of being a cancer hospital, our catchment area has increased. Earlier, only patients from two or three districts used to come but now patients from more than 10 districts come to us.

items.statement: Managing debtor-creditor balance by slowing vendor payments if needed; weekly monitoring of collections; strengthening IT for patient-wise tracking
items.quote: Suppose if there is a little mismatch, like our purchases, our vendors major component is of supply and medicine we will slow down the payment and this will create a balance. We will increase the recovery and if there is a mismatch in that we will slow down our payment that we have speed up.

items.statement: Debt around Rs.40 crores; no external funding needed for growth; 20% unused working capital limits
items.quote: No, look for growth investments have already been made. We do not need any funding from outside for growth. The capacity that we have built, we have to use that capacity in a better way.

items.statement: Aggressive cost control to achieve EBITDA targets; employee cost growth to moderate to 20% from 30% jump in FY25
items.quote: We are working on cost control very aggressively, we are on to it and we believe that the EBITDA target will be achieved.

items.statement: Hired DM Hemato Oncologist (only one in Jharkhand); attracting doctors from across India; conducive environment with no clinical interference
items.quote: Recently, we added one DM Hemato Oncology, which is not available in the entire Jharkhand. So we believe that we will be able to add doctors because over a period of time, we have built a good brand.

items.statement: Super Speciality hospital ARPOB Rs.17,505 (up from Rs.17,177); Cancer hospital ARPOB Rs.30,500 annually, Rs.65,481 in Q4; linear accelerator utilization 20/day targeting 80/day
items.quote: Our ARPOB in the Super Speciality hospital increased from 17,505 from 17,177 last year. In the cancer hospital, our ARPOB stood at approximately 30,500.

items.statement: Bed occupancy: Super Speciality 61% (10,576 inpatients, 1.05 lakh outpatients); Cancer hospital 30%
items.quote: In financial year 2025, the hospital achieved a bed occupancy rate of approximately 61%, serving more than 10,576 inpatients and more than 1.05 lakh outpatients.

items.statement: Cancer hospital 92% cashless patients (Ayushman Bharat, Mukhyamantri Gambhir Bimari Yojana 66%); Super Speciality 50% cash, 50% cashless; cash patients only 5-8%
items.quote: In the cancer hospital, we have 92% cashless patients, and cashless patients are either from Ayushman Bharat or government sponsored schemes. So government response for these schemes money comes when government allocates funds.

items.statement: Land dispute resolved - High Court removed Asarfi as party; affidavit submitted by opposing parties; no pending litigation on hospital land
items.quote: Yes, land issue is resolved to the extent that they submitted to people who are fighting with us, they submitted affidavit that we do not want to fight with Asarfi Hospital right now. So this issue gets resolved.

items.statement: Cancer revenue 60% from non-admitted patients (radiation, medical oncology); sold eye unit equipment to SharpSight, now renting facility to them
items.quote: Cancer hospital bed capacity occupancy does not denote the actual numbers. When you talk about the numbers of Medica Calcutta, which has been taken over by Manipal, they have 65-bed occupancy and having a turnover of Rs.110 crores.

items.statement: Dividend under consideration; will implement when situation improves
items.quote: We are definitely considering it, we are working on it. As soon as some situation improves, we will definitely do that.

items.statement: Affiliated with National Board of Examination for DNB courses; 150+ health videos, 139+ camps, 110 health talks across 10 districts in last 6 months
items.quote: We have added another feather which is we have been affiliated by National Board of Examination for running DNB Courses.

items.statement: Food delivery GOV growth guidance 18-22% YoY for FY26, trending toward lower end
items.quote: We have spoken about an 18% to 22% kind of year -on-year growth guidance, and we are towards the lower end of that range.

items.statement: Instamart contribution margin breakeven targeted within 3-5 quarters, could be Q3 FY26 or Q1 FY27
items.quote: As I said, we are seeking flexibility over two more quarters, it could happen in December, it could happen in the June quarter of the next calendar year.

items.statement: Instamart AOV growth guidance upgraded to high-teens for coming year
items.quote: We have continued to guide that we will be doing double digit. If you have observed that we have now upped this guidance, we expect that over the coming year we will be able to deliver high teens growth on the AOV.

items.statement: Capex Rs 425 crore in Q4 FY25 for 314 stores and warehouse expansion; peak capex cycle behind us
items.quote: We do believe that a large part of the overall CAPEX cycle that we had started for this deployment journey is now behind us, and going forward you should see that reducing in a significant way.

items.statement: Per dark store capex not more than Rs 80 lakh, higher for Megapods
items.quote: As we had guided, our per dark store expenditure is not more than Rs. 80 lakhs, it could be higher on the Megapods.

items.statement: Added 314 dark stores in Q4 FY25; will densify Tier 1 towns where stores hit 2,000-2,500 orders
items.quote: We have added 314 stores last quarter, as well as we have been increasing our warehouse footprint, and that has led to the overall capex deployment.

items.statement: No specific store count guidance; store additions to be derivative of growth not driver
items.quote: From here on, once the network is already laid out, we do believe that the store expansion should be a derivative of growth and not the other way around.

items.statement: Instamart added 2.8 million MTU in Q4 FY25, more than previous six quarters combined
items.quote: Just in the last quarter we have added more users as compared to the last six quarters, right, we added 2.8 million MTU.

items.statement: Bolt contributes 12% of overall food delivery order volumes
items.quote: Bolt has grown at a faster clip and contributes 12% of overall order volumes today.

items.statement: Food delivery adjusted EBITDA run-rate near Rs 1,000 crore; 80 bps operating leverage in FY25
items.quote: If you look at the trajectory of our food delivery business, it is now run rating at a close to Rs. 1,000 crores EBITDA.

items.statement: Food delivery contribution margin to expand 100-150 bps to hit steady-state EBITDA guidance
items.quote: Contribution margin, there's an expansion that we expect by another 100 to 150 basis points to hit to our steady state EBITDA guidance.

items.statement: Instamart contribution margin -5.6% in Q4; peak investment behind us, CM to improve quarter-on-quarter
items.quote: The peak of the contribution margin investment is behind us. As you have seen, our network has expanded very rapidly over the H2 of last financial year, which means there's a certain amount of underutilization of the cost that is sitting into our P&L which will start decreasing quarter-on-quarter from here on.

items.statement: Out-of-home (Dineout) turned profitable; steady-state target 4% EBITDA margin
items.quote: We do expect that this business, at a steady state, again, can deliver in the ZIP code of 4% positive EBITDA for us.

items.statement: Maxxsaver kicks in above Rs 999; fulfillment cost advantage offsets discount to keep economics same ballpark
items.quote: Structurally, the Maxxsaver option which kicks in for majority of the customers at greater than Rs. 999. So, the economics overall is not very different. There is obviously a discount that we give to the customer. But the fulfillment cost advantage that w e get out of a higher order value allows us to be at the same ballpark

items.statement: Megapods have higher AOV and throughput; mature Megapods show highest profitability
items.quote: Matured Megapods which have come up in places where they were already mature, it has actually the highest profitability for us.

items.statement: Food delivery demand improved in Feb-Mar vs Jan; 28-day February had calendar effect
items.quote: We did see play out that way where February and March were stronger than January. Also remember, this has a February which was a 28-day month, so there is that effect, yes.

items.statement: Quick commerce MTU growth 40% QoQ in Q4; GOV growth lagged due to new cohort lower spend
items.quote: Our MTU growth is essentially higher than our GOV and OPD growth. The way to look at it is that early consumers, be it whatever quarter, whatever time that you acquire, we will be spending less in that specific quarter.

items.statement: Competition intensity stable from existing players; new entrants expected but unclear
items.quote: From the existing quick commerce players we have not seen any magnitude of going up or down in the recent past. At the same time, there is the expectation of newer set of competition coming in, but enough is not known yet to be able to give you specific guidance on that.

items.statement: Working capital increase due to ad revenue collection timing; expected to normalize next quarter
items.quote: On the working capital side, this is more of a point in time period. You should see some of it starting to come back. There is the difference between, I know we have seen some of our advertising revenues that we collect from brands, there has been an increase in the number of days outstanding. But that should be correct in the next quarter.

items.statement: Cash balance Rs 6,700 crore; food delivery and dine-out profitable and accreting to treasury
items.quote: Currently we have a very strong balance sheet. As you see, Rs. 6,700 crores and the food delivery business and the dine-out business also turning profitable which continue to accrue to the treasury balance.

items.statement: Non-grocery share rising in Instamart, improving margin mix; Maxxsaver and Megapods drive higher AOV
items.quote: As the share of overall non-grocery increases, you should expect that there will be higher margin that currently the other categories operate on.

items.statement: New user cohorts show healthy retention; mature cohorts retain without incentives
items.quote: Whenever a cohort becomes mature, they do not actually need any kind of incentive for them to be operating on our platform, okay. And that we have seen consistently. The retention rate, the repeat rate keeps on going up without any incentive at all, okay.

items.statement: Open to becoming IOCC (inventory-led) in future when domestic ownership rises; no near-term plan
items.quote: At some point in the future when we believe that is the right time, we may also want to consider it. But there is no plan in the near future, as I said, commercials also do not have a screaming reason for us to do it.

items.statement: Macro volatile with geopolitical changes; food delivery growth at lower end of guidance range
items.quote: The macro is too volatile for us to talk about or get a clear read on the impact, since there are multiple moving parts including recent geopolitical changes which are happening, right.

items.statement: Instamart NOV/GOV gap narrowed from 85% to 76% in two quarters due to mix and incentives
items.quote: Overall NOV is not just a factor of also our expanding selection, right? So as the share of overall non-grocery increases, you should expect that there will be higher margin that currently the other categories operate on.

items.statement: Food delivery leadership team stable with significant vintage; teams operating well across cities
items.quote: Most of our leadership is now significant vintage, right, in the food delivery space, understand the category well. So there are some fundamental basics which are operating for us, right.

items.statement: Management reaffirmed three-year EBITDA target of Rs 1,800-2,200 crore by FY28 and said they remain on track; no specific FY26 revenue or EBITDA guidance given
items.quote: we remain on track to deliver that three-year numbers. Of course, not all of it is back ended. I think we have also given clarity on initiatives that will lead us to that range

items.statement: FY25 capex was Rs 1,372 crore; FY26 capex expected at Rs 950-1,000 crore, bulk for Zone-4 completion
items.quote: Based on our current plan, we expect the capex in FY26 to be about 950-1000 crs.

items.statement: Zone-4 projects commissioning staggered through FY26; multipurpose and calcium chloride plants expected to start in Q3 FY26; volume contribution from Zone-4 mainly from FY27
items.quote: Zone-4 staggered commissioning will happen throughout let's say Q3, Q4 of this financial. Especially the multipurpose plant, the calcium chloride plant is expected to start up in Q3.

items.statement: Volume growth 17% YoY in FY25; Q4 volumes up 14% QoQ (non-energy) and 21% QoQ (energy); demand stabilizing across end-user industries
items.quote: If you look at year-on-year numbers, FY '24 versus FY '25, we are roughly at around 17% growth at overall portfolio level.

items.statement: EBITDA grew 3% YoY to Rs 1,016 crore in FY25; Q4 EBITDA up 13% QoQ to Rs 266 crore; margin recovery dependent on China overcapacity correction and tariff outcomes
items.quote: EBIDTA grew by about 3% to Rs 1,016 crs on consolidated basis.

items.statement: Agrochemical pricing weak due to China overcapacity; MMA pricing linked to aniline and gasoline-naphtha spreads; tariff impact mixed across product portfolio
items.quote: given the amount of over capacity that exists in China, that incr emental volume growth is also served by marginal pricing, and that's where we are not seeing uptick on pricing/margins at this

items.statement: Energy applications volumes up 21% QoQ; base business (Nitro Toluene, NCB, Ethylation) showing volume recovery; DCB chain weak due to polymer/auto demand pressure
items.quote: Volumes for Energy applications grew 21% Q-o-Q driven by our strategy to diversify and widen the customer base and geographical spread.

items.statement: MMA customer base diversifying beyond Middle East to US, Europe and India; some customers in holding pattern due to tariff uncertainty but returning in recent weeks
items.quote: Now we are seeing increasing supplies going to the US, some of the supplies going into Europe, as well as the Indian volume is also looking up.

items.statement: Gross working capital days expected at 70-80 days in FY26; payables increased due to higher aniline imports on longer credit; net debt expected to reduce by Rs 200-300 crore in FY26
items.quote: So it should be somewhere between 70 to 80 days on a gross basis. We will have to work out some numbers, but yes, it should be that way.

items.statement: Net debt ~Rs 3,500 crore at FY25 end; expected to reduce by Rs 200-300 crore in FY26 as capex intensity declines and working capital unlocks cash
items.quote: directionally, I expect the number to be lower by maybe Rs. 200-300 crore kind of range.

items.statement: US tariff impact mixed: some products (e.g., MPD) benefit as non-exempt and competing with China; some exempt products see India sourcing interest; MMA faces negative impact as tariffs add cost
items.quote: the overall US tariff impact in terms of AIL is a bit mixed, right. Because it is complex, we have a wide variety of product portfolio, and differen t products have different

items.statement: Signed two renewable PPAs (solar and hybrid) with Cleanmax and Prozeal; one to start delivering within CY2025, second by end FY26 or early FY27; will lower operational costs
items.quote: one of the contracts to start delivering within this calendar year, and the second one is expected to begin by end FY26 or early FY27. Upon commencement, this will lower operational costs

items.statement: MMA capacity utilization ramp-up targeted over next two years; current capacity to be absorbed in 2-year timeframe via market development
items.quote: over the course of the next two years we are targeting to utilize that capacity and that's where I think we will remain focused.

items.statement: Board recommended final dividend of Rs 1 per share (20% of face value Rs 5) for FY25
items.quote: the Board has recommended a final dividend of Rs. 1 per share (20% of face value of Rs. 5/- each) for FY25.

items.statement: Tariff second/third order effects uncertain; China dumping risk for agro intermediates; gasoline-naphtha spread forecasting difficult; customer decision delays due to uncertainty
items.quote: the second and third order level of impact is yet to become visible and our sense is it will take a few months to play out.

items.statement: Long-term contracts performing well: 20-year nitric acid agreements on track; polymer application with global major running well; advanced specialty polymer intermediate ramping up
items.quote: I think the 20-year purchase agreements that we have for nitric acid continues to perform exactly as per contract, no issues on that front.

items.statement: New MMA competition emerging in China (Jiangsu New Materials 4 lakh ton planned); Aarti has head start in supply chain and freight advantages for bulk shipments
items.quote: I think competition will come, right. I think people do track us closely, and in that context it is expected that competition will come up as and when we scale up certain products.

items.statement: No management changes or key hires mentioned in transcript
items.quote: Today, we are joined by senior members of the management team, including Mr. Suyog Kotecha – Executive Director and Chief Executive Officer; and Mr. Chetan Gandhi – Chief Financial Officer.

items.statement: ARPOB growth projected to be inflation-linked; Thane and Pune mature, Indore may have one more year of case-mix optimization above inflation
items.quote: As I was saying that the projection for ARPOB growth should be inflation-linked. Thane and Pune, both are mature d hospitals. So besides inflation, there is no other lever for ARPOB growth. Indore may be slightly higher than inflation because for maybe one more year, it has a second lever that is of case mix optimization that is more tertiary work

items.statement: Volume in Thane expected stable; Pune and Indore could see volume growth
items.quote: The volume in Thane should be stable. In Pune and Indore, we could expect some growth in volumes.

items.statement: New Pune hospital 500 beds, capex ~INR500 crores excluding land; land on 10-year lease with purchase option after year 3
items.quote: So the new Pune hospital is supposed to be 500 beds in size. We think that the capex incurred for that project should be somewhere in the tune of INR500 crores excluding land.

items.statement: Dombivli hospital construction on track, expected commissioning Q1 FY27; Pune hospital at excavation stage, construction to begin post-monsoon
items.quote: The Dombivli Hospital construction is progressing as per plan with an expected commissioning within a year in Q1 of FY '27. The new Pune hospital is at the excavation stage after receiv ing all the environmental clearances. The construction is expected to begin post monsoon

items.statement: Indore expansion added 78 beds commissioned 1 Jan 2025; 11-bed ICU ready but will be operationalized based on occupancy demand
items.quote: We executed a substantial expansion project, adding 2 additional floors to the existing hospital building, resulting in 78 new beds. These beds were commissioned on 1st January 2025. Furthermore, we have constructed an 11-bed ICU, which is now ready for commissioning, but will be operationalized based on occupancy demand.

items.statement: Thane expansion: received UDCPR approval for potential additional floor; environmental clearances pending; interim reconfiguration added 2 OTs, second MRI, second cath lab, expanded Daycare/chemo from 14 to 22 beds, new OPD cluster
items.quote: We have received approval from the Municipal Corporation to develop the building in accordance with the new UDCPR regulations. This could potentially entitle us to increase FSI, allowing us to add an additional floor to the Thane Hospital. However, this is contingent upon obtaining environmental clearances and some other necessary statutory permissions.

items.statement: Mira Road land acquired, at post-purchase regulatory stage (7/12 updation); architectural drawings to start shortly
items.quote: In Mira Road, the land has been acquired, and we are at the post-purchase regulatory stage of 7/12 updation, etc., and we will start working on the architectural drawings for that project shortly.

items.statement: Dombivli Phase 1 ~250 beds (of 500 total) expected to inaugurate next financial year; Pune Phase 1 ~250 beds a couple of years later; both to ramp up over subsequent years
items.quote: next financial year, Dombivli should get inaugurated and that should add about 250 -odd beds to our capacity in P hase 1, which can be ramped up over the next couple of years as the capacity expands and then Pune a couple of years after that

items.statement: Thane occupancy at 72% (mid-70s considered peak due to midnight measurement); limited scope for further occupancy increase
items.quote: Thane hospital occupancies are 72% currently. Anything in mid-70% is, in our view, peak occupancy because we measure it at midnight. So there isn't too much scope to increase occupancy in Thane at current levels.

items.statement: Thane population ~3 million and growing; new competitor hospitals will be able to build teams but demand sufficient for all
items.quote: The supply of doctors in Thane is also extremely high as is the population of Thane, which is extremely high and growing at 3 million people. So I don't think that even if there is zero attrition from our side, the new hospitals will struggle in building teams. They will be able to build teams also. And with the population, I think on the demand side, there should not be challenge for any of the 3

items.statement: Thane additional floor expected to contribute incrementally to EBITDA margins as fixed costs already covered
items.quote: Yes, ideally, if and when this floor does come up, we definitely think that it should contribute on a unit level a little more to the EBITDA margins because most of the fixed costs are taken care of and the added capacity in terms of manpower, power, etc., does not need as much fixed cost now.

items.statement: FY25 occupancy split: Thane 72.1%, Pune 65.5%, Indore 54.9%; Q4 FY25 occupancy: Thane 71.1%, Pune 61.1%, Indore 42.1% (dilution from 78 new beds)
items.quote: So this is for the whole year, Thane 72.1%, Pune 65.5% and Indore 54.9%. And for the quarter, we have Thane 71.1%, Pune 61.1% and Indore 42.1%.

items.statement: FY25 payer mix: insurance 55.8%, self-pay 42.9%, government schemes 1.3%
items.quote: The payer mix split, insurance stood at 55.8%, self-payers 42.9% and government schemes at 1.3%.

items.statement: Zero senior doctor attrition at Thane; strong sticky teams across locations; new hospitals will also find doctors given supply and population
items.quote: So far, not a single one of our senior doctors has moved out and stopped association with us. So we continue to report 0 attrition at the senior consultant level. Going forward also, I don't perceive that to be a major risk factor.

items.statement: Competitors entering Thane (IT services, Max hospital); management sees no doctor attrition risk and sufficient demand for all
items.quote: With new hospitals coming in, the supply of doctors in Thane is also extremely high as is the population of Thane, which is extremely high and growing at 3 million people. So I don't think that even if there is zero attrition from our side, the new hospitals will struggle in building teams.

items.statement: Thane additional floor contingent on environmental clearances; state environmental committee currently not very active
items.quote: Currently, the environmental committee for the state and for this region is not very active. So once those committees start getting active and Thane starts coming back on the fold of the permission stage, we will move the applications.

items.statement: Open to acquisitions in Western India if quality and value justifiable; no target multiple; greenfield remains first choice
items.quote: If a good opportunity at a good value does present itself, we are not averse to it, but we will insist that the quality of asset and the value at which we are able to acquire it seems justifiable in our mind. If that does happen, we will look at an acquisition.

items.statement: No plan to expand beyond Western India; full-service flagship hub model only; no OPD-only satellite model
items.quote: currently, there is absolute clarity that we will not go beyond western part of India for now. And on the acquisition side, again, it is just to complete the whole story that greenfield remains the first choice. But if there is a sensible acquisition oppor tunity, we are not averse to it

items.statement: Cash position ~INR600 crores (INR325 crores new debt + INR275 crores existing reserves); surplus internal accruals available for future expansion
items.quote: As you see on our balance sheet today, our cash position stands at about INR600 crores, comprising of INR325 crores from the new debt and INR275 crores from our existing cash reserves.

items.statement: FY26 double-digit revenue growth and EBITDA margin 25%+ expected
items.quote: on our current modelling, we will continue to have, based on what we have guided, sales double-digit growth and then EBITDA & RoCE 25% and above at this point of time

items.statement: FY26 ETR expected similar to FY25 level
items.quote: We expect the ETR for FY26 to be similar to the current fiscal level.

items.statement: FY26 capex expected in similar range as FY25
items.quote: We believe, at this point of time, it would be in the similar range for FY26 as well.

items.statement: NRT business full-year FY26 revenue around ₹2,400 crores
items.quote: Yes. Certainly, give or take, that would be the range.

items.statement: Q4 consolidated gross margin 55.6%, down 300 bps YoY and 312 bps QoQ
items.quote: The consolidated gross profit margin for Q4 was 55.6%, reflecting a YoY decline of 300 basis points and a sequential decline of 312 basis points.

items.statement: FY25 consolidated gross margin stable at 58.5%
items.quote: For the full fiscal year, the consolidated gross margin remained stable at 58.5%, consistent with FY24.

items.statement: Q4 EBITDA margin 29.1%, up 267 bps YoY and 160 bps QoQ
items.quote: EBITDA margin was 29.1%, an increase of 267 basis points YoY and 160 basis points sequentially.

items.statement: FY25 EBITDA margin 28.3%, down 143 bps YoY
items.quote: The annual EBITDA margin stood at 28.3%, down from 29.7% in FY24, reflecting a decrease of 143 basis points.

items.statement: NRT business EBITDA margin zone of 25%
items.quote: So, for this business, earlier we have also spoken, our EBITDA margin is in zone of 25%.

items.statement: US price erosion very low single-digit in FY25
items.quote: the price erosion that was in the US was relatively low, primarily, as most of the products, I believe, exhausted the potential of the price erosion. So , it's normally when there is no price erosion in United States, it's not always a goo d sign. But, in our case, it was a very low single -digit price erosion within the fiscal

items.statement: R&D: 249 global generic filings in FY25; 95 in Q4
items.quote: Additionally, we completed 95 global generic filings, bringing the total for the fiscal year to 249.

items.statement: Semaglutide launch targeted calendar 2026 in markets where IP allows
items.quote: So we are gearing up to launch it during the calendar '26, in all the markets that the IP landscape will allow us to launch.

items.statement: Abatacept Phase III ongoing; filing targeted end of CY2025
items.quote: We were planning to submit the product somewhere in the end of this calendar year, end of '25, to be ready to launch the intravenous (IV), immediately after patent expiration.

items.statement: Biosimilar partnerships: daratumumab (Henlius, US/EU), ustekinumab & golimumab (Bio-Thera, SE Asia), denosumab filing accepted by USFDA
items.quote: We secured exclusive commercialization rights for the daratumumab biosimilar candidate from Henlius, in the United States and Europe, reinforcing our oncology portfolio. We signed an agreement with Bio-Thera to commercialize ustekinumab and golimumab biosimilar candidates, with a primary focus on Southeast Asian markets. The United States Food and Drug Administration (USFDA) also accepted the fili

items.statement: NRT integration: UK completed, Nordics next phase
items.quote: The United Kingdom was successfully integrated at the start of this month and we are on track to complete the integration of the Nordics in the next phase.

items.statement: New India partnerships: Sanofi for Beyfortus (nirsevimab), ALK-Abello for Sensimune, Jan Aushadi participation
items.quote: We expanded our collaboration with Sanofi to introduce BeyfortusTM (nirsevimab), a novel drug for preventing respiratory syncytial virus (RSV). In partnership with ALK-Abelló, we launched Sensimune TM, an immunotherapy product for house dust mite-induced allergies. We commenced participation in the Government of India's Jan Aushadi program with one of our products.

items.statement: CTO-2 API facility received VAI status from USFDA after Nov 2024 inspection
items.quote: On the regulatory front, our API manufacturing facility, CTO-2, located in Bollaram, Hyderabad, received a Voluntary Action Indicated (VAI) status from the USFDA, following a successful GMP inspection conducted in November 2024.

items.statement: US unannounced inspections ongoing; facilities ready
items.quote: Just this year, the inspection that we had in CTO-3 and CTO-6 were unannounced inspections. Our facilities are ready for it. This was always the guidelines in the United States for years that it's unannounced.

items.statement: FX hedges: USD 786M hedged at min ₹85.90/USD; RUB 2,500M hedged at min ₹0.91/RUB
items.quote: An amount of USD 786 million has been hedged using structured derivative contracts maturing over the course of the next financial year. These contracts provide a minimum protection rate of ₹85.90 per US dollar, while retaining the potential for upside participation in the event of US dollar appreciation. An amount of RUB 2,500 million has been hedged with a minimum protection rate of ₹0.91 per Rus

items.statement: Operating working capital ₹12,590 crores, down ₹192 crores QoQ on improved receivables
items.quote: Operating working capital as of March 31, 2025, stood at ₹12,590 crores, a reduction of ₹192 crores compared to December 31, 2024, primarily driven by improved receivables management.

items.statement: Net cash surplus ₹2,454 crores ($287M) post NRT acquisition payout
items.quote: As of year-end, the company maintained a net surplus cash position of ₹2,454 crores (i.e., $287 million) post NRT acquisition pay-out in September.

items.statement: Dividend recommended ₹8 per share (800% of face value) for FY25
items.quote: Based on the company's performance, the Board has recommended payment of a dividend of ₹8 per equity share of face value ₹1/- each, equivalent to 800% of face value, for the year ended March 31, 2025, subject to approval of the members of the company.

items.statement: Tariff uncertainty on generics; preparing for supply sustainability; no US manufacturing footprint planned
items.quote: First, obviously, I wish I knew when and how much tariff will come. We are preparing ourselves for the scenarios, and we are, obviously, watching carefully the information as it will come. At this stage, the main effort is to ensure sustainability of supply. So the main acti vity, as we speak, is to work closely with our customers and see what is the need , in terms of future inventories as well a

items.statement: Net debt expected around Rs.3,000 crore in FY26 with debt-to-EBITDA below 2x
items.quote: As of now, we expect it to be in the vicinity of Rs. 3,000 crores. But in terms of net debt-to-EBITDA, it definitely should be below two for this financial year.

items.statement: Debt-to-EBITDA not expected to exceed much beyond 2x over next two years
items.quote: The next two years, I do not see my debt-to-EBITDA exceeding much beyond two.

items.statement: Industry volume growth expected 6-8% in FY26; Birla Corp aims to be in line or better
items.quote: This year industry is expected to grow maybe between 6% and 8%. We should be in line with industry if not better.

items.statement: Total expansion CAPEX of Rs.4,759 crore for 6.2 mtpa including Kundanganj Line-III
items.quote: Rs.4,759 crores is the number including Kundanganj Line-III.

items.statement: Capacity to reach 27.6 mtpa by FY29; 25 mtpa by Q3 FY28 with Maihar Line-II, Prayagraj, Gaya Phase-I
items.quote: As you rightly mentioned, our capacity will go to 27.6 million tons by FY29, but if you see maybe by December Q3 FY28 we should be reaching the Maihar Line-II and two grinding setups at Prayagr aj and Gaya Phase-I, which will add on our capacity to roughly 25 million tonnes

items.statement: Kundanganj Line-III (1.4 mtpa) expected Q2 FY26; Maihar Line-II, Gaya Phase-I, Prayagraj by CY27
items.quote: By calendar year '27 we are expecting Ma ihar Line-II, Phase-I of Gaya, Prayagraj and of course Kundanganj Line-III is expected in the second quarter of this financial year

items.statement: Clinker capacity currently 13 mtpa; additional 3.7 mtpa planned via Maihar Line-II
items.quote: So total clinker capacity is around 13 million ton s as of today and plan for another 3.7 million tons . That is the main Maihar Line-II

items.statement: Mukutban operating at ~80% utilization; targeting 85% next year
items.quote: We have been operating close to 80% capacity utilization, next year it will be 85%.

items.statement: Q4 realization up ~7% QoQ driven by North and East price increases; no one-off incentives
items.quote: If you look at in the Quarter 4 across the country mostly the price in the North region gone up and the east also gone up, but our volume a lso if you look at the western region has gone up . So that has resulted into increase of our realization of almost 7% in the Quarter 4

items.statement: Management refuses to extrapolate Q4 EBITDA/ton; realization not linear across quarters
items.quote: We are not going to hazard any guess in terms of our EBITDA, how it is going to move forward and it will be I think misleading, or it could be erroneous to extrapolate the EBITDA and the subsequent quarter basis what has happened in Q4?

items.statement: Bikram coal mine start Q3 FY26; meaningful production FY27; Marki Barka mine start FY28
items.quote: In terms of coal mines, Bikram coal mine, in Q3 of this year we are expecting to start that coal mine, but meaningful production will start from next financial year only. As regards the other coal mine, which is Marki Barka, that we expect to start only in FY28.

items.statement: No absolute virtue in captive coal mining; will optimize fuel mix based on cost economics
items.quote: There is no salvation in just saying what is the self-sufficiency. Coal mine captive versus purchase will all depend always on the cost equations. Sometimes you may actually decide to mine less if your cost of mining is more than your purchase of coal.

items.statement: Q1 FY26 realization similar to Q4 average; no major variation
items.quote: Ongoing almost remains same. There is no much variation.

items.statement: No veracity to reports of mining ban near Chittorgarh Fort; case progressing per Supreme Court process
items.quote: We have no such information on this. That statement was made, but we have not found any veracity and we will be surprised if such position is taken because this is contrary to anything which has been stated in the past and the case has been progressing in a particular manner.

items.statement: Rs.346 crore working capital inflow in Q4 from other financial assets linked to incentives
items.quote: We got some incentive. That probably would answer your questions about the change in current assets.

items.statement: Rs.100 crore intercorporate deposit given to another company at arm's length; name not disclosed
items.quote: Rs.100 crores is an intercorporate deposit we have given to another company at arm's length basis.

items.statement: No immediate plans to sell non-strategic equity investments; sufficient internal accruals for CAPEX
items.quote: Those are not strategic investment for us, but currently we do not have any plans, we feel that we have got enough internal accruals to cater to CAPEX requirement, so as of now, we do not have any immediate plans to sell those investments.

items.statement: RMC business strategy being finalized; beginning in UP; clearer picture by next quarter
items.quote: We are still firming up our strategy. We have made a beginning in UP. We are finalizing our strategy. Hopefully by next quarter we should be able to give you a clearer picture on this.

items.statement: Jute business management revamp done; integrated into main operations for E-team focus
items.quote: We have had a revamp in the management structure of the jute business. We are approaching it in a much more integrated manner, not treating it at an arm's length as a different business which is handled differently, we are increasingly integrating it into our main operations so that it gets that kind of management focus from our E-team and the central management.

items.statement: Management avoids industry predictions; focuses on own execution and stakeholder commitments
items.quote: We are not that large to influence industry trends or basically make those predictions. We have a clear strategy and we try to stay to that and stay close to our promises to our stakeholders as well as our investors without getting carried away by what is happening around us.

items.statement: Total incentives accrued Rs.103 crore in FY25; Rs.41 crore in Q4 FY25
items.quote: For example, the total incentives that we have accrued in this year is Rs.103 crores, of which in this current quarter Q4 we have accrued Rs.41

items.statement: Standalone EBITDA margin expected to rise 3-4% from Q4 FY25's 23.5% as prices move toward reference price of INR135/mm/sqm
items.quote: In the last quarter, we earned 23.5%, where the price was INR127.6 and we are increasing the price to the level of reference price, which is INR135 or so. So obviously, we are going to have some incremental EBITDA coming in, in the financial year. So, somebody had asked in the call earlier, whether 3% to 4% increase can be expected. So, we said yes.

items.statement: Consolidated EBITDA expected significantly positive in FY26 with Indian operations rising to INR90+ cr/quarter offsetting German losses of ~INR27 cr/quarter
items.quote: No, we will be having significant EBITDA positive because the EBITDA from Indian operations has been about, say, INR77 crores in the quarter 4, which is expected to rise to at least INR90-plus crores. And then we have about, say, INR27 crores losses per quarter. So obviously, we are leaving almost INR63 crores per quarter as the EBITDA positive.

items.statement: Expansion capacity revised upward from 500 TPD to 600 TPD, project cost to be finalized next month, targeting commissioning in Q3 FY27 (Oct-Dec 2026)
items.quote: We have received many offers, and we are hard at work, trying to finalize which offer to take, from whom and so on. So in my speech, I have said we expect the production to be seen/visible in the third quarter of the next financial year. And that is just simply how long it takes.

items.statement: Board approved enabling resolution to raise up to INR500 cr via equity or convertible instruments for future opportunities
items.quote: The Board has also approved further raising of funds through the issuance of instruments of security, including equity shares or any other security convertible into equity shares, including warrants in one or more tranches for an amount not exceeding INR500 crores, in accordance with the regulations and subject to necessary approvals, including the approval of the members of the company and such o

items.statement: Domestic solar glass capacity currently 2,300 TPD (~15 GW); another 15 GW including 12 GW captive by new producer commissioning by end CY2025
items.quote: The present solar glass capacity in the country is 2,300 tons per day, which is about 15 gigawatts. Another 15 gigawatts of capacity, including 12 gigawatts for captive by a new producer is getting commissioned by the end of calendar year 2025.

items.statement: Borosil standalone net glass capacity 6.5 GW at ~95% utilization; gross furnace capacity 1,000 TPD
items.quote: So just to simply tell you, we have 1,000 ton capacity per day. So the gross production what we can do in the year is 365,000 tons. And broadly 75% is -- 70% to 75% is what you can expect to take and supply. So that works out to 6.5 gigawatt.

items.statement: Domestic solar installations hit record 25 GW in FY25 (module consumption ~35 GW) vs 15 GW prior year; expect 40-45 GW annually going forward
items.quote: The country has seen its highest ever solar installations at 25 gigawatts, which means modules consumption of about 35 gigawatts in the year just completed as against 15 gigawatts during the previous year. We expect the installations to rise to 40 to 45 gigawatts annually going forward.

items.statement: Demand-supply gap persists: domestic supply 15 GW vs 35 GW demand (55-60% imports); even after 15 GW new capacity, supply 30 GW vs 50+ GW demand
items.quote: The demand currently is about 35 gigawatts and the supply from India is about 15 gigawatts, which leaves a gap of 20 gigawatts, which is coming by way of imports. And as we foresee the demand to grow to about 40 gigawatts to 45 gigawatts going forward in terms of installations, the module or the glass demand will be north of 50 gigawatts. So, there is a huge surge in demand, which is expected and

items.statement: Blended margins for FY26 expected 300-400 bps higher than Q4 FY25 on better realizations
items.quote: So given our exit realization and where the major imports are from -- and our average realization -- is it safe to assume that the blended margins for roll up next year can be 300 to 400 bps higher than Q4? Ashok Jain: Yes, we can assume that safely.

items.statement: Domestic selling prices now close to reference price of INR135-140/mm/sqm (landed value at port); Q4 FY25 avg INR127.6/mm/sqm
items.quote: The company's domestic selling prices are now close to the level of the reference prices, landed value at port of discharge of around INR135 to INR140 per millimeter per square meter.

items.statement: Realization vs China antidumping duty ~7-8% lower; vs Vietnam much higher; Malaysia imports rising but priced between China/Vietnam and don't offer 3.2mm glass
items.quote: But even to compare it only against China, which is at the highest amount of duty, then from that perspective, it was about, say, 7%, 8% lower. Mohit Kumar: But then we have Vietnam? Ashok Jain: Vietnam -- but Vietnam has a lower duty. So as compared to Vietnam, we were much higher. And Malaysia has no antidumping duty. So even compared to that also, we were very high. But we are moving towards th

items.statement: Definitive antidumping duty imposed 9 May 2025 on solar glass from China/Vietnam valid till 3 Dec 2029 (5 years from preliminary notification)
items.quote: I'm happy to announce that the Ministry of Finance has on Friday, 9th May announced a definitive antidumping duty on all imports of solar glass originating in or exported from China and Vietnam, which shall remain valid till 3rd December 2029 for a period of 5 years from the date of issue of the preliminary duty notification.

items.statement: CVD on Vietnam also notified; ALMM mechanism from April 2024 driving local module usage and glass demand
items.quote: Use of locally produced modules has risen sharply after the implementation of ALMM mechanism from April 2024, which is leading to an increased demand for the -- all the com ponents, including solar glass

items.statement: Export sales dropped sharply to INR91.73 cr (8.3% of turnover) in FY25 from INR199.78 cr due to weak EU demand from Chinese module dumping; Turkey also weak
items.quote: Export sales during financial year '25 at INR91.73 crores, comprising 8.3% of the turnover, has actually dropped sharply from the previous year's INR199.78 crores, led by a significant decline in the demand in European markets as a result of dumping of modules from China at artificially low prices.

items.statement: New German government announced strong support for domestic solar manufacturing; EU mandate requires 40% of 65 GW installations from EU sources; Borosil only EU solar glass maker
items.quote: Last year, the total installation of solar photovoltaic in the European Union was 65 gigawatts. Now according to the European Union Parliament, there is a law that mandates 40% of this must come from European sources. Our c ompany is the only company manufacturing solar glass in the entire European Union. So , we expect a surge of demand

items.statement: December stock cleared; no inventory overhang currently
items.quote: And the stock is not a problem. In December itself, we had cleared all the stocks. So we are not carrying stocks any longer. And even the industry players have been able to clear their stocks to a great extent. So that's not a problem any longer.

items.statement: INR204.42 cr raised via preferential issue (INR100 cr promoters, INR104.42 cr warrants 25%); INR185 cr used to repay GMB step-down subsidiary loan
items.quote: A total sum of INR204.42 crores was received towards the issue, comprising INR100 crores from promoters against shares and INR104.42 crores towards 25% amount against warrants. INR185 crores from this amount has been utilized to repay the loan liability of our step-down subsidiary, GMB.

items.statement: Balance preferential issue funds for expansion; remaining warrant conversion (75%) plus mix of equity, debt, internal accruals to fund revised capex
items.quote: The balance is available for utilization against expansion project. We are re-evaluating the size of expansion projects as against the earlier plan of 500 tons per day. We expect project cost to be finalized by next month with the target to commission the new facility during third quarter of 2026, '27. The balance payments against warrants for conversion into equity shares will be used for this pr

items.statement: Gas contracts mix of Henry Hub (US) and oil-linked; oil price drop gives marginal benefit; no spot gas; Henry Hub prices unchanged
items.quote: But we have a basket of contracts, which are partially into Henry Hub, which is U.S.-based gas and partly oil gas. So when the oil prices have gone down, there is some benefit in the gas prices, which will accrue to us, but Henry Hub prices have not gone down. So there is a mix which we have used in order to reduce the volatility in our gas contracts. But yes, some benefits will accrue because the

items.statement: Domestic demand shifting to 2+2mm bifacial glass (60-70% of demand); consumes ~25kg/module vs 20.5kg for 3.2mm; net ~10% higher glass consumption per GW
items.quote: Now almost 60%, 70% of the demand is converted to 2 plus 2. And when you say the demand, it is now split in the mix right now by 2:1 or like that. But when you do it 2 plus 2, then the gigawatt will be slightly lower. Because you consume almost 25 kg glass in 1 module in bifacial, 2 plus 2 as against 20.5 kg in a 3.2 module. So to that extent, the glass consumption goes up. And -- but at the same

items.statement: Captive 16.5 MW solar-wind hybrid plant expected commissioning Q2 FY26 to supply 65-70% of electricity demand
items.quote: We shall also see the benefits of an additional 16.5 megawatt solar plus wind hybrid power plant, which is expected to be commissioned during second quarter financial year '26. This will not only save costs for us, but will also enable us to meet a significantly higher portion, which is 65% to 70% of our demand for electricity from captive sources of renewable energy.

items.statement: Tariff war impact uncertain; waiting 90 days to assess effect on business
items.quote: While it is difficult to assess the full impact of the ongoing tariff war, the initial indications suggest rise in demand from the However, we have to wait for the 90 days period to be over before understanding the likely impact it will have on our business.

items.statement: German subsidiary has fixed overheads (oxygen/gas plants, admin) creating dead cost; cold-end restart may cut EBITDA losses 50% but not to zero
items.quote: So, this cold end operation thing we'll observe for 2, 3 months, and then we'll see how to take it forward. But it is difficult to bring it down to 0. As you may see, there are overheads which are fixed cost, like say, oxygen plant cost or gas plant cost or e mployees cost, administrative expenses and all the things. So, there is a certain dead cost or stand still cost, which still remains despite

items.statement: Furnace maintenance due in 5-6 years; ready with spares/refractories; would take 45-60 days glass-to-glass if needed
items.quote: We are prepared for the furnace to -- we are prepared to repair the furnace as and when it becomes necessary. So there is a certain time line after 5, 6 years that we prepare all the equipment, all the necessary spare parts, etcetera, refractories and so on. And we are absolutely ready for the furnace to be repaired on the day that we feel it becomes necessary. As of now, the furnaces are producin

items.statement: Domestic welding market volumes were flat in FY25; international business grew over 25%
items.quote: The domestic market has been at the end of the year fairly flat on that account. The export market has obviously had a little volume growth.

items.statement: Overall revenue growth approximately 5% for FY25
items.quote: Revenue growth is approximately 5% for last year.

items.statement: Services order book built to 70-80% of Rs 50-60 crore breakeven level
items.quote: And we started building up our order book to anywhere around 70%, 80% of that level already.

items.statement: Services segment EBIT margin improved from -24% to -19% in FY25; target breakeven post H1 FY26
items.quote: EBIT margins on the services business, which was at about 24% in FY'24 has actually improved to a, still a negative, but has improved to a 19%.

items.statement: Operating margin bare minimum 10%; must be better than that
items.quote: It's a bare minimum as far as I am concerned is 10%. It has to be little bit better than that and there will be no how to make it better than that.

items.statement: FY25 capex ~Rs 40 crore; FY26 capex expected within 15-20% of that level
items.quote: I think we will be within the region of that up down minus 15%, 20% as far as it goes. It should be about 15%-20% up down from that because there are still upgradations that we have to do looking at the long term plans.

items.statement: Flux cored wire line stabilized in FY25; further investments planned in flux cored and stainless steel products
items.quote: We continue to make more investments in the flux cored wire space, where we stabilized a new line last year and we expect to make more investments over there as well. Similarly, in stainless steel products, where we see a lot of potential.

items.statement: Focus on richer product basket: high-end consumables (nickel, stainless), EV welders, solar-powered version in development
items.quote: We remain focused on improving our product mix, a basket with richer products. And that is where high-end welding consumables, whether they are related to nickels and other stainless steels and stuff like that are coming into play.

items.statement: Building larger framework of key customers in India welding business; strengthening distribution network geographically
items.quote: The one big change we talked of in previous meetings that I still would like to push on is as an organization, especially in the India welding business, we need to add on a larger framework of key customers that we work with.

items.statement: Positioned as India's only Tier 1 non-MNC welding player; investing in talent and high-spec products to compete with MNCs
items.quote: As Ador, we view ourselves simply as India's tier 1 welding player and probably the only one that is not an MNC. So which means you do not have the external support that an MNC would on certain technologies or products and stuff like that.

items.statement: Target to double revenue over next 4 years by outperforming market growth
items.quote: We have got a mandate internally that we would like to be able to double our revenue over the next 4 years. And that means outperforming the market growth rate, of course.

items.statement: International revenue grew ~25% in FY25 (~Rs 122 cr base); FY26 growth expected more muted; core markets Middle East, expanding in US and Australia
items.quote: The international business continued to have robust growth at more than 25%.

items.statement: Export margins pretty much in line with India; entering US with lower-margin products initially to build volume and brand
items.quote: Pretty much in line and as long as the dollar doesn't shift down too much and remains where it does or moves up over CCI benefit, but pretty much in line with India.

items.statement: New management team more brutal about passing steel price changes faster; not worried about margin impact from steel price movements
items.quote: I think we are just going to be a lot more brutal about passing things on a lot faster and having the strength to do that and I think that is exactly where the management changes are coming and I am seeing that that they are doing it effectively.

items.statement: Operating working capital improved by approximately 18 days in FY25
items.quote: Efficient operation work capital has improved by approximately 18 days, and these numbers will be available to you.

items.statement: Company is pretty much debt-free
items.quote: In other highlights, we are pretty much debt-free.

items.statement: Merger integration ~98% complete; benefits to play out over next 6-18 months
items.quote: The merger has finally been completed in September, October last year. And most of the integration work, I would say, up to approximately a 98% level has been completed now.

items.statement: Key hires: Lajpat Yadav as CEO Indian Welding Business, Suryanarayan as Head Corporate Strategy; building performance culture
items.quote: Mr. Lajpat Yadav has joined us as CEO of the Indian Welding Business and Mr. Suryanarayan has joined us as Head of Corporate Strategy.

items.statement: ONGC Uran project ~80% complete on ground, ~70% revenue recognized; expect commissioning over next 3-4 months
items.quote: As far as UNGC order goes, I think on the ground, I would say we are close to about 80% of the project being done. As far as revenue goes, about 70% revenue down, 80% on the ground, 80%-85% going through this period of quick commissioning over the next 3-4 months.

items.statement: Services division needs Rs 50-60 crore annual revenue of smaller projects to breakeven; order book at 70-80% of that level
items.quote: We need to do approximately in the region of, I would say anywhere in the region of approximately Rs. 50, Rs. 60 crores of business of that type of work, non-large-scale projects to be able to breakeven and then show profitability from there.

items.statement: Focus on securing approvals in nuclear, thermal, defence sectors for upcoming capex spends
items.quote: This year, what is going to be very critical for us is ensuring that the approvals we have in place and adding them in the nuclear space, thermal space, and defence space, all the places we expect a reasonable amount of CAPEX stuff to happen.

items.statement: Will not take large EPC projects; limiting future flare projects to Rs 15-20 crore scope
items.quote: We will not take on such large projects at all. We will only take on projects where the design and scope is within a limited understanding of us. Most of our order book will be very limited to up to about Rs. 15, Rs. 20 crores.

items.statement: M&R division revenue drop: ~15% from product transfer to welding products, ~5-8% from soft demand in cement/steel segments
items.quote: About 15% or so will be on account of that. The balance will be on account of we have been a little soft in terms of our numbers this year, that is it.

items.statement: 3D printing business not feasible for long-term investment; dynamics changed too much
items.quote: I don't think it's feasible to invest long term in that business. And right now, I am not going to say anything more than that right now. I am just going to keep that with me. I don't think it's feasible. We have been through a lot

items.statement: FY25 capex primarily on new consumable lines (flux cored, import substitution) at Silvassa, Raipur; operational from Q4
items.quote: Rs. 40 crores of CAPEX primarily went in new consumables additions or new lines to be done like I said stabilizing a little bit of all that. I think most of it was on that account. Most of it is on the consumable lines plants.

items.statement: Sectors like railways, thermal, defence, general infra, heavy engineering on robust growth path
items.quote: We do believe sectors such as railways, thermal, defense, general infra, heavy engineering to remain on a fairly robust growth path going forward from here.

items.statement: Diesel engine welders doing well abroad (75% export); Indian market order potential more aggressive this year
items.quote: In fact, last year there was a standard change that had a small impact for the Indian market. But in fact, we sell 75% of those products go in the international market where it does not have an impact.

items.statement: Management does not provide forward-looking numbers for top line, profitability, or margins per IR policy
items.quote: Again, as per our IR policy, we are not giving or sharing any forward-looking numbers, whether for the quarter or for the year, whether in terms of the top line, profitability margin or profitability.

items.statement: Summer 2025 started with encouraging momentum but post-March weather turned mild and erratic, muting performance so far
items.quote: Summer of '25 commence with quite encouraging momentum. So in South India and India, summer set in well in time, and we witnessed robust demand in the initial phase. However, post 31st March, as all summer-related industries are witnessing, and we are no exception, we are facing mild and erratic weather.

items.statement: Consolidated EBITDA margin expanded over 500 bps to 20.05% in FY25; standalone EBITDA margin expanded over 400 bps to 24.25%
items.quote: There has been decent expansion in EBITDA margin by more than 500 bps at a consol level and more than 400 bps at a standalone level.

items.statement: Channel inventory is slightly higher than last year at same time but season still has 7-11 weeks remaining in key regions
items.quote: This inventory that is there in the channel at this moment is slightly higher than what we had at the same time in the last year. That said, this is still too early in the day for the season to pan out.

items.statement: Adjacent categories (tower fans, kitchen cooling fans, water heaters) and LSV together now contribute decent double-digit percentage of standalone revenue, up from low single digits
items.quote: Adjacent category, LSV put together on a stand-alone basis itself, which was earlier in a small single-digit percentage is now decent double-digit percentage.

items.statement: Rural and semi-urban penetration driving growth; modern trade, D2C, and institutional sales expanding
items.quote: We have quite decent penetration, apart from general trade, through several other trade channels in semi-urban as well as rural market. And still, we see a huge potential to expand in modern trade across the subchannels with the large format stores, regional large format stores, also D2C, also institution sales etc.

items.statement: Exports at ₹117 crores (10% of standalone revenue); strong growth in Middle East, Africa, Europe; Sri Lanka recovered; Egypt and Sudan challenged by remittance issues
items.quote: domestic turnover is ₹1,065 crores and the export is ₹117 crores. Nrupesh Shah: So broadly, you can say that, 90% is domestic and 10% is export

items.statement: US market presents massive opportunity post-China tariffs; receiving serious inquiries from top US retailers but 8-week lead time limits immediate supply
items.quote: U.S. is a massive opportunity. And as Nrupesh bhai had mentioned in his presentation, we already have some serious inquiries from the large U.S. buyers, including the top retailers. They wanted us to supply a sizable quantity in this season, which would be starting pretty soon.

items.statement: IMPCO Mexico and Climate Technologies Australia put on block on April 12; investment banker appointed with milestones; process just begun
items.quote: On 12th of April, we decided and finalized to put IMPCO Mexico and Climate Technologies, Australia on block. So it's less than a month since we have decided. We have appointed the investment banker with a specific milestone. So, process has just begun.

items.statement: IMPCO Mexico to buy technology transfer and 9 IPRs from GSK China for ~₹43 crores; net ~₹40 crores to GSK for loan repayment to Symphony
items.quote: IMPCO Mexico is going to buy technology transfer as well as 9 IPRs from GSK China, which were specifically developed for IMPCO Mexico. And in new scenario, it has been found worthwhile to sell to IMPCO Mexico. The transaction value is about ₹43 crores. And considering GSK's strong financials and cash flow position, it won't need this amount. And hence, net of expenses close to ₹40 crores, which GS

items.statement: GSK China repaid ₹13.5 crores loan; outstanding loan to Symphony now ~₹49 crores; expected full repayment by end FY26
items.quote: It has repaid loan of ₹13.5 crores out of its profitability and internal accruals and hence current outstanding including interest accrued is about ₹49 crores.

items.statement: Board recommended final dividend of ₹8 per share (400% of face value); total FY25 payout ₹178 crores (84% of consolidated profit vs 60% guidance)
items.quote: The Board has recommended final dividend of ₹8, a face value of ₹2 that is 400%. In all, this amounts to total payout , during FY '25, ₹178 crores, which is 84% of the consolidated profit vis-a-vis our stated guidance of at least 60 % payout.

items.statement: Consolidated capital employed reduced to ₹248 crores from over ₹300 crores despite revenue growth; standalone capital employed negative ₹32 crores
items.quote: Total capital employed in the business based on monthly average capital deployed is ₹248 crores versus previous year in excess of ₹300 crores. So capital deployed is lower despite increase in top line and bottom line.

items.statement: Consolidated ROCE in core business 101%; Return on Net Worth up from 18% to 28%
items.quote: Translating into ROCE in core business 101% and return on net worth % is up from 18% to 28% at a consol level.

items.statement: Gross margin expansion driven by 17 new model launches, value engineering, and supply chain streamlining
items.quote: There has also been Y-o-Y gross margin expansion on account of, as guided earlier launch of 17 new models as well as value engineering and substantially streamline the supply chain in addition to operating leverage and economies of scale.

items.statement: Climate Technologies Australia impaired ₹50 crores on equity investment; Pathways write-off ~₹50 crores with ₹49 lakhs recovered; legal actions ongoing
items.quote: total equity investment as well as loan given to Climate Technologies Australia is substantial, out of which small part as recommended by auditors as per Ind-AS, as well as accounting standard amounting to about ₹50 crores to take as an impairment

items.statement: Production for new models began in January and February; advance placement of inventory in channels ahead of season
items.quote: when December quarter was muted, we had guided that we are sitting on decent amount of advances, especially for new models as their production was to begin starting for some models in January and some models in

items.statement: In US market, only Chinese players compete in air coolers; tariffs on China create significant opportunity for Symphony
items.quote: As far as air coolers are concerned, it is only Chinese companies which are in competition. And with them out of the race, I think we believe that we have a very good opportunity in the U.S. market.

items.statement: Employee cost as percentage of turnover within historical band; absolute cost not reduced but operating leverage improved
items.quote: No there is no reduction in absolute amount of employee cost. But obviously, the scale of operation and economies of scale have played the role because as you will appreciate whether the employee cost or any overhead not necessarily go up in line with the growth of sales and profitability.

items.statement: March quarter collections decent; unbilled advances contributed less than 25% of quarter sales

items.statement: BLDC technology already used in coolers and tower fans; evaluating BLDC fan category but no commitment yet

items.statement: No specific FY26 revenue or EBITDA guidance given; management expects volume-led growth but not significant margin recovery.
items.quote: We are not talking about specific yearly guidance, we mentioned that last time, right. We have set out a strategy for the three years and I think the only thing I can confirm is we remain on track to deliver that three-year numbers.

items.quote: I believe there will be a potential uptake of maybe around Rs. 100 crore to Rs.200 crore in next year, assuming the volumes continue to grow in the trajectory they are.

items.statement: Board recommended final dividend of Rs 1 per share (20% of face value Rs 5) for FY25.
items.quote: Considering the annual performance, the Board has recommended a final dividend of Rs. 1 per share (20% of face value of Rs. 5/- each) for FY25.

items.statement: FY25 revenue Rs 8,046 crore (+15% YoY), EBITDA Rs 1,016 crore (+3% YoY), PAT Rs 331 crore.
items.quote: We clocked in total revenue of Rs 8,046 crs posting a growth of about 15%, while EBIDTA grew by about 3% to Rs 1,016 crs on consolidated basis. items.statement: Q4 export revenue Rs 1,240 crore (55% of revenue vs ~48-50% prior); higher freight costs increased other expenses.
items.quote: The export number for the quarter was roughly Rs. 1,240 crore.

So the impact coming out from US tariffs, especially on the agrochemical sector, I think the second and third order level of impact is yet to become visible and our sense is it will take a few months to play out.

items.statement: FY26 EBITDA margin target 10-11% for Apollo Pipes standalone
items.quote: Apollo Pipes, like I said, is at around as you can see, it's around 8% EBITDA margin, right? Definitely, we will want to take it up to 10% to 11% in next 2 years.

items.statement: Kisan EBITDA margin target 5% in FY26 and 8-9% in 2-3 years
items.quote: We believe that in FY '26, these margins could inch up to around 5%. And in FY '27, there will be further improvement of 200, 250 bps. So as we see that in next 2, 3 years, the company has a capability to generate 8% to 9% EBITDA margins easily.

items.statement: Consolidated ROCE target 25% in next 2-3 years
items.quote: However, we are confident of achieving 25% ROCE in next 2 years as we increase our sales volume at 25% CAGR with margin improvement.

items.quote: So agri has done well so far, right? Last year, agri volume had double-digit growth for us. So far in Q1, we are seeing the same momentum.

items.quote: In FY '24, the contribution from this segment was around 12% to 15%. And this year, it fell below 5% in FY '25. So our volume kind of declined by almost 60%, 65%, right? And for FY '26, we have not factored in any substantial volume recovery in HDPE pipes for JJM.

items.quote: And the margins, which right now are at 8.5%, they will inch up to around 10% to 12%, right, in the next 2 to 3 years.

items.quote: EBITDA spreads like for Apollo Pipes should be INR1,000 per ton at least higher than what it was in FY '25.

items.quote: Even if macro doesn't do too good as we expect in second half, I don't think there will be a large miss to our guidance, right? items.statement: Adjusted EBITDA margin was 17.4% in Q1 FY2025, down 40 bps QoQ but up 296 bps YoY, after absorbing wage hikes.

items.quote: We expect some decisions to take place in Q2. Maybe in the worst case, some decisions might go into Q3. And then we have some deals which we are beginning now, which will naturally go into Q3.

items.statement: Revenue INR 442.5 crore ($51.1M), down 1.5% QoQ, up 6.2% YoY; adjusted EBITDA INR 76.8 crore, up 28.1% YoY; PAT INR 38.6 crore ($4.5M).

items.statement: Board declared interim dividend of INR 6 per share for FY2025.

items.statement: Gross margin 36.7% vs 37.9% QoQ and 33.7% YoY; SG&A decreased INR 4.7 crore due to lower AR provision, travel, and year-end true-up.

items.statement: Winning against larger competitors in platform engineering and AI deals; differentiated by operator mindset and domain focus in mid-market GCCs.

items.statement: Company remains debt-free with cash balance exceeding Rs. 750 crore

items.quote: So Disha, the cash balance that we carrying on the balance sheet, the board is cognizant of it. We have a great growth opportunity in front of us, both organically and inorganically.
