items.quote: I am happy to state, the company has delivered its highest ever revenues, both on a quarterly and a full year basis.

items.statement: MSWIL supplies to top 9 of top 10 selling four-wheeler models in India as of FY25
items.quote: I would like to highlight MSWIL is supplying to the Top 9 customers of the Top 10 selling vehicles four wheelers in India as of Financial Year '25.

items.statement: FY26 capex planned at approximately Rs 200 crores
items.quote: CAPEX is about Rs. 200 crores also, isn't it Mahender and Anurag? Anurag Gahlot: Yes, sir. It is approximately in this line

items.statement: Three new Greenfields expected to generate Rs 2,100 crores annualized revenue at full ramp-up
items.quote: the total sales from these three new Greenfields is Rs. 2,100 crores on an annualized basis. And once the volumes will pick up, which we are expecting in H2, when these three plants all volumes will picked up, and at that time this sales will get realized on the annual basis.

items.statement: Gross margin dip QoQ and YoY due to product mix variation and copper pass-through time lag
items.quote: So it's a combination of both. Obviously, product mix is one of the reasons where the margin varies on different products that we have, different wiring harness . Also, as far as copper is concerned, even though there is a pass-through arrangement with the customer, there is a time lag.

items.statement: Copper is pass-through with quarterly/half-yearly arrangements; no self-hedging; time lag of 3-6 months for pass-through
items.quote: We have pass through arrangements as we discussed earlier, whether it's quarterly or half yearly, so it's a pass through item for us.

items.statement: EV revenue share is 4% of total, purely high-voltage harnesses; Greenfields serve mix of EV and ICE models
items.quote: Out of the total revenue of the company, about 4% has come from the EV side. But these investments are in these new plants , in Greenfield and it's a mix of EV and ICE engine vehicles which are being produced by the car maker.

items.statement: 7,000-7,500 employees for three Greenfields being hired in staggered manner; one plant fully staffed, other two hiring aligned with Q1/Q2 ramp-up
items.quote: Right, sir . See, as you have seen that one plant has already ramped up , s o that manpower is fully there. The other two plants is falling on Q1 and Q2, and the some of the trials has already been started because in the phase when the mass production ramps up. So the partially yes , that manpower has been hired.

items.statement: High-voltage harness margins differ from low-voltage; localization efforts ongoing to improve margins; timeline not fixed at 2-3 years
items.quote: I think first of all, it is wrong to say that there will be no profitability into the high voltages harness also. And it is going to happen only after two to three years only. Yes, there are different margins into the different businesses.

items.statement: Company supports all powertrains (ICE, hybrid, EV, CNG) and follows customer plans without betting on technology winners
items.quote: We are supporting all the power trains . And for us it's very difficult which one will do how much. So we are working on all kinds of power trains and we support the customers, be it ICE, be it hybrid, EV, CNG, multiple options the customers are all working on with different possibilities.

items.statement: Greenfield delay compensation discussed mutually with customers; startup costs borne if delays occur
items.quote: Sir, this is a very, I mean, private discussion with the customers. And of course, if there are impacts, then always it's discussed mutually.

items.statement: ARPOB growth projected to be inflation-linked; Thane and Pune mature, Indore may have one more year of case-mix upside
items.quote: As I was saying that the projection for ARPOB growth should be inflation-linked. Thane and Pune, both are mature d hospitals. So besides inflation, there is no other lever for ARPOB growth. Indore may be slightly higher than inflation because for maybe one more year, it has a second lever that is of case mix optimization that is more tertiary work

items.statement: Volume growth expected stable at Thane, some growth at Pune and Indore
items.quote: The volume in Thane should be stable. In Pune and Indore, we could expect some growth in volumes.

items.statement: New Pune hospital 500 beds, capex ~INR500 cr excluding land; land on 10-year lease with purchase option after year 3
items.quote: So the new Pune hospital is supposed to be 500 beds in size. We think that the capex incurred for that project should be somewhere in the tune of INR500 crores excluding land.

items.statement: Dombivli hospital construction on track, commissioning expected Q1 FY27; Pune excavation stage, construction post-monsoon; Mira Road land acquired, regulatory stage
items.quote: The Dombivli Hospital construction is progressing as per plan with an expected commissioning within a year in Q1 of FY '27. The new Pune hospital is at the excavation stage after receiv ing all the environmental clearances. The construction is expected to begin post monsoon

items.statement: Indore expansion added 78 beds commissioned 1 Jan 2025; 11-bed ICU ready, to be operationalized based on demand
items.quote: We executed a substantial expansion project, adding 2 additional floors to the existing hospital building, resulting in 78 new beds. These beds were commissioned on 1st January 2025. Furthermore, we have constructed an 11-bed ICU, which is now ready for commissioning, but will be operationalized based on occupancy demand.

items.statement: Thane received UDCPR approval for potential additional floor; environmental and statutory clearances pending
items.quote: We have received approval from the Municipal Corporation to develop the building in accordance with the new UDCPR regulations. This could potentially entitle us to increase FSI, allowing us to add an additional floor to the Thane Hospital. However, this is contingent upon obtaining environmental clearances and some other necessary statutory permissions.

items.statement: Thane brownfield capex: decommissioned 22-bed economy ward, added 2 OTs, second MRI, second cath lab, expanded Daycare/chemo from 14 to 22 beds, new OPD cluster, overhauled engineering infrastructure
items.quote: We decommissioned our 22 -bed economy ward and strategically reconfigured certain areas to create 2 new operating theaters, a second MRI machine, a second cardiac cath lab, and expansion of our Daycare and chemo suites from 14 to 22 beds and a new OPD cluster. We have also undertaken a comprehensive overhaul of some of our ag eing engineering infrastructure, including chillers and cooling towers

items.statement: Dombivli Phase 1 ~250 beds, full 500 beds; Pune Phase 1 ~250 beds, full 500 beds; both to ramp up over next couple of years
items.quote: So both are 500 beds. Phase 1 will be around 250, and then we will ramp it up as per need.

items.statement: Thane occupancy at 72% considered peak; limited scope to increase further
items.quote: So Thane hospital occupancies are 72% currently. Anything in mid-70% is, in our view, peak occupancy because we measure it at midnight. So there isn't too much scope to increase occupancy in Thane at current levels.

items.statement: Additional Thane floor expected to improve unit-level EBITDA margins due to lower incremental fixed costs
items.quote: Yes, ideally, if and when this floor does come up, we definitely think that it should contribute on a unit level a little more to the EBITDA margins because most of the fixed costs are taken care of and the added capacity in terms of manpower, power, etc., does not need as much fixed cost now.

items.statement: Cash position ~INR600 cr (INR325 cr new debt + INR275 cr existing reserves) available for land purchase or strategic acquisition
items.quote: As you see on our balance sheet today, our cash position stands at about INR600 crores, comprising of INR325 crores from the new debt and INR275 crores from our existing cash reserves.

items.statement: Zero senior doctor attrition at Thane; strong sticky teams; new competitor hospitals not seen as major risk given high doctor supply and population growth
items.quote: Aashita, so yes, so far, not a single one of our senior doctors has moved out and stopped association with us. So we continue to report 0 attrition at the senior consultant level. Going forward also, I don't perceive that to be a major risk factor.

items.statement: FY25 occupancy by unit: Thane 72.1%, Pune 65.5%, Indore 54.9%
items.quote: The breakup is 72.1% occupancy for Thane, 65.5% occupancy for Pune and 54.9% occupancy for the Indore hospital.

items.statement: Thane additional floor contingent on environmental clearances and statutory permissions; state environmental committee currently not very active
items.quote: Currently, the environmental committee for the state and for this region is not very active. So once those committees start getting active and Thane starts coming back on the fold of the permission stage, we will move the applications.

items.statement: Indore Phase 2 (111 beds) will be considered only when occupancy reaches 60-65% (currently ~42-45%)
items.quote: See, like I just answered some time back, if you look at the occupancy for this quarter in Indore is 40%, 45%, right? Once this number reaches 60%, 65%, we will start thinking about expansion.

items.statement: Aim to achieve 14% EBITDA margin in FY26, up from 12.3% in FY25
items.quote: However, we are aiming to achieve 14% EBITDA margins in this coming financial year.

items.statement: Expect mid-teens revenue growth and to outperform two-wheeler industry in FY26
items.quote: I can only assure you that we will be growing in the mid-teens and we will outperform the market, outperform the industry again in this financial year because we have the confirmed orders to that extent.

items.statement: Wheel assembly exit to improve EBITDA margin by 80 bps in FY26; internal efficiencies to add 70 bps
items.quote: In my interview in the morning I said that we will be improving by 150 basis points, so that becomes 13.8%. And I said out of this 150 basis points, 80 basis points will come because the wheel assembly has gone, and 70 basis points will come for the internal more efficiencies and economies of scale.

items.statement: Wheel assembly customer shifted 60% business from Q4 FY25; FY26 revenue impact ~Rs 300 crore
items.quote: As mentioned in DRHP, our Wheel Assembly business has very low margin and we were requesting the customer for the last two years to shift this business to someone else. Now the customer has shifted 60% business from Q4 FY25. In FY26 it will impact our revenues by approximately Rs. 300 crore.

items.statement: Plan Rs 450 crore capex in FY26; Rs 150-200 crore for alloy wheel plant for Japanese collaboration
items.quote: Yes, this is entire. That's what we propose to do. As I said that we will be making additional capacities. And out of that the bigger amount of about Rs. 150 crore to Rs. 200 crore will be for this alloy wheel plant for the Japanese collaboration, of which we will see the results in the next financial year.

items.statement: Additional Rs 200 crore investment in Karoli plant in FY26; total invested Rs 490 crore till March 2025
items.quote: Karoli we have already invested Rs. 490 crore, as I mentioned, till March end. The investments are still carrying on because we have a huge potential in the growth in Karoli, so another approximately Rs. 200 crore we will be spending this year also further.

items.statement: Bangalore plant invested Rs 155 crore till March 2025; additional Rs 100 crore in FY26; total ~Rs 250 crore for Rs 400-500 crore revenue potential
items.quote: See, in the till 31 st March we have invested Rs. 155 crore in the Bangalore plant, which is our third plant. And we will be investing Rs. 100 crore more this year. So that will be an investment of about Rs. 250 crore. So it will give us a revenue of approximately Rs. 400 crore to Rs. 500 crore or so.

items.statement: Karoli plant at 50-55% utilization currently; peak revenue potential Rs 1,100-1,200 crore
items.quote: The peak potential of the Karoli plant will be around Rs. 1,100 crore to Rs. 1,200 crore, which we will see in the times to come. At the moment, the Karoli plant, we have revenues of about Rs. 500 crore to Rs. 600 crore, and it's operating on 50% capacity utilization.

items.statement: Bangalore plant expected 60-70% utilization by Q4 FY26; all other plants at full capacity
items.quote: And even this new plant in Bangalore, we expect by end of the last quarter of FY26 we should have a capacity utilization of 60% to 70%. Rest all plants are in full capacity.

items.statement: Advanced Braking revenue grew 16% in FY25; Aluminum Lightweighting grew 28%; Safety Control Cables grew 14%
items.quote: Our all three product segments performed well in FY25 in terms of revenue growth. We have sustained our market leadership position in the Advanced Braking system. Our Advanced Braking system revenue grew by 9% in Q4 and 16% in FY25 on year-on-year basis. The Aluminum Lightweighting Precision Solutions revenue grew by 21% in Q4 and 28% in FY25 on a year-on-year basis. The Safety Control Cable reven

items.statement: Expect two-wheeler industry growth of 6-8% in FY26 driven by monsoon, rate cuts, tax benefits
items.quote: Well, as far as the Two-Wheeler industry is concerned, we are also very hopeful that it will grow about 6% to 8%, what Hero has said. And we are confident because of the various reasons, just like I mentioned, good monsoon, interest rate cut, and the tax benefits that the government gave in the Budget.

items.statement: Debt-to-equity improved to 0.38x from 0.42x; debt-to-EBITDA at 0.83x in FY25
items.quote: We have also improved our debt profile with debt to equity reducing to 0.38x against 0.42x last year. Our average debt to EBITDA is at 0.83x in FY25.

items.statement: Board recommended 75% dividend (Rs 1.5 per share on face value Rs 2) for FY25
items.quote: The Board has recommended a dividend of 75%, i.e. Rs. 1.5 per equity share on the face value of Rs. 2 each.

items.statement: Signed technical collaboration with LIOHO Taiwan for HPDC alloy wheels (Feb 2024); strategic partnership with Kyushu Yanagawa Japan for HPDC alloy wheels (Mar 2025); JV with AISIN Group Japan for passenger car aftermarket (Apr 2024)
items.quote: We signed Technical Collaboration Agreement with LIOHO, Taiwan, to manufacture Two-Wheeler HPDC alloy wheels in February'24. The capacity is already built up and the product is under testing. We entered into a strategic partnership with Kyushu Yanagawa Seiki Co. Ltd., Japan, in March'25 for high pressure die casted alloy wheels for Two-Wheelers. We also signed a joint venture agreement with AISIN

items.statement: ROCE improved from 23.64% to 27.5% in FY25; target similar ROCE in FY26 with further debt-to-equity improvement
items.quote: One thing we forgot to mention that this year we improved our ROCE with the capacity utilization from 23.64% to 27.5%. I may assure you that next year also we will be doing very well and we will be achieving an ROCE close to this with the debt to equity also further improving and the performance growing on a very sound footing.

items.statement: Working capital improved due to good inventory management and customers paying before time
items.quote: One driver is certainly the very good inventory management, and the second is I think our customers are also so good that they are paying us before time even.

items.statement: CRISIL upgraded long-term credit rating from AA- to AA; short-term rating reaffirmed at A1+
items.quote: CRISIL Ratings upgraded our long term credit rating from "AA-" to "AA", while reaffirming our short term rating at CRISIL "A1+". This upgrade reflects the company has improved capital structure, better financial flexibility and strong volume growth.

items.statement: HPDC alloy wheel technology from Taiwan and Japan partnerships; Taiwan for broader market, Japan for Japanese OEMs; both ICE and EV compatible
items.quote: we have the first-mover advantage with that technology and we want to be the best in the class. That has been the philosophy of the company. So we will imbibe both the technologies. And the Japanese player will be feeding the Japanese Customer more, and the Taiwanese player will be feeding the rest of the market, that has been the philosophy behind it, number one. And the

items.statement: HPDC alloy wheel testing advanced; clearances expected by June-July 2025; supplies to start in H2 FY26
items.quote: However, we also expect that the alloy wheels with high pressure die casting that we made with the Taiwan technology is under an advanced stage of testing. And we hope to get the clearances by June or July end. And we are confident of starting the supplies in the H2 of this financial.

items.statement: HPDC alloy wheels to compete with gravity die casting players; target all OEMs for scooter and motorcycle alloy wheels
items.quote: So the top players, we will target all the OEMs for the scooter and motorcycle alloy wheels. So, let the product be tested and approved. Then it is for them to judge what are the advantages and whose share or whether they do not cut anybody's share, they just cut the import part or something.

items.statement: No management changes mentioned; focus on first-mover advantage in technology partnerships
items.quote: We keep on looking for good technical opportunities. As you have seen that we like to have the first-mover advantage, so we are talking to different people. And once something materializes, the whole market will know through the stock exchange.

items.statement: Guidance: branch addition 40-45 for the year, margins around 6%, credit cost 40-50 bps, loan growth 30-35% to reach AUM Rs 30,000 cr by March 2030
items.value: 40-45 branches; ~6% margin; 40-50 bps credit cost; 30-35% loan growth
items.quote: We continue to maintain a guidance of: • Branch addition of 40 to 45 for the year • Margins of around 6% • Credit cost of around 40 to 50 bps • Loan growth of around 3 0% to 35% to reach AUM of Rs. 30,000 crores by March 2030

items.statement: AUM grew 35% YoY to Rs 8,189 cr; Q4 disbursements Rs 933 cr (+25% YoY); FY25 disbursements Rs 3,335 cr (+25% YoY)
items.value: AUM Rs 8,189 cr; Q4 disbursement Rs 933 cr; FY25 disbursement Rs 3,335 cr
items.quote: We deliver ed an AUM growth of 35% year-on-year, reaching an AUM of Rs. 8,189 crores. In quarter 4 financial year '25, we disbursed Rs. 933 crores, registering a growth of 25% year -on-year, whereas in financial year '25, we disbursed Rs. 3,335 crores, registering a growth of 25% year-on-year

items.statement: Lending margin improved 10 bps QoQ to 6.2%, consistently above 6% guidance; portfolio yield stable at 14.9%; bucket cost of funds down 10 bps to 8.7%
items.quote: Our lending margins are up by 10 basis points to 6.2% and are consistently above 6%, in line with our guidance for medium term.

items.statement: Added 43 new branches in FY25 as per plan; total branch network 266
items.quote: During the quarter, our branch network expanded to 266 branches in total and during the year, we added 43 new branches as per the plan.

items.statement: DPD 30 at 3.1% (-60 bps QoQ); Stage 3 at 1% (-20 bps QoQ); Q4 credit cost 20 bps, FY25 credit cost 40 bps in line with guidance; PCR Stage 3 stable at 25%; total ECL Rs 64 cr vs regulatory Rs 37 cr
items.quote: On asset quality side, DPD 30 is at 3.1%, down by 60 basis points quarter-on-quarter. Stage 3 is at 1%, down by 20 bps quarter -on- quarter. With improvement in asset quality, credit cost for the quarter is 20 basis points and for the year, it is at 40 basi s points, which is in line with our guidance

items.statement: Incremental cost of funds 8.6% in Q4 (8.7% ex-NHB); disbursement yield 15%; 30% liabilities linked to repo/T-bill, 55% to MCLR, 15% fixed
items.quote: Disbursement yield are currently at about 15% and our incremental cost of fund for Q4 was about 8.6%.

items.statement: Unique customer collection rate 97%+; write-offs Rs 8 cr in FY25 with Rs 6 cr recovery from prior write-offs
items.quote: So unique customer collection is at about 97% plus.

items.statement: Liquidity Rs 1,480 cr including Rs 900 cr undrawn sanctions; undrawn NHB sanction Rs 200 cr to be drawn in Q1 FY26; ALM positive across buckets; fixed-rate portfolio funded by variable liabilities reduced from 45% to 18%
items.quote: On liquidity side, we are comfortably placed with liquidity of Rs. 1,480 crores, including undrawn sanction of about Rs. 900 crores. Our ALM is positive across all the buckets.

items.statement: Equity raise likely in ~3 years before leverage reaches 5x; current leverage 2.9x, targeting 4x in 2 years; CRAR allows up to 9x but rating agencies comfortable up to 5x
items.quote: So our brief thought process is that once we start touching 4x kind of leverage, then we start working on like equity raise and probably try to close the equity before touching the 5x kind of leverage.

items.statement: Attrition improved YoY but not at satisfaction level; Board approved next ESOP tranche covering larger employee set including frontline staff
items.quote: So compared to last year, there is an improvement in attrition, but not to our level of satisfaction. That is one thing. Attrition is still a challenge on that side. Particularly for controlling this attrition, I think Board has been kind enough. They have just approved the next tranche of stock options, which is going to cover the large set of people.

items.statement: Competitive moat: Tier 2/3 focus, Rs 10-11 lakh ticket size, direct sourcing via own branches (not DSA), 15-year operational DNA makes replication difficult for large players
items.quote: We are a player of Tier 2, Tier 3 markets, basically, which is a deep down into geography. Maintaining our ticket size of around Rs. 10-11 lakhs and sourcing is through our direct team instead of depending upon third-party channels.

items.statement: Housing loans 57% of AUM (67% on-book); LAP 43% (DA only on LAP); targeting 60-61% housing share over time; no loans above 80% LTV; average LTV 52%
items.quote: But if you look at the on-balance sheet portfolio, so as you have rightly said that for direct assignment, we do it for LAP portfolio. So at the on-book balance sheet level, the proportion of housing loan is at about 67%.

items.statement: Self-employed focus in Tier 2/3; ticket size Rs 5-30 lakh; salaried 20% of portfolio (8-9% cash salary); insurance cross-sell: property >90% penetration, credit life >80%; 4 insurance partners
items.quote: We are largely catering the self-employed customer in these markets of Tier 2, Tier 3 and which includes all set of gamut on the customers, who are serving this vicinity.

items.statement: ROA 5.8% (Q4), 5.6% (FY25); ROE 16.3% (Q4), 15.1% (FY25); leverage 2.9x; opex/AUM down 10 bps QoQ, 20 bps YoY
items.quote: RoA for the quarter is 5.8% and R oA for the full year is 5.6%. R oE for the full year is 15.1%. During the quarter, we have crossed the milestone of 16% ROE for the first-time post IPO and ended the quarter with RoE of 16.3% at a leverage of 2.9x

items.statement: Karnataka 6.3% of portfolio (-20-30 bps); Tamil Nadu 6%; MFI overlap 3.5-4% of total book (vintage, range-bound delinquency); restructured book 15-20 bps delta between 30+ DPD and Stage 2+3
items.quote: About Karnataka, we have portfolio of around 6.3%, there is a slight dip of some 20 bps, 30 bps.

items.statement: Board approved ESG policy for sustainable finance; on-book housing loan share 67% compliant with RBI PBC criteria
items.quote: Lastly, as we remain committed towards sustainable finance, the Board has approved the ESG policy.

items.statement: Branch expansion experiment: front-loaded 43 branches in FY25 (mostly Q1); FY26 will try different approach but same 40-45 target
items.quote: As an experiment, what we did last year, most of our branches got opened in the first quarter itself. That I think if you see go back on the data side also, quarter 1, we tried to open the branch as per the plan that time.

items.statement: Demand for affordable housing finance accelerating across Tier 2, Tier 3 and fast-growing micro markets; rising disposable income reshaping aspirations
items.quote: Demand for affordable housing finance continues to accelerate a cross Tier 2, Tier 3 and fast -growing micro markets. Rising disposable income driven by expanding job opportunities in various sectors are reshaping consumer aspiration in these regions

items.statement: FY26 PAT margin target around 2.5%; FY27 PAT margin target 3.5-4% with dyeing unit
items.quote: In FY26, PAT margin should be around 2.5%. With the dyeing unit by FY27, margins should rise to around 3.5-4%.

items.statement: Expect 3x net profit growth by FY27
items.quote: Yes, we expect 3x growth in net profit by FY27.

items.statement: Target net profit of ₹30 crores by FY27
items.quote: We're targeting net profit of ₹30 crores by FY27.

items.statement: Top-line growth of 10-15% expected from new processing and dyeing unit
items.quote: We expect top-line growth of 10-15% due to the addition of a processing and dyeing unit, which provides backward integration.

items.statement: ₹9 crores for finishing unit acquisition (₹4 crores equity + ₹5 crores unsecured loans)
items.quote: ₹4 crores for acquisition and ₹5 crores via unsecured loans. Total investment: ₹9 crores.

items.statement: ₹60 crores for backward integration dyeing unit
items.quote: About ₹60 crores for the dyeing unit. We're expecting an additional net profit of ₹12-13 crores from this.

items.statement: ₹7-8 crores for 2.5 MW solar plant to meet 90% power needs
items.quote: The project capex is around ₹7-8 crores for solar to reach 90% of our power requirement, and the saving will be around ₹2.5 crores.

items.statement: Current capacity utilization around 89%, will reach full capacity soon
items.quote: Around 89%. We'll reach full capacity soon.

items.statement: No immediate capacity expansion plans; focus on profitability first, expansion after two years
items.quote: No immediate plans. First, we'll focus on profitability through the new units. Capacity expansion will come after two years.

items.statement: Finishing unit acquisition expected to add ₹5-6 crores annual profit
items.quote: With this acquisition, profits from finishing will be consolidated, which we expect to increase profits by ₹5-6 crores annually.

items.statement: Steady-state EBITDA margin for weaving unit 3% in FY26, can reach 4-4.5%; composite unit 7-8%
items.quote: 3.5%? Riken: Yes, and if all goes well, it can go up to 4 –4.5% in weaving. For the entire composite unit, it can reach 7–8

items.statement: 70-75% revenue from value-added products
items.quote: Around 70-75% of revenue comes from value-added products.

items.statement: US cotton landed cost 7-8% more expensive than Indian cotton due to 10% import duty; only 2-3% cotton imported
items.quote: The US cotton landed cost is around 7-8% more expensive than Indian cotton due to an import duty of around 10%. At present, only 2-3% of our cotton consumption is imported.

items.statement: Cotton yarn prices expected to remain stable for next year
items.quote: We expect cotton yarn prices to be stable this year. In the last two years, there was already a correction in cotton and yarn prices, so t hey should remain stable for the next one year

items.statement: Improved receivable cycles and tighter inventory controls supported cash generation; net debt-to-equity reduced to 0.14x
items.quote: This has materially supported internal cash generation, enabling us to reduce our net debt-to-equity ratio to 0.14x.

items.statement: Acquired 60% stake in Teesta Spintex (finishing unit) from other promoters in April; now 100% owned by Shanti Spintex
items.quote: Earlier I was having a 40% stake in that, and 60% stake was outside. So what happened is we acquired the balance 60% in this April only from the other promoters. And now, in order to ensure that there is no diversion of interest, we are shifting 100% equity to Shanti Spintex now.

items.statement: UK FTA reduces garment duty 8-12%, making India more competitive vs China/Pakistan; India's 5-6% UK apparel share expected to grow
items.quote: The FTA with the UK will reduce the duty on garments, which used to be 8-12%. This will make Indian garments more competitive compared to China and Pakistan. Currently, India holds a 5-6% share in the UK apparel market, which we expect to grow.

items.statement: Finishing unit acquisition from related party at near book value to avoid valuation questions
items.quote: Because it was a related party, so we didn't want any questions or anything to be raised. So that's why we preferred to transfer it at cost or at least some margin on that.

items.statement: Revenue growth guidance of 10-15% for FY26 with pure EPC EBITDA margin of 11-12%
items.quote: we are expecting to deliver a growth rate of normally 10% to 15% against the top line. And accordingly, the margin will also increase in absolute number. As far as the EBITDA margin is concerned, so we have informed that our pure EPC margin will range between 11% to 12%.

items.statement: Order book of INR10,862 crores as of March 31, 2025 with bill-to-book ratio of 3.2x
items.quote: As of March 31, '25, we have a robust order book of INR10,862 crores, reflecting a healthy bill-to-book ratio of 3.2x.

items.statement: Order inflow target of INR5,500 crores for FY26
items.quote: So last year, we committed INR5,000 crores. We got INR5,400 crores. So this year, we are targeting INR5,500 crores.

items.statement: Asset-light model with minimal capex of INR15-20 crores annually, relying 80-90% on leased equipment
items.quote: we are an asset-light company. So we don't have a major any capex plan. We normally -- as per the company philosophy, we normally take all the machinery and equipment, whatever we require for our project on a lease basis.

items.statement: Q4 FY25 consolidated EBITDA margin at 12.6% vs 14.6% for full year FY25
items.quote: EBITDA for the quarter stood at INR1,279 million with an EBITDA margin of 12.6%.

items.statement: FY25 consolidated EBITDA margin at 14.6% with PAT margin of 8.4%
items.quote: EBITDA for the year was at INR4,995 million compared to INR4,923 million in FY '24 with an EBITDA margin of 14.6%. PAT for FY '25 stood at INR2,866 million with a net margin of 8.4%.

items.statement: Consolidated gross debt of INR13,967 million with net debt-equity ratio of 1.5x as of March 31, 2025
items.quote: On a consol idated basis, our gross debt stood at INR13,967 million, which includes INR685 million in equipment term loan, INR4,337 million in term loans, INR6,806 million in HAM term loans and INR2,139 million in working capital loans. On net debt-equity ratio remains very effective and comfortable at 1.5x for the year ended FY '25

items.statement: Net working capital cycle of 62 days as of March 31, 2025 with standalone receivables of INR850 crores
items.quote: Coming to the working capital, our net working capital cycle stood at 62 days as on 31 March 2025. This is calculated considering the inventory days, WIP position, receivable and vendor payments.

items.statement: NHAI projects account for 79.9% of total order book with 23 ongoing projects across 8 states
items.quote: Notably, NHAI projects account for 79.9% of our total order book.

items.statement: Order book composition: 85.3% elevated roads/highways/specialized structures, 13.3% railway/metro, rest airport runway/bus terminal
items.quote: Our order book comprised of 85.3% from elevated roads, highways, specialized structures, flyovers, tunnels, 13.3% from railway, metro and the rest of the business verticals like airport runway and bus terminal.

items.statement: Targeting to start at least 3 more HAM projects in FY26 with appointed dates expected in next two quarters
items.quote: And going forward, I think in this year only, we'll have at least three more HAM projects starting. We should be getting the

items.statement: Three HAM projects expected to be operational in FY26 generating ~INR250 crores annual annuity for 15 years
items.quote: And of course, the HAM are better projects like all three projects, once they're completed, our annuity would be around INR250 crores coming every year. So you can understand this kind of amount coming for next 15 years.

items.statement: Equity investment of INR400 crores already made in HAM projects with additional commitment of INR800 crores over project periods
items.quote: we have already invested a sum of close to INR 400 crores in the existing HAM projects, including the new one, Southern Ayodhya Bypass. And as far as the remaining is concerned, so we have an equity commitment of close to INR800 crores.

items.statement: Equity deployment of ~INR250 crores expected in FY26 depending on appointed dates for new HAM projects
items.quote: it will be closed it, somewhere close to INR250 crores in this year, depending upon the AD.

items.statement: Tender pipeline of INR70,000 crores quoted across metro, railway, water, irrigation and heavy civil segments
items.quote: Tender pipeline we've already quoted tenders worth INR 70,000 crores. And that too in a different verticals, metro, railway, water, irrigation and heavy products.

items.statement: Ramban-Banihal tunnel project facing delays due to security situation with 70% workforce departed, only MEP and roadwork remaining
items.quote: current situation, right now, we can't answer anything because all our teams, they were scared, their families have already called them, and they have 70% of the teams have left aside because the situation is very bad there.

items.statement: NHAI now requiring 80% land availability before issuing appointed date for HAM projects, causing delays in project starts
items.quote: Last year, what has happened is the NHAI till the time land has given total clear or they have the 3G, they are not allowed to take out the pace that they don't get the approvals or they are unable to issue the LOA.

items.statement: Q4 FY25 margin decline attributed to increased contracting costs and related costs during the quarter
items.quote: The decline as you witness is a marginal decline. That is basically on account of the increase in some contracting costs and other related costs, which we witnessed during this quarter.

items.statement: HAM receivables under service concession of INR1,024 crores to be collected over 15-year annuity period per SPV model
items.quote: So this receivable amount will be paid off along with the interest over a period of 15 years. This is the model. And on that basis, your IRR is carved out.

items.statement: Company sees healthy competition in new verticals like metro, irrigation, water with fewer players and successful bidding track record
items.quote: We're always open to work into new states, new verticals and we keep tracking these kind of new tenders where the competition is healthy and less players are there. And we've been successful also in doing this.

items.statement: 70% workforce left Ramban-Banihal project due to security concerns impacting completion timeline
items.quote: all our teams, they were scared, their families have already called them, and they have 70% of the teams have left aside because the situation is very bad there.

items.statement: Management reaffirmed FY26 guidance of 8-10% revenue growth and 18-20% EBITDA margin.
items.quote: Yes, Abhishek, we are sticking to that same guidance.

items.statement: FY25 EBITDA margin improved 390 bps to 14.4% driven by 8% operating cost decline.
items.quote: team's efforts towards effective cost management across the businesses has led to a decline of 8% in overall operating costs during the year, resulting in a 390 basis point EBITDA margin improvement to 14.4

items.statement: No further cost cutting room; future margin expansion must come from revenue growth.
items.quote: there is no more room for cost cutting, for expansion in the EBITDA margin. Anything that has to come now has to come from revenue growth

items.statement: Ad revenue declined 11% in FY25 due to weak consumption; Q4 impacted by sports calendar and high base.
items.quote: The linear ad spending environment continues to remain soft during the year, especially for general entertainment. As a result, our FY '25 ad revenues were down by 11%.

items.statement: Management expects ad revenue to grow in high-single digits in FY26, aided by FTA re-entry.
items.quote: I certainly expect, as I said, I am an optimist and I do believe that advertising revenue, if it does not grow significantly, but it will certainly grow in the inflationary number that you have given in a high-single digit kind of stakes.

items.statement: Linear subscription revenue flat QoQ in Q4 FY25 due to pay TV churn; digital subscription grew.
items.quote: During Q4 F Y'25, subscription revenue remained flat Q-o-Q due to a slowdown in the linear subscription, which was partially offset by the increase in digital subscription revenue.

items.statement: ZEE5 EBITDA loss reduced 50% YoY to INR 5.5B in FY25 from INR 11.1B in FY24.
items.quote: Further, during the year, ZEE5 EBITDA loss has reduced by INR 5.6 billion to INR 5.5 billion from INR 11.1 billion in FY'24. That is about 50% reduction in the EBITDA loss Y -o-Y.

items.statement: ZEE5 breakeven targeted within 3-year timeline from 2025, may shift slightly due to market softness.
items.quote: counting 2025, we were looking at a 3-year timeline in sort of breakeven. Given the softness in the market, it may shift a little bit up or down

items.statement: Zee Studios plans 18-21 film releases in FY26, handpicked based on content resonance.
items.quote: We are looking at anywhere between 18 to 21 films that we will do next year. These will be largely handpicked on the basis of the content that resonates with the audiences

items.statement: Content acquisition capex equals P&L charge; no separate capex number disclosed for music.
items.quote: Whatever capex we incur for acquisition of content is on the basis of what we run through our P&L. So, if we run INR 100 through our P&L, then INR 100 is available to us for newer acquisitions.

items.statement: Strong FCF in Q4 FY25 driven by working capital optimization and tax refunds.
items.quote: During the quarter, we generated a strong FCF driven by optimization of working capital and tax refunds.

items.statement: Cash and treasury investments stood at INR 24.1B as of March 2025.
items.quote: The cash and treasury investments increased during the quarter and as of March '25 stood at INR 24.1 billion

items.statement: Evaluating assets for INR 200 crore FCCB fund deployment; no finalization yet.
items.quote: we are still evaluating a couple of assets as we speak, but we'll come back to you as soon as we find the right mix of the right valuation and give any assets which gives us the right scalable opportunities.

items.statement: ZEE5 claims top 3 active subscriber base in India; exact number not disclosed.
items.quote: We don't generally give that number, but we are in the top 3 active subscriber base compared to our competitors in the country.

items.statement: Promoter has publicly stated intent to increase stake; timing depends on Board decision.
items.quote: the promoter has always stated publicly that they would want to increase their stake at a certain stage going forward.

items.statement: US film tax proposal impact minimal as international revenue is a fraction of movie business.
items.quote: the U.S. or the international territories is a fraction of the overall revenue of any of our businesses. From that perspective, any impact to that is going to be miniscule from our perspective.

items.statement: Content inventory advances and deposits declined to INR 70.5B in March 2025, down INR 3.7B YoY.
items.quote: March '25 content inventory advances and deposits were at INR 70.5 billion, lower by INR 3.7 billion on a Y-o-Y basis.

items.statement: Other expenses in Q4 FY25 reduced to INR 87 crore due to bad debt provision reversals.
items.quote: there has been certain recoveries of bad debts, so which have been provisions made earlier, which have been reversed, which are no longer required, which has resulted into this reduced other expenses line item.

items.statement: Linear TV viewership share 16.8% in FY25; Zee Marathi showed uptick but Q4 dropped 20 bps YoY due to sports.
items.quote: Our viewership share during FY '25 was 16.8%. Encouragingly, our efforts to regain viewership share of Zee Marathi have shown some uptick during the year. In Q4 FY'25, our viewership share dropped by 20 basis points Y-o-Y due to the busy sports calendar

items.statement: Zee Music Company remains #2 music channel with 18,000+ songs, 164M YouTube subscribers, 190B video views in FY25.
items.quote: Zee Music Company continues to be the #2 music channel driven by its new-age music catalogue and rich library with over 18,000 songs and garnering over 164 million subscribers on YouTube and nearly 190 billion total video views during FY'25.

items.statement: Music segment growth tapered to single digits in FY25 due to homegrown streaming platform shutdowns.
items.quote: we have seen a growth kind of tapering in single digits, the main reason being some of the homegrown streaming platforms have shut down, or they have slowed down.

items.statement: Linear TV price hikes historically in single digits; pay TV churn ongoing but TV penetration still growing.
items.quote: the price hikes, if you look at historically have been in single digits itself. The price hikes have not been very significant from that perspective. I think the churn is happening by a natural cause, but we are also still seeing the television penetration in India is still growing.

items.statement: Expect acceleration in profit and asset base in FY26 towards pre-embargo trend line
items.quote: We expect to see acceleration in profit and asset base in FY26 as well, towards the normal trend line that is our pre -RBI embargo levels.

items.statement: Credit cost guidance of 2.5% to 2.7% for FY26
items.quote: I mean, because you are still guiding for a credit cost of 2.5 to 2.7%, right?

items.statement: Aim to return off-book assets (co-lending and assignments) to 40% of AUM by end of FY26
items.quote: Our endeavor will be to go back to 40%. Anusha Raheja: In FY26, you say? Nirmal Jain: That's right. So by the end of FY26, I can

items.statement: Microfinance credit cost expected around 5% for FY26
items.quote: We are looking on an average credit cost of around 5% for the FY '26.

items.statement: Credit cost expected to normalize to earlier levels in FY27 as MSME mix changes
items.quote: As our MSME portfolio mix will also change in this year, we'll see that next year probably credit cost will get back to our earlier levels.

items.statement: Gold loan yield has started improving, up 20 bps this quarter, with room for further improvement
items.quote: If you see this quarter is up by 20 basis points on the portfolio level. And it's okay. There are competitive pressures which we cannot ignore. So, it might improve at a slow pace, but still, it has some more room to improve.

items.statement: Cost-to-income ratio target to return to FY24 levels in FY26
items.quote: But if we can bring it to FY24 level, I think that should be a good target.

items.statement: Gold loan growth momentum to continue even after recouping lost ground
items.quote: Yes, actually, the market seems good. And we'll have a growth momentum continuing. Even after we have recovered our lost ground.

items.statement: MSME secured portfolio (LAP) to see significant ramp-up in next few quarters
items.quote: So we'l l see a big, or maybe a significant ramp up in the secured portfolio in the next few quarters

items.statement: NIM improvement expected from gold loan mix normalization, lower cost of funds, and dollar bond hedging adjustment
items.quote: Our NIM will also improve because we see that the interest rate cost seems to have peaked down. And maybe, you know, in a liquidity type situation, we've paid higher price. And also, in the mix, when the gold loan is the significant driver, we'll see the NIM improvement.

items.statement: Gold loan margins to inch up quarter after quarter back to normal levels
items.quote: So our margins will be inching up, we'll get back to our normal margins, you know, quarter after quarter this year as well as next year.

items.statement: Consolidated AUM rose 10% QoQ to INR 78,341 crores in Q4 FY25
items.quote: Our consolidated profit after tax was INR 251 crores which is quarter over quarter up 208% and our AUM in aggregate rose by 10% sequentially to INR 78,341 crores.

items.statement: Gold loan AUM grew 40% QoQ in Q4 FY25
items.quote: Gold loans saw a significant 40% sequential growth, reaffirming our customer loyalty and franchise while MSME loans, which is our strategic focus for the future, co ntinued their steady rise up 18% year on year

items.statement: Assigned loan book at INR 12,789 crores, up 3% QoQ; co-lending book at INR 10,606 crores, up 15% QoQ
items.quote: The assigned loan book stands at around INR 12,789 crore, up 3% QoQ and down 22% YoY, and the co-lending book has gone up by around 15% Q-on-Q and is down 10% YoY basis at INR 10,606 crores.

items.statement: Consolidated GNPA improved to 2.2% from 2.4% QoQ; NNPA at ~1%
items.quote: I am also very happy to report that asset quality has improved further with our GNPA declining to 2.2% from 2.4% in the previous quarter.

items.statement: Provision coverage ratio on NPA stands at around 100%
items.quote: Our ECL provision is driven by IndAS, and our provision coverage ratio on our NPA stands at around 100%.

items.statement: Home finance micro-LAP portfolio of INR 2,400 crores saw some asset quality spillover from unsecured segment
items.quote: Yes, Mohit, out of this total book which we have, it's about INR2,400 crores.

items.statement: Plan aggressive investment in digital and AI technology in FY26
items.quote: We plan an aggressive investment in digital as well as AI technology in the current year to maintain our edge in the sector.

items.statement: Gold loan pricing: no new loans below ~15% (1.2% per month); competitive pressures acknowledged
items.quote: We have. So, we don't, as of now, we don't have any product or any scheme less than 1.2% per month, which typically, most of the gold companies will have 99% paisa or 83% paisa also, which is equivalent to 9 %, 10% or 12%. As of now, we are not doing new loan s of less than around 15% or so.

items.statement: Mobilized ~INR 8,500 crores in Q4 FY25 including USD 425 million MTN bond and INR 1,500 crores domestic NCD
items.quote: On the funding side, we mobilized close to INR 8,500 crores during the quarter, which included the MTN- the medium-term note dollar bond issue of USD 325 million, which was topped up by another USD 100 million, so USD 425 million in aggregate, and a successful domestic NCD placement of about INR 1,500 crores during the quarter.

items.statement: RBI draft co-lending guidelines comments due May 12; final guidelines expected this quarter
items.quote: Now RBI has come up with a new draft guidelines for co -lending, for which they invited for comments till, I think, 12th May, which is Monday. So let's see the final set of guidelines and then we'll know how co-lending will evolve.

items.statement: RBI draft gold loan guidelines propose maintaining 75% LTV throughout loan tenure; gold price appreciation provides buffer
items.quote: Actually gold prices are up significantly. So, instead of 75, say, you bring it down to 70 or whatever, then more or less will be covered throughout. But then that just will recalibrate the loanable value if these guidelines become effective.

items.statement: Management anticipates another record year for Triveni Turbines in FY26, though quarterly results may be lumpy.
items.quote: But needless to say, that we are anticipating another record year for the Triveni Turbines in FY 26.

items.statement: FY25 order booking grew 26% YoY to ₹23.63 billion, a record high.
items.quote: We are very proud that we have had the highest ever annual order booking of ₹23.63 billion during FY 25, an increase of 26% y-o-y.

items.statement: Closing order book as of March 31, 2025 stood at a record ₹19.09 billion, up 23% YoY.
items.quote: And has this left us with a record outstanding carry-forward order book as of the 31 st of March 2025 of ₹19.09 billion, an increase of 23% y-o-y.

items.statement: FY25 EBITDA margin expanded 280 bps YoY to 25.8% driven by higher aftermarket and export mix.
items.quote: We had the highest ever EBITDA of ₹5.18 billion, up 36% year-on-year with a margin of 25.8%, which is an increase of 280 basis points (bps) year-over-year (y-o-y).

items.statement: FY26 capex forecast is ₹1.65 billion, including ₹0.44 billion carry-forward from FY25, for R&D, testing, assembly capacity and international subsidiaries.
items.quote: The total capex forecast for this current year, FY 26 is about ₹1.65 billion, which includes a carry -forward of about ₹0.44 billion from the previous financial year which is FY 25.

items.statement: Currently operating on a two-shift basis; adding a new bay at Sompura facility to augment assembly and testing capacity, not a major constraint.
items.quote: We are currently operating on a two-shift basis, and we don't see capacity as a real constraint. We are adding a bay, which is more from an assembly perspective and some manufacturing capacity, which is part of our capex plan for the current year.

items.statement: Domestic market declined ~10% in FY25; order finalisation timelines elongated due to uncertainty, but enquiry pipeline grew 120% domestically and 30% internationally.
items.quote: While the enquiry book is extremely robust, the market in India has declined as we calculated for FY 25 by 10%. While we were anticipating Q4 to be more robust in terms of domestic order finalisations, the robust level of enquiries gives us good confidence that sectors will come back into our order book within the coming quarters.

items.statement: Export order booking grew 23% YoY to ₹12.59 billion in FY25; export outstanding order book up 36% to ₹10.9 billion (57% of closing order book).
items.quote: The Company continues to see good international demand, which is r eflected in the export order booking, which has grown by 23% y-o-y to ₹12.59 billion during the year.

items.statement: Product order booking grew 38% to ₹17.41 billion in FY25, driven by renewables, industrial power, API turbines and CO2 energy storage foray.
items.quote: The product order booking has grown by an impressive 38% to ₹17.41 billion in FY 25. The key drivers for growth in product order booking were the finalisation of orders in the renewabl e energy sector, industrial clients for industrial power generation and power producers and API turbines.

items.statement: Aftermarket revenue share ~33% of sales; expected to rise ~1% per year, driven by refurbishment growth potential.
items.quote: We're quite happy with the 33 % -odd aftermarket as a percentage of sales. Yes, we'd expect it to rise by 1% odd every year consistently so that it's contributing more.

items.statement: API enquiry pipeline robust; approved vendor at major global refineries and petrochemical complexes; strong growth in drive and power turbines across Middle East, SE Asia, Americas, Europe.
items.quote: We have been in the approved vendor list of major refineries, the petrochemical complexes across the globe. And even last financial year, some more positive results we were able to gain in terms of getting into the approved vendor list, which has given a strong enquiry pipeline.

items.statement: API market highly competitive with established global OEMs; no new entrants expected; differentiation via quick backend support from India and technical acceptability.
items.quote: API market wise, as we got ourselves approved in all the refineries, majority of the reputed refineries, the pipeline is building up. At the same time, these are very, very competitive market, and we are fighting with all the competition across the globe in different territories.

items.statement: India-UK FTA neutral for business as turbine imports already at zero duty; benefit only if it spurs UK capex in waste-to-energy and green power.
items.quote: Most of these FTAs are neutral to us because our product is not heavily taxed as a dutiable item, both ways. Imports into the country are pretty much at zero duty anyway.

items.statement: Receivables and other current assets spiked in March due to back-ended dispatches; largely reversed in April-May; other financial assets reflect FDs >12 months.
items.quote: In the quarter ending Q4 FY 25, we had certain back ending of orders, which happened in the month of March, which you'll see from a balance sheet where we have higher receivables as well as certain other current assets. Both of these are short term in nature and would have already been reversed to a significant extent in the month of April to return to a low receivable metric.

items.statement: Board recommended final dividend of 200% (₹2/share) for FY25, in addition to interim dividend of 200% (₹2/share).
items.quote: The Board has also recommended payment of final dividend of 200%, which is ₹2 per equity share for the financial year FY 24-25, which is subject to the approval of our shareholders. But this is in addition to the interim dividend of 200%, which is also ₹2 per equity share of ₹1 each.

items.statement: Focused on internal talent development, external hiring, continuous learning, diversity and industry collaboration to build future-ready workforce.
items.quote: People continue to remain the cornerstone of our organi sational excellence and through a focused approach to internal talent development, external hiring as well as continuous learning diversity as well as industry collaboration. We are building a future-ready workforce aligned with our customer -first mindset and innovation-driven agenda.

items.statement: Elongation of domestic order finalisation timelines due to macro uncertainty; unclear if one-quarter or multi-quarter phenomenon.
items.quote: So I think what you could say right now is that there has been an elongation of order finalisation timelines. And that is something that is a concern, but we'll have to wait and see if this is something that is a one quarter thing or something that continues for multiple quarters.

items.statement: CO2 energy storage order of ₹290 crore from NTPC Kudgi with Energy Dome; developmental project, margin in line with domestic margins; scope >50% value add; scalability to be assessed by Q3-Q4 FY26.
items.quote: We also continue to develop new and innovative solutions, utili sing carbon -dioxide as a means for fluid transmission, which includes an order, which we have received along with our Italian partner Energy Dome, with NTPC, which is a ₹290 crore (₹2.90 billion) order for 160-MW hour long-duration energy storage project at NTPC's Kudgi Supercritical Thermal Power Plant.

items.statement: US subsidiary expansion capex on track with slight timing deferment; building flexibility to manufacture turbines locally depending on tariff structure.
items.quote: The capex that we had planned, we are on track. There's a little bit of a deferment just because of timing issues. But we are going ahead. And we are creating the flexibility in our infrastructure there. So, depending upon how the tariff structures take shape, we would have the flexibility to be able to even make turbines there.

items.statement: US market enquiry pipeline strong for aftermarket (refurbishment, spares) and product (API, geothermal, industrial power); Canadian orders routed via India entity due to tariff uncertainty.
items.quote: We see the API market in the United States as well as distinct geothermal and industrial power generation, including energy efficien cy as key growth drivers. The U.S. itself as a $25 trillion economy with the capital base that it has, presents many opportunities.

items.statement: Revenue CAGR 33% and PBT CAGR 41% over FY22-FY25; revenue grew 2.36x, PBT grew 2.82x in three years.
items.quote: The Company has grown very rapidly in the last three years between FY 22 and FY 25, the revenue of the Company has grown to 2.36x with a CAGR of 33%. And in the same period, between FY 22 and FY 25, the PBT has grown to 2.82x with a CAGR of 41%.

items.statement: Margin accretion from aftermarket/export mix; raw material pricing stable with long-term vendor rates; pricing decisions made with full cost visibility.
items.quote: Margin accretion happened because of both aftermarket as a percentage of revenue going up as well as the fact that we have a higher export as a percentage of sales. So, both of these factors have contributed positively to the margin. In terms of volatility in raw material pricing and increased overhead cost, those were larger factors in FY 22, FY 23, where the rate volatility that we saw post-COVI

items.statement: No M&A discussed; growth strategy focused on organic R&D, new products (CO2 storage, SMR), capacity augmentation and market expansion.
items.quote: No. There is a very strong need for us to continue with our research and development, which is to ensure that our current product range, not only is relevant and ex panding in its niche applications , b ut equally to introduce new technology and new products such as what we try to do with our carbon -dioxide based systems.

items.statement: Sanjay Sachdeva joined as MD and CEO from Unilever with global consumer business experience
items.quote: I am extremely delighted to welcome Mr. Sanjay Sachdeva into Bajaj Electricals Limited as our new Managing Director and Chief Executive Officer.

items.statement: Targeting double-digit EBIT margin in Consumer Products in next three years, around 6% in current year
items.quote: we have aspirations, I think we have already given a guidance that would like to be a double-digit EBIT business in the next three years or so. And in the current year we will be targeting somewhere around 6%.

items.statement: Consumer Products EBIT margin expanded to 3.9% from 1.8% YoY due to 3.6% gross margin expansion
items.quote: Our CP EBIT margin has expanded to 3.9% as against 1.8% in the corresponding quarter of the previous year. The increase in margin issue is due to a strong expansion in gross margin of 3.6%.

items.statement: Lighting Solutions EBIT margin at 7.8% vs 8.5% YoY, brand investments to remain high
items.quote: Our EBIT was at 7.8% as against 8.5% reported during the corresponding quarter of the previous year. The brand investments from this vertical will continue to be high for the next few quarters.

items.statement: Will take price increases to mitigate inflation, partly absorb through savings
items.quote: there will be maybe another price increase this year. So there will be therefore both premiumization and price increases to mitigate inflation will be

items.statement: MFI channel issue continues, not resolved, impacting demand since last year and into Q1
items.quote: we still have an issue on the MFI front, MFIs have still not started going on full steam as it was earlier.

items.statement: Consumer Products grew 8.4% YoY driven by domestic appliances, fans, trade revival; Morphy Richards high double-digit growth
items.quote: The Consumer Products business registered a strong revenue growth of 8.4% on the back of a good demand for domestic appliances, followed by fans, and continued trade revival.

items.statement: Professional Lighting order book healthy at Rs. 248 crores, nearly double last year
items.quote: Coming to Professional Lighting. The order book stays healthy at Rs. 248 crores. And we are committed to growing this business.

items.statement: Normal capex ~Rs. 100 crores; with new factory approval total capex could be Rs. 400-450 crores
items.quote: the normal CAPEX will be close to about Rs. 100-odd crores. But as you would have seen in the last, I mean , the budget board meeting we had said that we are also evaluat ing a factory for which a principal approval of about Rs. 300 crores have been taken. So if that materializes, the CAPEX would be in the range of Rs. 400 - Rs. 450 crores

items.statement: Evaluating new manufacturing unit in India, exploratory work commenced
items.quote: Further, on the proposal to explore the possibilities, opportunities and feasibility of setting up the company's manufacturing unit at a suitable location in India, the company has already commenced the evaluation and exploratory work.

items.statement: Board approved wholly owned subsidiary in UAE for Middle East expansion, activity on track
items.quote: With regards to our export strategy and with a view to expand company's international footprint and enhanced business opportunities in the Middle East and other untapped markets, the Board have already approved the incorporation of a wholly owned subsidiary of the company in UAE.

items.statement: Positive cash flow from operations Rs. 87 crores in Q4, surplus funds Rs. 509 crores
items.quote: We continue to generate positive cash flow from operations of Rs. 87 crores for the quarter. We ended the quarter with the surplus funds of Rs. 509 crores.

items.statement: Brand spend at 2.4% of sales in Q4, full year ~3%, planning to increase to 3.5-4% next year
items.quote: full year is around 3% for the year. And next year, we plan to take it up so somewhere would be in about 3.5% to 4%.

items.statement: Consumer Lighting mix improvement drove 2.5% FLM margin expansion, premiumization ongoing
items.quote: we continuously improve our first level margins with the product mix, and which has helped us to improve that by almost 2.5% (overall) in the FLM itself, which will continue.

items.statement: Nex brand growing slower than expected but upward trajectory, expanded portfolio with coolers, rebranded as Nex by Bajaj
items.quote: the Nex brand, it's going a little slower than what we had anticipated, but it's still on the up ward trajectory. A nd we have expanded the portfolio by launching coolers under that brand

items.statement: RBI MFI restrictions easing but demand recovery not expected quickly
items.quote: RBI eases the limitations that they had put on the MFIs, I do not think that demand is going to come back quickly.

items.statement: Geopolitical uncertainty from US tariffs and India-Pakistan tensions impacting North zone demand
items.quote: recent tariff announcement by US A dministration have heightened policy uncertainty, posing new headwinds for global growth and inflation

items.statement: Revenue from operations Rs. 1,265 crores, up 6.5% YoY; PBT Rs. 71 crores, up 191% YoY
items.quote: The company has achieved revenue from operations of Rs. 1,265 crores, as against Rs. 1,188 crores, a healthy growth of 6.5% over the 4th Quarter of the previous year. The company's profit before tax has zoomed to Rs. 71 crores, which is an increase of 191%.

items.statement: Adjusted PBT Rs. 148 crores vs Rs. 132 crores, up 12.4% YoY excluding one-time items
items.quote: By adjusting these one-time impacts, we delivered a profit before tax of Rs. 148 crores as against Rs. 132 crores, thereby resulting in a significant improvement of 12.4%.

items.statement: Nashik VRS completed, 115 of 117 workers opted for VRS
items.quote: The VRS in Nashik is over. Out of the 117 workers, 115 workers opted for the VRS so that is done with.

items.statement: EPR charge Rs. 9.5 crores this year, similar to last year, will increase to ~Rs. 18 crores next year
items.quote: EPR for this year is about. Rs. 9.5 crores and last year also was similar. Going forward next year it will be a charge of about Rs. 18 crores.

items.statement: Consultancy fees for VAVE, GTM, UAE subsidiary to continue for at least couple of years
items.quote: a lot of the initiatives are still going on. For example , the V AVE it's going to continue. We are having our GTM exercise, which is continuing. Lot of the things relating to the new initiatives like setup of subsidiary in Ras Al -Khaimah, UAE. So yes , you will th ese expenses continuing for at least a couple of years

items.statement: FY26 total capex guided at Rs 1,200 crore

items.statement: RBI draft co-lending guidelines comments due 12th May; final guidelines awaited for gold loan LTV maintenance throughout tenure
items.quote: Now RBI has come up with a new draft guidelines for co -lending, for which they invited for comments till, I think, 12th May, which is Monday. So let's see the final set of guidelines and then we'll know how co-lending will evolve.

items.statement: Tamil Nadu microfinance bill passed but no disruption seen; collections holding at ~96% in Karnataka
items.quote: Both, we would have hit around 96% in collection efficiency in Karnataka.

items.statement: Credit cost elevated due to lingering MFI pain and high-yielding unsecured MSME portfolio; normalization expected in FY27
items.quote: There's some bit of pain in MFI that may linger on and unsecured MSME portfolio also can have, you know, I mean, because the high yielding portfolio, so it can always have slightly higher credit losses also. So these two factors are there primarily f or the estimation of credit losses this year

items.statement: Gold price decline would impact industry; LTV guideline changes may require recalibration
items.quote: So if the gold loan prices fall significantly, I think there'll be impact on the industry as a whole.

items.statement: Interest spread guidance 6.9-7% for FY26 vs 6.7% in FY25
items.quote: when we are guiding for interest spreads of 6.9% to 7% versus 6.7% in FY25

items.statement: Capital adequacy: NBFC 18.5%, Housing Finance 47.2%, Microfinance 32.4% as of March 31, 2025
items.quote: As of 31st of March, we hold a healthy capital adequacy of around 18.5 in the NBFC, housing finance at 47.2, and microfinance at 32.4%, well above the threshold of 15% regulatory defined.

items.statement: FY26 new screen additions guided at 100-110 screens
items.quote: even in this environment to open 77 screens, if I can say it myself, I think it's a very positive step for the company because these are brand -new 77 screens and great catchments, great locations. Even -- so this year also about 110-odd screens will be there.

items.statement: FY26 capex guided at INR400-425 crores
items.quote: In terms of our capex, we expect that financial year '25, '26, we will incur a total capex of roughly in the range of INR400 crores to INR425 crores, which will be split across new projects, we will be spending slightly higher on renovating our existing high -value properties as well as maintenance and IT-related capex.

items.statement: FY26 capex split: INR250-300 crores on new projects, balance on renovations, maintenance and IT
items.quote: I think broadly, we will spend roughly INR250 crores to INR300 crores on new projects, which will include projects which are currently under fit-out and will open in the next few months, plus giving advances for new handovers that we take for fit-outs. And the balance we intend to spend across renovations, maintenance of our existing circuit as well as IT-related capex.

items.statement: 23 cinemas with 101 screens signed under capital-light model, most operational in next 12-24 months
items.quote: We have already signed 23 cinemas with a total of 101 screens under the capital-light model, most of which are expected to become operational over the next 12 to 24 months.

items.statement: Opened 77 new screens and exited 72 underperforming screens in FY25
items.quote: In line with our focus on profitability growth, we made a strategic decision to exit 72 underperforming screens and opened 77 new screens during the year.

items.statement: Current portfolio: 1,743 screens across 352 cinemas in 111 cities in India and Sri Lanka
items.quote: Our current screen portfolio stands at 1,743 screens across 352 cinemas in 111 cities in India and Sri Lanka.

items.statement: Fixed costs per screen nearly flat at 0.6% YoY; 5-year CAGR of 0.8% vs CPI of 5.3%
items.quote: On a comparable screen basis, total fixed costs were nearly flat at just 0.6% year-on-year growth. In fact, over a 5-year period from FY '20 to FY '25, on a per-screen basis, the company's total fixed cost per screen has increased by a CAGR of only 0.8% as compared to the CPI inflation rate of 5.3% in the economy.

items.statement: Film hire cost reduced to 44.6% in FY25 from normal 45-46% range due to fewer blockbusters and re-releases
items.quote: Our film hire cost is normally in the range of 45% to 46%. However, in financial year '25, it was 44.6% simply because there were no -- the number of movies which crossed INR500 crores plus were lesser. As a result, in our film hire contract, we -- there was a less amount of bonus payouts that happened.

items.statement: Asset-light model margins lower than lease model due to revenue sharing with developers
items.quote: But yes, the margins -- EBITDA margins will be lower versus a classic lease model simply because you need to share something in return of the investment made by the developer.

items.statement: Net debt reduced from INR1,430 crores (Mar 2023) to INR952 crores (Mar 2025), down INR478 crores since merger
items.quote: We're pleased to share that we continue to strengthen our balance sheet with net debt reduced from INR1,430 crores in March 2023 to INR952 crores in March 2025, a significant INR478 crores since the merger.

items.statement: Net debt reduced by INR342 crores in FY25 through security deposit recovery, GST refunds, creditor renegotiation
items.quote: Net debt has reduced by INR 342 crores in year ending 31st Mar'25

items.statement: Target negligible net debt over next 2-3 years; dividends/buybacks only after deleveraging
items.quote: We would ideally want to come down to a negligible net debt level over the course of medium term, over the course of next 2 to 3 years. So that's our priority number one. And once we have achieved that goal, then the Board will decide on dividends and other alternatives uses of cash.

items.statement: FY25 footfalls: 136.9 million; Q4 FY25: 30.5 million
items.quote: We welcomed 30.5 million guests across our cinemas in Q4 FY '25 and 136.9 million guests in FY '25.

items.statement: Hindi box office down 26% in FY25 due to 14% fewer releases, no major superstar films, postponements
items.quote: Hindi box office dropped by 26% this year due to 14% fewer releases, no major superstar films and several postponements.

items.statement: Hindi dubbed collections surged 150%+ with Pushpa 2, Kalki; Chhaava biggest Q4 hit at ~INR700 crores
items.quote: On the other hand, Hindi dubbed collections surged by over 150% with titles like Pushpa 2 and Kalki resonating nationwide showing how audience tastes are shifting towards big pan India stories. Chhaava was the biggest hit of the fourth quarter grossing aro und INR700 crores at the box office

items.statement: Strong FY26 Hindi pipeline: Sitaare Zameen Par, War 2, Housefull 5, Jolly LLB 3, Delhi Files, Thama, Alpha
items.quote: The year ahead looks very exciting with potential Bollywood tent poles like Sitaare Zameen Par, War 2, Housefull 5 , Jolly LLB 3, Delhi Files, Thama, Alpha among others.

items.statement: Hollywood outlook extremely buoyant for FY26 with Mission Impossible 8, Fantastic 4, Superman, Jurassic World, Avatar 3
items.quote: This would be a strong year for Hollywood. And if you look at the advance that we've had for Mission Impossible 8, which is coming out on 17th May, that's an indicator of things to come. Fortunately, we have a lot of sequels, films from big franchises, Marvel has -Marvel has just delivered Thunderbolts, did really well.

items.statement: ATP maintained at INR259 in FY25 despite value promotions (Cinema Lovers Days at INR99, Blockbuster Tuesdays at INR99/149)
items.quote: Despite content challenges, we balanced value promotions with strategic pricing on big releases, maintaining a steady ATP of INR259 same as previous year.

items.statement: Re-releases contributed 7.1 million incremental footfalls and ~INR124 crores gross ticket collections in FY25
items.quote: Our strategic focus on curating rereleases delivered strong results, contributing an incremental 7.1 million footfalls and approximately INR124 crores in gross ticket collections during the year.

items.statement: 5% of FY25 admissions from re-releases which have lower film hire charges
items.quote: Also, we did a lot of re -releases during the year. 5% of the admissions during last year came from rerelease and rereleases typically have lower film hire charges as compared to a fresh film.

items.statement: Theatrical window at 8 weeks and increasing; Aamir Khan's Sitaare Zameen Par not releasing on OTT at all
items.quote: Well, you see the window is 8 weeks just now, a nd it is only going to increase. If you look at the recent announcement by even Aamir Khan's new movie, Sitaare Zameen Par, in fact, he's not releasing it on OTT at

items.statement: Significant cash buildup in Q4 from expedited receivables collection and ticket aggregator advances on convenience fee
items.quote: A lot of work has been done in terms of expediting collections across all our receivables. There's been a lot of work around working with the ticket aggregators in terms of advances on convenience fee. And as a result, quarter 4, we saw a significant buildup of cash.

items.statement: Karnataka movie price cap at INR200 not implemented, currently in abeyance
items.quote: So as of now, this has not basically been implemented by the government. So as of now, it is in abeyance. So until such time the matter comes up, there's no -- there's no need of any analysis to be done on that count.

items.statement: Q1 FY26 India box office tracking similar to global ~7% higher than same period last year
items.quote: In India, if you look at the first quarter year till date, similar numbers.

items.statement: Content volatility risk: gaps in release slate cause box office fluctuations; mitigated by re-releases and pricing initiatives
items.quote: Box office in FY '25 witnessed an uneven release slate across quarters, resulting in noticeable gaps in content flow and fluctuations in theatrical performance.

items.statement: FY26 operating revenue guidance of Rs 6,355 cr for PG Electroplast (30% YoY) and Rs 855 cr for Goodworth JV (57% YoY), implying group revenue of Rs 7,200 cr (33% YoY)
items.quote: For FY26 our operating revenue guidance stands at Rs. 6,355 crores in PG Electroplast which is a 30% growth over FY25 numbers and at Rs. 855 crores in our JV Company Goodworth Electronics which is a 57% growth over FY25 numbers. This implies an operating revenue of Rs. 7,200 crores at a group level which is a growth of around 33% over our FY25 numbers.

items.statement: FY26 net profit guidance of Rs 405 cr for PG Electroplast (39% YoY growth)
items.quote: We are also guiding for a net profit of Rs. 405 crores in PG Electroplast which is a growth of 39% over FY25 net profit of Rs. 291 crores.

items.statement: FY26 product business revenue growth guidance of 35% from Rs 3,526 cr to Rs 4,770 cr
items.quote: The growth in product business is expected to be around 35% from Rs. 3,526 crores to Rs. 4,770 crores in FY26.

items.statement: FY26 capex guidance of Rs 800-900 cr including refrigerator plant (Rs 300 cr), washing machine plant (Rs 90 cr), RAC expansion (Rs 200-250 cr incl. compressor), and land/building across four locations
items.quote: The CAPEX guidance for FY26 is in the range of Rs. 800 to 900 crores. The Company has planned to further expand the RAC capacity with a new Greenfield plant in Bhiwadi. Also, a new Greenfield facility is being planned in Greater Noida for washing machines. The Company is on the verge of finalizing a land parcel for its refrigerator plant in South India.

items.statement: Over next 2 years, gross block to nearly double from ~Rs 1,200 cr to ~Rs 2,200 cr with ~Rs 600 cr for land/building across four Greenfield sites
items.quote: Over the next 2 years almost Rs. (+600) crores is going to be in land and building.

items.statement: New Greenfield plants planned: RAC in Bhiwadi, washing machines in Greater Noida, refrigerator in South India; SUPA facilities expansion for RAC; compressor plant building construction started, targeting Q4 FY26 commercialization
items.quote: The Company has planned to further expand the RAC capacity with a new Greenfield plant in Bhiwadi. Also, a new Greenfield facility is being planned in Greater Noida for washing machines. The Company is on the verge of finalizing a land parcel for its refrigerator plant in South India. The SUPA facilities will be expanded further with a new building and further capacity enhancement for the RAC busi

items.statement: Compressor plant building construction started, contract finalization underway, targeting Q4 FY26 commercialization; majority for captive use, margin accretive
items.quote: The building is already being made, and the contract is on the verge of finalization right now.

items.statement: Order book and visibility for product business remains robust; on track to grow product business significantly in FY26; new product offerings in washing machines and room ACs received good response
items.quote: Order book and visibility for the product business remains robust and the Company is on track to grow the product business significantly again in FY26. Our new product offerings in washing machines and room ACs have received a very good response, and the Company continues to see increased interest in its product offerings from new and existing clients and we remain very confident in the future gro

items.statement: EBITDA margins expected to remain flattish in FY26; sustainable margins maintained; PLI incentive of Rs 37.5 cr included in guidance
items.quote: I think you can assume them to be remaining flattish this year. We think the sustainable margins that we have are sustainable.

items.statement: Goodworth JV: FY25 revenue Rs 544 cr with small loss, EBITDA ~1%; FY26 budgeting 1.5-2% EBITDA margin, expecting profitability; ~2% sustainable EBITDA margin
items.quote: Coming to Goodworth this year we did Rs. 544 crores turnover and we had a small loss there. At EBITDA level though we profit about 1% margin, next year we hope to improve that. We are budgeting in about 1.5% to 2% kind of the EBITDA margin in that business and you can assume that next year we should see some profitability.

items.statement: Plastic division value growth targeted at 5-10% due to falling petroleum prices passed through to clients; volume growth good but ASPs dropping
items.quote: Basically, the issue is petroleum prices are on a lower trend right now. And all plastic businesses the prices are driven by a petroleum crude price. So, we are seeing that the drop in the raw material prices and this business being a straight passed to business to our clients. So, what we see the ASPs will drop, overall volume growth will be good but at a value level growth we are targeting aroun

items.statement: Government allowed compressor imports until 15 April 2026, resolving BIS-related availability issue for one year; compressor plant to come online by then
