items.quote: Government of India has recently issued a notification where they have allowed the import of compressors for one more year. So, you can import compressors up to the 15 th April 2026. So, compressor availability which was seeming to be an issue till two or three weeks back is largely resolved for at least one year

items.statement: High inventory (~Rs 1,300 cr) due to strategic compressor stocking amid BIS uncertainty; expected to normalize in April-June quarter; GST credits and capital advances also elevated other current assets
items.quote: Yes, so if you look at our cash flow this year, basically we are carrying a very large amount of inventory and we had a close to about Rs. 1,300 crores of inventory closing inventory at the end of the quarter.

items.statement: No fund raise planned; capex funded from internal accruals and cash on balance sheet
items.quote: This will be funded largely by the operating by the cash that we have on the balance sheet today.

items.statement: Board approved final dividend of Rs 0.25 per share (25 paisa)
items.quote: Also, our Board of directors today have approved the final dividend of Rs. 0.25, that is 25 paisa per share.

items.statement: PLI incentive: Rs 30 cr booked in Q4 FY25 for FY24 (cash basis); Rs 37.5 cr accrued for FY25 to be booked in FY26; state incentive Rs 6 cr/year
items.quote: Rs. 31.5 crores. Rs. 30 crores is a PLI and Rs. 1.5 crores is the state government incentive which we have booked.

items.statement: Net fixed asset turnover crossed 5x in FY25; targeting 4-4.5x sustainable; aiming to sustain as new capex commissioned
items.quote: Our net fixed asset turn has crossed 5 this year and we hope to sustain that in coming years as our CAPEX get commissioned and we are able to fully sweat them.

items.statement: FY25: Operating revenue Rs 4,869 cr (+77% YoY), product business Rs 3,525 cr (+111% YoY, 72.4% of revenue), room AC Rs 3,009 cr (+128% YoY), washing machine +43% YoY, air cooler +80% YoY
items.quote: For this financial year our operating revenues for the Company has grown by 77% and crossed Rs. 4,869 crores with the product business contributing around 72.4% of the total operating revenue.

items.statement: FY25 EBITDA Rs 519 cr (+81% YoY), net profit Rs 291 cr (+112% YoY); Q4 FY25 revenue Rs 1,910 cr (+77%), EBITDA Rs 232 cr (+93%), net profit Rs 146.4 cr (+105%)
items.quote: EBITDA increased by 81% and stood at Rs. 519 crores and net profit rose by 112% to Rs. 291 crores.

items.statement: Serving 35+ brands, diversifying risk; outsourcing trend reversing in favor of EMS players; working with e-commerce/modern retail brands gaining share
items.quote: We are servicing more than 35 brands. And also, you have to understand, there are multiple drivers in our business. It's not only the industry growth; it is also how much outsourcing is happening versus how much insourcing is happening.

items.statement: PLI enabled scale; new entrants face high barriers; established players with scale have leadership position; outsourcing economics favor EMS given seasonality and BEE rating changes
items.quote: Now obviously the companies which have been able to take advantage of the PLI and grow and make, scale up their business will surely have a leadership position in the segment. And as you know the scale itself becomes a good competitive edge if it can be rightly harnessed by leveraging your strengths of customer relationships, sourcing relationship and doing the right product development.

items.statement: Refrigerator plant to produce both DC and FF categories; developing front-load washing machine platforms; EV assembly pending client government clearances (3-4 months to set up, low margin high asset turn initially)
items.quote: The capacity what we are putting up will be capable of making both DC and FF category of refrigerator. And the supplies and the production will happen as per the customer demands.

items.statement: Demand uncertainty from early monsoon/rains in South; channel inventory concerns for some brands; but company confident due to diversified brand portfolio and outsourcing tailwinds
items.quote: April has been a good month for us. We were on track of our budgeted numbers; In May also we have not seen any significant cancellation as of yet. June, month we will see, we will watch out how things pan out. But from whatever kind of inputs we have, we think at our end we have yet to see some very significant impact.

items.statement: R&D spend ~0.5-0.75% of turnover; team significantly augmented; products becoming industry benchmarks; some innovations copied by brands
items.quote: Right now, that number on an overall basis including maybe whatever expenditure we are doing on other than manpower maybe just about 0.5% to 0.75% of our turnover but it is likely to see increase in terms of absolute amount.

items.statement: Management anticipates another record year for Triveni Turbines in FY26.
items.quote: But needless to say, that we are anticipating another record year for the Triveni Turbines in FY 26.

items.statement: FY25 order booking grew 26% YoY to ₹23.63 billion, a record high.
items.quote: We are very proud that we have had the highest ever annual order booking of ₹23.63 billion during FY 25, an increase of 26% y-o-y.

items.statement: Closing order book as of March 31, 2025 stood at a record ₹19.09 billion, up 23% YoY.
items.quote: And has this left us with a record outstanding carry-forward order book as of the 31 st of March 2025 of ₹19.09 billion, an increase of 23% y-o-y.

items.statement: FY25 EBITDA margin expanded 280 bps YoY to 25.8% driven by higher aftermarket and export mix.
items.quote: We had the highest ever EBITDA of ₹5.18 billion, up 36% year-on-year with a margin of 25.8%, which is an increase of 280 basis points (bps) year-over-year (y-o-y).

items.statement: FY26 capex forecast is ₹1.65 billion including ₹0.44 billion carry-forward from FY25.
items.quote: The total capex forecast for this current year, FY 26 is about ₹1.65 billion, which includes a carry -forward of about ₹0.44 billion from the previous financial year which is FY 25.

items.statement: Operating on two-shift basis; adding a new bay at Sompura facility to augment assembly and testing capacity.
items.quote: We are currently operating on a two-shift basis, and we don't see capacity as a real constraint. We are adding a bay, which is more from an assembly perspective and some manufacturing capacity, which is part of our capex plan for the current year.

items.statement: Domestic market declined ~10% in FY25; order finalisation timelines elongated due to uncertainty.
items.quote: While the enquiry book is extremely robust, the market in India has declined as we calculated for FY 25 by 10%.

items.statement: International enquiry book grew over 30% and domestic enquiry book grew 120% in FY25.
items.quote: In FY 25, the international enquiry book has grown by over 30%, while the domestic enquiry book has grown by an even more impressive 120%.

items.statement: Product order booking grew 38% to ₹17.41 billion; API, renewables, industrial power and CO2 storage drove growth.
items.quote: The product order booking has grown by an impressive 38% to ₹17.41 billion in FY 25. The key drivers for growth in product order booking were the finalisation of orders in the renewabl e energy sector, industrial clients for industrial power generation and power producers and API turbines.

items.statement: Aftermarket revenue share ~33% of sales; expected to rise ~1% annually driven by refurbishment growth.
items.quote: We're quite happy with the 33 %-odd aftermarket as a percentage of sales. Yes, we'd expect it to rise by 1% odd every year consistently so that it's contributing more.

items.statement: Secured ₹2.90 billion CO2 energy storage order from NTPC Kudgi with Energy Dome; scope >50% value addition.
items.quote: We also continue to develop new and innovative solutions, utili sing carbon -dioxide as a means for fluid transmission, which includes an order, which we have received along with our Italian partner Energy Dome, with NTPC, which is a ₹290 crore (₹2.90 billion) order for 160-MW hour long-duration energy storage project at NTPC's Kudgi Supercritical Thermal Power Plant.

items.statement: API market highly competitive with global OEMs; Triveni differentiated by quick backend support and technical acceptability.
items.quote: API market wise, as we got ourselves approved in all the refineries, majority of the reputed refineries, the pipeline is building up. At the same time, these are very, very competitive market, and we are fighting with all the competition across the globe in different territories.

items.statement: India-UK FTA neutral for business as turbine imports already at zero duty; benefit depends on UK capex demand.
items.quote: Most of these FTAs are neutral to us because our product is not heavily taxed as a dutiable item, both ways. Imports into the country are pretty much at zero duty anyway.

items.statement: Receivables and other current assets spiked in March due to back-ended dispatches; largely reversed in April-May.
items.quote: In the quarter ending Q4 FY 25, we had certain back ending of orders, which happened in the month of March, which you'll see from a balance sheet where we have higher receivables as well as certain other current assets. Both of these are short term in nature and would have already been reversed to a significant extent in the month of April to return to a low receivable metric.

items.statement: Board recommended final dividend of 200% (₹2/share) plus interim dividend of 200% (₹2/share) for FY25.
items.quote: The Board has also recommended payment of final dividend of 200%, which is ₹2 per equity share for the financial year FY 24-25, which is subject to the approval of our shareholders. But this is in addition to the interim dividend of 200%, which is also ₹2 per equity share of ₹1 each.

items.statement: US subsidiary team to expand to almost twice first-year size in years 2-3; backend supported from India for cost efficiency.
items.quote: We are looking at expanding it to almost twice the size that we had in the first year, in the second and third year.

items.statement: Elongation of domestic order finalisation timelines due to macro uncertainty; unclear if one-quarter or multi-quarter issue.
items.quote: So I think what you could say right now is that there has been an elongation of order finalisation timelines. And that is something that is a concern, but we'll have to wait and see if this is something that is a one quarter thing or something that continues for multiple quarters.

items.statement: Removed ₹1.40 billion of slow-moving orders from order book in Q4; advances held so expected to return medium-term.
items.quote: We've cleaned up our order booking by taking out approximately ₹140 crore (₹1.40 billion) from our order book of slow moving orders, which we have advances of. And we're confident because we have advances that these will come back in the medium term.

name: Multi Commodity Exchange of India Ltd

items.statement: FY25 consolidated income INR 1,208 crores, up 59% YoY
items.quote: Very happy to announce that we've had a phenomenal year, closing the year at INR1,208 crores of consolidated income, which is 59% year -on-year growth.

items.statement: FY25 EBITDA INR 761.5 crores, up 63% YoY; PAT INR 560 crores at 46% margin
items.quote: EBITDA for the year closed at INR 761.5 crores at 63% and profit after tax is INR 560 crores at a 46% margin.

items.statement: FY25 average daily throughput (futures + options) nearly doubled to INR 2.2 trillion from INR 1 trillion
items.quote: the ADT that is average daily throughput of both futures and options together nearly doubling at 101%, touching INR 2.2 trillion from INR 1 trillion.

items.statement: FY25 options premium ADT grew ~85% YoY
items.quote: the premium ADT of options, which have also grown by about 85% so those are really the drivers

items.statement: FY25 deliveries: 7 MT gold, 663 MT silver, ~70,000 MT base metals
items.quote: We've really seen about 7 metric ton of gold, 663 metric ton of silver, and more than -- or close to 70,000 metric ton of base metals delivered through the exchange mechanism.

items.statement: Record commodity futures turnover INR 71,500 crores on 4 April 2025 post tariff announcement
items.quote: We've also had record turnover of -- in our commodity futures on the back of the tariff announcement. This, of course, happened on the 4th of April, so just after the close of the year, but at INR 71,500 crores has been a big high

items.statement: Traded clients grew 39% YoY to 13 lakh; 140 FPIs onboarded
items.quote: We've had a 39% growth year-on-year with -- of traded clients touching 13 lakhs and participation across all categories of commercial participants, retail participants as well a s financial institutions. In fact, we have about 140 FPIs who have been onboarded on MCX

items.statement: Gold 10g futures launched 1 April 2025, strong offtake in first month
items.quote: we did have a good launch of our Gold Ten futures, that is actually in this year because it happened on the 1st of April, it was time d to kind of match with Akshaya Tritiya and has given us some very, very good response in the first month itself

items.statement: Silver micro options (30kg, 5kg, 1kg) planned for launch in shorter time frame
items.quote: we are looking at launching in silver, micro option s, the 30 kg, 5 kg and the 1 kg. So these are all in play. And these would also be in the shorter time frame

items.statement: Index options (BULLDEX, METLDEX) and electricity futures ready, awaiting regulatory approval
items.quote: we have full readiness from our side, and we are waiting for the right green signal to take this to market. So we believe that between our indices and new products such as electricity, we will really look at significant growth in the coming time.

items.statement: Depreciation to continue at current levels due to regulatory changes, network expansion, tech refresh and BAU
items.quote: We do expect capitalization to sort of depreciation and amortization to continue at these levels because as we are growing significantly, and I think we just discussed that we are looking at -- we have doubled our volumes. And obviously, the tech refresh is a continuous process that would need to be there.

items.statement: FY26 expense ratios expected to stay flat; no specific capex number disclosed
items.quote: We won't be able to call out a specific number, but I can tell you, overall, at an expense level, we expect our ratios to stay flat.

items.statement: Q4 employee cost delta: 75% one-time performance payout, 25% capacity building
items.quote: if I were to look at the employee expenses, I would cut it at about 75%-25% in terms of the delta with 75% going into a one -time incremental expense associated with performance and 25% is really the readiness from a capacity building standpoint

items.statement: FY26 tech cost seen around INR 90-110 cr, employee cost INR 150-160 cr (full-year basis)
items.quote: the numbers would be around these levels

items.statement: No regulatory approval for co-location yet; will not comment until clarity
items.quote: We will not be able to comment on this at this stage because it's really based on what media is saying. Until we have regulatory clarity, we won't be able to comment on this.

items.statement: Clearing corporation segregation consultation applies to equity exchanges; not expected for commodity clearing corporation soon
items.quote: as it stands, this implication is there for the equity exchanges. So at this stage, the Commodity Clearing Corporation has a lot more complexity involved and handles warehouses and d eliveries and so on and so forth. So we are not really expecting this any time now

items.statement: FPI participation limited to crude oil and natural gas; 140 FPIs onboarded, early days
items.quote: Now we also have to bear in mind that FPIs are only allowed to trad e in crude oil and natural gas. So as and when more and more products come under the ambit and more and more FPIs come into the market, we will see more participation increasing

items.statement: DII participation limited due to mutual fund restrictions; working with industry to expand
items.quote: our DII portfolio is fairly limited at this point, primarily because there are a number of restrictions in -- for mutual funds and so on to participate in commodity derivatives. But there are some changes to that, that we are working with the industry to understand the needs of the industry

items.statement: Geopolitical volatility (e.g., Trump tariffs) creates spikes; baseline participation expected to rise post events
items.quote: the baseline, we see both experience with an event goes on to create the exposure and experience needed. Hopefully at the end of an event, there is a higher participation than at the beginning of the event. So yes, the baseline goes up.

items.statement: Q4 FY25 option revenue INR 179 cr, futures revenue INR 75 cr
items.quote: The option revenue for this quarter is INR 179 crores and futures revenue is INR 75 crores.

items.statement: Q4 FY25 FPI turnover ~INR 16,500 cr options, INR 600 cr futures (~7% of total)
items.quote: it is roughly around INR 16,500 crores in options, and it is about INR 600 crores in futures. So you can say about 7% of the total turnover.

items.statement: Base metal volumes nearly doubled in FY25; transition to India pricing/deliverable contracts ongoing
items.quote: In terms of growth in base metals in the year which we have ended, we've seen almost a doubling of volumes in the base metal contracts as well.

items.statement: Expect a good year ahead; expense ratios to stay flat
items.quote: We expect to have a good year ahead, and we'll stay in touch.

items.statement: Target to cross Rs 800 Cr quarterly revenue in next four quarters
items.quote: our target now is to move to 800. So, in the next four quarters, we should be crossing 800.

items.statement: Long-term EBITDA margin target of 30%
items.quote: definitely the margin may inch towards 27-30% depending upon how the license works and how the Purple Fabric comes.

items.statement: Capex investment around $20 million and Rs 160-170 Cr capitalised product capex for FY26
items.quote: Capex investment on capitalisation will be around same as last year, we aimed for 140. This year should see the same figure, 20 million dollars. Therefore, 20 million dollars will be my Capex investment, while Rs.160-170 Cr will be my Capex investment on the product side, which will be capitalised.

items.statement: Seeing shift from traditional digital transformation to AI-driven transformation deals
items.quote: There's a big trend on AI, plus eMACH.ai. So, the complete deals are there eMACH.ai deals and the AI deals.

items.statement: Purple Fabric demand expanding from insurance to lending, payments, trade and supply chain finance
items.quote: It's gone into lending, payments, and it's getting into trade and supply chain finance.

items.statement: 43 new customer wins and 53 digital go-lives in FY25
items.quote: we ended the year with 43 new customer wins and 53 successful digital go-lives

items.statement: 9 new logos and 16 go-lives in Q4 FY25 across geographies
items.quote: Just in Q4, we on boarded nine new logos and executed 16 go-lives across geographies from Africa and Asia to the Middle East, the UK, and Europe.

items.statement: Rs 200 Cr landmark AI transformation deal with London market brokerage firm over 3 years
items.quote: This is a 200-Cr engagement, which is one of the earliest real-world implementations of our new platform, Purple Fabric

items.statement: Multi-country wholesale banking deal with European global bank for eMACH.ai treasury and transaction banking
items.quote: a multi-country wholesale banking deal with a European headquartered global bank that selected eMACH.ai to drive composable transformation across its treasury and transaction banking businesses

items.statement: Purple Fabric funnel component at 10-15% and growing
items.quote: As of now, the funnel has a 10 to 15% component from Purple Fabric. More components are getting built up

items.statement: Purple Fabric ARR target of Rs 1,000 Cr in next three years with pipeline built
items.quote: We are quite sure of Rs.1,000 Cr. We are now in the last 4-5 months, we built up the entire use cases or business cases to make it Rs.1,000 Cr business in for next three years for Purple Fabric.

items.statement: Q4 FY25 EBITDA margin at 30%, annualised at 23%
items.quote: We delivered a healthy EBITDA of Rs.227 Crores for the quarter, representing an EBITDA margin of 30%.

items.statement: License-linked revenue target 60% in 2-3 years from current 50%, driving 10 percentage point margin improvement
items.quote: Ideally, our target is to make it 60% in the next 2-3 years. If my License Linked Revenue at 60%, obviously, the margin will increase by 10 percentage points.

items.statement: Three horizon margin model: Horizon 1 at 30-35%, Horizon 2 at 20-25%, Horizon 3 at 5-10%
items.quote: Horizon 1 becomes a 30% to 35% margin business, Horizon 2 develops into a 20% to 25% margin business, and Horizon 3, which is the investment business, will operate at a 5% to 10% margin.

items.statement: Geographic revenue split: 45% from US/Canada/Europe, 55% evenly across India, IMEA, APAC
items.quote: my US, North America, and Europe segments account for about 45% of total revenue, coming from the US, North America, Canada, and Europe. While the remaining 55% is evenly distributed equally among India, IMEA, and APAC.

items.statement: Central1 acquisition added 171 Canadian banking customers (one-third of market), profitable in first month
items.quote: Sometimes you miss those 171 banking customers in the Canadian market; these 171 is one-third of the banking market over there, where we can cross-sell lending and core banking. So, that is the misinterpreted signal. Even though we started operating Central1 on the 1st of March, we only had one month of revenue, and it was

items.statement: Investing Rs 40 Cr per annum to build Direct-to-Corporate capacity (iGPX, iCPX, iAPX products)
items.quote: We are investing close to Rs. 40 Cr per annum to build the capacity, which the GeM team has developed, creating three products using my eMACH.ai architecture in less than 12 months.

items.statement: Sales force of 100+ selling Purple Fabric alongside existing portfolio; Europe sales force in place, Americas building up
items.quote: Today it's an integrated sales force. Because the sales force is not separate from Purple Fabric but as all the sales force which is more than 100 plus sales force is selling Purple Fabric along with their current portfolio.

items.statement: AI augmenting employee capability, not replacing headcount; productivity gains absorbed salary hikes keeping cost base flat
items.quote: AI doesn't give only productivity. It gives you accuracy and better success chances. So, first of all I want to clarify the role of AI is to augment the capability of the manager in the company, not replacing him.

items.statement: Annual recurring revenue (ARR) at Rs 870 Cr based on Q4 run-rate, increased ~Rs 175 Cr quarter-on-quarter
items.quote: Our annual recurring revenue based on Q4 run rate stood at Rs.870 Crores

items.statement: 68 digital experts built on Purple Fabric Enterprise Knowledge Garden
items.quote: We have got about 68 digital experts available already

items.statement: Not accepting outcome-based revenue models due to risk; will consider later
items.quote: We are not accepting this. We don't want to take that risk right now. We will do it later.

items.statement: Purple Fabric has 18+ AI guardrails for explainability, fairness, auditability, security and entitlements
items.quote: We have embedded 18+ AI guardrails, ensuring explainability, fairness, and auditability of both data and decisions, apart from enforcing security and entitlements at the level of roles, workspaces, and tenants.

items.statement: Revenue growth guidance of 30% CAGR sustained for 10 years; Q4 FY25 revenue grew 30% YoY surpassing guidance
items.quote: For the full year, we have achieved the resounding 30% revenue growth, continuing our consistent track record of maintaining a 30% CAGR revenue growth for the past 10 years.

items.statement: Store expansion guidance of 25-30 stores annually with focus on Uttar Pradesh; may increase guidance later
items.quote: We plan to add 25-30 stores annually with a sharp focus on expanding our presence in Uttar Pradesh, where we see significant potential.

items.statement: EBITDA margin guidance maintained at 8-10% range despite new store openings impacting Q4 margins
items.quote: We think that for the quarter it has come down by slightly more, but please do understand that most of our, in fact, around about I will tell you the exact figure, 14 out of 30 stores that has been opened in Q4.

items.statement: Average store size increased to 4,500 sq ft from 4,000 sq ft; new stores in UP averaging 5,500 sq ft driving higher capex and working capital needs
items.quote: So in fact what you said that the biggest contributor is that we are opening larger format stores. So stores have now, average store size has become 4500, which was 4000 previously.

items.statement: Opened 30 stores in FY25 reaching 175 total stores; 112 in Bihar, 29 in Jharkhand, 34 in UP across 20 districts including 6 in Lucknow
items.quote: We opened 30 stores in FY '25 where most of our new stores came in Uttar Pradesh. With that, we have now reached a total of 175 stores.

items.statement: UP store potential estimated at 200 stores in 2-3 years, double the Bihar count of 112 stores
items.quote: If Bihar can accommodate 112 stores, Vijay, so we can fairly well assume that in next, let us say, 2-3 years then we can have 200 stores in UP.

items.statement: Q4 FY25 saw 30% revenue growth with strong rebound in Feb-Mar after Jan slowdown; early summer onset supported momentum
items.quote: While January saw a brief slowdown, February and March witnessed a sharp rebound with strong consumer demand driving remarkable growth.

items.statement: April 2025 demand slow due to unseasonal rains but company still growing in single digits; bullish on second half of May and June
items.quote: I have already told that demand has been slow, but despite that Aditya Vision is in growth, our company and we are seeing that, yes, this thing happens once in a while.

items.statement: FY25 EBITDA margin maintained at 9% despite 30% revenue growth; Q4 FY25 EBITDA margin 8.7% impacted by 50% new stores opening in Q4
items.quote: In this fast growth period also, we maintained EBITDA margins at 9%.

items.statement: Gross margin declined 22 bps for FY25; Q4 gross margin 17% vs 17.5% YoY due to new store operating costs
items.quote: Actually, we believe in a basket way of gross margins and gross margin in this Financial Year has gone down by 22 bps.

items.statement: Inventory peaked at Rs 698 cr at March end due to proactive compressor stocking; average FY25 inventory Rs 494 cr; expected to liquidate quickly in Q1
items.quote: Consequently, our inventory peaked at Rs. 698 crores as of March end. However, when viewed across the year, the average inventory level for FY '25 stood at less than Rs. 500 crores.

items.statement: Negative cash flow in Q4 due to strategic inventory buildup; historically turns positive after summer season liquidation; payable days kept low for upfront discounts
items.quote: This strategic buildup of inventory ahead of busy season resulted into negative cash flow, which historically gets into positive territory at the end of the summer season.

items.statement: Payables increased Rs 90 cr due to IGST purchases and transit time for goods; not a structural change from cash-and-carry model
items.quote: So most of the products we are in fact buying from manufacturers on IGST basis, so these products are built from the company and it takes some time to reach our stores.

items.statement: Same-store sales growth (SSSG) 19% in Q4 FY25 and 15% for full FY25 reflecting core market strength
items.quote: Our same-store sales growth stood at 19% for Q4 FY '25 and 15% for the entire full year, reflecting continued strength in core markets.

items.statement: Room AC contributes 45-50% of Q1 revenue; April typically 25% of quarter sales with peak in May-June
items.quote: It is about around 45%-50%.

items.statement: Revenue mix: Bihar 80% (77% in Q4), Jharkhand 12% (13% in Q4), UP 8% (10% in Q4) for FY25
items.quote: For the full year, FY '25, Bihar accounted for 80% of our total revenue, with Jharkhand and Uttar Pradesh contributing 12% and 8% respectively.

items.statement: Compressor supply uncertainty due to government restrictions and US tariff diversion from China drove proactive inventory buildup
items.quote: There were restrictions from government and the tariff position was also being discussed, so many, in fact export were diverted to USA from China.

items.statement: Focus on compressor products (ACs, refrigerators) for summer season; larger format stores enable better assortment and customer experience
items.quote: As far as categories are concerned in fact, right now, we are focusing on compressor products in this quarter.

items.statement: UP store throughput per store similar to Jharkhand; larger format stores to match competitive experience in high-density areas
items.quote: It is almost similar. It is not very significantly different.

items.statement: Unseasonal rains delayed summer demand in April; compressor supply chain uncertainty due to geopolitical factors
items.quote: There has been unseasonal rain so far, but market has been slow. But despite that we are in growth and major part of the quarter is still around there.

items.statement: Staff costs increased materially in Q4 due to 50% of new stores (14 of 30) opening in Q4 bringing operating costs forward
items.quote: As I told you just now that almost 50% of our store addition was in Q4. So obviously operating cost, employee cost, all the costs were coming in quarter 4.

items.statement: Management expects raw material prices to remain stabilized in coming quarters as global supply conditions improve
items.quote: While these pressures impacted our margins, we hope raw material prices will remain stabilized in the coming quarters as global supply conditions improve.

items.statement: JNPA SEZ facility capex estimated at INR700-750 crores over 18-24 months
items.quote: That we had already told earlier that it is around total INR750 crores, but it will happen stage -wise as we go along.

items.statement: INR110 crores spent on JNPA land procurement in FY25
items.quote: out of which the main portion belongs to our JNPA, the land procurement, around INR110 crores.

items.statement: U.S. manufacturing facility Phase 1 equity infusion of INR45 crores for initial procedures and land
items.quote: It is only for the initial equity to start with the procedures and to do certain things.

items.statement: JNPA SEZ facility construction to commence soon, completion in 18-24 months, production in phased manner
items.quote: As previously mentioned, construction will commence soon and is expected to be completed within 18 to 24 months. Commencement of production will happen in a phased manner once operational.

items.statement: Badlapur unit resumed full operations in Q3 FY25 after fire incident shutdown
items.quote: We resumed full operations at our Badlapur manufacturing unit in Q3 FY '25.

items.statement: Patalganga plant (E-73) expected to reach full capacity by March FY26 or H1 FY27
items.quote: And that plant is also now getting full. And I think by March FY '26 or latest by first half of '27, this is also going to get full.

items.statement: U.S. plant Phase 1 capacity conservative, existing customers ensure quick fill-up
items.quote: when we are going for U.S. plant, we will go with a very conservative capacity to start with, because we already have a very good existing market over there.

items.statement: Domestic demand strong across all product segments, export momentum renewed across global markets
items.quote: Demand in the domestic market remains strong across all our product segments. On the export front, we saw renewed momentum across global markets.

items.statement: EBITDA margin 22.6% in FY25, down from prior year due to raw material, logistics, utility cost pressures
items.quote: The EBITDA margins for FY '25 stood at 22.6%.

items.statement: Raw material prices rose notably from Q2 FY25 through Q4 FY25 due to global supply chain imbalances
items.quote: Raw material prices saw a notable upward trend starting from Q2 FY '25 and continuing through Q4 FY '25.

items.statement: Logistics costs normalized in H2 FY25 after elevated H1 due to shipping bottlenecks
items.quote: Logistic costs, which were significantly elevated in the first half of the year due to the global shipping bottlenecks and supply chain disruptions, began to normalize in the second half.

items.statement: Utility costs rose due to higher per unit energy costs and higher production volumes
items.quote: We also experienced a rise in utility costs during the year. This was primarily driven by increased per unit energy costs and higher production volumes needed to meet sustained demand across both domestic and export markets.

items.statement: Price pass-through on raw material increases done where no long-term contracts; absorbed cost on 1-year contracts
items.quote: Wherever there were no long-term contracts, we passed on. But wherever there were long-term contracts, we had to bear that additional cost.

items.statement: Inventory days elevated by ~13 days due to supply chain disruptions and geopolitical conditions
items.quote: So yes, we have little elevated the inventories both on raw material and certain on finished goods side at a consolidated level, looking at the supply chain disruptions which are posing and certain geopolitical conditions which were arising.

items.statement: Expansions to be funded by mix of internal accruals and debt financing
items.quote: We are open, and we will be taking certain debt. So our project will be funded both with a good amount of mix of internal accruals and the debt financing.

items.statement: Cash balance ~INR1,150-1,200 crores (short-term + long-term FDs) to fund SEZ and U.S. expansions, M&A
items.quote: So that put together with the short -term cash around INR950-odd crores. So total is like INR1,150 crores, INR1,200 crores cash that we have on books?

items.statement: Actively exploring M&A opportunities for complementary products in desirable geographies
items.quote: We are still working on that. So that -- we need to keep some cash for that.

items.statement: JNPA SEZ environmental clearance received, remaining regulatory approvals expected shortly
items.quote: We have obtained environmental clearance, (EC) for the state facility and are in the process of securing remaining approvals from other regulatory authorities, which are expected to be received shortly.

items.statement: Gujarat land acquisition cancelled by government, earnest money refunded
items.quote: You are talking about the Gujarat land, that we have already said that we are not going to get it. Government has told us clearly. We got the refund of that earnest money deposit also.

items.statement: U.S. entity incorporation planned for local manufacturing to reduce lead times, logistics costs, comply with regulations
items.quote: We also intend to incorporate a new entity in the United States. This marks a significant step in our global expansion strategy. The entity will house a full -fledged manufacturing facility, enabling us to strengthen our local presence in the U.S. market.

items.statement: UAE subsidiary incorporation planned for sales office first, manufacturing later
items.quote: In parallel, we are also in process of incorporating a wholly owned subsidiary in the UAE. This step is intended to have our local presence in the Middle East and enhance supply chain efficiencies.

items.statement: Large customers prefer 12-month contracts despite volatility; small raw material share for them
items.quote: See, there are customers, the large customers, irrespective of the situation, they will go for long-term contracts only. Arun bhai, you are aware that our products are used 0.1%, 0.2%. So these are small raw materials for them.

items.statement: Technical edge in certain specialty products vs global majors like Cargill, Emery; 25 years in international markets
items.quote: But there are certain technical products where we have an edge over them. So slowly, we are getting into that. Slowly, the customers are also understanding the superiority of the technology, superiority of the product properties and the performance.

items.statement: Global industry volume growth 5-6% CAGR, India domestic growth 8-10%
items.quote: Globally -- you can say that all products together average 5% to 6% is okay globally. But in India it is a little bit higher, maybe 8% to 10%.

items.statement: U.S. expansion risks: hiring right local talent, regulatory compliance, cultural differences; Phase 1 conservative to learn
items.quote: We are a little bit cautious because we don't have experience of running the plant in U.S. with U.S. regulations and U.S. systems and all that. And we need to appoint the right people to manage the plant, manage the company over there.

items.statement: FY26 NBFC AUM growth expected around 20%
items.quote: So, we expect this year the AUM to grow by around 20% but we would have better visibility as we go down the year, Quarter-on-Quarter.

items.statement: Secured AUM target 75% in next 3-4 years
items.quote: Currently, I think by the end of this year it was about 64% roughly and in the next three to four years our plan is to increase secured AUM to 75% and we are working on that.

items.statement: Expect FY26 better for NBFC AUM growth, portfolio quality and spreads
items.quote: We are also very hopeful and confident about having this year FY’26 to b e much better year for us in terms of the AUM growth as well as the quality of our portfolio and in addition to that, we expect spreads or margins to be better

items.statement: F&O volumes moderated after stricter norms and geopolitical tensions
items.quote: One of the most notable industry-wide developments has been the moderation and derivative trading volumes following the introduction of stricter norms in the F&O segment.

items.statement: Market activity improving with FPI selling stopped and DII buying strong
items.quote: But now even the India Pakistan thing has been sorted out and even FPI have stopped their selling and they are now in positive for last two months and continuously DI buying, SIP of more than Rs. 25,000 crore every month is coming.

items.statement: Q4 FY25 consolidated EBITDA margin 14.9%, FY25 23.6%
items.quote: For Q4 FY '25, operating income stood at Rs. 421.5 crore , operating EBITDA was approximately Rs. 63 crores. EBITDA margin came at 14.9%.

items.statement: Expect NBFC spreads/margins better in FY26 due to higher yields and lower cost of finance
items.quote: we expect spreads or margins to be better because we are working on increasing our yields on our asset book as well as there are certain tailwinds in terms of the cost of finance

items.statement: FY25 consolidated revenue Rs 1,775.7 crore, up 8.4% YoY
items.quote: For the full year Financial Year '2 5 revenue grew by 8.4% YOY to Rs. 1775.7 crore with EBITDA at Rs. 419.4 crore and PAT at Rs. 146.8 crore.

items.statement: Broking DP AUA added Rs 36,413 crore in FY25, up 46%
items.quote: In broking DP AUA, asset under administration , we added Rs. 36,413 crores in our DP AUA during FY'25 marking a 46% growth.

items.statement: Mutual fund AUM rose to Rs 4,178 crore, up 9.9% YoY
items.quote: Mutual fund AUM rose to Rs. 4178 crores up 9.9% YOY.

items.statement: NBFC AUM reached Rs 1,291 crore, up 4.2% YoY
items.quote: NBFC AU M reached Rs. 1,291 crores up by 4.2% YOY.

items.statement: Insurance policies sold crossed 10 lakh in FY25
items.quote: Total in surance policies sold across Rs. 10 lakh mark in FY'25.

items.statement: NBFC GNPA 3.6%, NNPA 2.2% in FY25, up from 2.22% GNPA last year
items.quote: The GNPA, NNPA were 3.6% and 2.2% respectively.

items.statement: GNPA increased to 3.55% from 2.22% last year, large accounts under monitoring
items.quote: you rightly also said the GNPA numbers for us also increased to 3.5 5% as compared to around 2.2 2% last year.

items.statement: Expect GNPA recovery during FY26 as large accounts resolve
items.quote: So, there are certain large accounts which are included in the GNPA and we are closely monitoring the recoveries in those accounts. As and when there is recovery in one or two accounts, we would see the numbers going down.

items.statement: SEBI restricted weekly options to Nifty/Sensex, one expiry per exchange, increased expiry margins
items.quote: under stock broking certain regulatory changes had come under the earlier SEBI chairman regime where the weekly options has been restricted to only NIFTY and SENSEX . Earlier we used to have five, s ix other contracts where weekly options were their and even the expiry has been restricted to only one expiry per exchange.

items.statement: New SEBI chairman seen as friendly, open to review policies
items.quote: with the new Chairman, SEBI seems to be very friendly and is open to review the policies and we feel that it would be positive for the market and certain things would be done.

items.statement: Branch network expanded to 208 from 188 in FY24
items.quote: Branch network expanded to 208 from 188 in FY'24.

items.statement: NBFC active through 41 branches across 9 states
items.quote: In our NBFC operations we are active through 41 branches covering 9 states, steadily expanding our leading footprint.

items.statement: Added over 1 lakh new Demat accounts in FY25
items.quote: Over 1 lakh new Demat accounts were opened.

items.statement: Added 13,930 new SIPs in FY25
items.quote: We added 13,930 new SIP's in FY'25.

items.statement: Wealth advisory AUM raised Rs 948 crore, up 4.4% YoY
items.quote: Wealth advisory AUM raised Rs. 948 crores a 4.4% increase YOY.

items.statement: Geopolitical risk remains a concern, led to visible slowdown in market activity
items.quote: India is still on a strong path, but geopolitical risk remains a concern which has led to a visible slowdown in market activity.

items.statement: Fair value loss of Rs 9.32 crore in Q4 due to mark-to-market on investment portfolio
items.quote: Since markets were down in march quarter, there is some negative balances but as the market improves this will be better in future.

items.statement: NBFC cost of finance tailwinds from interest rate reduction and RBI risk weight revision
items.quote: there are certain tailwinds in terms of the cost of finance which is available for the NBFC s d ue to the reduction in interest rates and revision in RBIs stands on risk weight on bank loan to NBFC.

items.statement: Standalone EBITDA growth guided at 12-15% for FY26 over FY25 base
items.quote: On a standalone basis, we are guiding an EBITDA growth of around 12% to 15% in FY'26 over the higher base of FY '25.

items.statement: CDMO/CMO revenue estimated to grow 30-40% in FY26
items.quote: On the back of strong manufacturing capabilities and sound R&D setup , the CDMO/CMO revenue is estimated to grow around 30% to 40% in FY'26.

items.statement: FY26 capex guided at Rs 400-450 crore, similar to FY25 spend
items.quote: Yes, I think FY'26, overall the CAPEX number is around Rs. 400 to 450 crores total capex that we will end up doing in FY'26.

items.statement: Capex breakup: Atali remainder ~Rs 200 cr, Xanthine expansion ~Rs 100 cr, maintenance and R&D capex
items.quote: Yes, total CAPEX is broken into the remainder of Atali CAPEX, which is almost around Rs. 200 crore remaining there and some CAPEX of Xanthine product around, we have to spend close to Rs. 100 crore plus there and then other maintenance CAPEX and other R&D CAPEX.

items.statement: Xanthine capacity expansion to 9,000 MT progressing, phased commissioning in H2 FY26, full operationalization by Q1 FY27
items.quote: For our Xanthine der ivative business, the capacity expansion to 9 ,000 metric tons is progressing as planned, with phased commissioning estimated in H2 FY'26.

items.statement: Atali greenfield project mechanical completion expected end of current quarter, phased operationalization, full ramp-up by end of FY26
items.quote: The greenfield project at Atali , Gujarat is in final stages of completion. The mechanical completion is expected to finish around the end of this current quarter. It's planned to get operationalized in phases and the full ramp-up is expected by the end of this financial year.

items.statement: Xanthine capacity utilization target 80-90% over next 3 years, 50% sales targeted to beverages and regulated customers
items.quote: The Xanthine capacity of 9000 MT is likely to be operationalized fully by Q1 FY '27. In the next 3 years, we aspire for capacity utilization of 80% -90%, with 50% sales targeted to beverages and regulated customers

items.statement: Atali adding 450 KL capacity, total multipurpose capacity to reach 1,500+ KL post completion
items.quote: Secondly, regarding this 1,100 KL capacity is our overall capacity currently which we have in all the multipurpose plants that we run, whereas we are adding 450 KL additional capacity with Atali.

items.statement: CDMO: 21 customers, 61 active projects (33 commercial, 27 development)
items.quote: The CDMO/CMO segment has contributed 27 % of the turnover in this quarter and we are currently working with 21 customers. The number of active projects is now 61 projects against last quarter's 56, out of which 33 projects are at the commercial stage and 27 are under the different stages of development.

items.statement: ~70-75% of 33 commercial CDMO projects contributed revenue in FY25
items.quote: Yes, that number we will have to work out that exactly how many we have in FY'25. I think we should have worked on at least 75% of the project roughly exact number we will have to double check but roughly 70-75%.

items.statement: FY25 EBITDA margin expanded to 26% in Q4 (from 23% YoY), full year EBITDA Rs 464 cr (+20% YoY)
items.quote: EBITDA for the quarter was Rs. 146 crores, a 24 % increase YoY. EBITDA margins expanded to 26% up from 23% in Q4 FY'24. For the full year FY'25, we achieved an annual EBITDA of Rs. 464 crores growing by 20 % YoY.

items.statement: CDMO gross margins reasonably higher than API and Xanthine; overall EBITDA growth guided 12-15% FY26
items.quote: I don't know from where you are getting this margin data. I don't know what numbers you have because whatever I stated is that the CDMO overall gross margins are reasonably higher than the API and the other two businesses.

items.statement: Xanthine derivative prices stable, have bottomed out; pharma grade realization ~20% higher than consumer grade
items.quote: Overall, the Xanthine derivative prices are stabl e. Of course , they are low but stable and we understand that the prices have bottomed out.

items.statement: Corticosteroid product range stable, limited quantities make source switching difficult for customers
items.quote: The corticosteroid product range is very stable. There could be some pricing correction, but however, these products go in very limited quantities, so it is very difficult for our customers to change the source also.

items.statement: API & Intermediate: 52% regulated markets, 38% RoW, 10% non-regulated in Q4
items.quote: The sub -segment-wise breakup is 52 % in the regulated market, 38% in RoW, and 10% non-regulated market, which aligns with our long-term focus towards the regulated market.

items.statement: Xanthine: 54% beverage volume, rest pharmaceutical/unallocated in FY25
items.quote: We have given the breakup this time that how much we have done with the beverages. I think we have done around 54 % of our total volume and other is all pharmaceutical and unallocatable volume.

items.statement: CDMO: 75-80% sales from Phase-III/commercialized products, rest from early phases
items.quote: So bulk of our sales is coming from phase -III onwards, you know. So currently, Phase-III and commercialization product would constitute to be 75% to 80% of overall value of sales and smaller amount from the early phases.

items.statement: CDMO working with 21 customers, added 6 new customers and ~20 new products in last year
items.quote: In last one year we have added almost 20 new products with 6 new customers. You have seen the growth of customer addition as well as the number of projects that we have done over a period.

items.statement: CDMO competes with European, Indian and Chinese players; some competitors larger but Aarti near $250M revenue
items.quote: Yes, we are competing European, Indian and Chinese, all three. In different products, we have different competitors. And that's how overall basket is lined up.

items.statement: API exempt from US duties; no threat anticipated to API business from US policy changes
items.quote: Yes, overall direct US export is not very significant as such in overall total revenue, but API is exempt from all these duties. We don't anticipate APIs will come under duty.

items.statement: Borrowings likely to increase by Rs 100-125 crore in FY26, debt/equity ~0.23-0.25
items.quote: So next year in current year, think the borrowing is likely to go up by about Rs. 100 crores to Rs. 125 crores, which would basically mean debt equity of roughly in the range o f 0.23 to 0.25.

items.statement: Final dividend Rs 2.5/share for Q4 FY25, total FY25 dividend Rs 5/share
items.quote: In line with the strong financial results and our commitment to enhancing shareholder value, the board has declared a dividend of Rs. 2.5 per share for Q4 FY'25, the final dividend, bringing total dividend for the full year to Rs. 5 per share.

items.statement: Net cash from operations Rs 332 crore in FY25
items.quote: In FY'25, our net cash from the operations remained strong at Rs. 332 crores, providing us the financial flexibility to reinvest in capacity expansion in R&D.

items.statement: CDMO revenue recognition volatile, not linear; large volume customers dictate shipment timing
items.quote: No. It will be volatile, because if we have large volume customers buying at certain period of quarter, we are helpless, we have to supply them then.

items.statement: Sustainability: EcoVadis Gold Rating (top 5% globally), SBTi approval for all three scopes (6th Indian Pharma CDMO)
items.quote: Recently, we earned EcoVadis Gold Rating ranking among the top 5 % globally in sustainability. Another milestone has been the approval of GHG emission reduction targets by SBT i. With this, we have become the sixth Indian Pharma CDMO player to earn SBTi approval for all the three scopes.

items.statement: Aarti USA revenue declining (Q4 ~Rs 7 cr) but not winding up
items.quote: If I have to give you number, in last quarter Q4, the topline was around Rs. 7 crores or so. It is definitely coming down, but it's not going to wind up.

items.statement: Ganesh Polychem: shutdown 3-4 months for lower-cost route upgrade; Q4 and Q1 FY26 impacted, normalization expected after
items.quote: Yes, for the Ganesh business that we have, there have been some slowdown in overall demand and what we have done is produce a significant quantity in earlier quarter and then we are actually upgrading our facility to move to a lower cost production route of synthesis for these products and that's why we have a shutdown which is ongoing for that site, which is almost 3-4 months.

items.statement: FY26 revenue guidance of Rs 700 crore and PAT of Rs 44-45 crore
items.quote: In Q1 for the full fiscal year, I am still hopeful that we will achieve a top line of around Rs. 700 crores and the bottom line would be around Rs. 44 crores to Rs. 45 crores.

items.statement: FY27 revenue target of Rs 1,000 crore and PAT of Rs 55 crore unchanged
items.quote: Yes, Kunal. So, see, as and when we get nearer to the subject , my guidance has to be more on the side of truth. Whatever I have spoken, my whole thing is that, yes, Rs. 1,000 crores is what we are looking at for FY ‘27 and Rs. 55 crores bottom line is what we are looking for .

items.statement: Expect 30% revenue growth in FY26; Q2 and Q3 will show stronger demand picture
items.quote: We are still talking about 30-digit revenue growth and that is pretty good. The Company has its expansion plans in place, and we are sure that Rs. 44 crores is the bottom line that I have previously told also.

items.statement: Margins expected to remain in line with current levels; no business model change
items.quote: So the structure then, the business model that we are preparing, the margins should be in line. If there is any business model change or something , there will be a very concrete intimation.

items.statement: Job work revenue Rs 8.5 crore in Q4 vs guided Rs 5-6 crore due to advance Akshay Tritiya demand
items.quote: So see, job work demand we have already received in advance in Q4 of this year, so the guided figure was Rs. 5 crores to Rs. 6 crores, we have done Rs. 8.5 crores.

items.statement: No new factory CAPEX needed; existing 2-ton capacity sufficient for growth as gold price doubled
items.quote: Right now CAPEX plan, so the factory that we were supposed to plan about a 4-ton factory or a 5 ton factory. So if you understand that at that time, during the IPO, the price was Rs. 50,000 a gram. And we had 1 ton capacity. So now the price is Rs. 1 lakh a gram, so already in the same CAPEX we were already achieving the same amount.

items.statement: Two new retail stores planned: Surat operational in Q3 FY26, Rajkot in Q1 FY27; primarily lease model
items.quote: in Q3 of this financial year, and another one will be in the Q1 of the next financial year, that is what the plans are. Palash Kawale: Okay. And what is the total CAPEX for these two stores? Harit Zaveri: We are primarily looking for a lease model, but let's see if there is any plans for the CAPEX, we will surely let the investors know about

items.statement: Retail capacity: current store Rs 500-600 crore; new stores add Rs 400 crore+ capacity; target retail revenue Rs 400 crore FY26, Rs 500 crore overall, Rs 600-700 crore next year
items.quote: I think what we are anticipating is that retail should go about Rs. 400 crores this year , the same store sales growth will be Rs. 400 crores in retail this year and overall retail should be about Rs. 500 crores. And next year it will be around Rs. 600 crores to 600 and Rs. 650 crores, Rs. 700 odd crores in retail itself for the upcoming.

items.statement: B2B factory capacity 2 tons = Rs 2,000 crore at current gold prices; volume utilization higher due to job work
items.quote: Now we have gotten sufficient capacity in B2B. Now when you talk about B2C, B2C runs in rupee terms. So let's say Ahmedabad showroom is, let's say , Rs. 5 00 crores showroom. We are already expecting that by next year it should be around Rs. 400 crores will be touching.

items.statement: Equity raise possible after debt-funded infrastructure in place; no immediate equity dilution planned
items.quote: Equity, see, right now the first aim is to fuel the growth as much as we can by debt . And then once we have a right kind of infrastructure and stuff in place for the robust next jump, we are sure that equities getting money and raising funds are part and parcel of operations .

items.statement: Income tax order of Rs 25 crore for bonus shares issued as private company; appeal filed at CIT; expected resolution next quarter; no financial impact expected
items.quote: So income tax matter, they have ordered us for Rs. 25 crores of income tax appeal for issuance of bonus shares when we were a Private Limited Company. I think that order we have already filed across CIT appeal. We particularly think that it's a very baseless order and we have filed our replies into CIT appeal. We are hopeful of hearing in a very early stage. And I think by next quarter we should b

items.statement: No new B2B customers targeted; focusing on deeper penetration with existing corporate retailer clients who are expanding stores
items.quote: We already have customers in place. We will be doing penetration among those customers. We are happy to add any new customers if the market has. There's already players which are planning to expand more on more number of stores. So, we are happy to be a partner in their growth.

items.statement: Industry FY26 expected to be very strong with tailwinds from distribution expansion, new products, and marketing efforts
items.quote: I believe for the industry FY26 can be a very strong one. The overall distribution for the industry is higher as we speak in FY26 compared to FY25. Given the work done by many of our peers over the last one year. So, I believe that will help overall industry volumes

items.statement: EV adoption in FY26 expected to be stronger than FY25 as industry addresses barriers like battery life, charging anxiety, and resale value
items.quote: I believe EV adoption for this year will be strong. I believe growth should be stronger in FY '26 compared to '25. And that's also because I am starting to notice that, I think all of us in the industry are starting to work more on industry barriers.

items.statement: Unit economics levers include EL platform, LFP battery transition (15-20% cheaper than NMC), value engineering, and new Chhatrapati Sambhaji Nagar factory
items.quote: LFP battery packs are obviously generally cheaper than NMC battery packs. And overall value engineering and the new factory in Chhatrapati Sambhaji Nagar should help. So, very strong trends on unit economics.

items.statement: Operating leverage kicking in as fixed costs (R&D, marketing, corporate overheads) not scaling with sales; marketing spend percentage expected to decline
items.quote: Operating leverage is also starting to kick in. As you can see, the EBITDA and the PAT improved at a better rate than gross margin. As volumes go up, I think there will be a lot more operating leverage to tap into.

items.statement: Software attach rate reached 88% in FY25, contributing over 600 bps to revenue with high EBITDA margins
items.quote: But with a very strong performance in Q4, software has ended up at an 88% attach rate for our sales over the course of the entire year. Very strong consumer reception with a very strong mobile app rating and it's contributing more than 600 bps to our revenue as we speak.

items.statement: Chhatrapati Sambhaji Nagar greenfield facility timeline 1-2 years, expected to start coming alive sometime next year
items.quote: It's a greenfield facility, Gunjan, so it's the kind of stuff which will take one to two years. Sometime next year, you should see it starting to come on life, but exact timeline we'll share a little later.

items.statement: COGS per unit reduced 19% from INR148,900 to INR120,700 in FY25 driven by Rizta introduction, lithium price cooling, and 31% R&D cost reduction over 3-3.5 years
items.quote: Our COGS per unit saw a very strong reduction in FY25. They were down from 148,900 to 120,700 in FY25, a 19% reduction over the course of a year. This was driven partly by the introduction of Rizta, partly by cooling down of lithium-ion cell prices, but also strongly by our work on engineering and R&D.

items.statement: LFP battery packs 15-20% cheaper than NMC globally; more supply chain resilient with fewer price fluctuations
items.quote: LFP generally tends to be 15%-20% cheaper compared to NMC globally, most reports will call it out. And that looks like a dependable number in the coming year. Also, the big advantage of LFP is it's a more supply chain resilient chemistry.

items.statement: Strong upgrade play with 70% household 2-wheeler penetration; customers buying second/specific-purpose scooters or upgrading; 125cc scooter share likely crossed 50%
items.quote: So, what we see is a very strong upgrade play, where consumers who have grown up, or have had a 2-wheeler for a while, are trying to either buy a second one, a more specific purpose one in their family, or they are trying to upgrade their existing vehicle.

items.statement: Non-South markets showing strong response; Gujarat market share jumped from 4-5% to 20-25% driven by Rizta family scooter; software attach rates stable at 88% despite mass-market product
items.quote: Particularly strong response for us has been, like the one example that I definitely will call out is Gujarat, where Ather continuously used to be single digit market share, often 4%-5%. But in recent quarters, we have hit 20% market share. In fact, even 25% in some months.

items.statement: Peers at 700-800 stores vs Ather at 351; hundreds of cities untapped where competition present but Ather absent; Rizta enables viable dealer economics for expansion
items.quote: Our peers have been operating at 700 stores, 800 stores. Obviously, there are really press releases of even higher numbers that you would have seen. While Ather has delivered this volume with like 200 stores, 300 stores until now.

items.statement: New store format breakeven in few quarters vs several years previously; early signs very promising; hundreds of stores headroom vs peers at 800+
items.quote: Today the new format stores that we open breakeven at a much smaller timeline. They are down from taking several years to get to steady state and years to profitability to literally down to a few quarters now. And the early signs of the core stores that we have opened in the last couple of quarters are very, very promising.

items.statement: Domestic cell sourcing strategic imperative; MOUs with Amara Raja, live relationships with LG; bullish on India cell manufacturing (Panasonic-IOCL, Reliance LFP, Exide); timeline couple of years
items.quote: We've already announced MOUs with the likes of Amara Raja and we already have live relationships with the likes of LG. And what also gives us a lot of confidence are the announcements by many very strong cell manufacturing companies globally who are starting to set up operations in India.

items.statement: India-produced cells may not bring big cost advantage near term (flat to marginally higher); quality journey needed for first-time-right metrics matching imported quality
items.quote: I believe India produced cells may not necessarily bring a big cost advantage in the near term because frankly it's going to be hard to beat China's massive scale and pricing structures overall. But I also believe that there will be ways the government will make it work to at least make the price competitive.

items.statement: FY25: 155,000 units sold (42% YoY), INR2,305 cr total income (29% YoY), adjusted gross margin INR428 cr (172% YoY), AGM 9% to ~19% (1,000 bps), EBITDA -23% vs -36% (1,300 bps improvement)
items.quote: level, we sold 155,000 units, which is a 42% growth year on year compared to FY24. Total income of INR2,305 crores, which is a 29% growth year on year. The difference is largely down to subsidy and a little bit pricing differential between 450 and Rizta. Adjusted gross margin for us was a very, very strong story in FY25. The business generated INR428 crores in adjusted gross margin, which is up 17

items.statement: Q4 FY25: 47,400 units sold (35% YoY), INR687 cr total income (28% YoY), EBITDA improved 1,900 bps to -23%
items.quote: Q4 FY25 to Q4 FY24, units sold were up 35%, 47,400 units. Total income was up 28%, INR687 crores and EBITDA was better by 1,900 bps to minus 23%.

items.statement: Subsidy reduction from INR10,000 to INR5,000 has ~3% revenue impact; industry preparing for post-subsidy world; pricing becoming independent of subsidy
items.quote: For Athers P&L, that's a roughly 3% impact on revenue, something that, given the strong trend of cost reduction, we have a strong ability to absorb. I think the impact of subsidy in the interim now is limited.

items.statement: Resale value supported by product quality, pricing discipline (new variants vs discounting), 8-year battery warranty with 70% range guarantee transferable to new owner
items.quote: We have taken a different view at this. Our view has been that you actually do a disservice to your customer and your market by doing that. There are other ways of handling a cooling down of prices. What we have done at Ather is instead of reducing the price of the same variant, we would rather create a new variant altogether and offer that at a more compelling price.

items.statement: Employee benefit expenses dropped from INR154 cr to INR109 cr in Q4 FY25 due to stock option vesting in prior period
items.quote: I believe there were a few stock options that particularly vested in that time period that caused a change.

items.statement: PLA plant commissioning targeted by Q3 FY27 with gross capex of Rs 2,850 crore (net Rs 1,750 crore after 50% subsidy)
items.quote: The 80,000 tonne capacity of our PLA plant is on track for commissioning by Q3 F Y27 with a capex of Rs. 2850 crores (gross) or net figure is Rs. 1750 crores accounting for government subsidy of 50

items.statement: PLA plant expected to generate around Rs 2,000 crore annual revenue and ~35% EBITDA margin
items.quote: The facility will produce 100% bio-based PLA using sugar as feed stock and is expected to generate around Rs. 2000 crore annual revenue, and hopefully, since it's the first time we are entering into this business, that's why the word hopefully, EBITDA margin of ~35%.

items.statement: Sugar price around Rs 41/kg expected to maintain; marginal uptick possible in coming months
items.quote: So right now, as we have informed you, our price is around Rs.41/kg. I think this is what has been prevailing in this quarter, approximately around this range. So, I would say that this price level should definitely maintain. And the rest would depend on the government's policy for next year. So, if at all, we'll see a marginal uptick in the coming months.

items.statement: Sugar sales volume estimated around 10 lakh tonnes for FY26
items.quote: So maybe 10 lakh tonnes is what we can, but this is a guess as of now.

items.statement: India domestic sugar consumption estimated at ~28 million tonnes for 2024-25 season
items.quote: On the demand side, India's domestic consumption is estimated at approximately 28 million tonnes.

items.statement: Government's 1 million tonne export quota contributed to firming sugar prices
items.quote: Government's 1 million tonne export quota has also contributed to firming of sugar price for our company around Rs. 41/kg because of the current prevailing price.

items.statement: Distillery segment impacted by no ethanol price revision for juice and B-heavy routes despite FRP increase
items.quote: However, the distillery segment, as you know, was impacted by government's decision not to revise the ethanol price for juice and B-heavy routes, despite revision in FRP.

items.statement: Maize ethanol purchased by OMCs at Rs 71.86/litre vs juice ethanol at Rs 65.61/litre; maize price remains stagnant
items.quote: So even now, if I go back to mathematics for the oil company, the maize-based ethanol is being bought at Rs.71.86 per liter and the juice ethanol is at Rs. 65.61 per liter.

items.statement: Sugar inventory of ~7.1 lakh tonnes as of 31 March, ~7.5 lakh tonnes including April production; to be liquidated by November
items.quote: as of 31st of March, we are holding around 7.1 lakh ton nes of sugar and in the month of April, we also produced something. If you take that into account, it will be around 7.5 million tonnes. This entire inventory will be liquidated within November

items.statement: PLA plant capacity 80,000 tonnes per annum; requires ~1.25 lakh tonnes sugar diversion (1.7x output)
items.quote: So , sugar is basically we have said around 1.7 x of 80,000 ton nes which is around 1.25 lakh tonnes

items.statement: Grain ethanol capacity ~5-6 crore litres; used as balancing factor post juice season at Maizapur unit
items.quote: I would say, because you need some shutdown time, more Rs. 5-5.5 crore liter. So, maize is equal to balancing factor post juice in Maizapur. We have one single capacity.

items.statement: Varietal rebalancing reduced Co-0238 (red rot affected) from ~25% to 6% of cane crushed; new varieties acclimatizing well
items.quote: Now we only have as also forecasted previously, now we have only 6% of 0238 which is affected by red rot. All the other varieties are very healthy and all the new varieties which are also put into the stream are acclimatizing well.

items.statement: Balrampur gross recovery dropped only 0.44% vs UP average 0.62%; recovery 0.7% better than UP average
items.quote: while UP has had a n odd 0.62% drop, Balrampur has only had 0.44%. This is on a gross sugar available in the sugar cane. It's called Pol % cane, which is only what we can measure today because of the ethanol diversion. So, while our drop difference is only 0.16% as compared to UP, but if we see it in absolute terms, our recovery is 0.7% better than UP average

items.statement: PLA sales targeted primarily domestic; export only after value addition (compounding/converting) within India
items.quote: So the goal is of course all domestic because if you're trying to go green, it hardly makes sense to sort of export it directly. Having said that, the export market does have a demand, but we would not probably like to export directly without one step of at least value addition of a compounding or a converting done within the country.

items.statement: No ethanol price increase for juice/B-heavy routes in 2024-25 ethanol year despite FRP revision; government understood pain point, FRP linkage expected next year
items.quote: For 2024-25 ethanol year, while diversion of sugarcane juice and B-heavy molasses is permitted, so the restriction on quantum was lifted but there was no price increase given. This marks a shift from the government's prior practice of aligning ethanol prices with changes in FRP making sugar diversion for ethanol unattractive.

items.statement: UP Chief Minister indicated reallocation of cane area from defaulters to good paymasters; SAP declared with practical mindset
items.quote: if you've seen the honorable Chief Minister's statement of f late, he has said that he would reallocate area from defaulters to good paymasters. So , one definitely remains hopeful on that front. And those areas itself have a lot of scope to develop because they have been belonging to not so good paymasters and therefore the farmer does not develop cane

items.statement: India sugar production estimated at 26 million tonnes net (29.5 gross, 3.5 diversion) for 2024-25 season, down from 32 million tonnes previous year
items.quote: According to the latest estimates, India's production for season 2024-25 is projected at 26 million tonnes on a net basis after diversion, accounting for a diversion of 3.5 million tonnes. (which means gross 29.5 million tonnes, 3.5 million tonnes diversion, 26 million tonnes net production). This marks a decline from 32 million tonnes net in the previous year.

items.statement: UP sugar production estimated at 9.28 million tonnes net for 2024-25, down from 10.35 million tonnes previous season
items.quote: In UP, production is estimated at 9.28 million tonnes, down from 10.35 million tonnes in the previous season, on a net basis.

items.statement: Closing sugar stock as on 1 Oct 2025 expected around 5.2 million tonnes; tight inventory supporting firm prices
items.quote: Consequently, the closing stock of the current year, that is stock as on 1st October 2025, is expected to be around 5.2 million tonnes. The tight inventory position is anticipated to support firm sugar prices.

items.statement: No ethanol price revision despite FRP increase could undermine E30 blending target by 2030
items.quote: If this persists, it could undermine the government's E30 blending program by 2030.

items.statement: Red rot disease peak passed; only 6% Co-0238 remaining, easily monitored
items.quote: East UP has a minimum red rot in the state, minimum. And for us, Avantika, how much do we have left? Avantika Saraogi: We have only 6%. Vivek Saraogi: Yes, only 6%. So that's the peak of red rot.

items.statement: PLA project to create significant employment opportunities in manufacturing and research
items.quote: Powered entirely by renewable energy, the plant will not only drive sustainability but also create significant employment opportunit ies in manufacturing and research

items.statement: Cane crushing down only 1.73% season-on-season, lowest decline among East UP factories
items.quote: Our proactive approach to varietal rebalancing and farm engagement helped increase came throughput and achieve a comparatively better recovery to peers. In fact, our crushing was down only 1.73% season-on-season and gross recovery dropped by 0.44%, which is the lowest decline among factories in East UP.

items.statement: PLA plant powered entirely by renewable energy; targeting applications where cost impact on final product is negligible (bottle caps, straws, textiles, medical)
items.quote: Powered entirely by renewable energy, the plant will not only drive sustainability but also create significant employment opportunit ies in manufacturing and research. By leveraging our agri-based value chain, the project positions us to meet India's rising demand for green alternatives and reinforces our role in advancing nation’s circular economy and climate goals

items.statement: India's PLA straws approved by BIS; straw market alone 100,000 tonnes resin vs 80,000 tonnes plant capacity
items.quote: India's consumption of straws alone is 100,000 ton nes of resin and PLA straws have been approved by BIS and this is a very big win , I would say as of last month or so, and it should be gazetted soon and this is sort of a, I just want to show that our volume is only 80,000 tons. India's one single application also if we capitalize on, the market is 100,000 tonnes large

items.statement: FSSAI and compostability approvals for food-grade PLA already underway; USFDA not required directly for resin supplier
items.quote: No. It's not required for food grade. Food grade certification is required for food grade like FSSAI and things like that in our country. Post that USFDA might be required for the compound or the converter who is then finally making the product. For us, the food grade, in fact, the compostability and FSSAI approvals are already well underway.

items.statement: Target annual pre-sales of over Rs.15,000 crores in about three years
items.quote: Building on all these levers, we also strive to achieve over Rs.15,000 crores in the next few years in annual pre-sales.

items.statement: FY26 launch pipeline of Rs.14,000 crores GDV across 8-9 projects, skewed to H2
items.quote: We are planning to launch around Rs.14,000 crores of new launch phases or new projects. Largely, this is up in the Q3 and Q4.

items.statement: Business development target of Rs.15,000-20,000 crores new GDV in FY26 across four markets
items.quote: Last year, added GDV worth about Rs.25,000 crores. This year we are looking at, at least about Rs.15,000 crores to Rs.20,000 crores, new GDV to be added and it will be focused in all markets.

items.statement: FY25 booking value more than doubled to Rs.8,087 crores; collections doubled to Rs.2,706 crores
items.quote: For the full year Financial Year '25, the booking value more than doubled to Rs.8,087 crores on the back of our seven projects phase launches. Our collection increased by 100% year-on-year to Rs.2,706 crores.

items.statement: Q4 FY25 booking value doubled to Rs.5,738 crores; collections grew over 100% to Rs.1,073 crores
items.quote: In Q4 Financial Year '25, the real estate business performed exceptionally well with stellar sales at our three new projects and two new phases launched across NCR, Bengaluru and Pune regions. Booking value doubled on the year to Rs.5,738 crores. Collection too grew by more than 100% to Rs.1,073 crores.

items.statement: FY26 EBITDA expected to be low as no major handovers; bulk EBITDA from FY28 onwards
items.quote: In FY26 there is no handover happening up. So there will not be too much emphasis on EBITDA. Collections are going to be strong, sales we are focusing on, but the bulk of the EBITDA will happen in the future year.

items.statement: Worli project targets average price over Rs.50,000/sq ft and cost ~Rs.25,000/sq ft for 45-50% margins
items.quote: What I have said always is that by the time we complete this construction over the next six, seven, eight years, we will achieve an average price over Rs.50,000 and a cost approximately about Rs.25,000 maybe including all inflation. So we should get close to maybe 45-50% margins, that is what I have maintained.

items.statement: FY25 project development spend Rs.6,000+ crores including Rs.1,600 crores construction and Rs.1,300 crores Worli acquisition
items.quote: Other than construction finance, it includes BD cost of the projects that we have acquired. A significant part of that about close to Rs.1,300 crores is towards the Worli acquisition, 10 acres.

items.statement: Consolidated debt Rs.3,575 crores; net debt-equity 0.92; Rs.2,000 crores paper debt to be repaid from divestment proceeds
items.quote: our current consolidated debt stands at Rs.3,575 crores and roughly our networth is around Rs.3,900 crores. So the debt-equity is around 0.92. Now, post the paper business divestment cash flow coming in, we will have to actually repa y close to around Rs.2,000 crores of debt

items.statement: Post divestment, net debt near zero with Rs.1,200-1,300 crores treasury balance; fresh borrowing only if growth capital exhausted
items.quote: So even if you consider some capital gain, tax, payment, etc., we will still be having some Rs.1,200, Rs.1,300 crores in our treasury. So that probably will be used for any acquisitions that we plan in the near future. And if we still require more amount, at that time we will be doing fresh

items.statement: Board approved divestment of Pulp & Paper business to ITC for Rs.3,498 crores slump sale; closure expected by Q2 FY26
items.quote: the Board of Directors of ABREL approved the Divestment of the Paper business through business transfer agreement envisaging a slump sale to ITC subject to consideration of Rs.3,498 crore s subject to achievement of certain condition precedent. We expect the divestment process to conclude by Q2 Financial Year ‘26

items.statement: Provision of Rs.124 crores for JV liabilities (Rs.81 cr) and leasehold land write-off (Rs.43 cr) after textile closure
items.quote: So the net amount that we have to provide is about Rs.81 crores. And the second, so if you see the number of Rs.124 crores, so Rs.81 Aditya Birla Real Estate Limited May 15, 2025 crores is this and the next Rs.43 crores is with respect to the carrying cost we had of the property, the only lease land which is now as per the Supreme Court we have handed it over to the BMC

items.statement: Thane project delayed due to new NGT requirement for central environmental clearance; applied to central government
