items.quote: Yes, yes. We have applied to central government. Our project has come under that. That is why it has got little impact. Otherwise we were planning to launch it in the last financial year. So we have applied to Delhi for our clearance.

items.statement: NCR project sold 3,000+ units in 15 days; Sarjapur launch Rs.850+ crores in a week; demand strong for right product
items.quote: happened in NCR was truly exceptional. Nobody thought in a short period of time of 15 days we could have kind of cracked a 3,000 plus booking in such a short period of time. So that was really exceptional. What happened in Sarjapur in Bengaluru, it is a very remarkable performance in my view, because this has been the highest launch for us in Bangalore. Nowhere in such a short period have we clock

items.statement: Demand continues very strong; right pricing, location, brand, design, sizing drives massive hunger
items.quote: Amit, demand continues to be very strong. I have always maintained that the right pricing, right location and combination of right brand, right design, right sizing, I think the market continues to have massive hunger or demand for such kind of products.

items.statement: Total GDV near Rs.70,000 crores after adding Rs.25,000+ crores in FY25
items.quote: Added projects having GDV of more than Rs.25,000 crores, taking the total GD V of company close to Rs.70,000 crores

items.statement: Noida Sector 150 project 50:50 chance; agreement expires this month; will re-evaluate
items.quote: Looks a little dicey because it has not made much progress from where we had, during the time we have signed, it is still hanging in balance, so it is 50:50, I am not too confident about concluding this deal. The agreement expires in some time later this month. So we will have to evaluate it in a fresh manner.

items.statement: Board approved buyback of equity shares up to INR20 crores
items.quote: The Board of Directors at its meet ing held today this afternoon approved the annual financial results of the company and along with that, approved buyback of equity shares of the company up to a total consideration of INR20 crores

items.statement: Sugar season 2024-25 cane crush marginally higher than previous season at 29.79 lakh tons
items.quote: However, in sugar season '24-'25, the company has crushed total 29.79 lakh tons sugarcane, which is marginally higher than 29.65 la kh tons in the previous sugar season

items.statement: FY25 cane crush dropped 22% to 28.49 lakh tons due to lower yield and red rot
items.quote: However, higher sugar realization by about 4% duri ng the year at INR38,736 per ton and increase in sugar sales volume by 0.19 lakh tons during the year, in addition to increase in Portabl e Spirits volumes, partly compensated for adverse factors, including l ower ethanol volumes by 537.69 lakh

items.statement: Average sugar realization increased 4% to INR38,736 per ton in FY25
items.quote: Average sugar realization in the year has been INR38,736 per ton, which is higher by INR1,377 per ton of last year's average realization.

items.quote: In ethanol segment, in this year, the total ethano l production from all feedstocks is 678.37 lakh lakh liters, which includ es 303.69 lakh liters from maize, which is 45% of the total production as against 1,189.78 lakh liters in the previous

And the end game obviously is to have majority in the Company and to acquire the Company at some point in time , but at the right time.

items.statement: Income tax assessment order leaves carry-forward losses at Rs. 32 crore as of March 31, 2024; appeal pending at Commissioner level; no tax expected for June quarter
items.quote: If you see we have already informed the Stock Exchange that post the assessment done by the Income Tax Department, our carry-forward losses stand at around Rs. 32 crore as on March 31st, 2024. However, we have appealed against the assessment done by the Income Tax Department with Commissioner Income Tax and that proceedings are currently underway. We will be able to give you an exact or rather mor

items.statement: Mansion House trademark dispute in West Bengal: status quo maintained, next hearing June 9, 2025
items.quote: As on the date, the status quo is maintained. I wouldn't, of course, the matter being sub judice get into more specific details at this point. But just two things I would like to add is that, you know, we have been the exclusive and uninterrupted users of this mark since 1983 and continue to remain so.

items.statement: Net sales realization per case Rs. 1,182 in Q4 FY25, impacted by Andhra price reduction; expected to improve with premiumization
items.quote: Our net sales realization per case stood at Rs. 1,182 for Q4 on the back of the price reduction taken in Andhra Pradesh. This NSR will now form the base and we expect the same to improve on the back of our premiumization strategies.

items.statement: UK FTA not expected to significantly impact luxury portfolio as Indian brands have clear positioning; brandy not significantly impacted
items.quote: With regards to the super premium luxury business that we have guided towards even with a whisky launch , to be very frank, I think there is a very clear positioning that Indian brands have created for themselves, whether it is the Indian single malts or the Indian malts that are coming in . So, we frankly don't see a significant impact on industry as such.

items.statement: Signed celebrity for Brandy category marketing; teaser campaign rolled out
items.quote: And for the first time, I think we will also be using a celebrity. We have signed on a celebrity, a nd our teaser campaign has just been rolled out today as we speak.

items.statement: EBITDA guidance: INR103 cr in FY25 to INR200 cr in FY26 and INR400 cr in FY27 with minimum 25% ROCE
items.quote: I can tell you wit h full confidence that this EBITDA of INR100 crores will grow to INR200 crores in FY '26 and INR400 crores in FY '27

items.statement: Revenue guidance: INR18,000 cr target for FY27 maintained despite steel price decline of 10-15%
items.quote: So, what has happened is that the steel prices are down by 10% to 15% at the time when we gave the guidance, right? But our EBITDA per ton and EBITDA is intact.

items.statement: Board approved INR600 cr capex over 3-5 years mainly for service centres (INR30-40 cr each), fully funded from operating cash flows
items.quote: Now this majority of this capex is for service centres. Like I said, one service centre cost us around INR30 crores to INR40 crores in terms of fixed assets.

items.statement: Capex will be 100% funded from internal operating cash flows, no external capital or debt needed
items.quote: One thing I can assure you that whatever capex we do every year, that will be fully funded from operating cash flows.

items.statement: Five service centres operational (Raipur, Bangalore, Ghaziabad, Dubai, Pune); adding five more at identified locations (Jaipur, Kanpur, Patna, Siliguri, Ahmedabad, Indore, Bhubaneshwar)
items.quote: Now this volume will double as we add five more service centres at the identified locations such as Jaipur, Kanpur, Patna, Siliguri, Ahmedabad, Indore and Bhubaneshwar.

items.statement: Service centre capacity per centre revised up to 8,000-10,000 tons/month (capacity 12,000-13,000 tons/month), reducing number of centres needed
items.quote: But what we have learned by operating 5 service centres is that 1 service centre now can-do business of 8,000 to 10,000 tons.

items.statement: Solar structures: 50,000 tons order visibility for FY26 execution, expected to double in FY27
items.quote: And we already have 50,000 tons worth of order visibility, which will be executed in FY '26, and this will easily double in FY '27.

items.statement: B2B metal trading: 50,000 tons/month currently, expecting 50% growth in FY26 with sharp ramp-up in H2 as more steel capacity comes online
items.quote: This will grow by 50% next year.

items.statement: TMT distribution: 11,000 tons/month current run rate, targeting 50% increase to 180,000 tons in FY26
items.quote: Now for FY '26, our target is 180,000 tons for TMT.

items.statement: Non-TMT distribution: INR40 cr monthly run rate (INR500 cr annual), targeting INR1,000 cr revenue in FY26
items.quote: For FY '26, our target is INR1,000 crores.

items.statement: Service centre EBITDA ~INR2,000/ton vs B2B trading ~INR750-1,000/ton; solar expected INR3,000-4,000/ton; non-TMT distribution 2-2.5% EBITDA margin
items.quote: On service centre, we should be doing around INR2,000 per ton EBITDA. On solar business, anyways, we have not captured any earnings in FY '26, but it should be like minimum INR3,000, INR4,000 per ton EBITDA business.

items.statement: TMT royalty model: INR500/ton royalty currently, targeting INR750-1,000/ton; margins temporarily lower due to brand investment, expanding to 4-5% later
items.quote: We expect it to increase to INR750 and INR1,000 per ton eventually.

items.statement: WC stretched to 30 days in March due to advance payments to mills ahead of tariffs and higher sales; already normalized in May, targeting 10-15 days by June end
items.quote: In the June quarter, we are confident that the working capital will come back to 10 to 15 days, which has always been our target.

items.statement: Service centre WC slightly higher than B2B (20 days vs lower) but offset by 4% vs 1.5% EBITDA margin; overall cash conversion to normalize by June
items.quote: The working capital in service centre will be slightly higher than B2B metal trading. But again, in B2B metal trading, if we are earning, say, 1.5% EBITDA margin, in service centre, we earn 4% EBITDA margin.

items.statement: No debt on books; Dubai entity has INR147 cr loans for working capital against INR110 cr cash balance and INR60 cr capex
items.quote: We don't have any debt. We don't have debtors on books as such; 10 to 15 days debtor cycle is very much manageable.

items.statement: INR250 cr expected from warrant conversion in next 10 days, maintaining high cash position
items.quote: Plus, there is around INR250 crores, which is coming in the company in the next 10 days on the conversion of warrants.

items.statement: Advance payments to steel mills in late March secured supply ahead of import tariffs; some pricing benefit possible but primary goal was supply security
items.quote: So, our mindset was more to secure the supply of steel rather than going for short-term benefits.

items.statement: Shifted TMT distribution to royalty model (INR500/ton) from revenue booking; removes working capital and credit risk from balance sheet
items.quote: Now we have changed it to royalty-based model, wherein the revenue doesn't get booked into my account neither the cost of materials. It is only the royalty, which gets booked into our account.

items.statement: Solar structures (Sun Steel brand) operational at Ghaziabad; expanding to Pune, Raipur, Hyderabad/Chennai service centres to serve key solar park regions
items.quote: we're going to do it in t hree locations, Amol, one in Ghaziabad, which is already operational. Then we're going to install some mills in Pune

items.statement: Servicing 2,257 customers across B2B traders, factories, service centres, and IPPs for solar; procuring from 225 suppliers including 4 of top 6 steel mills
items.quote: Today, we are servicing 2,257 customers, and we are procuring raw materials from 225 suppliers, which consists of large steel mills.

items.statement: TMT royalty partners have minimum volume commitments via MOUs; partners benefit from 70-80% utilization vs 50% previously
items.quote: We do tell them that you need to sell minimum quantity of TMT, right, every month, every quarter, every year.

items.statement: Not reliant on imports; business model built on domestic steel capacity expansion (70-80% increase 2023-2027); believes 10 SG Marts needed to service steel sector by 2030
items.quote: And we believe you need at least 10 SG Marts to service only steel sector, the way the capacities are getting built up by 2030.

items.statement: Import safeguard duties/tariffs support domestic sourcing strategy; advance purchases made ahead of tariff imposition
items.quote: One is that we made a lot of advance payments to the steel mills towards the last week of March of 2025, ahead of the tariffs, which were coming.

items.statement: Dubai service centre: INR60 cr capex, 10,000 tons/month volume, INR50-60 cr monthly revenue, margins higher than India (INR1,800-2,000/ton in India)
items.quote: Volume we are doing is around 10,000 tons a month. Margins are also a bit higher there.

items.statement: Team built over 1.5 years: Amit Thakur (B2B Metal), Achit Arora (Service Centres), Anamika Gulati (Renewable), Suraj Kumar (CFO), Shiv Bansal (Distribution)
items.quote: I am glad to welcome Mr. Amit Thakur, who is Director and he heads our B2B Metal trading. Mr. Achit Arora, who is Vice President, Marketing, and he heads our Service Centre business, Ms. Anamika Gulati who joined recently to take care of our renewable business.

items.statement: Main risk identified: non-availability of steel (not seen as challenge); business model shockproof with no debt, low inventory, 10-15 day debtor cycle
items.quote: So, the only risk to this could be non-availability of steel, which we don't see as a challenge. Other risks, we don't have any debt.

items.statement: EBITDA per ton KPIs: B2B INR750-1,000, Service Centre INR2,000, Solar INR3,000-4,000, TMT royalty INR500-1,000, Non-TMT distribution 2-2.5% margin
items.quote: On B2B metal trading, right, we should be doing around INR750 to INR1,000 per ton of EBITDA. On service centre, we should be doing around INR2,000 per ton EBITDA.

items.statement: Ferroalloy division expected to perform better in FY26 than FY25 due to product diversification and market mix
items.quote: we foresee a better scenario for FY26 than for FY25, mainly because we are seeing that the product diversification into ferrosilicon 9 Nava Ltd Q4FY25 earnings Conference Call 16.05.2025 is helping out

items.statement: Solar plant commissioning targeted by July 2026, 300 MW expansion by August 2026, Avocado revenue by end of 2025, Sugar by March 2028
items.quote: the solar we are looking at commissioning by July 12 Nava Ltd Q4FY25 earnings Conference Call 16.05.2025 2026, the expansion of 300 MW we are looking at commissioning in August 2026 and the Agro i.e., Avocado will start generating some revenue at least by end of

items.statement: Maintenance capex around $25 million per year; peak debt for expansion projects estimated at $250-300 million
items.quote: Debt should be around $250 million to $300 million, taking all the expansion projects together

items.statement: Maamba Solar project cost envisaged at US$90 million (US$63 million debt, US$27 million equity)
items.quote: the project cost we envisage is US$90 million, US$63 million would come in the form of debt and US$27 would come in the form of equity

items.statement: 150 MW short-term bilateral contracts committed until September; 60 MW CPP conversion to IPP approved in Odisha
items.quote: most of about 60% of our power capacity is already committed up until September through the short-term bilateral contracts

items.statement: $105 million pending collection from MEL with $16.8 million ECL provision; $55 million received post year-end
items.quote: we still have $105 million, which is pending to be collected and the corresponding ECL provision that is existing in the books is $16.8 million

items.statement: Zambia Solar tariff 7.8 cents/kWh escalating yearly; Phase-II 300 MW tariff starts at 9.5 cents/kWh escalating yearly
items.quote: The tariff for solar is actually 7.8 cents. That's the tariff that we have negotiated. That kind of escalates year-on-year

items.statement: Coal procurement diversification reduced net fuel cost for power generation
items.quote: we have done a diversification of coal procurement from what was existing to many other sources, which has reduced the net fuel cost

items.statement: Ferroalloy focus shifting to niche products like ferrosilicon for US and Japan markets with better margins
items.quote: we are focusing more in terms of niche products in markets like Japan, where there is a reasonable margin to be made

items.statement: Ferroalloy dependence on Japanese market increased in FY26 providing better margins than domestic or other exports
items.quote: our dependence on the Japanese market has increased over the course of FY26, which provides reasonably better margin than, say, domestic sales or export to any other country

items.statement: Ferroalloy expansion in India not viable due to massive oversupply and lack of captive raw material (40% of cost)
items.quote: it really does not make sense at this juncture given that there is a massive oversupply of material in the market

items.statement: Odisha approved conversion of 60 MW CPP to IPP enabling higher PLF
items.quote: the final approval for Odisha to convert these 60 MW CPP into IPP has just come through

items.statement: Zambia Solar PPA tariff in USD cents; Phase-II 300 MW PPA for 20 years at 9.5 cents starting tariff
items.quote: The PPA is for 20 years

items.statement: Consolidated net debt near zero excluding Phase-II non-recourse debt of ~$94 million; $55 million received in April unrelated to Phase-II debt
items.quote: apart from the Phase-II, which is 300 MW in Maamba where we have a current debt of about $94 million, we don't have any other debt at the NAVA level

items.statement: Completed share buyback of Rs.360 crores in Q4 FY25 and stock split in Q3 FY25
items.quote: we completed two corporate actions during the last financial year - a stock split in Quarter 3 and a share buyback for R s.360 crores in Quarter 4

items.statement: Maintained healthy dividend distribution alongside buyback and stock split
items.quote: In addition to these, we continue to maintain our dividend distribution at a healthy rate

items.statement: Ashwin Devineni designated as Managing Director; Nikhil Devineni joined board as Executive Director
items.quote: congratulating Mr. Ashwin Devineni on his designation as the Managing Director of the company and Mr. Nikhil Devineni to join the board as Executive Director

items.statement: MEL repaid shareholder loan in full to sponsor after receiving $55 million post year-end
items.quote: Post the close of the financial year MEL received US$ 55 million, which has helped it repay i ts shareholder loan in full to the sponsor

items.statement: Ivory Coast project hinges on raw material security (geophysical studies ongoing 6-12 months) and land acquisition (3 months)
items.quote: this entire project essentially hinges on two main factors. One is raw material security and the second is acquiring the land

items.statement: Iron ore magnetite mine in Zambia halted due to declining grade at depth making commercial viability unfeasible
items.quote: we finally concluded that the commercial viability in terms of mining probably was not there. So we decided to take a halt on further activities

items.statement: Lithium exploration underway on 11,000 hectares in Zambia; too early to assess commercial viability
items.quote: exploration activities for lithium is currently underway. So it's a t a very early stage right now to finalize any future

items.statement: Major maintenance shutdown for MCL planned in early 2027 (once every four years)
items.quote: we have a major shutdown which spans once every four years and that shutdown we are probably going to be taking during the early part of 2027

items.statement: Standalone other income jumped Rs.110 crores due to dividends from two subsidiaries
items.quote: in the last financial year, we have received dividend from two subsidiaries. So in standalone it is shown as other income. Those two dividends put together is Rs.110 crores

items.statement: Investments of Rs.1,325 crores in FY25 include Rs.475 crores in CWIP and rest in long-term bonds/securities
items.quote: these are investments in bonds and other securities which have matured beyond one year

items.statement: Management guides for 10-12% revenue growth and double-digit EBITDA growth for FY26 and the next 3 years.
items.quote: I would say 10% to 12%. I think that's a good conservative number for us to play with right now.

items.statement: Management targets double-digit top-line and bottom-line (EBITDA) growth for the next 3 years.
items.quote: We are comfortable that, in a conservative side, we should be able to deliver both double-digit top line growth and double-digit bottom-line growth towards EBITDA.

items.statement: Q4 FY25 EBITDA margin was 10.9%; full year FY25 margin was 9.1%.
items.quote: We delivered INR 127.3 crores of revenue and a 10.9% EBITDA margin for the quarter, which enabled us to deliver a consolidated INR 498 crores of revenue and a 9.1% EBITDA margin for the full financial year.

items.statement: Management aims to consistently deliver double-digit EBITDA margin and sees revenue growth as the key lever for margin expansion.
items.quote: I think we have the right things in place where we should be able to consistently deli ver double -digit EBITDA margin

items.statement: Industrial vertical grew well and won large customers; automotive vertical saw substantial slowdown due to Tier 1 project shutdowns in Q2/Q3 FY25.
items.quote: While the industrial vertical continued to grow, and they did fairly well, and we were able to win a substantial number of large customers, our automotive business-along with the whole external environment -saw a subs tantial slowdown

items.statement: Healthcare (HCLS) vertical grew from zero to INR 18-19 crores in FY25 and has strong growth potential.
items.quote: We went from 0 to INR 18 crores, INR 19 crores last year. So, it's very hard to predict how big it can become, but the growth will be there.

items.statement: Revenue is concentrated in top 50 clients; company invoiced 80 clients globally as of March 31, 2025, and plans to reduce count by focusing on top accounts.
items.quote: If you look at last financial year, we invoiced a total of 80-odd clients globally, as of March 31, 2025. We believe over the next 3 years, that number will gradually keep coming down, as we keep betting on our top 50 clients.

items.statement: Capex budget for FY26 is approximately INR 12 crores for office upgrades in Pune, Chennai, and new sales offices in UK, Michigan, Munich, plus hardware and lab upgrades.
items.quote: Total c apex budget is approximately INR 12 crores, which includes upgrading all our office infrastructure in Pune, in Chennai and of course, new sales offices in U.K., in Michigan and in Munich, Germany

items.statement: Headcount remained flat at ~2,500 while revenue doubled from INR 250 crores to INR 500 crores, indicating significant productivity improvement.
items.quote: When we were INR 250 crores, we were 2,500 people. We are INR 500 crores, now we have 2,500 people.

items.statement: Hired new P&L leader for Transportation & Mobility vertical and a new CIO; searching for IE&HM vertical leader.
items.quote: We've recently hired a new leader to head our T&M vertical and we'll be very happy to introduce all of you to this gentleman next quarter. And we also brought on a new CIO, a first for us.

items.statement: Board declared dividend of INR 5 per share for 10th consecutive year; evaluating buybacks and acquisitions.
items.quote: The Board has declared a dividend today of INR 5 a share, which is our 10th consecutive year. We are evaluating buybacks. We're evaluating a lot of other stuff.

items.statement: Entire revenue of INR 498 crores is non-India (North America and Europe); company invoices in INR for GCC business and USD/EUR for onsite.
items.quote: Our entire INR 498 crores is non-India business. We have no India business.

items.statement: Salary increments effective July 1 annually; H1B visa costs hit in Q4; management believes fixed costs are stable and revenue growth will drive margin expansion.
items.quote: For us, it's every year from July 1 to July 1 is our increment cycle. April to June is the appraisal cycle and July 1 is the increment cycle.

items.statement: Management adopts conservative guidance due to macro uncertainties (tariffs, automotive slowdown, geopolitical instability) and assumes flat automotive revenue for FY26.
items.quote: We have taken a lot more assumptions. Our budgeting is a lot more informed than before. We assumed a flat year for us in automotive.

items.statement: Q4 FY25 revenue grew 3.2% QoQ and 7.5% YoY to INR 127.3 crores; full year revenue INR 498 crores.
items.quote: In terms of revenue, we had a sequential growth of 3.2% and 7.5% on a year-on-year basis.

items.statement: Top 5, 10, 25 clients growing; deploying dedicated Account Managers and Delivery Managers for top 50 clients to deepen engagement across geographies and LOBs.
items.quote: Our top 50 customers will have very focused ASMs and ADMs, which is account managers for each client and one or multiple delivery managers for each large OEM client.

items.statement: Vendor consolidation by OEMs benefits Onward; company aims to win 10 of 80 active clients to scale faster, acknowledging wins and losses are part of the process.
items.quote: For us as a young company, especially post the pandemic, we've gone from literally 0 to INR 500 crores of revenue. So, for us, it's a beautiful run. We are only celebrating in-house. Now where are we celebrating and why did Onward win is obviously because there was continuously vendor consolidation or vendor evaluation from the large global multinationals in US and Europe.

items.statement: Three service lines - Digital (AI, data, cloud), Embedded Electronics, Mechanical Engineering - grow based on customer demand cycle with no internal preference.
items.quote: We remain focused on all three lines of businesses, which is digital, (which includes AI, data analytics, cloud) embedded electronics and mechanical engineering services. We don't have a preference. All three grow based on the customer demand cycle.

items.statement: Tariff changes and 'Make in India' initiative driving GCC setup in India; company is positioned to support clients in US, Europe, and India GCC models.
items.quote: In terms of preference, things have changed, especially with the whole new discussions on tariffs and the Make in India initiative or support every global company setting up large GCCs in India.

items.statement: Other expenses (travel and software subcontracting) decreased by INR 2 crores in Q4 FY25 vs Q3 FY25 and Q4 FY24.
items.quote: Other expenses are predominantly travel. And I think it must be software outsourcing or subcontracting. I can get you the exact numbers, details, Sandeep.

items.statement: Evaluating inorganic opportunities in high-growth verticals; cash deployment priority is scaling business organically first.
items.quote: We're continuously looking for the right opportunities in both the high-end verticals or both the high-growth verticals that we have.

items.statement: LTM attrition at 17.3% as of FY25 end; company gave highest increments in industry last year despite downturn, reducing attrition substantially.
items.quote: I think we've shared our LTM attrition data as well now. I think it's at 17.3% or something.

items.statement: Ambition to reach INR 6,000 crore revenue in FY27 from INR 4,130 crore in FY25
items.quote: We have always maintained that it's our ambition to reach INR6,000 crores in FY '27. So, which is two years away, right? So we are working towards that.

items.statement: Value-added products grew 20% in Q4 FY25 while milk grew 4.5%; targeting 7-8% milk growth
items.quote: Value-added products grew at 20% in the last quarter, but milk grew only 4.5%. It is a fact, right? So yes, we would like milk to grow at around 7 percentage to 8 percentage, right?

items.statement: EBITDA margin expanded 248 bps to 8% in FY25; long-term expansion expected via VAP mix, premiumization, automation
items.quote: EBITDA , INR3,310 million, up 58% year -on-year with margin expansion of 248 basis points to 8%.

items.statement: Took price hikes of ~1.4% on milk and 4-5% on VAP in Q4 FY25; passed on large part of 3% raw milk cost increase
items.quote: We had corrected the milk prices also relatively during this period by about 1.4% and that -- and various value-added products in the range of 4 to 5 percentage.

items.statement: Raw milk prices up 3% YoY in Q4 FY25; currently stable but flush season and buffalo flush later in year are uncertainties
items.quote: We had raw milk prices, which had increased by 3% or so compared to previous year same quarter. And market milk prices had gone up.

items.statement: VAP contribution 32% of revenue (excl. fat); with consumer packed fats 37.8% in Q4 FY25, up 3.7% YoY
items.quote: Value-added products contribution grew 2.3%, now accounting for 32% of total revenues without considering fat products.

items.statement: Ice cream plant capacity expansion to be commissioned by end of calendar year; full impact next financial year
items.quote: We have made a capex investment in enhancing our capacity of ice cream plant, which will get commissioned by the end of this calendar year. And next financial year, we will have the full force of that new capex investment.

items.statement: Novandie plant near Mumbai being repurposed for curd and broader VAP portfolio; expect >50% utilization immediately
items.quote: We believe that the plant utilization will go north of 50% almost immediately. And within a quarter or two itself we should be able to turn around the operations very comfortably.

items.statement: Acquired majority stake in Novandie, transitioning from JV to subsidiary; one-time INR 87 mn impairment charge in Q4
items.quote: Heritage Foods has acquired majority stake of Novandie, transitioning from a joint venture to a subsidiary company.

items.statement: Milk procurement averaged 1.72 million liters per day in FY25 with no milk holidays and timely payments
items.quote: In FY '25, we processed an average of 1.72 million liters of milk per day with no milk holidays and timely payments as a matter of principle.

items.statement: Retail reach of 180,000 outlets via 7,300+ distributors; 859 parlors and 386 happiness points; strong in modern trade, quick commerce, e-commerce
items.quote: Our retail reach of 180,000 outlets served via 7,300 -plus distributors. Our Heritage franchisee -operated outlets, 859 parlors and 386 happiness points.

items.statement: Government focus on rural dairy economy through subsidies, infrastructure investments, tax exemptions seen as positive
items.quote: The government's focus on strengthening rural dairy economy through subsidies, infrastructure investments and tax exemptions has been a positive step towards supporting the sector.

items.statement: Seasonal volatility and unpredictable weather (unseasonal rains in South) identified as key risk alongside raw milk price volatility
items.quote: Yes, one risk we have apart from the -- what you call the raw milk price volatility is actually the seasonal volatility. It's actually -- it's a risk that everybody should be aware of.

items.statement: Renewable energy capacity installed at 12.14 MW; among few Indian dairy brands embedding green power directly into operations
items.quote: Our renewable energy investments now stand at 12.14 megawatt capacity installed, making Heritage one of the very few Indian dairy brands to embed green power directly into its operations.

items.statement: Volume growth guidance of 5-10% for FY26
items.quote: And for the current year we can say that roughly 5 % to 10% growth on volumes is what we can consider.

items.statement: Standalone EBITDA margin guidance of 16-18% for FY26
items.quote: EBITDA margins, again depending on the product mix, anywhere between 16% to 18%.

items.statement: Order book of Rs. 2,100 crores as of 31st March, executable in 4-5 months
items.quote: So, our order book as on 31st March was close to Rs. 2,100 crores.

items.statement: Ratnamani Finow Spooling Solutions order book exceeds Rs. 600 crores
items.quote: Importantly, it now holds a robust order book exceeding Rs. 600 crores.

items.statement: Saudi JV CAPEX: 60% in FY26, 40% in FY27; operational by December 2026
items.value: 60% odd this year and 40% next year
items.quote: Say for Saudi about, the total roadmap is that we will be operational by December 2026. So, 60% odd this year and 40% next year.

items.statement: Odisha Phase-II CAPEX of Rs. 40-50 crores pending
items.quote: Odisha Phase-II about Rs. 40-50 odd crores.

items.statement: Subsidiary CAPEX of Rs. 200-250 crores each for RTL and Ratnamani Finow over 1-1.5 years
items.quote: For RTL and Ratnamani Finow between Rs. 200 to 250 crores each.

items.statement: Odisha spiral welded plant Phase-I commissioned, Phase-II by end of calendar year
items.quote: One was a spiral welded plant in Odisha wherein the Phase-I for the Odisha project is already commissioned and Phase-II will subsequently happen. So, by the end of this calendar year Phase-II will also be into commercial production.

items.statement: Stainless steel cold finishing capacity ramp-up in 3-6 months
items.quote: And then we had the stainless-steel cold finishing capacities that also the production has started. However, the ramp up will take another 3 to 6 months.

items.statement: Ratnamani Finow capacity to triple with new plant by end of calendar year or Q1 next calendar year
items.period: end of this calendar year or first quarter of the next calendar year
items.quote: So there by end of this calendar year or first quarter of the next calendar year, we will have the expansion which is Rs. 250 odd crores in place. So thereby increasing our capacity three folds.

items.statement: Ravi Technoforge adding one automatic line, production in 18 months
items.quote: For Ravi Technoforge, we are going to expand, we are increasing one automatic line. So there 18 months from now that will come into production.

items.statement: Q4 FY25 gross profit and EBITDA margins improved 3% and 2% YoY
items.quote: With a greater focus on value added products and these contributing higher to the top line, we saw our gross profit and EBITDA margin improve by 3% and 2% respectively over the corresponding quarter last year.

items.statement: Full year FY25 gross profit margin maintained at 34%, EBITDA declined marginally by 1%
items.quote: On a full year basis, we maintained a healthy gross profit margin of 34% though our EBITDA declined marginally by 1%.

items.statement: Ravi Technoforge targeting EBITDA margin of 14% in FY26
items.quote: We feel that the margins should be closer to 14% at EBITDA levels.

items.statement: Ratnamani Finow Spooling Solutions targeting Rs. 350+ crores revenue with ~20% EBITDA margin in FY26
items.quote: So, what we have targeted this year is revenue of Rs. (+350) crores with an EBITDA margin of roughly 20%.

items.statement: Domestic oil & gas line pipe demand muted; water segment demand in Gujarat, Rajasthan, Maharashtra, Madhya Pradesh
items.quote: The demand especially for line pipes is quite muted and that too for the oil and gas segment. Water segment we are seeing some demand in Gujarat, Rajasthan, Maharashtra, Madhya Pradesh.

items.statement: Healthy order inflow from Middle East and US for LNG projects; EU slow but stable
items.quote: Both Middle-east as well as US for LNG projects for stainless steel we are seeing quite a healthy order inflow as well as in the MENA region because a lot of oil and gas projects are going on in Abu Dhabi as well as Saudi and Qatar.

items.statement: Order book uptake expected from middle of Q2 FY26 for line pipes segment
items.quote: So yes, from the middle of the second quarter we will see the uptake in line pipes segment at least.

items.statement: Water segment contributed 15-18% of revenue in FY25 vs 5-7% in FY24
items.quote: Of the total revenue, roughly between 15% to 18% odd.

items.statement: Shift from oil & gas to water segment in line pipes impacted margins in FY25
items.quote: One major shift between '24 and '25 is majority of the orders in '24 were for the oil and gas segment in line pipes and in '25, it was say 50% of line by business was from water.

items.statement: Boiler tube margins expected to normalize to 17-18% due to pierced product acceptance by NTPC
items.quote: However, the competitive scenario for this particular product being pierced product accepted by the government, we feel that the margins for the boiler products will not remain as it was in the past.

items.statement: Export mix: ~55% of order book; MENA 25-30% of exports, US 15-20%, Europe 15-20%
items.quote: Roughly 55% odd export and 45% domestic.

items.statement: Working capital cycle higher in FY25 due to water sector orders with longer cycles
items.quote: So, working capital cycle may be because of the product mix. As I informed earlier on the call that a lot of orders from the water sector were executed where normally the working capital cycle is a little higher than the other products.

items.statement: Standalone zero debt as of FY25 end; generated Rs. 521 crores from operations
items.quote: On a standalone basis, we generated Rs. 521 crores from operations and closed the year with zero debt.

items.statement: Board approved dividend of Rs. 14 per share (700%) for FY25
items.quote: Considering the robust performance for the year the board has approved a dividend of Rs. 14 per share that is 700% which is subject to approval of the AGM.

items.statement: Saudi Arabia JV with SESCO (75:25) for stainless steel cold finishing facility
items.quote: We are also excited to announce our joint venture with SESCO in Saudi Arabia. We are in the process of establishing a stainless-steel manufacturing facility in the region.

items.statement: Capacity utilization FY25: Stainless steel ~60%, Carbon steel spiral/ERW ~55%, LSAW ~50%
items.quote: So, on an average say stainless steel about 60% and for carbon steel spiral and ERW 55% and LSAW close to 50%.

items.statement: Backward integration into steel making under study; viability depends on scale beyond captive needs
items.quote: However difficult to say at the moment because the capacity for manufacturing pipes is quite less than what a steel plant would be viable at. So standalone, only for supplying to your pipe manufacturing may be not viable, but we have to see the whole picture because certain grades, if you want to develop it is only possible with the steel plant.

items.statement: Management expects a down year in FY26 with revenue lower than FY25, and may not return to FY25 levels even by FY27.
items.quote: I will, however, say that we expect a down year in FY '26. We expect our revenue numbers to be down. as our biggest customerhas in-housed or in-sourced a significant portion of their volume, then obviously, we will see a drop.

items.statement: Long-term target of 50% revenue from non-fastener businesses by 2030.
items.quote: Long-term priorities are to have 50% revenue coming in from non-fastener businesses.

items.statement: Targeting 25%+ ROCE on new businesses over next 5 years.
items.quote: I think for the new businesses, I think we would be comfortable looking at anywhere 25% plus ROCE on the new businesses.

items.statement: FY25 capex of INR59 crores spent primarily on SGEM facility upgradation, capacity enhancements, and new product segments.
items.quote: We spent about INR59 crores in capex in FY '25. Investments were primarily in the SGEM facility upgradation and capacity enhancements, and additionally, investments for our new product segments.

items.statement: Revenue target of INR200 crores by 2030 for Power Transmission segment (relays/HVDC contactors).
items.quote: Revenue target is about INR200 crores by 2030 for this one particular product segment.

items.statement: HVDC contactors/relays budgeted at INR10 crores for FY26, targeting INR30-35 crores in FY27.
items.quote: On high-voltage DC contractors and relays, we have budgeted for INR10 crores this fiscal. And over the next 2 years, we hope we get to INR30 crores, to INR35 crores for next fiscal.

items.statement: Consolidated adjusted EBITDA margin expanded to 12.8% in FY25 from 12.4% in FY24.
items.quote: Adjusted EBITDA on a consolidated basis rose by 13.8% to INR132.4 crores with margins expanding to 12.8%.

items.statement: Standalone operating EBITDA margin on like-to-like basis better than 14.9% of FY24, probably 15%+ in FY25.
items.quote: But just I want to highlight the operating EBITDA on a like-to-like comparison is better than 14.9% of FY '24. It's probably 15% plus in FY '25.

items.statement: Auto industry slowing in FY25: passenger vehicles grew marginally, commercial vehicles negative, only 2-wheelers showed substantial growth.
items.quote: One, the auto industry, if you know, is slowing down, relatively slowing down. Passenger vehicle industry grew marginally last year in FY '25. Commercial vehicles were negative. The only substantial growth in FY'25 came in the 2-wheeler business.

items.statement: Ola in-sourced MCU for Gen 3 platform; will continue supplying Gen 2 but volumes low due to Ola operational issues.
items.quote: Ola has decided to make the motor control units and motors, the integrated unit in-house for their Gen 3 platform. However, for the Gen 2 platform, we will continue to supply to them.

items.statement: Working with 30+ customers across categories with awarded contracts or advanced testing; pipeline includes many more in early dialogue.
items.quote: In terms of the customer pipeline, we have more than 30 customers that we are working with at current -- this is across all categories. And when I said 30 customers, these are customers with whom we have either got been awarded the contracts or where we have an advanced stage of testing.

items.statement: Tata Motors is the LCV customer not buying MCU from Sterling Gtake.
items.quote: That was on the -- the question was on the LCV space. And if you want to know the answer, that's Tata Motors.

items.statement: Revenue split ~63% fasteners, 37% EV components in FY25.
items.quote: Revenue split is approximately 63% fasteners and 37% EV components.

items.statement: New products launching early FY26: onboard chargers, DC/DC converters, magnet-free motors.
items.quote: New products like onboard chargers, DC/DC converters, magnet-free motors will be introduced in early FY '26.

items.statement: Magnetics partnership with Yongin Electronics: 4 lines for high-frequency transformers, EMI filters, common mode chokes, inductors for chargers, DC/DCs, power electronics.
items.quote: We are putting 4 different lines for 4 different components within a subset of magnetics. So the first one is high-frequency transformers. The second one is EMI filters. The third one is common moat chokes and the fourth one is inductors.

items.statement: Steel price reduction provisions taken in Q4 FY25 (multi-crores) adjusted against top line revenue.
items.quote: So, we have taken provisions for steel price reductions, and those provisions are in multi-crores, which we have adjusted against the top line revenue number.

items.statement: Magnet-free motor BOM cost expected similar or lower than permanent magnet motors; magnets were ~30% of motor cost before trade tensions.
items.quote: The BOM cost should be the same or lower. In a large electric motor, magnets constitute up to 30% of the cost of the motor. That is at the prices that prevailed before these trade tensions took hold, okay?

items.statement: SGEM current monthly run rate 15,000-20,000 units depending on month; lower for commercial vehicle MCUs (25/day LCV, 10/day HCV).
items.quote: Depending on month-to-month, we are hoping to do anywhere between 15,000 and 20,000 units a month, depending on the month. Some months could be lower.

items.statement: Major infrastructure upgrade and capacity expansion at SGEM Factory developed as EV campus; Dyno installed, SAP implemented.
items.quote: Major infrastructure upgrade and capacity expansion at SGEM Factory, and we have developed it as an EV campus. SAP got implemented at SGEM as well and is live.

items.statement: Company remains net debt-free with INR12 crores surplus cash as of FY25.
items.quote: Net debt position, the company remains surplus. We have a INR12 crores surplus cash. In other words, we're pretty much net debt-free.

items.statement: ICRA upgraded long-term rating from AA- stable to AA- positive in FY25.
items.quote: ICRA upgraded long-term rating from AA- stable to AA- positive.

items.statement: OEM integration trend varies: Ola in-sourced MCU but other major 2W players (Bajaj, TVS, Hero) still outsource; dual sourcing expected as volumes scale.
items.quote: Ola has in-housed or in-sourced the motor control unit. It is not a function. It's just -- if you look at other players, Bajaj or TVS Motors or Hero, this product line is still outsourced to partners outside.

items.statement: Substantial one-time expenses in FY25 for future product expansion (magnetics with Korean partner for Hyundai/Kia, relays with Kunshan Guoli, magnet-free motors with AEM).
items.quote: We have substantial one-time expenses for future product expansion. As you have seen, we have announced 3 different products in the last 12 months, namely magnetics with the Korean company, for Hyundai Kia, Relay business with the Chinese company, Kunshan Guoli coming up in Bangalore. And you saw the announcement for magnet-free/ rare earth-free motors going forward.

items.statement: Revenue growth target of 20-25% annually
items.quote: we continue to commit to 20% to 25% revenue growth. But having said that, we don't really want to put that as an aspiration because for some of our segments we see a great traction.

items.statement: EBITDA margin target of 20%+ for mature businesses
items.quote: for all our mature businesses, we can definitely see a 20% plus margin EBITDA. And for Green Shoots that we have added, some of those are contributing good margins already.

items.statement: Margins to remain stressed in H1 FY26, improvement expected in H2 FY26
items.quote: margins will remain stressed at least for QI and Q2, 1.e., H1 of the next financial year because the investment that we are doing in our Sales team and the composition of revenue that we are accruing in our books so far will yield results in H2 of FY 26

items.statement: EBITDA margin declined to ~14-15% due to Managed Services hardware, US investments and sales hiring

items.statement: Major contract renewal pending outcome in first week of June 2025
items.quote: one of our major contracts is still in discussions, outcome of which will be known in first week of June 2025.

items.statement: Sales team expanded to 19 members with 3 international, continuous performance assessment
items.quote: Today, as of March 2025, we have a Sales team of about 19 members. Also, as part of an update, we have inaugurated new sales office in Mumbai.

items.quote: the composition of the total revenue from our core segments has contributed about 63% of our revenue and while the green shoots segments introduced as part of the Project Butterfly has contributed 37% for this financial year.

items.statement: International revenue 12-15%, targeting 25% with 5 US logos added
items.quote: currently, our international revenues are maybe at about 12% to 15% contributing overall to our overall revenue profile. How do we increase that to about 25% of our overall business? That will be one of our focus areas.

items.statement: Receivables INR67Cr as of March 2025, INR11-12Cr collected in May 2025 from Q3 delays
items.quote: our receivable position as of March 2025 stands at around INR67 crores on a consolidated basis, and we have realized close to INR11 crores from therein, which got delayed, like I said, from Q3.

items.statement: Robust liquidity position ~INR100Cr including cash, receivables and depreciation
items.quote: the arithmetic that we just did close to INR100 crores of overall position, that definitely gives us confidence to make investments like what we are doing already in our Sales and Product teams.

items.statement: Government Managed Services business being moved to new subsidiary for margin clarity and liability isolation
items.quote: We're taking this conscious decision to move some of this Government business into a subsidiary, which will anyway reflect in our consolidated numbers, but it will just give us that stronger segment-wise focus internally as an organization.

items.statement: Employee count reduced to 482 from 517, costs redeployed to Sales and Product teams
items.quote: Employee strength stand at 482 as of March 2025 as against 517 in March 2024 last year. During this year, we have taken some measures to optimize our overall employee cost and redeployed those costs in Sales and Product teams.

items.statement: Revenue INR153.7Cr (+32% YoY), EBITDA INR25.53Cr (+12% YoY)
items.quote: On a consolidated basis, we did a INR153.7 crores compared to last year of INR116 crores. That's a 32% increase in the top line. And on the EBITDA side, we have given an EBITDA of INR25.53 crores, which is again an increase of 12%.

items.statement: US recession viewed as opportunity for outsourcing, no direct US government exposure
items.quote: See, the threat of recession, we are looking at it as an opportunity for us because any threat of recession means they have to cut down on their costs and what better than to kind of outsource that to India.

items.quote: Government business has its own business nuances like in terms of the performance bank guarantees, operational requirements, partner associations, and the related exposure.

items.quote: As we reflect on the financial performance of the optical business, in line with our guidance, Q4 FY25 revenue stands at Rs.979 crores, which shows a healthy improvement YoY basis. EBITDA for the quarter stands at Rs.125 crores at 12.8% of the revenue.

items.statement: Re-entered major US customer for high fiber count OFC after a year; secured large orders from leading US OSP for OFC and interconnect; STL Digital signed major tech outsourcing deal with top Indian conglomerate
items.quote: In Q4 FY25 we made strong strides with key global wins. STL digital also signed a major tech outsourcing deal with a top Indian conglomerate and continued repeat engagements with a leadin

items.quote: We have fully invested into our capacities in terms of all the way from glass, to fiber, to cable and connectivity. So, we do feel that we are well invested. I do see that over the coming quarters, our utilization of the factories will go from 50% to 70% plus.

items.statement: Inventory drawdown over 18-21 months largely complete in North America; some pockets may remain for another quarter
items.quote: Inventory levels, I would say broadly last 18 months, maybe even 21 months a drawdown of that inventory. We have been sharing that update in our calls. items.statement: EXM business expected to grow in mid to high teens in FY26
items.quote: We believe that the EXM business should grow in mid to high teens in FY '26.

items.quote: EBITDA margins have been marginally depressed due to the growth investments we have made this year - client-specific, operational leadership and sales resources primarily both for domestic EXM sales and shared U.S. sales resources for CXM as part of the wider Digitide organization Sales investments / structure.

items.statement: Manila operational leadership investment largely complete, no significant adds expected in FY26
items.quote: We believe that the investment base so far in terms of overall country account relationship management leadership, I think should be sufficient, and we don't see any significant add to that, at least in FY '26 is concerned.

items.statement: EXM added 63 new logos with ACV of INR 30 crores in FY25, up 50% YoY

items.quote: Our total funnel is almost INR 27 crores at this point in time of which we have won INR 5 crores. Again, on the SME SaaS market, in a short period of time, we have built a funnel of INR 13 crores and won deals of about INR 2 crores.

items.statement: PSU contracts signed in India and Manila in Q4, revenue to start in FY26 after 2-3 month transition
items.quote: The contract has been signed. And then of course, as you know, it gets into a transition phase over 2 - 3 months, if not more. So, the revenue from these 2 contracts will come in FY '26.

items.statement: Manila seat capacity grew from 600 to nearly 2,000 seats over 18 months
items.quote: From where we were maybe about 18 months ago with 600 seats, we are almost touching close to 2,000 seats as we speak in Manila.

items.statement: International EXM PEPM realization nearly double domestic rates

items.statement: EXM international contribution grew from 24% to 30% YoY
items.quote: Our overall international contribution to EXM revenues also moved up from 24% in FY '24 to 30% in FY '25.

items.statement: Q4 operating cash flow INR 48.2 crores, up 87.5% YoY with 137% OCF to EBITDA conversion
items.quote: Our operating cash flow for the quarter was INR 48.2 crores, a growth of 87.5% Y-o-Y and OCF to EBITDA conversion remained strong at about 137%.

items.statement: Shareholding transferred from Quess Corp to Digitide Solutions via 3-way demerger effective April 1, 2025
items.quote: Our shareholding has been transferred from Quess Corp to Digitide Solutions, which aims to be a global provider of AI -driven digital transformation and business process solutions. items.statement: Dividend paused for Q4 due to demerger process; consistent predictable policy to resume at appropriate time
items.quote: We are just taking a pause to sort of go through the demerger process. We'll see if we have to make any incremental investments into our overall capabilities or otherwise, so I think it's a pause and therefore, we have decided not to declare a dividend for this quarter.

items.statement: Diversity improved from 44% to 47% in FY25; high ratings on Glassdoor, AmbitionBox
items.quote: Our relentless commitment on diversity and inclusion have been yielding results with general diversity improving from 44% in FY '24 to 47% in FY '25. We continue to receive high ratings and increasing feedback on social media, Glassdoor, AmbitionBox, etc.

items.statement: EXM processed 44.3 lakh employee records in Q4; base at 14.8 lakh as of March 31, 2025
items.quote: We processed 44.3 lakhs employee records for the quarter. And our base now stands at just short of 15 lakhs, at 14.8 lakhs as of 31st of March.

items.statement: EXM employee records processed per FTE improved 11% YoY for full year and Q4
items.quote: Our employee record s processed per FTE improved by 11%, both year -on-year, full year and year-on-year, quarter 4

items.quote: the num ber this year is about just under INR 2 crores, this number was higher last year. I think at least 50% higher, if my memory serves me right. So, we will continue to see that because we see a lot of our customers’ employees moving to the new tax regime

items.statement: NIM guidance for FY26 is 3.2% to 3.4%
items.quote: Our NIM guidance, we have said that we would be between 3.2% to 3.4% for this new Financial Year.

items.statement: Credit cost target for FY26 below 0.5%

items.statement: Cost-to-income ratio target 55% by end of FY26

items.statement: Advances target Rs 90,000 crore by end of FY26
items.quote: Our target would be to achieve closer to Rs. 90,000 crores as of this financial year end.

items.statement: NIM improved to 3.19% in FY25 from 3.52% in FY24; Q4 FY25 NIM 2.98% vs 3.02% in Q3 FY25
items.quote: The NIM has grown, and it has been 3.19% in FY'25 was 3.52%. Here again the NIM stood at 2.98% for the last quarter which is Q4 compared to 3.02% for the previous quarter.

items.quote: Excluding the impact of the reclassification of penal charges which has happened the NIM for FY'25 would have been 3.25% on a comparable basis with the previous year and that for the quarter would have been 3.06%.

items.statement: Credit growth slowed due to geopolitical factors impacting GDP; system credit growth lower than expected

items.quote: Gross advances stood at closer to Rs. 78,000 crores, Rs. 77,958.72 crores to be very precise as of March '25 reflecting a year-on-year growth of 6.8% over March '24.

items.statement: GNPA 3.08% (down 45 bps YoY), NNPA 1.31% (down 27 bps YoY); slippage ratio 1.71% for FY25 vs 2.8% FY24; target below 2% for FY26
items.quote: The stressed assets, which is very significant in terms of improvement to the book quality, with gross NPAs improving to 3.08% in March '25 compared to 3.11% in the previous quarter. the previous year ended, it was 3.53%.

items.quote: The standard restructured asset, here again the bank has done significantly well, including related accounts to that sub-1,000 crores, it was Rs. 994.77 crores as of March '25 compared to Rs. 1,113.65 crores the previous quarter and Rs. 1,579.35 crores as of 31st March '24.
