items.quote: As on date, we have 100+ studios operational in country where we display -- I mean, sort of our experience center for VIR laminate, VIR MDF, and I'm sure this will help us to push plywood also from this market, from this store. And also, we have 4,000+ dealers and distributors in our network.

items.statement: Fire incident recovery underway; insurance covers material loss and loss of profit
items.quote: We have taken adequate insurance in terms of loss of material. And secondly, the FLOP, that is a loss of profit policy is also there. So now we have already started the operations. The process for this insurance will start. And we are just expecting that we will definitely recover in terms of material 100%, in terms of profit also.

items.statement: MDF domestic volume FY25 1.97 lakh cbm; target to exceed in FY26
items.quote: In '24-'25, our domestic volume is almost 1.97 lakh compared to last year, it was 1.98 lakh. And we are pretty sure that we want to cross this mark this financial year.

items.statement: MDF revenue growth target 8-10% in FY26
items.quote: And we would take an expected growth somewhere around 8% to 10% in the business of MDF.

items.statement: Warrant proceeds INR 44 crore pending (deadline 22 June) for Jumbo Phase 2
items.quote: If you see the actual position of our warrant where almost INR 44 crores is still pending. So in due course of time, the fund will come. The last date for receipt is 22nd June. So we will definitely receive the pending amount. And this will be specifically for the Jumbo Phase 2 project only.

items.statement: Raised INR175 crore QIP in August 2024, used for debt reduction and business expansion
items.quote: We successfully raised a QIP of INR175 crores in August 2024, out of which funds were majorly used for reduction of debt and expansion of our existing businesses.

items.statement: Debt reduced; CRISIL rating upgraded from BBB+ to A- pre-QIP and A- to A post-QIP; promoter pledge released from 51% to 35%
items.quote: And also prior to the QIP, CRISIL ratings had upgraded our rating from BBB+ to A-. And now it has been upgraded in December from A- to A post the QIP. The consortium banks h ave also partly released the pledge of shares from 51% to 35% approximately of the total shares and we expect this to come down further in the ensuing years

items.statement: Commissioned steel girder and component manufacturing facility in West Bengal with initial capacity of 10,000 metric tons per annum
items.quote: We have commissioned a steel girder and component manufacturing facility in West Bengal, District Hooghly, with an initial capacity of 10,000 metric tons per annum, which was also informed with the stock exchanges earlier.

items.statement: Order book backlog at INR3,486 crore with order inflow of INR1,575 crore during FY25 including incremental orders from existing contracts
items.quote: Order book backlog stands at a healthy INR3,486 crores with an order inflow of approximately INR1,575 crores during the year, incl uding incremental orders from the existing contracts

items.statement: Key contracts won: INR547 crore Kona Expressway from RVNL and INR481 crore bridge near Kolaghat from South Eastern Railway
items.quote: Key contracts that we have received during the year were the INR547 crore s contracts for construction of the Kona Expressway from RVNL and INR481 crore s contract from South Eastern Railway for construc tion of a bridge near Kolaghat in West Bengal

items.statement: Guided 20%+ revenue growth for FY26 with EBITDA margin maintained at 13%+; PBT and PAT expected to improve ~30% due to lower finance cost
items.quote: So in terms of growth outlook, we expect a growth in 20% plus this year.

items.statement: Long-term EBITDA margin guided at 13%+ on both standalone and consolidated basis; confident of maintaining given order book
items.quote: We are quite confident of maintaining our long-term EBITDA margin of 13% from the operations given the order book that we have. And this is the level that we have also guided historically.

items.statement: Current debt at INR122 crore (working capital, equipment finance, bill discounting); expected to reduce by INR20-21 crore to below INR100 crore in FY26
items.quote: The current debt position is approximately INR122 crores. This is a mixture of working capital debt, some term debt from the equipment finance that we do have, because we have added a lot of equipment this year, and some bill discounting limits that we do have on the TReDS platform of the government.

items.statement: Standalone finance cost reduced from INR32 crore to INR24.5 crore in FY25; expect further reduction of INR6-7 crore to below INR20 crore in FY26 despite 20-22% growth
items.quote: Having said all that, so it has come down from INR32 crores to INR25 crores, wh ich is a reduction of INR7 crores in this financial year. We expect a further reduction of INR6 crores to INR7 crores in this financial year, means INR25 crores to INR26 crores, which will bring it down below INR20 crores for the year

items.statement: Capex budget approved by Board: spent INR55-60 crore in FY25; expect INR35-40 crore in FY26 for new capabilities and geographies
items.quote: So we do have a capex budget that is approved by the Board. So last year, we spent almost INR55 crores, INR60 crores in terms of capex. This year, we expect to spend approximately INR35 crores to INR40 crores in terms of capex.

items.statement: Guided order inflow of approximately INR2,000 crore for FY26; have bid for contracts >INR1,000 crore but price bids not opened
items.quote: Approximately INR2,000 crores.

items.statement: Concrete Sleeper segment: if all factories 100% operational, revenue capacity of INR250 crore; domestic facility potential INR125 crore
items.quote: If all factories are 100% operational, we could do almost INR250 crores.

items.statement: Ghana sleeper facility trial runs done, product approved by German lab; commercial production expected in next 1-2 months; new government sworn in January 2025
items.quote: Ghana facility, the trial runs have already happened. The product has been approved by the laboratory in Germany. The commercial production will start in the next 1 to 2 months.

items.statement: Consolidated EBITDA margin to improve and converge to standalone levels once Ghana facility starts; Sleeper segment EBIT margin expected 15-16%
items.quote: So obviously, like I said earlier, with the Ghana facility starting, the loss that we have booked there in terms of the Ghana facility will stop getting booked and rather we'll book profit. So the margins will improve on the consol level as well and will be closer to the margins that we have on a standalone basis.

items.statement: CFO reduction due to disproportionate creditor reduction from QIP proceeds and increase in contract assets from milestone-based payments (NHAI Ganga Bridge); expect payments in 1-2 months
items.quote: In terms of reduction in CFO, it's a good question. So reduction in CFO has happened mostly on account of disproportionate reduction in debtors, which we use from the CIB proceeds -- creditors, sorry, which we use from the CIB proceeds. It is also on account of what you call increase in contract assets, because there are some EPC contracts that we are having, especially the NHAI Ganga Bridge and o

items.statement: BG utilization at INR230 crore against sanctioned limit of INR350 crore; surety bonds also available from insurance companies
items.quote: BG utilization is approximately INR230 crores. We have a sanction limit of almost INR350 crores from the banks. In addition to that, there is some surety bonds also available from insurance companies, which are allowed.

items.statement: Board declared final dividend of INR1 per share, total dividend for FY25 at INR3 per share; record date July 31, 2025
items.quote: The company has -- the Board has declared a final dividend of INR1 per share, taking the total dividend for the year to INR3 per share. This is subject to approval from the shareholders in the forthcoming AGM. The record date for the same is fixed on July 31, 2025.

items.statement: Backward integration steel facility to save INR3-4 crore on EBITDA (not significant vs INR150+ crore EBITDA); used for in-house consumption, inter-company sales only
items.quote: So impact on EBITDA margin for that would not be a very significant number, maybe about INR3 crores to INR4 crores. So on an EBITDA of INR150 crores plus, it's not a significant number.

items.statement: Consolidated forex loss of INR3.5 crore in FY25 vs gain of INR12.5 crore in FY24 due to Ghana currency volatility; contract in euros but balance sheet in local currency causes mark-to-market loss
items.quote: So this is on a consolidated basis, it's not on the standalone financials that you're speaking about. This is with respect to the currency fluctuation in Ghana, specifically, which has also led to the loss there.

items.statement: Quarterly revenue growth expected at 15%+ each quarter; H2 slightly stronger historically
items.quote: So H2 will be slightly stronger, which has historically been there as well. But having said that, I think that quarterly, there should be a growth of almost 15% plus every quarter.

items.statement: Current monthly execution run rate >INR100 crore in last 45 days
items.quote: In the last 45 days, yes, we are doing more than INR100 crores a month.

items.statement: Execution risk on large bridge projects over rivers; mitigated by experienced team and daily monitoring of construction methodology
items.quote: Obviously, there's a risk in terms of executi on. We are constructing bridges over rivers, so we need to take care of t he construction methodology, et c. There's a full team, which is quite experienced, to handle all this and takes care of all the risk and daily monitors the project execution to ensure that the timely commission of the contract within the budget is

items.statement: Order book at 2.92x FY25 revenue providing strong visibility; Infrastructure segment 94% of revenue with INR3,265 crore backlog
items.quote: And coming back to the order book, we have on date a net unexecuted order book of INR3,486 crores, representing almost 2.92x our FY '25 numbers, providing strong visibility.

items.statement: Sleeper segment revenue INR93 crore in FY25 (domestic INR66 crore, South Africa contribution); expect INR150 crore in FY26 if Ghana starts
items.quote: We expect the domestic business to do almost the same level, about INR75-odd crores this year as well compared to INR66 crores last year. And the international business should contribute a similar amount. So overall, we should do almost INR150 crores this year from this business.

items.statement: No management changes mentioned; focus on experienced project execution team for risk management
items.quote: There's a full team, which is quite experienced, to handle all this and takes care of all the risk and daily monitors the project execution to ensure that the timely commission of the contract within the budget is done.

items.statement: Ghana IMF bailout and presidential election caused delays; new government sworn in January 2025, operations expected to streamline in 1-2 months
items.quote: Ghana had -- as you may be aware, there was a bail-out package given by IMF for Ghana. Post that, they also had a domestic election for the President. Now the new government has been sworn in, in January. So now the things are coming back on track and we expect that to now streamline in the next 1 to 2 months.

items.statement: Announced greenfield manufacturing facility with Rs 350 Cr first-phase outlay, primarily for fans, production expected in 2.5 years
items.quote: I'm very pleased to announce that the company is very actively exploring the development of a greenfield manufacturing facility. This will involve a proposed investment of about Rs. 350 Cr.

items.statement: Greenfield facility first phase focuses on fans with plans to add other production lines later
items.quote: The first phase will primarily focus on fans with plans to upscale going forward, adding other production lines and laying the foundation for sustained innovation and growth in the company in the years ahead.

items.statement: Entering rooftop solar business targeting Rs 20,000 Cr addressable market, leveraging brand trust and distribution
items.quote: I'm happy to inform one more category, large category that we are entering as a part of our Crompton 2.0 strategy. We are expanding into the rooftop solar business.

items.statement: Solar pumps revenue reached ~Rs 200 Cr in FY25, up from near zero three years ago
items.quote: Now this year, that's just gone by, we recorded approximate sales of about Rs. 200 Cr, that has come out of practically three years ago.

items.statement: Standalone EBITDA margin improved to 10.5% in FY25, highest-ever EBITDA of Rs 819 Cr
items.quote: In FY25, we achieved the highest-ever standalone EBITDA of Rs. 819 Cr. Our margin profile has strengthened with margins improving to 10.5%.

items.statement: Lighting segment EBIT margin expanded to 11.8% in FY25 and 15.9% in Q4 FY25
items.quote: EBIT performance was robust, margins expanded to about 11.8% in FY25 and a sharp rise to 15.9% in Q4 supported by a rich product mix and new product introductions.

items.statement: Butterfly Q4 FY25 EBITDA margin at 8.6%, FY25 EBIT turned positive to Rs 42 Cr
items.quote: This is altered in EBITDA margin of 8.6% for Q4 FY25. The business delivered a sharp turnaround in profitability YoY with EBIT rising to Rs. 42 Cr in FY25 and a Q4 swing of Rs. 11 Cr.

items.statement: Consumer demand remained subdued in Q4 FY25, unseasonal rains delayed summer season
items.quote: Finally, although consumer demand continued to be subdued in Q4, we are quite optimistic about the trajectory that the business is taking.

items.statement: Lighting panels business became largest segment, surpassing lamps and battens
items.quote: For the year gone by, the panels business is now for a company which has always been very heavy in lamps and battens, panels are now our largest business.

items.statement: Appliances delivered high-teen growth in FY25, air coolers >50%, mixer grinders 30%+
items.quote: Appliances delivered a high-teen growth. As you know, appliances comprise two parts. One part of it is what we call LDA, which is the Large Domestic Appliances, which is the air coolers and water heaters business and separately the kitchen appliances busin ess, which we call SDA. But since we've talked about appliances together previously, I'm going to talk about them together here as well. High -

items.statement: Butterfly revenue grew 12% YoY in Q4 FY25 to Rs 187 Cr, annual revenue Rs 865 Cr
items.quote: The annual revenue was at Rs. 865 Cr. The Q4 FY25 revenue was Rs. 187 Cr, marking a 12% growth YoY.

items.statement: Butterfly targets mid-teens revenue growth and near double-digit EBITDA margin in 3-5 years
items.quote: In the medium to long run, in the next three to five years, we expect Butterfly to grow at about mid-teens and reach close to double-digit EBITDA margin.

items.statement: Butterfly FY26 EBITDA margin target 8-8.5% with significant brand investment
items.quote: We are at about 7 -7.5% EBITDA margin. The idea is to take to about 8 -8.5%, but that's also on the back of significant investments will go behind the brand, considering FY26 is going to be a year of relaunch and repositioning.

items.statement: Butterfly gross margin improved from efficiency gains, price increases, trade term resets and input cost optimisation
items.quote: Importantly, the gross margin has improved materially as well. And this has come from efficiency improvements, price increases. Now we've been telling you that this is something that we've been doing. That has meant resetting terms of trade with many of our trading partners, but we've taken the p ain and now you can see some of the benefits, optimisation of input costs and of trade scheme.

items.statement: Launched Nucleus (BLDC) and X-Tech (induction) motor platforms for fans, differentiating via platform-first strategy
items.quote: You would have seen that we announced two platforms for the next generation of motor technologies, one for BLDC and the other for induction motors. We have very consciously decided to adopt a Platform -First approach, and that's culminated in the launch of Nucleus and X-Tech.

items.statement: Won solar pump orders from MEDA and MSEDL in Q4 FY25, strengthening organisation structure
items.quote: In Q4 specifically, we won orders from MEDA and MSEDL on the solar pump side. We are now moving ahead into the next level of stepping up our investments in the solar pumps business.

items.statement: Solar rooftop business initially subsidy-driven under PM scheme, expected to become mainstream beyond subsidies in 4-5 years
items.quote: This is also starting with an initiative from the Government of India, which is a subsidy -driven business. The payback for the consumer is very strong, which is what is driving move towards solar rooftop compared to other modes of electricity. But again, as we have seen in EV and as we would see at a point of time in solar pumps, this would also become mainstream even when the government initiati

items.statement: Trade inventory higher than normal due to unseasonal rains, expected to normalise as weather improves
items.quote: The trade does stock up ahead of the season. That is obviously a feature of how the market behaves. And if unseasonal rains arrive, then obviously, the trade is holding higher stocks than they would have anticipated at this point in time.

items.statement: Company remains strongly net debt positive, capital position strong to fund greenfield capex
items.quote: Fortunately, as you know, our capital position continues to be quite strong. We are strongly net debt positive company, let me put it this way.

items.statement: Consolidated profit grew 28% in FY25, revenue grew ~5%
items.quote: The consolidated revenue growth was a lso about 5% and consolidated profit growth is about 28%.

items.statement: Large Kitchen Appliances revenue ~Rs 60 Cr, EBITDA losses narrowing, ranked third on Amazon
items.quote: Large Kitchen Appliances clocked a revenue of about Rs. 60 Cr while EBITDA remains negative, losses have continued to narrow, and Crompton is also gaining traction online. And now I think we are apparently ranked third on Amazon.

items.statement: Greenfield capex to be ROCE accretive, aims to improve sourcing control and returns
items.quote: Look, at the end of the day again, don't want to get into specifics as yet, but we do think that this investment will generate good ROCE for us

items.statement: Seasonal timing shifts (extended winters, delayed summers) require agile supply chain and front-end operations
items.quote: We've had extended winters, we've had shortened winters, but that's the trade , that you have to have an agile system, growth and your supply chain as well as at the front end to be able to deal with these.

items.statement: Butterfly team restructured, brand repositioning and NPD launches planned ahead of kitchen season
items.quote: There's a fair amount of activity on the brand as well as on the new product launches at Butterfly. The idea would be that we get those out particularly ahead of the season, because the kitchen appliance season is different from the fans and air cooler season.

items.statement: Butterfly to expand pan-India from South stronghold after strengthening core products and brand
items.quote: It is our intent over time to take Butterfly to other parts of India. What you're seeing happen just now is Butterfly focusing on strengthening the core.

items.statement: Fan margins back to pre-BEE 1.0 levels, driven by pricing actions and new launches
items.quote: During the year, as you would have seen, our margins are now back to pre-BEE 1.0 levels. The pricing actions and a slate of new launches has helped us enhance competitiveness.

items.statement: ECD segment grew 11% in FY25 and 6% YoY in Q4 FY25
items.quote: In the ECD segment, which grew 11% in FY25 and 6% YoY in Q4, we saw a solid performance across all subcategories.

items.statement: Visa application volumes grew 31% YoY to 37.51 lakh in FY25 with net revenue per application up 35% to INR 2,903
items.quote: We achieved a record high in visa volumes reaching 37.51 lakh in FY '25 from 28.65 lakh in FY '24, with the net revenue per application increasing to INR 2,903 from INR 2,146 in FY '24, a growth of 35%.

items.statement: Q4 FY25 visa volumes grew 38% YoY to 9.8 lakh applications with net revenue per application at INR 3,149, up 26% YoY
items.quote: The growth was fuelled by a 38% Y-o-Y increase in application volume from 7.1 lakh in Q4 FY '24 to 9.8 lakh in Q4 FY '25, with net revenue per application standing strong at INR 3,149, a growth of 26% Y-o-Y from INR 2,500 in Q4 FY '24.

items.statement: Consolidated EBITDA margin expanded 808 bps YoY to 28.7% in FY25 driven by self-managed model transition and higher realization
items.quote: EBITDA grew by 82% Y-o-Y to INR 629 crores from INR 346 crores in FY '24 with EBITDA margin improving from 808 basis points Y-o-Y to 28.7% compared to 20.6% in FY '24.

items.statement: Company bidding for $1 billion worth of contracts coming up for renewal in next 12-18 months across multiple geographies
items.quote: There is $1 billion worth of contracts that are coming up for renewal that we are clear that we have been in touch with those governments. So definitely, we will be bidding for that.

items.statement: Invested over INR 1,000 crores in strategic acquisitions (iDATA, Citizenship Invest, Aadifidelis) during FY25
items.quote: In FY '25, we invested more than INR 1,000 crores across strategic acquisitions.

items.statement: Opened new visa centers in Colombia, Peru, Gambia, Sri Lanka, Philippines, Egypt, UAE, Vietnam and transitioned to self-managed model in China and Ecuador
items.quote: We have successfully opened new centres across various countries, including Colombia, Peru, Gambia, Sri Lanka, Philippines, Egypt, UAE, Vietnam and others. Additionally, in China, we have transitioned to enhance our operational efficiency further. Ecuador also saw a significant transition this year.

items.statement: Digital ecosystem expanded to 44,800+ CSPs and 142,000+ touch points by end of FY25
items.quote: At the end of FY '25, the digital ecosystem had expanded to 44,800+ CSPs and 142,000+ touch points, enhancing both accessibility and service delivery across the under-served area.

items.statement: China visa volumes nearly back to pre-COVID levels with transition to self-managed model completed in January 2025
items.quote: China, the volume is almost, not 100%, but it's almost back to pre-COVID level. We have seen a good growth in terms of our revenue from China. And we've also transitioned to our own model there.

items.statement: Ended FY25 with net cash of INR 928 crores after deploying over INR 1,000 crores in acquisitions
items.quote: On the balance sheet front, we continue to maintain a robust financial position with net cash of INR 928 crores as on March 31, 2025, even after deploying over INR 1,000 crores in strategic acquisitions during the year.

items.statement: Board recommended dividend of INR 1 per share (100% of face value) for FY25
items.quote: The Board of Directors of the company have recommended a dividend of INR 1 per share.

items.statement: SLW Media was a INR 70 lakh brand investment, not an acquisition; it is profitable with no further investment planned
items.quote: We have explained in the past that we have not acquired, this was a INR 70 lakh investment that we did to enhance our brand and that is doing very strong. And that is profitable. We have no further investment that we are making in that company.

items.statement: BLS E-Services network grew to 120,000+ centers with new public and private bank partnerships; expanding into B2C insurance and loan distribution
items.quote: Our network has grown to more than 120,000 centers. We have enrolled multiple new public sector & private sector banks BLS International Services Limited May 16, 2025 We have started different adjacent businesses, higher-margin businesses I've been talking about in the past years, the B2C segment, like insurance services, etc., that have started to increase our profitability

items.statement: No business impact from India-Turkey tensions as company operates with European governments across 70 countries globally
items.quote: We are working in 70 countries with multiple European governments in different parts of the world and delivery of services in different parts of the world. So we are a global company now. So there is no issue anywhere in the world.

items.statement: Other costs increased to 47% of expenses due to self-managed model shift - own employees, rentals, and location administration costs replaced partner commissions
items.quote: So where the commission used to be paid in the cost of services, now we have our own employees and the rentals and the location administration costs, all are being paid by us. Therefore, there's an increase in the other expenses, whereas if you see the cost of services are coming down. Overall, the margins are improving.

items.statement: Visa business operates in qualified market with only 3 global players; governments re-awarding tenders and reducing monopoly by adding qualified players
items.quote: Governments are building trust on us. They're re-awarding tenders to us. New governments want to reduce the monopoly, give work to multiple players, which are qualified, which only have 3 in the world.

items.statement: Completed acquisition of NSEIT (DEXIT Global Ltd.) effective 20th February for Rs.231.8 crores, funded by Rs.200 crores six-year debt.
items.quote: Effective twentieth February, NSEIT, has become an integral part of CL Educate group. Congratulations to all of you. As you are aware, but those of you who might have missed it, the purchase price was Rs.231.8 crores. And two very important things, to mention, in the same breath is that we acquired this company by taking a debt of Rs.200 crores, which is a six-year debt.

items.statement: Plan to become zero-debt company again in 36 months via internal accruals, potential DEX stake sale, IPO, and land asset liquidation.
items.quote: And one of the things that we are looking forward to is, to put the plan in place to become a zero debt company again in thirty six months. Some necessary steps have been initiated already, and this will be the first full quarter of NSEIT with us.

items.statement: No specific quarterly or annual guidance provided; test prep churn expected for 1-1.5 years, MarTech to expand revenue and improve margins, DEX full-year consolidation from FY26.
items.quote: Again for people who've been with us for a while know that we don't give a specific guidance, outlook for, you know, each business line and for the company as a whole. But, as, Gautam mentioned specific to the test prep business, it is going through a little bit of churn, and it has been, a bit of a challenging period for that.

items.statement: DEX core on-demand business grew 16% YoY; ICAI client added delivering >Rs.25 crores in Year 1 against 3-year Rs.75 crore target; AYUSH order won, DRDO expected later this year.
items.quote: Happy to share that, we had mentioned at that time that we were expecting about a 75 crore business from this o ver the next three years. The first year has indeed delivered in excess of 25 crores, and we hope to add to this over the years ahead.

items.statement: Plan to add 25,000 seats of captive capacity over next 18-24 months to bid for large exams like JEE, NEET, Bank SSC per new NTA guidelines.
items.quote: So we'll share more details about, the OPEX costs and so on related with our capacity enhancements, but we're looking to add 25,000 seats of captive capacity over the next 18 to 24 months.

items.statement: MarTech margins negatively impacted by stricter customer pricing and higher delivery costs; reengineering supply side to optimize costs and improve pricing.
items.quote: As I've been sharing for the previous investor calls, last two to four quarters, we have seen, our margins slightly impacted, largely by environmental factors where our customers have been asking for more stricter pricing, as a result of which our margins have been negatively impacted, and delivery cost have also slightly marginally increased across geographies.

items.statement: Test prep witnessing structural churn: students shifting to self-prep, smaller/cheaper products; MBA billing down 7% YoY; CUET not living up to expectations.
items.quote: If you look at the last one year, the compared to the previous year when we had done about Rs.200 Cr of the revenue, we are down to about Rs.189.5 Cr. Decline of about 7%, and this has obviously resulted in the EBITDA also coming down, from Rs.22 Cr to a Rs.15.6 Cr.

items.statement: Launched 'Attend From Anywhere' hybrid model and 'Open CAT' self-prep platform for MBA; developing adaptive testing platform; focusing on BBA/IPM and Law school programs where parents drive decisions.
items.quote: We have launched something which is called Attend From Anywhere (AFA). We have started this process. We did this experiment about three months ago, and it seems to be very, very promising. And we are looking at expanding it to others.

items.statement: MarTech added 12 new clients in last 12-18 months; international revenue grew 35% YoY to Rs.43.5 crores; DEX added IIM Bangalore and GITAM Group as new university exam clients.
items.quote: The new c lient acquisition has been gaining extremely positive traction, over the last twelve to eighteen months. We have added 12 new customers in various verticals, and we expect that over the next four to eight quarters, not only will the revenue contribution fr om these new accounts increase significantly, but the newer accounts itself will increase significantly.

items.statement: DEX delivered 55M+ exams over 20 years; 237 company-managed centers, elastic network across 780 districts; 1 lakh+ concurrent students in single session capability.
items.quote: 55 million plus, examinations have been delivered over the last twenty years, by, DEX. And, the exams listed on the top half of the page are predominantly those, that are delivered to the company managed locations, w hich are largely on demand

items.statement: DEX revenue seasonal: Q1/Q4 lower, Q2/Q3 higher due to event-based exam scheduling; core on-demand revenue uniform across quarters.
items.quote: If I were to take last year as an example, Q1 and Q4 tend to be a little bit lower, and Q2 and Q3 tend to be a little bit higher for DEX, in terms of the way revenue tends to be spaced out.

items.statement: NTA structural changes post-NEET paper leak increased operational delivery costs; new NTA guidelines require distinct captive capacity for large exam RFPs.
items.quote: NTA also introduced certain structural changes in terms of the way exams need to be managed and delivered going forward, which re sulted in us in an increase in the operational delivery costs of actually running those exams and managing those centers which delivered those exams.

items.statement: Test prep center expansion slowed to 15-20 new centers annually due to CUET underperformance; previously added ~20 centers in last year.
items.quote: In the last one year, I think we added we added about 20 o dd new centers. And going forward, it's going to b e similar until unless we are able to get, the product, which is going to cater two tier- three tier cities also. So going forward, I'll say about 15-20 new centers on an annual basis what we can safely assume with the current product range.

items.statement: Discontinued JEE, NEET, Bank SSC, CA test prep lines (Rs.9.3 crore loss) to avoid conflict of interest with DEX assessment business; acquisition expenses Rs.4.2 crore and incremental interest Rs.2.7 crore booked as exceptional items.
items.quote: In addition to this, there were significant amount of expenses which we incurred towards closing this transaction, including costs associated with legal and other, transaction related costs. And the acquisition related expenses of Rs.4.2 crores as per IndAS cannot be amortized, and they, have been accounted for as an exceptional item appearing in the P&L for this quarter.

items.statement: Potential strategic stake sale in DEX and IPO in 24-36 months to accelerate debt repayment; land assets may be liquidated over 2-3 years.
items.quote: We will look at a couple of s pecific ways to do that, including, potentially a strategic, stake sale from DEX and an IPO, also in the future. And, of course, over and above that, any internal accruals that we can use to retire the debt earlier, both from generated from DEX or from, the CL business, we will obviously leverage that as well.

items.statement: DEX operates 237 company-managed centers, 1000+ field force, elastic network across 780 districts; tech stack includes proprietary OS with 6 copyrights and 2 patents.
items.quote: DEX has been in the assessment business now for the better part of twenty plus years and is currently the number two player in this market space behind TCS iON. The organization has built a network of 237 company managed centers and has an, elastic network across schools, colleges, which allows it to deliver exams, as Satya mentioned, across all 780 districts of India.

items.statement: FY26 volume growth guidance 11-12% and EBITDA margin 12-13%

items.statement: FY26 ad spend capped at 5-5.5% of revenue (~INR90 cr)

items.statement: Gross margin currently ~33.5%, may improve 0.5-1%

items.statement: Target to reduce net working capital days by 10-12 days in FY26

items.statement: No major capex planned for next 2-3 years; maintenance INR5-10 cr
items.quote: So no new capex is being planned. And for next 2 to 3 years, we are not planning any major capex in the company.

items.statement: Pepe Jeans JV FY25 revenue INR34 cr, PAT INR5 cr

items.statement: Force NXT volume grew 14.5% in FY25, targeting 20% growth in FY26

items.quote: So this year, we have changed some strategies in our EBO also. We are trying to open 7 to 10 EBOs, but it would be like a mix of FOFO model plus FICO model.

items.statement: Target net debt-free by FY27-28
items.quote: We have only working capital loan from the bank. And we have the target by FY '27, '28, we convert ourselves in the net positive debt-free company.

items.statement: Final dividend INR3 per share recommended (18.7% payout)
items.quote: We are also pleased to announce that the Board has recommended a final dividend of INR3 per share, resulting in a dividend payout of 18.7%, subject to shareholder approval.

items.statement: Raw material prices stagnant; no major input cost pressure

items.statement: Q1 demand lean in April post-Eid; good demand from Tier 2/3 cities
items.quote: So see, as always, like after the festival of Eid, there's a dip or it's a leaner period in the market. So April was a bit lean as usual. But again, we are seeing good demand from the market, like from Tier 2, Tier 3 cities, especially, there has been a good demand in the market.

items.statement: Competitive intensity high but expected to subside eventually
items.quote: Prerna, the thing is it is not sustainable to be never ending. So it will subside eventually, and things are getting better day by day.

items.statement: FY25 EBITDA margin 10.7% (+59 bps); Q4 EBITDA margin 10.3%

items.statement: FY25 gross margin 33.2% (+100 bps)

items.quote: Dollar Protect, our rainguard segment, recorded an impressive volume growth of 40.3% year-on-year basis. Force NXT registered a 13.4% year-on-year volume growth, while our thermal segment grew 21% in volume over the same period.

items.statement: North India 47% of revenue; East 24%, West 21%, South 8% in FY25

items.quote: So with respect to the kids wear, we have given out samples to a few of the states like Punjab, Haryana and then some of the samples have been given out to Rajasthan also to check and get the feedback about the product. And this year, we'll be like manufacturing the kids 0 to 3 years products also and deliver to the market.

items.statement: Lakshya expansion: completing Jharkhand; Odisha, Bihar done; starting Madhya Pradesh
items.quote: Other than this, we also completed the Odisha and Bihar in this year and also try to start the MP, Madhya Pradesh during this year.

items.quote: So this has been done like we got a real big help from the Lakshya distributors also through this particular project. items.statement: FY26 outlook: revenue growth around 10%, EBITDA growth 15-20%
items.quote: And from an o utlook standpoint, as we pivot from reset to growth during FY '26, we will build on the foundation that we've laid out in FY '25. And we expect the business top line to grow by around 10% and the EBITDA to grow around 15% to 20

items.statement: No formal guidance given; provided outlook instead
items.quote: We have decided not to give a guidance. We've give n more like an outlook. And we believe that we need the whole year to constantly perform on our balance sheet, improve our free cash generation and then start focusing on aggressive growth.

items.statement: Gross margin expanded from 37.8% to 51.5% in FY25 (+1,370 bps)
items.quote: Since you've been watching our results, y ou've seen that our gross margin has expanded from 37.8% in FY '24 to 51.5% in FY '25, an increase of almost 1,370 basis points.

items.statement: EBITDA margin expanded from negative to 16.5% in FY25 (+2,360 bps)
items.quote: On EBITDA as well, EBITDA margin has expanded from negative numbers in FY '24 to 16.5% in FY '25, an increase of almost 2,360 basis points.

items.statement: Sustainable gross margin for Catalog business seen at 53-55%
items.quote: And the current gross margin on the Catalog business at around 53%-55% is sustainable, in our view.

items.statement: CRAMS and Polymers gross margin around 65%
items.quote: And currently the gross margin on the CRAMS and Polymers business, the base is significantly smaller, is higher at around 65%.

items.statement: Target EBITDA margin improvement of 200-300 bps over time
items.quote: I think we have the ability to move this by 200, 300 basis points. Will it happen in the next financial, i.e. this financial year? Yes, that's what we hope so

items.quote: As regards why our ibuprofen franchise is getting severe competiti ve pressure is because there is an excess capacity currently, mainly coming out of India, India with new plants and with newer plants, newer technologies.

items.quote: The pricing that currently prevails in the market, which we can't be very specific, does not even cover our costs of manufacturing, so it doesn't make any sense for us to invest high working capital in a business that doesn't deliver value for now.

items.statement: Expect quarter-on-quarter sales growth to resume in Q1 FY26
items.quote: Management: In 1Q '26, we should expect quarter-on-quarter growth.

items.statement: Regulated markets now 76% of business; plain ibuprofen share down to <45% including derivatives
items.quote: Our contribution from our profitable markets, which is the regulated markets, continues to be strong. We are currently clocking that at 76% of our overall business that is attributable to the regulated markets.

items.quote: We don't give specifics. We don't give any specifics on products, typically it used to be as high as 60%, but now currently it is less than 45%, including derivatives.

items.quote: At the same time, we continue to grow in what I call as the value-added Ibuprofen or the Ibuprofen derivatives business and the non-ibuprofen range of products.

items.statement: Building incremental capacities to debottleneck higher-margin products
items.quote: We've also taken up additional capacities. We're also building additional capacities, incremental capacities as I would say, to try and debottleneck our higher-margin products.

items.quote: We haven't yet started putting capital in Vizag to ensure that we can onboard customers. Until that is done, we are not on boarding customers.

items.statement: Gross debt reduced from ~INR1,000 cr to INR776 cr in FY25; targeting INR647 cr by end May 2025
items.quote: In this journey of maintaining a healthier balance sheet during FY '25, we have been able to reduce our debt significantly from a historic number of close to INR1,000-odd crores in FY '24 to roughly INR776 crores as we ended FY '25. items.quote: Further, we actually have a line of sight, once we have our second call money of the rights issue realized in May '26, by Q1 FY '27. We expect our net debt-to-EBITDA to come down to a range of 1.7 to 1.8.

items.quote: Subject to the shareholders and statutory approvals, once we have our new CRAMS and polymer entity carved out, we plan to further have a push down of debt of close to INR200-odd crores to the new entity, which should make our catalogue business balance sheet much lighter, and our net debt-to-EBITDA will be somewhere around 1.5 times of EBITDA.

items.statement: Finance cost expected to reduce by ~200 bps in FY26
items.quote: Arun Kumar: We are expecting this to reduce by about 200 basis points.

items.quote: As we continued to have a stretched working capital scenario during FY '25, which was partially driven by our muted revenue growth, we had to access certain short -term debt for some short-term intervals at an incremental borrowing cost.

items.statement: INR11 cr incremental finance cost in FY25 from short-term borrowing
items.quote: And hence, we see close to INR 11 crore s incremental finance cost in FY '25.

items.statement: Operating cost base reduced by ~INR1,300 cr YoY (22% reduction); Q4 exit run rate INR109 cr vs INR130 cr
items.quote: I'm also glad to report to you all that as a company we have reduced our operating cost base by close to INR1,300 million year-on-year, which reflects roughly 22% reduction in our operating costs. And from a quarterly exit run rate of close to INR130-odd crores in FY '24, we are currently at INR109 crores cost base in FY '25 Q4.

items.statement: Six inspections since Apr 2024 including two US FDA (Vizag May 2024, Ambernath May 2025) - both zero 483 observations
items.quote: We've been through six inspections since April '24, two of them being U.S. FDA inspections. The first was Viz ag in May '24, and more recently, Ambernath in May '25. Both these inspections were cleared with zero 483 inspectional observations.

items.statement: WHO approvals for Mangalore, Ambernath, Pondicherry; EU GMP for Mangalore
items.quote: We've received WHO approvals for our facilities in Mangalore, Ambernath and Pondicherry. And our Mangalore facility has received the EU GMP certificate as well.

items.quote: On the CRAMS and polymers new entity update, it's subject to regulators' approval. We coined a new name for the company. items.statement: CRAMS business currently ~INR100 cr; focused on complex chemistry contract manufacturing
items.quote: It's a very small business for us. It's just about INR100 crores.

And if we can re -pivot it to growth, which we're all working towards, with the theme of profit maximization and debt correction, I th ink the future is bright. So Sarat and I are here for the long term. That's all we can say.

items.statement: Aiming for ~20% top-line growth in FY26 with EBITDA margin ~20% and PAT margin 15-16%
items.quote: we are aspiring to reach the highest ever revenue in the coming FY and then we are aiming to get about 20% growth in the top line and commensurate growth in the bottom line.

items.statement: Reiterated FY26 guidance of ~20% revenue growth, EBITDA margin ~20%, PAT margin 15-16%
items.quote: The EBITDA margins would, we foresee will settle down somewhere around about 20% odd and PAT margins about 15% - 16% in the coming FY.

items.statement: FY25 closed with all-time high order book of nearly INR 8,900 crores
items.quote: ending the FY with an all-time high order book of nearly INR 8,900 crores.

items.quote: We got more than 150 plus orders totaling to INR 1,400 crores in Q4

items.quote: the CapEx would be very minimal. It would definitely not be exceeding about INR 50 to INR 75 crores odd. So, definitely well below INR 100 crores

items.quote: our dividend payout ratio in FY24 overall was 95.2%. In FY25, we maintained that level , at about 95.4%.

items.statement: Consultancy revenue grew 11% YoY in Q4 FY25; sequential growth healthy; order inflow strike rate >1 order/day maintained

items.quote: What you see as INR 4,200 crores in the as a turnkey in the order book, that's not really a construction, I mean, not like an EPC construction company. Primarily our role is still as a consultant.

items.quote: a consultancy order book of about INR 400 crores (including turnkey). You will see in this FY, and that's our focus, that's the next milestone which we are trying to achieve besides growth in export order book, definitely growth in the international consultancy order book.

items.statement: Margins under pressure from shift to competitive bidding; erstwhile higher margins not achievable

items.statement: Aspirational milestones: break highest-ever revenue record in FY26 and highest-ever profit in subsequent years
items.quote: we have set ourselves to aspirational milestones of this FY trying to reach and break the record of highest ever revenue. We will see how it pans out. items.quote: The credit cost stood at INR 583 crore for Q4 FY25 and INR 1,929 crore or 7.7% for FY25.

items.statement: Average cost of borrowing stable at 9.8% for last seven quarters

items.quote: We added 2.61 lakh borrowers in Q4 FY25, of which 43% were new -to-credit, with the FY25 new borrower addition count at 7.49 lakh.

items.statement: Opened 100 branches in FY25 across established and new geographies

items.quote: Our 'Evolve with Customer' strategy is helping deepen our customer engagement, with Retail Finance reaching INR 1,543 crore, contributing 5.9% of the AUM, compared to 2.7% a year ago.

items.quote: But then the average total unsecured debt of CA Grameen borrowers has declined 14 % YOY, while average monthly obligations have declined by 10% YOY.

items.statement: Employee strength increased from 19,333 Dec 2024 to 20,970 Mar 2025, attrition 30.5% annualised in Q4
items.quote: As guided, we strengthened our employee strength from 19,333 in December 2024 to 20,970 by the end of Mar ch 2025. Importantly, we maintained a firm grip on employee retention, achieving an annualised attrition rate of 30.5% in Q4 FY25, amid high churn across the industry.

items.statement: MD Udaya Kumar Hebbar retiring 25 June 2025, becoming non-executive Nominee Director; CEO Ganesh Narayanan appointed MD & CEO for 5 years from 26 June 2025
items.quote: over the forum for the Q&A session, I would like to inform you all that I shall be retiring from my role of Managing Director on 25th June 2025. items.statement: Liquidity adequate at INR 2,336 crore (8.4% of assets), sanctions in hand INR 3,618 crore, pipeline INR 4,664 crore
items.quote: The liquidity levels, including cash and cash equivalents , remain adequate at INR 2,336 crore, amounting to 8.4% of total assets. Additionally, we have sanctions in hands of INR 3,618 crore and INR. 4,664 crore worth sanctions in pipeline.

items.statement: Cost-to-income ratio 31.9%, PPOP INR 634 crore Q4 FY25, INR 2,638 crore FY25

items.statement: Capital adequacy comfortable at 25.4%

items.statement: FY25 ROA 1.9%, ROE 7.7%; 8-year cross-cycle ROA 3.6%, ROE 14.4%

items.statement: Karnataka ordinance caused operational disruptions Jan-Mar 2025, disbursement rates dropped to 57% Feb, 65% Mar

items.statement: Tamil Nadu bill currently no ground impact, but monitoring proactively
