items.quote: The New-to-credit % trend has increased from 30 -35% to 40-43% levels over the past couple of quarters, demonstrating the underlying potential of the microfinance business across the country.

items.statement: Deep rural unmet demand 30-40% even in 80% MFI-covered districts, new-to-credit 43% shows opportunity
items.quote: If you look at the entire India, even by 80% of the MFI covered districts, high districts, still you have more than 30%-40% of unmet demand there. So we can continue to address that in the deep rural.

items.statement: Target mid-single digit growth for both Spencer's and Natures Basket in FY26 driven by online and same-store growth
items.quote: We want to target mid-single digit growth as far as Spencer's and Natures Basket is concerned, driven by online in both parts of the business, but also driven by same store growth in both the businesses.

items.statement: Target operational EBITDA breakeven for both Spencer's and Natures Basket by end of FY26
items.quote: by the end of FY '26 at an EBITDA level both businesses will break even

items.statement: Target Natures Basket revenue of Rs. 320 crores in FY26 with 30% gross margins and 8% store EBITDA
items.quote: we believe that we can drive turnover in the range of about Rs. 320 crores for the next fiscal year. And drive it with the existing numbe r of stores , with margins around 30% , with operating costs which should be lower; and therefore, target getting to a level of store EBITDA which a premium business like this should be generating an EBITDA which should be in the level of about 8

items.statement: Target Jiffy revenue exit rate of above Rs. 25 crores per month by end of FY26 with 3 lakh orders monthly at Rs. 750 AOV
items.quote: we are talking about an exit of around above Rs. 25 crores a month.

items.statement: Plan calibrated store expansion of 3-4 stores in Calcutta, 3-4 in Lucknow, 1 each in Banaras, Allahabad and Gorakhpur for Spencer's in FY26
items.quote: we are looking at 3-4 stores in Calcutta, we are looking at 3-4 stores in Lucknow and then 1 in Banaras and 1 in Allahabad and potentially 1 in Gorakhpur. So, I think that will be the plan as far as new store additions are concerned.

items.statement: Natures Basket to add 2 renovated stores returning to 34 total stores in FY26
items.quote: We have 32 stores right now, there are 2 more stores which were shut last year for renovation, which will come on board. So, we will come back to 34 stores in this fiscal year very soon.

items.statement: Spencer's FY25 EBITDA improved to Rs. 53 crores (3.1% of sales) from breakeven in FY24 after Rs. 76 crores operating cost reduction
items.quote: EBITDA for Spencer's for the full year to be Rs. 53 crores versus breakeven last year. So, I think this EBITDA represents about 3.1% of sales and gives us confidence that that's the right trajectory for Spencer's.

items.statement: Natures Basket FY25 gross margins declined 90 bps; target to rebuild to near 30% in FY26 through assortment optimization
items.quote: the slight depletion in gross margins, 90 basis point s depletion in gross margins which we experien ced in FY ’25, that is going to be built back and the team is quite confident of getting to levels which are going to be closer to the 30% mark as far as Natures Basket is

items.statement: Spencer's like-for-like sales flat in FY25 and Q4 FY25; Natures Basket Q4 FY25 sales down 13% due to supply chain issues and new store ramp-up delays
items.quote: If you look at it at LFL level , l ike-for-like operating regions in Spencer’s, it was relatively flat and so was Natures Basket where there was no exit from stores or regions

items.statement: Jiffy Q4 FY25 saw 58% user growth to 70,000 monthly transacting users and 47% order growth to 1.8 lakh monthly orders
items.quote: The year-on-year Q4 of FY ‘25 versus FY ‘24 we saw 58% year-on-year user growth, which is close to 70,000 monthly transacting users. Our order growth ha s been in the order of 47%. So , we do an average of about 1.8 lakh bills per

items.statement: Target online mix to reach 20% of total revenue for both Spencer's and Natures Basket from current 13-14%
items.quote: The intent is, for both businesses, for the online part to be closer to 20% of the overall business mix. Currently, we are at 13-14%, both in Natures Basket as well as in Spencer's. So, the idea is that if we get to a level which is 80% offline, 20% online.

items.statement: Natures Basket Elysium membership program enrolled 4,300 members in first 3 months; target 15,000 by end FY26 driving 25% of revenue
items.quote: the first three months o f operation, we have had 4 ,300-odd members who enrolled, and really the goal is to drive up to 15,000 members by the end of this fiscal . And we expect about 25% of the overall revenues to be accounted for by this set of loyal repeat customers who will be covered under the Elysium program

items.statement: Net debt at Rs. 860 crores; exploring equity raise but market cap not supportive; will refinance maturing debt using available credit lines
items.quote: The debt position obviously remains high and we are aware of that. Last one year we took a board enabling resolution to raise some equity and we are actually constantly exploring various options to raise equity. But the fact that market capitalization is not supportive at the moment is something which has a bearing on our mind. Having said that, obviously , this is part of a large industrial house

items.statement: Quick commerce channel shift impacting modern trade; Spencer's countering with Jiffy but limiting investment due to balance sheet constraints
items.quote: quick commerce is gaining at the expense of both kiranas and modern trade. So yes, I mean , if we see lack of growth, that's because consumers are adopting quick commerce. And which is also the reason why we are not oblivious to that and we have refined our earlier slotted delivery proposition to a quick comme rce kind of delivery proposition by launching Jiffy. So ye s, clearly there is a channel

items.statement: Natures Basket optimizing inventory for higher GMROI/GMROF to improve turns and working capital efficiency
items.quote: the team is constantly looking at the product assortment with a complete evaluation of the product portfolio from a point of view of optimizing sales and space efficiency. So, while we carry a wide assortment, the width is there. We are also looking at how this inventory performs, which are the best sellers, where do we get the highest GMROI and GMROF and therefore really carry and buy an inventor

items.statement: Spencer's FY25 margins down 80 bps due to inventory liquidation during 47 store closures in Q2
items.quote: Margins were 80 basis point s down but again; this is Spencer’s largely attributed to the drop in margins which happened in Q2 as a result of the liquidation when we were shutting down 47 stores. We h ad to do a judicious liquidation of inventory which was there, rather than carrying that inventory and bringing it to the other regions

items.statement: Order backlog reached a record Rs 19,245.9 crore at end of March 2025
items.quote: At the end of March 31, 2025, our order backlog stood at Rs. 19,245.9 crores, providing revenue visibility across several quarters going back.

items.statement: Full-year orders surged 228% to a record Rs 18,173.8 crore in FY25
items.quote: For the full year, orders reached a record of Rs.18,173.8 crores, as you can see from the slide, up by 228%.

items.statement: Q4 FY25 orders grew 56% year-on-year to Rs 2,190.9 crore led by transmission and renewable segments
items.quote: In the quarter under review, we achieved a 56% year-on-year order growth amounting to Rs.2,190.9 crores, led by energy transition also due to the industry cyclical nature.

items.statement: Full-year EBITDA margin improved by 250 basis points year-on-year in FY25
items.quote: Both PBT and PAT also significantly up by 133% and our EBITDA margin has improved by 250 basis points compared to last year.

items.statement: Q4 FY25 operational EBITDA margin reached 12.3% on strong execution and better product mix
items.quote: Operational EBITDA, if you see for the stand-alone quarter 4, it stood at Rs.235.6 crores, basically resulting in a double-digit operational EBITDA of 12.3%.

items.statement: Company targets to sustain double-digit EBITDA margin for the full year FY26
items.quote: But what we said last time that we will reach a double-digit margin in this quarter, but our thing is that overall year-wise, we will maintain the double-digit EBITDA.

items.statement: Plan to invest approximately Rs 2,000 crore over the next 4 to 5 years funded by QIP proceeds
items.quote: we have already declared that we'll be spending approx. Rs.2,000 crores in a span of 4 to 5 years.

items.statement: FY26 capex expected to be 4x to 5x the FY25 level of Rs 130 crore
items.quote: obviously, in the next few years, it will be, let's say, 4x to 5x kind of thing.

items.statement: Expanding manufacturing capabilities across all four business units including transformers, high voltage, grid automation and grid integration
items.quote: we are expanding our manufacturing capabilities, capacities in all the four business units.

items.statement: HVDC project execution capacity is flexible with global supply chain; currently managing three HVDC projects simultaneously
items.quote: If you ask about our HVDC project portfolio, we have three projects by the end of 31st March. We have a Marinus Link project, for which we will start supplying shortly, then we have Mumbai project and then other projects which we got recently.

items.statement: Exports contributed 37% of total orders in FY25 (excluding HVDC) and grew 77% year-on-year
items.quote: In terms of contribution to total orders, exports contributed almost 37%, excluding HVDC and services contributed around 7.4%.

items.statement: Export strategy follows three-pronged approach: global feeder factories, allocated markets, and component supply to feeder factories
items.quote: Our export strategy, as I was explaining to you also, you know very well that it is a three-pronged strategy. First one, we have some of the products with the global feeder factories, and that is the same.

items.statement: Transmission segment orders surged 91% year-on-year in Q4 FY25; renewables grew 386%; railways & metro up 24%
items.quote: The transmission segment saw a 91% growth surge, where the renewables saw year-on-year growth of 386% and railways & metro are up by 24% year-on-year.

items.statement: Data center and industry segments saw year-on-year declines of 56% and 33% in Q4 FY25 but expected to recover in coming quarters
items.quote: However, the data center and industry saw a year-on-year decline of 56% and 33% respectively. But we believe this is a seasonal decline and a timing factor.

items.statement: Signed first service level agreement with world's largest data center provider for dry type transformers
items.quote: I'm also delighted to inform you that our service team has signed a first service level agreement with the world's largest data center provider for dry type transformers of various ratings.

items.statement: Service business unit launched from April 1, 2025 targeting Rs 2,000 crore annual orders in 3-5 years from current Rs 500-600 crore
items.quote: of future addressable market is in the range of Rs.2,000 crores per year. HITACHI 23/23 Our orders are in the ballpark in the plus/minus in that range. And that's what we are looking at it in that. Right now, we are around Rs.500 crores- Rs.600 crores of our orders

items.statement: Company is debt-free with no short-term borrowings as of March 31, 2025
items.quote: We are debt-free since last quarter.

items.statement: Completed first QIP raising Rs 2,520.82 crore; two-thirds allocated to expansion capex, 25% to corporate capex, 10% to working capital
items.quote: About QIP proceeds, we talked about very clearly and two-thirds of that we used in our expansion capex. And then the rest 25% is our capex corporate usage and 10% is working capital.

items.statement: HVDC projects will have low working capital initially, ramping up significantly in year 2; company has plan in place
items.quote: Being a big project, initially, when we start, it will start with the low working capital requirement. But once we pick up maybe in the year 2, the working capital requirement will be more for sure. But for that, already we are equipped, and we are having a plan in place.

items.statement: Government increased FY26 energy sector budget to Rs 26,550 crore from Rs 19,000 crore; interstate transmission system expects Rs 1 lakh crore investment over next two years
items.quote: reiterated its commitment to the same by increasing the FY '25-'26 budget for the energy sector to Rs.26,550 crores compared to the Rs.19,000 crores of the previous year. With India moving fast to meet its commitment of renewable energy installed capacity, the interstate transmission system expects close to Rs.1 lakh crores investment over the next two financial years

items.statement: Reciprocal tariffs may impact various industries; company maintaining vigil to minimize impact and retain export growth momentum
items.quote: India is comparatively less exposed to the reciprocal tariff, of course, we really have to wait and see how this will pan out to be. But it will impact various industries whenever it happens, but so we have to keep a constant vigil and devise a mechanism to minimize the same and retain the exports growth momentum clocked in the previous quarters.

items.statement: Focus on re-skilling and upskilling entire workforce; building capabilities across factories, project sites, engineering and future talent
items.quote: To stand the test of time and meet energy requirements of today and in the future, we'll continue to re-skill, upskill our entire workforce. And we continue to build capacities, not only our factories, our project sites, also for our engineering capabilities, but also our future talent required for our growth.

items.statement: More than 80% of global production portfolio manufactured locally in India; CRGO steel for transformers still imported
items.quote: but for all the portfolio put together, whatever we're producing globally, more than 80% we produce locally here. The value add is a different then what we produce. For example, transformer, we don't have a CRGO here and so we import it

items.statement: HVDC technology leadership with 150 GW installations globally across LCC and VSC; technology agnostic with full localization capability
items.quote: Throughout the world, we have close to 150 gigawatts worth of installations, both combined LCC and VSC technology. So, we are agnostic of technology. And just for information, the project, which we are almost in the final stage of completion, in Mumbai, is a VSC technology.

items.statement: Revised store opening target to 60-80 new restaurants per year for next four years, aiming for ~800 restaurants by FY29
items.quote: We are looking to open 60 to 80 new restaurants every year for the next four years. This will take us to about 800 restaurants by FY '29.

items.statement: Targeting gross margin improvement of 0.5-0.7% annually over next four years to reach ~70% by FY29
items.quote: We are targeting an annual increase of 0.5% to 0.7% over the next four years. And this will take us closer to a number of about 70% by FY '29.

items.statement: Gross margin improved 70bps YoY to 67.7% in FY25, driven by supply chain efficiencies and pricing
items.quote: Our gross margin, which ended last year at 67%, went from 67% to 67.7%, that's a 0.7% improvement year-over-year.

items.statement: Company-level EBITDA grew 32% YoY to Rs 99.4 crore in FY25
items.quote: Our company-level EBITDA was Rs. 99.4 crores, which is up 32% over the last year.

items.statement: Restaurant-level EBITDA grew 21.2% YoY to Rs 206.8 crore in FY25
items.quote: Our restaurant-level EBITDA was up 21.2%, which is Rs. 206 crores.

items.statement: Dine-in traffic grew 9% in FY25 on top of 5.2% in FY24, driven by value campaigns
items.quote: We saw dine-in traffic growth of about 9%, this is on top of our value campaign that we have started.

items.statement: India Q4 FY25 SSSG of 5.1% and full year SSSG of 1.1%, led by traffic growth
items.quote: SSSG was up 1.1% for the whole year, 5.1% for the last quarter.

items.statement: BK Cafe now in 90% of India restaurants (464 stores), up from 77% previous year
items.quote: We now have 464 BK Cafes as of last quarter across the country, which is about 90% of our store base.

items.statement: Launched Korean-inspired product range including Korean Paneer Burger, Chicken Burger, Fried Chicken, Wings and Fries
items.quote: We recently launched a new range of Korean products on our menu, with the Korean Paneer Burger, Chicken Burger, Fried Chicken, Wings, and Fries.

items.statement: BK App transactions grew 3x YoY, app user base grew 2.5x, app installs up 28% YoY
items.quote: We also saw a 2.5x growth in our app user base, and a 3x growth in orders via BK app.

items.statement: Average capex per new store in India ~Rs 2.7 crore, consistent for 3-4 years despite adding cafes and kiosks
items.quote: We still continue to spend roughly around Rs. 2.7 odd crores to set up a restaurant in India.

items.statement: FY26 capex guidance: Rs 3 crore per new store (incl. deposits) for 60-80 stores, plus Rs 10-15 crore incremental digital/refurbishment capex
items.quote: Roughly Rs. 2.7 crores plus the deposit that we placed. So roughly including that will be around Rs. 3-odd crores.

items.statement: India store count reached 513 as of March 2025, added 58 stores in FY25
items.quote: As of 31st March 2025, the year that ended, we added 58 restaurants year-over-year to reach 513 restaurants on that date.

items.statement: Indonesia BK store count reduced to 143 after closing 8 stores in FY25 (36 total closures)
items.quote: We had closed 24 restaurants previous, now we have closed another eight. So, there's a total of 36 restaurants that we have rationalized.

items.statement: Indonesia beef inflation and currency depreciation impacted restaurant margins; pricing taken across industry
items.quote: We have had some inflation in beef prices over there, and also some currency depletion over there. So, you have seen those two things happen simultaneously.

items.statement: India delivery profitability improved 1% in FY25; focus on profitable delivery growth continues
items.quote: We have moved that profitability by 1% in this year over FY '24, and we continue to kind of drive that piece this year as well.

items.statement: India G&A run rate reduced from Rs 65 crore to Rs 40 crore; targeting further Rs 4-5 crore reduction
items.quote: We were over Rs. 65 crores in G&A, as we have taken over the business, today we have brought that down to a run rate of Rs. 40 crores.

items.statement: Indonesia restaurant-level EBITDA margin declined due to higher marketing spend (8% of sales) to drive sales recovery
items.quote: It was around 8% if I remember the numbers from the last two quarters ad spend that we did.

items.statement: Indonesia Burger King full year SSSG +2%, dine-in ADS 18.5M; Popeyes 25 stores, ADS 14.1M
items.quote: Burger King, we did report a positive 2% SSSG for the full year. When Sandeep talks about it from the recent trends, you will be happy to see that the overall SSSG is now starting to see positive at 5% overall and 10% on dine-in basis as well.

items.statement: Franchise agreement with RBI amended due to COVID, enabling revised 800-store target by FY29
items.quote: Because of COVID we had rearranged an agreement with our franchisor. So, this guidance that you are seeing is reflective of that agreement that we changed with them.

items.statement: Indonesia corporate overheads reduced from Rs 65 crore to Rs 40 crore run rate via G&A rationalization and severance completion
items.quote: We were over Rs. 65 crores in G&A, as we have taken over the business, today we have brought that down to a run rate of Rs. 40 crores, so about Rs. 25 crores reduction.

items.statement: 90% of India restaurants now have self-ordering kiosks and table ordering; all future stores will include them
items.quote: 90% of our restaurants now have self-ordering kiosks and table ordering. So, literally everywhere that this was possible to do, we have completed doing that.

items.statement: India QSR industry ran negative SSSG in FY25; Burger King outperformed via value, cafe, innovation strategy
items.quote: This last two years as you have seen, especially the last year, that the industry has run a negative SSSG. In that environment to kind of hold on to our previous year's sales, that was in itself a very big challenge.

items.statement: April 2025 strong, May 2025 decent despite geopolitical issues; momentum continuing into FY26
items.quote: We have had a very strong April, and save a few days when we had this issue with the war, we have actually had a decent May as well. So, we continue on the track.

items.statement: CMC revenue guidance: originally INR1,000 cr, then raised to INR1,100-1,200 cr for FY27; on course to achieve
items.quote: originally, we had sort of indicated INR1,000 crores, then we uppe d it to INR1,100 crores to INR1,200 crores. So the endeavor is definitely to sort of su rpass that as well. But like we hold that guidance for the present

items.statement: Greenfield R32 project capex INR340 cr, completion by Oct 2026; ~40% spend in FY26
items.quote: The investm ent for this Greenfield R32 project will be around INR340 crores, and we expect to complete this by October '26

items.statement: Cuddalore paste PVC plant to reach optimum utilization ~10 kt/quarter in next 2 quarters
items.quote: We expect to reach an optimum utilization in the new Cuddalore plant on a steady state of approximately 10 kt per quarter in the next 2 quarters.

items.statement: MPB3 Phase 3 commissioning by Q3 FY26; MPB4 civil structure as big as MPB3, equipment decision based on pipeline
items.quote: Project activities for Phase 3 of the multipurpose block 3 is expected to be completed by Q3 of FY '26.

items.statement: Domestic R32 demand ~23-25 kt now, expected >50 kt by turn of decade; domestic AC demand growing ~15%/yr
items.quote: The demand right now is around, I think, the 23 kt to 25 kt that is there today. And by the turn of this decade itself, that is likely to touch in e xcess of, we believe, around 50,000 tons

items.statement: Suspension PVC apparent consumption grew 8% YoY to 4.3 mn tons in FY25; govt procurement expected to kickstart in Q1 FY26
items.quote: On a year-on-year basis, however, the apparent dom estic consumption of SPVC grew by 8% from just over 4 million metric tons in FY '24 to 4 .3 million metric tons in FY '25

items.statement: Suspension PVC spread normally $180-220/ton; conversion cost ~$60-65/ton; paste PVC more integrated, margins ~2x suspension over 10-yr period
items.quote: the differential between PVC and VCM normally hover s around $200 or so. It can be anywhere between $180 to $220, depending on where we are

items.statement: CMC business PBT positive with reasonable EBITDA margin; scope for improvement as new products ramp
items.quote: we are making a reasonable EBITDA margin already. And I only said that there is scope for further imp rovement given that we are launching a number of new products, there is some learning

items.statement: Green power initiative (solar+wind hybrid) from next year to bring significant cost savings for electrochemical operations
items.quote: we have, of course, announced our foray, we are working on a green powe r initiative, where we are looking at a hybrid of solar and wind, which will come in from next year, and that will have significant cost savings

items.statement: Antidumping duty on paste PVC from 6 countries imposed end-Mar 2025 for 5 yrs; EU/Japan investigation initiated; SPVC duty pending Supreme Court on grade exclusions
items.quote: Towards the end of March '25, the Government of In dia imposed antidumping duty on paste PVC resin imported from China, Korea, Malaysia, Nor way, Taiwan and Thailand for a period of 5 years

items.statement: BIS/QCO for PVC extended to 24 Jun 2025; ~3.5-4x capacity licensed globally vs India need; expect no further extension, low-quality imports to stop post-Jun 24
items.quote: This was something that had been extended till the 24th of June 2025. And we are now from publicly available data, what we can see is that th ere has been significant progress on the licensing of capacities outside of India, and there is significantly better coverage, coverage of around 3.5x to 4x of what India needs

items.statement: CMC: 4 of 6 LOIs in commercial production, 5th mid-2025; pipeline healthy, commercializing new products in FY26
items.quote: Out of the 6 letter of intents we supplied, 4 of them, we have started manufacturing and supplying commercial quantities. And the fifth one, we are commercializing sometime this year, in the middle of this year.

items.statement: CMC commercialized 3 new products in FY25; targeting 3-4 in FY26; mostly agchem with some non-agchem diversification
items.quote: Last, we commercialized 3 new products. And our plan for this year is to have a similar number around 3 to 4, and the pipeline continues to be strong.

items.statement: CMC engaging all key global agrochemical innovators; site visits/audits completed; diversifying into other specialty chemicals
items.quote: we are engaging very actively with all the key -- the innovators in this space. A ll of them have interacted, visited the site, audited the site

items.statement: China suspension PVC imports surged to 1.2 mn tons in FY25 from 0.25 mn tons 3 yrs ago; dumping driven by China's weak housing demand
items.quote: In FY '25, the import s from China surged to around 1.2 million metric tons from only around 2,50,000 metric tons just 3 years ago

items.statement: Net debt INR1,117 cr at FY25 end; cash ~INR700 cr; R32 capex funded by mix of debt and internal accruals
items.quote: Net debt stood at INR1,117 crores at the end of the year.

items.statement: CRISIL downgraded long-term rating to A+ (stable) from AA- (negative); short-term A1+ reaffirmed
items.quote: CRISIL have downgraded the long-term ratings of the company and its subsid iary, CCVL, to A+ (with a stable outlook) from AA- (with negative outlook

items.statement: Specialty Chemicals revenue INR1,764 cr in FY25, up 53% YoY; CMC >80% growth, crossed INR500 cr sales
items.quote: Specialty Chemicals revenue came in at INR1,764 crores, marking a year-on-year growt h of 53

items.statement: Value-added Chemicals revenue INR624 cr in FY25, up 24% YoY; volumes up 19% driven by caustic soda and hydrogen peroxide
items.quote: Revenue from Value-added Chemicals stood at INR624 crores, reflecting a 24% year-on-year increase mainly driven by higher caustic soda

items.statement: Suspension PVC revenue INR2,298 cr in FY25, down 6% YoY on lower realizations and volumes
items.quote: Suspension PVC revenue for the year stood at INR2,298 crores, a 6% drop year-on-year due to lower realizations and lower volumes.

items.statement: R32 HF sourcing: mix of domestic and imports; discussions underway; methylene dichloride partly internal, partly purchased
items.quote: HF, we have done extensive studies again. We haveit will be a mix of both domestic and imports, and we are pretty confident of the sourcin g of HF

items.statement: SPVC antidumping duty implementation pending Supreme Court decision on grade exclusions; legal challenge at final stage
items.quote: The antidumping duty on suspension PVC has not yet been implemented, awaiting a judicial decision on the exclusion of certain grades.

items.statement: R32 quota allocation uncertainty: country quota based on CO2e of HFC production 2024-26 + 65% of 2009 HCFC level; individual quotas later by MOEFCC
items.quote: This is based on the country's production. See, thi s will be calculated of the carbon dioxide equivalent of the country's production of HFCs betw een '24 and '26 and the 65% of the HCFC production in 2009 level

items.statement: China carbide-based PVC capacity (80% of total) using mercury catalyst; China to stop primary mercury mining by end-2031, expected phaseout
items.quote: By 2031, like I had mentioned i n earlier calls as well, by the end of 2031, China has announced that they're going to stop the mining of primary mercury

items.statement: Management expects to maintain ~15% average CAGR growth trajectory going forward
items.quote: See, if you see our past tense, then we have that average growth rate of about 15% and we intend to maintain that track record.

items.statement: Equipment business revenue share targeted at 20-25% of group revenue in near future
items.quote: It should definitely be a higher proportion, we should be able to have at least 20% - 25% coming from the equipment business in the overall scheme of things.

items.statement: McNally equipment business expected to contribute 20-25% of group revenue in near future
items.quote: The share of McNally will definitely grow in the near future as we go forward, and that is how we see McNally contributing to the group revenues of about 20% to 25% having share in the group revenue in the near future.

items.statement: Chile project capex of $30-35 million, Dahej debottlenecking ~Rs.30 crore, maintenance capex $5-6 million annually
items.quote: As far as the CAPEX guidance is concerned, we have our Chile project, which will have about $30 to $35 million of CAPEX expenditure. Then we have our Dahej debottlenecking project which is ongoing and apart from that we have about $5 to $6 million of maintenance CAPEX every year.

items.statement: Chile facility commercial production expected by mid next calendar year after receiving all statutory approvals
items.quote: I am pleased to inform all of you that all such approvals have now been received, and we have all the clearances to commence construction, and the commercial production of our new facility is expected to be operative by middle of next calendar year.

items.statement: Average capacity utilization at 60-65%, capacity not a constraint with planned expansions
items.quote: See Chirag, the average capacity utilization which we have is about 60% - 65% and we plan for our capacities well ahead in advance. So capacity is not a constraint for us at any point of time.

items.statement: Order book of Rs.1,029.2 crores as of March 31, 2025 with Rs.591.2 crores executable within one year
items.value: Rs.1,029.2 cr (Rs.591.2 cr executable within 1 year)
items.quote: We have an order book of Rs.1,029.2 crores as at 31st March 2025 out of which executable orders within one year is Rs.591.2 crores.

items.statement: FY25 group EBITDA margin 23%, Q4 FY25 EBITDA margin 29%, blended gross margin ~57% maintained
items.quote: The total revenues of the group for the year ended 31st March 2025, stood at Rs.1,681.8 crores, with an EBITDA of Rs.387.4 crores, that is an annual EBITDA margin of 23%.

items.statement: Equipment business full-year EBITDA margin target decent but 16-17% challenging, improved from last year
items.quote: And it's all about an operating leverage, and we intend to keep the growth momentum but yes, 16% - 17% on a full year basis for an equipment business looks little challenging, but yes, we have a target to have decent EBITDA margins going forward.

items.statement: Robust demand for gold and copper mining products driven by geopolitical uncertainty, central bank gold buying, and copper demand doubling by 2050 for green transition
items.quote: A significant portion of our products and solutions are customized for the gold and copper mines, and we believe there is a robust demand for both these metals.

items.statement: Sourcing as a Service GMV $730 million in FY25, revenue ~$18 million
items.quote: So for the full financial year as far as our Sourcing as a Service business is concerned, we did a GMV of $730 million, which translates into revenue of close to $18 million in this financial year.

items.statement: Ted Baker total revenue $61 million in FY25 (vs $63 million FY24), agency business disrupted for 6-7 months due to retail partner bankruptcy
items.quote: Ted Baker, the total revenue that we did was around $61 million, including both wholesale and agency business, which was a tad lower than what we did in the last financial year. Last financial year, it was $63 million.

items.statement: Knit Gallery acquisition closed, 3.5-acre land and 2,200 machines; capacity can double at small incremental cost as UK-India FTA ramps up; no immediate capex needed
items.quote: Therein the annualized revenue that we could expect from that business is close to ₹350-odd crores. So that business, we have added with good customer base. There is 3.5-acre land that is already there under a long-term arrangement in Knit Gallery facility. We have no immediate need for any capex.

items.statement: Bangladesh factories: Progress at mid-60s% utilization targeting 70%, GoodEarth at 57% targeting 65%; 10-15% more revenue extractable without capex
items.quote: In Progress, they are closer to mid-60s. They're trying to inch it up to 70%. And in GoodEarth factory, they are 57%, they're trying to ramp up to 65%. So without spending any money in terms of capex in GoodEarth and Progress, we believe closer to 10% to 15% more revenue can be extracted.

items.statement: Net working capital days increased to 17 in FY25 due to business mix and trade terms; targeting reduction to low single digits in FY26
items.quote: Net working capital days increased to 17, largely -- and this was largely on account of changes in business mix and terms of trade. We are working on and are pretty confident that we should be able to contain and reduce our working capital days in fiscal '26.

items.statement: Proposed dividend ₹3.35/share (₹1.65 interim paid), amounting to 30% of FY25 PAT
items.quote: Lastly, I'm pleased to share that we have proposed a dividend payout of ₹3.35 per share, of which ₹1.65 per share was paid as interim dividend, amounting to 30% of financial year '25 PAT, maintaining our capital return track record.

items.statement: Opened major US accounts: Walmart, Target, American Eagle, Ralph Lauren, TJ Maxx; 9 out of 10 accounts pitched get opened
items.quote: In the last 6 months, we've opened major accounts like Walmart, Target, American Eagle, Ralph Lauren. So some of the biggest U.S. retailers who are almost impossible and not looking to add any new vendors in their metrics have opened PDS account.

items.statement: US retailers in consolidation mode, not adding new suppliers; PDS wins accounts due to track record, management quality, product capabilities, geographical spread
items.quote: Generally, today, retailers are in a consolidation mode. They're not really looking at opening new suppliers, bringing in new suppliers on board. But looking at the PDS track record, the quality of our management, our product capabilities and geographical spread, we end up opening 9 out of 10 accounts we pitch to.

items.statement: UK-India FTA opens significant runway for Indian sourcing; Knit Gallery acquisition positions PDS to scale volumes for UK customers
items.quote: Firstly, the U.K.-India FTA has opened up a significant runway for Indian sourcing. With the recent acquisition of Knit Gallery, we are now well positioned to scale up sourcing volumes for our existing marquee U.K. customers.

items.statement: Bangladesh retirement age increased from 58 to 60 by government, causing ₹9-10 cr actuarial valuation impact in OCI
items.quote: One is in Bangladesh; the retirement age was increased by the government from 58 to 60 years. So we got the actuarial valuation calculation done. That has an impact of about ₹9 to ₹10crs, which is part of ₹48crs.

items.statement: Bangladeshi currency depreciated ~12% vs USD in FY25, causing ~₹20-21 cr FX loss in OCI
items.quote: This is largely the FX., the depreciation of the Bangladeshi currency by almost 12% this year vis-a-vis the dollar. And if you put that on my balance sheet in Bangladesh, it translates to about out of this ₹23crs, almost ₹20 - 21crs is on account of the FX depreciation.

items.statement: Michael Yee (Foundry Group founder) joined to lead North America strategy; Mark Green being replaced but retained for key relationships
items.quote: We're very pleased to welcome Michael Yee, Founder of Foundry Group to the PDS platform. Michael comes with a vast experience of working with renowned retailers like MGF, GAP, Kate Spade, and he brings key customer relationships on board.

items.statement: Second-line leadership curated over 2 years ready to take charge; platform cost realignment expected to yield benefits from Q2 FY26
items.quote: We also realized that in our corporate setup in a platform, there is the second line of leadership that we have been carefully curating and we believe they are all set now to take charge, and this may also help us in terms of optimizing cost.

items.statement: Agency business decline (including Ted Baker) pressured margins; wholesale relationships intact and strengthened; New Lobster shifting to B2B model
items.quote: This business started on a very promising note for us but had to foresee retail bankruptcies, the franchisees that were appointed by Authentic Brands Group in U.K. and U.S. went through an administration process. And as a result, almost half of the sales, which were agency sales, got impacted.

items.statement: Geopolitical tensions (Bangladesh, India-Pakistan, US tariffs) create uncertainty; management keeping margin of safety in targets
items.quote: The only reason one is a bit conservative is because there are so many geopolitical developments that keep happening across the world, Bangladesh and then the war around India and then U.S. tariffs, etcetera. So we're just keeping a bit of margin around that.

items.statement: GMV grew 25% YoY to ₹18,744 cr (~$2.2B) in FY25; 45% of $5B GMV target achieved in 2 years
items.quote: Despite the persistent macroeconomic and geopolitical uncertainties across the key global markets, we could successfully achieve 25% year-on-year growth in gross merchandise value. It touched of around ₹18,744crs, which is approximately USD2.2 billion.

items.statement: ROCE 19% reported, 27% adjusted for new vertical investments in FY25
items.quote: Our return on capital employed stood at 19% and when adjusted for new vertical investments, it was at a healthy 27%.

items.statement: BCG cost optimization program across 3 verticals and platform; savings identified at halfway point, benefits visible from H2 FY26
items.quote: Even at the half-point point of the implementation of the BCG program, we have identified savings that we believe will start flowing through in the coming quarters. This has been a kind of change management program wherein with BCG's analysis, the process system augmentation that they are doing, we believe the benefits are tangible and surely going to be visible in H2.

items.statement: Commissioned 3.8 MW DC solar plant taking total to 9 MW DC; 10 MW DC solar plant in Nanded initiated; Unit-5 dyes trial by end-May; Unit-6 NPK trial near Diwali 2025
items.value: 9 MW DC solar, 10 MW DC planned
items.quote: During the quarter, we commissioned an additional 3.8 megawatts DC solar power plant, taking the total solar capacity to 9 megawatts DC, and parallel site development at Unit-6 is also progressing as planned. We have also initiated work on a 10 megawatts DC solar plant in Nanded for our captive consumption under the Open Access Scheme.

items.statement: Fertilizer volume target of 300,000 tons for FY26 (vs 260,000 tons achieved in FY25); expects 20% growth in fertilizer business
items.quote: We had planned for total sales of 300,000 tons wherein we couldn't achieve 300,000 tons, we were left at 2,60,000 tons only. In this particular year, we believe, looking at the present situation of the phosphatic fertilizers globally, in my opinion we should be able to achieve at least this target what we had planned for the last year.

items.statement: Rock phosphate purchased at 15-20% lower levels for coming season; prices since improved to 5-7% correction; sulfur prices increased unexpectedly
items.quote: we have bought the product at lower levels of at least 15% to 20% for coming this season. And from thereafter, now I see that the 15%, 20% correction which was there, that has still improved to 5% to 7% level.

items.statement: Global phosphatic fertilizer shortage driving SSP demand; DAP shortage and phosphoric acid price increase creating opportunity for SSP business
items.quote: the phosphatic fertilizer across the globe is in deep shortage , and the prices of like phosphoric acid and D AP has gone up tremendously. So, I believe it's a good opportunity, especially for the SSP business, because of the increase in subsidy there would be an increased demand also because of the shortage of other phosphatic

items.statement: Chemical volumes stable at 56,626 tons (-1% YoY); Fertilizer volumes 2.61 lakh tons (+24% YoY); Chemical revenue Rs 424.6 cr (+7%), Fertilizer revenue Rs 381 cr (+15.8%)
items.quote: The annual volume in the Fertilizer segment is 2.61 lakhs metric tons marking at 24% growth over FY ’24. Chemical volumes remain ed relatively stable at 56, 626 metric tons, marginally lower by 1% on a year-on-year basis

items.statement: Preponed rock phosphate buying by 2 months (Feb-Mar) due to favorable pricing; bought excessive quantity for future fertilizer season
items.quote: We have bought a sufficient rock phosphate, particularly for the coming season of fertilizers in the month of February and March. We generally do not buy this much of quantity, but we thought, and we saw that right now the rock phosphate, which is our major raw material, is at the bottom of level in the last one or two years or so.

items.statement: Bangladesh exposure ~4% of total business; developing Vietnam, Indonesia, Sri Lanka, Egypt markets as alternatives
items.quote: Right, it is hardly 4% of the total business. Even after there is internal disturbance also, we have not seen much impact on the business, and still my confidence level is that this will not have major impact on our relationships with Bangladesh.

items.statement: Net cash from operations improved to Rs 37.5 crore from Rs 16.2 crore; inventory buildup due to preponed rock phosphate purchase
items.quote: Net cash from the operat ions improved significantly to Rs. 37.5 crores from Rs. 16.2 crores in FY ‘24, driven by improved profitability and efficient capital management

items.statement: Acid complex shutdown extended to 52-53 days (vs normal 30-35) due to unforeseen maintenance; forced external acid purchases at higher cost
items.quote: unfortunately our shutdown continued for almost two to two and a half months in our acid complex. Generally, this shutdown is always kept up to a level of 30 to 35 days, but because of some unseen circumstances, there was some major work which came up suddenly beyond our expectation, which took bit longer time for restarting the plant.

items.statement: Promoter equity transfer to mother as part of family trust creation for long-term succession planning and stability
items.quote: We are in the process of making a family trust. So the equity transfer to my mother is a part of the process for our entire equity transferring to the family trust for a long-term succession plan, for a better stability and this long-term sustainability.

items.statement: Management does not provide explicit revenue guidance but expects growth trajectory around 28% YoY average seen in last three years to be the new normal
items.quote: So, I would hope that this is a new normal for the company or in that range. And this is what we try to achieve going forward.

items.statement: SupTech segment grew 34% YoY driven by new wins and ongoing implementations across regulators
items.quote: In terms of segment performance, SupTech led the growth with a 34% year-on-year increase, driven by new wins and ongoing implementations across regulators.

items.statement: TaxTech segment grew 20% YoY aided by Indian tax compliance traction and early work on Malaysian e-invoicing mandate
items.quote: TaxTech grew by 20%, aided by traction in the Indian tax compliance ecosystem and early work on the Malaysian e-invoicing mandate.

items.statement: RegTech segment posted 12% YoY growth with new customers onboarded in Europe and U.S.
items.quote: RegTech posted a 12% growth with new customers onboarded in Europe and U.S. under

items.statement: FY25 EBITDA margin improved to ~17% from ~15% in FY24; other expenses grew 25% YoY to INR44.89 crores due to sales, marketing and partner payments
items.quote: I think the EBITDA margin on a year-to-year basis there is a small increase. It's about 17% versus 15%. In other expenses outside of salaries, we have partner payments, we have SG&A expenses, and we have other general expenses, which come in.

items.statement: South African deposit insurance platform implementation ~35% remaining; Qatar Central Bank deal won; good handful of RFPs in pipeline for SupTech
items.quote: So, I would say maybe about 35% is still left to be executed. And we are working on a number of other deals which are in the pipeline as well.

items.statement: ARR reached ~INR75 crores; recurring revenue share increasing
items.quote: Anyway, if you look at the ARR of the company, that has already gone up. We are at about INR75 crores of ARR roughly.

items.statement: Software development costs for new revenue streams (e.g., Malaysian e-invoicing) are capitalized; other product development expensed
items.quote: Whenever we build new products from which we expect to generate revenue, this is a policy to capitalize those expenses. And also, if we are going for an existing product, but there is a new revenue stream or a mandate which is kicking in and we are developing some modules in that, we go on capitalizing those expenses.

items.statement: Actively recruiting salespeople in North America and Europe; building sales engine and playbook first before deploying resources on ground
items.quote: I think we have been in the phase of recruitment now more actively than ever before in the geographies in North America and, more importantly, Europe.

items.statement: RegTech pivoting to three buckets: XBRL mandates, disclosure management (non-mandate, higher value), and ESG/sustainability reporting; disclosure management seen as key growth driver
items.quote: So clearly, when there is a mandate, what happens is there is a driving imperative for enterprises to immediately adopt a solution. There is an external deadline of pressure. So, we've historically seen tailwinds when mandates are announced. What we were looking at even in the ESG space, there was to be an ESG report ing mandate rolling out from this year, and that was going to provide us added ta

items.statement: TaxTech core is SaaS subscription for GST compliance; expanding into accounts payable automation, litigation management, CFO dashboards; Malaysia e-invoicing launched; targeting Singapore and UAE
items.quote: The core offering of the Taxtech segment is a suite of SaaS platform being sold to enterprises and taxpayers to enable their entire GST compliance, GST filings, returns filing, doing the monthly reconciliation, e-way bill and e-invoici ng, which is charged on a subscription-based model, depending on the number of tax IDs and the volume of transactions that these companies perform on a monthly basi

items.statement: Cross-selling disclosure management to existing 6,000+ customers underway; pipeline growing significantly but sales cycles longer without mandate-driven urgency
items.quote: There is ample opportunity for us to go and cross-sell. We are already in motion and play. In fact, we've already cross-sold disclosure management to multiple existing customers along with new logos. So that is in play.

items.statement: Management does not consider NPST a direct competitor in regulatory reporting (financial/risk reporting); NPST operates in AML/fraud detection
items.quote: Not in the segment we operate. Of course, there are other segments, which includes anti-money laundering and fraud detection, where we don't operate. But in the regulatory reporting area, which is more to do with financial and risk reporting, we haven't come across them.

items.statement: FERC Phase 2 and ESG mandates delayed by legislative/political processes; voluntary ESG reporting provides interim opportunity
items.quote: FERC, there it's a phased rollout. The first phase has been rolled out. You're absolutely right. The second phase is up in discussion. Like I said, it is being run through the legislative procedure within the energy companies in the U.S. So that is happening. Time lines, I don't want to comment. I don't want to get ahead of myself. There is a lot of, I would say, external f actors, political facto

items.statement: Africa contributed 35% of FY25 revenue led by South African Reserve Bank; U.S. and Europe strong for RegTech ARR growth; India stable under TaxTech
items.quote: In terms of geographic mix, Africa contributed 35% of the top line for full year, led by our work with the South African Reserve Bank under SupTech segment. The U.S. and Europe remains strong market for our RegTech products with decent ARR growth. Our Indian business remains stable, primarily under the TaxTech platform.

items.statement: Cash and mutual fund investments ~INR50 crores; INR20 crores raised via private placement plus accruals; cash to be deployed thoughtfully over 3-5 years to scale SaaS business
items.quote: In fact, if you add the mutual fund investments that we have made, cash balance is about INR50 crores. It is not INR35 crores. So, as I mentioned in my first set of remarks, we want to make sure that we are very frugal, and we calibrate our expenses. And we want to do our spends mostly related to our SaaS business. We want to scale it up over the next 3 to 5 years in a substantial way.

items.statement: No debt mentioned; company funded by private placement (INR20 crores) and internal accruals
items.quote: But the money that we raised about INR20 crores through private placement, plus we have generated enough cash through accruals during the last 1 to 2 years. So, both together, the cash balance reflects about INR53 crores or so.

items.statement: Raised INR20 crores via private placement in FY25
items.quote: But the money that we raised about INR20 crores through private placement, plus we have generated enough cash through accruals during the last 1 to 2 years.

items.statement: Acquisitions not in current operating plan but all options on table for 5-year horizon
items.quote: If you look at the next 5 years, I won't be able to answer that question. All kind of options will be on the table, including acquisitions. But this is something definitely not baked into our current operating plan. That's what I would say.

items.statement: Building AI team/cell to drive initiatives across firm; using AI for auto-tagging XBRL, GST litigation responses, development automation
items.quote: We also have a couple of other examples of the use of AI, for example, I think we have also talked in the past of the use of AI in a couple of other instances like, for example, in our GST business where we used it to support our litigation management systems. So, where you can automatically read the litigation or the GST and notice, craft an appropriate first response. So, we have spoken about th

items.statement: SupTech RFP decisions delayed by external factors; some Middle East RFPs stuck since September without evaluation
items.quote: For example, we had bid with one of the Middle East regulators and I think the RFP the bid had got in maybe in September. But even now it has not moved even into the evaluation process. So, there are in situation like that which happens.

items.statement: State/MSME DataTech initiative (Karnataka, Telangana, Goa MOUs) pre-revenue; monetization expected after community build-up; better update in H2 FY26 call
items.quote: We have signed these 3 MOUs with 3 state governments. But like Balu already mentioned at the beginning, this business of ours, which is the MSME or the DataTech business is a pre-revenue business. So, at this point in time, we do not see these as, from a kind of a revenue perspective, we do not see this contributing to revenues in the coming years in any significant or meaningful way.

items.statement: Expects revenue growth to accelerate to 12-15% in FY26 from 8.5% in FY25, with double-digit growth targeted for FY26
items.quote: we are confident of continuing uptick in revenue growth with even better like -to-like growth, higher square foot addition and fast pivot from online B2 B to online B2C

items.statement: Targets EBITDA margin expansion of 100 bps annually going forward
items.quote: We are confident of increasing margins by 100 bps every year going forward.

items.statement: Plans net square foot addition of 1.5 lakh sq ft in FY26, up from 1.22 lakh sq ft in FY25
items.quote: In FY26 in our view, should go up to more than 1.5 lakh square ft., and we want to look at a CAGR of between 12% to 15%, more like 15% for square foot expansion.

items.statement: FY25 EBITDA margin improved 100 bps to 13.8% (INR 637 cr), GP margin up 130 bps to 53.5%
items.quote: Annual EBITDA has gone up by 100 basis points to INR 637 crores, a growth of 17% in value over last year. FY25 EBITDA is now very close to 14% mark.

items.statement: Q4 FY25 EBITDA margin at 14.3%, up 80 bps YoY; GP margin at 53.9%, up 270 bps YoY
items.quote: The EBITDA stood at 14.3%. The gains in EBITDA have flown into PBT and PAT, which have grown handsomely at a healthy pace.

items.statement: Retail LTL growth at 5.2% in Q4 FY25; direct channels (retail + online B2C) growing strongly, wholesale at low single digits
items.quote: In quarter 4 also, all brands have grown double digit in revenue, except for BIS except for footwear, where there are issues with BIS, but which are getting sorted out and the growth in footwear also has gone up.

items.statement: Adjacent categories (footwear, innerwear, womenswear) contribute >20% of revenue, growing ~20%; footwear at INR 300 cr targeting INR 500 cr, innerwear targeting INR 200 cr
items.quote: we have guided that the adjacent category revenue share is more than 20% of the company's revenue. And footwear has already crossed INR 300 crore s mark. It's in the journey to reach INR 500

items.statement: Capex remained at expected range of ~INR 100 cr in FY25 with asset-light mindset
items.quote: And with our asset-light mindset, capex has remained in the expected range of close to INR 100 crores.

items.statement: Added 1.22 lakh net sq ft in FY25 (highest ever), 50 net new stores; average store size increasing
items.quote: We've added nearly 1.2 lakh net square foot in this year, which is one of the highest ever for AFL. So, in this quarter, we added 50,000 square feet, which is again a very healthy pace of expansion.

items.statement: Retail discounting reduced ~2% in Q4 FY25, driving GP margin improvement; marketing spend >4% of revenue in last 3 quarters
items.quote: Discounting reduction of nearly 2% in retail, this is a key achievement of this quarter and is a reflection of the strength of our brand portfolio and the quality of execution.

items.statement: Direct channels (EBO retail + online B2C) gaining revenue mix share; retail mix up 2% in Q4, online B2C growing >25%
items.quote: Retail channel grew 13% and gained 2% of revenue mix. Online B2C business also grew at more than 20%, with significant improvement in channel margins.

items.statement: Wholesale channel at low single-digit growth but tertiary sales at high single digits; inventory cleanup done to improve freshness index
items.quote: Wholesale channel has recorded low single-digit in FY 25, while the consumer sales had grown at a higher single-digit level.

items.statement: Inventory turns improved from 3x to 4x consistently; NWC consistently below 60 days; further improvement expected but at slower pace
items.quote: We moved from 3 turns to 4 turns consistently, if you look at last many quarters. So, from where we are on inventory, for example, further increase will happen.

items.statement: Gross and net debt reduced by ~INR 75 cr in FY25; strong free cash flow generation
items.quote: Business has generated good improvement on FOCF and there is a reduction in debt of nearly INR 75 crores at both gross and net level.

items.statement: ROCE crossed 20% milestone in FY25, up ~400 bps YoY; 3-year revenue CAGR 18%, EBITDA CAGR 36%
items.quote: We are delighted to report that AFL crossed the milestone of generating more than 20% return on capital employed this year.

items.statement: New business development head joining; team beefed up for store expansion
items.quote: We've beefed up the team on business development, a new head is in the process of joining.

items.statement: Growth dependent on market conditions, wholesale channel recovery, and government policy tailwinds (tax, interest rates)
items.quote: While a lot of growth is linked to external market condition and business does get influenced by economic reality, we are confident of continuing uptick in revenue growth.

items.statement: BIS certification issues in footwear largely resolved; inventory availability improving, normal levels expected in 6 months
items.quote: But now BIS is in many ways is behind us. The inventory has started to come. So, in next 6 months, we are very confident that all the supply chain initiatives we have taken on the footwear business, the inventory availability assortment will reach its normal level.

items.statement: Moved to lower 25% tax regime for one subsidiary; exceptional DTA charge of INR 120 cr in Q4; comparable PAT grew >70% YoY
items.quote: As there is better visibility on profitability in one of the subsidiaries, we decided to move to a lower tax regime of 25%, which will be beneficial from a reported PAT, cash flow and ROCE standpoint going forward. This led to an exceptional DTA charge of INR 120 crores in quarter 4.

items.statement: Medium-term guidance: consolidated revenue CAGR ~75% over next 3 fiscals, Operating EBITDA CAGR ~45%, EBITDA margin stabilizing at 11% by FY28, PAT CAGR ~40% with PAT margin ~5% by FY28, ROCE >18%
items.quote: Over the next 3 fiscals, we anticipate consolidated revenue to grow at a CAGR of approximately 75%, driven by the phased commissioning of the Bokaro greenfield project and our organic growth. Operating EBITDA is expected to grow at a CAGR of 45% over the same period with the Operating EBITDA margin stabilizing at 11% by FY '28 as we progressively integrate the new and existing business lines.
