items.quote: indicated in the past, the EBITDA margins on the existing business will be around 23% to 24%. That's a stable state. Jev Mehta: And with respect to the top line? Harsh Bansal: The top line, like I just mentioned to the caller before you, if the only place where we are left to ramp up is the pipes and tubes, if that ramps up to the capacity, we expect maybe INR 850 crores or

items.statement: Greenfield Bokaro project: INR 803 crores over 24 months, Phase 1 operational by end FY26, qualified under PLI 1.1 Scheme
items.quote: Lastly, in a decisive step, the company has initiated a greenfield investment in Bokaro, focused on downstream processing and manufacturing of coated and plated steel. With a total investment of INR 803 crores over the next 24 months, Phase 1 of the facility is expected to be operational by the end of FY '26. We are also proud to be qualified under the Government of India's PLI 1.1 Scheme for this

items.statement: Bokaro project debt ~INR 500 crores out of INR 800 crores outlay; net debt INR 120 crores as of March 2025
items.quote: In terms of the debt for Bokaro, our total project outlay over the next 24 months is expected to be about INR 800-odd crores. And our debt is expected to be in the range of INR 500 crores out of that.

items.statement: Q4 FY25 operating EBITDA margin 21.2% (down from 24.5% Q3) due to INR 12.5 cr low-margin trading; adjusted core margin ~23%
items.quote: The decline in operating EBITDA margin from 24.5% in Quarter 3 FY '25 to 21.2% in Quarter 4 is primarily due to a revenue of INR 12.5 crores from HR, CR, GP coil trading. This activity was undertaken to gain market insights as part of our preparation for the upcoming Bokaro project and generated negligible margins.

items.statement: Blended EBITDA margin to moderate to 11% by FY28 as raw material cost becomes >80% of revenue in new downstream model
items.quote: Accordingly, consolidated Operating EBITDA Margins will moderate as the legacy business blends with a more input-intensive model. However, this should not be viewed as a deterioration in performance. Rather, it reflects a conscious pivot towards scaling volumes, deepening the value chain integration, expanding our market reach and enhancing stakeholder value.

items.statement: Pipe & tube utilization improved substantially in Q4; capacity expansion scaled to 700k tonnes from 1M tonnes
items.quote: So the Quarter 4 numbers are there, you will see a substantial improvement in the utilization of Pipes and Tubes. And this is slower than we had expected. And therefore, we had scaled out our number. But we are seeing a healthy growth that we are hoping it picks up even faster.

items.statement: Long-term contract with key customer (Tata Steel) renewed through FY29; small TMT facility contract mutually short-closed
items.quote: First, we successfully renewed our long-term contracts with our key customer, extending it through FY '29. This reaffirms the trust placed in us and our role as a dependable partner in the steel ecosystem. In addition to this, we have re-affirmed our commitment to the growth in the tube segment and followed it up with further capital outlay.

items.statement: Cash conversion cycle improved to 56 days in March 2025 from 96 days in March 2024 via inventory and receivables management
items.quote: Notably, our Cash Conversion Cycle improved significantly to 56 days in March '25 from 96 days in March '24. This improvement was driven by disciplined working capital management, specifically more efficient inventory utilization aligned with our ongoing capacity expansion and a sharper focus on maintaining lower trade receivables.

items.statement: Input cost variation largely transferable to customers in value-added downstream products
items.quote: And Mehta, just to further clarify to what Sanjeev ji said, in this sector, most of the input variation is transferable to the customers. So there is very little component that one has to absorb when you're talking about value-added.

items.statement: Bokaro project expected IRR 25%+ and payback <=5 years
items.quote: So we expect IRR of 25% plus and a payback not exceeding maybe 5 years.

items.statement: Board recommended final dividend of INR 0.43 per share for FY25
items.quote: We are also delighted to announce that the Board has recommended a final dividend of 0.43 rupees per share, subject to shareholder approval.

items.statement: Bokaro Phase 1 (color coated) by end FY26, further phases FY27, full stabilized operations FY28; pipe & tube capacity 534k tonnes
items.quote: So Mehta, the expansion will happen over the next 24 months. The reason why we have given a guidance up to FY '28 is because that will be the first year of full operations. And so you will have certain plants coming on line in FY '25. Certain more -- sorry, FY '26, certain more in FY '27 and we expect the plant to operate in fully commissioned mode in FY '28.

items.statement: Management will actively consider equity raise suggestion to fund expansion instead of pure debt
items.quote: I very well appreciate that suggestion, Bhavesh ji. We will take it into active consideration. Thank you so much.

items.statement: Interest cost to rise to INR 3-4 crores/quarter from INR 1.3-1.4 crores in Q4 as new borrowings kick in
items.quote: no, it will not be INR 1 crore. It will be similar to the previous quarters. Harsh Bansal: That's right. Bhavesh: Similar to previous quarters, so INR 3 crores to INR 4 crores? Harsh Bansal: Yes. Yes

items.statement: Qualified under Government of India PLI 1.1 Scheme for Bokaro investment
items.quote: We are also proud to be qualified under the Government of India's PLI 1.1 Scheme for this investment.

items.statement: Bokaro Phase 1: color coated steel for construction, housing, warehouses; subsequent phases for defense and solar
items.quote: It will be from this plant, but some of the products which may follow subsequent to Color Coated.

items.statement: Order book at end of Q4 FY25 stood at INR24,346 crores; 30 projects worth INR14,370 crores under execution as on date
items.quote: Moving on the update on the order book, at the end of Q4 of the order book stood at INR24,346 crores. As on date, the company has 30 projects worth INR14,370 crores that are under execution.

items.statement: Two projects worth INR4,810 crores awaiting appointed date; four projects worth INR5,166 crores at L1 status; bids of INR6,500 crores yet to be opened
items.quote: As on date, two projects worth INR4,810 crores are awaiting appointed date, one in HAM in Bihar and one DBFOT toll project spreading across Rajasthan, UP and MP. For four projects that is two roads and one each railway and OFC worth INR5,166 crores are having L1 status.

items.statement: FY26 order inflow target of INR20,000 crores across sectors including highways INR11,500 crores, railway INR2,000 crores, metro INR1,000 crores, power transmission INR2,000 crores, ropeway/hydro/tunnel INR3,500 crores, logistics and telecom
items.quote: And for this, the target of this year's order booking is around INR20,000 crores. In the highway sector, there is INR11,500 crores. In the railway, there is 2,000 crores. In the metro, there is INR1,000 crores In the railway and metro, there is 3,000 crores In the power transmission, there is INR2,000 crores. In the ropeway and hydro and tunnel, there is INR3,500 crores. And in logistics and telec

items.statement: Normalized EBITDA margin expected to remain flat around 12%-13% for FY26 and FY27 due to competitive pressure and escalation issues
items.quote: Look, we should still consider the margin as flat. So, there are a lot of things, one is the pressure of our competition, and apart from that, the prices in the market, the way there are escalation issues, we have flat expectations on that.

items.statement: Q4 FY25 standalone EBITDA margin at 17.51% vs 17.69% in Q4 FY24; FY25 full year standalone margin 13.88% vs 14.58% in FY24
items.quote: Revenue from operations in Q4 of '25 stood at INR2,129.30 crores as against INR2,310.35 crores in the corresponding period in previous financial year. The EBITDA margin for the current quarter stood at 17.51% as against 17.69% in the corresponding period in previous financial year.

items.statement: FY25 capex INR135 crores including corporate office building; FY26 capex target INR100-125 crores including INR40-50 crores for corporate office
items.quote: 2025 capex in machinery is in the range of INR70 crores, INR80 crores. But then we are building our corporate office as well. So, total capex which has to be including that corporate office building and machinery is around INR135 crores. INR135 crores, INR134 crores. And for next year, we are targeting another INR100 crores, INR125 crores not more than that.

items.statement: Repaid INR361 crores debt in Q4 FY25; standalone debt-equity improved to 0.07x; consolidated debt-equity 0.59x with INR4,966 crores borrowings
items.quote: During the quarter, the company has repaid the debt of INR361 crores which has resulted in improved debt equity ratio to 0.07 which is one of the best in the sector.

items.statement: Working capital days increased to 117 days in FY25 from 112 days in FY24 due to increase in SPV debtors; standalone trade receivables INR1,842 crores including INR1,691 crores HAM debtors
items.quote: The working capital in days at the end of fiscal 2025 is INR117 days as compared to INR112 days at the end of fiscal 2024. This increase is primarily on account of increase in SPV debtors.

items.statement: Transferred one operational HAM asset to Indus Infra InvIT for INR225.58 crores; gain shown as exceptional item; InvIT dividend income targeted at INR225-250 crores annually
items.quote: During the quarter, the company transferred one operational HAM asset to Indus Infra InvIT for a total consideration of INR225.58 crores. The resulting gain on this transaction is shown as an exceptional item in financial statements.

items.statement: MoRTH imposed additional performance security for bids below estimated cost and mandated timelines for land/environment clearances to synchronize approval and awarding process
items.quote: Further, MoRTH has imposed additional performance security on bidders of road projects for bids lower than estimated cost of the project. Also, it mandates timelines for land and environment clearances. It gives us the confidence to enhance our order book as the initiatives are designed to better synchronize the approval, awarding process, and declaration of appointed dates.

items.statement: Two Maharashtra EPC projects at L1 worth INR4,300 crores awaiting land acquisition; LOA expected between Q2 and Q3 FY26
items.quote: This is an EPC project of Maharashtra State Government and we are expecting that it should come in between the second and third quarter because the land acquisition work is still going on, not been done. There are some issues in the land. So, as soon as the land acquisition is done, it will be 80% safe. Government will award these projects.

items.statement: Five operational HAM assets eligible for InvIT transfer (four received COD in FY25); power transmission InvIT MOU expired; evaluating monetization options for BOT and power transmission assets
items.quote: So, as on date, we are having five more operational assets. So, the operational assets in last year, there are four assets, which we have received COD in last year. And to put it in InvIT, the condition is 1 year of track record of operation. So, whatever COD we took in last year, that can be transferred to that InvIT.

items.statement: Equity investment in HAM/BOT projects: INR2,000 crores invested so far, INR2,875 crores pending over next 3 years; targeting INR1,000 crores in FY26 and INR1,000 crores in FY27
items.quote: So total equity so far, we have invested INR2,000 crores and still pending is INR2,875-odd crores, which is to be put in over the next 3 years of time. For current year, we are targeting INR1,000 crores number. And for next year, again, it would be in the same range INR1,000 crores.

items.statement: Competitive bidding up to 46% below estimate persists; awarding activity muted in first three quarters of FY25 but picked up in Q4; government focus on infrastructure with INR11.21 lakh crores capex outlay in Union Budget 2025-26
items.quote: Also, the instances under bidding up to 46% continue to persist. This is although concerning and we are continuing to keep a close watch. We do accept a decent flow of awarding utilities, especially large projects, continuing in the next financial year. As the Central Government continues to focus on infrastructure development, this is evident from the fact that the capital investment outlay for t

items.statement: Highway sector pipeline INR75,000 crores; government announced 22 new greenfield expressways and 30,000 km two-lane to four-lane conversion with INR10 lakh crores investment; metro network to double to 1,700 km by FY26
items.quote: Investment in national highways and expressways are projected to grow by 1.4x between financial year '26 and financial year '29. Government targets building 22 new greenfield expressways. Recently, Government has announced to convert 30,000 km two-lane highways into four-lane with an investment of INR10 lakh crores.

items.statement: No management changes mentioned; strong team and focus on project delivery highlighted as success drivers
items.quote: Our strong team and focus on project delivery will continue to drive our success.

items.statement: Management expects long-term revenue CAGR of ~30% and believes 2-3x industry growth is typical, though health is currently growing 4-5x industry rate.
items.quote: From a long-term perspective, we believe 30% is the right CAGR for us to sort of p lan for. However, I'm honestly being surprised by health, but at the same time let me kind of put it to you another

items.statement: Health insurance demand remains very strong, growing 4-5x industry rate for 9 consecutive quarters, driven by younger customers (30-40 age group) experiencing hospitalization incidents.
items.quote: In health we seem to be doing it up to 4-5x of the industry growth rates on an overall basis for new business acquisition. Now see the real deal for Policybazaar has been that the customers come to us.

items.statement: Renewals contribution margin now estimated at 77-80% (down from prior 85% disclosure) due to smarter cost allocation including claims and customer service costs.
items.quote: At this point, what I would say is, it's somewhere between 77% to 80%, that is where we are. Of course, some streams like life might be at 93% but overall it comes around at that point.

items.statement: Total insurance premium for FY25 was ₹23,486 Cr (up 45% YoY in new core online premium); Q4 premium ₹7,030 Cr (up 37% YoY).
items.quote: With this, the total insurance premium for the year was ₹23,486 Cr, with a growth of 45% in the new core online insurance premium and 48% in the new health and life insurance premium.

items.statement: Trail revenue (ARR) grew 42% YoY to ₹817 Cr in Q4 FY25, a key driver of long-term profit growth.
items.quote: Our trail revenue is now at ₹817 Cr from ₹577 Cr last year in the same quarter; 42% growth YoY. This is at an ARR of ₹817 Cr.

items.statement: Core business premium split: ₹16,144 Cr total; POSP ~₹5,000 Cr; Corporate ~₹1,000 Cr; Dubai ~₹1,100 Cr; new vs renewal ~50:50.
items.quote: Our core business is ₹16,144 Cr for the year. POSP is about ₹5,000 Cr; Corporate is about ₹1,000 Cr; Dubai is a little more than ₹1,100 Cr. On the core; new and renewal continue to be at about 50:50.

items.statement: Healthcare initiative: acquired one hospital asset, planning to buy 2-3 operating hospitals and 2-3 shell projects in NCR; hiring doctors and hospital builders; long-term project with no rapid changes expected.
items.quote: We've had the round, we've had the money come in, we've acquired one asset, in the sense we paid for it, we've taken it over. We are looking to do the same with maybe 3-4 other assets.

items.statement: Fresh health business operates at -15% to -20% margin; renewals at high profitability; core online (ex fresh health & renewals) at ~20% margin; new initiatives at 0 to few % margin.
items.quote: The fresh health bus iness, we are getting sharper and sharper at defining this, comes at a negative margin, of 15% -20%. And the renewals business comes at a fairly high profitable cliff. On the other hand, our overall core business, if you leave out renewals, and if you leave out fresh health, that operates at broadly a 20% kind of margin

items.statement: Receivables increased due to 1/n commission accounting by insurers and shift to monthly premium collection mode in health; impact to normalize over 2-3 quarters and play out over couple of years.
items.quote: Receivables have got multiple things but one of the big shifts that's going to drive over the next few years, and we should all keep that in mind is going to be the 1/n, which essentially means that while the business is happening, there is a shift in how the money is being collected.

items.statement: Q4 call centre costs flat QoQ (vs growth in Q2/Q3); some volume-based incentives back-loaded to Q4 but missed savings targets reduced this benefit.
items.quote: Our Q4 call centre cost, we did not grow it. But the way we do most of our accounting, we have some volume-based targets and some volume-based incentive targets, etc. We don't account for them till they are hit.

items.statement: Closing cash balance ₹5,400 Cr; no debt raise or repayment discussed.
items.quote: Our closing cash balance was ₹5,400 Cr.

items.statement: UAE insurance premium grew 76% YoY and turned profitable; management confident profitability is sustainable.
items.quote: Our UAE insurance premium has grown 76% YoY, and there is a bit of a positive surprise there. That business has turned profitable and I feel confident it's turned profitable kind of forever.

items.statement: Motor and two-wheeler insurance returned to >30% growth after period of subdued performance.
items.quote: We have seen other parts of our business -like motor, two-wheeler and travel returning to the above 30% growth which it wasn't for some time.

items.statement: Savings business challenged with negative industry growth in Feb-Mar; focusing on pension, child insurance, capital guarantee solutions to revive growth.
items.quote: I think our savings business at this point is very challenged. We are struggling to grow, and we're thinking very hard on that - how do we grow. Of course, there's a pensions area, there is a child insurance area.

items.statement: PB Partners (agent platform) shifting to smaller, higher-quality advisors; employee-per-business ratio improving; platform leads market in scale and efficiency.
items.quote: We have moved the business increasingly towards smaller and higher quality advisors, so we're working a lot on that. And it's showing a very decided move in that direction and consistently so.

items.statement: Policybazaar channel is most profitable and fastest-growing for insurers due to deep tech integration, low OpEx, and better claims ratios from new customer acquisition.
items.quote: Overall, this is the most profitable and fastest growing channel for all of these insurance companies, and the way our discussions happen with them in terms of new product introductions, all the innovation that we can do for the customer, the claim servicing part, everything continues to be very, very strong.

items.statement: IRDAI 1/n commission accounting and monthly premium modes impacting receivables; insurers focused on combined operating ratio but Policybazaar channel pressures manageable, no change in economic structure seen.
items.quote: Clearly now health insurers, like other general insurers, are focused on the combined operating ratio. I think on that basis, if I were to summarize what Yashish said, our channel comes out on a fairly attractive end of the spectrum.

items.statement: Health renewal persistency at all-time highs: R1 (first-year) persistency at record levels driven by high No Claim Bonus products; R2+ (second year+) steady.
items.quote: Our first-year persistency has increased a lot, and we are at all-time highs. Our R2+, which is second year and beyond is very consistent, it has largely been very steady over the last few years.

items.statement: AI viewed as opportunity for customer service automation (renewals, claims, endorsements) and sales efficiency (reducing non-talk time, agent prompts); 'man in the middle' model preferred; tech cost savings expected.
items.quote: The biggest impact of deep tech for everyone, including us, is on the customer service because that can be automated to a large extent as we look for next 1-3 years. This include renewals, claim support, all sort of endorsements, all sort of service elements.

items.statement: Headcount optimization in call centres expected over 3 years as AI automates service and sales processes; consumer brand seen as key differentiator as AI becomes commodity.
items.quote: If you look at it on a year on year basis, if I look three years out, a lot of things would have happened, and I see no reason why that wouldn't happen.

items.statement: PB Money platform scaling for deeper customer risk understanding (income data) and cross-sell of savings products (bonds, FDs, mutual funds); monetization via direct savings sales and indirect credit underwriting improvement.
items.quote: Monetization largely will come from selling bonds and fixed deposits this year, and it also helps indirectly in monetization, because we have a better understanding of a customer's credit, and hence it will lead to growth in some of our unsecured lending areas.

items.statement: Expects product growth to sustain at mid to high-teens in FY26
items.quote: Notwithstanding, I would say, mixed and challenging market conditions, we expect the product growth levels to sustain at mid to high -teens.

items.statement: A&SP spends will continue to step up in FY26 to drive growth
items.quote: Our spends and our investments in advertising and promotion, will sustain as we grow our categories and grow our business.

items.statement: Full year growth and full year margin expansion ambition for FY26
items.quote: To conclude, we would stay focused on our ambition of driving full year growth and full year margin expansion.

items.statement: Category growth in water, cleaning, air has decisively inflected to mid to high-teens
items.quote: The categories in which we operate, water, cleaning, etcetera, all have decisively inflected in the trajectory enabled by our own innovation and interventions, increased category visibility and activity and greater recognition by consumers on the importance of health and hygiene.

items.statement: Robotics segment growing 75-110% YoY for next few years
items.quote: Robotics as a segment has been growing by 100% YoY for the last 3 years or more and we expect that rate to be in the same ballpark of between 75%, 80% to 100%, 110% in the next few years as well.

items.statement: FY25 adjusted EBITDA margin expanded 136 bps to 11.7% despite 121 bps higher A&SP
items.quote: Margins grew YoY in every single quarter , and we ended the year with 11.7% margin, an expansion of 136 basis points over FY24. It may be noted that this expansion is after 121 basis points increase in advertising and promotion expenses.

items.statement: Q4 FY25 adjusted EBITDA margin reached 13%, up 183 bps YoY
items.quote: Adjusted EBITDA margins expanded 183 basis points YoY, and we ended the year with a 13% margin in Q4.

items.statement: Gross margins range-bound at 58.3% for FY25 vs 58.8% in FY24
items.quote: Gross margins have been range bound and for the year , were at 58.3% versus 58.8% in FY 24.

items.statement: Service business gross margin profile structurally higher than product business
items.quote: No, the service business will always have a gross margin profile, which is much higher than the product business. So that is something which will continue.

items.statement: ESOP charges on steady state basis will be Rs 5-5.5 crores per quarter
items.quote: On a steady state basis, this charge will be in the range of Rs. 5 crores to Rs. 5.5 crores every quarter.

items.statement: AMC unit sales grew in FY25; green shoots visible in service revenue
items.quote: We've also made many interventions to drive service revenue which have led to a growth in AMC unit sales last year. I'm pleased to share that we are now seeing green shoots in terms of service revenue.

items.statement: AMC booking is lead indicator of future service revenue; value growth beginning to come through
items.quote: AMC booking is the lead indicator of future revenue. And I think there, we are seeing value growth beginning to come through.

items.statement: Cost program institutionalized; IT costs reduced in absolute terms; vendor renegotiations yielding price advantages
items.quote: We've done several interventions in terms of technology, in terms of contract changes, in terms of renegotiations, etcetera. And I'm pleased to share that we've seen those effects come out, and when you see the numbers that will come up in the annual report, you will see the impact of that play out, not just in percentage revenue terms, but even in absolute terms, so that's one area.

items.statement: COGS optimization through vendor negotiations and bill-of-materials review
items.quote: We've now had volume growth for a while now. And now when we are going back to our vendors and discussing prices and sharing our plans for the coming year, the reaction and the support and the partnership that we are getting from them is giving us very clear price advantages.

items.statement: Premium portfolio grew faster than average, enabling balanced portfolio across price points
items.quote: Our premium portfolio grew faster overall versus our average growth last year. We talked about our high-teens growth overall and within that, premium grew faster and allowed us to clearly balance our portfolio.

items.statement: Launched 2-year filter life products (Aura 2x, Aquaguard Enhance NXT) to reduce cost of ownership
items.quote: The product that was launched online last year was called Aura 2x and what has been rolled out in modern trade and retail is a product called Aquaguard Enhance NXT, both of them have a 2-year filter life, in other words, filters need to be changed only after 2 years.

items.statement: Signed Shraddha Kapoor as brand ambassador for vacuum cleaner portfolio
items.quote: On a related note, I'm happy to share that we have signed up Shraddha Kapoor as a brand ambassador for our vacuum cleaner portfolio.

items.statement: Market leader in robotics despite fierce global competition; category growth benefits Eureka Forbes
items.quote: Despite fierce competition from other global players, we are now the market leaders in robotics. And you will see us build out the portfolio even further, and increase our investments , both on the go -to-market side and on the category creation and awareness creation side.

items.statement: Third-party service providers addressed via call masking, QR code filters, tiered AMCs, consumer campaigns, technician incentives
items.quote: First, I would say, at a very basic level, the first port of call was to make sure that the customer data does not go to these particular players. And hence, we had put in call masking , 1.5 years back. So today for example, a customer would not know a technician's number or vice versa, so that's one example that is there.

items.statement: Net surplus of Rs 284 crores at FY25 year-end (excluding lease liability)
items.quote: Our net surplus at year-end, excluding lease liability, was Rs. 284 crores.

items.statement: Finance costs reduced 42.1% YoY in FY25 due to cash generation
items.quote: Cash generation led to a 42.1% reduction in finance costs.

items.statement: Technician app launched with lock feature preventing new calls until pending complaints resolved
items.quote: About 3 months back, we have launched a new technician app, and that's gone live over the last 45 days or so. One element of that just to illustrate and to respond to your question, one feature of that is that if there is a customer pending complaint open, no other call can be attended until that complaint is resolved.

items.statement: NPS at lifetime high levels in FY25 including Q4
items.quote: Our NPS levels now are at lifetime high levels and beyond what we've had ever in the past.

items.statement: Service failure moments remain a focus area; edge cases need better management
items.quote: But in the edge cases, when there is a service failure, we need to get better at managing those service failure moments. Good service brands, every service brand will have moments of failure, that's the universal truth. But how you manage the moment of failure, how do we resurrect and salvage that customer and win the customer back is the critical differentiating strength for service brands, and t

items.statement: Exceptional net income of Rs 2.1 crores in Q4 FY25 from insurance claim (Rs 10 cr) net of inventory write-off (Rs 7.9 cr)
items.quote: This quarter had an exceptional net income of Rs. 2.1 crores. This has two parts. One part relates to the receipt of full and final insurance claim settlement for the fire at our Delhi warehouse last year. This amount is Rs. 10 crores. There were non -cash charges of Rs. 7.9 crores which were incurred related to inventory write-off.

items.statement: Capex intensity target of 3.5-4% of revenue long-term; FY25 Capex at 5.2% of revenue
items.quote: We anticipate going forward that Capex intensity in the business will continue to remain largely stable and slowly taper its way towards our long- term targets of between 3.5% and 4%.

items.statement: FY27 Capex expected to hit 4% range due to Ecom Express automation assets reducing need for new parcel sortation systems
items.quote: I think there is a fair bit of chance that in FY27, we will be able to start hitting our long-term Capex targets on the back of excess automation equipment that we will acquire in Ecom acquisition.

items.statement: PTL service EBITDA margin expanded 700bps QoQ to 10.8% in Q4 FY25 driven by yield improvement, operating leverage, fleet utilization
items.quote: The big change obviously is in the Part Truckload business where service EBITDA margins have grown from 3.8% in Q3 FY25 to 10.8% in Q4 FY25, an expansion of 700 basis points.

items.statement: Express Parcel service EBITDA margin 15.9% in Q4 FY25 vs 15.6% in Q3; FY25 margin 16.2% vs 18.4% in FY24 due to pricing overhang
items.quote: The Express Parcel business came in at 15.9% in Q4 in terms of service EBITDA versus 15.6% in Q3. Overall, there continues to be an overhang from Q3 and from some of the pricing actions that we saw last financial year.

items.statement: Expect Express Parcel margins to expand in FY26 and beyond as pricing overhang clears and Ecom Express volumes integrate
items.quote: We do anticipate, however, that margins will expand in FY26 and beyond.

items.statement: PTL tonnage grew 19.4% YoY and 11% QoQ to 460,000 tons in Q4 FY25; FY25 tonnage 1.7M tons, up 18.7% YoY
items.quote: Overall tonnage has grown from 384,000 tons of freight to nearly 460,000 tons of freight in Q4 FY25, which is a 19% growth YoY and an 11% growth QoQ.

items.statement: Express Parcel volumes flat YoY at 177M packages in Q4 FY25; FY25 volumes 752M, flat YoY but up 90M vs FY23
items.quote: We delivered 177 million packages in our Express Parcel business, year -on-year largely flat and about 460,000 tons of freight in our Part Truckload business.

items.statement: Active customer base grew from 33,000 to 44,000 YoY; driven by both PTL SME push via Delhivery One and Express Parcel
items.quote: The total active customer base of the company has continued to expand rapidly. We had 33,000 customers at the same time last year. We ended Q4 FY25 with an overall customer count of about 44,000.

items.statement: Largest customer revenue share ~16%, no material change YoY; PTL growth reduced concentration
items.quote: Last year we disclosed that our largest customer was about 16% of our revenues, 16%, I don't think there is a material change to this number.

items.statement: PTL yield improved to Rs 11.3/kg in Q4 FY25 from Rs 10.9/kg in Q4 FY24; like-for-like stronger due to HPCL lower-yield volume
items.quote: Overall, yields have gone up, I think to about Rs. 11.3 per kilo of freight delivered compared to, I think, Rs. 10.9 in Q4 of FY24.

items.statement: Delhivery did not lead pricing move in FY25; competitors priced at negative gross margins; suicidal pricing largely ended
items.quote: I think last year was the one year where we did not lead the pricing move in the market. As I've mentioned, we did see that competition in this industry, in order to wrest short -term market share, took certain pricing calls, which at that time and perhaps in hindsight, we judged correctly.

items.statement: Fleet utilization improved from ~65% pre-Q3 to >70% in Q4 FY25; definition of capacity changing due to better routing, loading, software
items.quote: I think, look, we've always said that our utilization prior to Q3 was in the sort of 65% kind of range. Q4 on a similar comparable basis would have gone beyond 70%.

items.statement: Real estate reduced from 20.5M to 20.1M sq ft QoQ; gateways constant at 111, automated sort centers at 45, sorters at 65
items.quote: If you go back to the statistics slide at the start, the reduction in real estate is actually not that significant. I think it's from about 20.5 million square feet to about 20.1 million square feet or thereabouts.

items.statement: Ecom Express acquisition under CCI review; integration cost Rs 300 cr (lease liabilities + operating losses); volume retention assumption 30% of Ecom standalone
items.quote: Our purchase consideration already includes or factors in about Rs. 300 crores of integration costs. These have been considered, and we anticipate that we should be well within this envelope.

items.statement: Ecom Express volumes ~40% of Delhivery Express Parcel volumes; network tonnage <20% of Delhivery; integration lower risk than Spoton
items.quote: In terms of relative scale, Ecom Express' volumes are about 40% of Delhivery's Express Parcel volumes. In terms of overall tonnage or freight carried, the network tonnage of Ecom Express' network is less than 20% of Delhivery's total tonnage.

items.statement: Early volume migration from Ecom to Delhivery seen in March-May; April and May volumes higher than March despite seasonality
items.quote: From there going into March, we saw an uptick in overall volumes as customers began to shift some of their volumes into the Delhivery network. On formal announcement of the deal, this has continued and has been solidified.

items.statement: Express Parcel and PTL working capital days near target; 2-3 days improvement room each; Supply Chain Services has significant room; overall 1-2 days improvement over 2-3 years
items.quote: I think there is still room to reduce working capital days in these two businesses by two to three days for each of them. However, in our Supply Chain Services business, we have a significant room for improvement.

items.statement: Rapid commerce: 18 dark stores in 3 cities; older stores at 350-400 orders/day; target 50 stores in FY26; breakeven at 700-800 orders/day in 4-5 months
items.quote: We are in three cities as of this quarter and about 18 dark stores. In terms of orders per dark stores, the older dark stores are now clocking at about 350 to 400 orders per day, while the newer ones, of course, have a certain ramp up time.

items.statement: Delhivery Direct (on-demand 2W/3W) launched in Ahmedabad, Delhi, Mumbai; Bangalore in 45 days; supply creation phase losses
items.quote: We've also launched Delhi and Bombay, so there will be some amount of burn that will come from those two locations. And as those start scaling up, I think our anticipation is once we get to perhaps a couple of thousand orders a day in these cities that burn also starts dropping very significantly.

items.statement: Delhivery only profitable 3PL player; competitors with Ecom-like models saw loss expansion in Q4; consolidation inevitable for loss-making networks
items.quote: At the pricing that currently prevails in the market, Delhivery is the only profitable player in this industry and to the best of our understanding our remaining competitors with model similar to Ecom Express have also seen an expansion in their losses in Q4.

items.statement: Captive logistics more expensive and less reliable than Delhivery; marketplaces seeking nuanced off-ramp (heavy goods, specific destinations, B2B)
items.quote: Financially, I've said this before, the captive model is more expensive and a franchise based captive model also delivers less reliable service than the Delhivery model.

items.statement: PTL growth runway unchanged; 80% of market unorganized; Delhivery organizing industry; will continue profitable growth
items.quote: The reality is that Delhivery is effectively organizing this industry. And as long as, whatever, nearly 80% of this industry continues to remain unorganized, there's very, very large headroom for growth for Delhivery in this space.

items.statement: Express Parcel: industry growth irrelevant; Delhivery gains share in both growth and sluggish scenarios due to cost/service advantage
items.quote: Irrespective of what happens to the market. I think from a Delhivery standpoint, we are very satisfied with where we are, and we anticipate that with this acquisition and consolidation, there will be additional growth in our parcel volumes.

items.statement: Express Parcel margin decline due to parcel mix shift (weight, distance, client mix); no structural change; expect return to 18% margins
items.quote: It is entirely down to parcel mix. It's not just the mix in terms of clients, it's also the mix in terms of weight and distances, both of which also have an impact on overall profitability.

items.statement: Cash and equivalents Rs 5,493 cr pre-Ecom Express consideration payout
items.quote: The company continues to be extremely well capitalized. We have about Rs. 5,493 crores of cash and cash equivalents on the balance sheet.

items.statement: Management does not provide specific numerical forecasts but targets continued historical growth excluding one-time large orders
items.quote: generally we do not give any forecast in th e number per se. However, what you have said is I will say right. But the way we work right now is , because we knew from day one that these are one-time orders and may or may not repeat, so from day one how we have kept even internal targets and everything that we always exclude those one-time orders from the revenue that we are doing as well as our gro

items.statement: Healthy demand for product offerings expected to continue driven by electronics adoption and government manufacturing policies
items.quote: The overall year was marked by healthy demand for our product offerings. And we are optimistic that this demand will continue. As we always say, electronics is becoming a big part of life day by day, as well as the alignment of government policies for manu facturing in India, especially in the segment of electronics

items.statement: Geopolitical tension (Pahalgam incident) subdued a strong start to FY26; management maintains 30-35% growth forecast.
items.quote: This current, little border issue that after Pahalgam that happened, unfortunately, it has had its ripple effect on business. It's not that it's not, without totally without consequence. So from what was a sterling quarter that was starting off, it got subdued very badly.

items.statement: Semiconductor gas qualification takes 2-3 years per product but creates high entry barriers and stable, high-margin revenue once approved.
items.quote: There's an approval process. Each product will take two to three years to get approved. Once it's approved, it's like an entry barrier. Nobody else can enter.

items.statement: HPC business aims to double in about 4.5 years at current growth rate
items.quote: the target is that we should be double of where we currently are, at this rate in about four and a-half years' time

items.statement: Foods business targets 8-10% growth and recovery of market share in ethnic foods category
items.quote: we should not only be able to arrest it, but we will continue to grow between 8% to 10% growth that we have set for ourselves

items.statement: Palm plantation targets 0.5 million hectares over next 5 years covering 60% of requirement
items.quote: We reiterate our plan to take area under plantation to 0.5 million hectares over next five years, which will cover about 60% of our requirement

items.statement: Palm plantation expansion: 40,000 hectares in FY26, 125,000 hectares in FY27
items.quote: this year the target is that we should do 40,000 hectares, next year the pick-up will be 125,000 hectares

items.statement: Palm plantation EBITDA margin expected at 16-18% consistently
items.quote: we are pretty confident of this being in the ballpark range of 16% to 18% on a consistent basis

items.statement: Oral Care targets 10% growth driven by new variants and deeper segmentation
items.quote: the target is that if we can continue to grow higher than the market, at somewhere around 10% is the ballpark number for dental care

items.statement: Foods portfolio targets 8-10% EBITDA margin construct
items.quote: between 8% to 10% margin construct that we have always maintained in the Food business overall, we will do that

items.statement: Edible Oil volume growth expected at 2-3% in FY26
items.quote: On Edible Oil, though, the growth that we see in volumes is typically between 2% and 3%, and we are pretty confident of getting it back this year

items.statement: Total cultivated land at 89,546 hectares with 44.81% in prime 7-25 year age bracket
items.quote: As of March '25, our total cultivated land stood at Rs. 89,546 hectares, with 44.81% of our plantation falling within the prime age bracket of 7 years to 25 years

items.statement: Signed MOU with Manipur government for 2,700 hectares oil palm cultivation starting April 2025
items.quote: we recently signed a MOU with the Government of Manipur under National Mission on Edible Oils - Oil Palm. We are set to cultivate 2,700 hectares of oil palm plantations. The cultivation has begun from April '25

items.statement: Expect demand revival in H2 FY26 from income tax relief, falling food inflation, summer and wedding season
items.quote: The falling cost basket of Food inflation, along with lower taxes and other supportive government policies is likely to aid a recovery in mass market urban demand. This impact should be visible from the second half of the fiscal year

items.statement: Q4 FY25 consolidated: Revenue Rs 9,692.21 cr (17.8% YoY), Gross margin 17.09%, EBITDA margin 5.87%, PAT margin 3.68%
items.value: Revenue Rs. 9,692.21 crores; Gross margin 17.09%; EBITDA margin 5.87%; PAT margin 3.68%
items.quote: Our revenue from operations stood at Rs. 9,692.21 crores, with 17.8% growth on year-on-year basis. The gross profits were Rs. 1,656.39 crores, with a margin of 17.09%. The total EBITDA came in at Rs. 568.88 crores, reflecting a margin of 5.87%. And while PAT was Rs. 358.54 crores, with a margin of 3.68%.

items.statement: FY25: Total income Rs 34,289.40 cr, EBITDA Rs 2,079.06 cr (36.89% YoY), PAT Rs 1,301.34 cr (70.08% YoY)
items.value: Total income Rs. 34,289.40 crores; EBITDA Rs. 2,079.06 crores; PAT Rs. 1,301.34 crores
items.quote: The total income stood at Rs. 34,289.40 crores; the total EBITDA of Rs. 2,079.06 crores, with year-on-year growth of 36.89%; PAT grew by 70.08% to reach Rs. 1,301.34 crores.

items.statement: HPC segment Q4: Revenue Rs 728.48 cr, EBITDA margin 15.74%
items.quote: the quarterly revenue for the HPC business segment amounted to Rs. 728.48 crores and the EBITDA margin was 15.74%

items.statement: Edible Oil segment Q4: Revenue Rs 6,764.08 cr, EBITDA margin 4.66%
items.quote: Our Edible Oil business posted revenues of Rs. 6,764.08 crores, with an EBITDA margin of 4.66%.

items.statement: Palm plantation segment Q4: Revenue Rs 229.32 cr, EBITDA margin 5.27%
items.quote: Within this, the palm plantation segment generated revenue of Rs. 229.32 crores, with EBITDA margin of 5.27%.

items.statement: Direct distribution at 2 million outlets, indirect estimated at 1-1.25x direct; products available at 4+ million outlets
items.quote: This is a direct distribution, and our estimation is that to more than 100% of this, 1:1 or maybe even 1.25x of this should be indirect distribution. So, all the sort of work, so currently our products are available at more than 4 million retail outlets, 2 million directly

items.statement: Key commodity prices (palm oil, wheat, sugar, rice) remained elevated in Q4 exerting cost pressure
items.quote: On the cost front, the key commodity prices, particularly palm oil, wheat, sugar and rice remained at elevated levels during the quarter, exerting significant cost pressures.

items.statement: HPC revenue mix: Dental Rs 398.14 cr, Skin Rs 178.49 cr, Home Rs 88 cr, Hair & others balance
items.value: Dental Rs. 398.14 crores; Skin Rs. 178.49 crores; Home Rs. 88 crores
items.quote: Of the HPC segment, the dental care revenue was recorded at Rs. 398.14 crores, followed by skin care at Rs. 178.49 crores, home care at Rs. 88 crores, and the balance for hair care and other products.

items.statement: Modern trade grew 7% YoY, e-commerce grew 28% YoY in FY25
items.quote: FY '25 saw 7% year-on-year growth in the modern retail sales and 28% rise in e-commerce.

items.statement: Signed MOU with Manipur govt under National Mission on Edible Oils - Oil Palm for 2,700 hectares
items.quote: we recently signed a MOU with the Government of Manipur under National Mission on Edible Oils - Oil Palm. We are set to cultivate 2,700 hectares of oil palm plantations

items.statement: No major capex plans for next 4 years; regular maintenance capex only
items.quote: right now there are no major CAPEX plans that we have on cards to be spent over next four years, we do not need to spend on CAPEX

items.statement: ESOP cost Rs 122 cr in FY25 (Rs 10 cr/month) for fair valuation adjustment
items.quote: This year we have debited near about Rs. 122 crores, Rs. 10 crores per month as ESOP cost for the fair valuation adjustment of ESOPs into the cost.

items.statement: Edible oil volumes: 23.64 lakh tons FY25 (down 5% YoY); Palm 10.5L tons, Soybean 5.4L tons, Sunflower 1.4L tons, Mustard 60K tons
items.quote: The overall quantity that we have done is 23.64 lakh metric tons, 2.36 million tons. Out of this, 10.5 lakh tons is palm oil, 5.4 lakh tons is soybean oil, 60,000 tons is mustard oil, 1.4 lakh tons is sunflower oil

items.statement: Staples demand challenged by free food grain welfare schemes dampening wheat flour demand
items.quote: some policies like distribution of free food grains under various welfare schemes dampened the demand for certain staples, such as wheat flour

items.statement: PBT margin target 16-19% for FY26 including other income
items.quote: 16% to 19% range is where we want it to end, and that is where we are ending the full year

items.statement: Capex to double from current INR130-150 cr to INR250-300 cr over next 2-3 years
items.quote: We expect the capex to double at least in the next 2 to 3 years.

items.statement: Automotive growth driven by small commercial vehicles, tractors, SUVs and EVs; industrial flat to slightly up in steel, food & beverage at GDP rates, wind 3-4% growth, railways and infrastructure robust
items.quote: Automotive is seeing some fairly strong growth in commercial vehicles, especially smaller commercial vehicles, driven partly by the e-commerce and the quick delivery.

items.statement: Q4 FY25 PBT margin jumped to 23.3% from 11.9% due to cost savings and transfer pricing catch-up; full year PBT margin slightly down 0.6 pp but in 16-19% range
items.quote: Margin grew from -- so if you look at profit before tax: It grew from 11.9% to 23.3%.

items.statement: FY25 consolidated EBITDA margin ~17.5% vs 18.1% in FY24; dip due to volume-driven growth vs price increases and portfolio pruning in FY24
items.quote: the overall EBITDA for the current financial year is around 17.5%, whereas last year was around 18.1%.

items.statement: Inventory built up to support automotive OEM demand and expected railway orders; will normalize in next 2 quarters
items.quote: we built up some inventory to satisfy that demand, but also I would believe that on industrial side there were some customers, especially railways, etcetera, where we felt that the orders are going to come in, so we built up some inventory.

items.statement: New industrial plant at Pune on existing land; no land acquisition; significant chunk of capex for industrial, auto also needs capacity
items.quote: we would be setting up a new plant in the Pune location, all right, for the industrial legal entity

items.statement: Current industrial localization 30%+, ISEA level 50%+, target 70% at ISEA level; capacity expansion for both segments
items.quote: In the long term, we want to be localized close to 70% at an ISEA level, right?

items.statement: Transfer pricing adjustment completed for FY25 in Q4; impacted purchase of traded goods line item; volatility may continue but will be corrected annually
items.quote: The transfer pricing adjustment which has happened in the current quarter is driven based on the transfer pricing guidelines and rules which are set by an international body.

items.statement: FY25 revenue mix: industrial 52%, automotive 40%, exports 8%; key sub-segments: distribution 23%, two-wheelers 13%, rail 7%, general machinery 9%, cars 5%, power transmission 5%, auto aftermarket 10%
items.quote: For FY '25, if you look at -- the overall automotive share was around 40%. And industrial was around 52% and exports was around 8%.

items.statement: Automotive OEMs driving inventory buildup; railway customers with orders in hand to be invoiced over next months
items.quote: We do have orders in hand actually, but those are just -- will be sold, will be invoiced over the next few months.

items.statement: Cash flow down due to net working capital change from higher sales and inventory at year-end; receivables up few days temporarily; expect normalization in next 2 quarters
items.quote: the net cash flow. And that's mainly due to a change in net working capital towards the end of the year, more sales, more inventory involved and so the change in net working capital impacted the cash flow, but nothing to worry about.

items.statement: Higher other income from interest on cash balances and income from sister company continuing till 2029
items.quote: the bump-up in the other income is driven on account of the cash that the company is sitting with, right, that kind of results in higher interest income. Plus we have also income coming from one of our sister companies, right, which will continue till 2029.

items.statement: Demerger on track: NCLT filing done in Q2 CY25; shareholder and creditor meetings next; listing targeted by Q4 CY25 or Q3 CY26
items.quote: We are broadly on track. Q2, which is this -- of calendar year '25, which is now, we have filed with the NCLT. We're waiting for the final approval. And then we'll take it to shareholders, and we'll have a creditor meeting also. So broadly on track to finish the listing by Q4 calendar year of this year or Q3 calendar year 25-26.

items.statement: Senior management evaluated on sales growth and operating margin only; no separate export metric; no change in evaluation in last 3 years
items.quote: It's always been sales growth and operating margin.

items.statement: New industrial business lines: services (remote monitoring, remanufacturing, predictive failure analysis) and new metals segment products for long steel products
items.quote: So I think one is in the services business, which is the -- not just the aftermarket sale of bearings but to remote monitoring, remanufacturing, et cetera of bearings; as well as kind of tying it to reliability and uptime to industrial production and customers.

items.statement: Margin volatility from transfer pricing adjustments on traded goods; managed annually per international guidelines
items.quote: in case you see future volatility, it will -- from a financial year perspective, corrected as it has been corrected for this financial year.

items.statement: Exports INR390 cr in FY25 (3% growth); not split by auto/industrial due to consolidated manufacturing; common products serve both segments
items.quote: for the year are 390 crores. Can you split it for auto and industrial? Ashish Saraf: We currently do not split exports into auto and industrial

items.statement: FY26 volume guidance: iron ore mining 3Mt, pellet 3Mt, sponge iron 5.94 lakh tons, steel billets 500k tons, rolled products 375k tons, ferro alloys ~90k tons
items.quote: Coming to the volume guidance for FY '26, company expects iron ore mining and pellet production of 3 million tons each in FY '26, sponge iron production of 5.94 lakh tons, steel billets 500,000 tons, rolled products 375,000 tons and ferro alloys around 90,000 tons

items.statement: FY26 EBITDA margin target ~20%+ similar to FY25 level
items.quote: See, as per our current guidance volume for FY '26, we are confident we should be able to achieve what we have achieved in FY '25, which is about 20%, 20% plus.

items.statement: FY26 revenue growth expected 5-7% from new pellet plant and rolling mill volumes
items.quote: So we can say roughly about 5 to 7 additional -- or probably 5%, 7% of additional volume we can see this year in terms of profit top line, 5% to 7%.

items.statement: FY26 capex outflow ~INR850-900 crores; remaining capex on ongoing projects ~INR950-1000 crores as of March 2025
items.quote: FY '26 with the current pellet project mines beneficiation, mines expansion and a few other energy incentive initiatives, we envisage the total outflow will be about, say, INR850 crores for this year.

items.statement: Pending capex: beneficiation plant INR150 cr, pellet plant INR334 cr, solar power INR380 cr, energy efficiency INR56 cr, total ~INR950-1000 cr
items.quote: So there is a pending beneficiation plant capex of INR150 crores, pellet plant is INR334 crores yet to be spent. All these numbers are based on March '25. Solar power project, there is a INR380 crore requirement. Energy efficiency project, INR56 crores. Altogether, INR950 crores to INR1,000 crores approximately.

items.statement: Ari Dongri iron ore mining expansion from 2.35Mt to 6Mt (4.5Mt ore + 1.5Mt BMQ) approval expected by Q3 FY26
items.quote: On the capacity front, approval for expansion in iron ore mining capacity in the Ari Dongri mine from 2.35 to 6 million tons. The same is expected by Q3 FY '26.

items.statement: 2Mt pellet plant expansion commissioning expected Q2 FY26
items.quote: The 2 million ton mining pellet expansion is progressing as per plan and is expected to be commissioned in Q2 FY '26.

items.statement: Steel melting shop capacity increase by 50k tons to 575k tons by Q4 FY26
items.quote: Additionally, company plans to increase capacity of steel melting shop by another 50,000 tons, bringing the total capacity to 575,000 metric tons. This expansion is expected to be commissioned by Q4 FY '26.

items.statement: Additional 30MW solar plant for captive use; total solar capacity to reach 290MW
items.quote: Following this expansion, the overall solar power capacity will rise to 290 megawatts entirely for captive use.

items.statement: Waste heat recovery project with Siemens Energy targeted completion by March 2026
items.quote: On decarbonizaton front, GPIL has signed an MOU with Siemens Energy to implement waste heat recovery project, which is currently underway and targeted completion by March '26.

items.statement: Carbon capture unit (5 ton/day) with IIT Mumbai technology transfer expected by March 2026
items.quote: Furthermore, a letter of intent has been issued to IIT Mumbai for technology transfer for technology transfer for 5 ton per day carbon capture unit also expected to be completed by March '26.

items.statement: Boria Tibu mine to resume full operations from end of May 2025 after IBM clearance
items.quote: So from end of May, the Boria Tibu mine will be back in operation at full flow.

items.statement: New structural rolling mill commissioned in Q4 FY25; FY26 production target 1.5 lakh tons
items.quote: And from the new structural rolling mill, which we have commissioned. So this year, we envisage production of 1.5 lakh tons.

items.statement: Tilda greenfield steel plant land allotment expected in 4-6 weeks, EC by Q2 FY26
items.quote: Finally, the file has started moving. So we are confident we should be able to get the land by next 4 to 6 weeks. And once the land is there, we should get the EC by a couple of months. So as of now, we expect the EC -- we should get the EC by Q2 of this financial year.

items.statement: Pellet sales jumped in Q4 due to inventory clearance and lower captive consumption during sponge iron kiln shutdown
items.quote: So if you remember, in end of Q3, there was a pile of inventory of pellets because of the subdued market conditions, plus my 2 bigger kilns, so almost for 45 days in this quarter, my captive consumption was only 40% for pellets. So that additional 60% of pellet volume for Q4 as well as the inventory in Q3, both were sold and cleared in this quarter.

items.statement: Pellet prices softened from INR10,000 to INR9,400-9,500 (5-7% drop) in Q1 FY26; Q4 and Q1 prices similar
items.quote: Pellet prices have softened compared to a high of INR10,000 in last quarter to about, say, INR9,400, INR9,500 this quarter at the moment currently. So we have seen a little bit of downside about 5% to 7%.

items.statement: Landed cost of imported coal Q4 FY25 ~INR11,750; Q1 FY26 ~INR11,500; sharp ~10% drop expected from Q2 FY26
items.quote: See, for Q4, the landed cost of coal was close to about INR11,750, the imported coal. And for Q1, the pricing will be somewhere about INR11,500, a slight reduction. But from Q2 onwards, we can see a sharp drop of almost 10% because even the international market has corrected quite a bit.

items.statement: High-grade pellet premium over commercial grade remains constant at ~INR500-1,000 regardless of base price
items.quote: So for example -- today, for example, the pricing is INR9,500. So pellet will be at INR10,000, INR11,000. If the pricing becomes INR9,000, our pellet will be INR10,500. So the delta between both the grades is constant.

items.statement: Domestic pellet demand strong in Raipur region due to DRI capacity additions; Eastern region oversupplied
items.quote: But for Raipur market, the demand is much more because of the DRI capacity, which has been added in last 2, 3 years since COVID. So abnormal capacities of DRI has been added in the Raipur market in the last 2, 3 years, because of which, for us, the pressure of selling is very seldom.

items.statement: Secondary steel market demand weakened in May 2025 impacting sponge iron, coal and pellet prices
items.quote: The demand has gone down definitely at least for the secondary market, which has impacted the entire supply chain, right from sponge iron, domestic coal and even the pellet prices.

items.statement: FY26 iron ore requirement: 2.4Mt from Ari Dongri, 0.35-0.4Mt from Boria Tibu, 0.2-0.25Mt from EC expansion, 0.7-0.8Mt market purchase
items.quote: The remaining Fines, roughly, say, about 0.7 million to 0.8 million, including my new plant capacity, we will be sourcing from the market.

items.statement: Acquired 43.96% stake in Jammu Pigments (non-ferrous recycling); FY25 net sales INR860 cr, EBITDA INR79 cr, PAT INR37 cr
items.quote: During the financial year '25, the company has acquired 43.96% stake in Jammu Pigments on a fully diluted basis. The company is engaged in recycling of nonferrous metals and JPL has expertise in processing complex mixture of industrial waste of non-ferrous metals.

items.statement: Jammu Pigments productivity improvements underway; no formal FY26 guidance given yet
items.quote: We'll not be able to give you the guidance on Jammu Pigment. But I can only tell you that we are actively engaged with the company. And a lot of improvements have been done over a period of last 3 months and more improvements are on the way in terms of productivity improvement.

items.statement: Net cash INR863 crores as of March 31, 2025; Board approved INR300 cr borrowing for cash flow management during expansions
items.quote: The company has a net cash of INR863 crores as on March 31, 2025, with healthy balance sheet.

items.statement: Intercorporate loans exposure INR200-250 crores (mix of long-term INR118 cr and short-term treasury deposits)
items.quote: So total exposure will be in the range of INR200 crores to INR250 crores, including long-term loans. So it will be a mix of long-term and short-term loans.

items.statement: Board recommended dividend of INR1 per share (100% of paid-up capital) for FY25
items.quote: The Board has recommended a dividend of INR1 per share, that is 100% on the paid-up share capital of the company.

items.statement: Safeguard duty imposed for 6 months on HR coil/value-added products; caused temporary ~10% price increase in March-April, reversed by May
items.quote: See, of course, so we know government has imposed a duty for 6 months with a minimum pricing mark. But we all need to understand the duty has been imposed on basically the HR coil or value-added products, which are usually catered by the primary steel market, right?

items.statement: FY25 consolidated EBITDA margin 22%, PAT margin 15% despite realization declines
items.quote: Despite challenges, EBITDA margin and PAT margin stood strong at 22% and 15%, respectively.

items.statement: FY25 highest ever production in sponge iron, steel billets, ferro alloys and power
items.quote: I'm happy to share that GPIL has achieved highest ever production in sponge iron, steel billets, ferro alloys and power in FY '25.

items.statement: Ari Dongri EC approval delayed due to new third-party composite report requirement; confident of approval by Q3 FY26
items.quote: So now they want to report from a third party. Earlier, we had given them reports, but now they want a third-party report. So that is still another 6 to 8 weeks. So that is why it is delayed. Otherwise, the process is on. We should be able to get this report by first half June.

items.statement: Capex guidance of INR 190 crores for FY26
items.quote: We are expecting to have a capex spend of about INR 190 crores for FY '25-'26.

items.statement: Capex focused on Oragadam plant expansion and new lines at other plants for export support
items.quote: This would be more towards expansion of our Oragadam plant and introduction of some lines at some of the other plants for export support and all that.

items.statement: CV industry expected to rebound driven by infrastructure investments and fleet renewal
items.quote: We see clear signs of recovery driven by infrastructure investments, fleet renewal needs, and supportive government initiatives like the PM-eBus Sewa program.

items.statement: Q4 FY25 EBITDA margin 22.8%, full year 22.1%; PBT 18.2% of product sales
items.quote: Our PBT stood at 18.2% of product sales in FY 2024 -25, and we maintained healthy EBITDA margins of 22.8% for Q4 FY 2024-25 and 22.1% for the year.

items.statement: No one-time effects in Q4 margins; all routine and repeatable
items.quote: There are no onetime effects in the quarterly results this time. All routine and repeatable.

items.statement: Secured large order for ~800 units of SCALAR EVO Pulse from leading Indian trailer manufacturer
items.quote: I'm happy to share that the company has secured a large order for ~800 units of SCALAR EVO Pulse from a leading Indian trailer manufacturer.

items.statement: Received repeat order for Video Management Solution (VMS) from leading OEM
items.quote: We also received a repeat order for Video Management Solution (VMS) from a leading OEM.

items.statement: ESC price delta estimated around INR 25,000 per vehicle at full volume localization
items.quote: in the case of ESC, when it is in the f ull volume and people localized, the prices should be in the range of maybe around INR 25,000 delta

items.statement: ADAS regulation opportunity estimated at least above INR 40,000 per vehicle combined with ESC
items.quote: All this put together, in my view, it should be in the range of at least above INR 40,000, but we have to see, because it also depends on the type of solutions that is offered and the localization content, et cetera.

items.statement: OE sales declined 9.8% in FY25 due to unfavorable model mix and exit of low-margin bleeder parts
items.quote: The Company's OE sales were further impacted, declining by 9.8%, primarily due to an unfavourable model mix, owing to a shift away from heavy-duty vehicles toward Intermediate and Light Commercial Vehicles (ILCVs) - alongside a Y-o-Y 12% drop in trailer production. Additionally, the company took a strategic decision to exit low margin 'bleeder' parts to improve our profitability.

items.statement: Aftermarket grew 5.5% in FY25 but declined 4.6% in Q4 due to supply chain disruptions
items.quote: In FY 2024 -25, our Aftermarket business delivered a steady Y -o-Y overall growth of 5.5%. However, in Q4 FY 2024-25, we experienced a decline of (4.6%), primarily due to supply chain disruptions that affected product availability and fulfilment timelines.

items.statement: Services exports grew 17.4% in FY25 to INR 443.4 crores; Q4 growth 15% to INR 112.3 crores
items.quote: Export of services recorded a growth of 15.0% in Q4 FY 2024-25 compared to the same quarter last year. In FY 2024 –25, export of services grew by 17.4%, driven by a sustained increase in engineering activities delivered from India to our global centers.

items.statement: Export headwinds anticipated from emerging U.S. tariff impacts
items.quote: Looking ahead, we anticipate some headwinds in our export outlook, primarily due to emerging tariff impacts from the U.S. market.

items.statement: Petroleum companies mandating T-EBS/T-ABS for LPG transport in several states creating retrofit opportunity
items.quote: In a recent development, petroleum companies have floated tenders for LPG transportation contracts, mandating the use of Trailer Electronic Braking Systems (T -EBS) in Karnataka, Gujarat, Assam, and Rajasthan, and Trailer Anti-lock Braking Systems (T-ABS) in other states. This regulatory shift has opened a significant opportunity for retrofitting existing vehicles through the aftermarket channel,

items.statement: New manufacturing lines commissioned at Oragadam plant for e-mobility products; capacities scaled up across plants for braking systems
items.quote: New manufacturing lines for next -generation e-mobility products have been commissioned at this plant to produce e-compressors, ASP cartridges, hydraulic ESCs for Indian OEMs, and wheel-end products such as actuators, brake chambers, and ASAs for both domestic and export markets.

items.statement: New assembly lines at Jamshedpur and Lucknow; over 25 parts transferred improving delivery and reducing transport emissions
items.quote: New assembly lines have been established at the Jamshedpur and Lucknow plants, enhancing agility and customer responsiveness. Over 25 parts have been transferred to these plants, impro ving delivery performance, enhancing flexibility through proximity -based operations, and supporting our sustainability objectives by reducing transportation emissions.

items.statement: Debtor terms changed from 45 to 60-90 days for some customers in FY25; FY25 base to be used for future
items.quote: In the last year, we did change our terms for some of the customers from 45 days to 60 days and some even to 90 days. it works on both sides. So it's always a commercial negotiation in terms of balancing the payment terms with other commercials that we see.

items.statement: No guidance on working capital development; FY25 as base
items.quote: You can take FY '25 as a base. We would not provide a guidance on how this is going to develop.

items.statement: Vehicle production in Q4 FY25 was 119,000 units
items.quote: Vehicle production is 1,19,000.

items.statement: LCV segment revenue potential estimated at EUR 90 million in ~5 years
items.quote: To your question, roughly, our estimate right now, maybe in a matter of 5 years from now, it should be in the range of EUR 90 million. Very rough estimate.

items.statement: LCV hydraulic ESC content per vehicle ~INR 20,000; target INR 25,000 with more products
items.quote: But if you look at the product that I indicated, it's typically about INR 20,000. If you add some more products, maybe we can talk about INR 25,000 value per vehicle could be a target we can start with.

items.statement: No current competitor for hydraulic ESC in LCV segment; ZF first to market 3 years ago
items.quote: Actually, in this particular segment, where we are supplying the hydraulic ESC, there is no player in India right now, because this is a light commercial vehicle, not a passenger car segment.

items.statement: ZF aims to maintain lead position in ADAS/ESC via local engineering, manufacturing, service network and customer connect
items.quote: We believe we will maintain our lead position.

items.statement: Energy efficiency program executed 103 projects achieving 12% reduction in overall energy consumption
items.quote: This initiative led to the successful execution of 103 projects, resulting in a 12% reduction in overall energy consumption.

items.statement: Rooftop solar installed: 500KWp at Jamshedpur (25% plant energy), 60KWp at Pantnagar (40% plant energy)
items.quote: To promote the use of renewable energy, we installed on -site roof solar panels of 500KWp to support 25% of the plant's energy consumption in Jamshedpur and 60KWp to support 40% of the plant's energy consumption in Pantnagar.

items.statement: Canteen electrification at Ambattur saves 66,000 litres diesel and 151 tons CO2e annually
items.quote: Additionally, in a conscious drive to phase out fossil fuels in operations, the electrification of the canteen was completed at Ambattur, saving approximately 66,000 litres of diesel per annum and eliminating 151 tons of CO2 equivalent (CO2e).

items.statement: Employees won 16 National and 19 Regional awards in TEI competitions in FY25
items.quote: I am happy to share that, in FY 2024-2025, our teams won 16 National Awards and 19 Regional Awards in competitions organized by the CII, ACMA, and QCFI, along with many more awards at regional levels.

items.statement: Completed acquisition of Del Monte Foods Limited on 6th February 2025, making it a wholly-owned subsidiary; 35.4% stake issued to Bharti Group and Del Monte Pacific Limited
items.quote: In Feb '25, we also completed the acquisition of Del Monte Foods Limited by taking 100% stake of this organization. So to all the investors who are present here, I'm very happy to inform that we have completed this acquisition on 6th February '25. Del Monte Foods is now a wholly-owned subsidiary of Sundrop Brands.

items.statement: Expect low capex for next 3 years, limited to packaging lines and maintenance, due to 40-70% capacity utilization in core categories
