items.quote: To further accelerate our growth momentum, we are happy to report that in FY '25, we successfully raised INR157 crores through the issuance of preferential warrants.

items.statement: Proposed dividend of INR1 per share for FY25, subject to shareholder approval
items.quote: In addition, in recognition of our strong financial and operational performance in FY '25, we are pleased to propose a dividend of INR1 per share, subject to shareholders' approval.

items.statement: Tendering activity slowed for 4-5 months post-September but has picked up recently; three large CHP tenders expected in coming weeks; seismic and O&M tenders also in pipeline
items.quote: But now the tendering activities has picked up recently. We have submitted a bid for a large tender, which we are expecting to open sometime in near future. And there's a clear sight of few tenders which were we interested, which will be coming up in next 2, 3 months.

items.statement: Added new clients in FY25: AGCL (O&M compression on BOOT basis), Invenire Energy, Hardy, Sun Petro; Coal India subsidiaries remain key but treated as independent entities
items.quote: Yes. So, as you may be aware, we have received one O&M contract of compression on the boot basis from AGCL. So that is the new client we have onboarded. Then we have been working with Invenire energy, and Hardy, which are our new client for operation & metal segment. Apart from that, Vedanta Oil India, ONGC, Coal India and Coal India's various affiliates and subsidiaries continue to remain our cli

items.statement: Trade receivables rose to INR224 crores from INR135 crores due to Q4 revenue surge and retention money (INR55 crores); INR150 crores <90 days, only INR14 crores >90 days; retention release of INR25-30 crores expected in FY26
items.quote: Out of that INR224 crores of the overall receivables, roughly around INR55 crores of receivables pertains to retention, which will release -- some part will get released in FY '26. As I mentioned that we'll be completing 3 projects into this year and some part will get released into the next year.

items.statement: Net cash position of ~INR80 crores after short-term debt; Kuiper acquisition funded via 5-year acquisition loan and internal cash; working capital limits in place; preferential warrants provide INR110 crores undrawn
items.quote: So, as you must have seen, we are a positive cash company. After excluding whatever the short-term debt we have, we have roughly around INR80 crores of net cash and bank balances.

items.statement: Executing 6 coal handling projects; 3 to complete in FY26, 2 by Sep-Oct, 1 by Dec; Kuiper adds O&M platform in Middle East (Saudi, Qatar, UAE) with 2-3 year revenue visibility
items.quote: So, we have been currently executing six coal handling projects. And in the last year, we have done almost -- you must have seen the breakup of our segment. So, the entire Mineral segment business contributes to the coal handling project.

items.statement: Q4 Oil & Gas margin compressed due to cost escalation on one seismic project from weather delays; claim discussions ongoing with client; recovery not in FY26 guidance
items.quote: In one of our particular project where part of the project has been done into the Q4, there has been the cost escalation. So, in the Oil & Gas segment, that's the reason the margin for the Q4 specifically in the oil & gas segment has slightly tapered off.

items.statement: Kuiper revenue dipped in 2024 due to Saudi offshore project slowdown; recovery underway; integration and margin improvement plans post-acquisition completion
items.quote: And definitely, the last year, there was some dip into the Kuiper business turnover because Saudi Arabia has de-hired some offshore assets and have slowed down some offshore projects, which has led to the temporary dip into the numbers in the last year.

items.statement: FY26 revenue guidance split ~50% Oil & Gas, ~50% Minerals & Energy (Infra); Oil & Gas includes seismic, O&M, production facilities; Minerals driven by coal handling EPC
items.quote: Yes. So, we are looking roughly around 50% - 50%, between 45% to 50% coming from our Infra segment and another 50% is coming from our oil & gas segment. That's what we have been looking in our guidance.

items.statement: Environmental clearance received for Mewad field (Indrora cluster); awaiting clearance for Indrora field; commercialization planned in FY26 post clearances
items.quote: Yes. So out of those two fields, we have received an environmental clearances for one of those field, which we intend to commercialize in FY '26. We have a plan to drill some wells and commercialize that. And for the Cambay field, we are still waiting for the clearances.

items.statement: Proposed ESOP pool of 2% equity capital to align key talent with growth journey
items.quote: As part of our ongoing focus on long-term value creation, we proposed to establish an ESOP pool amounting to 2% of the equity capital aimed at strengthening alignment with key talent and reinforcing their commitment to the company's growth journey.

items.statement: Kuiper operates in Middle East (Saudi Arabia, Qatar, UAE) and Southeast Asia; provides platform for Asian Energy to cross-sell O&M services internationally
items.quote: Kuiper Group is a globally reputed provider of integrated manpower solutions tailored for the energy sector with a strong operational performance across the Middle East and Southeast Asia, including critical energy markets such as Saudi Arabia, Qatar and the UAE.

items.statement: Contra call on coal 3 years ago when sector was written off; now benefiting from 80GW coal expansion plan and 1.5B ton domestic coal target by 2030
items.quote: I mean, this came as a positive surprise to us, as I mentioned earlier, about the coal business. I mean, 3 years back, everybody was writing off hydrocarbon coal business and we took this contra call that India will need a lot of coal to meet the power requirement.

items.statement: Company does not provide specific revenue or earnings guidance
items.quote: As you all are aware, Nucleus Software does not provide any specific revenue earnings guidance.

items.statement: Order book at INR 600+ crores end of quarter, down from INR 700 crores previous quarter
items.quote: So the order book, which is pending as on today at the end of the quarter, I would say, is INR 600 plus crores. So that is the order book on which we are sitting.

items.statement: Added three new logos in quarter, four in last two quarters; lost two customers in last 5-6 months
items.quote: We managed to add three new logos in this quarter and also got some incremental support from our customers, existing customers.

items.statement: Top five clients contribute 27.8% of revenue, down from 28.1% previous quarter
items.quote: Revenue contribution from the top five clients for the quarter is 27.8% against 28.1% in the previous quarter.

items.statement: Middle East: 7 of top 10 banks are customers including Tier-1 and Tier-2; Europe has limited presence with Tier-1 customers
items.quote: We have if I talk on Middle East, we have 7 out of top 10 customers, 10 banks with us. Both Tier-1, Tier-2, they work with us, deliver their enterprise software solutions to run their assets out of the business.

items.statement: Product revenue 199.6 crore (87% of total), services 29.4 crore (13%); license+implementation 10-12% of revenue
items.quote: Product revenue for the quarter is at Rs. 199.6 crore against Rs. 174.8 crore QoQ and Rs. 179.4 crore YoY. For the year, it is Rs. 713.8 crore against Rs. 711.4 crore for the previous year.

items.statement: EBITDA 74.3 crore (32.5% margin) vs 33 crore QoQ and 58 crore YoY; cost of delivery 57.3% of revenue vs 70.7% QoQ
items.quote: EBITDA for the quarter is at Rs. 74.3 crore against Rs. 33.0 crore QoQ, Rs. 58.0 crore YoY.

items.statement: Provision reversal of INR 8.5 crore boosted operating profit; most profit growth from revenue increase with limited cost rise
items.quote: Yes on account of provision reversal, the benefit is of INR 8.5 crores. See, most of the growth in the operating profit that you see is because of the growth in revenue that has happened, we being a product company, we don't see a proportionate rise in cost when we get our revenue up.

items.statement: Pricing model uses both transaction-based and user-based pricing; AI capabilities will add value across existing models
items.quote: We are using both. I mean, we are using transaction-based pricing as well as user-based pricing. our pricing model consists of both transactions based as well as user-based pricing. And there are other variants of this model.

items.statement: Completed pricing rebase for most customers in previous quarter
items.quote: as we mentioned in our last quarterly investor call, we have done pricing, rebased learning for most of our customers. So I think that exercise is already done by now.

items.statement: Gross fixed asset addition of INR 8.5 crore in quarter, primarily computers/servers (6.93 crore)
items.quote: During the quarter, there is a gross addition of fixed assets of Rs. 8.50 crore, consisting primarily of Rs. 6.93 crore on Computer & Servers, Rs. 1.01 crore on Building and Plant & Machinery, 0.29 crore Furniture & Fixtures, Rs. 0.19 crore on Software and Rs. 0.08 crore on Office Equipment's.

items.statement: Receivables increased to INR 137.4 crore from INR 109.6 crore previous quarter
items.quote: With regards to receivables, we are at Rs. 137.4 crore against INR 109.6 crore previous quarter.

items.statement: No borrowings mentioned; cash and equivalents INR 877.3 crore (mutual funds 597.4 cr, FDs 196.1 cr, tax-free bonds 33.3 cr, current accounts 50.5 cr)
items.quote: Total cash and cash equivalent as of 31st March 2025 are Rs. 877.3 crore against Rs. 877.9 crore as on December 31, 2024. This includes balance in current accounts of Rs. 50.5 crore various schemes of mutual fund Rs. 597.4 crore, fixed deposits of Rs. 196.1 crore, investments in tax free bonds of Rs. 33.3 crore.

items.statement: No buyback or special dividend planned in current quarter; board has not discussed
items.quote: So buyback is something which we are not thinking now. I mean, we are not thinking for both buyback and the special dividend at least in this quarter. I mean, we had our Board meeting. So we haven't discussed any of these two at least in this meeting.

items.statement: Attrition around 11% (voluntary + involuntary), substantially below industry average; variable bonus linked to org performance paid year-end
items.quote: Our voluntary plus involuntary attrition would be at around 11% and lesser. That's on attrition and in terms of measures that we are taking to retain, we have two focus areas.

items.statement: Added employees in quarter to invest in technology; employee cost reduction of INR 8.5 cr from provision true-up for variable pay
items.quote: in terms of employees, we have added employees in the last quarter. We are seeing opportunities. We are seeing space for investment in our technology and that is the reason we are adding employees.

items.statement: Sales cycle 8-18 months, now involving board-level discussions; milestone revenue 12-14% of quarterly revenue
items.quote: So the typical sales cycle in the enterprise software's is a little longer now. So it's typically varied from 8 months to 18 months.

items.statement: R&D cost approximately 5-6% of total cost incurred per quarter
items.quote: R&D cost of the total cost that we incur, R&D cost would be approximately 5% to 6% of the total cost at the incurred in a quarter.

items.statement: AI strategy defined across retail lending and transaction banking; use cases being rolled out each release; AI embedded horizontally across all product lines
items.quote: Essentially, you all know it is a time of AI enabled now, we took our time to decide our AI strategy, but we are now clear in our both our products, whether it is retail lending, transaction banking. We now have a list of use cases, a long list of use cases, which we, want to build.

items.statement: North America strategy focused on specific lending platform line of business; Australia strengthened by long-term relationships and strong pipeline
items.quote: On the North America side, we do have a strong strategy, a very focused strategy on a very specific line of business with a clear focus on and a specific focus on the lending platform.

items.statement: Revenue growth driven by new customers, existing customer expansion, and delivery efficiency; spread across customers and business lines
items.quote: So the addition in revenue, obviously, as you spoke, has come from addition of new business from new customer, but even more importantly, the trust that has been shown by our existing customers and they have given additional business, which we have kind of delivered and therefore converted to revenue in this quarter.

items.statement: Geopolitical and regulatory dynamics create uncertainty for North America expansion timeline
items.quote: But yes, time will tell because the government dynamic, the geopolitical dynamics are such that it will be difficult for us to comment on anything beyond this.

items.statement: Foreign currency hedges: USD 3.25 million forward contracts at avg rate 86.24, MTM gain INR 0.06 crore
items.quote: In terms of foreign currency hedges, on 31 March 2025, we had USD 3.25 million of forward contracts at an average rate of 86.24, there is a mark to market gain of Rs. 0.06 crore, which is taken to the hedging reserve in the balance sheet.

items.statement: Overall FMCG demand stable; rural outperforms urban; smaller unit packs and premiumization trends strong
items.quote: During the quarter, while the overall FMCG demand remained stable, several categories exhibited notable growth, reflecting positive consumer traction and evolving preferences.

items.statement: Rural markets continue to outperform urban areas buoyed by stronger consumer sentiment
items.quote: Consumption trend overview indicates that rural markets continue to outperform urban areas, buoyed by stronger consumer sentiment.

items.statement: Consolidated net sales grew 17% YoY to INR 9,106 million with 13% volume growth
items.quote: The Company recorded its consolidated net sales growth of 17%, reaching INR 9,106 million rupees, accompanied by a volume growth of 13% on a year-on-year basis for the quarter.

items.statement: FY25 revenue grew 16.2% to INR 26,912 million with 12.4% volume growth
items.quote: For the Financial Year 2025, the Company achieved growth of 16.2% with a volume growth of 12.4%, amounting to INR 26,912 million rupees.

items.statement: Personal Care segment grew 22.5% in Q4 and 33.4% in FY25; Food & Nutrition grew 15.4% in Q4 and 13% in FY25
items.quote: The Personal Care segment continued to demonstrate strong consumer traction, achieving notable double-digit growth of 22.5% for the quarter, along with 33.4% growth for Financial Year 2025.

items.statement: Organized trade saliency reached 23% in FY25; e-commerce 10%, non-trade 13%; quick commerce 41% of e-commerce
items.quote: Organized trade saliency continued to improve, reaching 23% for Financial Year 2025, of this e-commerce contributed 10% and non-trade contributed 13%.

items.statement: Household penetration grew nearly 4x market average per Nielsen/Kantar MAT March 2025

items.statement: Gross margins stable with modest upward trend; 42 bps expansion in Q4, 168 bps in FY25, 361 bps over FY24-25
items.quote: Gross margins have demonstrated stability with modest upward trend in a year-to-year comparison, despite ongoing inflationary challenges.

items.statement: EBITDA grew 17.1% to INR 1,900 million in Q4; FY25 EBITDA grew 23.2% to INR 3,797 million
items.quote: On the EBITDA front, the Company delivered a growth of 17.1%, reaching INR 1,900 million rupees for the quarter, while net profit after tax increased 14.4% to INR 1,719 million rupees.

items.statement: EBITDA margin target of 17-18% over next couple of years driven by gross margin improvement and operating leverage
items.quote: So, Tejash, I think we have been maintaining our clear intent is to move these numbers to 17%, 18% in the next couple of years.

items.statement: Gross margin has scope for another couple of percentage points improvement over next couple of years
items.quote: We are quite conscious of the fact that we intend to get there. We will, therefore, use our pricing power, mix of cost management actions to keep on the journey of gross margin improvement, which still has scope for another couple of percentage point improvement over the next couple of years.

items.statement: A&P spend targeting ~13% of sales (+/-0.5%) with room for 0.5-1% further improvement
items.quote: A&P, I think we have started hitting closer to our wish list percentage to sales. Maybe there is room for another 0.5% or 1% improvement, but that will play by the year essentially.

items.statement: Board recommended final dividend of INR 6 per share (60%, 20% increase) and 1:5 stock split
items.quote: In line with this, the Board has recommended a final dividend of INR 6 rupees per equity share of face value INR 10, which is 60%, representing a 20% increase over the dividend declared in the previous financial year.

items.statement: Cash conversion from operations at INR 3,800 million vs EBITDA INR 3,797 million reflects 100% realization
items.quote: The Company's cash conversion from operations at INR 3,800 rupees million to EBITDA of INR 3,797 million rupees reflects a strong realization of 100%.

items.statement: Rite Bite (Naturell India) acquired 100% in Q3 FY25; grew >50% in 4 months; margins positive low single digits; FY26 cash EPS accretive
items.quote: We have seen higher than 50% growth on this brand, supported by tailwinds and a lot of good execution by the team. The margins have been positive, low single digits, and we hope to build on this as we go along.

items.statement: Rite Bite expected to continue ~25% CAGR over 3-5 years; FY26 cash EPS accretive
items.quote: We hope to continue doing that. Right now, we are tracking reasonably well on that.

items.statement: Acquisition strategy: bolt-on only, INR 100-200 crore range preferred, synergistic with portfolio, funded from internal accruals
items.quote: INR 100 crores, INR 200 crores typically does fit in. It gets consummated far more easily. There is a proof point of the performance and there is a headroom for growth.

items.statement: Everyuth face scrub market share 48.5% (+321 bps); peel-off 77.7% (+6 bps); facial cleansing 7.7% (#5 rank)
items.quote: Everyuth's Scrub maintained its leadership position with 48.5% market share, marking a remarkable increase of 321.4 basis points over the same period last year.

items.statement: Nycil prickly heat powder market share 33.8% (#1); Glucon D glucose powder 58.8% (#1); Sugar Free sugar substitute 95.9% (#1)
items.quote: Nycil has maintained its #1 position with a market share of 33.8%.

items.quote: It will be, I think, if I remember the numbers right, about 18% to 20% approximately.

items.statement: Glucon D and Nycil highly seasonal: only 10-15% of sales in Q2/Q3
items.quote: For these 2 products, skewness is much larger. So only 10%, 15% of these products sell in the quarter 2, quarter 3.

items.quote: So typically, there is a spike which comes at the start of the season. So, we start building the inventory. So typically, Jan, Feb, March, especially January and February, the distributors are carrying fairly high inventory.

items.statement: No cash tax payout expected until FY27 due to deferred tax assets
items.quote: So, FY '26 and FY '27, there won't be any cash tax payout. There would be certainly deferred tax liability on the tax front, but there won't be any cash tax payout.

items.statement: Revenue target to cross INR 5,000 crores in 3-5 years; international business to reach 8-10% of portfolio
items.quote: Put together, quantitatively, we would like to cross a benchmark of INR 5,000 crores, whether it happens in 3 years or 5 years is mathematics.

items.statement: Edible oil prices and dextrose monohydrate volatility remain key concerns; milk prices rising recently
items.quote: On the macroeconomic front, easing food inflation is contributing to a decline in overall inflation, though volatility in edible oil prices and dextrose monohydrate remains a key concern.

items.statement: Employee cost increase due to variable pay from good performance and acquired business team on payroll; some moderation expected
items.quote: Employee spends growth is driven by a couple of factors. One, of course, is the fact that we have variable pay as part of the cost structure, and there has been good performance, which we have to do.

items.statement: No forward guidance given for Q1 FY26; some markets impacted but working to maintain double-digit growth commitment
items.quote: We do not give forward guidance, so we'll not be able to comment specifically on it.

items.statement: FY25 revenue INR1,171 cr, up 46% YoY; Adjusted EBITDA INR356 cr, up 18% YoY; PBT INR276 cr, up 2% YoY
items.quote: Financial year '25 saw our highest annual revenue of INR1,171 crores, a 46% growth over financial year '24. Also our highest Adjusted EBITDA of INR356 crores, which is 18% growth over financial year '24 and PBT of INR276 crores, which is 2% higher than last year.

items.statement: Content investment INR316 cr in FY25, up 62% YoY; committed INR1,000+ cr over FY25-27, INR525-530 cr already secured
items.quote: Between financial year '25 to '27, we committed to invest over INR1,000 crores in new music content. Of this, content worth close to INR525 crores - INR530 crores are already secured.

items.statement: Music vertical (licensing + artist management) medium-term growth 22-23% per annum
items.quote: We believe music vertical comprising our licensing and artist management to grow at 22% to 23% per annum over the medium term.

items.statement: Video vertical expected 25% CAGR over next 5 years
items.quote: We expect over the next 5 years, this vertical to keep on growing at a CAGR of 25%.

items.statement: Overall company PBT expected to double over next 3-4 years
items.quote: At the overall company level, we expect PBT to double over the next 3 to 4 years.

items.statement: Annual adjusted EBITDA margin guidance maintained at 32-33%
items.quote: We maintain our annual adjusted EBITDA guidance of 32% to 33%.

items.statement: PBT to start moving up by Q3-Q4 FY26
items.quote: PBT numbers, which are on the lower side for this financial year will start moving up by Q3, Q4 of the financial year '26.

items.statement: 5-year payback period maintained for new content acquisitions
items.quote: With all this investment in new content, we maintain our guidance of 5 -year payback period.

items.statement: Carvaan expected to reach mid-single-digit margins by end of FY26
items.quote: We are fairly certain that we will start touching single middle-digit margins by the end of financial year '26.

items.statement: Digital footprint across YouTube, Instagram, Facebook grew from 239M to 350M in FY25
items.quote: The other big highlight of the year for us was that our digital footprint across YouTube, Instagram and Facebook grew from 239 million as of last year to 350 million during the year.

items.statement: Paid subscription revenue grew very high double-digit percentage in FY25
items.quote: We are already seeing the green shoots, as I mentioned in my opening statement, that the revenue that Saregama makes from paid subscription part of the streaming platforms has grown by a very high double-digit percentage during the year.

items.statement: Subscription economy expected to take off in 4-5 quarters
items.quote: I'll say in 4-5 quarters, you will see paid subscription really taking off.

items.statement: Strong content pipeline for next 12 months including Thug Life, Tu Meri Main Tera, Love and War, Paradise, HIT 3, Dhurandhar, Idly Kadai, Vaadivaasal, Parasakthi, DEVIL
items.quote: Our lineup for the next 12 months is all in place, where we have music from some of the biggest films that are going to get released this year.

items.statement: Acquired 22 small music labels across 7 languages controlling 2,800 songs for INR17 cr
items.quote: This year, we also ended up acquiring 22 small music labels across 7 languages with overall who control 2,800 songs. These are all low pro file under the radar acquisitions, typically in languages where we are not very strong, relatively more smaller languages of the country. This costed us close to INR17 crores.

items.statement: Music licensing margins expected to improve by end of FY26 as charge-off on new content becomes lower than revenue from last 2 years' acquisitions
items.quote: You will start seeing improvement on the music revenue -- music margins of us, which is licensing plus artist management as we start hitting the end of this financial year because that's the time the charge-off on account of the new music is going to be far lower than the benefits of last 2 years content acquisitions revenue.

items.statement: Royalty expenses coming down despite music revenue growth due to royalty-free non-Hindi content and deferred Hindi film royalties
items.quote: Second, the royalty expense s, if you see on the overall basis, you're going to see the number coming down in spite of the music revenue going up because all the newer content that we people are picking up, if it is non -Hindi film content, it is all royalty -free music, it's only onet ime payment.

items.statement: Content acquisition spend INR300+ cr in FY25 on new content and marketing
items.quote: The last 12 months have been the most aggressive from Saregama side in terms of new content release. We spent close to INR300 crores on new content alone and its marketing.

items.statement: Charge-off on new content 48% higher YoY in FY25
items.quote: This year, the charge-off on account of new content was 48% higher than last year.

items.quote: Every major web show in India from Aashram Season 4 on Amazon MX Player to The Kapil Sharma Season 3 and 4 on Netflix or the IPL opening ceremony on Star or a big movie like Salman starrer Sikandar, or Balayya starrer Telugu movie, Daaku Maharaaj, they all have one thing in common. items.statement: Targeting 25-30% share of all new music released in India; music licensing revenue to double in 3-3.5 years
items.quote: Overall, with a stated goal of acquiring 25% to 30% of all new music released in India, the music licensing vertical should double its revenue in the next 3, 3.5 years.

items.statement: Music label agreements protect against theatre-to-OTT shifts with fee adjustments

items.statement: Live Events business has high IRR with capital locked for very short duration; targeting high single-digit margins
items.quote: The very nature of the Live Events business is that the capital gets locked in it for a very, very short duration. So the best case scenario is high single -digit margin, but a very high IRR.

items.statement: Content acquisitions funded through QIP and internal accruals
items.quote: And all this acquisition that we are doing will be funded through QIP and internal accruals.

items.statement: Acquired remaining 40% of Pocket Aces; 8-9% left to acquire over next 12-15 months; exceptional gain INR4.9 cr from liability write-back
items.quote: Now when we have acquired the remaining 40% , and we also need to acquire the remaining 8%-9%, we have reassessed the liability. There is a write -back of liability on account of the lower consideration, and there is a corresponding impact on account of reduction in goodwill. The net impact of this entire amount is about INR4.9 crores, which is shown as an exceptional item.

items.statement: Quarterly results not comparable due to seasonality, movie release timing, event scheduling, society payout cycles; evaluate on 12-month rolling basis
items.quote: Please look at our business on a 12 -month rolling basis. You cannot lo ok at our business on a quarterly basis. It just does not work that way.

items.statement: Management targets double-digit revenue growth for FY26
items.quote: The revenue guidance, as I would say like I have said earlier, we would always look at double-digit growth and we would always assume, and our work would always be towards making sure the organization grows at a consistent pace of double-digit growth.

items.statement: FY26 capex guided at Rs 1,400 crores plus maintenance capex
items.quote: Yes, so it would be Rs.1,400 crores plus some maintenance CAPEX, I mean, that would be the one that we would be looking forward to.

items.statement: Kakinada Phase-I capex nearly complete with Rs 200 crores remaining
items.quote: About Rs.200 crores is what we are looking at Phase-I.

items.quote: So Kakinada is a total of 500 acres. In 500 acres we have occupied about Phase-I we have used 200 acres and we have built production blocks which about seven of them which will help us in taking care of certain raw materials s o that it helps us in our backward integration

items.statement: Phased production commenced at Kakinada Unit-III supporting backward integration
items.quote: Phased production has already commenced, supporting our backward integration strategy and enhancing our capability to manage input costs effectively.

items.statement: Two long-term custom synthesis contracts signed; commercialization expected late 2026 to early 2027 subject to regulatory approvals
items.quote: Yes, we are talking about sometime in 3rd Quarter end of 2026 or 4th Quarter or January of 2027 around that time hopefully if all regulatory approvals come in place.

items.statement: FY25 product mix: Generics 46%, Custom Synthesis 54%; Q4 FY25 mix: Generics 49%, Custom Synthesis 51%
items.quote: Product mix for Generics to Custom Synthesis for current financial year is 46% and 54% respectively. Product mix for Generics to Custom Synthesis for current quarter is 49% and 51% respectively.

items.statement: Custom synthesis seeing strong sustained momentum with high customer engagement, RFP uptick and site visits
items.quote: We are witnessing strong and sustained momentum in this business. Customers engagement level remains high with a healthy upt ick in RFPs and regular site visits, reinforcing our stature as a Partner of Choice in the CDMO space

items.statement: Peptide business gaining significant traction driven by global demand for GLP-1, GIP, GLP-2 analogs
items.quote: Our peptide business is gaining significant traction as a global demand for novel peptide-based therapies including GLP-1's, GIPs and GLP-2 analogs, continue to accelerate.

items.statement: Generic segment faces persistent pricing pressure and high competitive intensity
items.quote: While pricing headwinds remain a persistent challenge, we have successfully maintained stable volumes in all our core products. The competitive intensity in the market continues to be high.

items.statement: Raw material pricing stable this quarter; multi-source procurement across US, EU, Middle East, Asia and domestic sources continues
items.quote: This quarter we witnessed relative stability in raw material pricing, which is an encouraging sign given the fluctuations seen in the previous quarters. items.statement: Red Sea disruptions extending inbound lead times by 2-3 weeks; proactive logistics planning and safety stock optimization implemented
items.quote: Specifically, the security situation in the Red Sea has necessitated widespread rerouting of cargo vessels around the Cape of Good Hope in South Africa. This alternate route has extended lead times for shipments from both the US and Europe by approximately two to three weeks.

items.statement: FY25 exports at 88% of sales; Europe and US account for 73% of sales; forex gain of Rs 48 crores for FY25

items.statement: Inventory at Rs 3,033 crores as of March 2025; management wishes to maintain lean inventory but levels depend on product mix and sourcing

items.statement: Q4 FY25 margin strength attributed to product mix; management recommends viewing margins on yearly basis

items.statement: Constant currency revenue growth of 18% in FY25 vs -2% in FY24

items.statement: Investing in next-generation technologies: continuous flow chemistry and biocatalysis for sustainable small molecule manufacturing
items.quote: In parallel, we continue to invest in next-generation technologies such as Continuous Flow Chemistry and Biocatalysis, both which are integral to our strategy for sustainable and scalable small molecules manufacturing.

items.statement: R&D capabilities expanded in peptide chemistry, solid-phase and liquid-phase synthesis, flow chemistry and biocatalysis over last 2-3 years
items.quote: been very active in peptide chemistry, we have been very active in fragments, then we have gone into solid-phase peptide synthesis, liquid- phase peptide synthesis. Apart from this, we have gone into flow chemistry , biocatalysis

items.statement: Red Sea maritime disruptions causing extended shipping times and elevated freight costs to EU, US and Latin America
items.quote: Vessel diversions and increased congestion at transshipment ports have resulted in extended shipping times and elevated freight costs, especially to key markets such as European Union, the United States and Latin America.

items.statement: Consolidated EBITDA margin 10.8% in Q4 vs 12.4% in Q3 and 14.2% a year ago; full year EBITDA Rs 63.8 cr vs Rs 73.4 cr in FY24
items.quote: On a consolidated basis, our EBITDA margin in Q4 are at 10.8% compared to 12.4% in Q3 and 14.2% a year ago. For the full year, our EBITDA is at Rs. 63.8 crore as compared to Rs. 73.4 crore in FY '24, a decline of 13.2 percentage.

items.statement: Year-on-year growth in profiles and paid subscriptions resumed from March 2025, continuing in April and May
items.quote: We can see that year -on-year growth in the profiles. So in terms of marketing spend as a percentage of revenue, when the revenue starts moving up, the marketing spend as a percent revenue will come down.

items.statement: Industry-wide profile degrowth in FY25 attributed to post-COVID normalization; growth resumed from March 2025
items.quote: Last year was one of the years where that the overall industry had a degrowth in the profile. And again, all it is due to the post -COVID effect where during the COVID time, there was a surge in the profile. After that, there is a thing, I think we see that things are getting normalized. We can see that year -on-year growth in the profiles.

items.statement: Added 2.5 lakh paid subscriptions in Q4 (3.3% QoQ growth, 9% YoY decline); ~1 million paid subscriptions added in FY25
items.quote: We added 2.5 lakhs paid subscription during the quarter, a growth of 3.3% quarter-over-quarter and decline of 9 % year-on-year. We added close t o 1 million paid subscription during the year.

items.statement: ATV for matchmaking grew 1.7% QoQ and 4.5% YoY in Q4; full year ATV grew 2.7%
items.quote: ATV for the matchmaking business grew by 1.7% quarter-over-quarter and 4.5% year-on-year. It is in line with our customer acquisition strategy. For t he full year, ATV grew by 2.7%.

items.statement: Marketing spend at Rs 46.7 cr in Q4 vs Rs 46.2 cr in Q3 and Rs 47.9 cr YoY; full year Rs 185.2 cr vs Rs 182.5 cr in FY24; expect spend to remain at current level or slightly reduce
items.quote: Marketing expenses are at Rs. 46.7 crore as compared to Rs. 46.2 crore in Q3 and Rs. 47.9 crore a year ago. Marketing expenses for the full year were at Rs. 185.2 crore as compared to Rs. 182.5 crore in FY '24.

items.statement: Marketing spend to remain at current level or reduce; percentage of revenue to decline as revenue grows; competitive intensity may allow future reduction
items.quote: We don't see the marketing spend is going to increase from the current level of spend at this point of time. So the marketing spend will remain at this level, maybe at a slightly reduced level, or maybe at this point of time at a similar level. So the revenue increases, the percentage of spend on marketing will come down.

items.statement: Paused wedding loan due to low conversions; AstroChat rebranded to AstroFreeChat with 5 min free consulting; 1,000+ daily downloads, few hundred consultations; ManyJobs monetization starting soon; MakeMyWedding targeting 100+ paid bookings
items.quote: We have decided to pause the wedding loan as the conversions are not at the expected level, and we may revisit in the future. We have changed AstroChat to AstroFreeChat and offer 5 minutes of free consulting. We are organically generating over 1,000 downloads per day and a few hundred consulting per day.

items.statement: ManyJobs monetization expected in coming months; MakeMyWedding model involves customer payment and commission from service providers; wedding loan paused to reduce losses
items.quote: The monetization for many jobs will start very soon. So, maybe next month or maybe a subsequent month. We have reached a desired level of registration with the employers and we intent to monetize in the near future.

items.statement: Majority of users are individuals (not parents); youngsters in driver's seat but with parental consent; broad base across tiers, segments, geographies
items.quote: I wouldn't say that only one segment. So whether the individuals looking for taking the lead or the parents taking the lead, we made note that majority of users are individuals themselves. So definitely the way that the matrimony industry has transformed the way Indian people find a life partner.

items.statement: Leader across India except North India; optimizing marketing for regular visibility in North India using Bharat Matrimony and community brands; Jodi brand also being promoted
items.quote: Other than North India market, we are a leader across India. So, North India, frankly, it is the market we like to grow our market share and win in the long term. So, we are at this point in time, looking at hav ing continuous visibility because it was not the case last couple of years.

items.statement: Competitive intensity keeps marketing spend elevated; third player (Jeevansathi) reduced spend but limited to North India; Matrimony investing in multiple brands (community, Jodi) from same budget
items.quote: If the competitive intensity reduces, we will also reduce the marketing spend. But at this point in time, there are players that are spending at a similar level. It's important for us to spend that level of marketing. Plus, we also have multiple brands. Now we also have the new brand like Jodi.

items.statement: CCI verdict against Google billing abuse of dominance; NCLT upheld Google orders; no payments to Google required; protected under current regulatory framework
items.quote: There is a CCI verdict against Google that the Google billing was an abuse of dominance and on the user choice of billing against CCI , the investigation is going on. There is a directive by CCI to Google and recently NCL T also upheld the Google orders. So at this point in time, so we are all protected, no payment to Google and it is not required.

items.statement: Open to inorganic growth in related industries; no current opportunities in core matchmaking; may pursue acquisitions in coming years
items.quote: there are any right opportunities, we definitely look into it. But we actually probably continue to keep these options open in terms of any opportunity to the Company in a re lated industry. We don't have any opportunity to occur in the matchmaking business, matrimony business, but if there are any related or growth opportunities, we will definitely look into it

items.statement: Created ~22,000 success stories in Q4; success story ratio to paid subscriptions declined from ~14% in FY20 to 10-11% range; attributed to profile degrowth, inauspicious dates, voluntary reporting
items.quote: We created about 22,000 success stories in the quarter.

items.statement: Average time to find life partner 9-12 months; packages range 3 months to 1 year; majority prefer shorter duration despite push for longer packages
items.quote: Yes, so it may take an average of 9 to 12 months for someone to find a life partner. So we have various packages. We have from 3 months to 1 year package. So it's ideally better if someone goes for the one-year package because of the benefit it brings and also the cost advantage.

items.statement: Cash balance Rs 324.3 crore; return on capital employed 14.2%
items.quote: Cash balance is at Rs. 324.3 crores and return on capital employed 14.2%.

items.statement: Forward-looking statements involve risks and uncertainties that could cause actual results to differ materially; no obligation to update unless required by law
items.quote: Certain statements during this call could be forward -looking statements on our business. This involves a n umber of risks and uncertainties that could cause the actual results to differ materially from such forward-looking statements. We do not undertake to update any such forward -looking statements that may be made from time to time by or on behalf of the Company unless it is required by law.

items.statement: Completed second buyback in last 2 years
items.quote: This year also marked t he successful completion of our second buyback in the last 2 years.

items.statement: Electronics division EBITDA margin target 10-12% over next 2 years
items.quote: Looking ahead, we are strategically adding margin -accretive applications such as industrials, auto, aerospace and defense, with an aim to reach 10% to 12% margin for this division over the next 2 years.

items.statement: Electronics division revenue growth target 30-40% for FY26
items.quote: Top line, we can't tell right now. But yes, I think we are very optimistic of -- or at least 30% plus growth, 30% to 40% growth range for this division.

items.statement: Consumer Durable division to outpace industry growth by 10-12 percentage points
items.quote: With our strategic focus across the RAC, CAC component and non -RAC component verticals, we are well positioned to outpace the industry growth by a minimum margin of 10% to 12%.

items.statement: Railway division revenue to double over next 2 financial years
items.quote: Backed by the strong order book and product portfolio expansion , w e remain optimistic of doubling this division's revenue over the next 2 financial years.

items.statement: CAC business expected to grow 20-30% in FY26
items.quote: We expect this division to grow at least by 20%, 25% to 30% range this year.

items.statement: FY26 capex ex-ECMS INR500 cr; with ECMS INR800-900 cr including Ascent expansion and Korea Circuits JV
items.quote: I think this year, the capex will be somewhere about -- close to about INR800 crores to INR900 crores, which is ongoing Ascent Circuit capex because last year, only the land came in and now the building and machinery are going to be added up, plus the new joint venture, Korea Circuits land and some part of the building will come in this year.

items.statement: ECMS application INR3,000 cr over 5 years for PCB categories across 3 entities
items.quote: In ECMS, we will be putting in an application of about INR3,000 crores, which is to be spent over a period of scheme in 5 years.

items.statement: Ascent Circuit expansion INR650 cr; commercial production by Q4 FY26
items.quote: Yes, that's right. It's a INR650 crore expansion.

items.statement: Korea Circuits JV INR2,500 cr over 5 years; Phase 1 commissioning Q4 FY27
items.quote: So in Korea circuit JV, we will be putting in an application of close to about INR2,500 crores, which is to be spent on a period of 5 years.

items.statement: Ascent Circuit operating at ~90% capacity; adding 30,000 sqm plant
items.quote: Well, currently, Ascent is moving at almost 90% of capacity, and that's why we are putting up another 30,000 square meter plant.

items.statement: Korea Circuits Phase 1: 10,000 sqm HDI facility
items.quote: And Korea Circuits will be -- the first phase will be 10,000 square meter of HDI to begin with, and then we'll keep on adding as we move ahead.

items.statement: Electronics division 2-year order book ~INR5,000 cr
items.quote: If I speak about 2 years order book, we are already sitting at close to about INR5,000 crores of order book kind of a thing at the moment from various customers, with various applications.

items.statement: Railway division order book INR20 bn+; received INR500 cr doors order and first couplers order
items.quote: we have received more than about INR500 crores of orders for the doors as well. And we have just recently last week received our first order for the couplers as well.

items.statement: Electronics division EBITDA margin 6.9% in FY25; target 10-12% in 2 years
items.quote: I was expecting -- personally, I was expecting that we'll cross 7.5% to 8% in this division, but it has come down to 6.9% because more of consumer durable applications were sold.

items.statement: PCB manufacturing (Korea JV) EBITDA margin 18-20%
items.quote: That's right. That's what generally the sector operates at. And they serve very high marquee customers like Micron and Samsung in the HDI category, and that's where we are already in touch with those customers at the moment.

items.statement: Consumer Durable division EBITDA INR562 cr, up 59% YoY
items.quote: Operating EBITDA for the year increased by 59% year-on-year and stood at INR562 crores compared to INR353 crores in financial year '24.

items.statement: RAC industry expected to reach 30-35 million units in 5 years
items.quote: What we expect that this industry should be in the range of 30 million to 35 million in the next 5 years' time, which is a good CAGR.

items.statement: April and May RAC demand strong for Amber despite weak summer
items.quote: But just to tell all of you, we have done pretty well in April. May is also going very, very fine for us.

items.statement: Net working capital days 9 days in FY25; maintainable at 10-15 days at year-end
items.quote: Our net working capital days for the year stood at 9 days through the efficient working capital management.

items.statement: Working capital days maintainable at 10-15 days on consolidated level at year-end
items.quote: But at the year-end kind of a thing, we think that, yes, it should be in the range of 10 to 15 days on a consol level.

items.statement: Net debt INR780 cr in FY25 vs INR615 cr in FY24
items.quote: On the balance sheet front, net debt stood at INR780 crores against INR615 crores underscoring our disciplined approach towards capital efficiency.

items.statement: Electronics division exploring capex funding from institutions for ECMS investment
items.quote: Coming to the funding part, as an Electronics division, we are already in touch for raising the funds for this kind of -- meeting the objective because we are going to get back. So we are already in touch with various institutions for that.

items.statement: ECMS scheme: 48% central govt reimbursement (25% on commissioning, 23% over 5 years TLI) plus ~35% state incentives
items.quote: So out of 48%, 25% will be reimbursed after the plant is commissioned and 23% will come in next 5 years after achieving the turnover -linked incentive and employee-linked incentives also.

items.statement: Electronics division adding industrial, auto, aerospace, defense applications to improve margin
items.quote: What we are adding is automobile, industrial, energy sector and the defense sector. That is what we are adding. And that is why we are very confident that the trajectory will go beyond 10%.

items.statement: Korea Circuits JV signed offtake agreement for first 2 years production capacity
items.quote: we have been able to successfully sign offtake agreement with Korea Circuits, where first 2 years of the production capacity will be offtaken to Korea Circui ts by Korea Circuits team to their existing customers from India.

items.statement: India PCB consumption INR32,000 cr (9% domestic); TAM $10 bn in 5 years; Amber targets 10% share
items.quote: So there is a TAM of about $10 billion of consumption, even if we assume that 50% will still be imported at that time, still, there is current level of INR3,000 crores worth of PCB getting manufactured, going to almost about $5 billion. So that's the opportunity size. And we expect to at least have 10% of this opportunity size moving forward.

items.statement: JV losses INR30 cr in FY25; expected to reduce to INR20-25 cr in FY26
items.quote: I think it a little -- it should come down by another INR10 crores or so. So INR20 crores to INR25 crores should be the range moving forward.

items.statement: Unexecuted order book of INR300 crores to be executed over next 2.5-3 years
items.quote: Our present order book is a total of INR300 crores -- unexecuted order book is a total of INR300 crores to be executed in the next 2.5 to 3 years.

items.statement: Total order book INR570 crores, 98% domestic, Mozambique project USD3 lakh
items.quote: The entire order book, 98% of the order book is domestic itself. Mozambique project is USD3 lakh only. So going ahead, but -- unexecuted order book is around INR300 crores, INR570 crores is the total order book that is there.

items.statement: 90% revenue from highways, 5-10% from railways and metros, targeting airports, public health engineering, urban infrastructure
items.quote: So right now, 90% of the revenue is coming from the highway sector only because we have just started working in the railways and metro sector and around 5% to 10% of the revenue is coming from the railway sector, railways and metros together.

items.statement: Target 60-70% domestic order book, 20-30% international order book going forward
items.quote: So I think with the client base improving, we can see improvements, thereby like we target that 60%, 70% of the order book will still come from the domestic market, but 20%, 30%, we are targeting that the international order book would increase.

items.statement: Purchased Mobile Bridge Inspection Unit and Falling Weight Deflectometer, added high-tech software for highway and bridge design
items.quote: We recently also made 2 purchases. That is one Mobile Bridge Inspection Unit and Falling Weight Deflectometer. So with these purchases now, the operational capacity has further strengthened.

items.statement: 450+ employees, 60-100 engineers at head office can handle 100 more projects, attrition 2-3%
items.quote: So right now, we have a total employee strength of 450 plus. We have a dedicated business development and a human resource team, which is working constantly towards the recruitment of new manpower as and when it is required, project to project.

items.statement: Debtor days reduced from 160-180 to 90-120 days, receivable cycle 60-90 days from NHAI/MoRTH
items.quote: So earlier, if you see the last 2 or 3 financial years, the debtor days was close to 160, 180, which has come down to a total receivable cycle of 90 to 120.

items.statement: CC limit over INR8.5 crores from HDFC and PNB, due for enhancement, exhausted bank guarantee limits
items.quote: Along with that, we definitely have support from our bankers, HDFC and PNB, where we have a total CC limit of over INR 8.5 crores and which is due for enhancement also now.

items.statement: Raised INR33.24 crores via preferential issue diluting 3 lakh shares, used for working capital and bank guarantees
items.quote: Recently when we did the preferential issue, we raised a total of INR 33.24 crores by diluting around 3 Lakh shares. So out of those INR33 crores, most of it were used for working capital, then another 25%, 30% of it is still lying with us for the future bank guarantees.

items.statement: NHAI debarment case hearings completed April 22, expecting stay or squash order soon, 8 of 10 past cases got stay in favour of consultants
items.quote: On 22nd of April, the hearings are completed. And we also heard that online hearing video conferencing. So according to our council also, the hearings went in a positive way inside of Dhruv and our joint venture partner, Global. And any time we are expecting either a stay order or squash according to our council.

items.statement: Targeting Zambia, Tanzania, Ghana, Nigeria in Africa; Saudi Arabia, UAE in Middle East; Vietnam, Cambodia in SE Asia; Nepal, Bangladesh in South Asia
items.quote: Along with Mozambique, we are targeting Zambia, Tanzania, Ghana, Nigeria in the African region. In Middle East, there is Saudi Arabia and Dubai, UAE. In Southeast Asia, there is Vietnam, Cambodia and South Asia, Nepal and Bangladesh. So, these are the territories we are expecting future orders.

items.statement: Entered private sector with HCC bridge design proof checking INR1.09 crores, targeting more private sector orders
items.quote: In Maharashtra, we signed an agreement worth INR1.09 crores with the HCC that is Hindustan Construction Company for Design Proof Checking of a key 2-lane bridge across Agardanda Creek on the Revas-Reddi Highway. This marks our entry into the private sector as well.

items.statement: Q4 FY25 order wins: West Central Railway INR11.05 cr, Bharatmala INR9.27 cr, 2 greenfield highways Kanpur INR7.85 cr, NHAI O&M INR6.37 cr, MMRDA Metro Line 5 INR1.35 cr, Indore Municipal Corp INR1.25 cr
items.quote: We were awarded with a general consultancy contract worth INR11.05 crores by West Central Railway segment so far, marking a significant diversification in our portfolio. We also received a INR9.27 crores order for independent engineer services under the Bharatmala Pariyojna.

items.statement: Q4 FY25 EBITDA INR4.09 cr up 75% YoY, PAT INR1.99 cr up 360% YoY, FY25 EBITDA INR15.78 cr up 6.96% YoY, PAT INR6.9 cr up 17.26% YoY
items.quote: In Q4 FY '25, Dhruv Consultancy Services reported a notable financial growth with a total income of INR28.03 crores, reflecting a 12.09% year-on-year increase. The EBITDA stood at INR4.09 crores, making a year-on-year growth of 75%. Profit after tax was INR1.99 crores, showing a significant increase of 360% as compared to FY '24.

items.statement: Political instability risk in African countries, riots in Manipur, mitigated by targeting only funded projects via World Bank, AfDB, ADB, EXIM Bank
items.quote: So one very big risk that is there is the political instability in such countries, because where there is infrastructure development going on in a large scale, the countries are either developing or underdeveloped. So yes, there is a political risk. There is a chance of riots and a lot of like delays in award of assignment.

items.statement: Strong second line leadership with CEO, CTO, design heads, business development VPs, HR VP; succession planning in place with 15-20 year veterans
items.quote: We have a CEO, we have a CTO, we have design heads. We have business development Vice Presidents. We have an HR Vice President. So these people are now looking at stronger -- with these people coming in, the execution capabilities have enhanced.

items.statement: Government plans 400 airports by 2050, 226 new airports in Tier 2/3 cities, targeting early entry in airport consultancy
items.quote: As far as airports are concerned, the central government has already made an announcement of constructing airports in Tier 2, Tier 3 cities with 226 new airports coming up. So there is a huge market available in the airport sector as well.

items.statement: Formed 21 strategic alliances with local consultants in different countries for international bids, JV partnerships for eligibility and local support
items.quote: We have formed such -- around 21 such strategic alliances in different, different countries, which is helping us bag assignments in the international market also.

items.statement: Private sector assignments have huge profitability margins, will improve cash flows and reduce need for equity/debt funding
items.quote: And going ahead also with private sector assignments coming in having huge profitability margins, I think cash flows would be much more on a positive side and stress -- there would be less stress on equity raising or debt funding as the cash flows are becoming more and more supportive.

items.statement: FY26 MDF domestic volume growth of 10-12% from existing plants; 72,000 cubic meters from new line; 84,000 cubic meters export volume
items.quote: So combined as a company, this would give us about a 30 % volume growth, including the production considered for the new line. So, this is what we expect to stand for the current year.

items.statement: FY26 MDF EBITDA margin ~12% and plywood EBITDA margin 7-8% excluding EPCG incentive
items.quote: I think I would be looking at approximately a 12% margin in MDF and a 7% to 8% margin in plywood, of course excluding the EPCG incentive.

items.statement: EPCG incentive balance of Rs. 51 crore to accrue over FY26 and FY27 proportionate to sales
items.quote: So the balance of about Rs. 51 crore is expected over FY'26 and FY'27.

items.statement: Tax rate expected around 20% for FY26
items.quote: But for FY'26, I would probably expect the tax rate of around 20%.

items.statement: Depreciation of approximately Rs. 100-102 crore for FY26
items.quote: I would say depreciation of approximately Rs. 100 crore to Rs. 102 crore.

items.statement: Capex for FY26 not more than Rs. 30-35 crore including balance new line capex
items.quote: No, I would say not more than Rs. 30 - Rs. 35 crore, yes.

items.statement: New thin MDF line targeting 35% capacity utilization in FY26; substantial contribution from Q2
items.quote: We are targeting capacity utilization of 35% for FY'26.

items.statement: Uttarakhand MDF at 80%, Andhra Pradesh at 50%, blended at 60% on 661,899 cubic meters capacity in Q4 FY25
items.quote: Uttarakhand MDF unit operated at 80% and Andhra Pradesh plant operated at 50% with blended capacity utilization at 60% on proportionately increased capacity of 661,899 cubic meters.

items.statement: Export volume target of ~84,000 cubic meters for FY26
items.quote: Yes, approximately about 84,000 cubic meters.

items.statement: Q4 FY25 MDF EBITDA margin 16.3% QoQ higher due to EPCG; plywood EBITDA margin 12.1% higher due to provision write-back
items.quote: MDF EBITDA margins at 16.3% were higher quarter-on-quarter due to EPCG scheme incentives. Plywood volumes were lower by 12% year-on-year. EBITDA margins at 12.1% were higher due to write back of provisions for turnover discounts.

items.statement: FY25 gross margins fell 900 bps to 46.9%; EBITDA margins fell 615 bps to 10.9% due to 3.7% realization fall and 23% wood price increase
items.quote: Gross margins of the company fell by 900 basis points to 46.9%. EBITDA margins at 10.9% were lower by 615 basis points and post-tax profits at Rs. 72.11 crore were lower by 49%.

items.statement: Timber prices expected to fall 5-7% in FY26; Q4 FY25 North consumption Rs. 6.67/kg, South Rs. 6.38/kg
items.quote: I think we would probably expect to see around 5% to 7% fall in timber prices during F Y'26

items.statement: MDF industry demand growing 15-20%; imports down to ~1,100 cubic meters/month; no major new capacity coming in FY26
items.quote: Market demand for the general growth of the MDF industry continues to remain strong as opposed to other industries at 15 % to 20%. And what we foresee is that there are no major additional capacities also coming in.

items.statement: BIS QCO implementation from February 2026 expected to boost domestic furniture manufacturing and MDF/plywood demand
items.quote: Domestic furniture manufacturing industry prospects will receive a boost with the expected implementation of BIS QCO from February 2026. This should also lead to increased demand for furniture manufactured in the country and consequently, raw materials like MDF and plywood.

items.statement: Value-added mix 50% volume, 62% value in Q4 FY25 and full year; thin MDF to be 15-20% higher realization than current blended
items.quote: For the quarter it was 50 % in volume terms and 62% in value terms and the figure was similar for the full year also.

items.statement: Thin MDF industrial grade realizations ~Rs. 25,000-26,000/cubic meter; value-added mix on new line may take ~3 years to reach 50%
items.quote: For the thin-grade industrial MDF, realisations will be approximately about 25,000 to 26,000 per cubic meter.

items.statement: Action Tesa in talks for Greenfield MDF line in South India; Greenply at optimum utilization leading to price discipline
items.quote: I think, not on the unorganized, but we know that Action is in talks with regards to installing a line in the south of India.

items.statement: BIS QCO to reduce unorganized segment price-cutting power as compliance costs increase
items.quote: Due to the BIS implementation, we also see the threat from the unorganized segment minimizing going forward because when the new standards are declared and brought into notification, for compliance, there will definitely be a cost increase on account of the unorganized players.

items.statement: Q4 FY25 export margin ~1.75%; thin MDF exports 25-30% higher price; dollar movement to aid rupee realizations
items.quote: And the margins in Q4 were approximately about 1.75%.

items.statement: Net working capital 36 days in Q4 FY25, up 8 days YoY due to lower turnover and high inventory
items.quote: Net working capital at 36 days has shown an increase of 8 days year-on-year due to lower turnover and high inventory levels.

items.statement: Net debt Rs. 165 crore as of March 31, 2025 inclusive of Rs. 336 crore for expansion project
items.quote: Net debt stands at Rs. 165 crore as on 31st March 2025, inclusive of Rs. 336 crore for the expansion project.

items.statement: Timber procurement through contractor network within 30-450 km radius; small direct farmer supply
items.quote: Yes, we have a network of contractors who procure most of the material for us. Apart from that, we have a few farmers who come directly to the plant and supply the material but that would be a small proportion of the total.

items.statement: Sales network 85% channel (B2C), 15% OEM; consumption majority B2B for readymade furniture
items.quote: So, if you look at it in terms of sales network, it's primarily B2C because almost 85% of our sales happen through the channel and only about 15% is to the OEM manufacturers. But if you look at it in terms of consumption, majority of the MDF uses raw materials in producing readymade furniture. So, in consumption terms, it's more B2B.

items.statement: BIS QCO implementation from February 2026; commercial grade MDF sales discontinued in Q4 FY25 (nil vs 40,924 cubic meters YoY)
items.quote: MDF domestic sales volumes fell by 25 % year-on-year. This was on account of discontinuing sales of commercial grade MDF in anticipation of implementation of BIS QCOs. Commercial grade in Quarter 4 FY'25 was Nil as opposed to 40,924 cubic meters in Quarter 4 FY'24.

items.statement: Admin and employee expenses down ~Rs. 15 crore in FY25; employee costs flat despite 8% increment
items.quote: I think the admin expenses and employee expenses put together have come down by approximately Rs. 15 crore this year and employee costs in spite of 8% increment last year have remained almost fixed year-on-year.

items.statement: South India MDF supply ~1.3 million cubic meters from 3-4 manufacturers; South generates 35-40% of domestic demand
items.quote: Okay, there only about 3 or 4 MDF manufacturers present in South India. So we have Greenpanel, Century, Rushil Decor and one unorganized company. So the total supply would be about 1.3 million cubic meters and approximately 35% to 40% of the demand is generated from South India.

items.statement: New thin MDF line still under supplier control in optimization phase; handover expected by Q2 FY26
items.quote: Because at the moment, the line is still under the control of the plant supplier. And it is still under the optimization phase. Because it's, let's say, a very technologically advanced line. And it's a very high speed line. Hence, it's a longer period of optimization. Hence, we foresee that by quarter two, we should have the line handed over to us.

items.statement: FY26 volume growth expected in mid-teens; revenue growth expected in high single digits due to pricing pressure
items.quote: Looking ahead at FY' 26 we expect volume growth in mid -teens. However, given the pricing pressure we expect the revenue growth to be in the high single digits as it stands.

items.statement: EBITDA margins expected to remain in 28% to 30% band for foreseeable future
items.quote: We would like to reiterate that margins will continue to be in the 28% to 30% band in the foreseeable future.

items.statement: Q4 FY25 EBITDA margin at 32.1%, up 520 bps YoY and 80 bps QoQ driven by favorable product mix and new launches
items.quote: Our EBITDA margin for the quarter was 32.1%, up 520 bps Y-o-Y and 80 bps Q-o-Q. Primarily driven by a more favorable product mix coupled with product launches especially in the ROW markets.

items.statement: FY25 EBITDA margin maintained at 30% despite absence of PLI benefits
items.quote: On an overall basis, we reported revenue of Rs.2387 crore, reflecting a Y-o-Y growth of 4.5% in-line with our FY'25 guidance. Notably, we were able to maintain margins at 30% Y -o-Y, despite the absence of PLI benefits this year.

items.statement: US market experiencing slower than expected growth due to external challenges and customer destocking; expected to turn around in FY26
