items.statement: Tax rate appears 34% due to MAT in subsidiary; cash outflow 25%; to normalize to 25% in FY26
items.quote: The tax rate is already 25%. It is only on the face of it that you see 34. The actual outflow is 25% still.

items.statement: Seasonality: Q1 weaker due to labor shortages in North India (50-60% of sales); H2 stronger, Q3 best quarter
items.quote: Generally, H2 is better than the 1st half and 2nd Quarter is also good. 2nd is good. 3rd is the best.

items.statement: Order book remains extremely strong with long-term contracts providing revenue visibility
items.quote: Our order book remains extremely strong, and due to long-term contracts with major clients, we have greater visibility on the frame to plan, to implement, and to execute.

items.statement: Received INR 1,089 crore 4-year contract from Vedanta for end-to-end supply chain management
items.quote: One of the biggest highlights continues to be the INR 1,089 crores four-year contract from Vedanta Limited, where we manage end-to-end supply chain for aluminum, big iron and magnesium cargo from their plant in Jharsuguda to key ports and hubs around the country.

items.statement: Received INR 170 crore contract from Hindustan Zinc and INR 41 crore 3-year project from Tata Steel
items.quote: In addition to this ultra-large order, we've received several very large orders, including the INR170 crores contract from Hindustan Zinc Limited , and a three-year INR41 crores project from Tata Steel Limited.

items.statement: Recent orders include INR 23 crore from Sriram Alkalies and INR 70 crore from Bharat Aluminium Company
items.quote: Recently, in the last two weeks, we received two large orders, one from Sriram Alkalies & Chemicals, which is a unit of DCM Sriram Limited, for rake, container rake, tanker rake, transportation of CSL to Vedanta. The order is valued at INR23 crores. And the last order, which we received around the 15th of May, just a few days ago, was a consolidated finished goods material handling contract from B

items.statement: Domestic volumes grew 31% YoY to 79,840 TEUs driven by specialized container demand
items.quote: On the domestic side, our volumes grew by a healthy 31%, led by strong demand, particularly for specialized containers.

items.statement: EXIM volumes declined 12% YoY to 133,635 TEUs due to port congestion and geopolitical tensions
items.quote: In contrast, EXIM volumes declined by 12%, affected by continued congestion at transshipment ports, irregular vessel Western Carriers ( schedules, and geopolitical tensions

items.statement: Expect strong domestic growth in FY26 driven by specialized containers, new rail services, and tanker rake projects
items.quote: We are fairly very confident that we'll have a stellar year in domestic business. We don't see many headwinds in that.

items.statement: EXIM volumes expected to recover as Red Sea route reopens and shipping capacity increases
items.quote: The prospect of a large-scale return of container ships to the Red Sea following ceasefire by US and Houthi militia in Yemen would flood the market with shipping capacity as global TUE per mile demand would decline by about 6% if the ships could sail through the Red Sea and the Suez Canal instead of the larger route around Cape of Good Hope in Africa

items.statement: EBITDA margin just south of 7% in FY25, impacted by EXIM pressures but within anticipated range
items.quote: EBITDA came in at a strong INR120 crores with a margin of just south of 7%, while PAT stood at INR65 crores with a margin of 3.8%.

items.statement: Expect margins to improve steadily in FY26 as EXIM recovers and domestic volumes grow
items.quote: While margins were impacted by pressures in the EXIM segment, they remained within our anticipated range, and we expect margins to improve steadily going forward.

items.statement: Undertook INR 70 crore capex in FY25 for specialized handling equipment and containers
items.quote: Of course, to support our long-term contracts and improve operational agility, we undertook a massive capex this year of approximately INR70 crores.

items.statement: Plan INR 100 crore capex in FY26, largest in company history, funded partly by IPO proceeds
items.quote: My intention this year is to increase it further. We are intending to do a capex of approximately INR100 crores in this financial, sir, based on the strong demand that we are seeing. And this will be, you know, spread across the year. And this will again be the largest capex in the history of our company, sir.

items.statement: INR 156 crore of IPO proceeds remain unutilized, held in FDs, to be deployed for FY26 capex
items.quote: And till date we have about INR156 crores still with us, which will go into the capex that I was talking about. Part of it will go into the capex. So, about INR156 crores is still with us, sir. Out of the INR400 crores raised in primary, sir.

items.statement: Procured ~300 FEUs (40-ft specialized containers) in FY25 aligned with customer specifications
items.quote: In response of this extremely strong demand, we procured approximately 300 further FEUs, containers aligned with the customer specifications during the year, reinforcing our commitment to customized service delivery.

items.statement: Launched new rail services from Western India to Bengaluru (south), Jaipur (north), with Indore and Kathuwas starting soon
items.quote: We have already started services in two destinations, one in north and one in south. Western Carriers ( The destination in the south is Bengaluru, and the destination in north is Jaipur. We will shortly be starting our train freight services in Central India, Indore, and to another destination in north, which is Kathuwas, by the end of this

items.statement: Successfully completed first tanker rail movement from Ankleshwar to Lanjigarh for DCM Shriram
items.quote: We also recently, like I pointed out, started the first tanker rail movement from Ankleshwar to Lanjigarh for DCM Sriram, and this has been done, completed successfully, and this is expected to constantly go on increasing as the months go forward.

items.statement: Over 80% revenue from clients with 3+ year relationships, high retention validates trust
items.quote: We take particular pride in our high customer retention. More than 80% of our revenues are contributed by clients who've been with us for over three years.

items.statement: Multimodal logistics market (rail+road) valued at INR 1,714 billion in FY24, projected 22% CAGR to INR 4,667 billion by FY29
items.quote: If I remember correctly a lot of research reports have pointed out that the growth from multimodal logistics is supposed to be very, very steep going forward also, sir. And it is an area of great opportunity. So, according to the 1Lattice report, multimodal, that is the space that we work in that is the rail and road market in India, was valued at about 1,714 billion in FY24. And this is projected

items.statement: Working capital cycle stretched to 120-150 days for new project rollouts vs 90-130 days historically
items.quote: Whereas in the past, many projects were rolled out within 90 to 130 days, we are now seeing something like 120 to 150 days rolled out on many projects, and in some cases even longer.

items.statement: Expect working capital cycle to improve dramatically in FY26 as projects move from launch to implementation
items.quote: As a lot of these projects have gone from launch to implementation, we expect the payment cycle to improve dramatically. So, we expect margins to be much better and going towards where we were earlier.

items.statement: Withdrew CARE Ratings; CRISIL rating remains strong at A-minus
items.quote: We have already withdrawn the CARE ratings. We have the two companies, one was CARE and the other was CRISIL. CRISIL continues to be with us and our rating is a strong A-minus with them.

items.statement: Rail freight and diesel costs stable YoY, no significant near-term pressure expected
items.quote: For the rail business, it's always the rail freight. And for the road business, it's always or the road component of the business is diesel. I'm happy to say that for the road component, which is the first mile and the last mile, diesel prices have remained more or less flat-lined for the last year or so. So, there's not been much of a pressure in increasing that. And rail freight also has remaine

items.statement: No formal FY26 revenue/EBITDA guidance given due to geopolitical uncertainty; may provide in next quarter
items.quote: It would be very foolhardy of me to come up with strong guidance. So I don't want to give guidance for the entire year at this time. Maybe if the situation is far more predictable, maybe in the next quarter I would like to give a guidance.

items.statement: Expect FY26 to be a stellar year if EXIM recovers to prior levels alongside strong domestic demand
items.quote: But I would like to say that we expect this to be a stellar year since we see very good demand in the domestic business and we are seeing green shoots of growth again in our EXIM business. So if you can come back to where the EXIM delivered numbers were in the earlier years, we can consider this, we can predict this to be a stellar year for us.

items.statement: Northern Dedicated Freight Corridor ~75-80% complete, expected commissioning by Dec 2025 or Mar 2026
items.quote: The Northern Dedicated Freight Corridor, you know, is about 75%, 80% done. Last time we checked, Varnama in Baroda, the Northern Freight Corridor was working. And from Baroda to JNPT, the work is going on and going on in full swing. We expect this to be completed by December 2025 or maybe, you know, March '26.

items.statement: Geopolitical volatility and Middle East dynamics create uncertainty for EXIM recovery timing
items.quote: But it's a wait and watch. As you know, the situation in the Middle East remains quite dynamic. So, it would be very hard for me to predict if it will happen tomorrow or maybe take some time.

items.statement: Expect overall company contribution margins to return above 30% as lending distribution recovers
items.quote: We do expect that overall margins for the company will come back upwards of 30% and that will allow us to cover our fixed costs and therefore drive profitability back into the results.

items.statement: Expect lending business to recover to levels of 4 quarters ago by H2 FY26
items.quote: We should sort of go back to at least what we used to do 4 quarters back as far as lending is concerned over the second-half of this year.

items.statement: Lending contribution margin to stabilize at ~40% as book transitions to new FLDG contracts over 2-3 quarters
items.quote: We do feel that as it stabilizes over the next 2 or 3 quarters, t he portfolio contribution margin which lending used to get to us of about 40% that should stabilize in the same ballpark

items.statement: Net payment margin improved QoQ from 13 bps to 15 bps in Q4 FY25
items.quote: In the last quarter, actually the net payment margin has gone up from 13 bps to 15 bps as you compared quarter-on-quarter.

items.statement: Payment business net contribution margin sustainable at 20%+ without MDR benefit
items.quote: Yes, I think it should stay in the same zone, 20% plus even without the PPI and UPI there.

items.statement: Payments GMV grew from Rs 38,000 cr in FY24 to Rs 1,15,000 cr in FY25, doubling year-over-year
items.quote: if you see our numbers, last year we have done Rs. 38,000 crores in FY '24 for the full year, we had payment GMV o f Rs. 38,000 crores and this year we have done Rs. 1,15,000 crores of total

items.statement: Pocket UPI and RuPay card identified as hero products driving payment growth with high retention
items.quote: our hero product currently is Pocket UPI and followed by Ru Pay card, which is in the process of actually just getting the right growth numbers

items.statement: UPI share of payment GMV increased from ~30% to 36% in Q4 FY25
items.quote: So earlier, roughly it was nearly 30%, which has gone to 36% now, right.

items.statement: ZIP EMI GMV grew 32% QoQ between Q3 and Q4 FY25 while shorter duration ZIP product being discontinued
items.quote: Between Q3 and Q4 that number has grown 32% quarter-on-quarter and like I mentioned at the top of the call in my opening remarks that given in any case, we work with partners both banks, NBFCs, we are seeing positive commentary from lending partners about a potential recovery in the second-half of the year.

items.statement: Received full PA-PG license for ZaakPay from RBI, removing prior uncertainty
items.quote: We have received the full PAPG license from RBI and now we believe we can play an even larger role in the payments ecosystem.

items.statement: MDR on PPI UPI under discussion by RBI and industry, expected to go live soon and benefit Pocket UPI
items.quote: MDR on UPI, MDR on PPI, UPI, something that is already in motion from RBI and it is under discussion in the payments ecosystem across multiple industry players and should go live soon.

items.statement: IPO proceeds received late December, deployment started second half of January across payments pre-funding, customer acquisition, incentives and lending FLDG FDs
items.quote: Given the fact that the IPO proceeds only came to us at the flag end of December and we started using them in a way towards the second-half of January as we did those expenses.

items.statement: Merchant side scaling includes sound box, card, EDC machine deployment and merchant lending but remains small vs consumer side
items.quote: We are trying to scale up on the merchant side also across devices as well as merchant lending, but currently that is a small business for us and it will take us a little bit of time to scale that up.

items.statement: Borrowings and liabilities increased from Rs 450-620 cr due to daily wallet/merchant outstanding from 3x payment scale-up, settles next day
items.quote: Because of the scale up of the business, you should expect that the liabilities for one day will go up and if we scale up payments even further next year, this will be again a higher number, but that gets paid off the next day.

items.statement: Indirect costs optimized from Rs 119 cr to Rs 110 cr QoQ, expected to remain at this level or lower with AI-driven cost stripping
items.quote: We have in fact come down from about Rs. 119 crores to about Rs. 110 crores this quarter. And I think going forward, we will continue to optimize on these costs.

items.statement: Payment business gross margin (net payment revenue minus gateway cost minus incentives) at 23.9% in Q4 FY25
items.quote: If you see the EBITDA margin last quarter, the gross margin is at 23.9%, which is net payment revenue minus payment gateway cost minus user incentive.

items.statement: Lending net take rate after DLG and credit costs stable at 4-4.5% range in steady state
items.quote: Take rates in lending have continued to remain stable. So from a unit economics perspective, net take that we earn, which is after the DLG costs and other credit costs, etc., can be about 4%-4.5% range.

items.statement: Adding ~20 million users annually; significant headroom to double or triple user base over 3-5 years
items.quote: Our current run rate is about 20 million or so, which we are adding on a yearly basis. What that does is actually exposes more people to the idea of Pocket UPI and therefore increases the opportunity for them to come and become retained in our customer base.

items.statement: Welcome wallet competition as it grows overall pie; MobiKwik remains dominant wallet player
items.quote: We do want wallet as a sector within all the larger payments sector to also grow. Currently, we are the dominating player in this sector, but there are other players also that have a play.

items.statement: Lending recovery dependent on partner disbursement pace; worst is behind but growth tied to partner appetite
items.quote: we will only grow at the pace they want to grow, but we are equally confident that t he worst___9.05__ is behind us

items.statement: Lending expenses elevated due to front-loaded DLG cost booking (since Sept) and back-ended revenue recognition on lower disbursement base
items.quote: We have also moved to the DLG model starting September where a larger part of the cost gets booked upfront, pretty much all the cost gets booked upfront and very small revenue comes upfront. So the revenue is back-ended, cost is front-ended and that is causing the overall lending related expenses to be slightly elevated mathematically.

items.statement: Credit growth expected to be more than 2% above industry growth for FY26
items.quote: We expect our credit growth to be more than 2% over the industry growth.

items.statement: NIM guided at 3.7-3.75% for full year FY26
items.quote: With respect to margins , as two more rate cuts are expected, we expect that NIM to be in the range of 3.7-3.75 for the full year.

items.statement: Cost-to-income ratio expected around 50% for FY26
items.quote: Considering our branch expansion and additional manpower plant, our cost to income ratio Classification | EXTERNAL would continue to be around 50% in ‘25-26

items.statement: GNPA expected below 150 bps and net NPA below 1% for FY26
items.quote: GNPA is expected to be less than 150 basis point s and net NPA to be less than 1% for the full year.

items.statement: Slippages expected below 1% of asset book for FY26
items.quote: Slippages would be expected to be below 1% of our asset book.

items.statement: ROA expected in range of 1.55-1.65% for FY26
items.quote: We expect with the reasons adduced above, we will continue to maintain our ROA. It will be in the range of 1.55-1.65.

items.statement: CD ratio to be maintained around 85% for FY26
items.quote: The CD ratio would be maintained at around 85% levels during the coming year too.

items.statement: Plan to open 19 lite branches and 9 regular branches by end of H1 FY26
items.quote: With respect to branch expansion for the current year, we have planned opening 19 lite branches and 9 regular branches before the end of the first half of the current year, mostly in the Southern and Western parts of the country.

items.statement: RAM verticals grew 20% YoY, constitute 86% of advances portfolio
items.quote: In tune with that RAM verticals have grown by 20% year-on-year that is 3% quarter-on-quarter constituting 86% of the overall advances portfolio.

items.statement: Commercial loan book grew 21% YoY, share increased to 36%
items.quote: The commercial business continued to grow at 21% over the previous year, with significant contributions from various channels during the year.

items.statement: Agriculture loan book grew 20% YoY, 6% QoQ
items.quote: In spite of various challenges, the agriculture loan book had a growth of 20% year-on-year, 6% quarter-on-quarter and achieved all the targets and sub targets under priority sector for all the quarters of the year.

items.statement: Co-lending Amazon BNPL book at Rs. 844 crores, onboarding norms tightened
items.quote: Our co-lending Amazon BNPL program is performing well, and the book is around Rs. 844 crores. In view of the household elevated leverage, we are cautious in ramping up this book.

items.statement: Precious metal division wound down, outstanding reduced from Rs. 674 cr to Rs. 41 cr
items.quote: Also, we have decided to wind up the precious metal division, which we st arted in 2019 as it was not ROA accretive . We had outstanding of Rs. 674 crores at the beginning of the year and reduced to Rs. 41 crores on 31/03/2025.

items.statement: Co-lending with NBFCs book above Rs. 472 crores, consciously lowered due to lower margins
items.quote: Our partnerships for co-lending with NBFCs continue to perform well and the loan book under this segment is above Rs. 472 crores. We have consciously lowered this book due to lower margins.

items.statement: NIM maintained at 4.05% in Q4 FY25 and 4.09% for full year FY25, down 11 bps YoY
items.quote: I am happy to say that we were able to maintain NIM for the 4th quarter at 4.05% and for the full year at 4.09%. NIM dropped during the year by 11 basis points from 4.2 during the previous year.

items.statement: Cost of deposits increased 8 bps sequentially in Q4 (guided 10 bps), full year cost 5.61% up 42 bps YoY
items.quote: The cost of deposits increased by 8 basis points sequentially as against 10 basis points guided by us in the last call. For the full year, the cost of deposits was 5.61% showing an increase of 42 basis points from 5.19% of the previous year.

items.statement: Yield on advances increased 3 bps sequentially in Q4 despite rate cut, full year 10.15% up 20 bps YoY
items.quote: The yield on advances increased by 3 basis points during the quarter in spite of the rate cut. For the full year, the yield on advances was 10.15%, showing an increase of 20 basis points from 9.95% of the previous year.

items.statement: Yield on investments increased 14 bps sequentially in Q4, full year 6.61% up 38 bps YoY
items.quote: The yield on investments has increased by 14 basis points during the quarter. For the full year, the yield on investments was at 6.61%, showing an increase of 38 basis points from 6.23% of the previous year.

items.statement: Gross NPA 0.76%, Net NPA 0.2%, standard restructured 0.64% with 41.24% provision coverage
items.quote: Due to lower slippages, recoveries, upgrades, and write-off, our gross NPA has come down to 0.76%. Our net NPA remains at a level of 0.2 and we would continue to maintain the net NPA at less than 1% of our book.

items.statement: Gross slippages Rs. 179 cr in Q4, Rs. 482 cr for FY25 (0.57% of loan book)
items.quote: Our gross slippage during the quarter was at Rs. 179 crores and for the full year it was Rs. 482 crores which is 0.57% of our loan book.

items.statement: SMA 30+ at Rs. 254 cr (0.3% of loan book) down from 0.38% previous year
items.quote: SMA 30+ numbers were at Rs. 254 crores as at 31/03/2025, which is 0.3% of our loan book reduced from 0.38% of the previous year, indicating continued maintenance of control over this aspect.

items.statement: Recovered Rs. 182 cr from technically written-off accounts in Q4, Rs. 638 cr for FY25 vs Rs. 341 cr in FY24
items.quote: With our persistent focus on recovery from technically written-off books, we were able to recover a sum of Rs. 182 crores during the quarter . Total recovery during the year is Rs. 638 crores as against Rs. 341 crores of Financial Year '23-24.

items.statement: Credit cost 0.64% annualized in Q4, Rs. 25 cr prudential provisions added (cumulative Rs. 100 cr)
items.quote: For the quarter under review, we have provided a sum of Rs. 136 crores towards NPA migrations, standard assets and prudential provisions and credit costs works out to 0.64% on an annualized basis. As done in the last 3 quarters, we have provided a sum of Rs. 25 crores towards the prudential provisions and cumulative provision available under this is Rs. 100 crores.

items.statement: CRAR at 18.17%, no need to raise capital in FY26 for growth plan
items.quote: Our CRAR Basel-III continues to be healthy and is at 18.17% providing us comfortable headroom for growth. There may not be any need to raise money in Financial Year '25-26 for the growth plan.

items.statement: Declared dividend of 130% for FY25 vs 120% previous year, subject to shareholder approval
items.quote: I am happy to share that we have declared a dividend of 130% as against 120% last year and this is subject to shareholder 's approval.

items.statement: Mr. J. Natarajan (Executive Director) demitting office, Mr. Sankar Balabhadra Patruni joined as new Executive Director
items.quote: Before I conclude, I would like to thank our E D, Mr. J. Natarajan, who is demitting office on Wednesday for his excellent support and guidance for the growth of the Bank over the years.

items.statement: CASA grew 3% YoY, term deposits grew 20% YoY, deposit base crossed Rs. 1 trillion
items.quote: Our CASA grew by 3% over the previous year . Financial Year ' 24-25 was the first full year of our acquisition channel. The Bank had also launched new variants in CASA products. This resulted in opening more than 19,000 plus a ccounts with balances more than Rs. 400 crores.

items.statement: Digital transactions grew 115% YoY, share at 98%, DLite App has 1.3M monthly active users and 5M downloads
items.quote: Our digital transactions grew by 115% in Financial Year '25 and the share of digital transactions stands at 98%. We have rolled out our new version of our mobile DLite App with enhanced features during the year. I am happy to say that the rating for the App is 4.7 in Google Play Store and 4.1 in Apple Store and there are 1.3 million monthly active users for our DLite App and 5 million downloads fo

items.statement: Outlook for FY26 cautiously optimistic due to border escalation uncertainties and margin pressures
items.quote: The sudden escalation at the border in the last few days has also added more uncertainties for the coming year. Considering the above , the outlook for the Financial Year '25-26 remains cautiously optimistic, we need to navigate margin pressures too and monitor asset quality closely.

items.statement: Operating profit margin guidance of 2.3% to 2.5% for near term; software mix shift may lift margins slowly over 3-4 years
items.quote: We have been talking about between 2.3 % to 2.5% of operating profit. We will be happy if we are able to stay in this consistently, but definitely, as I have said, because of the focus on the software and this thing - subscription vertical, we think this can go up in future, but I think for now we should stay with between 2.3 to 2.5%.

items.statement: Gross margins broadly stable; large deals in Technology Solutions at lower margins will pressure weighted average
items.quote: I think we should be able to maintain this. I mean, there can be some mixed change, but otherwise, broadly, we should be able to maintain this.

items.statement: Cloud Solutions Group resell/subscription margins 5.5-6%; professional services margins 20%+
items.quote: So, see, somewhere between 5.5 and 6, so it is on the higher side, is what we appropriate from the pure resell and the subscription model. And there is additional margins to be had on professional services, which can be anywhere from around 20% plus.

items.statement: India revenue grew 26% YoY in Q4; UAE 24%; Saudi Arabia 7%; Africa 11%
items.quote: From a geography perspective, the revenue growth was contributed by a strong growth in India at 26%, UAE at 24%. We are also seeing signs of growth recovery in the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia at 7%. And Africa has continued its momentum both East and West Africa at 11% year-on-year growth rates.

items.statement: Saudi Arabia is third largest geography; expect strong double-digit growth for next 3 years driven by AI infrastructure, cloud, and PC penetration catch-up
items.quote: We do expect a good strong double-digit growth coming back in Saudi both in the coming year and future years. Because all parts of the market as I mentioned earlier, it's not just the infrastructure side. If we look at the mid-market, there is a very big mid-market in Saudi that's going to grow. Even the PC penetration in Saudi for a 36 million population, there are only 5 million PCs in the marke

items.statement: India growth driven by data center infrastructure, premium mobility, upcountry expansion, GCCs, startups, and AI services
items.quote: Largely for India will be the value infrastructure, the premiumization and touching the premium market as well as the new areas like GCCs and startups, etc.

items.statement: Large deals in Technology Solutions Group less than 20% of business; run rate ~80%
items.quote: It's hard to comment because the deals happen every quarter and I would say the large deals will be less than 20% of our business. The run rate should definitely continue to be around 80%.

items.statement: Capex range Rs. 40-60 crore per quarter; spike in Q4 due to ProConnect new business
items.value: Rs. 40 crores to Rs. 60 crores per quarter
items.quote: Our CAPEX, Rucha, has always been limited. And this CAPEX is more specific and that too has happened more in ProConnect because of the new businesses that they had got, but otherwise it will range between Rs. 40 crores to Rs. 60 crores per quarter.

items.statement: Q4 closing working capital 34 days, same as prior year; AR days up but offset by lower inventory and higher payable days
items.quote: We achieved a 34-day closing working capital, which is same as compared to the previous year Q4.

items.statement: Full-year inventory provision 1 bps, bad debts 6 bps, both below historical averages of 5 bps and 10 bps
items.quote: For the full year, inventory provision is about 1 bps and bad debts about 6 bps, lower than what has been our traditional average, which is about 5 bps in inventory and about 10 bps in AR.

items.statement: Arena debt ~$170 million; Paynet proceeds $74 million used to repay debt, targeting ~$100 million
items.quote: Arena debt levels are currently at about $170 odd million. This money that we have got is about $70 million. So, ideally, it should come down to about $100 million.

items.statement: Paynet divestment closed; proceeds INR 626 crore (~US$74 million) received net of expenses
items.quote: All approvals were obtained during the quarter, and the deal was closed, and the proceeds of INR 626 crores, roughly US$74 million, was received, net of related expenses.

items.statement: Final dividend Rs. 6.8 per share for FY25; similar to FY24; ~40% of profits excluding Paynet gain
items.quote: We had deliberations at the Board yesterday, and we are happy to declare Rs. 6.8 per share of final dividend for the year ended 31st March 2025. The dividend amount for FY '25 is similar to FY '24 dividend, and this constitutes nearly 40% of our total profits for the year without considering the one-off impact on account of Paynet divestment.

items.statement: UAE corporate tax rising from 9% to 15% under global minimum tax; FY26 effective tax rate guided 25-27%
items.quote: Next year, the global minimum tax is coming in impacting some of the economies including the UAE where from 9% it will move to 15% . So, we expect next year , the tax rate should range between 25 % to 27%, maybe closer to th is thing

items.statement: Tariff changes and geopolitical tensions monitored; no short-term direct impact but potential supply chain disruptions as brands diversify manufacturing
items.quote: The direct tariff impact on the geographies we are in, there doesn't seem to be any short-term impact. However, we can expect some supply chain disruptions because people are putting capacities in different places and if for some reason, there is an upside or a downside in the geography and the sourcing was coming from one place and the source is now coming from multiple places, there could be som

items.statement: India-Turkey geopolitical situation seen as purely commercial; no business impact expected
items.quote: We are an Indian headquartered Company, and we really are proud of our heritage and values, deeply rooted in India. And we are a global Company. We are in 40 countries. And it's purely commercial. Our presence and work we do is managed by a local team. So, we don't see there is no political inclination to any of the businesses we are in. It's purely commercial. So, we don't see any impact on this.

items.statement: Software mix to exceed 20% of revenue in 2-3 years from 15% today; Technology Solutions mix rising; Endpoint Solutions may accelerate with Windows 10-11 refresh and AI PCs
items.quote: Today it's 15. We should be more than 20 and higher as a percentage of our total business. Clearly, the Technology Solutions Group as a mix also should be higher because that's the part of the business you have already seen it's grown between 25% and 30% over the course of the quarter and high double digit during the year. So, mix on both those will go up. I wouldn't be surprised. The PC market ha

items.statement: Market growth opportunity 15-20% in India, UAE, Saudi (75% of business); cloud growing 18-20%; India IT 10-12%, Middle East 8-10% per Gartner
items.quote: Clearly, from a market perspective, in the three big geographies, which are 75% of our total business, which is India, UAE and Saudi, there is a growth rate of about 20% to be had. Now it will depend on how we execute, what we can take, what is appropriate for Redington, basis margin, and basis all of the other factors that we work on. It will depend on that. items.quote: As stated earlier, we want to double our sales as a company over the next 3 years and inc h closer to our ambition of being a $1 billion company

items.statement: FY25 was challenging with uncertain macroeconomic and weak demand scenario across markets
items.quote: Overall, uncertain macroeconomic and weak demand scenario across our markets made FY '25 a challenging year.

items.statement: Price declines of 2% to 5% across most product categories, Pipes decline more than 10% driven by PVC resin meltdown
items.quote: Further, there were price decl ines by 2% to 5% across most of our product categories, placing significant margin pressures. For P ipes, the decline was more than 10%, driven by a meltdown in PVC resin prices

items.statement: Margin erosion significantly lower than price decline due to agile cost management and contribution margin improvement missions
items.quote: Therefore, nearly across all the categories, this is an important point to note. The margin erosion was significantly lower than the price decline experienced in the market.

items.statement: Consolidated revenue FY25 Rs.3,615 crore, 7% higher than last year; Q4 revenue grew 9% YoY to Rs.929 crore
items.quote: In terms of results, our consolidated revenue in FY25 was Rs.3,615 crore, which was 7% higher than last year, and we finished at an operating EBITDA of Rs.88 crore.

items.statement: Pipes volume growth 76% for FY25 and 80% in Q4, establishing as one of fastest-growing players
items.quote: So, at a headline level, the volume growth for the year in pipes for us was 76% and which is what significantly drove our revenue performance this time.

items.statement: Chennai AAC block Line 2 commissioned, doubling capacity to 4 lakh cubic meters per year
items.quote: The first milest one I want to share with you all is commissioning of our Chennai Line 2 and with that, we have doubled our AAC block capacity in Chennai to 4 lakh cubic meters per year, making it one of the largest such facilities in the country

items.statement: New greenfield OPVC pipes plant in Patna started, Phase 1 capacity ~5,000 tons per annum, revenue potential north of Rs.100 crore, capex Rs.35-40 crore
items.quote: The second update is on the start of a new state-of-the-art greenfield plant for OPVC pipes in Patna, which represents the next generation of pipe technology and makes us one of very few players in the industry to have access to this technology.

items.statement: Parador Q4 revenue grew 10% YoY with 8% volume growth and 2% price increase, first price increase in 10-12 quarters
items.quote: In quarter 4 alone, and quarter 4 for us was one of the best quarters we've had in nearly 3 years. Our revenue grew by 10% was a combination of both volume growth at 8% and a 2% price increase.

items.statement: Parador steady-state operating margin target 8-10% at pre-war revenue levels; at EUR 160M annualized run rate margins positive at 4-5%
items.quote: the steady-state margin and if we start replicating the revenue numbers that we were doing pre -war situation is in the 8% to 10% range at an operating margin level

items.statement: FY26 capex planned ~Rs.200 crore, 40% in Pipes, 20% Parador, 20% Walls, 20% Roofs and Construction Chemicals
items.quote: So not factoring in any inorganic or any major new plant that we may get on to. But given the plans that we have, it's in the zone of a bout Rs.200 crore for this year

items.statement: Working capital efficiency programs yielding visible gains, reduced working capital marginally despite 7% revenue growth
items.quote: Our working capital efficiency programs are yielding visible gains, which has helped us to reduce our working capital marginally despite 7% growth in revenue at consolidated level.

items.statement: Pipes B2C/B2B/B2G mix FY25: 75%/15%/10%; forward mix target 70% B2C, 30% B2B+B2G
items.quote: If I look back at FY'25 aggregate portfolio of Pipes, about 75% B2C, 15% B2B, and 10% B2G. As we look ahead, I think the mix of 70% on B2C side and 30% on B2B plus B2G is how it should pan out as we go forward.

items.statement: PVC resin prices at near decadal levels end March; antidumping duty not yet introduced, BIS standards for CPVC imports expected around June
items.quote: Contrary to what you are describing, the antidumping duty for our relevant grades has still not been introduced. So, there is an industry-wide expectation that that should happen. When it happens, I think it's anybody's guess, but hopefully in the near term.

items.statement: Construction Chemicals crossed Rs.100 crore per annum run rate in March, revenue grew 23% in FY25
items.quote: Important milestone crossed here. At a March run rate level, we crossed the Rs.100 crore per annum mark for this business, which is significant given that this business was started less than 2 years ago.

items.statement: Roofing price drop 1.5-2% in FY25; demand sentiment largely flat
items.quote: So there has been a drop of about 1.5% to 2%.

items.statement: Capacity utilization: Roofing ~85%, Walls ~80-90% (down to ~80% with new plant), Pipes ~70%, Crestia ~20-25%, Parador ~55-60%
items.quote: In terms of Pipes business, our utilization is in the range of 70%, whereas in case of Crestia, it is in the range of 20% to 25%.

items.statement: New CHRO, CIO, CBO for Walls business in India; dedicated leadership for CC and Putty; Parador onboarded new CHRO and CFO
items.quote: For BirlaNu, we recently welcomed our new CHRO, CIO and CBO for our Walls business in India and created dedicated leadership for our CC and Putty business. For Parador, we onboarded our new CHRO and CFO.

items.statement: Crestia acquisition integrated successfully, grew Topline brand in retail segment
items.quote: In this segment, apart from numbers, the successful acquisition and integration of Crestia was a key achievement. With that, we have grown the Topline brand in the retail segment.

items.statement: Parador expanding into US, India, China, Middle East; US most aggressive effort with team and channel partners in place
items.quote: U.S. will probably be the most aggressive as far as our efforts are concerned. As we speak, we have got our first team members in place. We have our channel partners in place.

items.statement: Parador commercial channel share 12-14% in FY25 (growing), non-Central Europe sales 18-20%
items.quote: So commercial will still be about, if I'm not wrong, in the 12% to 14% range and growing because the same number last year was lower. Non-Central European sales will be in the zone of about 18% to 20%.

items.statement: Cautious on FY26 due to prevailing macroeconomic, tariff and geopolitical uncertainties across India, Europe and global markets
items.quote: As we enter FY26, w e remain cautious of the prevailing macroeconomic tariff and geopolitical uncertainties across India, Europe and the global markets

items.statement: Resist giving clear FY26 revenue/EBITDA guidance; focus on volume growth, market share growth, profitability improvement
items.quote: would resist giving a very clear guidance. At the same time, we are conscious we need to do significantly better on the growth rates and BIRLANU LTD’S Q4FY25 EARNINGS CALL TRANSCRIPT on the profitability in this financial

items.statement: Internal IRR benchmark 18-20%, payback 3-4 years for capital deployment in new product lines
items.quote: We normally monitor payback of 3 to 4 years and IRR is in the range of around 18% to 20%.

items.statement: Mid-single digit consolidated revenue growth guided for FY26
items.quote: We are looking for mid single digit level growth this year given the industry headwinds and the uncertainties of the climatic situation.

items.statement: Consolidated EBITDA margin guided around 25% for FY26
items.quote: We would be looking at in the range of around 25%.

items.statement: Effective tax rate guided at 22-23% for next 2-3 years
items.quote: We expect ETR to be in the range of 22% - 23% for the next 2-3 years.

items.statement: Capex guided at Rs 800-900 crore for FY26
items.quote: FY25-26 CAPEX should be in the range of around Rs. 800 - Rs. 900 crore

items.statement: Gross margin guided at 50-52% for FY26
items.quote: Yes, this will remain around 50% - 52% depending on the final product mix that we are able to achieve.

items.statement: Trade working capital days guided at 65-70 days for FY26
items.quote: For the next year, you may consider the range, what we have, so we are at around 73 odd days, the same could be taken around 65-70 days.

items.statement: Order book estimated at $1.3 billion plus as of Q4 FY25
items.quote: Est around 1.3 billion USD plus, but we don't have exact number in front.

items.statement: Two multi-product plants under construction; one to commission in FY26, next by March FY27
items.quote: As we had said in the past, we are doing our CAPEX with two multi -products plants which are under construction. We expect to commission one this year, maybe the next in the beginning of March next year.

items.statement: Capex split: ~Rs 100 crore for PI Health Sciences pharma, balance for Ag-Chem manufacturing
items.quote: So broadly in the Rs. 800 - Rs. 900, when you look at it to around Rs. 100 crore would be in the PI HS, the pharma business and the balance will be in the manufacturing in the Ag-Chem business.

items.statement: Domestic branded revenue grew 21% YoY in Q4 FY25 driven by strong rabi season
items.quote: Our domestic branded revenue grew by 21% YoY supported by a strong rabi season, marked by increased acreages in wheat, rice and pulses.

items.statement: Domestic business guided at 15-20% growth, 2x industry average
items.quote: we are looking at a 15%-20% growth which is 2x of the industry average growth.

items.statement: Consolidated EBITDA margin 27.4% for FY25; standalone EBITDA grew 17%
items.quote: On a consolidated basis, the EBITDA grew by 8% for the full year to 27.4%. On a standalone basis, EBITDA grew by 17%

items.statement: Pharma business EBITDA loss of Rs 180-190 crore in FY25; breakeven not expected in FY26
items.quote: EBITDA loss for the full year for pharma business has been in the range of around Rs. 180 - Rs. 190 crore.

items.statement: Pharma business built with 60-65% gross margins; operating leverage to improve profitability with scale
items.quote: Going forward, what I can say at this point in time, the business is built with gross margins of around 60%-65%. And with the scale up of the revenue, the operating leverage will start kicking in

items.statement: New products contribute 15-18% of Ag-Chem exports; biologicals 18-20% of domestic agri-brands
items.quote: When we are talking about new product launches and their contribution to our Ag-Chem export business is around 15% to 18%. And similarly, the biologicals business to our Ag-Chem brands business accounts for around 18% to 20%.

items.statement: Biologicals revenue currently ~Rs 250 crore; targeting 5x to Rs 1,000-1,200 crore in 5 years
items.quote: today we are at something around Rs. 250 crore right now. This would probably move up to 5x, it will be Rs. 1,000 to Rs. 1,200 crore in the next 5 years.

items.statement: 15 molecules commercialised over past 3 years; ~50% of new enquiries non-agchem
items.quote: Over the past 3 years alone we have commercialised over 15 molecules. Our pipeline remains robust, with approximately 50% of new enquiries being non-agricultural chemical molecules.

items.statement: Pharma CRDMO onboarded 2 new big pharma customers; targeting 2-3 more in FY26
items.quote: We also have on-boarded 2 new big pharma customers and the goal in FY26 is to add another 2 or 3, so that we can have a sound base of big pharma that gives consistent revenue

items.statement: Price softening in existing Ag-Chem exports due to input cost reductions passed through
items.quote: Yes, there is obviously some price softening and that is on the basis of input cost softening. So over last 1 to 1.5 year, post COVID, input prices have come down and given our business model of CSM Exports, where these input cost improvements are also passed through

items.statement: Trade working capital increased to 73 days; inventory days reduced from 62 to 45 days in FY25
items.quote: The Trade working capital in terms of Days of Sales has increased to 73 days while better inventory management has led to reduction in inventory day from 62 days to 45 days.

items.statement: Net cash balance of Rs 40,926 million; net worth increased to Rs 101,570 million
items.quote: Our balance sheet further strengthened during the year. Our Networth increased to Rs. 101,570 million and healthy net cash balance of Rs. 40,926 million.

items.statement: Plant Health Care acquisition adds peptide specialization for global biologicals platform
items.quote: Our acquisition of Plant Health Care having specialization in Peptides marks a significant step with an intent to becoming a platform technology-based biologicals product solutions and biologicals company to serve the global markets.

items.statement: Asset turnover sustainable at 2.2x-2.5x
items.quote: Yes. anything between 2.2x - 2.5x is what we will consider a sustainable number of asset turn.

items.statement: Export growth challenged by global headwinds; recovery expected from H2 FY26 with new product launches
items.quote: we believe that from H2, the export business would start picking up well with the launch of our new products and the growth in those areas.

items.statement: NCE PIOXANILIPROLE in Phase 3 trials; commercialization expected in first country in next couple of years
items.quote: We expect to commercialize in the very first country in the next couple of years.

items.statement: Expect 30-40% revenue increase and 80-90% EBITDA improvement from existing complex over 3-4 years; EBITDA could reach 3x FY25 with new Madhapur hotel
items.quote: From the existing complex that we are currently operating, we expect a 30% to 40% increase in revenue as we see the renovation being completed, which could lead to almost an 80% to 90% improvement in the EBITDA. Having said that, we also, in the same 3-4 year timeline, we are looking at opening our next hotel, which is in Madhapur, which is a 200-key inventory, in which case we can see our EBITDA

items.statement: Expect EBITDA margin to breach and sustain above 30% post-renovation; new Madhapur hotel to drive margins higher
items.quote: Particularly with the renovation in mind, we've managed now to get closer to the 30% mark. And in fact, once the renovation is completed and our ADRs further improve, we only see this EBITDA margin, breaching that 30% mark. And I think that from that standpoint, from that point on, we probably maintain that 30% above EBITDA margin.

items.statement: Plan INR120 crore capex over 2-3 years for Marriott upgrades, convention center expansion, Courtyard completion, lobby and F&B renovations
items.quote: The first, we expect a capex renovation of about INR120 crores over the next two to three years. This is mainly for the upgradation of Marriott, which is a 295 room hotel. The upgradation of the convention center, which is about 10,000 square feet, which will be converted to a 20,000 square feet convention center.

items.statement: Plan QIP to raise INR100-120 crore for Madhapur hotel project; prefer minimal debt on books
items.quote: we are looking at another QIP exercise which would raise another INR100 crores to INR120 crores into the company. So, what we plan and what the management thinks is that, preferably we'd have as less debt as possible on the books of the company

Phase 2 will consist of the upgradation of 168 rooms of Marriott and Convention Center in Marriott to 20,000 square feet from present 10,000 square feet.

The proposed property spans approximately 7,000 square yards and is expected to feature around 200 rooms.

items.statement: Hyderabad RevPAR growth led top cities in 2024 vs 2023; driven by business travel recovery, MICE activity, leisure demand, GCC growth, and constrained new supply
items.quote: Hyderabad has emerged as one of the top performing cities in terms of revenue per occupied room growth in 2024 compared to 2023. The city has gained strong momentum driven by the recovery of business travel, increased corporate and social MICE activity, and a rise in leisure demand.

items.statement: FY25: Marriott ADR INR6,864 (+1.66% YoY), occupancy 69.4%, RevPAR INR4,765 (+13.5% YoY); Courtyard ADR INR6,758 (+2.15% YoY), occupancy 72.6%, RevPAR INR4,908 (-6.29% YoY due to renovation); Combined occupancy 70.3% (+350bps YoY), RevPAR IN

The combined occupancy rate of the entire complex stood at 70.3%, compared to 66.8% in the previous year.

items.statement: Current debt INR50 crore; may add INR50 crore over 3-4 years; target net debt/EBITDA ~1x at INR100 crore EBITDA with 3 hotels operational
items.quote: So, the debt level which is currently on the books of the company is about INR50 crores. So, we possibly maybe have to add another INR50 crores of debt over the next 3 years, 4 years. And we expect once the renovation to be completed and all three projects, all three properties are operational, to have EBITDA close to INR100 crores. So, that's possibly putting the ratio at about 1 is to 1.

items.statement: Completed rights issue raising INR49.52 crore; planning QIP of INR100-120 crore for Madhapur project
items.value: INR49.52 cr raised, INR100-120 cr planned

items.quote: Mr. Venkata Krishna Reddy has taken over as our new Chief Financial Officer, while Mr. Pradyumna Kodali has assumed the role of Chief Operating Officer. items.statement: Actively evaluating brownfield, half-built, distressed hotel assets and commercial-to-hotel conversions in Tier 1 cities (Bangalore, Goa, Pune, Chandigarh) and high-tourism destinations; no concrete deals yet
items.quote: We are looking for these opportunities on a very continuous and serious basis. And we analyzed several already half-built properties or brownfield projects which are almost in the completion stage. And we try to see that if we can take them over, or also some distressed assets which could form a part of our portfolio easily.

items.statement: All resolution plan payments discharged ahead of 3-year timeline; NCLAT approval completed October 2023
items.quote: Our management team officially took charge in October 2023 following the final approval of the resolution plan by the National Company Law Appellate Tribunal. items.statement: Expect significant ADR growth post-renovation flowing through to EBITDA; operational efficiencies and back-of-house upgrades drove 59% YoY EBITDA growth in Q4 despite only 5% revenue growth
items.quote: And continuing going forward, along with the renovation, we also expect our ADRs to significantly grow up, a major part of it which flows through straight to our profit, wherein you will see a larger rise in the EBITDA than you see in the revenue.

items.statement: Capex payback expected within 2-2.5 years per HVS Anarock study; management confident in ROI
items.quote: based on the reports that we've received and EBITDAs that we expect to have once the renovation is entirely completed, this amount that we are infusing as capex is possibly going to be returned within two to two and a half years.

items.statement: Revenue guidance of ~Rs 925-930 crore for FY26 (15% growth) with potential to reach Rs 1,000 crore annual run rate by Q3/Q4
items.quote: I think the guidance what we had given is a 15% increase in revenues should be around Rs. 925 crores, Rs. 930 crores for this year.

items.statement: EBITDA margin guidance maintained at 18-20% for FY26
items.quote: Yes. We stand to maintain 18% to 20% our margin guidance, we stick to that.

items.quote: We have earmarked a CAPEX of Rs. 7 crores to Rs. 10 crores for expanding our Stainless-Steel capacity with additional 70,000 units. With this expansion, we are increasing the total capacity to 250,000 units. We expect the new capacity to be operational as early as Q3 FY '26.

items.statement: Karran/Lowe's deal adds 150k quartz sinks annually across 1,800+ US stores starting this summer
items.quote: As informed earlier through a press release, a key highlight for Q4 '25 had been a significant deal with a US major retail chain through our customer KARRAN, which is going to add additional capacity and supply of 150,000 quartz sinks across spread 1800 plus stores across United States.

items.quote: Howdens was the largest kitchen manufactured in the UK, which we had signed the deal last year, so we are exclusive to Howdens. It's a very strong business, about 80,000 to100,000 sinks a year just for Howdens, and they are still going very strong.

items.statement: Strong export tailwinds from US tariffs on China/Vietnam, FTA with UK, EU FTA progressing; demand across UK, Europe, India, Southeast Asia, Israel
items.quote: Overall, we see a strong momentum in exports in not just but UK, Europe, India, Southeast countries, including Israel, which are showing significant amount of growth.

items.statement: Q4 FY25 EBITDA margin 17.5% (up from ~16% YoY); FY25 margin 17.3% impacted by high MMA prices, freight, manpower, marketing spend
items.quote: EBITDA for Q4 FY'25 stood at Rs. 35.8 crores with a margin of 17.5%.

items.statement: MMA prices and freight costs have cooled down; Q4 margins improved significantly vs prior quarters
items.quote: Yes, both these prices have cooled down, the freight charges as well as our material prices, especially the MMA price are very high, as our CFO said. So it's already cooled down at this point of time. So that's why you would have seen our margins for Q4 have improved quite significantly than previous quarters.

items.statement: US deals (Lowe's, IKEA) bring higher value-added products, improving per-unit realization from Q1 FY26
items.quote: For example, a single bowl will cost much less. Now since the US, which is a high value-added product which is going to now have, with the new crack down deal with the US major, this will increase the per piece realization, and I think which you will see from the Q1 results.

items.statement: First kitchen/bathroom countertop fabrication facility in Delhi within 150-180 days (end of Q3), launching Cary Stone surface brand for seamless sink-countertop integration
items.quote: Surfaces and countertops, so we have a timeline, we should be achieving within 150 to 180 days. Reet Ranawat: Okay, got it. Thank you so much. Chirag Parekh: So it will happen approximately by end of Q3, latest, this year

items.statement: Domestic dealer network expanded from 1,500 to 4,000; targeting 140 to 200 galleries by end of FY26; 80% B2C, 20-25% B2C in domestic market
items.quote: We have significantly expanded our dealer network from 1,500 to 4,000. Like I said, we are going to thrust a lot of building new galleries which we plan to achieve from 140 to 200 galleries by end of this fiscal year.

items.statement: UAE subsidiary: 80% appliances/20% sinks revenue mix; Emaar developer win; second showroom in Sharjah opening July; UAE revenue Rs 14.4 crore FY25
items.quote: Our ratio is reversed now, with the sales of 80% Appliances at 20% sinks in UAE, with the riding success with the first Dubai showroom, we are now opening a second showroom in Sharjah of 3,000 square feet on the main Sheikh Zayed Road to add better value and range of Appliances and sinks.

items.statement: UK subsidiary: revenue grew GBP 9M to 12M; emerging as top 3 kitchen category player; 12-14 new customers added; ceramic sinks, new faucets launched
items.quote: As far as the UK is concerned, we are immensely focusing on new products. We have launched ceramic sinks, we have launched new kind of Faucets, we have introduced new kind of sinks, we have additional about 12 to 14 new customers onboard.

items.statement: US subsidiary United Granite: turned from -8-10% to ~2-3% EBITDA by shifting to high-value exotic marbles/quartz; targeting profitability in FY26
items.quote: We have started cutting the marbles and quartz of very high and unique exotic marbles and quarts, which is leading to higher profit margins. So which, we were about negative 8% to 10%, and we have now crossed the breakeven, I think we are at about 2% or 3% profit now.

items.statement: Working capital days at 87 (up from strategic inventory build for BIS compliance and in-house manufacturing); expected to normalize in coming quarters
items.quote: Working capital days stood at 87 days based on the sales. Our working capital days for March '25 increased primarily due to strategic decision to increase the level of imported inventory of our finished goods, primarily owing to BIS standard implementation from March 2025.

items.statement: Inventory build-up temporary; working capital days expected to decrease as BIS inventory consumed and operating cycle normalizes
items.quote: Yes. So we are working because there are some one-time inventory stock we have built up for our future demand because of the BIS issues. But that will get consumed. items.statement: Gross debt Rs 265.5 crore (Mar 2025); debt-to-equity <0.5; cash balance Rs 68 crore including FD earmarked for capex

items.statement: BIS standards implemented March 2025 driving inventory build; investing in next-gen technology for global quality compliance
items.quote: With BIS restrictions, we have no choice but to invest in the next generation technology to meet the global quality standard to enhance our competitive edge.

items.statement: US tariffs (10% baseline) create tailwind; no reciprocal duty on sinks; exports ~30% to US, 30% of export revenue
items.quote: So I think that now everybody is getting 10% duty attraction to anything imported into the US. But we do not see any significant increase in the tariffs as there is no reciprocal duty on sinks.

items.statement: Quartz sink volume 645k units (12% 3-yr CAGR); Stainless steel sink 155k units (20% 3-yr CAGR); Appliances 63.2k units FY25
items.quote: Sales volume for quartz sink stood at 6,45,000 units, Stainless-Steel Sink stood at 1,55,000 units, kitchen Appliances and others stood at 63,200 units in FY'25.

items.statement: Stainless steel sink inquiries rising from US/Europe due to China/Vietnam tariffs; PVD machines invested; supplies started to Kohler India, Hafele, IKEA
items.quote: Thanks to the tariff for that we have started receiving overwhelming response now for Stainless-Steel Sinks also since there's a big tariff on China and Vietnam. We have always maintained high technology. We have invested in PVD new machines, and we have made some significant breakthrough with Kohler India and Hafele to start selling them Stainless-Steel kitchen sinks.

items.statement: Tariff uncertainty remains ('sword hanging'); demand sustainability unclear; capacity ramp execution risk in 90 days
items.quote: It's very, very hard to predict how the markets are reacting at this point. You still have this tariff sword hanging up. But right now all looks good, but we will have more clarity in the coming quarters how it looks.

items.statement: Revenue target of Rs 3,000 crore for FY26, implying ~17% growth; confident of sustaining 17-18% corporate growth for next 3 years
items.quote: Yes, very much, Bino , because we have done Rs. 2,600 crores. So we are very optimistic that we are very much on track for the Rs. 3,000 crores.

items.statement: US business targeting $300 million order book within 2 years from current $220 million
items.quote: But we are optimistic that we would basically look at a $300 million order book status within the next 2 years.

items.statement: R&D spend expected to remain 1.9-2% of revenue annually
items.quote: Moving on, we do expect the R&D expenditure to remain between, say, 1.9% to 2% on a year-on-year basis.

items.statement: Domestic formulation business grew 8.5% in FY25 excluding Warren Remedies impact, at par or better than industry
items.quote: If you look at the consolidated picture of India business performance, you will see that we have grown at more than 8.5%, which is at par or even better than the industry growth.

items.statement: OTC toothpaste brands showing 18-19% value growth at tertiary level per Nielsen
items.quote: As per Nielsen at tertiary level, our brand is growing at 18%, 19% in value.

items.statement: New products contribute 4.5% to domestic growth vs industry average of 2.5%
items.quote: Today, at IRL, our contribution of new products to total growth is in excess of 4.5%, which is way higher than the industry average of 2.5%.

items.statement: Solid oral US revenue grew from INR52 crores to INR81 crores in FY25 while sterile revenue dropped from INR200 crores to INR42 crores
items.quote: Whereas oral solids, which were only INR52 crores last year are at INR81 crores now.

items.statement: US FDA allowed restart of a couple of lines at Plant II Goa; incremental sales expected from Q2 FY26
items.quote: As recently as about 24 hours ago, we have also received some positive communication from U.S. FDA, which allows us to restart a couple of our lines in Plant II.

items.statement: EMA inspection of Plant II Goa successful with no critical or major observations
items.quote: Plant II in Goa, our sterile facility, which is under warning letter, was earlier inspected by EMA or the European Medicine Agency, and t he audit has gone very successfully. We have no criticals, no majors and a few minors

items.statement: US FDA remediation updates to be completed by July-August 2025, site ready for inspection after August
items.quote: last updates, most of the updates on the remediation would be completed by July or August this year. So I think as a site, we have to be ready any time after that

items.statement: Consolidated peak debt at INR960 crores (Indoco: INR400 cr long-term + INR211 cr short-term; Warren: INR330 cr long-term + INR20 cr short-term)
items.quote: So all put together, close to about -- debt level is about INR960 crores.

items.statement: Debt repayment to be organic from cash accruals; borrowing costs 8.5-8.75% currently
items.quote: From our cash accruals, we'll repay the loans. And you will be surprised that even today, our loans are in the range of 8.5% to 8.75%.

items.statement: Warren Remedies channel transition from ethical to OTC caused temporary supply chain disruption, now settled
items.quote: The setback we got this year has largely got to do with the channel change. Earlier in the ethical business, we were -- we had the system where a carry and forward agent would carry our product and the primary sale happened directly to the stockist. Here, we have super distributors who then sell out.

items.statement: Remediation costs at Plant II running at INR4 crores per quarter, continuing until December 2025
items.quote: So we spent close to INR4 crores per quarter on remediation expenses. And this has happened for all 4 quarters this year.

items.statement: Brinzolamide US market size ~$65 million with 3 players; Dorzolamide market shrunk with many players
items.quote: Brinzolamide, the market right now is about $65 million. There are about three players in the market. So that is about brinzolamide. Dorzolamide has many players, and the market has shrunk considerably.

items.statement: Rating agency downgraded credit rating; management expects upgrade once performance normalizes as in 2016-2018 cycle
items.quote: This is a limited period phenomenon, which we have to face. And as soon as we are out of it, they will come down and upgrade us once again.

items.statement: R&D spend maintained at ~5% of sales; being selective on new projects given current challenges
items.quote: We are not planning to increase or decrease, but we are maintaining it at 5%. Even on a lower top line this year, in absolute terms, it has come down because we are now being a little bit more picky about the products we take up.

items.statement: Print EBITDA margin expanded ~400 bps YoY in FY25 due to softer newsprint prices and advertising yield improvement
items.quote: With a margin expansion, also, of ~400 basis points.

items.statement: Print segment EBITDA grew 67% YoY to INR 121 cr in FY25 driven by newsprint savings and ad yield improvement
items.quote: quarter ended with EBITDA of INR 61 cr and on a full year basis, it was INR 121 cr, which is a growth of 67%.

items.statement: Print ad revenues flat to marginally declining in Q4 and FY25; Hindi print ad revenue declined 5% QoQ and 4% YoY
items.quote: ad revenues are flat to marginally declining across the quarter and year.

items.statement: Hindi print circulation revenue declined 7% QoQ and 9% YoY in FY25
items.quote: On circulation revenue, you see 7% decline on a quarterly basis and a 9% decline on an annual basis.

items.statement: English print circulation revenue declined 27% QoQ and 14% YoY in FY25
items.quote: In circulation revenue, there's a decline of 27% for the quarter, and, on a full year basis, it's a decline of 14%.

items.statement: Radio revenue grew 72% QoQ to INR 82 cr and 30% YoY to INR 204 cr in FY25 driven by on-ground events
items.quote: On the top line, you can see the quarterly numbers grew 72% to INR 82 cr, and on a full year basis to INR 204 cr, which is an increase of 30%.

items.statement: Radio margins remain under pressure due to higher cost structure of scaled on-ground events
items.quote: when we go into the non-FCT streams of revenue, there is bound to be a related cost also associated with it.

items.statement: Digital revenue grew 35% QoQ to INR 58 cr and 38% YoY to INR 212 cr in FY25 led by OTTplay and Shine
items.quote: On a quarterly basis, revenue grew 35% to INR 58 cr, and on a full year basis to INR 212 cr, which is an increase of 38%.

items.statement: Digital segment losses reduced from INR 114 cr to INR 102 cr in FY25 while revenue scaled from INR 154 cr to INR 212 cr
items.quote: From INR 154 cr of revenue last year, Digital revenues have grown to INR 212 cr, while the losses we have reduced from INR 114 cr to INR 102 cr.

items.statement: Management expects OTTplay to reach break-even by end of FY26 but may invest more if scaling faster
items.quote: hopefully by the end of this year, we should be in a break-even situation. But it depends, if we scale fast enough, we may invest more on the business as well.

items.statement: No specific revenue or earnings guidance provided; annual plan is a growth plan
items.quote: In line with our usual practice, we would not be sharing specific guidance on revenue or on earnings projections.

items.statement: Newsprint price decline drove significant margin expansion in Print segment
items.quote: most of the margin expansion is attributed to the savings in newsprint that's come through.

items.statement: Advertising yield improvement contributed to Print margins despite weak volume growth
items.quote: basis a mix of categories and absolute price increases there has been an overall yield improvement in advertising revenue despite growth not being that strong and therefore that has also contributed to the margins.

items.statement: Employee cost decreased QoQ from INR 114 cr to INR 108 cr due to rationalization and Q3 festive incentives not recurring
items.quote: In some businesses we've had some rationalization, so therefore that accounts for part of the difference and yes there could be some reversals, in the quarter.

items.statement: HMVL ad-for-equity investment portfolio on fully diluted basis north of INR 1,000 cr; substantial part on HMVL balance sheet
items.quote: on a fully diluted basis our investment position will be, north of INR 1000 cr.

items.statement: HMVL investment in electric mobility company is ad-for-equity, no cash deployed
items.quote: it is not a cash investment, it is an AFE investment, so there is no cash being deployed for that investment.

items.statement: Other income includes substantial treasury gains from favourable yield movements and profit on sale of AFE investments
items.quote: We've had a substantial gain in treasury given that there's been favourable yield movement in line of rate actions as well as anticipated actions in the market.

items.statement: Radio peers ENIL and DB have non-metro advantage growing faster than HT's metro-focused portfolio
items.quote: both of them have the advantage of being in non-metro, which is actually growing faster than metro while we are a metro player.

items.statement: Consolidated revenue grew 7% YoY to positive PAT of INR 20 cr in FY25; EBITDA grew 58%
items.quote: On a full year basis, the revenue growth was 7%, and PAT came to a positive number at INR 20 cr, which is a substantial increase. And EBITDA grew by 58%.

items.statement: Net cash position robust with cash in excess of INR 1,000 cr as of March 31, 2025
items.quote: If you see the net cash position, we have as of 31st March, cash in excess of INR 1,000 cr on the books.

items.statement: Employee cost rationalization undertaken in some businesses during Q4 FY25
items.quote: In some businesses we've had some rationalization, so therefore that accounts for part of the difference

items.quote: Unless the regulatory changes come in, there'll be some level of pressure on margins because that platform has not seen revenues come back, post-Covid to the extent say Print has or Digital has, etc.

items.quote: investments in future looking businesses that will create long-term sustainable value for all shareholders is something that we are at, and we will strive to do our best.

items.quote: The f ull-year revenue for ProConnect consolidated is about Rs. 957 crores . That is at a consolidated level. It continues to have an operating margin of about between 10% to 12%. And the profit after tax has been very good the current year, close to Rs. 30 crores.

items.quote: Maybe we have gone slightly overboard in terms of OPEX control. We are very conscious .
