items.quote: But I do believe in the next 2, 3 years, these numbers will rationalize and will add maybe 2%, 3%, 4% I would say 2% to 3% would be added to our EBITDA with the rationalization of these numbers over the next 2, 3 years.

items.statement: Opalware capacity utilization ~90%; peak revenue on current capacity ~INR430-440 crore at 100% utilization
items.quote: As far as opal utilization is concerned, we're at about 90% utilization.

items.statement: Borosilicate pressware plant capital employed ~INR200 crore; full utilization should deliver >24% ROCE
items.quote: On the capital employed altogether, it's roughly INR200 crores on the borosilicate front on the pressware, which includes the capex as well as probably some working capital that we have.

items.statement: Major risk of running out of Hydra inventory without sufficient local sourcing; INR150+ crore inventory at sale value may not cover full year
items.quote: We have a major risk for running out of inventory in Hydra without having sufficient local sourcing available to supply. And that's a risk to our revenue and to our margins, absolutely.

items.statement: Hydra inventory may last until Diwali; working with Indian suppliers to debottleneck; revenue loss possible in H2 FY26
items.quote: I think we'll have enough to pass Diwali.

items.statement: No material price cuts in borosilicate pressware despite capacity addition; price action within single-digit percentages if any
items.quote: If any price action, it would be within single -digit percentages, 5% minus maybe.

items.statement: Plan A: reach full borosilicate utilization without price cuts; Plan B: may drop prices in exports/other areas to utilize capacity
items.quote: Obviously, we would prefer that we go to the full utilization without price, and that's the plan A. But obviously, as a company, we have to look at plan B also. So plan B, we have taken that we again, we will may have to drop some prices in some maybe in exports or in some other areas to utilize the entire capacity.

items.statement: Higher discounting observed in Opalware market; launching premium Larah Premia at higher prices to differentiate
items.quote: As far as discounting, of course, we do keep tabs on because that impacts our pricing. And as far as that is concerned, we have seen some higher discounting

items.statement: B2B pharma sales down ~INR30 crore in Opalware due to UCPMP 2024; pivoted to e-commerce and quick commerce
items.quote: Look, we lost about INR30 crores this year on B2B in opal. So that was a big setback for us.

items.statement: BIS/QCO implementation on vacuum flasks (Hydra) and appliances caused inventory buildup; two consecutive years of regulatory challenges
items.quote: So last year, it was the BIS on the vacuum flask, which is our Hydra range. And this year, now we've got BIS on appliances. So we had two consecutive years with two separate product categories, which are being imported, which have these BIS notifications.

items.statement: Certified Great Place to Work; ESOP 2020 scheme with fresh stock options approved November 2024
items.quote: We're also thrilled to inform you that on the HR front, Borosil Limited has been officially certified great place to work.

items.statement: Operating ROCE 11.5% in FY25 vs 15.1% in FY24; dip due to front-loaded capex in borosilicate and opal capacity not at full utilization
items.quote: During FY '25, the company earned an operating profit, again, excluding exceptional and onetime items and income from investments of INR96.7 crores, and this translates into an operating ROCE of 11.5%. ROCE moderated to 11.5% in FY '25 from 15.1% last year.

items.statement: Enabling resolution for INR250 crore fundraise passed; no plans to raise money in FY26 unless dramatic change
items.quote: See, it's an enabling resolution, we take it every year, because in the past, we had an issue, when we had to raise money, then we couldn't raise because we then had to go for an EGM. So it's an enabling resolution. We are not at the moment planning to raise any money.

items.statement: FY26 consolidated milk procurement target of 20 lakh litres per day (18 lakh India + Africa), up from 17.1 lakh in FY25
items.quote: And in '25-'26 we are already targeting 18 lakhs average, so that only is in India, and including Africa it is 20 lakhs.

items.statement: FY26 Orgafeed revenue target of Rs 200 crore, up from Rs 132 crore in FY25
items.quote: So this year we are expecting, see the last '24-'25 we have done Rs. 132 crores, now this year almost we are expecting Rs. 200 crores.

items.statement: Africa business expected to grow at 15-16% in FY26 after 71% growth in FY25
items.quote: Africa will not show this significant a move as we have seen this year of the growth rates being almost 60% , 70%, because I think the Kenya acquisition that came in, we played out well and it has taken a significant year. But this should also main tain in line with our 15% , 16% growth rates is what we are considering even for the Africa

items.statement: Maharashtra greenfield project with Rs 280 crore outlay, expected completion by end of FY27, adding 10 lakh litres per day processing capacity
items.quote: We have started work towards expansion in Maharashtra , it is a greenfield project with a total outlay of Rs. 280 crores on the standalone project itself. Investment in this is through a combination of debt and internal accruals. The plant is expected to be ready by the end of the Financial Year '27, thereby increasing our processing capacity by 10 lakh liters per day.

items.statement: FY25 revenue grew 19% YoY to Rs 3,720 crore; PAT grew 55.9% to Rs 260 crore
items.value: Rs 3,720 crore revenue, Rs 260 crore PAT
items.quote: For the full year FY '25 revenue grew by 19% year -over-year and stood at Rs. 3,720 crores and we closed the year with a PAT of Rs. 260 crores.

items.statement: FY25 EBITDA margin improved 100 bps; Q4 EBITDA margin 9.2%; stable margins maintained through net SMP/butter selling strategy
items.quote: In FY '25 our margins were pretty much stable , as Mr. Sunil Reddy rightly mentioned that we were able to minimize the fluctuations resulting from seasonality trend in the business. We were able to achieve this stability by improving our procurement strength and eventually becoming the net sellers.

items.statement: SMP prices currently Rs 255-260/kg; bulk butter sold at Rs 430-435/kg in Q4
items.quote: SMP, this 4th Quarter we have sold roughly about Rs. 250. And butter we have sold bulk butter around Rs. 430, Rs. 435. So, now SMP is around Rs. 255- Rs. 260 range.

items.statement: Africa revenue crossed Rs 100 crore for first time, up 71% YoY; Kenya acquisition added 60,000 litres/day
items.quote: Speaking of international business, we have delivered outstanding results in Kenya and Uganda with a revenue growth of 71% year -on-year basis crossing the mark of Rs. 100 crores for the first time since we entered this geography.

items.statement: Operating cash flow Rs 520 crore in FY25; cash and equivalents Rs 746 crore as of March 31, 2025; inventory Rs 160 crore (Rs 100 crore finished goods)
items.value: Rs 520 crore OCF, Rs 746 crore cash
items.quote: We see healthy cash flow from our operations which stood at Rs. 520 crores. Speaking of cash, our total cash and cash equivalents position as on 31 March, 2025, stands at Rs. 746 crores.

items.statement: Board approved dividend of Rs 2 per share (20% of face value) for FY25
items.quote: I am happy to share with you that the Board has approved dividend distribution of Rs. 2 per share, that is 20% of the face value.

items.statement: Employee cost to grow 5-6% YoY in FY26 in line with increments; expected to remain stable as percentage of revenue
items.quote: It will almost maintain our growth rate, so what we maintain I think for the overall 5% , 6% increase in the cost, that will always go on a year-on-year basis for what we give as increments.

items.statement: Early monsoon in South India softening milk procurement prices; one price reduction round taken, another expected soon
items.quote: Price is already softening and we have already taken one round of price reduction. And maybe we are expecting it will go for one more round also very soon.

items.statement: VAP demand surge seen end of Q4, expected to continue in Q1 FY26; curd volume grew 6.5% YoY in Q4
items.quote: We have also started witnessing an increase in VAP demand towards the end of the quarter. Our value-added product sale for the quarter contributed 32% of our total revenues and we expect this demand to continue in Q1 FY '26 to increase our VAP share.

items.statement: Orgafeed currently serves 30% of farmer base; targeting scale-up via Rs 200 crore revenue in FY26; bottleneck is supply and collection from farmers
items.quote: Currently we cater around 30% of our farmers with a capacity utilization still below 50%. Orgafeed is not only providing a strategic edge while maintaining a relationship with the farmers, but is also strongly positioned to deliver a faster growth in the coming years.

items.statement: Private sector milk prices 15-20% higher than cooperatives; gap of Rs 7-8/litre maintained in Tamil Nadu and Karnataka
items.quote: So the price difference between cooperatives and us is still there, but the significant 15%, 20% higher will be the private sector. Although they have taken a price increase, it's only been maybe they have taken a price increase of 5% , 6%, and we are still maintaining our higher prices and the gap still maintains.

items.statement: Other income includes Rs 9.5 crore provision reversal from favourable Telangana GST Commissioner Appeal and AP High Court order on flavoured milk classification
items.quote: Other income stood at Rs. 25.8 crores, this includes the provision reversal amount of Rs. 9.5 crores on the back of securing a favorable Telangana GST Commissioner Appeal , and also a AP High Court order with respect to flavored milk classification.

items.statement: Acquisition remains ongoing focus; past track record of successful acquisitions; actively looking at northern states for geographic expansion
items.quote: We constantly dabble between build-versus-buy thought process and hence the acquisition is an ongoing focus area for us. With a past track record of successful acquisitions, we are well -placed to expand our geographical presence.

items.statement: Ghee sales doubled from 2 to 4.5 tonnes/day in existing markets; targeting another doubling in FY26; profitability similar to consolidated EBITDA margin (9-10%)
items.quote: But I think we have almost doubled ou r consumer sales in the presence of markets that we were from almost saying that let's say it was 2 tonnes a day to 4.5 tonnes a day of sales in the markets. So the markets are now, we have not yet penetrated as deeply as we were earlier in the northern states. We are now again relaunching so it will take some time to get there. But in the states where we are

items.statement: FY26 HALS revenue target Rs 210 crore
items.quote: And for '26, we are expecting closer to Rs. 210 crores.

items.statement: FY26 HALS volume target 4,500 tons
items.quote: And going forward in FY ‘26, our target is to touch 4,500 tons of sales.

items.statement: FY26 consolidated EBITDA margin target around 40%
items.quote: So at company level, we are looking for 40% EBITDA margin, because it's not only HALS.

items.statement: FY26 consolidated operating profit growth 18-20%
items.quote: So, I mean, the operating profit growth rate could be in line with what we have recorded this year, which is in the range of 18% to 20%.

items.statement: FY26 CAPEX Rs 300 crore
items.quote: Rs. 300 crores overall. And for FY ‘26, Rs. 300 crores.

items.statement: HALS peak revenue Rs 565-570 crore at full capacity
items.quote: We are looking at about Rs. 565-70 odd crores.

items.statement: HALS realization target Rs 495-500 per kg at full utilization
items.quote: Say you can assume about Rs. 495, to Rs. 500.

items.statement: Performance Chemical 1 commercialization by Q3 FY26, Performance Chemical 2 by Q4 FY26
items.quote: Construction for the new performance chemical product, which is expected to commercialize by Q3 FY ‘26 is on track. CAPEX for performance chemical 2 has started and we expect the plant to commercialize by Q4 FY ‘26.

items.statement: HALS total capacity over 10,000 tons
items.quote: FY '28. So the total capacity is over 10,000 tons.

items.statement: MEHQ and BHA capacity utilization 70-72%
items.quote: We have about 70%-72% capacity utilization. So, we still have window there.

items.statement: Two new performance chemical plants each around 10,000-ton capacity
items.quote: See, both are around 10,000-ton capacities and closer to commercialization, I think, in the next con call, we will give a little bit more picture on the performance chemical products.

items.statement: MEHQ volume growth 4-5% YoY
items.quote: I think for MEHQ volumes it should be around 4% to 5% on a year-on-year basis.

items.statement: TBHQ and BHA growing at 4-5% industry rate
items.quote: Both are growing at 4%-5% industry norms.

items.statement: HALS blended realization ~Rs 425/kg, RMC ~65%
items.quote: For the quarter, HALS sales value is broadly in line with the last quarter and blended realization is approximately 425 per kg while the RMC at portfolio level is around ~65%.

items.statement: Q4 COGS increase due to pharma segment mix shift
items.quote: So, the reason is the product mix that has led to a higher RMC as a percentage of sales during this quarter. So, if you note, there has been a meaningful growth in pharma segment, where the margin contribution is lower than the performance segment.

items.statement: FY25 HALS volume ~1,900 tons, revenue ~Rs 80 crore
items.quote: For the full year FY ‘25, the HALS sales volume was roughly 1,900 ton, which gave us a sale of roughly Rs. 80 crores.

items.statement: Revenue mix: performance chemicals 69%, pharma/agro 19%, FMCG 12%
items.quote: The revenue contribution from performance segment, pharma and agro segment and FMCG segment remain at 69%, 19% and 12% respectively.

items.statement: New products: HALS series, DHDT pharma intermediate, BHT, two performance chemicals for FY26 commercialization
items.quote: These include the entire HAL S series, DHDT, which is a pharma intermediate and BHT, along with two new products in the performance chemical segment, which are slated for commercialization in FY '26.

items.statement: DHDT facing teething issues, commercial production in ~4 weeks
items.quote: We still are facing some teething issues. The product, the chemistry which was done in lab and pilot is behaving very differently on plant scale. Every day we are learning a lot of new things about it. So, probably, it will take at least four weeks more to set right the process before we get into commercial scales.

items.statement: Barbituric acid production starting August 2025
items.quote: We will start by August. Month of August.

items.statement: BHT already sold small quantities in US, volumes increasing
items.quote: We have already sold some quantities in the U.S., and you will see progressively the volumes are increasing over the next few quarters.

items.statement: HALS customer validations in Middle East, Southeast Asia, Europe
items.quote: Successful validation by key customers based in Middle East, South east Asia and Europe are lead indicators pointing to sales momentum acceleration going forward.

items.statement: Working capital increased due to HALS inventory build; expected to normalize by FY26 end
items.quote: Of course, what is happening is, we have started producing HALS on a larger scale. So, the stocks are higher, but the sales are comparatively lower because we need produce a minimum quantum

items.statement: Final dividend Rs 4/share, FY25 payout ratio 22%
items.quote: We are pleased to report that the Board has recommended final dividend of Rs. 4 per share. Total payout ratio is higher at 22% for FY ‘25 compared to the previous year.

items.statement: Cash balance Rs 400 crore despite higher payout and CAPEX
items.quote: Led by strong focus towards cash conversion, the cash balance continues to be meaningful at Rs. 400 crores despite increased payout ratio and sizable CAPEX in the new subsidiary.

items.statement: HALS Phase-2 expansion decision at 60-65% capacity utilization
items.quote: Once we start getting majority of approvals globally, once we start seeing decent ramp up, when we start seeing that okay we are seeing about 60%, 65% capacity utilization scenario, that is the time we should go for Phase-2.

items.statement: FY25 sales growth 17% (25% volume, -8% realization)
items.quote: So, around 25% was the volume impact and low er realization offsetted that impact by around 8%. So, that's how you see around 17% growth in the sales for full year FY

items.statement: Revenue potential Rs 2,500-3,000 crore at inflection point
items.quote: Rs. 2,500 crores to Rs. 3,000 crores is the revenue potential.

items.statement: FY26 revenue growth guided at 20-25% with EBITDA margins of 35-40%
items.quote: We anticipate a good ramp-up in order inflow in FY '26 and remain confident in achieving 25% to 30% -- or 20% to 25% revenue growth for FY '26 while maintain ing strong EBITDA margins at 35% to 40%.

items.statement: Order book at INR730 crore as of March 31, INR860 crore including negotiated contracts as on date
items.quote: As of March 31, our order book stands at INR730 crores and as on date, order book is at INR860 crores, including negotiated contracts.

items.statement: FY26 order inflow expected between INR1,000-2,000 crore
items.quote: Regarding FY' 26, some of the orders have got delayed, what we were supposed to get in FY '25, but we expect those contracts to happen. And maybe it's somewhere between INR1,000 crores and INR2,000 crores is what we expect during the course of this year to get orders.

items.statement: FY25 gross margin 61%, PAT margin 31%; Q4 gross margin 49% due to low-margin strategic contract
items.quote: Gross margin for the full year was 61% and PAT margin was 31%. PAT grew by 22% in line with our guidance.

items.statement: Sustainable EBITDA margin guided at 35-40%
items.quote: See that's what we have told 35% to 40% EBITDA margin, we will be able to sustain.

items.statement: Defence ministry focused on doubling orders and steady supply chain over next 4-5 years; company well placed to benefit
items.quote: The defence ministry focused on doubling orders and ensuring a steady supply chain over the next 4 -5 years. Data Patterns is well placed to benefit from the growing defence sector in India.

items.statement: Shift from component supplier to integrated systems supplier; developing full radars, EW suites, seekers, communication equipment
items.quote: We are shifting our focus to complete systems to grow our addressable market. Our goal is to become a leading system supplier, serving both India and other countries.

items.statement: INR150 crore capex planned over next 1-2 years for production, test and validation infrastructure
items.quote: We're also spending about INR150 crores in the next 1 to 2 years' time to create infrastructure to production , test and validate systems which we expect the contracts to happen in 2 to 3 years coming.

items.statement: INR140-150 crore spent on product development in last 1.5 years
items.quote: The major revenue stream we're expecting, where investments have happened, to the extent of INR140 crores to INR150 crores were spent in the last 1.5 years in product development.

items.statement: TAM for developed products estimated at INR20,000-30,000 crore over 5-6 years
items.quote: We expect that the size of oppor tunities or the TAM for all this probably vary between INR20,000 crores to INR30,000 crores.

items.statement: BrahMos seeker flight test successful; expect development and production orders from BrahMos
items.quote: We're happy to announce that the flight was carried about three to four weeks back. There's an excellent flight, textbook flight and textbook performance, we expect that in shortly, we should get more -- some more orders from BrahMo s for the development of additional units will be asked.

items.statement: Repeat orders from earlier deliveries expected to contribute over INR1,000 crore to order book
items.quote: I said repeat orders from what we've done earlier, which -- back-to-back orders which you've start getting should be a more of -- more than INR1,000 crores is what we are saying.

items.statement: Net working capital days increased to 468; expected to improve in 2-3 years as production mix increases
items.quote: I think given another 2 to 3 years' time and the development is lesser and the production is more, then the turnaround time will be faster, cash realization is faster, working capital days will come down.

items.statement: Board recommended dividend of INR7.9 per equity share of INR2 face value
items.quote: We are happy to inform you that our Board has recommend ed a dividend of INR7.9 per equity share of INR2 each, which is subject to approval of the shareholders.

items.statement: Workforce of nearly 1,600 people including 1,100 engineers; rapidly enhancing engineering capabilities
items.quote: Today, we are nearly 1,600 people working in Data Patterns, nearly 1,100 engineers are working here, rapidly enhancing our engineering capabilities and design capabilities.

items.statement: Order delays due to external factors beyond company control; competitive tenders not included in projections
items.quote: During the quarter, fresh order intake was lower than anticipated, largely influenced by external factors beyond the company's control. As a result , our overall order book for the year has been modest.

items.statement: No competitive tenders considered in order projections; only single-vendor repeat contracts projected
items.quote: See, whenever I talk about projected orders, we do not consider competitive tenders because competitive tenders can go either way. So we do not take that into consideration in our projections.

items.statement: Make in India initiative supporting domestic defence manufacturing; government pushing for Indian IP
items.quote: And coming to your second question on India, yes, definitely, there is support for Indian equipment, Indian IP. And it is up to us in India, the private sector, to stand up, be counted, build the systems.

items.statement: Developing fire control radars, airborne EW suite, ground/airborne/shipborne communication, ELINT/COMINT/jammer, UAV detection radars, seekers for air defence
items.quote: The major revenue stream we're expecting, where investments have happened, to the extent of INR140 crores to INR150 crores were spent in the last 1.5 years in product development, comes in the category of fire control radars, airborne fire control radars, airborne electronic warfare suite, including receivers and jammers, ground and airborne or ship borne communication equipment as well as we've a

items.statement: Ashwini LLTR radar order expected from BEL in next 3-6 months; Sukhoi-30 upgrade products developed but no orders yet
items.quote: As regard Ashwini Radar, BEL has got the order last year, I think March -- February-March, they got the order, '24-'25. So we are in discussion with them. We expect that their requirements will flow down to us, and based on which we should be able to make an offer, and hop efully, when there's a contract in the next 3 to 6 months' time.

items.statement: Building infrastructure for seeker/radar validation and scenario simulators; bought additional land for expansion
items.quote: We are actually talking in three, four areas. I've also -- during the call also it has come out. We are working very, very aggressively on building full radars, all kinds of radars, airborne, ground-based radars, search, track, fire control, all of them, whether -- all of those radars we build.

items.statement: Exploring joint development with foreign company for high-end UAV-based radars with co-investment
items.quote: We're also looking at joint development of very, very high-end UAV-based radars, along with a foreign company. A joint development can happen that we are co-investing to see that we can address world markets.

items.statement: Emergency procurement and repeat orders expected to drive near-term order inflow; some fast-tracked due to border situation
items.quote: Third, because of what has happened with our border, it also likely that we'll get some orders, which is getting fast-tracked. So some orders also are likely to happen, which will all contribute to our order book.

items.statement: FY26 consolidated revenue growth guided at 18-20% including Uniclan
items.quote: overall for the business, we are expecting close to 18% to 20% of revenue growth for the coming financial year at a consolidated level.

items.statement: FY26 EBITDA margin guided at 16.5-17.5% and PAT margin around 10%
items.quote: in terms of EBITDA margin, we expect it to be between 16.5% to 17.5% and PAT margins to be around 10% in the current financial year FY'26.

items.statement: FY26 capex planned at INR 225-250 crore for 44-acre plant and adjacent land parcels
items.quote: the total capex planning that we've done is around INR 225 crores to INR 250 crores. This will be primarily for setting up the buildings at the 44-acre facility as well as land parcels that we've acquired recently adjacent to the current flagship unit.

items.statement: FY25 capex invested over INR 213 crore including capital advances
items.quote: During the financial year 2025, at a consolidated level, the company has invested over INR 213 crores towards capital expenditure, including capital advances.

items.statement: 44-acre expansion first building possession by Q3 FY26, commercial production Q4 FY26
items.quote: Our ongoing 44-acre expansion project construction is underway in full swing with anticipated possession of first building by Q3 FY'26 and beginning of commercial production slated in Q4 FY'26.

items.statement: Pencil capacity expansion from 5.5M to 8M per day in phases; wood processing phase complete
items.quote: our plan is to increase the capacities from 5.5 million to 8 million, but that will come up in phased manner. Right now, our existing infrastructure and resources are being focused on growing our capacities in our writing instrument and paper stationery category

items.statement: Pioneer Stationery capacity grew ~20% before back-to-school; fourth book machine line by June end
items.quote: Capacity at Pioneer Stationery almost grew by close to about 20% and that too before the back-to-school season. So that's worked very well for the company.

items.statement: Super Treads acquisition adds ~30% paper stationery capacity; 300 MT/month processing capacity
items.quote: our recent acquisition of Super Treads Private Limited which is a company based in Eastern India in Siliguri, West Bengal, that will help us to increase our capacities by another 30%-odd.

items.statement: Uniclan Q4 FY25 revenue INR 48.1 crore; run rate INR 15-17 crore/month; EBITDA margin 8-9%
items.quote: If you look at the Uniclan sales number for Q4 FY'25 Uniclan clocked revenues of INR 48.1 crores. The company's current run rate in terms of sales is around about INR 15 crores to INR17 odd crores per month, and we believe EBITDA margins to be about 8% to 9%.

items.statement: Q4 FY25 EBITDA margin 17.3% vs guided 16-17%; FY25 EBITDA margin expanded to 18.2% from 17.7%
items.quote: EBITDA for FY'25 grew by 27.8% to INR 348.4 crores as compared to INR 272.7 crores in FY'24, resulting in expansion of EBITDA margin from 17.7% in FY'24 to 18.2% in FY'25.

items.statement: PAT margin guided ~10% FY26 due to lower other income and INR 4.5 crore annual Uniclan brand amortization
items.quote: We believe keeping other factors constant on account of these reasons, we'll be able to maintain PAT levels of around 10% in the forthcoming financial year.

items.statement: Consolidated working capital ~60 days in FY25; target ~55 days with Uniclan integration
items.quote: On a consolidated basis, our working capital stood at around 60 days. This increase in working capital days is primarily on account of increase in debtors to keep pace with the demand coming from the market.

items.statement: Receivables increased due to Uniclan consolidation and extended credit for paper stationery
items.quote: this increase in debtors is attributed both to the acquisition of Uniclan because we consolidated only two-third of Uniclan's full financial year sales, while the debtors were consolidated at the year-end at the full level.

items.statement: Capex funded by INR 165+ crore unutilized IPO proceeds and internal accruals; balance sheet supports debt if needed
items.quote: we already have some amount which we raised during the IPO, which is still unutilized, about INR 165-plus crores as on 31st March, which continues to remain unutilized from the IPO proceeds that we raised, so that would be used. And rest of all should be funded through internal accruals.

items.statement: FY25 exports to FILA INR 166.5 crore, other exports INR 108 crore; FILA sales flat due to pencil capacity constraints
items.quote: in terms of FY'25, our exports to FILA was about INR 166.5 crores and exports to other third-party customers in other countries where we sell DOMS was about INR 108 crores.

items.statement: FILA distribution agreement gives exclusive rights in 100-150 countries; US sales through FILA only, no order cancellations
items.quote: one of the key components of the shareholder agreement has been the decision between the promoter shareholder group and the company to give FILA an exclusive right to distribute DOMS products in the geographies where they are currently present.

items.statement: Office supplies (pens, markers, highlighters) and paper stationery drove FY25 growth; scholastic stationery/art/kits grew ~8%
items.quote: If you see the growth in the last financial year, that has come majorly from the significant increase that has happened in office supplies, which is for pens, highlighters, markers where we've increased our capacity and paper stationery.

items.statement: SKIDO school bags launched for back-to-school; initial response encouraging (50% sold in 5-6 days)
items.quote: At SKIDO Industries, we launched our maiden range of DOMS branded school bags for the ongoing back-to-school season, and the initial response has been very encouraging.

items.statement: Uniclan commercialized own wet wipes plant in Q4 FY25; capacity 1.7 crore packs/year; replaces trading
items.quote: They've also commercialized their wet wipes -- own wet wipes manufacturing plant during this quarter towards the end of the quarter. So sales from wet wipes also will be added -- significant sales would be added in the current financial year.

items.statement: Uniclan reach: 70+ stockists, 1000+ distributors, 35,000+ retail outlets; reach constant, focus on integration
items.quote: Uniclan today still has about 70-plus stockist, but this includes the old stockist as well as the integrated stockist from the DOMS channel, close to 1,000-plus distributors and reaching about 35,000-plus retail outlets.

items.statement: DOMS distributor count ~4,750, touchpoints ~135,000; no contraction, focus on throughput per store
items.quote: So there has not been any contraction in the distribution reach. But at the same time, there has not been any significant expansion also because right now, like I said, Jinesh, earlier also, we always focused on maximizing the throughput each store.

items.statement: Proposed majority stake acquisition in Super Treads Private Limited for paper stationery capacity in East India
items.quote: The proposed acquisition of a majority stake in Super Treads Private Limited is aimed towards increasing our manufacturing capabilities and expanding our paper stationery infrastructure.

items.statement: Board recommended dividend of INR 3.15 per share for FY25 subject to approval
items.quote: we are pleased to share that the Board has recommended a dividend of INR 3.15 per share, subject to shareholders' approval.

items.statement: ESOP expense to continue; only 10% of total options granted so far under 5-year plan
items.quote: ESOP expense also, like I said, is something which has had an impact on our margins. That is also expected to continue because ESOP is like a 5-year plan. We've just given out ESOPs to the tune of 10% of the total options that we plan to give.

items.statement: Capacity constraints expected to persist 5-7 years; growth limited by phased capacity additions

items.statement: Zigly demerger planned in 3-4 years once scale achieved and losses reduce significantly
items.quote: We will separate it out at the right time as we said, we had indicated that in next three years to four years we will do it so as of now, those projections are not changing, we will be doing it at the right time once we see that overall, obviously as you rightly pointed out that we reach a decent scale. And at the same time, our losses in that business come down significantly.

items.statement: Peak revenue potential Rs.5000 crore with full asset utilization across all verticals
items.quote: With all the assets including Zigly, , with BOPP, CPP line, BOPET line to full potential, we should be, we can potentially touch close to Rs.5000 crores with full utilization of all assets across all business verticals.

items.statement: Target to scale shoe business to INR1,000 crores revenue within a short time, not in FY26
items.quote: our target is to be able to scale this up to INR1,000 crores within a short time.

items.statement: Expect 9% EBITDA margin in shoe business if expectations met
items.quote: Yes, your understanding is quite correct -- quite fair, Akhil, that we can generate a 9% EBITDA margin in this.

items.statement: Nashik ice cream factory commenced commercial production in May 2025; North India greenfield ice cream plant expected to begin operations by Q1 FY27
items.quote: We also have commenced commercial production at our new ice cream factory in Nashik this May and have also identified in North India, a new greenfield plant, which is expected to begin operations by Q1 FY '27.

items.statement: Shared manufacturing ROE target at least double dedicated manufacturing; dedicated manufacturing EBITDA absolute number guaranteed, shared manufacturing EBITDA margin to improve
items.quote: our expectation is that the ROE numbers should be at least double of our dedicated manufacturing. That's the target that we would work at.

items.statement: All three ice cream factories (Lucknow, Nashik, North India) have 100% guaranteed volume offtake agreements under anchor tenant hybrid model
items.quote: all the 3 ice cream factories, the one in Lucknow, the one in Nashik and the one coming up in North India have guaranteed volume offtake agreements.

items.statement: Consumer demand remains soft with macroeconomic headwinds; April-May not better than previous quarter; still not out of the woods except possibly shoes
items.quote: unfortunately, no. In case of some of the seasonal products, obviously, it helps. But then again, there have been rains, which have come in at wrong times at some of the places. So overall, I would say that it's -- still we are not out of the woods.

items.statement: Employee cost increased to 6.7% of sales in Q4 FY25 (FY25: 6.2%) mainly due to shoe business integration adding ~5,000 people; ESOP expense ~INR5 crores in Q4; future employee cost % uncertain as shoe business expands
items.quote: the increase in the labor cost is not predominantly due to the ESOPs. It's predominantly because we integrated the shoe business and got in nearly 5,000 -odd people coming into our system.

items.statement: Working capital requirement increased especially in shoe business; generated INR113 crores operating cash flow in FY25; cash and equivalents INR153 crores; net debt-to-equity 0.79
items.quote: The year also saw an increase in the working capital requirement of the company, especially in the shoe business. But despite this increase, the company was able to generate cash flow from operation of INR113 crores.

items.statement: Completed preferential share allotment in footwear subsidiary giving employees stake; rolled out ESOP scheme at HFL for retention and leadership pipeline
items.quote: First, we completed a preferential share allotment in our footwear subsidiary, giving them a tangible stake in our collective future. Second, we rolled out an ESOP scheme at HFL aimed at rewarding high performers, enhancing retention and attracting the nex t generation of leaders

items.statement: Proposing up to INR5 crores investment in Kabadiwala for substantial minority stake to gain strategic advantage in EPR compliance for plastic recycling
items.quote: the proposal right now, Faisal, is to invest up to INR5 crores in Kabadiwala, which gives us a substantial minority stake.

items.statement: EPR regulations notified requiring FMCG players to recycle post-consumer plastic; Kabadiwala investment aimed at EPR compliance and traceability
items.quote: EPR regulations have been notified and all FMCG players have to comply with this EPR regulations, which basically involves recycling of plastic post-consumer usage.

items.statement: Cautiously optimistic on export and private label opportunities from China Plus One sourcing shift due to potential US tariffs on China; early days across footwear, foot care, personal care, OTC pharma
items.quote: we are seeing some amount of increased interest in sourcing from India for the entire China Plus One thing working out, both in case of Footwear, in case of Foot Care and also surprisingly in case of Personal Care and OTC Pharma.

items.statement: Business shifting toward shared manufacturing (shoes, beverages) from dedicated manufacturing; shared manufacturing currently ~20% of gross block; medium-term mix expected similar but shared manufacturing margins to improve with shoe turnar
items.quote: nearly 80% of our capitalized gross block is attributable to dedicated manufacturing, while shared manufacturing accounts for the balance. In the medium term, we expect these percentage as far as the share of the business is concerned to be similar.

items.statement: Guides 50% revenue growth in FY26 on consolidated basis to ₹650-700 crore, and 25-30% CAGR in following years
items.quote: financial year, we have an excellent inquiry pipeline of ₹3,000-plus crores at a consolidated level, and we hope to have a conversion rate of 20% to 25%. This would ensure sufficient backlog through the year Kilburn Engineering Limited Q4 & FY25 Post Earnings Conference Call May 22, 2025 to achieve 50% growth, which also includes full year revenue of Monga

items.statement: Guides consolidated EBITDA margin of 20-22% for FY26
items.quote: See, Agastya, we've always mentioned that we will be able to maintain margins on 20-plus basis. And to be more specific, between 20 and 22, this is what we expect.

items.statement: Consolidated order backlog at ₹483 crore as of March 2025; Kilburn standalone order intake ₹493 crore, M.E. Energy ₹83 crore in FY25
items.quote: As mentioned earlier, the sustained demand has led to highest-ever order intake for Kilburn at ₹493 crores. Also, M.E. Energy achieved order of ₹83 crores. Monga Strayfield, our recent acquisition, has also had a good order intake. As a group, we have closed the year with an order backlog of ₹483 crores.

items.statement: Expects ₹600-700 crore order intake in FY26 at 20-25% conversion of ₹3,000+ crore inquiry pipeline
items.quote: On the order inflow front, as I said, we would have a conversion of around 20% to 25%. So if we're having a ₹3,000 crores pipeline, so you can expect ₹600 crores to ₹700 crores of order intake.

items.statement: Capex guidance for FY26 around ₹25 crore, fluid and not finalised; Phase 2 expansion at M.E. Energy Pune expected by mid-H2 FY26
items.quote: So as of now, I can tell you that we are targeting somewhere around ₹25 crores, but that is very fluid as of now. We haven't taken a call. Probably we'll need one more quarter to decide that.

items.statement: Ambernath factory fully operational, expected to add ₹100 crore revenue in FY26; M.E. Energy Phase 1 fully operational, Phase 2 by mid-H2 FY26; Saravali brownfield expansion planned
items.quote: On the Ambernath factory, as I said it is fully operational. So I would say that whatever we had targeted, ₹100 crores of addition into the turnover, that should happen in the current year, yes.

items.statement: Consolidated EBITDA margin guided at 20-22%; Kilburn standalone higher, M.E. Energy 15-17%, Monga Strayfield 24-25%
items.quote: When you look at the overall business, Monga Strayfield business is very profitable. So that's at about 24%, 25%. M.E. Energy is at around 15% to 17%. So blended margin for those businesses are around 20% odd. Kilburn is slightly higher, as we mentioned. So we are confident of between 20% to 22%.

items.statement: Inquiry pipeline grew 50% YoY to ₹3,000+ crore; seeing larger ticket sizes and new sectors (nuclear, cement, pharma)
items.quote: Well, if you recall, last year, it was ₹2,000 plus for both M.E. Energy and Kilburn put together. And now we also have Monga Strayfield. So between the three of us at consolidated level, we have ₹3,000 crores plus. So we are getting more inquiries than before, that's for sure.

items.statement: Margin improvement driven by better product mix including higher-margin JESA OCP Morocco project and Monga Strayfield contribution
items.quote: On the margin front, if you recall, we had a project from JESA for OCP for Morocco. So and that execution has commenced, and that was a project with little higher margins. So this was one of the contributing factors.

items.statement: Granules India pilot order (₹70 crore) on hold awaiting trial completion; Shree Cement reference order executed; L&T nuclear order won
items.quote: There's still one order which is on hold, where we had a large order from Granules which had come. We are still working with them on their pilot part of the order, which hopefully in the next three, four months should get completed, then that order will go into commercial production. So that's a ₹70-odd crore order.

items.statement: Export order backlog ~₹160 crore; targets 20-30% revenue from exports in 2-3 years
items.quote: Out of the order backlog, nearly ₹160 crores are export orders.

items.statement: Negative CFO due to debtor/unbilled revenue buildup from March dispatches (₹30-40 crore) and ICDs to subsidiaries; aims to improve via customer advances and vendor terms
items.quote: In the last month itself of March, we have dispatched around ₹30 crores to ₹40 crores of billing has been done. So that has led to increase in our debtors also. And even though the cash flows from operations is negative, we have put in funds for the buildup of this inventory through this share issue as well as sort of ICDs, which we have taken from our subsidiary companies.

items.statement: ₹200 crore warrant proceeds committed by June/July 2026; post-conversion share capital ₹52.6 crore (5.62 crore shares); utilisation: capex, term loan repayment, subsidiary investment, working capital, general corporate
items.quote: We have already taken our shareholder approval where the utilisation was mentioned. Part of it will go towards CapEx, part will be going towards repayment of our term loan. Part of that will be towards investment into our subsidiaries. On balance, we will decide what is for working capital as well as some general corporate use.

items.statement: Nuclear segment order book ₹50 crore; expects annual orders for next 4-5 years; carbon black, petrochemicals, fertilisers, nuclear seen as major contributors
items.quote: We have ₹50 crores today, which is there. We believe this will be an important segment in the next four, five years where every year some order should come through.

items.statement: No management changes mentioned; focus on leveraging combined strengths of Kilburn, M.E. Energy, Monga Strayfield as integrated group
items.quote: We will try to leverage the strengths of all the organisations put together to deliver a consolidated performance.

items.statement: Granules order (₹70 crore) spillover risk; soda ash sector slow due to Chinese dumping; project execution timeline variances can affect revenue recognition
items.quote: There's still one order which is on hold, where we had a large order from Granules which had come. We are still working with them on their pilot part of the order, which hopefully in the next three, four months should get completed, then that order will go into commercial production.

items.statement: NSE listing approved by board; timeline dependent on NSE process, no specific date given
items.quote: The Board has approved it that we are going to apply for the listing, then it is up to NSE to see what is the process and the time line, but we can't give a particular date.

items.statement: Peak revenue from existing capacity estimated at INR2,700-2,800 crores at current prices
items.quote: So, considering the current price, the peak revenue from the existing capacity is something around INR2,700 crores to INR2,800 crores.

items.statement: FY26 revenue growth expected at 10-15% driven by both volume and price
items.quote: We are expecting 10% to 15% growth in revenue from all the products. So, it is a mix of both volume and prices.

items.statement: FY26 EBITDA margin expected above 15% versus 12.7% in Q4 FY25
items.quote: In the last quarter i.e., in the fourth quarter of '25, we have EBITDA margin of approximately 13%. So, we are expecting more than 15% in the current year.

items.statement: Export revenue target of 40-45% over medium term from current 27%
items.quote: our export revenues stand at around 27% and we aim to scale this to about 40% over the medium term

items.statement: FY26 capex planned at INR150-200 crores including growth, infra and automation
items.quote: So, we are doing capex for INR150 crores to INR200 crores from the last 2, 3 years. So we have planned the same INR150 crores to INR200 crores in the current year.

items.statement: Paracetamol capacity enhanced to 10,800 MTPA via INR155 crore backward integrated unit
items.quote: This INR155 crore investment funded entirely through internal accruals has enhanced our IOL Chemicals and Paracetamol capacity to 10,800 MTPA

items.statement: Clopidogrel capacity expanded by 33%
items.quote: We also expanded Clopidogrel capacity by 33% reflecting our belief in the long-term growth potentials of cardiovascular APIs.

items.statement: 101 acres land acquired for greenfield expansion; environmental, industrial and NHAI clearances underway
items.quote: To support future growth, we have acquired 101 acres of land along the Chandigarh -Bathinda Highway, laying the groundwork for greenfield expansion. Approvals for industrial, environmental and NHI clearances are underway and progressing into FY 2026.

items.statement: Non-Ibuprofen portfolio now contributes 34% of API revenues, up from 18% five years ago
items.quote: This is a major step in strengthening our non -Ibu portfolio, which now contributes about 34% to the API revenues, up from 18% just 5 years ago.

items.statement: Ibuprofen demand and pricing showing positive traction; Paracetamol demand below expectations in FY25
items.quote: In Q4, we saw improved traction in the Ibuprofen segment despite continued price challenges alongside stable demand and pricing across our broader API basket.

items.statement: Levetiracetam volumes expected to increase with capacity enhancements, new customers and US DMF filing
items.quote: I think Levetiracetam, yes, the quantity will increase because we have already done some capacity enhancements for Levetiracetam also and we are approaching new customers as well and we have filed U.S. DMF for this product also.

items.statement: API prices believed to have bottomed out over last 2-3 quarters; ethyl acetate prices stable with raw material costs
items.quote: But as we have previously explained that the prices we think are at bottom out for all the API since last 2, 3

items.statement: Q4 FY25 EBITDA margin 12.7%, up 141 bps YoY; full year EBITDA margin ~11%
items.quote: EBITDA for quarter 4 of financial year '25 increased by 17% to approximately INR67 crores, up from approximately INR58 crores in the same quarter last year. This translates to an EBITDA margin of 12.7%, an improvement of 141 basis points year -on-year.

items.statement: Chemical segment EBITDA margin improved to 6% in Q4 FY25 from 3% in FY24; targeting 10%
items.quote: In the fourth quarter of '25, we have achieved 6% EBITDA margin from chemicals as compared to '24, 3%. So we are going forward to 10%.

items.statement: Ibuprofen margins currently higher than non-Ibu portfolio; non-Ibu products have potential to match or exceed Ibuprofen margins with regulatory market revenue
items.quote: No doubt our ibuprofen margins are presently more than all other non-Ibu segment. But all other non-Ibu segment products are also potential to have EBITDA margin equivalent or more than Ibuprofen also.

items.statement: China CDE approval received for Ibuprofen; targeting Europe, Brazil, US, Russia, Korea for non-Ibu exports
items.quote: From a regulatory standpoint, Ibuprofen approval from China CDE is an important milestone in expanding the IOL's global reach.

items.statement: Chemical exports increased to 18% of chemical revenue in FY25 from 10-12% previously after ethyl acetate recertification
items.quote: Earlier we were exporting around 10% to 12% of chemical revenue to the export market. After getting the recertification last year, the export revenue share of chemical business has been increased to around 18% during FY '25.

items.statement: 16 DMFs and 19 CEPs filed; acetic anhydride CEP for Europe under process; US FDA inspection timing uncertain
items.quote: With 16 DMF and 19 CEPs already filed, we are strengthening our foundation for a larger global presence.

items.statement: Net debt to equity at 0.09 reflecting minimal leverage and strong internal accruals
items.quote: Our net debt to equity ratio stood at 0.09 on account of working capital borrowing at the end of financial year '25 reflecting a minimal leverage and strong internal accruals.

items.statement: Power and fuel costs declined sharply in FY25 due to rice husk price drop; expected stable in FY26
items.quote: Actually, other expenses include power and fuel expenses. The prices of fuel are drastically down in the year of '25. The major, we have consumed rice as a fuel, which has came down drastically.

items.statement: Q4 FY25 API revenue split 65% Ibuprofen, 35% non-Ibuprofen
items.quote: For Q4, split means in terms of the revenue. So it's around 65%, 35%.

items.statement: Levetiracetam targeting Europe first via CEP, then US and India parallelly, also Brazil via ANVISA
items.quote: I think we have got CEP for this product. So first, the market which we are targeting will be Europe followed by other markets like U.S. and India parallelly. Brazil also, we have ANVISA for this product so we are also targeting Brazilian market also.

items.statement: No major new Ibuprofen competitors currently; open market but confident in cost efficiency and quality
items.quote: New players, we don't see any big problem as of now, but this is an open market so anybody can come. And we have our strategy, we have our operational efficiency, the quality and the marketing efficiency.

items.statement: Cash PAT for FY25 at INR185 crores, up from INR49.2 crores in Q4 FY24 to INR56.4 crores in Q4 FY25
items.quote: For the full financial year '25, cash PAT was INR185 crores underscoring our strong cash generation and the resilience of our core operations.

items.statement: US FDA inspection timing uncertain; company ready but no visibility on schedule
items.quote: As of now, we don't have any information for the inspection number one. And second, you commented that we have some pending approvals. So probably the approval process for all the filed products is under progress.

items.statement: No plans for DCDA manufacturing due to raw material supply-demand issues
items.quote: I think as of now there is no plans to go for DCDA manufacturing because the basic input material is having some problem with demand supply, like this is basically Inaudible 48:52 product.

items.statement: Domestic tile demand remained subdued in FY25; exports affected by ocean freight volatility and overcapacity from Morbi
items.quote: Domestic demand for tiles remained subdued and exports continued to be affected by the volatility of ocean freights.

items.statement: Gross margin improved to 35% in FY25 from 33.6% in FY24 due to cost savings and premiumization
items.quote: Our gross margin for FY '25 was 35% versus 33.6% in FY '24.

items.statement: GVT salience grew to 41% and vitrified mix reached highest ever 58.5% in FY25
items.quote: salience of GVT grew to 41% in FY '25 and the vitrified mix improved to the highest ever 58.5%.

items.statement: Total capex of INR234 crores invested between FY19-FY25 adding 10.9 million sqm capacity largely through internal accruals
items.quote: These capacity additions are part of the total INR234 crores invested in capex between FY '19 and FY '25, adding 10.9 million square meter of additional capacity largely funded through internal accruals.

items.statement: No growth capex planned for FY26; only maintenance and regulatory capex of INR5-10 crores
items.quote: FY '26 capex would be more on growth and regulatory -- sorry, more on maintenance and regulatory and not on growth capex. So no new line being thought of in this financial

items.statement: Overall capacity utilization around 55% in FY25, down from 65-70% in FY24 on expanded base
items.quote: For our own manufacturing, I think it will be about 55%-odd, if I remember right.

items.statement: Dora GVT line of 3.3 million sqm commissioned in FY24 enabled growth in South and West markets
items.quote: To support the shift towards GVT and expand our reach, particularly in the South and West markets, the Dora GVT line having 3.3 million square meters has come into existence in FY '24 and has enabled growth.

items.statement: Solar PPA at Sikandrabad lowered power costs; operational efficiency improvements pruned overall cost of operations
items.quote: The go-live of our solar power purchase agreement at Sikandrabad has lower power cost. By streamlining processes and improving existing systems, operational efficiency was enhanced, helping us to prune the overall cost of operations.

items.statement: Significant portion of cost savings passed to market to maintain competitiveness; retained part contributed to gross margins
items.quote: While a significant portion of these savings was passed on to the market to maintain competitiveness, OBL successfully retained a part contributing to our gross margins.

items.statement: Morbi overcapacity at ~60% utilization; more capacity coming online in H1 FY26 despite sluggish market
items.quote: We expect -- I think Morbi would have been at about 60% odd capacity utilization is our estimate last year, maybe even lower. And however, there is more capacity, which is going to come online in Morbi in H1 in spite of the sluggishness in the market.

items.statement: Freight rates structurally subdued for FY26 vs prior year but volatility remains due to China-US trade dynamics and tariff uncertainty
items.quote: I think structurally, the freight rates definitely will be subdued for this full year compared to what they were earlier. So that's one positive factor.

items.statement: Institutional sales (B2B/B2G) contribute 20-25% of revenue; government vertical rebuilt with focus on 805 departments
items.quote: The way we track our projects, Moksh, we do roughly around 20%, 25% institutional one way or another way. This is a combination of small or medium or large projects, all of that put together, private plus government.

items.statement: Supplies to major builders including DLF, Godrej, Tata, Shapoorji Pallonji, L&T, Shobha, Puravankara, Prestige
items.quote: We supply to DLF. We supply to Godrej, talking about private builders. We supply to Tata. We supply to Shapoorji Pallonji, L&T Construction, you name it. And you're talking Bangalore. We supply to Shobha. We supply to Puravankara. We supply to Prestige.

items.statement: Finance costs doubled in FY25 due to term loan for Dora plant capitalized Sep 2023; was largely debt-free in FY22-23
items.quote: On finance cost, specifically, we took the loan for that thing, which has been the interest of that has been a part of it because if you remember, in FY '22 and FY '23, we were largely debt-free. And we took up a term loan to finance the Dora line.

items.statement: Credit ratings retained: India Ratings IND A1, CRISIL A with negative outlook; resumed banking with SBI
items.quote: India Rating has retained it's IND A1 rating for us and CRISIL has reaffirmed its rating as A albeit with a negative outlook. OBL has also consolidated it's banking relationships and resumed banking once again with State Bank of India, a sign of the company's creditworthiness.

items.statement: CFO Himanshu Jindal resignation is personal choice after 6.5 years; no correlation with company performance
items.quote: I think very honestly, 6.5 is not what I intended to be. I think I mentioned it on our Board meeting today as well. But these professional bonds and the personal bonds that I've created here in OBL are life long. So I think that's how I would summarize it.

items.statement: Retail demand remains slow; H2 FY25 was slow and Q4 slow; no dramatic recovery signs yet
items.quote: Not yet, Shubham. Nothing very dramatic. It's -- quarter 4 has been slow. Actually, the whole of H2 has been slow. So far, nothing dramatically different has emerged.

items.statement: Expects H2 FY26 better than H1; export recovery of 15-20% would stabilize domestic pricing and trigger volume pickup
items.quote: We expect H2 to be much better than H1. That's one, if you ask me. And secondly, as I said before, Shubham, a lot depends on the export performance. Now if exports go up by 15%, 20%, say from next month, you will certainly see a lot of traction in the domestic market itself.

items.statement: Listed tile players' aggregate revenue flat at INR11,000-11,500 crores for three years (FY23-25)
items.quote: If you see the last three financial years, FY '23, '24, '25, the listed players have been in the -- total listed players have been in the INR11,000 crores to INR11,500 crores kind of a top line figure hasn't changed for 3 years now.

items.statement: OBL market share ~5-6% of listed universe (~INR11,500 cr); ~4-5% including top 5-6 unlisted players (~INR15,000 cr total)
items.quote: So we would be about 5% to 6% of the listed company universe. If you were to add the top five or six unlisted players then the market comes to about INR15,000 odd crores and then you can get the numbers there. So it would be about 4% to 5% of that.

items.statement: Morbi associations attempting price hikes (INR2/sq ft) but no materialization yet; indicates Morbi players also hurting
items.quote: They have like kind of all the producers have taken or we are going to increase our price by INR2 per square feet, we swear by this, we swear by that, we do this, we do that. A lot of those videos have been circulated to the trade that our price is increasing, this-is-this, that-is-that. But nothing that gives me is materialized there's still not any effect.

items.statement: No forward-looking volume or revenue projections given; INR1,000 cr top line timing depends on industry upturn
items.quote: We have kind of stayed away from giving any volume and forward-looking volume and revenue projections. So I will stick to this. I think the more relevant question is that when do we see the upturn in industry volumes and industry revenue.

items.statement: Dealers down-stocking due to falling prices; inventory levels at dealer points are low
items.quote: Dealers have been down stocking for some time, and they are reluctant to keep stocks because of the falling prices and all. So inventory levels at dealer points are kind of low.

items.statement: ASP gap with market leader narrowed from INR10 to INR7 per sq ft over FY23-25; premiumization to continue in FY26
items.quote: Compared to, say, FY '23 versus FY '25, we have closed our gap with the market leader, I would say, by about, say, every INR10 gap if it was there in '23, we are now at about INR7 gap now.

items.statement: Organized sector not losing market share to Morbi/unorganized; top unlisted players growing faster but not dramatically different
items.quote: I don't think organized sector is losing out on market share to Morbi per se.

items.statement: US business expected to grow in single digits in FY26
items.quote: For FY26, we believe US will still grow in single digit.

items.statement: EBITDA margin expected to exceed or be around 26% in FY26
items.quote: So, F Y26, we believe , we will exceed 26 or around 26% comfortably in terms of EBITDA margins and that’s our current best estimate

items.statement: Overall consolidated revenue expected to grow double-digit in FY26 led by India and international markets
items.quote: So, for the overall business, we are looking at a double-digit growth in revenue led by strong growths in India and international markets, and also our new growth themes like biologics, vaccines, and all scaling up.

items.statement: India formulations business expected to continue outperforming IPM market in FY26
items.quote: We believe, in India, we will continue to outperform the IPM market for the year.

items.statement: Vaccines business expected to contribute meaningfully in FY26
items.quote: Yes, we will see some good contribution from vaccines for FY26.

items.statement: Emerging markets expected to continue strong double-digit CAGR and faster scale-up
items.quote: Emerging market has been consistently growing at a strong double-digit CAGR and also improving profitability. And that trend is also continuing and we are quite positive for a faster scale up.

items.statement: No major fall-off expected in US business in FY27 due to important launches
items.quote: No, I mean, see, we have important launches in FY27. So, assuming we are doing well with our approvals and regulatory front, we don't see any major fall-out.

items.statement: 14 to 15 important critical launches planned for FY27
items.quote: But, I said irrespective of that, we have a lot of important launches in FY27, almost 14 to 15 important, critical launches in FY27.

items.statement: Digitalization and efficiency measures improved profitability by 50-70 bps, similar improvement expected going forward
items.quote: These measures have improved the profitability in the range of 50 to 70 basis points and we expect similar improvement going forward as well.

items.statement: FY25 consolidated EBITDA margin 30.4%, up 290 bps YoY; Q4 FY25 EBITDA margin 32.6%, up 310 bps YoY and 630 bps QoQ
items.quote: The business delivered 3 of 22 strong operating margin of 30.4% which is an improvement of 290 basis points over the previous year

items.statement: Gross margin improvement in Q4 driven by business mix, price increases in wellness, and cost reductions
items.quote: It is a mix of business as well as products. Even base business improvement is there. Contribution from US business, India business, wellness business. So, wellness, we have been able to take some price increase also. We were able to reduce our cost also in some of the products.

items.statement: Margins expected to be stable in FY26 barring product-specific impacts
items.quote: To the extent, you know, the product specific margin, obviously you would find some impact, but otherwise yes, margins are stable.

items.statement: US business delivered strong double-digit growth in FY25 led by volume expansion and new launches
items.quote: Our US business delivered sound performance with a strong double-digit growth through the year. This was led by both volume expansion and successful new product launches.

items.statement: India branded formulations grew 11% YoY in Q4 FY25, outpacing market; chronic portfolio at 43% per IQVIA MAT March 2025
items.quote: The branded formulation business in India grew faster than the market during the quarter with 11% year -on-year growth driven by h igh uptick in pillar brands and innovation

items.statement: Consumer wellness grew 17% YoY in Q4 FY25 with 13% volume growth; personal care and food & nutrition both double-digit
items.quote: Our consumer wellness business recorded revenues of 9.1 billion rupees, up 17% year-on-year with a 13% volume growth.

items.statement: International markets formulations grew 12% YoY in Q4 FY25
items.quote: International markets formulations business delivered robust growth during the quarter with revenues of 5.5 billion rupees, up 12% year-on-year.

items.statement: Base US business (ex-Revlimid) showing strong healthy growth with new contracts and supply chain resilience
items.quote: So, one thing, today, as of now, we have a very strong and healthy base business growth. This also includes when we have obviously lost share on Asacol. But we are seeing significant opportunities on our existing products in terms of new contracts and new requests.

items.statement: Filed 3 ANDAs, received 6 approvals, launched 5 products in US in Q4 FY25
