items.statement: Cellulosic fibre demand stable except minor drop in Indian market in Q4, offset by increased exports and specialty product mix changes
items.quote: In terms of our volumes, the demand has been quite stable, except that in quarter 4, we have seen some minor drop in the demand in the Indian market. So, we had to increase our exports.

items.statement: Paints market excluding Birla Opus was negative in FY25; with Birla Opus, market grew low single digits; FY26 could remain low single-digit growth
items.quote: if you exclude Birla Opus, then the market has actually been negative. So, the market has actually been negative. And if you add Birla Opus, then the market has been positive in low single-digit numbers.

items.statement: Cellulosic fibre profitability lower by 12% YoY due to higher key raw material prices partially absorbed; pulp prices now softening
items.quote: However, the profitability of this business during the year was lower by 12% on a Y -o-Y basis due to higher key raw material prices absorbed by the company partially.

items.statement: Negative chlorine realization for full year FY25 in range of ₹6,000-7,000 per tonne; showed improvement trend in Q4 touching minus ₹9,000 at lowest
items.quote: For the full year, negative chlorine realization was in the range of about ₹6000 to ₹7000, I won't quote an exact number, but in that range.

items.statement: Birla Opus pricing at par with market leader for consumers; offers 10% free on 20L and 10L emulsions to end users; economy segment competitors dropped prices but factored in plan
items.quote: So, Birla Opus is able to charge the consumers ready with the same price. In terms of other aspects, yes, we have seen that maybe in the economy segment, some of the competitors have tried to drop some prices, etc, but those are all factored in the plan.

items.statement: Birla Opus luxury and premium products contributing over 65% of revenue across all categories (emulsions, enamels, waterproofing, wood finishes, designer finishes)
items.quote: Our luxury and premium products are now contributing more than 65% to the company's revenue, a testimony to Birla Opus quality of products.

items.statement: Birla Opus reached 6,600 towns across 33 states/UTs with 137 depots; dealer count close to 50,000 target; tinting machine penetration near 80%
items.quote: Like we said, our objective was to hit 6,000-plus towns and try and track close to 50,000 dealers at the end of the first year. So, we are close to where we had targeted.

items.statement: Birla Pivot crossed ₹5,000 crore ARR in Q4 FY25 (3.3x YoY growth); 40,000+ SKUs, 300+ brands/OEMs, 35 categories, deliveries to 375 cities across 26 states/UTs
items.quote: Birla Pivot has crossed annual run rate (ARR) of ₹5,000 crores based on exit quarter 4 FY '25 in less than 2 years of inception and achieved a 3.3x revenue growth over FY '24.

items.statement: Paints industry undergoing structural consolidation through M&A expected to reshape competitive landscape
items.quote: The industry is also undergoing a structural shape with consolidation of players through merger and acquisition and same expected to reshape the competitive landscape.

items.statement: China demand slowdown and tariff uncertainty causing global VSF price correction; pulp prices down significantly in last 2-3 months
items.quote: China has seen a dip in the demand and because from mid -April onwards because of tariff uncertainty, there is some kind of a wait -and-watch approach being taken by the value chain player, which is getting a little better now.

items.statement: Epoxy business may get export upside from tariff differentials but majority sales domestic; Korean FTA on epoxy imports a concern
items.quote: Now assuming there will be differential tariffs on different countries, in some cases, of course, India will have an advantage, right? And while our current export volume is small, we may get some upside, a nd we may even get some ability to provide formulation products to the countries outside of India

items.statement: Birla Pivot focusing on working capital management and digitization; building logistics infrastructure and seamless fulfilment experience
items.quote: A lot of what we build is built ground up, given the complexity that is involved in how B2B e-commerce platform needs to operate. So , we continue to invest in that, continue to build capability around logistics infrastructure, around how we build seamless fulfilment experience.

items.statement: UltraTech cement capacity expected to reach 215 million tonnes with estimated EBITDA per tonne saving of ₹250-300 by 2027
items.quote: Cement business under UltraTech has been growing with total capacity expected to reach 215 million tonnes with estimated EBITDA per tonne saving of about ₹250 to ₹300 by 2027.

items.statement: Pavan Jain superannuating on 15th August 2025; Hemant Kadel to take over as CFO from 16th August 2025
items.quote: I take this opportunity to thank Mr. Pavan Jain, who is superannuating on 15th August 2025 for a stellar role played in shaping Grasim's transformative journey. I would also like to welcome Mr. Hemant Kadel, a Grasim veteran, and a colleague of Pavan, who will take over from him as Grasim's CFO from 16th of August 2025.

items.statement: Grasim standalone revenue highest ever at ₹8,926 crore in Q4 FY25, up 32% YoY reflecting new business success and existing business strength
items.quote: Grasim standalone revenue has risen to its highest level at ₹8,926 crore in quarter 4 FY '25, an impressive Y-o-Y growth of 32%.

items.statement: Cellulosic Fibres and Chemicals combined consistently delivered over ₹20,000 crore topline with over ₹2,500 crore EBITDA across cycles over past 3 years
items.quote: One highlight over the past 3 years, both Cellulosic Fibres and Chemicals business combinedly have consistently delivered top line of over ₹20,000 crores with EBITDA of over ₹2,500 crores across cycles reflecting the strength of these businesses.

items.statement: Global tariff uncertainty creating demand slowdown in China and wait-and-watch approach in VSF value chain; may impact H1 FY26 performance
items.quote: There is a demand slowdown in the China market. So, to that extent, yes, there will be a weakness. We don't give the guidance for FY '26 kind of profit numbers. We have given you the macro kind of situation.

name: Oil and Natural Gas Corporation Ltd

items.statement: Medium-term goals: mid-teen EBITDA, 35% MHCV market share, substantial non-MHCV growth, alt-fuel leadership, subsidiary value unlocking, ESG leadership
items.quote: We will continue to march steadfastly towards the medium -term goals shared with all of you - achieve mid-teen EBITDA, achi eve MHCV market share of 35%, substantial growth in our noncore, non -MHCV businesses, leadership in alternative fuel vehicles, value unlocking from subsidiaries and leadership in ESG.

items.statement: FY26 growth expected across all CV segments; buses, tractor-trailers, tippers to outperform; LCV/ICV/MAV no headwinds
items.quote: We believe that FY '26 would witness growth in all CV segments including LCV, ICV and MHCV goods and passenger.

items.statement: Q4 FY25 EBITDA margin 15%, highest ever quarterly; FY25 EBITDA margin 12.7% vs 12% FY24; material cost 70.6% of revenue in Q4, lowest in 8 quarters
items.quote: Our EBITDA margin for the quarter at 1 5% is the highes t ever quarterly EBITDA margin.

items.statement: Switch India order book 1,800 units at end FY25; OHM targeting 1,700 bus additions in FY26; defense order pipeline at all-time high, above INR1,000 crore revenue
items.quote: At the end of the year, Switch India has an order book of 1,800 number.

items.statement: FY25 capex INR954 crore + INR200 crore investments; FY26 capex ~INR1,000 crore focused on alt-fuel and EV critical components; subsidiary investments INR500-750 crore
items.quote: We'll be doing around INR1,000 crores. Essentially, these, the capital expenditure will be aimed towards developing the capability as well as towards getting into more on the new technologies.

items.statement: Added 108 MHCV and 106 LCV touch points in FY25; network 1,889 pan-India; Vijayawada bus plant inaugurated, Lucknow plant under construction to augment bus body capacity
items.quote: As of March '25, Ashok Leyland network has 1,889 touch points Pan-India.

items.statement: AC cabin norm impact 0.5-2% price increase per model; steel safeguard duty may raise prices INR3-5/kg in Q1-Q2, temporary 200-day measure; rubber and other commodities softening
items.quote: The impact on the price could be anywhere between 0.5% to 2%, depending on the model.

items.statement: Launched 6 new products in FY25 including SAATHI, Leo LCVs, iVAC, Oyster CNG/Vmax buses, 55t and 19t EV trucks; EV terminal tractor and 15m AC coach ready for commercial production in FY26
items.quote: Key highlights for the year were 6 new products, in cluding SAATHI and Leo in the LCV segment. iVAC, Intelligent Vehicle Acceleration Control, for improved economy and MHCV truck segment, cost-competitive fully-built Oyster CNG and Oyster V max in the bus segment, and 55-ton and 19-ton battery electric vehicle trucks.

items.statement: Ranked #1 in dealer satisfaction, #2 in customer and sales satisfaction indices; digital platforms leveraged for service transformation and premiumization
items.quote: In domestic MHCV, Ashok Leyland ranking has improved to number 1 in dealer satisfaction inde x and number 2 in customer satisfaction index and sales satisfaction index.

items.statement: LCV addressable 2-4t market share 18.6% in FY25 vs 19.3% prior; targeting 20% short-term, 25% medium-term; new Chinese EV truck entrants noted but AL technology maturity superior
items.quote: In the addressable 2–4-ton market, for FY 25 AL market share was at 18.6%, lower than 19.3% in the previous year.

items.statement: AC cabin regulation coming October; all affected segment products ready; safeguard duty on steel for 200 days; AC regulation accepted by customers, no resistance to price pass-through
items.quote: For the coming AC regulation, all our products in the affected segments are ready.

items.statement: Export volumes up 52% YoY in Q4, 29% YoY in FY25 to 15,255 units; strategy to add ASEAN as new home market with local assembly in Indonesia/Thailand; South Africa product launch this month
items.quote: Export volumes registered a growth of 52% in Q4 on a year -on-year basis. For the year ended March 25, exports volume at 15,255 numbers was higher by 29% against 11,853 numbers in the previous year.

items.statement: Finished goods inventory below 7,000 vehicles vs 8,000-9,000 prior; credit on MHCV trucks near zero (<1,000 vehicles); shifting to pull-based replenishment; payables timing-driven
items.quote: Earlier years, it used to be about 8,000, 9,000 vehicles at the year-end. But now this year, we have really brought it down below 7,000 vehicles.

items.statement: Net cash INR4,242 crore at end Q4 FY25 vs net debt INR89 crore end FY24; finance cost down 15% YoY; other income flat at INR250 crore
items.quote: At the end of the quarter, we were cash positive at INR4,242 crores against a net debt of INR89 crores at the end of the previous year.

items.statement: No fund raise mentioned; strong cash position enables self-funding of capex and subsidiary investments
items.quote: So, in a way that signals that we can invest much more actually in the future growth of the company.

items.statement: Switch UK restructuring: consultation to cease Sherburn manufacturing/assembly; production moving to efficient locations; not exiting market; eliminates GBP2-3m monthly loss
items.quote: You are a ware that the Board of Switch U K has given their approval to commence the consultation process with its employees which could potentially lead to cessation of manufacturing and assembly facilities in the Sherburn, UK facility.

items.statement: HLF consolidated GNPA 3.5%, NNPA 2.1%, both lower than prior year; PAT up 21%; AUM INR61,700 crore (+25% YoY)
items.quote: The asset quality is quite good, with the GNPA at 3.5% and NNPA at 2.1%. All these are much lower than the last year's levels.

items.statement: MHCV market share 30.9% in FY25; LCV 2-4t share 18.6%; Switch India Q4 EBITDA 12%, FY25 EBITDA 6%; OHM fleet availability 98%+
items.quote: For the year ended March '25, our market share stood at 30.9%.

items.statement: Steel safeguard duty and global tariff dynamics pose commodity headwinds; Western DFC operationalisation may impact rail competition; promoter share pledge clarified as treasury function, short-term, voting rights retained
items.quote: We expect commodity headwinds from safeg uard duties on steel and impact of emerging global tariff dynamics.

items.statement: Q4 FY25 revenue grew 28% YoY to INR 2,667 cr; full-year FY25 revenue grew 18% to INR 10,274 cr
items.quote: Revenue for quarter 4 , operating revenue stood at INR 2,667 crores, a strong 28% increase Y-o-Y, primarily led by our CNB business, which grew by 86%. The full-year FY '25, we reported INR 10,274 crores in revenue. That 's an 18% growth over FY '24.

items.statement: Full-year FY25 EBITDA grew 50% to INR 1,925 cr with margin improvement of 390 bps to 19%
items.quote: For the full year, EBITDA grew remarkably 50%, up to INR 1,925 crores, with a margin improvement of 390 basis points to 19%.

items.statement: Full-year FY25 net profit doubled YoY to INR 945 cr; net profit margin improved 381 bps to 9%
items.quote: FY '25, we delivered INR 945 crores in net profit, doubling Y-o-Y. Reflecting strong margin execution and cost discipline, the net profit margin improved by 381 basis points to 9%.

items.statement: Specialty product portfolio contributes 22% of total revenue led by crop-specific innovations and premium LDAN
items.quote: Notably, our specialty product portfolio now contributes 22% of our total revenue, led by our crop-specific innovations and our premium LDAN product.

items.statement: Board recommended 100% dividend for FY25
items.quote: Based on these good results and also balancing it out with the CAPEX plan, though the thought was to look at even higher dividends, but the Board in a conservative manner has recommended 100% dividend.

items.statement: FY26 total capex expected around INR 4,500 cr for Gopalpur and Dahej projects; INR 1,400 cr already capitalized
items.quote: In fact, the total CAPEX this year, which we talked about FY '26, the 2 new projects, total CAPEX is expected to be around INR 4,500 crores, total I am talking. Out of that, our capitalization is around INR 1,400 crores.

items.statement: Maintenance capex runs at INR 300-400 cr per year
items.quote: That's roughly around, I would say INR 300 crores to INR 400 crores. That 's the normal maintenance CAPEX, which will continue as a normal business.

items.statement: Gopalpur TAN project 75% complete; Dahej nitric acid project 48% complete; both expected commissioning in H2 FY26
items.quote: The Gopalpur progress is 75%, and Dahej project has progressed 48%. We stand committed , the commissioning of both the plant is expected in H2 FY '26.

items.statement: TAN licensed capacity is 587 Kt; currently constrained by nitric acid capacity
items.quote: It's 587. TAN capacity you are taking.

items.statement: TAN demand ~1.4 million tons vs domestic capacity ~1 million tons; industry net short with 6-7% YoY demand growth
items.quote: Currently, the demand of TAN is around 1.4 million , and the present capacity in Indian market is around 1 million. So, this industry is net -net short.

items.statement: Optimistic for kharif season supported by above-normal monsoon forecast and targeted approach across cotton, soybean, paddy, corn
items.quote: Looking ahead, we are optimistic for the kharif season, supported by forecast of above normal monsoon and our targeted approach across cotton, soybean, paddy, and corn through the Mahadhan brand.

items.statement: Q4 FY25 consolidated EBITDA margin 18% (down from mix change); TAN and CNB segments individually saw margin expansion
items.quote: Q4 EBITDA came in at INR 480 crores, up 10% Y -o-Y. While the margin for quarter stood at 18%, slightly lower due to change in business mix.

items.statement: New projects (Gopalpur, Dahej) target ROCE of 18-20% at 80-85% utilization; first year utilization expected at 70%
items.quote: In fact, both the new projects, what we have embarked on, we are looking at a healthy ROCE somewhere in the range of, I will say, 18% to 20%, and we will prefer to maintain that level for these 2 projects.

items.statement: Ammonia EBITDA breakeven at $310-320/ton; current ammonia price ~$300/ton (Q4 avg ~$330/ton)
items.quote: As we continue to maintain, our EBITDA breakeven is around $310, $320, at that price, the PCL remain EBITDA breakeven.

items.statement: IPA faces near-term margin pressures due to oversupply and weak acetone prices; nitric acid well positioned with improving downstream demand from TAN
items.quote: Talking about outlook, nitric acid remains well positioned with improving downstream demand from TAN, while IPA faces some near -term margin pressures due to oversupply and weak Deepak Fertilisers and Acetone prices

items.statement: Working capital as % of revenue declined from 17% to 12% in FY25; generated INR 1,400 cr free operating cash flow
items.quote: Working capital as a percentage of revenue declined from 17% to 12%. Despite capital expenditure or CAPEX of around INR 1,100 crores in FY '25, net debt was reduced to INR 3,305 crores from INR 3,426 crores a year ago.

items.statement: Net debt reduced to INR 3,305 cr from INR 3,426 cr YoY; net debt/EBITDA improved from 2.66x to 1.72x; net debt/equity at 0.53x
items.quote: Despite capital expenditure or CAPEX of around INR 1,100 crores in FY '25, net debt was reduced to INR 3,305 crores from INR 3,426 crores a year ago. As a result, our net debt -to-EBITDA ratio improved significantly from 2.66x to 1.72x in this year. Net debt to equity now stands at healthy 0.53.

items.statement: Croptek volume more than doubled in Q4 (+111% YoY); specialty fertilizers (Bensulf, WSF) volume rose 13% YoY; CNB manufactured volume surged 55% to 888 Kt in FY25
items.quote: Our crop-focused specialty product, Croptek, more than doubled in its volume in Q4, up 111% Y-o-Y basis. Specialty fertilizers' volume, which includes Bensulf and WSF rose 13% Y -o-Y.

items.statement: LDAN (premium specialty) grew 13% sequentially and 11% YoY; B2C revenue share increased to 18% in Q4 FY25
items.quote: LDAN, our premium specialty offering recorded 13% sequential and 11% Y -o-Y growth, increasing the B2C revenue share to 18%.

items.statement: B2C model in TAN expanding via TCO (Total Cost of Ownership) partnerships with end consumers (mines, infra); provides value-based pricing, stickiness, market share gains
items.quote: All 3 actually, not just one. It gives me value -based pricing because the way our TCO model work, as we have explained earlier, we are moving towards productivity solutions to the end consumer. We are not just selling products. We are working as a partnership to them and showing we can improve their mines' productivity or infra productivity.

items.statement: TAN industry net short (demand 1.4M vs capacity 1M); new entrant capacity (Chambal, GNFC) will ramp gradually; import substitution headroom exists
items.quote: By the time, this capacity is actually available in the market, net-net, we will again start seeing import higher than the supply available. So, we don't see a challenge in the TAN demand.

items.statement: Long-term Equinor LNG contract to kick in FY26; gas price benefits to flow from FY26 onward with some lag due to multiple supply sources
items.quote: Currently, our gas prices are more I will say since our long-term Equinor contract yet to get kicked in and that will get kicked in only next year, FY '26, and that's where we will start seeing the real benefit of gas price reduction happening.

items.statement: CNB bulk fertilizers volume grew 68% YoY to 2.1 lakh MT in Q4; FY25 manufactured volume crossed 1 million MT milestone (888 Kt)
items.quote: For the full -year FY '25, we have crossed 1 million metric ton milestone, with manufactured volume surged from 55% to 888 Kt.

items.statement: Management perplexed by valuation gap: Mining business valued at ~INR 13,000 cr (12x EBITDA) vs total company at ~INR 17,000-18,000 cr; seeks better investor understanding of integrated value chain
items.quote: Recently, when we did the CCD negotiations on the basis of just the Mining business, DMSL, we were in a position to garner the funding at 12x EBITDA, which puts the valuation of just the Mining business to INR 13,000-odd crores, whereas in totality, Deepak Fertilisers is somewhere getting valued at INR 17,000-odd or INR 18,000-odd crores.

items.statement: FY26 revenue growth of 18-20% in existing businesses; smart meter revenue of INR400-500 crore; EBITDA margin target of 10-10.5%
items.quote: Looking ahead to FY '26, we anticipate strong revenue growth, projecting an 18% to 20% increase in all our existing businesses. The smart meter segment is set to play a very pivotal role and is expected to contribute significantly to our revenues in FY '26. We remain focused on strengthe ning our margins through sustained operational efficiency and disciplined executions across all divisions

items.statement: Second smart meter order of INR50 crore secured from leading AMISP; advanced talks with other AMISPs for follow-up orders
items.quote: we are happy to share that a second order worth INR50 crores for sma rt energy meters from a leading AMISP in India has been secured. This reflects strong momentum and g rowing trust in our customers in our technology. We are in advanced talks with various oth er AMISPs also and optimistic about follow-up orders

items.statement: INR192 crore order from BBMP for energy saver project with 8-month implementation and 7-year annuity collection
items.quote: We are also very pleased to announce INR192 crores order from Bangalo re Corporation, BBMP, marking our re-entry into energy saver project space. In partnership with Schnell Energy Limited, we will install our in-house energy management system and streetlight controllers and replace streetlights with energy-efficient LEDs across parts of

items.statement: INR50 crore smart meter order to be executed in Q1 and Q2 FY26; more orders expected in Q1 and Q2
items.quote: Yes, definitely, FY '26, we're not going to wait for the full year. I think we would be executing this as soon as we get the clearances from AMISPs. Mostly it will be split in this Q1 and maybe a little bit in Q2. Shridhar Jadhav: And sir, the guidance of INR500 crores... Rajesh Doraiswamy: And we expect more orders coming in Q1 as

items.statement: Smart meter capex completed; Saudi facility capex of ~INR10 crore pending space allocation expected this quarter or next; only major FY26 capex besides maintenance
items.quote: The capex for smart meters is done, is completed. We are all set to j ust take up the production and fulfil the capacity that we have set up. So, there's no more capex that's required for smart meters. On the Saudi, we have not done any capex so far. We're just waiting for the allocation of space by the Saudi Industrial Corporation called Once we the space is allocated, which we expect to happen a

items.statement: Current debtor cycle 85-90 days; smart meter cycle expected at 45-60 days (B2B to AMISPs, not DISCOMs); funded via short-term debt
items.quote: Sir, currently, our working capital cycle or debtor cycle is at aroun d 85 days right now, 85 to 90 days approximately on a gross sale level basis. And for smart meter, I expec t this to be around 45 to 60 days. It is not going to be 200, 250 days because as I already mentioned in this call to one of the earlier questions, we are not getting into selling for the DISCOMs, where it is an 8-year payb

items.statement: Board recommended dividend of INR2.5 per equity share (face value INR10) for FY25, subject to shareholder approval
items.quote: Happy to share that the Board of Directors has recommended a dividend of INR2.5 per equity share of face value of INR10 each. This is subject to shareholders' approval.

items.statement: Smart meter realization INR2,300-2,700 per meter depending on model; expect 5-6% premium over new entrants as established player
items.quote: On the realization, I think we -- there are a few models of meters available. So, the price ranges anywhere between INR2,300 to INR2,700, depending on the model. So, we are also selling at these price levels. On a comparative basis, if you ask me, I thi nk in any market, in any product, an established high-quality player will definitely demand a premium of 5% to 6

items.statement: Kaycee Industries subsidiary: FY25 revenue INR53 crore (+9% YoY), EBITDA INR9 crore (+27% YoY), PAT margin 11% vs 9% prior; FY26 growth projected at 18-20%
items.value: INR53 cr revenue, INR9 cr EBITDA, 11% PAT margin
items.quote: Kaycee's top line grew 9% year- on-year in FY '25 to INR53 crores from INR49 crores in the previous corresponding year. EBITDA grew 27% year- on-year to INR9 crores from INR 7 crores last year. PAT margins at Kaycee are remaining at a very healt hy pace. PAT margin at 11% in FY '25 as compared to 9% in FY '24. Looking ahead to FY '26, we anticipate strong revenue growth, projecting an 18% to 20% i

items.statement: Export sales expected to decline 10%-15% in FY26 due to tariff uncertainty
items.quote: We are generally expecting that export sales could be sluggish to the tune of around 10%-15%. That is our expectation.

items.statement: Export sales could be down 10%-20% for FY26 as a whole
items.quote: On exports, we can broadly say we are looking at something in the region of 10%-20% down for the year as a whole.

items.statement: Hoping for customer acquisitions adding Rs. 100 crores export sales in FY27 and FY28
items.quote: We are discussing with several customers and we are hoping for some customer acquisitions in the next few weeks and months, that should improve. It should add in at least Rs. 100 crores of export sales in FY '27 and FY '28.

items.statement: FY26 capex of Rs. 300 crores funded by internal accruals and Rs. 160 crores term loans for repayment
items.quote: Going forward, for the last year, we spent Rs. 340 crores last year. And this year, we expect to spend a total of Rs. 300 crores in terms of CAPEX and about Rs. 160 crores will fall due for repayment.

items.statement: Management will slow down capex given challenging export environment
items.quote: Yes, 100% we will not go hammer and tong from the CAPEX side, we will slow down.

items.statement: 16,500 ton press to be commissioned by September-December 2025, production from January 2026
items.quote: The press is expected to be commissioned by around September to December of this year, in Q3 of this fiscal, Q4 of this calendar and would start production from let us say, January onwards.

items.statement: No forging capacity added in FY25; 5,000 tons capacity addition slated for Q3-Q4 FY26
items.quote: FY '25, we have not added any forging capacity. We remain where we are, the 16,500 tons is slated to come into production this year and about 5000 tons of other capacity is getting added in this year, again in Q3-Q4.

items.statement: EBITDA margin reached 19.91% in FY25, effectively at 20% target
items.quote: So as we have been guiding, our EBITDA levels have been steadily improving and now stand at the cusp of the 20% mark.

items.statement: Machined components focus expected to improve EBITDA margins further
items.quote: This foray into or this accent and focus on machine products will definitely mean positive on the EBITDA side. I am not able to give you any numbers, but the sense is that it should improve EBITDA levels or worst case, at least counter the inflationary levels and add to stability of EBITDA.

items.statement: Machined components at 58% of sales, targeting 65%-70% medium term
items.quote: Sorry, I read the figures in the wrong column, 58% is machined, 42% is as forging.

items.statement: Top products: front axle beams, knuckles, crankshafts constitute ~40% of sales
items.quote: These three parts alone constitute roughly 40% of our sales.

items.statement: Heavy forgings (HF) share dropped from 44% to 36% of sales in FY25
items.quote: What we call as our HF production today constitutes 36% of our sales. It was 44% in FY '24, it has dropped down marginally to 36%.

items.statement: US truck movement down 30%-40%, new orders at all-time low since mid-April
items.quote: Overall terms, if you see American truck movement is down by about 30%-40%, so new orders for trucks have fallen to an all-time low in mid-April and onwards.

items.statement: Export markets sluggish; US and Europe slowdown impacted H2 FY25 exports
items.quote: We have seen a slight slowdown in the US and European markets and that has resulted in a reduced number.

items.statement: Since April 1, export order inflow knocked down, many schedules cancelled
items.quote: Since the 1st of April, Freedom Day or Liberation Day, we have had a total knock-on inflow of export orders and that is many schedules have been cancelled.

items.statement: Raw material price softening and lower heavy forging sales caused 8% realization per ton drop in FY25
items.quote: Largely related to the, one second, just hold on, the heavy tonnage parts have come down in the last one year, so that is one cause for drop in realization per ton plus raw material prices have softened in the last one year, steel prices that also result in reduced.

items.statement: Raw material cost is pass-through; steel price changes flow through to customers
items.quote: See, raw material is a pass through, so any change that takes place on account of steel will be a pass through. We can't do anything on it.

items.statement: India expected to secure favorable trade agreement with US; China tariffs seen at 20%-30%
items.quote: The broad expectation in the market is that India would probably end up with a freight trade agreement or close to that with the US. We would be very surprised if that didn't happen. And China, tariff would be in the region of 20%-30%.

items.statement: Net debt at Rs. 970 crores in FY25, expected to remain flat or reduce by Rs. 30-40 crores in FY26
items.quote: Net debt stands at Rs. 970 crores in FY '25 and I would say we would expect that to remain almost at those levels, maybe come down by around Rs. 30-Rs. 40 crores in the next year.

items.statement: Receivables increased due to higher Q4 sales; no change in credit terms or defaults
items.quote: There is no specific change on the field in terms of receivables, so this must be due to last-minute sales going up and therefore the receivables has short through because of higher sales in the 4th Quarter.

items.statement: Expect Rs. 20-40 crores from working capital improvements to fund FY26 capex
items.quote: One combination is from internal accruals, one source, which is the larger one and to some extent, we would be mopping up from a little bit of working capital improvements and savings there too. So about Rs. 20-Rs. 30 crores, I would expect to, at least Rs. 40 crores would come from that.

items.statement: No orders lost; no customer losses expected in coming months
items.quote: Answer your questions, reassuring on a positive point of view, no orders have been lost as of yet, as of now, and none are expected to be lost in the ensuing weeks and months.

items.statement: 90%-95% of new business wins are machined components
items.quote: Today, MM Forgings has very clearly transitioned from being a forging as forged part supplier to a component supplier and most of our new business, 90%-95% plus of the new business coming in is only in machine parts.

items.statement: EV component subsidiary (Abhinava Rizel) has zero revenue so far; expects something by Q4 FY26 or FY27
items.quote: And be candid, earlier I said FY '25 and now we are already in FY '26 and I have none to show. So I would have said something by Q4 of this year or FY '27.

items.statement: Asset turn on Rs. 700 crores cumulative capex expected at ~1x (Rs. 600-700 crores revenue)
items.quote: All this goes into production at customer or project anticipated capacity that should give rise to a production of around Rs. 600-Rs. 700 crores.

items.statement: Export outlook fraught with risk due to Trump administration trade policy changes
items.quote: At this point of time, hazarding a guess on export markets is very fraught with risk because of the Trump administration, bringing in very many changes to global trade and therefore one does not know how all this will break, how all this will develop into.

items.statement: FY26 revenue target Rs 600 crore; EBITDA margin 18-20%
items.quote: Yes, our target is Rs. 600 crores for the current financial year and expect to reach Rs. 1,000 crore turnover by 2030. And EBITDA margin is between 18% to 20% is our future.

items.statement: Order book to be maintained around Rs 800 crore with regular inflow
items.quote: Yes, this will be maintained . Around Rs. 800 crores order book will be maintained with the regular inflow of orders.

items.statement: Current order book Rs 750 crore (81% defense), executable in 18 months
items.quote: Total order book is Rs. 750 crores, which is, of course, the period of this is expected to be executed in a period of 18 months.

items.statement: Export order book ~Rs 100 crore, balance domestic
items.quote: It's about 100 crores of export and balance is domestic.

items.statement: LD provisions of ~Rs 35 crore on one contract; appeal filed for waiver
items.quote: As of date, it will be around Rs. 35 crores.

items.statement: RDX/HMX plant at Katepalli: civil works by August, commissioning by October
items.quote: And as on date, we still feel that by August we will be completing the civil works and then fabrication. And then commissioning of the plant and then production and all those are expected by October.

items.statement: Bulk explosives plants at ~30% utilisation; two Coal India plants idle
items.quote: Yes, not 50, you can say we are at 30% capacity.

items.statement: Emergency procurement inquiries from MoD; too early to comment on order inflows
items.quote: There are different emergency procurements that are going on, but I think it is too early to comment on that.

items.statement: Fire at Katepalli propellant mixer building; plant temporarily closed by PCB; revenue impact ~Rs 25-30 crore in FY26
items.quote: The total revenue from this is expected to be Rs. 25 crores to Rs. 30 crores of the total revenue. So that there will be effect on that amount.

items.statement: Plant closure notice for whole Katepalli facility; expect clearance by end of month
items.quote: Pollution Control Board has , as a practice , they have declared a closure notice, which is a regular procedure. First the debris has to be cleared and then they will see that it has caused any pollution.

items.statement: Signed JV and shareholders agreement with Global Munition Limited (NIBE Group) in March 2025
items.quote: we have also signed a joint venture agreement and shareholders agreement with Global Munition Limited, a subsidiary of Ordnance and Maritime Limited , NIBE Group Company, to manufacture defense and aerospace products.

items.statement: Sole qualified source for 100% of propellant/energetics for QRSAM/Akash; energetic component 10-15% of missile value
items.quote: The 100% requirement of propellants and energetics flows to Premier Explosives because as on date, we are the only qualified source.

items.statement: Inventories and payables rose with 54% revenue growth; current assets up similarly
items.quote: Last year turnover was Rs. 271 crores. This year it is Rs. 417 crores. Turnover has also gone up. Accordingly, inventories have also gone up.

items.statement: Chaff/flare order 60% complete by next month; full completion by Dec-Mar
items.quote: We will be completing around 60% of the order by next month. And by December to March, we will be completing the complete order.

items.statement: MRSAM order >500 units from BDL; hardware supply rate ~30/month limits execution
items.quote: MRSAM, we have order of more than 500 numbers from BDL. BDL is the only integrating agency and Premier is the only propellant supplying agency. Only thing is, we are dependent on the hardware as FIM from BDL. Right now they are providing us around 30 numbers per month hardware.

items.statement: Orissa plant land identified; forest patches being cleared by government; Phase 1 timeline intact
items.quote: It's going according to our plan only . See, the government Revenue department, they have their own pace of working. But still, they are quite fast comparatively. In the last meeting also, I have shared that the land is identified. There are some patches of forest land is there in that 500 acres, which the government is working on that.

items.statement: Exports industrial explosives to Thailand and Philippines; not defense exports to Philippines
items.quote: Philippines, we are not working directly with Philippines. We are exporting industrial explosives to Thailand and Philippines. Not the defense.

items.statement: Bulk explosives margins volatile due to raw material cost increases; cautious on Coal India tenders
items.quote: Since, we don't have any Coal India order, so they are now idle. Next, Coal India tender, when it comes, again, we will have to participate and see that because of the prices and all those, which our margins have become very low because of raw material costs have gone up there.

items.statement: FY25 cash profit Rs 40 crore; targeting Rs 500-600 crore revenue in FY26 despite fire impact
items.quote: Even after that we are targeting about Rs. 500 crores to Rs. 600 crores for the current financial year.

items.statement: Q4 FY25 total sales volume fell 24% YoY to 13,337 MT; FY25 total volume down 10.7% YoY to 67,543 MT
items.quote: In Q4 Financial Year '25, total sales volume were 13,337 metric tons as against 17,554 metric tons in Q4 Financial Year '24, which was a decrease of roughly 24% on a year-on-year basis.

items.statement: Agri segment volume declined 9% YoY in Q4 FY25 to 9,154 MT; grew 5% YoY in FY25 to 53,696 MT
items.quote: Agri segment; 9,154 metric ton, a decline of 9% on a year-on-year basis.

items.statement: Building products volume grew 18% YoY in Q4 FY25 to 2,513 MT; grew 30% YoY in FY25 to 9,185 MT
items.quote: Building products; 2,513 metric ton, a growth of 18% on year-on-year basis.

items.statement: Industrial segment volume fell 68% YoY in Q4 FY25 to 1,671 MT; fell 73% YoY in FY25 to 4,662 MT
items.quote: Industrial segment, which as a policy we are keeping our presence low, registered a sales volume of 1,671 metric ton, a decline of 68% year-on-year basis.

items.statement: Q4 FY25 EBITDA was INR 0.2 crore; net loss INR 4 crore
items.quote: The Company's EBITDA stood at about INR 0.2 crores. The Company reported a net loss of around INR 4 crores for the quarter.

items.statement: FY25 EBITDA was INR 28 crore with 3.93% margin, down 294 bps YoY; net loss INR 4 crore
items.quote: The EBITDA of the Company was about 28 crores with an EBITDA margin percentage of 3.93% which decreased 294 basis points on year-on-year basis.

items.statement: Management targets EBITDA margin improvement towards 10% going forward; building products expected to offer better margins than agriculture
items.quote: We certainly see improvement in margins going forward. And we must be able to improve them towards, I mean, 10% around going forward.

items.statement: Agriculture market expected to grow at 8-10% range due to planned irrigation expansion
items.quote: So the agricultural market will keep growing at about 8% to 10% range, which is very clear because still there is a lot of area to be brought under, I mean, planned irrigation.

items.statement: Of Rs 55 crore raised, ~Rs 10 crore spent on capex so far; further plans in final stages
items.quote: So far, out of Rs. 55 crores raised, approximately Rs. 10 crores have been spent on capital expenditures. The rest of the plans are in discussion and in final stages.

items.statement: Total capex invested ~Rs 38-39 crore recently, focused on building material and column pipes; further investment planned for capacity, range and offerings
items.quote: And more than, I mean, we have invested, put together about 38 crore, 39 crore of CAPEX. And we are further going to invest for augmenting not only our capacity, but improving our range and our offerings.

items.statement: New facilities planned in regional markets to grow agri business; building material expansion in existing and new markets
items.quote: Yes, that's very much on cards and that's where we are planning some initiatives. As soon as they are finalized, we will keep you updated on that.

items.statement: Agri segment: ~80% PVC, HDPE (sprinklers/coils) gaining traction but smaller; building products focus increasing
items.quote: Exact numbers I would not have, but majority of portion, about 80% will be there. But majority is PVC. And HDPE is gaining traction, but it takes a long time to come to equivalent to PVC.

items.statement: Strong in MP, Rajasthan, Maharashtra with >40% market share in core areas; expanding to new regions
items.quote: In the areas where we are strong, we hold over 40% market share single-handedly. I mean, there are no specific numbers, but this is a general estimated number.

items.statement: Retained market share despite large competitors; differentiating via distribution, service, product range, ATL/BTL marketing
items.quote: And we have always retained our market share. Rather our data suggests that in this area we are now working towards improving our market share which is already at a higher side as compared to anyone else.

items.statement: Raw material prices now stable after prolonged decline; marginal price increase seen recently from manufacturers
items.quote: Redeeming feature is that after a long time raw material prices look to be stable. Not only that, recently we have seen one incidence of marginal price increase by the raw material manufacturers.

items.statement: PVC price pass-through to distributors within 24 hours of raw material price changes
items.quote: Normally within 24 hours it is communicated to everyone about the changes.

items.statement: PVC sourcing: 72% domestic (mainly Reliance), 20% imported; ADD outcome uncertain due to court proceedings; balancing local and import procurement
items.quote: ADD still no clarity because it's been through courts and courts had intervened. So till courts resolve the subject nothing clearly can be known.

items.statement: Extrusion machinery sourced domestically from Indian units of multinational manufacturers; no imports needed currently
items.quote: No, today fortunately in extrusion side India has few good manufacturers. All the multinationals have their plant here, the recognized internationally good extrusion manufacturers. So we are normally buying from them.

items.statement: Agri: cash-and-carry; Building products: controlled credit; Industrial: against letter of credit
items.quote: Agri is a cash and carry. BP is a credit which is controlled.

items.statement: Micro-irrigation (subsidy-based) not scaled; company stays away from government subsidy-driven business
items.quote: Most of business is related to government because this is all subsidy-based business and we as a Company have chosen to stay away from such businesses.

items.statement: Board approved 1:4 bonus shares and INR2 per share dividend (40%), taking total dividend to INR11.50 (230% on INR5 face value)
items.quote: I am glad to announce that Board of Directors has approved the bonus share 1:4, 1 share for every 4 shares in the meeting concluded yesterday. And we have announced a dividend of INR2 per share, that is 40% dividend for this quarter, and it takes the total dividend to INR11.50 at a share value of INR5, that is 230%.

items.statement: FY25 throughput reached 5.09 million TEUs, up 8% YoY (EXIM +7%, domestic +12%)
items.quote: CONCOR achieved ever highest throughput of 5.09 million TEUs, crossing the 5 million TEUs mark for the first time in its history. Throughput growth has been around 8% in the financial year.

items.statement: FY26 guidance: EXIM volume growth 10%, domestic 20%, overall combined 13%
items.quote: So at this moment, I would like to give guidance for FY '26. In EXIM, I am giving guidance of 10% growth, in domestic 20% growth. So overall, there will be 13% growth in this financial year in overall business combined EXIM and domestic.

items.statement: FY25 capex INR810 crore; FY26 capex budget approved at INR860 crore for containers, wagons, terminals, IT
items.quote: And all this was possible, and we achieved capex of INR810 crores in FY '25. For FY '26, Board of Directors have approved capex budget of INR860 crores, which will be primarily used for procuring containers, procuring wagons, development of terminals for -- and for management of management information system, that is IT equipments.

items.statement: Target by 2028: 100 terminals, 500+ rakes, 70,000 containers; FY25 added 11 rakes (total 388) and ~9,000 containers (fleet >53,000)
items.quote: Company has embarked on massive infrastructure creation after seeing the robust demand. By 2028, we have set a target of 100 terminals, 500-plus rakes and 70,000 containers of our own.

items.statement: Rail freight margin improved 55 bps to 25.65%; operating margin ~30% and EBITDA margin ~25% maintained YoY
items.quote: And one important thing is we have gained market share and despite not sacrificing our margins. In fact, our rail freight margin has increased by 55 basis points. So market share has also increased and rail freight margin has also increased from 25.10% to 25.65%.

items.statement: EXIM stable; domestic robust demand expected for bulk cement, tank containers, ceramic tiles, food grain; WDFC commissioning to JNPT by Dec 2025 to spur Q4 volumes
items.quote: As far as outlook for FY '26 is concerned, we see stability in EXIM business and with commissioning of WDFC up to JNPT by December 2025. We see a spurt in volumes in Q4 of this financial year. On domestic front, there is a robust demand. We expect good volumes of bulk cement and tank containers, ceramic tiles, food grain, etc.

items.statement: Pan-India EXIM market share up 40 bps to 55.2%; JNPT +9 bps to 58.44%, Mundra +127 bps to 37.7%, Pipavav +232 bps to 48.4%
items.quote: I also want to highlight that in EXIM, we have increased the market share on Pan-India basis by 40 basis points, JNPT only 9 basis points, Mundra port 127 basis points, Pipavav port 232 basis points.

items.statement: Double-stack rakes grew 16% to 6,302 in FY25; new wagon technology (80t payload) to further boost double-stacking
items.quote: We have seen a 16% growth in double-stack handling of rakes. This year, we crossed 6,000 rakes. We achieved 6,302 double-stack rakes this year. Last year, it was 5,440. So there was a growth of 16%.

items.statement: Signed agreements with UltraTech and My Home Cement for silos at Dronagiri; 20 shipping lines signed long-term agreements covering nearly all EXIM volume; talks with Vedanta, Jindal, JK Group, Tata, SAIL for domestic
items.quote: And one more thing on bulk cement front, we have signed agreement with 2 leading cement manufacturers, UltraTech Cement and My Home cement, where we have given 2 acre land each to them in our terminal at Dronagiri at Mumbai, and they will be setting up silos.

items.statement: Land licence fee (LLF) FY25 net INR370 crore (Q4 INR108 crore); FY26 expected similar net impact despite 7% gross increase due to land surrender
items.quote: FY '26 also, it will be in the same range, even though it will increase by 7%, but we are constantly working on surrendering the terminals that we don't need or the land within terminals that we don't need. So net impact will be around this number only.

items.statement: Empty running cost reduced 5.3% YoY to INR408 crore (EXIM INR121.3 cr, domestic INR286.7 cr); EXIM lead 701 km, domestic 1,321 km
items.quote: Empty running in this financial year was EXIM, it is INR121.3 crores. Domestic, it is INR286.7 crores and total was INR408 crores. And in both EXIM and domestic, it is less than last financial year. EXIM, it is reduced by 6.4%. Domestic, it is reduced by 5% and there's a total reduction of 5.3% in empty running.

items.statement: DPD (direct port delivery) and transshipment volumes cited as key reasons for rail coefficient decline at JNPT (15.7%), Mundra (24%), Pipavav (57.8%)
items.quote: primary reason is DPD. Are you familiar? What is DPD? Shreeji Kalekar: Yes, direct port delivery, right? Sanjay Swarup: Direct port delivery. So DPD is primarily moving by road. It is not moving by rail. This is first. And second reason is the port volumes include transshipment volumes also

items.statement: Four new terminals targeted for commissioning in FY26: Salawas (Jodhpur), Pathri (Haridwar), Mandalgarh (Bhilwara/Kota), Chunar (Varanasi)
items.quote: In this financial year, we have set up a target of commissioning 4 new terminals, and we are actively working with railways and DFC for getting land for setting up more terminals so that we are able to achieve the target of 100 terminals by 2028.

items.statement: Received 90 tank containers from Braithwaite; trial loading underway; expects stabilization by first week of June; tender floated for 500 more
items.quote: Actually, we have already received 90 containers from Braithwaite that are sufficient to form a rake. Now these containers are under trial loading at one of the cement plants. So we are quite hopeful of a breakthrough. So because for the first time they are being loaded, so you will appreciate that there is a teething issue. So people are working on it. Our officers are also working. Braithwaite o

items.statement: EBITDA margin target 24-25%+ for FY26; Q4 EXIM margin dip due to year-end volume discount settlements
items.quote: As I told you, we are able to maintain EBITDA level of 24% to 25% every year and despite growing also and -- which is quite good in logistics business. Normally, it is in single digit. So we will be able to maintain this business going forward.

items.statement: WDFC to JNPT commissioning by Dec 2025 critical for EXIM guidance; management confident no further delay
items.quote: It will not get delayed. It will be on time.

items.statement: Domestic realization expected slightly above FY25; overall EBITDA 24-25%+; tank container empty return cost covered by 5-year railway incentive and notified rates
items.quote: Yes, you can say it will be slightly more than FY '25. And overall EBITDA will be 24%, 25% or even more than that.

items.statement: EXIM trade: exports growing faster than imports currently; shipping lines indicate stabilized outlook for FY26
items.quote: At present, exports are very good as compared to imports. It keeps on happening. So -- but that is not an issue. We are able to overcome that challenge by increasing our double-stacking. So EXIM guidance of 10%, I find it quite achievable.

items.statement: Container fleet now fully owned at 53,000+; no leased containers
items.quote: It is all own container. Now there's no lease container.

items.statement: Coastal shipping MOU with SCI signed but no commercial breakthrough yet due to unfavorable rates
items.quote: We have signed an MOU with Shipping Corporation of India for coastal movement also. But till now, we are not able to achieve any breakthrough because of the various rates that we worked out and we shared with the trade. It was not favorable to them.

items.statement: JNPT rail coefficient 15.7% (FY24 16.6%); Mundra 24% (FY24 25.5%); Pipavav 57.8% (FY24 62.4%)
items.quote: JNPT last year, it was 16.6%. This year, it is 15.7%. Mundra last year, it was 25.5%. This year, it is 24%. Pipavav last year, it was 62.4%. This year, it is 57.8%.

items.statement: Rail coefficient at JNPT expected to double to ~30-35% within 1-1.5 years post WDFC commissioning
items.quote: I'm very optimistic that this rail coefficient will double.

items.statement: DFC double-stacking to enable cost savings on upper deck; part of savings to be passed to customers without margin sacrifice; light cargo to shift from road to rail
items.quote: When we run on -- train on DFC, all will be double-stack trains. For upper deck, there will be substantial cost saving. So without sacrificing my margins, I will share a part of these savings with my customers. And the light cargo, which is at present not coming to rail, it is moving by road. All this light cargo will come to rail.

items.statement: Depreciation impact: wagon life extended 15 to 30 years; Q4 impact INR13 crore (full year INR92 crore vs INR79 crore in Q3); deferred tax up, current tax down
items.quote: Depreciation, like in the last quarter, as you know, we have increased the life of our wagons from 15 years to 30 years. So that had an impact of INR79 crores in the December period. And if you see in the March period, the total impact is INR92 crores. So the impact in the March quarter is around INR13 crores because of that.

items.statement: FY26 revenue growth expected 15-20% driven by watch market recovery, precision engineering growth, and bracelet and packaging utilization
items.quote: In FY '26, we expect our revenue to grow in the range of 15% to 20%, majorly driven by recovery in the international watch market, growth of our precision engineering business and enhancement in the utilization and growth of the bracelet and packaging businesses.

items.statement: Standalone EBITDA margin expected to remain broadly similar to FY25's 23% in coming years
items.quote: The last year, our EBITDA margins was around 23%. And with the growth estimated in the range of 15% to 20% and majorly driven from the precision engineering, recovery into the watch component business as well as the bracelet and the packaging business, we expect the EBITDA margins to remain broadly in the similar range in the coming years.

items.statement: Anticipate gradual revival in international watch market beginning second half of FY26
items.quote: Based on current indicators and market feedback, we anticipate a gradual revival, beginning in the second half of FY '26.

items.statement: Standalone Q4 FY25 EBITDA margin 19%, full year 23.1%; consolidated full year EBITDA margin 18.1%
items.quote: EBITDA for quarter 4 stood at INR19.4 crores, with an EBITDA margin of 19%, while for FY '25 full year, EBITDA was INR88.5 crores -- and EBITDA margin of 23.1%.

items.statement: Precision engineering long-term growth indication maintained at 25% range; order positions for coming year already in place
items.quote: In our earlier calls, we have given a long-term indication for the precision engineering business where the growth of business will -- over the longer period, will be in the range of 25%. So we still maintain that. And accordingly, the order positions for getting that type of growth in the coming year are already there.

items.statement: FY25 capex INR30 crore; FY26 expected capex INR35 crore
items.quote: During the last year, financial year '25, we incurred a capex of around INR30 crores. And in the coming year, we expect to do a further capex of around INR35 crore.

items.statement: Bracelet capacity utilization at 50%, targeting 65% in FY26; capacity enhancement planned by end of fiscal year to ~90,000 units
items.quote: At present, the capacity utilization stands at about 50%, indicating substantial headroom for growth. With continuous improvements in operational efficiency and recovery of the market conditions, we anticipate capacity utilization rising to about 65% in FY '26.

items.statement: Packaging new unit capacity utilization expected to reach 60-70% in FY26
items.quote: The new unit has been established, which came into production, I think, in October. And here I think we will get also close to 60% or 70% capacity utilization during this year.

items.statement: Watch component export revenue declined 28%, domestic grew 13%; precision engineering revenue grew 55% to INR147 crore
items.quote: The total revenue of our watch component business comprising of watch hands and watch dials declined by nearly 20% compared to the previous year majorly due t o a decline in export revenue by 28%, whereas the domestic market revenue grew by 13% during the year

items.statement: Precision engineering FY25 revenue INR147 crore, up 55% YoY
items.quote: I am pleased to share that, in FY '25, we recorded a 55% year-on-year growth in revenue, taking our top line to INR147

items.statement: Bracelet division currently serves one customer (LVMH group); plans to add more customers as production expands
items.quote: right now we have that customer. We have that one customer. As our production expands, we are free to go to other custom ers, provided this one customer able to meet -- or we produce more than the needs of this customer, which could happen this year, but let's see how much this customer will actually lift

items.statement: Precision engineering adding new customers, segments, geographies; not dependent on single customer
items.quote: This is part and parcel of the business. We keep adding new customers, new segments, new geographies. I think it is not dependent only on one customer.

items.statement: Rupee-to-Swiss franc fluctuations favorable for watch component business
items.quote: The recent Indian rupee -to-Swiss franc currency fluctuations have been favorable for our company.

items.statement: Actively exploring non-Swiss European geographies (Germany, Scandinavia) and other markets to hedge Swiss watch exposure
items.quote: We are already sort of working on expanding our offering to some geographies that are not as impacted as the Swiss watch market. For example, the German -- the emerging watchmaking in Germany, in Scandinavia and some other interesting geographies.

items.statement: Packaging division targeting 20%+ CAGR revenue growth for next 5-10 years
items.quote: The revenue numbers again we are looking at growth upward of 20% CAGR. And I think this is sustainable for a good 5 to 10 years in the future anyways.

items.statement: Silvercity Brands (Favre Leuba) loss in FY25 below budget; FY26 loss expected but diminishing; breakeven targeted FY28
items.quote: There will still be a l oss, for sure. I'm not able to quantify the loss exactly, but it is as planned. It's part -- to be honest: There will be a loss this year. And there will be a diminished loss next year, but that's part of building a brand globally. And I think, from FY '28 onwards, it will start to -- the loss will disappear

items.statement: China Plus One strategy remains structural; India must move fast on approvals and technology to capture opportunity
items.quote: China Plus One is a reality. Now suddenly it has become -- because of the Trump policies and so on, it has become hot again. Tomorrow, there may be a deal between China and America. It will become -- it will cool down again, so we can't go on a quarterly basis.

items.statement: Factory visits for analysts and shareholders to be organized with SGA
items.quote: Yes, we will organize visit to our factories. We very much like to welcome analysts, shareholders. I think it's important to understand the business and it makes the whole interaction much more meaningful. So we will plan that with SGA.

items.statement: FY26 revenue growth guided at 8-12% with operating leverage; mid-teens growth projected for subsequent periods
items.quote: For FY '26, we expect to achieve revenue growth of 8% to 12% , with operating leverage. While macro risks persist, we are well positioned to navigate them thanks to our low cost vertically integrated model , and high agility. For subsequent periods, we project revenue growth in the mid teens range with operating leverage.

items.statement: FY26 gross margin guided at 62-63%
items.quote: Yes. So at the guidance level, we want to give between 62 % to 63% gross margin guidance for this current financial year FY '26, but will be operating in leverage coming from our HR SG&A line items, because we are seeing a lot of optimization happening in HR area with AI, with talent initiatives that we have across the whole organization.

items.statement: Content broadcasting cost guided at 18-19% of revenue for FY26
items.quote: But definitely this number will not be below for the next financial year , either it will be 18% to 19%, I can give the range for the next year, it will be the content broadcasting cost.

items.statement: Germany expected to be EBITDA positive in FY26 after $2-3M loss in FY25; Ideal World expected ~20% growth and ~1% EBITDA margin in FY26
items.quote: So for second-half, both of these units have done EBITDA breakeven. And first half of the year, both of the units have done EBITDA losses. The full financial year, we expect that the EBITDA margin from Germany operation will be in positive territory, which is right now around $2 million, $3 million losses that we have seen in the Germany operation in full financial year, that will be resulted in o

items.statement: Ideal World expected to reach company-average EBITDA margins by FY27; Germany expected EBIT positive by FY27 but margin guidance premature
items.quote: So let me just clarify, this is Sunil. Ideal World should be there in FY '27. Germany is still new, so to give a guidance of 8% to 10% kind of EBITDA in FY '27 is too premature. But what I can say is there will be EBITDA positive in FY '26 which we were negative almost $3 million. So that will help the group profitability by, I believe, 1.5 to 2 percentage point s average. But we will be EBITDA po

items.statement: US retail demand subdued in Jan due to tariff concerns; Feb-Mar showed improvement especially in e-commerce; 1% US growth reflects market share gain
items.quote: In the US, retail demand was subdued in January due to economic uncertainty and tariff concerns. February and March showed signs of improvement, particularly in e-commerce. A 1% growth in the US, while modest, reflects market share gain amid a challenging environment.

items.statement: UK retail challenging due to economic uncertainty and cautious consumer spending; Ideal World showed strong growth offsetting TJC softness
items.quote: The UK retail industry has continued to face a challenging environment, with growth held back by economic uncertainty and cautious consumer spending. While this a ffected TJC, the Ideal World continued to show strong growth and help support UK performance.

items.statement: Germany gained market share, maintained EBITDA breakeven in Q4; confident of better profitability in FY26
items.quote: Germany continued to gain market share, maintaining EBITDA breakeven for this current quarter as well. We are confident about achieving better profitability in FY '26. Notably, this has been a much faster turnaround than we experienced in the US and UK when we launched there originally, thanks to our past retail learnings.

items.statement: Current US business tracking mid-single digit growth for first 1.5 months of Q1 FY26; full-year guidance 8-12% accounts for uncertainty
items.quote: We are faring better than many other, for example, one of our peer just declared yesterday their negative comps after a very long time . And we are reading about negative comps, but our business is currently about mid-single digit growth level for the first one and a half month so far. So we are seeing about mid-single digit growth for US business for this quarter for us, for the year it's too ear

items.statement: Q4 gross margin 62.1%, FY25 gross margin 63.1%; target range +62% maintained via vertically integrated supply chain
items.quote: Our gross margin for the quarter remained robust at 62.1%, with a cumulative margin of 63.1% for the full year. We continue to see strong gross margins in our target range of +62%, backed by global supply chain.
