items.statement: Wholesale pharmacy segment expected to turn profitable from Q1 FY26
items.quote: We are confident that this will lead to a profitable turnover in wholesale pharmacy segment starting Q1 FY26.

items.statement: Quality Care Synergy Wheel initiatives to contribute INR 50-60 crores EBITDA with INR 20 crores run rate in Q4 FY25
items.quote: This year, we embarked on prioritizing our Synergy Wheel with five key Synergy initiatives, which will contribute INR 50 to 60 crores in EBITDA, with INR 20 crores as run rate for Q4 FY25.

items.statement: FY25 capex investment of INR 342 crores
items.quote: We have made a capital expenditure investment of INR 342 crores while maintaining our gross debt at lower levels than the last year at INR 642 crores.

items.statement: Organic expansion of over 2,100 beds to increase total network capacity to 7,300 beds funded through internal accruals
items.quote: Our upcoming organic expansion includes over 2,100 beds, which will increase our total network capacity to 7,300 beds. I want to highlight that this expansion will be funded through internal accruals and existing cash reserves without putting pressure on our balance sheet.

items.statement: Bengaluru expansion of 939 beds including 350 at CMI, 159 at Whitefield, 430 at new Sarjapur hospital (300 by H2 FY27, 130 by FY29)
items.quote: In Bengaluru, Aster will add a total of 939 beds, including 350 beds at Aster CMI hospitals, another 159 beds at Aster Whitefield, and 430 beds at the newly announced fourth hospital on Sarjapur Road, with 300 beds expected by H2 of FY27 and the remaining 130 beds by F Y29.

items.statement: Kerala to add 818 beds over next three years via Aster Kasargod (264) and Aster Capital Trivandrum (454); Hyderabad 300-bed Women and Children Hospital planned
items.quote: In Kerala, we will add 818 beds over the next three years with two major greenfield projects, Aster Kasargod, a 264-bed hospital, and Aster Capital in Trivandrum, a 454-bed facility, and in Hyderabad, a 300-bed state of the art Women and Children Hospital are planned to be commissioned.

items.statement: Quality Care to add 1,200 new beds over next three years (25% increase); Hyderabad cluster to add ~200 beds (100 at Malakpet, 80-90 at Banjara)
items.quote: In terms of network expansion, we are on track to add 1,200 new beds over the next three years, a 25% increase in capacity.

items.statement: FY25 operating EBITDA margin expanded to 19.5% from 16.8% in FY24; Q4 FY25 margin 19.3% vs 17.1%
items.quote: Operating EBITDA grew by 30% reaching INR 806 crores, with EBITDA margins expanding to 19.5% in FY25, up from 16.8% just a year ago.

items.statement: Hospital business EBITDA margin improved to 21.9% in FY25 from 19.5%; mature hospitals (>6 years) margin 24.3% with ROCE 34%
items.quote: Our hospital business continues to perform well with operating EBITDA margin improving to 21.9% in FY25, up from 19.5% last year. Specifically, our mature hospitals, those that have been operational for more than six years, have expanded their EBITDA margin to 24.3% in FY25, up from 22.4% a year ago with the return of capital employed of 34%.

items.statement: Karnataka-Maharashtra cluster EBITDA margin expanded to 28.8% in FY25 from 19.7%; Kerala cluster margin 23.4% vs 21.4%; Andhra-Telangana margin 12.7% vs 10%
items.quote: operating EBITDA margin expanded to 28.8% in FY25, up from 19.7% in the previous year

items.statement: Lab business turned EBITDA positive ~8% margin in FY25 after break-even in Q4 FY24
items.quote: Our lab business has demonstrated a strong performance, achieving 12% year-on-year growth of revenue in FY25, while maintaining a positive EBITDA margin of around 8% post-break-even in Q4 FY24.

items.statement: Manpower cost streamlined by ~70 bps in key functional areas via span of control enhancement
items.quote: We have further streamlined our manpower cost by approximately 70 basis points within key functional areas. This has been achieved by enhancing the span of control, allowing us to manage teams more efficiently and reduce supervisory layers, ultimately improving organization productivity and cost effectiveness.

items.statement: FY25 revenue grew 12% to INR 4,138 crores driven by 7% inpatient volume growth and 12% ARPOB increase; ALOS improved 6%
items.quote: Our overall business recorded a 12% revenue growth reaching INR 4,138 crores in full year FY25. This was driven by a 7% increase in in-patient volume and a 12% year-on-year increase in ARPOB, with an improvement in ALOS by 6%, reflecting much better clinical protocols.

items.statement: Q4 FY25 revenue INR 1,000 crores (+2% YoY) impacted by Kerala Ramadan, fewer days in Feb, lower international patients; core hospital revenue grew 4%
items.quote: During Q4 FY25, we witnessed revenue reaching INR 1,000 crores, up by 2% year-on-year, factoring revenue impact in the Kerala cluster, primarily due to a full month impact of Ramadan in March, a lesser day in February, and lower international patient volumes.

items.statement: Karnataka-Maharashtra cluster revenue grew 28% to INR 1,408 crores; Kerala cluster +5% to INR 2,108 crores; Andhra-Telangana +15% to INR 473 crores
items.quote: Starting with Karnataka and Maharashtra cluster, this cluster has demonstrated significant progress with a total bed capacity of 1,479 beds and 1,014 beds operational census beds. Occupancy has improved by 90 basis points year on year, rising from 61% to 62% in FY25. Especially when it comes to revenue for Karnataka and Maharashtra cluster, it grew impressively by 28% year on year, reaching 1,408

items.statement: Quality Care revenue grew 12% YoY in 2025; Q4 FY25 revenue +12%, EBITDA +16% driven by 10% inpatient ARPOB growth
items.quote: Quality Care delivered strong financial growth in 2025. Revenue increased by 12% year on year, EBITDA rose by 14%. In Q4 FY25, the revenue growth was 12% compared to Q4 FY24, while EBITDA grew 16% due to the impact of our strategic initiatives.

items.statement: Combined pro forma FY25 revenue INR 8,105 crores and adjusted EBITDA INR 1,661 crores (20.5% margin) post-merger
items.quote: For FY25, the combined entity reported a pro forma revenue of 8,105 crores and an adjusted EBITDA of 1,661 crores, translating to a healthy EBITDA margin of 20.5%.

items.statement: Merger with Quality Care: shareholders approved preferential issuance, CCI approval received, 5% stake swap completed, awaits stock exchange and NCLT approval
items.quote: Shareholders have approved the preferential issuance of shares. The CCI have granted the approval. We have also completed a strategic share swap: Aster acquired a 5% stake in QCIL in exchange for a 3.6% preferential allotment.

items.statement: Combined entity to have 38 hospitals, 10,300+ beds across 27 cities post-merger
items.quote: Through the merger with Aster DM Healthcare, the combined entity will emerge as one of India's top three hospital networks, with 38 hospitals and over 10,300 beds across 27 cities.

items.statement: Gross debt reduced to INR 642 crores; net cash position INR 739 crores; promoter pledge reduced from 99% to 41% after debt refinancing
items.quote: We have made a capital expenditure investment of INR 342 crores while maintaining our gross debt at lower levels than the last year at INR 642 crores. We continue to operate from a net cash position of INR 739 crores, leaving for reinforcing our strong balance sheet.

items.statement: Promoters reduced pledge from 99% to 41% after debt refinancing with top-tier global financial institution
items.quote: In line with our strategy, the promoters of Aster DM Healthcare have successfully reduced their pledge from 99% to 41% after completing a debt refinancing transaction with top tier global financial institution.

items.statement: ROCE improved over 300 bps to 19.5% in FY25 from 16.4%; core hospitals ROCE >25%
items.quote: Furthermore, we are pleased to report an improvement of over 300 basis points in ROCE, from 16.4% in the last year to 19.5% in the current year. Most notably, our core hospitals now operate at ROCE of over 25%.

items.statement: ARPOB increased 12% in FY25 driven by 6% ALOS improvement, specialty growth, and case mix shift
items.quote: ARPOB increased by 12% driven by multiple levers, a 6% improvement in ALOS, strong growth from Aster Whitefield Hospital and impressive performance across key specialties such as oncology, neurosciences and cardiology.

items.statement: Occupancy: Karnataka-Maharashtra 62% (+90 bps), Kerala 71%, Andhra-Telangana 54% (+460 bps)
items.quote: Occupancy has improved by 90 basis points year on year, rising from 61% to 62% in FY25.

items.statement: Kerala Q4 impact: ~2.5-3% revenue hit from full-month Ramadan in March vs partial last year; leadership transition at flagship Medcity
items.quote: So, when we look at Q4, definitely, all of March was Ramadan, and when it comes to MVT specifically, people usually start planning a few weeks in advance, right? So, we believe that almost 2.5%-3% of the revenue hit has been caused because of the Ramadan impact.

items.statement: Specialty mix diversified: no single specialty >15% of revenue; high-end treatments driving growth (oncology, neurosciences, cardiology, robotic surgery)
items.quote: Our strategic focus on a well-diversified specialty mix ensures that no single specialty accounts for more than 15% of the total revenue. This enhances our resilience and strengthens our long-term growth prospects in the healthcare sector.

items.statement: Medical tourism (MVT) re-engaging partners in key geographies, expanding to Africa and Southeast Asia via digital strategy and referral network
items.quote: On the MVT front, we are actively re-engaging with partners in key geographies and expanding our outreach into newer markets such as Africa and Southeast Asia by a more structured digital engagement strategy and an enhanced referral partner network.

items.statement: Quality Care hired 8 senior leaders including Group CFO, CTO, CHRO; Kerala leadership strengthened with new CEO, COO at Medcity
items.quote: Over the past year, we welcomed eight senior level leaders, including our group CFO, CTO, and CHRO, key appointments that will strengthen our leadership foundation.

items.statement: Targets 23-24% EBITDA margin at group level in next 3-4 years including QCIL synergies
items.quote: we are also aiming to reach 23-24% in next 3-4 years' timeline. So, we are very much committed in this regard.

items.statement: Expects 7-8% volume growth and 7-8% ARPOB growth going forward
items.quote: When we say that we grown at mid-teens, at least 7-8% will be with volumes and balance 7-8% will come from the ARPOB. Now volumes is something which we are very, very confident that will continue to grow at around 7-8% going forward.

items.statement: Q4 FY25 EBITDA margin at 19.3%, consistent with Q3; full-year margin improvement from 15-17% to 19%+ range
items.quote: if you look at the all the four quarters EBITDA margin we started with a 17 plus margin then we bounced in Q2 to more than 21% and Q3 also we closed at 19.3%, Q4 also it's 19.3% right

items.statement: Identifies 300-400 bps further margin improvement from material cost leverage, manpower efficiency, functional consolidation and overheads
items.quote: I think all these things put together; we should be able to look at another 300 to 400 bps improvement in the margins.

items.statement: Hospital segment EBITDA margin expected 100-200 bps above group 23-24% target
items.quote: I think overall, 23-24% and I think maybe another 100, 200 bps higher it should be for the hospital segment.

items.statement: 2,100 beds in pipeline costing ~INR 1,900 crore; INR 350-400 crore already spent; balance INR 1,500 crore over next 3-4 years
items.quote: We have 2,100 beds in pipeline, which will cost me approximately INR 1,900 crores. Out of INR 1,900 crores, we already incurred INR 350 to 400 crores. So, balance INR 1,500 crores, which we need to spend over a period of next three to four years

items.statement: Added 300 beds in Q4 FY25 (200 in Kerala); Mother & Child hospital (159 beds) in Whitefield coming up in FY26; Kasaragod hospital in FY26; Hyderabad women & child hospital in Q2 FY27
items.quote: we've added 300 beds out of that 200 beds in the last quarter have been in Kerala. So naturally, arithmetically, there'll be some dips that you will see.

items.statement: Hyderabad women & child hospital delayed to Q2 FY27 due to warm shell infrastructure work
items.quote: We'll be able to ensure that we could kick off the project and by 2027 we are very positive. At least the second quarter at least we should be able to kickstart the hospital.

items.statement: Q4 FY25 core hospital revenue grew 4%; 2% dip from conscious wholesale pharmacy reduction; 2.5-3% impact from Ramadan timing shift
items.quote: if you remove but only look at the hospital space, right, in the core entity, it has grown 4%. The other 2% dip has happened because we consciously reduced the wholesale pharmacy segment.

items.statement: MVT business reduced consciously in Maldives due to receivables risk; expanding into African countries and Iraq; oncology focus for MVT
items.quote: Maldives, we've seen major ramp up in the business in last year and we have also seen that they are not very good paymasters. We had to control the receivables and that's where you also see in the Q4 because we were able to reduce the Maldives, the business very consciously.

items.statement: DSO reduced from 85-90 days to below 80 days in Q4; ECL provisions improved
items.quote: Overall, our receivables used to be at somewhere 85 to 90 days DSO. We are able to reduce to below 80 days and because of which our ECL, the provisions have become better in Q4.

items.statement: QCIL to fund ~70% of expansion capex via debt at entity level
items.quote: we're looking at raising some debt at the entity level. And my sense currently, I may not have the exact numbers, is about 70% of what we'll invest in the project, CapEx

items.statement: Price hike of 3-3.5% planned for FY26 across payor mix; insurance contracts renewed every two years
items.quote: on the price increase, usually whatever the ARPOB growth what we achieve, the price increase would be somewhere between 3 - 3.5%.

items.statement: Procurement synergies driving material cost leverage; targeting 100 bps from volume doubling; 30-32 MW solar plants coming in H2 FY26
items.quote: We are already in the way to bring more than, I think, 30-32 megawatt plants, which is in the works today. So that is something which is going to kick in sometime in the second half of the year.

items.statement: Hired ~10 senior leaders including regional CEOs, group CFO, CHRO, HR head, sales & marketing head for Care, regional CEO for KIMS business
items.quote: In total, actually 10 odd people have come on board. Each one of them, you know, have a great pedigree, given what they've done in the past.

items.statement: Greenfield hospitals break-even at ~30% occupancy; Bangalore third hospital broke even in 3 months vs 18 months for first
items.quote: it's usually 30% you should be able to break-even Nikhil. I'm talking about on a full capacity basis if it's operational on a 30% capacity, you should be able to break even.

items.statement: QCIL FY26 synergy target INR 30 crore (run rate INR 20 crore in Q4); total QCIL synergy potential INR 50-60 crore pre-merger
items.quote: INR 50 to 60 crores is the synergy number that we're looking at the QCIL level. And this is outside of synergies that will be driven post the merger.

items.statement: Ramesh Hospitals put option (42.5%) expired March 2025; only 13% exercised; balance liability reversed giving ~INR 7 crore one-time benefit
items.quote: they had a put option, I would say limit up to, to basically the right was there up to March 2025. And beginning of the March, they actually raised a put option notice of around 13%.

items.statement: Andhra cluster occupancy dip due to clinician attrition in Guntur (cardiology, gynecology) and Ongole; replacements onboarded, expects recovery in current quarter
items.quote: We had two or three clinicians moving because of competition, and we are quickly filling up that, and it will happen. And we have already onboarded one or two clinicians and adding a few more and augment, and we are trying to ramp up the place as well.

items.statement: Pre-IndAS to post-IndAS EBITDA gap ~INR 92 crore annually; variable + fixed rent ~3% of revenue; expected to stay 2.5-3% for next 3-4 years
items.quote: as a percentage of revenue, the rental, both fixed and variable, you can model it out somewhere between 2.5% to 3% for the next three to four years.

items.statement: Commissioned Phase 1 of Begusarai plant with 24,000 MT capacity; total installed capacity now 397,500 MT
items.quote: A key highlight of the quarter was the successful commissioning of Phase 1 at our new manufacturing facility in Begusarai, Bihar, designed for a total installed capacity of approximately 60,000 metric tons per annum. The plant has begun operations with the initial capacity of 24,000 metric tons per annum.

items.statement: Balance 36,000 MT capacity at Begusarai to be commissioned within next 6 months
items.quote: The balance capacity at Begusarai is expected to be commissioned with full capacity within the next 6 months.

items.statement: FY26 capex planned at INR220 crores including INR70 crores for Begusarai, INR43 crores for Aquel, INR7-8 crores for Bhuj, INR100 crores maintenance
items.quote: So around INR220 crores will be the capex planned for FY '26 and in this, only INR100 crores is related to ongoing maintenance of plants and INR120 crores is one-off, which will give us a good capacity expansion in both Bathware as well as pipes and fittings in East India.

items.statement: Double-digit volume growth expected in FY26 on favorable base and new capacity
items.quote: So I think this year, we should have double-digit volume growth, given that last year was a tough year. So we will have a favorable base. And apart from that, we have added capacity with a new plant coming in, in Begusarai, where we have commenced commercial production in March month.

items.statement: Long-term EBITDA margin guidance maintained at around 12%
items.quote: So over the long term, we would still maintain our guidance of around 12% EBITDA margin for the long term.

items.statement: Q4 FY25 EBITDA margin at 7.6%, FY25 at 6.4%; inventory loss of INR25 crores in Q4, INR85-90 crores for FY25
items.quote: EBITDA for the quarter stood at INR55 crores, degrowth of 41% year -on-year, while margins stood at 7.6%.

items.statement: Adjusted gross margin 28.5% in Q4 after inventory loss; confident of achieving similar margins annually in FY26
items.quote: So this number we have achieved despite the competitive intensity. It's a function of one is product mix and operating leverage. Product mix has been favorable in the March quarter, like it usually is, especially from the plumbing segment, both CPVC and UPVC plumbing, which tend to be higher-margin products.

items.statement: CPVC grew double-digit in Q4 and FY25, driving realization and margin improvement
items.quote: Yes, we have had a better sale of value -added products, CPVC specifically. So we have been growing in CPVC at a good pace relative to PVC, and that trend has continued in the March quarter. As a result of which we have seen an improvement not only in reali zations, but also at operating margin level.

items.statement: Channel inventory low at <2 weeks vs normal 3-4 weeks; no aggressive restocking expected, stable PVC prices to normalize inventory
items.quote: Channel inventory as we speak is low for my channel partners because of the reluctance to stock material. So channel inventory is low. I think with this increase in prices, again, I don't see some very sharp U -turn recovery of PVC prices. I think prices wi ll continue to be stable.

items.statement: PVC prices bottomed out; Reliance increased prices by INR1,500/MT; expects stable range-bound prices around INR70-80/kg
items.quote: We have seen an increase in PVC prices of INR1,500 per metric ton a couple of days ago from Reliance. I don't expect -- so I'm keeping ADD aside first without ADD. I don't expect a very sharp uptick in prices. I think prices will continue to remain stable.

items.statement: FY25 working capital 99 days vs 95 days; receivables improved to 61 days from 83 days; inventory 88 days
items.quote: For the year FY '25, our working capital stood at 99 days compared to 95 days same period last year. Receivable have shown marked improvement and now stand at 61 days from 83 days in March end. Inventory days stood at 88 days as on 31st March 2025.

items.statement: Target inventory sweet spot 60-70 days (30 days RM, 30-40 days FG); raw material inventory to normalize by end of Q1 or early Q2
items.quote: So going forward, I believe around 30 days of raw material inventory and 30 to 40 days of finished good inventory. So around 60 to 70 days of inventory is what is a sweet spot for us that we have evaluated, and that is one change, and we are happy to imple ment that, and we have already done that.

items.statement: Bathware revenue INR30 crores FY25, Q4 INR10.5 crores with INR4.5 crores loss; FY25 Bathware loss INR17-18 crores
items.quote: For this quarter -- for the full year, I will say, the Bathware had clocked INR30 crores. This is what the number is. And for -- if you talk about this quarter, the sale was around INR10.5 crores and loss for this quarter was in the range of INR4.5 crores.

items.statement: Institutional sales done selectively through channel partners to avoid credit risk; focus on retail distribution and B2B relationships with developers/contractors
items.quote: So institutional sales, we have typically stayed away from because of the extended credit cycles. So we do participate in these kind of institutional projects, be it Jal Jeevan Mission or Swach Bharat, but we participate through our channel partners so tha t we don't take the credit risk directly on our books.

items.statement: Organized players gaining share from unorganized (30-35% of market); brand consciousness increasing; piping cost <1.5% of project cost limits price sensitivity
items.quote: And we still -- around 30%, 35% of this industry continues to be unorganized. So I am very happy to compete with organized players where there is a level playing field with respect to pricing and quality and credit

items.statement: CPVC range GreenPro certified by CII; enhances preference in B2B project segment
items.quote: In a significant sustainability milestone, we are proud to share that our CPVC product range is now officially GreenPro certified by the Confederation of Indian Industry.

items.statement: Launched BioFIT septic tanks for wastewater management; eco-friendly product aligning with sustainable infrastructure
items.quote: On the innovation front, we introduced a new range of septic tanks under the brand BioFIT for efficient wastewater management. Designed to support safe, affluent disposal through soak pits or dispersion trenches, these tanks promote natural filtration and purification, helping safeguard groundwater.

items.statement: Begusarai plant to contribute 20-25 KT in FY26; ideal utilization (60-70%) in 24-36 months; FY27 onwards closer to full utilization
items.quote: So I think this year, we could see around 20 Kt to 25 Kt coming in from the Begusarai facility. And maybe from FY '27 onwards, we would see closer to ideal capacity utilization. So I think 24 months -- 24 to 36 months is a fair benchmark to reach the ideal capacity utilization

items.statement: Dealer incentives of 3% continued in Q4 and Q1; will reduce gradually as PVC sentiment improves
items.quote: So that continued in March quarter, and that is continuing in Q1. We have added capacities. So we will continue to focus on growing. Like I said, it has to be done in a profitable manner with a slight reversal in PVC prices and a clear signal of bottoming out.

items.statement: Bihar Phase 1 capex INR180 crores capitalized in FY25; balance INR70 crores in FY26
items.quote: We have installed 24,000 capacity and related infrastructure for which we have capitalized around INR180 crores in our books of accounts. Remaining is around INR70 crores, which includes infra as well as new capacity, means which it will take to around 60 KT in next 6 months, we will be investing.

items.statement: Ad spend maintained at ~2% of sales; INR53 crores in FY25 (2.2%); same level planned for FY26
items.quote: As we have always maintained, means around 2% is something what we are maintaining. And we'll keep on having the same number for the next year also. So for this year, we have -- for this year, we have spent around INR53 crores which translates to around 2.2% kind of and the same kind of level we'll be investing in the next year as well.

items.statement: No plans for OPVC capacity; conscious decision to avoid government/infrastructure-driven businesses
items.quote: Currently, I think we are not evaluating OPVC. We are focusing more on new products, which will be for the retail and the private B2B projects. I think it's a conscious call to stay away from businesses that are more driven by government sales or infrastructure sales.

items.statement: Branding on Vande Bharat trains and Darjeeling Toy Train (UNESCO site) to enhance visibility
items.quote: We have collaborated with Indian Railways for branding on Vande Bharat trains, enhancing our presence on one of our India's most prestigious rail networks. Additionally, we are proud to announce our association with the Darjeeling Toy Train, a UNESCO World Heritage site, further strengthening our brand's visibility at iconic high footfall locations.

items.statement: Bathware expanded to 200+ retail touchpoints; new showrooms in UP and Rajasthan added to Goa, Jaipur, Pune
items.quote: During the quarter, we expanded our presence with new showrooms in Uttar Pradesh and Rajasthan, adding to our existing outlets in Goa, Jaipur, and Pune. With over 200 retail touch points across India, we are steadily building a robust distribution network and enhancing brand recall in the high potential value-added segment.

items.statement: FY26 revenue growth guided at double digits, with exports growing 50%+ and domestic contributing the rest
items.quote: We will grow by double digits, sir. For this year, the higher growth will come from our export business.

items.statement: FY26 gross margin target to improve by at least 100 bps from FY25's 38.1% despite export mix dilution
items.quote: Despite the growth on our export business, which we believe will get to 25%, you will see growth on our gross margins in percentage, overall gross margins.

items.statement: FY26 EBITDA margin target to improve by at least 100 bps from FY25's 10.4%
items.quote: We also want to improve our EBITDA margins at least by 1% in the current year.

items.statement: Annual capex going forward limited to Rs 25 crore for manufacturing plus tooling; total annual outlay including retail deposits not exceeding Rs 40 crore
items.quote: I think going forward, apart from our retail store expansion and tooling, we don't see a plan of investing more than Rs. 25 crores annually.

items.statement: Cast iron foundry commissioned with 2.2 million pieces annualized capacity, scalable to 4.4 million; manufacturing capacity can support Rs 2,500 crore production revenue
items.quote: We have fully commissioned it. We have started producing domestic products, but we have also got export orders for this and those are long-term orders.

items.statement: Strong export order book for ceramic-coated cookware, cast iron, and outdoor grills; IKEA supply to start end of Q3/early Q4 FY26
items.quote: We have a robust demand, but because of this new coating system that we have implemented for the cookware, we are ramping up our capability to manufacture them.

items.statement: FY25 gross margin 38.1% (+120 bps YoY), EBITDA margin 10.4% (+170 bps YoY); Q4 gross margin 38.6% (+150 bps), EBITDA margin 9.4% (+180 bps)
items.quote: Through disciplined execution and cost optimization, we achieved gross margins of 38.1% for the full year. Our EBITDA margin also saw a healthy improvement, expanding to 10.4% in FY'25 compared to 8.7% in the previous fiscal.

items.statement: Q4 FY25 demand subdued across channels; GT softness, institutional/MFI channel drop, export transition to ceramic coating; early signs of rural recovery visible
items.quote: The quarter was a subdued quarter. It was not as per our plan. There was softness in the demand.

items.statement: Export share 11% of FY25 revenue, targeting 25%+ in 3 years; new categories: ceramic cookware, cast iron, outdoor grills, chimneys, grooming, BLDC fans
items.quote: From the last year, we were at about 12% contribution to our overall revenue. In the next three years, we will be sure it will cross 25%.

items.statement: IKEA partnership for global cookware supply; Walmart growing; quick commerce presence on Swiggy, Instamart, Zepto, Big Basket
items.quote: One of the most notable milestones was our partnership with IKEA to develop and supply a range of cookware products for their global network of stores.

items.statement: Gaining market share in all categories; domestic gross margins approaching peer levels of 40-43%
items.quote: Each of the categories that we are in, we are acquiring market share.

items.statement: Inventory elevated due to unexecuted export orders and Chinese New Year import stocking; substantial improvement expected from Q1 FY26
items.quote: You will start seeing improvement in the absolute inventory starting from this quarter itself. But we are also cognizant of this that their inventory levels are little higher.

items.statement: Lease accounting adds Rs 9.5 crore extra charge vs actual rent in FY25 (Rs 3.4 crore in Q4); difference reverses after year 5
items.quote: For the whole year, the approximate difference between the rental and the lease accounting is about 9.5 crores.

items.statement: US tariffs on China seen as positive for India sourcing; retailers seeking alternate supply chains
items.quote: The tariff is actually a positive for a country like India. There is a strategy by many of these retailers that they would want to look at an alternate or additional source other than China.

items.statement: Export revenue ~Rs 160 crore in FY25 (11% of total); targeting 50%+ growth in FY26 and 25%+ revenue share in 3 years
items.quote: Exports, of course, today is about 12% of our, it is about Rs. 160 crores last year. We are very confident of growing upwards of 50%.

items.statement: Retail store count 262 (91 net additions in FY25); targeting 90-100 new stores in FY26 (~25 per quarter); COCO capped at 171, incremental COFO/FOFO
items.quote: By March 31st, 2025, this number has now grown to 262 stores covering 91 cities and across 20 states, reflecting a robust net addition of 91 stores during the year.

items.statement: Channel mix FY25: GT 34.4%, E-com 34.1%, MT 11.5%, Corporate 3.5%, Retail 5.7%, Export 10.9%
items.quote: Our GT has contributed 34.4%. Ecom is at 34.1%. Modern Trade is 11.5%, Our institutional sales, corporate sales is at 3.5%. Retail for the whole year is at 5.7%. And export is at 11%.

items.statement: No management changes mentioned; retail expansion driven by franchisee model
items.quote: We have capped our COCO to 170-171. All incremental stores are COFO stores or there are some FOFO stores but there is no increase that we will do on the COCO stores.

items.statement: Q4 FY25 revenue declined 3.8% YoY; PAT margin only 0.5% due to Rs 3.4 crore lease accounting impact; MFI/institutional channel volatility
items.quote: The consolidated revenue stood at Rs. 313 crores for the quarter versus Rs. 325.2 crores in the previous quarter last year, hence registering a degrowth of (-3.8%) year-on-year basis.

items.statement: Manufacturing self-sufficiency at 95% (up from 70% pre-IPO); incremental manufactured revenue 3x pre-IPO levels
items.quote: On the increased revenue base, our contribution from manufactured products has gone up from 70 to 95. So actually the incremental revenue from manufactured products has gone threefold from what it was pre IPO.

items.statement: Management guides for return to historical revenue growth of 25-30%+ from FY26 onwards
items.quote: we should be coming back to our historical growth rates, which h ave been in the range of 25% to 30% plus. And I think we should be able to continue to see that kind of a growth from '26 onwards

items.statement: EBITDA margin guided at historical range of 26-28% for FY26
items.quote: we expect that the newer products should also give us a similar kind of a margin range, 26% to 28%, which historically we've been guiding.

items.statement: INR670 crores capex completed as of March 2025, two facilities commercialized, one ready for commercialization next quarter
items.quote: As of March 31st, we have completed nearly INR670 c rores of the planned capex, two manufacturing facility already commercialized and 1 new manufacturing facility ready for commercialization in the upcoming quarter

items.statement: Current gross block plus new plant can support INR3,000-3,500 crores revenue at peak
items.quote: So current gross block, if I add the new plant as well, INR3,000 crores plus to INR3,500 crores plus kind of a revenue is expected -- can be expect ed from these

items.statement: Agrochemical demand recovery underway, key AI molecule ramp-up driving Q4 growth
items.quote: in the agrochemical segment is coming back, and that's what we are seeing. So the volumes are coming back. And especially, Anand bhai mentioned in his openin g remarks that is one of the key molecule, which has been also the ramp-up of that molecule

items.statement: Pharma and Polymer segments showing strong traction with new molecule launches
items.quote: Our Pharma and Polymer segment continue to show strong traction, supported by new molecule launches, growing customer demand.

items.statement: Top 10 customers contributed 71% of Q4 FY25 revenue
items.quote: Top 10 customers contributed about 71% of our total revenue in Q4 FY '25.

items.statement: Working capital intensity to improve with revenue growth, targeting ~200 days by FY27
items.quote: we would be looking at coming to around about 200-odd days, plus or minus 20 days of my working capital. That's what I have -- we as management have a target for us.

items.statement: Incremental revenue from new contracts expected at 150-180 working capital days
items.quote: You can take it as 150 to 180 days.

items.statement: INR185 crores long-term debt to be repaid via warrant conversion proceeds in FY26
items.quote: Approximately INR185 crores of long-term debt will be settled through this route, significantly aiding to deleverage the balance sheet.

items.statement: Long-term debt expected to be practically zero by FY27 after warrant conversion
items.quote: Long-term debt will be practically zero because that should largely be done through -- with the warrants conversion by this year itself.

items.statement: Raw material cost 30-40% of total cost, input price changes have limited impact on final product pricing
items.quote: my RMC i n the whole total costing will be around about 30% to 40% at best. So the impact of price of RM will be affecting my sales price is also so much less

items.statement: AI molecule market size 2,800 metric tons, targeting 5-10% share, triple-digit $/kg pricing
items.quote: this AI is having a pricing of tri ple digit in dollar terms in kg. And also, this is a large molecule with a 2,800 metric ton of the total market size. Our customer is expecting around 5% to 10% of revenue -- sorry, market share of that

items.statement: Inventory built during 2023 agro boom (INR900 crores revenue equivalent) yet to be fully liquidated
items.quote: I had a INR1,300 crores of revenue, of which 70-odd percent was coming from the agro, sorry, which would mean that around about INR900 crores of agro revenue was there. And based on that, I was building my inventory and supply chain, which I have not got enough opportunity to liquidate

items.statement: Regulatory approvals for AI molecule handled by customer, validated and order placed
items.quote: regulatory approvals are taken care by the customers. They have validated these regulatory app rovals from their end. And post that, they have given us an order

items.statement: Elementium product has strong IP protection, Anupam is primary supplier with vertical integration advantage from Tanfac
items.quote: a preferred choice. So with Elementium, we are the primary supplier for them for this product. And again, this is a product which is again a fluorinated product where our vertical integration really comes in very strongly from Tanfac

items.statement: Reaffirmed 15% revenue CAGR target and margin guidance of gross margin 55-57%, EBITDA ~30%, PAT ~15%
items.quote: We remain committed to our guidance of 15% CAGR. And don't forget it's CAGR, so we're not going to jump right back up to 15%, but I can see -- we see the business heading back that way.

items.statement: Gross margin guidance approximately 55%, EBITDA guidance 31% for quarter
items.quote: Our gross margins remain healthy running in the high 50% range and above our guidance of approximately 55%. While our revenue per square foot showed a slight degrowth, this is very much in line with our expectations

items.statement: EBITDA margin guidance around 30%, gross margin 55-57%, PAT around 15%
items.quote: broad guidance, as we have always given, gross margin in that range of 55% to 57%, EBITDA in that range of around 30% and PAT around 15% is what we would continue to endeavor to achieve.

items.statement: H1 FY25 impacted by fewer wedding dates, elections, weather; H2 returned to normal growth trajectory
items.quote: As you may remember, H1 was challenging for our business as we were impacted by fewer wedding dates, the distraction of a national election and unusual weather patterns that affected footfalls in various states. H2 had our business back towards our normal growth numbers

items.statement: Consumer sentiment settling into steady state pattern, seeing consistency after post-COVID volatility
items.quote: But overall, we're seeing the consumer sentiment settle into now a pattern that I would say is more reflective of a steady state of business as opposed to the lumpiness of the post-COVID -- highs and the post-COVID lows.

items.statement: FY25 standalone EBITDA grew 8%, PBT grew 7%, outpacing 6% revenue growth
items.quote: Similarly for the quarter, our EBITDA and PBT outpaced the revenue growth, posting an 8% EBITDA and a 7% growth for our standalone businesses.

items.statement: FY25 capex ~INR86 crores; new warehouse investment ~INR40 crores expected in H1 FY26
items.quote: Sameer, that cash outflow should happen in current year. Most probably, most of it will happen in the H1 of this current financial year.

items.statement: Opened 18 stores, closed 5 in Q4 FY25; 70 net new stores for FY25; crossed 900 store mark
items.quote: For the quarter, we opened 18 stores and closed 5 stores, which takes us to 70 net new stores for the year. We've had quite a few milestones for the year. We opened our first Foot Locker store.

items.statement: No fixed store opening target; committed to meaningful and profitable stores only; rental peaks flattening
items.quote: What we're committed to doing is opening stores that are meaningful and profitable for the organization however many that adds up to, right? So if it comes to a certain number, it comes to a certain number.

items.statement: Plan to open more Fila stores in H2 FY26; Foot Locker expansion slowed until BIS visibility improves in 6-9 months
items.quote: We do have more Foot Lockers planned to open later this year, so it's not like we are hitting total pause on it. But we have slowed it down until we get full visibility of how the brands are going to respond to BIS.

items.statement: Revenue per square foot slight degrowth due to new store mix; ASP growth historically 3-5%, footwear ASP up 5-6% this quarter
items.quote: Our revenue per square foot showed a slight degrowth, this is very much in line with our expectations, as this number is always going to be in fluenced by new stores and the mix of banners that we open

items.statement: E-commerce grew 45% in Q4, 20% for FY25; contribution 10.6%, expected to rise 1-2% in FY26
items.quote: Our e-commerce business continues to perform as it grew 45% for the quarter and wrapped up with a 20% year -on-year growth.

items.statement: BIS issues largely resolved for core business; Fila and Foot Locker still face BIS challenges on some products
items.quote: We were able to overcome the BIS issues for our core business, though its impact was minimal, and continue to grow profitably despite there being a much more aggressive discount environment in the market.

items.statement: 50% of Fila and Foot Locker manufactured in India; BIS-certified factories abroad being pursued; full brand manufacturing capabilities still evolving
items.quote: So when you try to do a brand, you really need width of assortment more than you need depth. So it's not a question of having scale, it's a question of having capabilities available to you in different models

items.statement: Working capital normalizing to 70-75 days range after BIS-related inventory front-loading tapered off
items.quote: We expect our working capital to be around this range. We don't want to become too efficient and then lose out sales. So it's a fine balance that we have to hit there, but around 70 to 75 day working capital is a decent number

items.statement: Balance sheet solid with INR775 crores treasury; annual cash accrual sufficient to fund store openings; no funding concerns
items.quote: If you see our balance sheet, we have a treasury of around INR775 crores. In terms of our expansion plan, as we've always said, our annual cash accrual should be enough to sort of fund all the store openings and plans that we have.

items.statement: Fila EBITDA loss reduced ~50% from INR58 crores in FY24; expect further improvement in FY26, better performance from FY27 with EBO stores
items.quote: last year, if you remember, overall loss that we had posted for Fila was around INR58 crores. This year, we have been able to reduce this amount significantly, somewhere closer about 50-odd percent.

items.statement: No significant ASP difference between metro and tier 2+ cities; aspirational demand across geographies
items.quote: See, we don't see significant difference, to be very frank. Obviously, you can't compare, say, Phoenix in Mumbai to say, our store in Patna. But I'm just saying, broadly, we don't see significant difference.

items.statement: South India (AP, Telangana) showing slight softness; possibly IT sector slowdown or Hyderabad public works; not significant concern
items.quote: So we are seeing a slight softness there. I think it's hard to pinpoint what exactly might be causing it. But yes, you're not incorrect that we noticed that other retailers have also, in our communications with them, expressed that same sentiment.

items.statement: BIS compliance remains challenge for Foot Locker and Fila; brands expected to resolve manufacturing in 6-9 months
items.quote: We fully expect the brands to step up and figure out and close the loop on manufacturing within the next 6 to 9 months. And at which point, we will accelerate the growth of Foot Locker.

items.statement: Achieved sustainability goal of recycling 1 pair for every pair sold ahead of schedule
items.quote: We achieved our goal of recycling 1 pair for every pair sold ahead of our schedule, reinforcing our customer trust and our commitment to responsible retailing.

items.statement: Aspiration to more than double revenue in next 5 years with substantial profitability increase
items.quote: Our aspiration is to grow the revenue to more than double in the next 5 years with profitability margin also seeing a substantial increase.

items.statement: Gross margin guidance of 11% to 13% maintained for FY25
items.quote: We ensured we remained within our previous communicated guidance of 11% to 13%.

items.statement: Adjusted EBITDA margin guidance of 7% to 9% maintained for FY25
items.quote: Adjusted EBITDA for FY '25 was INR 102 crores and adjusted EBITDA margin was 7.9%, in -line with the guidance of 7% to 9%.

items.statement: FY25 gross margin at 11.6% within guidance range
items.quote: Gross profit increased to INR 150 crores, up from INR 137 crores in FY '24, while achieving gross margin of 11.6% in FY '25, in -line with our given guidance of 11% to 13%.

items.statement: Non-lounge services expected to have 2-15% higher margins than lounge margins
items.quote: From the current lounge margins, it can be between 2% higher to as high as 10%, 15% also, higher than the current lounge margin.

items.statement: India travel industry likely to grow 12-15% annually for next 5 years
items.quote: India's travel industry is likely to grow at 12% to 15% annually for the next 5 years, with domestic travel increasing at 12% to 13% , and international travel at an accelerated rate of 18% to 20%.

items.statement: Credit card spending grew 15% to INR 21.16 lakh crores in FY25
items.quote: Credit card spending has also hit record high with India witnessing robust growth in credit card spending during FY '25, with total spend growing by 15% to reach an all-time high of INR 21.16 lakh crores, according to RBI.

items.statement: Non-lounge services contribution target of one-third of revenue in 5 years from current 7%
items.quote: Our aspiration is to scale this contribution up to a third of the revenues in the next 5 years through a slew of new and differentiated offerings.

items.statement: Added 30+ new clients and 6 new services in FY25
items.value: 30-plus new clients and six new services
items.quote: During the year, as part of our strategic planning, we have also expanded our skilled employee base who has helped us in onb oarding 30-plus new clients and six new services.

items.statement: Onboarded marquee enterprise clients including MakeMyTrip and Amazon
items.quote: Throughout the year, we have added marquee enterprise clients belonging to different industries like MakeMyTrip, Amazon and others.

items.statement: Solidified banking alliances with IDFC, Yes Bank, RBL Bank, Bandhan Bank
items.value: IDFC, Yes Bank, RBL Bank, Bandhan Bank
items.quote: On the banking front, we have solidified our alliances with new programs with leading players like IDFC, Y es Bank, RBL Bank, Bandhan Bank to name a few.

items.statement: Top 10 banks deeply integrated with Dreamfolks platform
items.quote: Bala did mention that almost top 10 banks are now deeply integrated with us, and that's the kind of trust that they have shown.

items.statement: Launched coffee at malls service across 83 outlets including Costa Coffee, Tim Hortons, Barista
items.quote: A notable initiative this year was the introduction of coffee at malls as a service at almost 83 outlets, like Costa Coffee, Tim Hortons, Barista and others.

items.statement: Added access to 3,000+ members-only social clubs across 150 destinations worldwide
items.value: 3,000 plus members-only social club across 150 destinations
items.quote: We also continue to enhance value for our premium customers by providing access to 3,000 plus members-only social club across 150 destinations worldwide.

items.statement: Expanded golf access to 40 domestic and 600 global clubs through partnerships
items.value: 40 domestic golf clubs in India and around 600 globally
items.quote: We now provide access to 40 domestic golf clubs in India and around 600 globally through our active partnership with top card issuers and aggregators.

items.statement: Domestic lounge coverage at 100% with 75 airport lounges and 14 railway lounges
items.quote: Our total domestic coverage remains 100%, for the airports with 75 lounges and railway with 14 lounges.

items.statement: International network expanded to 800+ airport lounges with 100+ new additions via Plaza Premium partnership
items.quote: international front, we offer access to wide network of almost 800 -plus airport lounges, ensuring travellers can enjoy comfort and convenience wherever they go. During this quarter, we have strengthened our partnership with Plaza Premium resulting in addition of over 100 new lounges

items.statement: Competitor closure creates advantage as banks migrated to Dreamfolks before closure
items.quote: So Shreyans, that actually is an advantage for Dreamfolks, right, so if the competition has been asked to close down. So, I would say that, yes, that's an opportunity.

items.statement: Operating cash flow improved in Q3-Q4 due to better receivables management
items.quote: The entire sales team in the last Q3 and Q4 have really done a good job in terms of one, of course, the receivables.

items.statement: Finance cost increased to INR 2.2 crores due to provision for delayed payments, not actual cost
items.quote: As per the contract, there were few delayed payments that happened. So we have just provided for this cost, and there is no as such actual cost.

items.statement: Lease liabilities increased due to office relocation and new lease accounting
items.quote: So for the lease liability, we moved our office to a new place. So as you know, as per the accounting treatment. So old lease was discontinued, and new lease was accounted for.

items.statement: Employee base expanded to target enterprise clients and new services, results expected in 4-5 years
items.quote: I will say that in the next 4 to 5 years, yo u will actually start seeing the results from all these services or, I would say, the investment in terms of whether it is other clients or other services will start coming in.

items.statement: New CFO Shekhar Sood appointed with two decades of global financial leadership experience
items.quote: I would like to take the pleasure to introduce you to our new CFO, Shekhar Sood. Shekhar brings in two decades of global financial leadership experience across listed entities, multinationals and high-growth companies.

items.statement: FY25 revenue grew 14% to INR 1,292 crores vs 7.5-8% growth in domestic air traffic and credit cards
items.quote: We finished the year with a revenue of INR 1,292 crores, which is a growth of 14% from the previous fiscal year. Notably, this growth outpaced that of our two main revenue drivers , domestic air passenger traffic and number of credit cards issued both of which experienced growth rates between 7.5% and 8% in FY '25.

items.statement: Worst of margin pressure from spend-based programs is over, better visibility on bank behavior patterns
items.quote: Yes, I should say that confidently, the worst is over. Also because of the reason which I told you, it doesn't mean that banks will not probably further go and increase the threshold of the consumer from the spend base d point of view.

items.statement: FY26 presales guidance of INR6,000-6,500 crores, implying 15-20% growth over FY25
items.quote: And while we are launching projects worth booking value of INR9,500 crores, the guidance that we have given to the market is INR6,000 crores to INR6,500 crores for FY '26, which implies 15% to 20% increase over spectacular result that we delivered in FY '25 of INR5,300-plus crores.

items.statement: Cumulative presales target of INR21,000 crores by FY28 at 15-20% CAGR
items.quote: We target cumulative presales of INR21,000 crores by FY '28, growing at 15% to 20% CAGR.

items.statement: FY25 presales of INR5,300 crores, exceeding revised full year guidance
items.quote: I'm delighted to share with all of you that on the residential front, we have delivered presales booking of INR5,300 crores in FY '25, thus overachieving our revised full year guidance.

items.statement: Collections crossed INR980 crores in FY25
items.quote: Further, our collections have crossed INR980 crores as well.

items.statement: Estate 128 Phase 1 and 2: INR2,700 crores presales, 100% sold, INR628 crores collected
items.quote: Estate 128 Noida Phase 1 and Phase 2, we have booked INR2,700 crores of presales, 100% sold, and we have collected INR628 crores in total till date.

items.statement: Estate 360: INR4,428 crores presales, 94% sold, INR807 crores collected
items.quote: Estate 360, our first launch in Gurugram last year, recorded a presale booking value of INR4,428 crores with 92% of the project sold as of March and that number as of today is 94%. This project has already received a collection of INR807 crores till date.

items.statement: Joint development adjacent to Estate 360: 4 msf potential, INR9,000 crores GDV, launch planned end of Q2 FY26
items.quote: The joint development on a land parcel of 18.23 acres adjacent to Estate 360, having a development potential of approximately 4 million square foot and has a GDV potential of approximately INR9,000 crores, and we are planning to launch this in this financial year towards the end of quarter 2 of FY '26.

items.statement: Delhi One Project: 2.5 msf, INR2,000+ crores GDV, INR120 crores annuity potential, launch Q3 FY26
items.quote: We are planning to launch this project in quarter 3 of FY '26, and this has a gross development value potential between sold and unsold inventory of INR2,000-plus crores, as well as annuity income potential of approximately INR120 crores from our leasing portfolio.

items.statement: Sector 105 Noida: 2.6 msf, INR3,000+ crores GDV, INR140+ crores annuity potential, 40-60 resi-commercial mix
items.quote: The project has a gross development value of over INR3,000 crores and annuity rental income potential of INR140-plus crores.

items.statement: Commercial capex of INR500 crores in FY26 across Gurgaon and Noida assets, funded via tied-up debt
items.quote: In terms of our commercial assets, we would be deploying across our 2 assets, Acreage Builders in Gurgaon and in Noida, amount of close to INR500 crores. These projects have been financially closed through a debt.

items.statement: FY26 residential collections expected ~INR2,000 crores, deployment ~INR1,100 crores, operating cash flow ~INR900 crores
items.quote: So what we are expecting to collect in next year on an average is -- for the large project is close to INR2,000 crores on the residential side. And we were expecting to deploy a number of close to INR1,100 crores in this project, resulting in an operating cash flow of close to INR900 crores coming from these projects.

items.statement: FY25 residential operating cash flow INR450-500 crores
items.quote: In the FY '25, we had an operating cash flow from residential in the range of INR450 crores to INR500 crores in FY '25.

items.statement: Gross debt INR1,350 crores as of March 2025, including INR852 crores lease rental discounting; cash surplus INR435 crores
items.quote: Our debt stood at INR1,350 crores, as of March 2025, of which around INR852 crores was on account of lease rental discounting in our commercial assets. The cash and cash equivalent, as on March 2025 stood at INR1,785 crores, resulting in a cash surplus of INR435 crores.

items.statement: New York Life committed INR300 crores to Sector 105 and INR250 crores to Delhi One; cumulative commitment INR1,800 crores
items.quote: Post this investment, the cumulative commitment of New York Life stands at INR1,800 crores in Max Estates.

items.statement: NYL to invest INR600 crores equity for 49% stake in Sector 105 and Delhi One mixed-use projects
items.quote: So broadly, we would be looking at INR 600 crores as equity infusion of NYL for 49% shareholding in the Sector 105 project and in Delhi One project.

items.statement: Max Square 2 (1 msf) OC expected Q2 FY28; Max 65 Gurgaon (1.6 msf) OC in phases Q2 FY28 (40%) and Q3 FY29 (60%)
items.quote: Max Square 2 in Noida, where we have a leasable area of 1 million square foot is on track. Construction is underway and is expected to receive its occupancy certificate by quarter 2 of fiscal year 2028. Coming to Gurgaon, Max 65 in Sector 65 Gurugram, where we have a leasable -- total leasable area of 1.6 million square foot, construction is underway and is on track and expected to receive occupan

items.statement: FY25 consolidated revenue INR161 crores, EBITDA INR45 crores, PBT INR38 crores, PAT INR27 crores
items.quote: The consolidated revenue stood at INR161 crores and a consolidated EBITDA of INR45 crores. On a profit before tax basis, we reported a number of INR38 crores and a profit after tax number of INR27 crores.

items.statement: Lease rental income grew 67% YoY to INR110 crores in FY25; run rate INR150 crores
items.quote: The lease rental income from our completed and leased portfolio showed a growth of 67% year-on-year, reporting a number of INR110 crores. And on a run rate basis, this number comes to INR150 crores.

items.statement: Peak annuity rental income potential ~INR700 crores in 3-5 years from current portfolio
items.quote: And this is anticipated to touch approximately INR700 crores in terms of annuity rental income basis peak occupancy of projects currently in our portfolio, both operational and under construction in the coming 3 to 5 years.

items.statement: Estate 128 Phase 2 achieved 40%+ price premium over Phase 1
items.quote: Phase 2 of Estate 128 saw a 40% plus price premium over Phase 1, reflecting strong demand for well-designed and end user-focused residential developments.

items.statement: Max Square commands 30%+ premium to local micro market
items.quote: Max Square has achieved a 99% occupancy within a year of launch, commanding 30% plus premium to the local micro market, showcasing strong leasing traction as well.

items.statement: Residential ticket size INR5.5-10 crores across Noida and Gurgaon; diversified across senior living and signature residences
items.quote: If you look at our ticket size that we operate in across all our micro markets, it's around INR5.5 crores to approximately INR9.5 crores, INR10 crores. That's the ticket size that we operate in. And within this, there are the 2 geographies of Noida and Gurgaon. And within that, we have -- this is segregated across senior living, which is Antara and Max Estates.

items.statement: Increasing competitive intensity in NCR micro markets; demand concentrating towards organized institutional players
items.quote: We do see that there is an increasing competitive intensity in all the micro markets that we operate in. And we believe that this is part of the trend towards a corporatization and more organized framework for the real estate industry, particularly in NCR.

items.statement: Team expanded to 350+ with in-house PMC capabilities, vendor partnerships, sales and leasing infrastructure
items.quote: We are now a 350-plus team that's focused on deep projects organization, in-house PMC capabilities, strategic partnership with a lot of our vendors in addition to the sales and leasing infrastructure that we've been able to put together.

items.statement: Some moderation in velocity and prices seen in Gurgaon micro markets
items.quote: Although we would also like to state that in some micro markets like Gurgaon, one may see a bit of moderation in velocity and prices.

items.statement: Delhi One Project received final NCLT and NCLAT approval for revival
items.quote: Delighted to share that we received final approval from NCLT and NCLAT for revival of Delhi One Project in Sector 16B, Noida, which is designed to be a luxury mixed-use development.

items.statement: Acquired 3 floors in Max Towers Noida from Max India for ~INR105 crores to consolidate ownership
items.quote: We have successfully completed -- on one hand, the acquisition of 3 floors in Max Towers, Noida from our group company, Max India Limited at a value of approximately INR105 crores.

items.statement: Q4 FY25 revenue grew 13.3% YoY; UVG grew 21.2% YoY
items.quote: In Q4, Honasa grew by 13.3%, a healthy double-digit growth. And the UVG growth, which demonstrates our consumer traction was healthier at 21.2%.

items.statement: FY25 revenue grew 7.7% YoY to INR 2,067 crores
items.quote: From FY '25 perspective, we've grown at about 7.7% to deliver INR2,067 crores in revenue.

items.statement: Gross margin improved YoY in Q4 and FY25; EBITDA stable QoQ in Q4
items.quote: Gross profit has improved Y -o-Y and EBITDA remained stable compared to last quarter, even after some of the experimentation that we have done in this quarter.

items.statement: Generated INR 74 crores cash in Q4 with negative 24 days working capital; improved from -11 to -18 days
items.quote: and we generated almost INR74 crores of cash being a negative 24 days working capital for the company.

items.statement: Target adding 50,000 more direct distribution outlets in GT channel in FY26 to reach 150,000
items.quote: In the coming year, we would like our GT channel to add at least 50,000 more outlets into our direct distribution from a 12 -month unique coverage perspective. So we would want to see this number which is 100,000 to get to 150,000 as we exit the next year

items.statement: Mamaearth focus categories (facewash, shampoo, sunscreen, moisturizer, baby) grew double-digit in e-commerce and modern trade in Q4; contribute 70% of brand
items.quote: And these focus categories, which contribute to about 70% to the brand in Q4 itself in channels like e-commerce and modern trade, where you see the impact of any of your actions earlier than other channels where there can be a lag and have actually grown in double digit for Q4

items.statement: Younger brands (Derma Co, Aqua Logica, etc.) grew 30%+ YoY in FY25
items.quote: Younger brands, of course, continue to drive good growth momentum for FY '25, young brands have grown at 30% plus Y -o-Y.

items.statement: Derma Co offline (GT+MT) reached INR 100 crores ARR in March 2025
items.quote: Derma Co now in offline, which is GT plus MT in March has done INR100 crores ARR.

items.statement: Mamaearth gained 100 bps YoY value share in face wash (top 5 offline); gained 22 bps in shampoo (bottles only)
items.quote: Brand has gained about 100 basis points Y-o-Y in face wash as a category becoming top 5 brands in face washes basis Nielsen in the offline market as well now. Even in shampoos, we have gained 22 basis points in value market share.

items.statement: Derma Co turned EBITDA neutral in FY24, single-digit EBITDA positive in FY25; trajectory to strengthen further
items.quote: So from a derma co perspective, last year was the year when the brand became EBITDA neutral. This year, the brand has become single-digit EBITDA positive. And I think we will continue to strengthen its EBITDA profile going into next year and the next

items.statement: A&P spend seen as leverage bucket; aim to reduce as % of sales over coming years
items.quote: From an A&P perspective, like we have mentioned in the past, that's the bucket where we see potential leverage and we will drive effectiveness to that end. And hence, if there is EBITDA improvement that will happen, that will be one of the buckets, which will add to that improvement.

items.statement: Acquired Cosmogenesis to strengthen R&D; new tech (penetration enhancers, nano-particle actives) improved product superiority
items.quote: This year, we've done a fair bit of strengthening across our R&D capabilities via the acquisition of Cosmogenesis and then further strengthening our R&D muscle. It's already showing in our product improvements and superiority that we've been driving.

items.statement: Building agentic AI workflows across marketing, supply chain, finance, customer service; skin analyzer, purchase assistants, social listening, content generation deployed
items.quote: Agentic workflows is something that at Honasa, we are taking extremely seriously, and we have got a dedicated team who is working on different agentic workflows, which can help make our different functions more effective across marketing, supply chain, finance, etcetera.

items.statement: Quick commerce shares higher than overall e-commerce shares in most categories; targeting QC share > e-com share
items.quote: In most of the categories a s we speak, our shares in QC are actually higher than our overall e-commerce share. So that's a healthy sign because if the channel grows, our overall share will sort of grow faster.

items.statement: Mamaearth small packs (50-100ml) showing good traction; 50ml:100ml ratio skewed 3x towards 50ml for market leaders; Honasa doubling down
items.quote: In the last 1 year, we have seen a very good traction on our execution on that pack. Of course, it got a little disturbed because of our execution breaking down because of GT changes, etcetera. And now that we are back to that early traction in PMF is actually established.

items.statement: No dividend policy yet; board evaluating cash allocation between growth opportunities and shareholder returns
items.quote: So honestly, don't have a definitive answer for you yet. At this point of time, we would love to also find opportunities of allocating this cash and investment towards more growth opportunities. items.statement: Turnover flat YoY; elongated TDI shutdown cost ~INR 300 cr revenue and ~INR 100 cr profit
items.quote: The company has clocked a turnover more or less equal to that of last year. This turnover reflects the elongated shutdown of TDII, which, otherwise, would have added to the topline of roughly INR 300 crores and profits of roughly INR100 crores.

items.statement: Q4 FY25 revenue ~INR 2,055 cr, PBT ~INR 287 cr; full year PBT INR 790 cr
items.quote: The Q4 has been quite good with the top line of roughly INR2,055 crores and the bottom line of INR287 crores of PBT, I'm talking about. And out of the INR790 crores of PBT, INR287 crores pertains to quarter 4.

items.statement: Fertilizer losses reduced by ~INR 64 cr despite lower volumes; chemical volumes and profitability improved
items.quote: Overall, if we see, the losses on account of fertilizer has come down by a factor of around INR64. crores, despite the fact that the volumes and the overall revenue has been lower. Whereas in case of chemical, the volumes have been higher, the profitability has also improved.

items.statement: Operating cash flow and profit nearly equal; no incremental working capital needed
items.quote: If you see the cash flow part of it, the profit and operating cash flow are more or less touching each other, which means there is no incremental working capital, which is called for during the year.

items.statement: Volume growth FY25 vs FY24: Acetic acid +7%, AN melt +9%, Aniline +15%, TG urea +52%, CNA +15%, Formic acid +6.7%, Methanol +73%
items.quote: As far as the sales volume is concerned, the acetic acid sales was 7% high than '23-24. AN melt sales was also high by 9%. Aniline sales was high by 15%. TG urea sales was high by 52%. And CNA sales was high by 15%. Formic acid sales was also high by 6.7%. Methanol by 73%.

items.statement: 3-week shutdown in early FY26; no further shutdowns planned for rest of FY26
items.quote: We already had a shutdown in the beginning of current financial year for about 3 weeks. So volume growth possibility is very less because of the factory shutdown for 3 weeks, more or less. And we do not have any further shutdown till the end of FY.

items.statement: TDI production down 31% YoY; Bharuch +9%, Dahej -44%; expect near installed capacity in FY26
items.quote: Combining both the plants, the production is down by 31%. TDIBharuch is more or less on the plus side, plus 9%, whereas TDI Dahej, because of the extended shutdown, we are down by 44% in the volume. And looking forward to current financial year, we do not foresce any major issue in achieving the installed capacity production. We'll be close to that mark.

items.quote: Yes, toluene, in fact many petrochemicals are going down, including toluene. So that advantage is actually taken away when it comes to the input cost advantage because the output prices are also under pressure.

items.quote: So the debt number is something that is already published, I think it's around Rs. 440 odd crores, a breakup is around Rs. 350 crores of working capital – Rs. 355 crores of working capital and the rest is in the form of long term debt.

items.statement: Dispatched first Tetra Recart export order to Finland; active discussions with major Canadian customer; onboarded MasterChef for ready-to-eat co-development
items.quote: We dispatched our first Tetra Recart export order to Finland and had an active discussion with a major customer in Canada. We have also onboarded a MasterChef to co-develop products for the ready to eat segment, building a strong pipeline of differentiated offerings.
