items.quote: Based on our product mix for the current order book, we are confident to maintain margins -- margin profile around 18% on a PBT level for the coming year also.

items.statement: Budgeted INR45 crores for test equipment and INR45 crores for additional production space; funded by internal accruals and term loans
items.quote: In terms of capital expenditure, we have budgeted to spend about INR45 crores for purchase of various test equipment to augment existing operations and another INR45 crores for building additional space at our production unit to take care of expected load in the coming years.

items.statement: Board approved preferential issue of ~INR174 crores to strengthen balance sheet
items.quote: Earlier this week, the Board has approved a fundraise of about INR174 crores by way of preferential issue. This raise will help us to strengthen our balance sheet as we look ahead.

items.statement: Board approved dividend of INR2.20 per share, up from INR2.00 last year
items.quote: Also, I would like to update you that Board has approved dividend distribution of about INR2.20 per share, up from INR2.00 of last year.

items.statement: MMIC/TR module supply chain: standby foundry in Europe tied up as backup to Taiwan source for gallium
items.quote: We have a standby foundry service in Europe. We already have a tie -up with them, and we are already given some kind of a development activity to build the wafers to get the st andby in case if we have any issue with Taiwan, where we are depending on for the current production.

items.statement: Strong order pipeline and robust demand for indigenous defense technologies; cautiously optimistic on 20% top line growth FY26
items.quote: As we look forward, we see a strong order pipeline and robust demand for our indigenous defense technologies. We are cautiously optimistic keeping in view of process timeline constraints, and we expect to achieve a top line growth of 20% in the coming financial year, that is FY '26 onwards, driven by a sustained government focus on self -reliance and strategic procurement.

items.statement: JV ARC FY26 order visibility ~$100+ million; FY26 revenue ~INR350+ crores
items.quote: The current year, that is in FY '26, we have a good visibility to book orders worth of close to $100 -plus million. And the revenue, we are expecting around INR350 crores plus.

items.statement: Consolidated revenue growth target of ~15% for FY26; acquired entities expected to grow 12-15%
items.quote: Our revenue growth broadly at a consol basis, we are still targeting 15% or in that ballpark. Difficult to put a margin number on it, primarily because there is so much of uncertainties.

items.statement: Near-term margin pressure of ~2% or slightly higher in H1 FY26 due to tariff absorption; long-term margin trajectory remains upward
items.quote: So it will be a few percentage points. I would say about 2% or maybe a little higher than that, but not much more than that.

items.statement: Three new factories (Madhya Pradesh, Karnataka, Jharkhand) to start contributing in Q3 FY26; incremental annual revenue potential INR325-350 crore
items.quote: The 3 new units incrementally will contribute to about INR325 crores to INR350 crores incrementally -- and so if you look at the current Q4, we were at about INR1,035 crores, right?

items.statement: New Indian factories to begin early contributions in Q3 FY26 and ramp up thereafter; Atraco Africa 500-machine expansion to play out in FY26
items.quote: The Indian capacities, which are this unit in Madhya Pradesh as well as the units in Karnataka and Jharkhand, they are all timed to come on stream in Q3 of this financial year, that is FY '26.

items.statement: Q1 order book intact and strong; Q2 order book slower due to tariff uncertainty as orders placed now land after 90-day pause window
items.quote: Q1 order book is th ere, it's intact, it's strong, etc. Q2 order book, which is the winter session- the winter season orders. They're a little slow to come by because people are just -- customers are just unclear on what the tariff is

items.statement: EU exports reached ~12% in Q4; stepping up engagement with UK customers ahead of FTA; India-UK FTA offers 12% duty advantage over China
items.quote: In Q4 of this year, the exports to EU reached about 12%. We are stepping up our engagement with UK-based customers in preparation for FTA.

items.statement: US reciprocal tariffs: 10% applies during 90-day pause (from April 9), China at 30%; India-UK FTA gives 12% duty advantage over China; AGOA for Kenya expires Sep 2025
items.quote: At the start of the year ,at the start of FY '26, the US announced steep reciprocal tariffs on April 2, which were later paused for 90 days from April 9. A 10% tariff still applies despite the pause, while China has a revised 30% tariff.

items.statement: Order traction remains strong despite headwinds; customers placing orders but Q2 order book filling slower than normal
items.quote: There is a fair amount of order traction for us, even despite all these headwinds, we are seeing customers come to us and place orders.

items.statement: Q4 gross margin lower due to product mix shift: less outerwear, more casual wear; material cost higher for products produced
items.quote: In the current quarter, there was a shift from, compared to the last quarter of last year, outerwear business, which is relatively less and more of casual wear was produced.

items.statement: Full-year volume: Gokaldas 33.22M pcs @ INR693, Atraco 27.68M @ INR306, Matrix 7.44M @ INR573; consolidated 68.34M @ INR524 avg realization
items.quote: For the full year, Gokaldas is 33.22 million @ INR 693 is the rate. Atraco is at 27.68 million at INR 306. Matrix is 7.44 million at INR 573 . And in total, 68.34 million at INR 524 is the average realization.

items.statement: African subsidiary EBITDA margin improvement potential 2-3%; Matrix improvement potential ~1%
items.quote: I think we may have a good amount of leverage from the Africa side where we may see 2% to 3% improvement in EBITDA margins there.

items.statement: Proceeding cautiously with additional capex beyond committed projects; waiting for tariff clarity before actioning new capacity plans
items.quote: The company is proceeding cautiously with additional capex and we'll commit to incremental capex as more clarity emerges on tariff and its business impact.

items.statement: Tariff uncertainty may cause margin pressure in H1 FY26; potential AGOA expiry for Kenya in Sep 2025 could add underlying tariff on top of 10% reciprocal tariff
items.quote: Now AGOA expires in September '25. So post September '25, any goods entering United States will go with normal tariff. That is 10% reciprocal tariff plus the underlying tariff.

items.statement: Walmart not showing slowdown in India sourcing; honoring commitments and placing orders; may be emphasizing India sourcing over other regions
items.quote: On the contrary, they are coming in and honoring all their commitment and are placing orders as we speak. So they are not showing any signs of slowdown.

items.statement: China's 30% tariff shifting some sourcing to Vietnam first; seeing traction from China/Vietnam customers but fabric ecosystem limits immediate shift to India
items.quote: So what happens is when there's such a high tariff in China, the immediate port of call for them would be Vietnam because that's just from a proximity standpoint.

items.statement: Non-cotton (synthetics) fabric not locally available in India; sourcing from Far East increases lead time and cost; India synthetic fabric ecosystem developing slowly
items.quote: The handicap that India has is that fabric is not locally available and so are several trims, which are not locally available. So basing the business on shipping raw materials from other regions increases the lead time and increases the cost for us.

items.statement: BRFL (Bombay Rayon) investment progressing well; capacity utilization improved from 15-20% to >50%; evaluating acquisition down the line
items.quote: When we invested in it in the month of June- July, the capacity utilization was of the order of 15%, 20%. Today, we are well crossing 50%.

items.statement: Promoter pledge is shareholder matter; company is board-managed and professionally run; no impact on business operations or growth targets
items.quote: As far as the company is concerned, the company is Board managed professionally run, and it will have no impact whatsoever on the way it is run or the business it will pursue or the aggressive growth that we target will not be impacted by any of these moves.

items.statement: Training started in Karnataka and Jharkhand factories; Madhya Pradesh training to begin in couple of months for Q3 FY26 ramp-up
items.quote: And in Madhya Pradesh, we will probably start that in a couple of months. But all of them will start early contributions in Q3 and then will start ramping up.

items.statement: Depreciation aberration in Q4 due to Ind AS lease capitalization for African assets; go-forward quarterly depreciation ~INR32.5 crore
items.quote: So the realistic depreciation levels would be about INR32.5 crores or thereabouts.

items.statement: Tariff burden negotiation ongoing across value chain (garment maker, fabric maker, yarn); allocation unclear; hope to pass through to end consumer eventually
items.quote: So now there is a negotiation saying, okay, since we have a 10% tariff, can the supply chain bear a portion of it. And when we say supply chain, it is not just a garment maker, it's also the fabric maker, etc

items.statement: Beyond FY26, margins on upward trajectory if tariff chaos excluded; confident of long-term growth prognosis
items.quote: If you keep the tariff-related chaos aside, the margins will be on an upward trajectory. There is no challenge on that front, and it will keep improving.

items.statement: FY25 consolidated total income INR3,915 crore (+63% YoY); organic growth 19% vs India export growth 10%; EBITDA INR424 crore (+49% YoY)
items.quote: The consolidated total income stood at INR3,915 crores, reflecting a year-on-year growth of 63%, primarily driven by contributions from both the acquired entities.

items.statement: Q4 FY25 EBITDA margin 13.7%; FY25 EBITDA INR424 crore (+49% YoY)
items.quote: In Q4 FY '25, the company delivered a total income of INR1,035 crores and an EBITDA margin of 13.7%.

items.statement: US imports surged 11% in Q1 CY25 to $20B due to pre-tariff front-loading; Q2-Q3 CY25 may see slowdown as inventory digests
items.quote: So Q1, there was a surge in US imports primarily because they wanted to bring in a lot of imports prior to the tariff kicking in.

items.statement: India-EU trade talks and India-US bilateral agreement negotiations ongoing; apparel high on agenda; could multiply business if concluded
items.quote: Coming on the heels of the UK FTA if India manages to enter into an FTA with EU and sign a bilateral agreement with US, there's a strong possibility of business growing manifold in India.

items.statement: Short-term challenges: tariff absorption, potential global demand softness, US recession risk; but long-term growth prognosis strong
items.quote: In the short term, we will see some challenges, particularly with respect to tariffs and the need to absorb some of the costs pertaining to the tariff because that's something which will impact the industry at large.

items.statement: Management targets 15-18% revenue growth for FY26
items.quote: keeping a 15 to 18% target of growth is something that we are really looking at and hopefully we should be on track with that considering the external conditions also.

items.statement: Value-added segment expected to grow 18-20% over next 2-3 years
items.quote: So typically 18 to 20% growth rate is what we usually go with looking at the current market trends even in the value added segments and the approvals of the products, which take quite longer in the value added segment compared to the traditional segments that we usually are in.

items.statement: Q4 FY25 EBITDA margin improved to 12.7% from 12.2% in Q3 FY25 and 12.5% in Q4 FY24
items.quote: Our EBITDA margins of quarter 4 for financial year 25 is improvised by 12.7%, then 12.2% of quarter 3 for the financial 25 and respectively 12.5% of quarter 4 of 24.

items.statement: FY25 EBITDA margin maintained at 12.8% despite raw material, freight and forex headwinds
items.quote: Amid high pressure from the raw material imports, freight cost and forex volatility, we continue to maintain our EBITDA margins to 12.8% in FY 24-25 without compromising our quality & innovation.

items.statement: Net profit margin rose to 6.7% in Q4 FY25 from 6% in Q3 FY25 and 6.4% in Q4 FY24
items.quote: The bottom line augmented to 6.7% in quarter 4 of 25, against 6% of quarter 3 for the financial 25 and eventually 6.4% of quarter 4 of financial 24.

items.statement: Annual revenue reached Rs 9,127 million in FY25, up 17.4% year-on-year
items.quote: We have achieved a significant milestone in our companies growth trajectory, recording annual revenue of 9127 millions in the previous year 24-25.

items.statement: Q4 FY25 revenue grew 6% sequentially over Q3 FY25 and year-on-year over Q4 FY24
items.quote: Revenue growth in quarter 4 of FY 25 has advanced by 6% over quarter 3 of FY 25 and quarter 4 of 24.

items.statement: Planned capex of Rs 15-18 crore for calcination facility at 20 Microns Nano Minerals
items.quote: So we will be investing about 15 to 1 8 crores of CapEx in 20 microns Nano Minerals Limited where we are putting up a calcination facility for the rubber industry.

items.statement: Company intends to invest significantly in capex for capacity expansion and mine acquisitions from FY26 onwards
items.quote: So I think this year onwards, we will be investing quite a lot in the CapEx to generate better capacities and acquisition of you know more mines.

items.statement: Malaysian mine mining operations expected to start within next 2 months
items.quote: We would start it somewhere in the next 2 months where we would actually get to understand what kind of ore would be useful for us in different parts of the process and the supply chain what we what would be a part of it.

items.statement: Sievert JV for construction chemicals inaugurated this month; first phase produces tile adhesives, second phase will add liquid construction chemicals
items.quote: Whereas the Sievert JV which we recently just inaugurated last month, sorry this month and that probably is regarding the construction chemicals business which we are going to be looking into where we are starting with tile adhesives. It's just the first phase that we have started with and then we will be going in with liquid construction chemicals in the second phase for the same.

items.statement: Paint sector contributes 48% of revenue, polymers 25%, rubber/paper/ceramics/others 5-9% each
items.quote: My paint sector has always been prevalent contributor with 48% of revenue share followed by polymers which have accounted for by 25% of the revenue and which has been followed by rubber, paper, ceramics and other applications ranging from 5% to 9%.

items.statement: Exports contributed 13% of total revenue, within expected 13-15% range
items.quote: Meanwhile, my exports contributed 13% to the total revenue, which is again towards my expectation that remained to 13 to 15% in range.

items.statement: Imported raw materials account for 36-37% of total raw material usage; inventory built up due to supply chain dependencies
items.quote: We are quite dependent on imported raw materials which account for 36 to 37% of our total raw material usage. And when you are dependent on imports, you have to build up on inventory because there is you know dependency on the freight factor, there is dependency on the availability of the vessels.

items.statement: Borrowings increased from Rs 121 crore to Rs 165 crore in FY25 primarily for working capital to support higher inventory
items.quote: So basically it's not the any long term or those kind of borrowings that have increased the overall scen ario. It's basically the working capital because of the additional inventory that we are trying to build in the organization.

items.statement: Additional borrowings used for working capital, not long-term capex; company prefers to keep reserves for capex
items.quote: So we would like to keep the reserves for the CapEx rather than you kn ow spend it on the working capital. And because that's something that's going to more add more value to the overall product, you know value chain compared to you know the borrowings that we do for the working capital.

items.statement: Owns 86.68% of IQ Marbles and ~90% of GTLQ in Malaysia; acquiring remaining shares at similar valuation
items.quote: So currently the step down subsidiary that you might be referring to which is step down subsidiary of 20 microns and the subsidiary of 20 Microns Malaysia which we recently acquired GTLQ and IQ (marbles). So in IQ (marbles) we have 86.68 % ownership of the company and in GTLQ we have about 90% owner ship of the company and 10% is with the minor stakeholders.

items.statement: Remaining stake acquisition in Malaysian subsidiaries will not exceed significantly more than already negotiated value
items.quote: But it would not exceed a sig nificant value than what we currently have negotiated with.

items.statement: No listed Indian peers; global competitors are large industrial mineral manufacturers; domestic competition is fragmented by mineral and region
items.quote: Now when we look at the global scenario, we do have competition coming in from the world's largest industrial mineral manufacturers who are very big on scale compared to 20 microns and we see them as comp etitors on a global platform. But when it comes to India, we have a lot of regional competitors and each mineral that we discuss about it will have different competition in the landscape.

items.statement: Customer stickiness driven by broad product basket across 20 Microns and Nano Minerals, R&D capabilities, application centers, and nationwide manufacturing/warehouse network
items.quote: Competitive advantage is the basket of products that we carry all the way from 20 microns to 20 microns nano minerals. We have a variety of products that we offer to May 27, 2025 16:00 (IST) the same industry. So that gives them you know a very heavy lineage of working with us

items.statement: DSIR recognition for R&D labs provides credibility and enables discounts/rebates on imported research instruments
items.quote: So apart from the credibility part, which we already had the ISO certification earlier and we have renewed this, we also import a lot of, you know, instruments, a very, very, expensive instruments considering the R&D facilities that we have as I mentioned to you earlier right now. So it definitely adds some benefits to getting discounts or rebates from the government when it comes to buying these

items.statement: Dividend maintained at 25% in FY25 despite external headwinds
items.quote: The approach enabled us our successful Malaysian acquisition and also sustained to declare dividends at 25%.

items.statement: Paint industry transformation and new entrants create uncertainty; too early to assess market share impact
items.quote: But it is too early right now for to comment on ce rtain big players which have already entered into the industry last year and to see where they, you know, move up to and, you know, kind of shake up the industry because there is a lot of room for everyone to come in now.

items.statement: Per capita paint consumption in India remains very low vs Western world; urbanization and repainting to drive long-term demand
items.quote: But yes, if we compare ourselves to the world, we are yet at a very low per capita consumption of paint compared to the Western world. So we do see a lot of urbanization, a lot of consumption, a lot of repainting which would happen which would kind of increase the demand of paints in the coming years.

items.statement: Kalinganagar first furnace commissioning targeted for June 2026, second furnace by September 2026
items.quote: we have planned to commission it mid of next year, the first furnace somewhere in June '26. So Indian Metals & that is on track

items.statement: Kalinganagar expansion to produce 50,000-60,000 tonnes in first year (FY27) after commissioning
items.quote: In the financial year, it will be around 50,000 to 60,000 production will be there.

items.statement: H1 FY26 ferrochrome production expected around 130,000 tonnes
items.quote: for the next half year, it will be around 130,000, two quarters.

items.statement: FY26 capex outlay estimated at INR800-900 crores across Kalinganagar, ethanol and underground mine projects
items.quote: overall, we expect in FY '26 around, INR800 crores to INR900 crores will be the outlay for all these three projects.

items.statement: Kalinganagar project total capex INR840 crores base plus INR60 crores capitalizable trial run costs, total INR900 crores
items.quote: the total amount that I said was at INR840 crores. And if you add up the capitalizable expenses that will be spent at the time of trial run, it will go up to somewhere around INR900 crores.

items.statement: Underground mine expansion capex INR1,000 crores over 5-6 years, front-loaded in first 3 years
items.quote: we have a plan approximately INR1,000 crores for increasing the capacity, but that will be spent out in about 5 to 6 years from now.

items.statement: 120 KLD ethanol project capex INR150 crores on track
items.quote: we are also under project completion of 120 KLD ethanol project, which is about INR150 crores, which is on course.

items.statement: Chrome ore production target 8.25 lakh tonnes in FY26 vs 7.02 lakh tonnes in FY25
items.quote: So this lakh, we have the plan of 8.25 lakh. So we'll be keep on increasing the ore production from the mines.

items.statement: Major equipment orders placed for Kalinganagar project including civil, structural, furnace equipment and power transformers
items.quote: The orders & LOIs have been placed for civil and structural works, major furnace equipments and power transformers.

items.statement: Q4 FY25 EBITDA cost per tonne ferrochrome INR76,980 vs INR77,800 in Q3 FY25 and INR82,836 in Q4 FY24
items.quote: the EBITDA cost is INR76,980 for quarter 4 FY '25.

items.statement: Q4 FY25 average net ferrochrome realization INR87,021 vs INR96,943 in Q3 FY25 and INR101,771 in Q4 FY24
items.quote: our average in this quarter, has come to INR87,021.

items.statement: Met coke cost per tonne ferrochrome INR15,150 in Q4 FY25; full-year average INR15,543 vs INR18,881 in FY24
items.quote: the met coke component in that is about INR15,150.

items.statement: Chrome ore cost per tonne (ex-mine) INR7,500 in Q4 FY25; specific consumption 2.35 tonnes ore per tonne ferrochrome
items.quote: It's about quarter 4 was INR7,500, primarily what Sandeep has given the reasons because of that, it is INR7,500.

items.statement: Variable power cost INR4.09 per unit in Q4 FY25, down INR0.28 YoY due to lower coal prices from rail transport
items.quote: in Q4 FY '25, the variable cost of power is INR4.09. And compared to Q4 FY '24, which is INR0.28 less than the -- in this quarter, Q4 FY '25.

items.statement: Renewable PPAs signed: 70 MW with JSW Green Energy at INR3.84/unit injection point, 40 MW with Ampin Energy at INR3.75/unit, both 25-year contracts supplying from June 2026
items.quote: signed a power purchase agreement with JSW Green Energy Group to acquire hybrid renewable power of 70 megawatt contracted demand. Further, we have entered into another binding term sheet with Ampin Energy Utility One Private Limited to acquire hybrid renewable energy of 40 megawatt contracted demand

items.statement: Met coke primarily sourced from Colombia, ultra-low phosphorous (0.030%) grade excluded from anti-dumping duty investigation
items.quote: Most of the coke is from Colombia only. And some part we are also exporting from other sources.

items.statement: Regional Director approved merger of Utkal Coal Limited with IMFA with appointed date 28 March 2025; IndAS entries passed in Q4 FY25
items.quote: the Regional Director, Eastern Region has approved the scheme of amalgamation of the merger of Utkal Coal Limited with IMFA with an appointed date of 28 March 2025.

items.statement: Statutory clearances received for 120 KLD ethanol project; boundary wall completed and major equipment orders placed
items.quote: IMFA has also received necessary statutory clearances for the 120 KLD ethanol project and has also placed all the major equipment orders. Boundary wall for the project has been also completed.

items.statement: Chrome ore inventory increased to 4+ months at plant sites and 2.5 months at mines vs 3 months and 1 month a year ago
items.quote: So right now, we are having about more than 4 months of inventory of ore at our plant site, both the plant sites. And also at mine about 2.5 months inventory is with us ready to dispatch.

items.statement: Net cash position INR535 crores as of 31 March 2025 (cash INR906 crores less working capital borrowings INR372 crores)
items.quote: If you see our overall cash position was about INR906 crores. This is excluding any security deposit that we have kept. So INR906 crores we are having. And our working capital borrowings was INR372 crores. So it is about INR535 crores approximately was the net cash balance.

items.statement: Capex funded through internal accruals; ~INR100 crores spent in first 45 days of FY26, major spend in H2
items.quote: on the capex, we are managing through our own internal accruals. So it has started, approximately, we would have spent approximately INR100-odd crores. But a major spend will come in the H2 of this current financial year.

items.statement: Free cash flow generated INR430 crores in FY25 before dividend payout
items.quote: the total free cash flow generated was INR430 crores. So that is the overall -- this is before payout of the dividend.

items.statement: Sales mix: 90-95% exports, 5-10% domestic; 80% long-term contracts (quarterly/monthly index-linked), 20% spot
items.quote: when we look at export to domestic, it will be in the similar range like what we have been doing roughly about 90 -10, 90% in export, 10% in domestic. That would be somewhat those numbers, 90% to 95% in exports and like 5% to 10% in domestic. LTC to spot, LTC would constitute about 80% of our sales.

items.statement: South African producers (Merafe/Glencore) reducing output due to high electricity costs; China dependent on SA ore imports giving IMFA captive mine cost advantage
items.quote: Electricity costs have gone up and the challenges with regards to the ferrochrome market per se. So they have reduced the production on a temporary basis.

items.statement: Price realization lag 1.5-2 months; Q1 FY26 realization expected to improve from Q4 lows but uncertain due to macro factors
items.quote: lag period is about 1.5 to 2 months for us to get the benefit out of it. But on the future outlook, I will just request Venkatesh just to give an overall viewpoint on the ferrochrome market price.

items.statement: Medium-term targets for FY25-FY29: revenue Rs 10,000-12,000 cr, EBITDA margin 12-14%, PAT margin 8-10%, RoCE 20-25%, RoE 18-22%, O&M revenue 20% of total, industrial revenue 30%, international revenue 50%+, EP share >33% of EPC, working cap
items.quote: On a three to five year s scale, on the first row you see what were the targets that we gave. On the second line you see what we have performed against those targets. And you can see almost on every single parameter we have either achieved , surpassed or in the direction of the target that we have given.

items.statement: Closing order backlog at Rs 14,000-15,000 cr with 43% O&M, 57% EPC; municipal-industrial mix 70:30; India-RoW mix 50:50; Rs 7,000-8,000 cr EPC backlog covers 2-3 years revenue
items.quote: This is our closing order backlog position , and here you can see , whether it is from an EPC - O&M mix, municipal - industrial mix, and India - RoW mix, and the growth year-over-year, it is very satisfying, we are on the right track.

items.statement: FY25 order intake ~Rs 6,000 cr; preferred bidder on Rs 3,000 cr projects
items.value: Rs 6,000 cr intake, Rs 3,000 cr preferred bidder
items.quote: The year we had an order intake of around Rs. 6,000 crores, and we are a preferred bidder in jobs worth Rs. 3,000 crores as we speak.

items.statement: FY25 EBITDA margin 13%, PAT margin 9%, RoE 15%, RoCE improved; all in line with medium-term outlook
items.quote: Our PAT at 9% and EBITDA at 13% is in line with the medium-term outlook that we had given to all of you.

items.statement: Net cash position improved 16x from Rs 44 cr (Mar'21) to Rs 705 cr (Mar'25); gross cash ~Rs 1,000 cr; free cash flow Rs 353 cr in FY25; credit rating upgraded to AA from A
items.quote: from a net cash positive position of Rs. 44 crores that we had in March'21, we are today at Rs. 705 crores which is a 16x improvement over a five-year period.

items.statement: Board recommended 200% dividend (Rs 4 per share) for FY25, first in 4-5 years, citing strong cash position
items.quote: our Board had no hesitation in saying we can afford and we should reward our shareholders. And they have agreed to give 200% dividend after four - five years.

items.statement: Conserving cash to invest in finance projects like HAM/BOOT; already done 4-5 such projects
items.quote: in the last three - four years I have been telling you we are conserving cash to invest in our finance projects like HAM or BOOT, which we have done already four - five projects.

items.statement: Perur desalination plant (Asia's largest) under construction; engineering done, supplies intact, site construction progressing; will serve 70-75% of Chennai population on completion
items.quote: this is Asia's largest desalination plant and Chennai is going to be India's and Asia's desal capital. Almost 40% to 50% is already being served , and with completion of his plant, it will be almost 70% - 75% of the population which will be served.

items.statement: India Cluster market prospect Rs 35,800 cr (Rs 24,000 cr municipal, Rs 11,000 cr industrial); driven by Namami Gange, Jal Jeevan Mission, AMRUT, power capacity addition 80 GW in 5 years, refining capacity growth to 98 MMT
items.quote: In terms of number, this is our interest, Rs. 35,800 crores of market prospect what we see is of our interest, which is of our relevance . And out of that , around Rs. 24,000 crores is municipal and Rs. 11,000 crores is industrial.

items.statement: MEA cluster market size $4.6 bn over 2-3 years ($3.2 bn Middle East, $1.4 bn Africa); desal and wastewater focus; NEOM, Qiddiya, Jubail, Ras Al-Khair driving demand
items.quote: So if you can see, the total market size that we see in the next two - three years coming as RFQs, consultants getting appointed, this is the market size that is actually moving. So , $4.6 billion is the market size.

items.statement: Key clients include ADB, World Bank, IFC, KfW, NWC (Saudi), Aramco/SAPCO; multilateral funding agencies provide elaborate due diligence and governance validation
items.quote: you see the funding agencies, the ADB, World Bank, IFC, KfW. A ll these agencies when they fund you , I am sure you know they are very elaborate due diligence process, legal, environmental.

items.statement: Competitive edge from 125+ proprietary IP rights, 1,000+ engineers, technology (flap walls, NEREDA), O&M track record, diversified portfolio across 25 countries, 50+ O&M sites in India
items.quote: Today we have more than 125 IP rights, which we use it for our proprietary projects. We do not license it, we do not sell it, it's only used for projects where we are working on it.

items.statement: Certified Great Place to Work; 2,000 employees globally; human capital and technology basket cited as two key assets
items.quote: Great Place to Work institute has certified that, yes, they see the enthusiasm of people working with us . And they proudly take forward the mission every day they work with us.

items.statement: Strategy Wriddhi targets: O&M 20% of revenue (currently on track), industrial 30% (at 28%), international 50%+ (at 41%), EP >33% of EPC revenue
items.quote: O&M, we are on track to get to the 20%, which is our medium term target to have O&M revenues at 20% of our overall revenue . And you can see all the return metrics , RoCE, RoE, EBITDA, PAT, all of them have near doubled or more than doubled.

items.statement: Working capital days at 110 in FY25; target ~100 days in medium term
items.quote: delivering a working capital days of 110.

items.statement: Manufactured water capability: top 3 globally in desalination and direct potable reuse; 25-year reference plant in Windhoek, Namibia; awarded Ghaziabad reuse project at Paris Water Expo
items.quote: We were the first Company globally to have a direct potable reuse. This is in Namibia's capital city of Windhoek, 25 years back and people last 25 years for generation have been drinking this water and they are healthy.

items.statement: Saudi and UAE localization requirements driving onshore team building; Saudi aggressive on local content, UAE starting similar requirements
items.quote: The market demands us to build a local team because of the localization that is their target. Saudi is very aggressive on it. We are seeing even Middle East being starting or UAE starting to get these local content.

items.statement: Bangladesh project progressed despite political turmoil; Russia prospects have gestation due to geopolitical fluidity and interest rates; Kuwait slow decision-making on tenders
items.quote: This is a project we are working on in Bangladesh. It is progressing well in spite of the turmoil that we saw in political situation, we have got over that.

items.statement: Non-binding equity partnership for municipal capital project platform to access HAM jobs without per-project investor search
items.quote: We also did the non-binding equity partnership to establish a municipal platform for capital project investments, again , in line with our asset-light strategy while remaining ready and relevant for accessing HAM jobs without having to go for each job to a new investor.

items.statement: Middle East order book target of $300-400 million for FY26
items.quote: So somewhere around at least we believe that $300 million - $400 million we could do in the Middle East.

items.statement: Maintain order backlog at 3x revenue over medium term
items.quote: at least a 3 x of our revenues is what we would like to maintain our order backlog position at . And we are today at 4x.

items.statement: EBITDA margin guidance range of 13% to 15% driven by project mix
items.quote: we gave you a range of guidance, EBITDA between 13% to 15%, when it is more of EPC where construction will pass through our books, it will be closer to the lower end . And when there is a higher mix of EP , it will be closer to the higher end.

items.statement: Margins improve from sale to execution through value engineering and cost control
items.quote: Invariably, most of the projects from the sale to execution, we improve the margin . And it's all because the way we execute the projects, the way we control our margins, the way we do value engineering, the way we do our procurement, control the cost at site.

items.statement: Annual bidding pipeline of Rs 15,000-20,000 crores with 30-35% win rate expected
items.quote: whatever we bid as a project we will bid anything between Rs. 15,000 crores to Rs. 20,000 crores every year. Of which we should be able to take 30% to 35%.

items.statement: Middle East win rate historically 25-30%
items.quote: our win rate in the market has been 25% - 30%.

items.statement: FY26 order inflow target of Rs 6,000-7,000 crores split equally between India and international
items.quote: if we target Rs. 6,000 - Rs. 7,000 crores of order, I think India should give us at least half of that, and half of it has to come from international.

items.statement: Preferred bidder status on Rs 3,000 crores orders including Saudi Rs 2,700 crore project
items.quote: We have maintained the number Rs. 3,000 crores and just now as I said, let's keep the fingers crossed for Saudi order , because a lot of people talked about it, various comments were coming, we did not respond to it. Let the results respond. We are very hopeful that what was due to us will come back to us.

items.statement: Working capital cycle reduced substantially, targeting further reduction
items.quote: you have seen this year our cash has increased, our working capital cycle has substantially reduced from the past. So already we are on the job doing exactly what you expect us to do. And definitely answer is why it cannot be reduced, it should be reduced, it must be reduced.

items.statement: 95% of order book funded by multilaterals or sovereign guarantees, not municipal payment guarantees
items.quote: 95% of our order book is funded from multilaterals or sovereign guarantee like Namami Gange. It's not again a state guarantee.

items.statement: No long-term borrowings, only working capital facilities of Rs 200-300 crores against Rs 1,000 crores cash
items.quote: we do not have any long-term borrowings today, we have only working capital. Only working capital for the bridge, that is all we have. And our continual endeavor has been and will continue to be reducing the borrowing usage.

items.statement: Norfund JV due diligence largely complete, legal contracting underway, expected to close in few months
items.quote: Right now the due diligence is on , technical is largely done, financial is majority done . And we have already started discussing with them on the l egal and the contracting part . I n the next few months, we should be able to close that formally

items.statement: Target one-third of EPC revenue from EP over five years, quarterly mix varies
items.quote: on a five year basis we still have one-third of our EPC coming from EP. So there may be a year where I will have 80% of my EPC coming from EP revenues . There will be year where it will be the other way.

items.statement: Senegal EP project with Eiffage nearing completion, expect PGTR handover in Q2 FY26
items.quote: We expect Q2 FY '26 for this project to come to its close with P GTR handing over.

items.statement: Ras Tanura EP project engineering completion in Q1, pre-commissioning activities underway
items.quote: this engineering is about to be completed in Q1 , this quarter it should complete. We have placed major orders, so pre-commissioning construction activities is going on.

items.statement: Al Haer STP project financially closed, basic engineering approved, site mobilized, excavation started
items.quote: The project now, it is financially closed, and we are executing it on full fledge. The basic engineering package is approved. The site and office is mobilized. Some excavation has started.

items.statement: No Indian peers seen in bidding for technology-focused EP projects
items.quote: I do not know who are my peers because we do not see any of the Indian competition when we go for bidding the kind of projects that we are bidding . We are completely a different Company; we focus on technology.

items.statement: Bid tactically, sometimes less than 1% lower than next bidder, overheads lower than competitors
items.quote: we are guessing each time what competition is going to do, and tactically we are placing our price sometimes just less than 1% lower than the next bidder. So we are not leaving a lot of money on the table.

items.statement: Multilateral funding for social causes will continue growing year-on-year despite US policy changes
items.quote: we have only seen this funding has gone up year -on-year and we believe that will continue to happen.

items.statement: Saudi Rs 2,700 crore project rebid with minor changes, evaluation ongoing, confident of preferred bidder status within weeks
items.quote: our project in question what you are asking came back with very minor, not even sm all, minor changes. You will be happy to know, we have rebid it, there were five bidders. And we are confident that the evaluation is going on. We will remain a preferred bidder. We are keeping our fingers crossed and we are very confident and hopeful that we should be able to share a good news with you very soon, n

items.statement: Hired 250+ trainees from top colleges this year to build young talent pipeline and succession plan
items.quote: we have brought in our 250+ odd trainees, which we never did in the past, which is making the organization very young. We have done about 60 – 70 - 80 kind of fresh trainees from the best of the colleges. But this year we decided to go big and making the organization very young.

items.statement: Achieved 0.6 million safe hours without LTI at Bahrain AMAS O&M project
items.quote: The main important part is that we have achieved 0.6 million safe hours from the inception of this project without a LTI.

items.statement: Cash to profit ratio of 1.2X indicating 20% more cash generated than book profit
items.quote: even if you have seen our cash to profit ratio, it is 1.2X. That shows that it's not only a book profit, it's actually the cash we have generated for that profit, 20% more than the book profit.

items.statement: Blue Seed initiative: 6 investable startups identified, 2 approved by board for due diligence, targeting 5-6 investments in next two quarters
items.quote: today, we have selected almost half a dozen companies where we have found that they are investable. Already two we have put up to the Board and got in principle , okay, we are starting the due diligence. And in another three we are doing little more work, maybe in next quarter we will have another three which will go to this. So, I believe in next two quarters we will have at least five or six com

items.statement: Other expenses negative Rs 13.5 crores due to ECL provision reversals from improved receivables quality
items.quote: the other expense negative that you see is primarily because of the ECL provision , so the provisions for receivables which are reversed. You know the quality of the order book and quality of receivables have been improving.

items.statement: Bangladesh order backlog increased due to forex translation, Zambia increased by $8-9 million variation order
items.quote: In case of Zambia, we have also received a variation order which is about $8 million - $9 million, if I remember right, and that has increased the order backlog. So the scope in the Zambia order has increased, and in case of Bangladesh it is primarily because of the forex translation.

items.statement: Oil price dip seen as temporary, Saudi private finance model insulates projects from oil price impact
items.quote: We strongly believe that it's a very, very limited time phenomenon. And the oil prices have not gone substantially down, marginally down. And today the cost of production of oil, especially in Saudi Arabia, is far, far lower than what they sell. So there's enough money on the table for the government to invest in infrastructure.

items.statement: Projected FY26 revenue growth of 11-12% supported mainly by volumes
items.quote: We project revenue growth of 11% to 12% in Financial Year '26, supported mainly by volumes.

items.statement: Projected FY26 EBITDA margin range of 10.5-11%
items.quote: We also expect our EBITDA margin to be in the range of 11%, 10.5% - 11% for the coming year.

items.statement: Target 10-12% annual revenue growth with 8-9% volume growth for next two years
items.quote: We are looking for a 10% to 12% growth every year, ma'am, with a volume growth of anywhere between 8% to 9% for next two years at least.

items.statement: Routine capex of Rs 12-15 crores planned for FY26, no major capex
items.quote: There is no major CAPEX planned. There will be a routine CAPEX of Rs. 12 crores to Rs. 15 crores for FY '26.

items.statement: FY25 EBITDA margin improved 90 bps to 10.5%, Q4 EBITDA margin 11% up 90 bps YoY
items.quote: EBITDA margin for the year stood at 10.5%, up by 90 basis points year-on-year.

items.statement: FY26 ad expenses projected at 6-6.5% of revenue vs 5% in FY25
items.quote: Currently, for the current year it was 5%. For FY '26 we project that ad expenses will be around 6% - 6.5%.

items.statement: Athleisure volumes grew 26% in FY25, trend expected to continue in FY26
items.quote: During the year, the athleisure category stood out with a significant growth of 26% in volumes, and this trend we expect to continue in Financial Year '26 as well.

items.statement: Modern trade grew 17% to Rs 63 crores (5% of revenue) in FY25
items.quote: Modern trade saw a robust growth of 17% in '25, taking the top-line to Rs. 63 crores, contributing 5% to overall revenues, highlighting our strong presence across the major e-commerce platforms.

items.statement: Exports grew 24% to Rs 31 crores (3% of revenue) in FY25, monitoring geopolitical risks
items.quote: Exports also performed well, growing by 24% to Rs. 31 crores, representing 3% of total revenues. While our export pipeline remains healthy, we are closely monitoring geopolitical development that may impact global demand.

items.statement: No planned price increases currently, monitoring yarn prices and competitive intensity
items.quote: Nothing at the moment, ma'am. We will monitor the yarn prices and all. For the time being it is stable and industry is quite competitive, so there is nothing for this quarter, probably, until and unless there is a sharp movement in yarn prices.

items.statement: Gross margin variation due to seasonal product mix: thermal/active wear in Q2-Q3 vs economy in Q4
items.quote: It's just that in quarter three the major part is basically thermal and active wear performs well, so there was a margin of 29%, and for Q4 the economy segment performs well. So, the mix changes according to the seasonality, so the gross margin varies.

items.statement: Women's wear revenue share declined to ~10%, shifting production from Tirupur to Calcutta for better control
items.quote: We understand that and we acknowledge there is a lacking there. So what we are doing, we are shifting our production base, which was earlier Tirupur to Calcutta, where we have a better control.

items.statement: FY25 net working capital days 231 (inventory 128, debtor 147, creditor 44), targeting 10-20 day reduction in FY26
items.quote: The net working capital days for FY '25 is 231 days, and we expect that to reduce by 10 - 20 days in FY '26.

items.statement: Onboarding dealers to channel financing and using SAP for demand forecasting to manage inventory
items.quote: We are taking necessary steps; means we are onboarding our dealers to the channel financing program to reduce our debtors. We are also using SAP applications to forecasting the demand and produce that much of the inventory which would be sufficient to cater the market.

items.statement: Cash generated from operations Rs 59 crores used to reduce debt, net cash surplus including investments Rs 24 crores
items.quote: Cash generated from operations stands at Rs. 59 crores positive, which has been majorly utilized in reducing our debt. Our net cash surplus, including investment, is amounting to Rs. 24 crores.

items.statement: Healthy cash balance of Rs 24 crores, evaluating organic and inorganic growth opportunities
items.quote: We have a healthy cash and cash equivalents in our balance sheet and we are not much leveraged. So, we always look for both organic and inorganic growth opportunities, and anything which will be materialized, we will use this cash and cash equivalent to acquire these both organic and inorganic opportunities.

items.statement: Board recommended dividend of Rs 3 per equity share for FY25 subject to shareholder approval
items.quote: I am pleased to share that the Board has recommended a dividend of Rs. 3 per equity share for Financial Year '25, subject to shareholder approval.

items.statement: Searching for senior EBO Head to scale store network from 33 to 100 stores, focusing on FOCO model
items.quote: So, honestly, we have around 33 EBOs now, but with just 33 EBOs we are yet to crack a very scalable model as of now. So, we are in search of a senior EBO Head, probably we have located him and he will be joining soon.

items.statement: Export/modern trade unit generating Rs 70-80 crores, focusing on own brands over white labeling for higher margins
items.quote: We are doing modern trade and export from that unit only, so it comes to roughly Rs. 70 crores, Rs. 80 crores. So that's a fair bit coming from there.

items.statement: Not affected by Bangladesh trade restrictions, see opportunity for export and domestic demand shift
items.quote: We are not affected, and there is no revenue for us coming from Bangladesh. But whatever is happening in Bangladesh, we see it as an opportunity both in terms of export from India to the country, and domestically we see demand coming up because lot of manufacturers from India take source lot of goods from Bangladesh for local consumption.

items.statement: Economy segment (Rs 70-80), mid-premium (Rs 80-150), premium (above Rs 150) for innerwear; economy and mid-premium larger base
items.quote: Economy, we consider around Rs. 70 to Rs. 80. Anything above Rs. 80 to say Rs. 150, we take as mid-premium, and above Rs. 150 is a premium to us. This is what we consider for innerwears.

items.statement: X-factor segment grew 11% to Rs 229 crores (19% of revenue) in FY25, momentum expected in FY26
items.quote: Our X-factor segment posted with 11% growth, generating Rs. 229 crores, and accounting for 19% of total revenue. We anticipate continued momentum in both modern trade and X-factor areas in Financial Year '26.

items.statement: Geopolitical developments may impact global export demand, monitoring closely
items.quote: While our export pipeline remains healthy, we are closely monitoring geopolitical development that may impact global demand.

items.statement: Orders grew 13.4% YoY to INR2,693 crores for FY25; Q4 orders up 11% to INR762 crores; backlog at INR1,253 crores
items.quote: For the 12-month period, we -- our or ders grew at 13.4% from INR2,375 crores to INR2,693. Only for the quarter 4 level, we have been -- we were at INR686 crores last year, and we are currently at INR762 crores, which is an 11% increase. And we are maintaining a healthy backlog of INR1,253

items.statement: Gross margin improved ~200 bps to 26% in FY25 driven by better pricing, product mix, and metal cost efficiencies
items.quote: Good improvement in our gross margins. And you can see the improvement in gross margins by about 2 points, and this has actually come from the better pricing that we are taking from the market, better mix of the basket of products and solutions or categories that we offer and overall getting some efficiencies with respect to the metal prices, etc..

items.statement: Kolkata plant breaker capacity expanding 9x from 5,000 to 45,000 units with INR90 cr investment by FY26-27
items.quote: Now coming to the Kolkata plant. We have a ca pacity of 5,000 breakers currently and which is also at 90% level of utilizati on. We will be adding another 40,000. So after this, our capacity will become 9x higher. We'll be having a capacity of 45,000, and we do -- and we want to explore markets within and outside India for this. Again, this also we expect to complete by '26, '27. INR90 crores appr

items.statement: Kolkata Phase 1 (vacuum interrupters) 50% commissioned; commercial production expected by end of FY25 or early FY26
items.quote: We have leased and commissioned 50% of what was planned. The rest was movement and all the thing at the new plant, which we are doing in, say, a quarter or 2 because we do not want to disturb the current production and the peeking requirement, which exis ts and as we see today is getting staggered and if the answer is when, it'd be sometime by the end of '25 or maybe early '26 is where we see that

items.statement: Private sector capex announcements for FY26 down 10-12% YoY; inflation at 3.1% may boost demand
items.quote: We see, as I was telling you that we have come to a steady path, we see slight, I would say, decline in the announcements which the private sector has been doing for FY '26, which essentially there is slight dip about 10% to 12%.

items.statement: Data centre segment contributes ~15% (+/-3%) of revenue
items.quote: It's about 15%, plus/minus 3%.

items.statement: Transactional business is sector-agnostic; partners penetrate all segments
items.quote: We do this all across. When I speak about transaction, it is -- we are not limiting that our partner would not operate or should only operate in sector 1, 2, 3. It is actually available to be -- they are expected to be penetrating and be reaching there at each and every sector or segment. So they are sort of sector or segment agnostic.

items.statement: Free cash flow INR245 crores in FY25, up 85% YoY; strong cash conversion and ECL provisioning benefits
items.quote: free cash flow is -- we generated INR245 crores of free cash flow , which is a huge improvement over last year, which is at 85% levels of improvement.

items.statement: Capex to be funded mainly from internal accruals; minor borrowing possible due to cash timing
items.quote: And happy to share that the mode of financing will be mainly internal accruals and maybe because of the timing of the cash out, we might resort to some kind of borrowing . But with the extremely good cash situation in the organization, we are happy to say that mostly we'll be funding it through the internal accruals.

items.statement: Mitigating risks from quality control orders and Omnibus Technical Regulation through indigenization
items.quote: trying to mitigate the uncertainties which are evolving because of few quality control orders and also the Omnibus Technical Regulation, which we are seeing in front of us.

items.statement: EBIT up 35% to INR382 crores in FY25
items.quote: EBIT, again, a significant improvement by 35% and we did INR382 crores.

items.statement: Trade uncertainties exist but company taking steps to avoid material impact
items.quote: There are certain trade uncertainties which are around us. We are not insulated to it. And your company has sort of -- taking right steps as to how this should not impact us materially.

items.statement: Order inflow reporting now includes intergroup orders; prior periods excluded them
items.quote: So we did not include intergroup orders. But going forward, we'll be including that.

items.statement: Other expenses up 33% due to sales-linked costs, branding (Elecrama), marketing, and internal capability building
items.quote: So with all that, we have some good amount of marketing and branding expenses, which have come. And as I said, now we have a strength to invest for the future. And when I say it's not about capex, it's also on the operating expenses where we are building internal capability on many fronts and so expenses of that nature have increased.

items.statement: Other income includes one-time write-back of old payables and interest on tax refund
items.quote: So we had -- we could write back a few payables which were very old ones and we took our vendor confirma tion and we could probably write back those payables. That was a onetime ex ercise. It never happened. It shouldn't happen again. And we also get some interest on income tax

items.statement: Employee costs up 11.2% YoY, in line with salary inflation and variable pay from higher sales
items.quote: Employee costs have increased by 12.3%, pretty -- sorry, 11.2%, pretty much in tune with the annual inflation or the salary in crease that we give and a small part of it has come from the variable expenses related to the additional

items.statement: Targets strong double-digit revenue growth in FY26; expects well over ₹1,000 crore of the ₹3,500 crore smart meter order book to be executed in FY26
items.quote: we expect well over ₹1,000 crore worth of orders to be executed in FY26

items.statement: Guides for FY26 capex of around ₹100 crore, split between maintenance (₹30-35 crore) and growth across metering, switchgear, wires and cables
items.quote: To summarise, we expect CapEx of around ₹100 crore in FY26. This will be a mix of maintenance and growth investments.

items.statement: Total order book stands at ₹3,500 crore, entirely comprising AMISP-led smart meter projects with multi-year visibility
items.quote: Today, the entire ₹3,500 crore order book comprises AMISP-led smart meter projects—providing multi-year visibility and a clear runway for execution.

items.statement: Smart meter rollout pace has accelerated nationally to over 100,000 meters per day; demand from nearly every AMISP is strong
items.quote: In fact, I came across a recent update suggesting that the national rollout has crossed 100,000 meters per day, which is a very positive indicator for the sector and for us.

items.statement: Current smart meter capacity slightly above 1.1 crore meters annually; modular design allows expansion in 3-4 months; sufficient headroom for next 3-4 quarters
items.quote: From a technical standpoint, with the recent Transcribed by ElevEase 11 HPL ELECTRIC & POWER LIMITED additions to our electronics manufacturing infrastructure, including new machines commissioned just last month, some of our interim production capability may already be slightly ahead of the 1.1 crore meter mark

items.statement: Q4 EBITDA margin hit record 16.7%; metering segment Q4 EBITDA margin ~18%, full-year FY25 ~17%; consumer/industrial full-year ~11.5%
items.quote: Q4 revenue stood at ₹493 crore, and EBITDA margin reached 16.7 percent, both record highs for the Company.

items.statement: Expects pricing pressure in smart metering as volumes scale and new players enter; plans to offset via automation, design optimization, and cost structure improvements
items.quote: So yes, as new players enter the space and volumes grow, we do expect average prices to come down. That said, our strategy is to offset that through scale, improved processes, and smarter engineering.

items.statement: Receivable days improved by ~20 days to ~129 days (including GST); inventory days stable; expects no material increase in working capital borrowings in FY26 despite higher revenue
items.quote: As a company, including the impact of GST, our current debtor days stand at approximately 129. This represents a notable improvement from earlier levels, where we were operating around 150 to 160 days.

items.statement: Credit rating upgraded by CRISIL (A- to higher) and India Ratings (A+ stable); finance costs flat YoY despite revenue growth; incremental debt in FY26 primarily for capex, funded by internal accruals and term debt
items.quote: Even in Q4, despite revenue growth and a slight increase in borrowings, our overall finance cost was lower on a year-on-year basis. For the full year as well, our finance costs remained flat despite the operational scale-up.

items.statement: Wires and cables grew ~24% YoY in FY25; domestic switchgear ~16%; lighting 6.6%; industrial switchgear soft but expected rebound in Q1-Q2 FY26; fans crossed 100,000 units shipped
items.quote: In FY25, growth in this segment was led by wires and cables, which delivered approximately 24 percent growth year-on-year. Domestic switchgear also performed well, growing by around 16 percent. Lighting grew by 6.6 percent.

items.statement: Supplying to most AMISPs; expect 2-3 additional AMISPs to onboard; order book steady at ₹3,500 crore indicating healthy repeat order replenishment
items.quote: Currently, we are already supplying to most of the AMISPs and expect two to three additional AMISPs to onboard in the near term as we expand our footprint.

items.statement: Does not name specific unlisted competitors; acknowledges industry maturation will bring pricing pressure; focuses on efficiency and innovation to maintain margins
items.quote: It’s difficult for me to name specific players, especially in the unlisted space. items.statement: Government mandates rollout through AMISPs via tenders with 2.5-3 year implementation timeframe; orders released in tranches based on supplier performance
items.quote: The government has mandated the rollout through AMI SPs via tenders. The AMI SPs are fully aware that they have a 2.5 to 3-year timeframe to not only install the meters but also get the entire AMI infrastructure up and running.

items.statement: Electric fans initially launched in 10-12 international markets with encouraging feedback; domestic rollout phased, targeting 75% market coverage by end of FY26, pan-India by next summer
items.quote: We initially launched our electric fans in international markets, and so far, we've supplied to around 10 to 12 countries where we've received encouraging feedback.

items.statement: Employee cost increase front-loaded for R&D and production hiring; headcount expansion phase largely complete; automation reducing manual labour (one line replaces up to 20 workers)
items.quote: We've done much of the hiring needed, so while normal increments will continue, we don't expect a big surge in headcount. Overall, manpower costs will be balanced by higher output and improved efficiency from automation.

items.statement: FY26 capex to be funded mainly through internal accruals and long-term term debt; no equity dilution anticipated
items.quote: Yeah, mainly through internal accruals and a certain term debt, long term debt.

items.statement: AMISP credit terms 90-120 days with LCs; direct debit from utilities to AMISPs adds stability; no signals of credit period lengthening in last two years
items.quote: The credit terms with AMISPs currently range between 90 to 120 days, and many of them are also operating on letters of credit (LCs). We believe these terms are likely to hold.

items.statement: Revenue to grow at 45-50% CAGR over next two years on standalone basis, excluding IDL acquisition
items.quote: Looking ahead, we expect the revenue growth which we have been giving guidance earlier also to grow at a CAGR of 45% to 50% over the next two years also, driven solely by the core business, excluding any contribution from the recent acquisition.

items.statement: Consolidated revenue to double in FY26 including IDL acquisition contribution
items.quote: If I take into account the contribution of the recent acquisition, I am very happy to share with you that our revenue would double in this financial year.

items.statement: Operating margins projected to improve in H1 FY26 due to favorable operating leverage and product mix
items.quote: The operating margins are projected to improve in the first half of FY '26 due to favorable operating leverage and product mix.

items.statement: Margin expansion to moderate in H2 FY26 and FY27 due to ongoing capital investments but PAT profitability maintained
items.quote: However, ongoing and planned capital investments are expected to moderate margin expansions in the latter half of FY '26 and into FY '27, but continuing to maintain the balance of the profitability in terms of the PAT.

items.statement: Unit-2 full operations from Q2 FY26; Unit-3 Phase-1 capex Rs. 150 crores, Phase-2 Rs. 100 crores starting Q4 FY26
items.value: Rs. 150 crores and for Phase-2 is around Rs. 100 crores
items.quote: The total capital expenditure allocated for Phase-1 is Rs. 150 crores and for Phase-2 is around Rs. 100 crores. The Phase-2 of Unit-3 is expected to commence work in Q4 FY '26.

items.statement: Unit-2 manufacturing operations to commence fully from Q2 FY26; Unit-3 Phase-1 occupation from September FY26
items.quote: 2 is scheduled to commence manufacturing its operations from the Q2 of this financial year. Partial operations have already started but a full-fledged operation will start from the FY '26. Our Unit-3, we will start occupying in different phases. items.statement: Working capital cycle days expected to reduce by 100-120 days from FY27 as programs transition to series production
items.quote: The working capital cycle days are expected to reduce by approximately 100 to 120 days from FY '27 onwards.

items.statement: Preferential round of Rs. 816 crores approved by exchanges, completion expected within six months for working capital, R&D, and general corporate purposes
items.quote: The proposed preferential round of Rs. 816 crores of fund raise, it will be utilized for the working capital requirement, for the R&D expenditure, and also to foster innovation in future technologies including investment in subsidiaries and other general corporate purposes.

items.statement: Acquired IDL Explosives Ltd for vertical integration into warheads, rocket propellants, and ammunition; financials consolidated from Q2 FY26
items.quote: We are also pleased to announce a significant strategic milesto ne, which is the acquisition of IDL Explosives Ltd. This marks a new chapter for Apollo Micro Systems as we move closer to becoming a fully integrated Tier-1 defense OEM

items.statement: Recent India-Pakistan conflict accelerated demand for indigenous defense solutions; company systems utilized in conflict
items.quote: And also, notably, the recent conflict between India and Pakistan has also furt her accelerated the overall requirement, and especially the demand for indigenous defense solution. And we are very happy that our solutions are utilized in the recent conflict

items.statement: Multi-influence ground mine combat trial successful; RFP and order expected in upcoming quarters of FY26

items.statement: No explicit debt/borrowing discussion; capex funded via advances (5% paid against bank guarantee) and LCs for machinery imports
items.quote: Some advance has been paid some 5% or so. The advance has been paid of this INR138 crores. But rest of them, LC has been opened. And when the shipment takes place, of course, at that point of time, we'll be paying for that.

items.statement: Transition period expected to end in Q1 FY26; meaningful revenue improvement from Q2 FY26 as new machines arrive, defence supplies start, routers/FWA/BharatNet ramp up
items.period: Q1 FY26 transition, Q2 FY26 improvement
items.quote: I think this transition phase we say, you can say quarter 1 maximum, this quarter. And quarter 2 will start showing much better results improvement. Quarter 3 would be even better, quarter 4 should even be better.

items.statement: EPC revenue estimate for FY26: INR1,200-1,500 cr (vs FY24 levels)
items.quote: To the best of my knowledge and order book which we have, it would be somewhere between INR1,200 crores to INR1,500 crores.

items.statement: Telecom products revenue estimate for FY26: INR1,200-1,500 cr (based on current order book and expected orders)
items.quote: I would again say it's something like INR1,200 crores to INR1,500 crores. I'm not giving any guidance. Don't take any of the number I've given as a guidance.

items.statement: Inaugurated state-of-the-art defence equipment manufacturing facility at Hosur, Tamil Nadu for thermal weapon sights, electronic fuzes, radio relays, surveillance radars
items.quote: We recently inaugurated state of the art defence equipment manufacturing facility in Hosur, Tamil Nadu. The new facility is dedicated to producing cutting-edge defense products, including HFCL's indigenously developed Thermal Weapon Sights, Electronic Fuzes, High Capacity Radio Relay systems and Surveillance Radars

items.statement: HTL subsidiary entered defence wire harness business (high-potential, low-capex, good profitability); executing initial orders for fighter jet upgrades and T-72 tanks
items.quote: Our subsidiary HTL Ltd. has ventured into the wire harness business for Defence Sector which is a high-potential, low-capex segment with good profitability prospects. We are already executing initial orders for critical applications in various fighter jet upgrades and T-72 tanks

items.statement: Received ESG score of 70.9 from SES ESG Research
items.quote: We are proud to share that HFCL has received an ESG score of 70.9 from SES ESG Research, a strong endorsement of our efforts to integrate environmental, social, and governance principles into every aspect of our operations.

items.statement: Management targets double-digit volume growth internally but does not provide formal guidance due to policy and uncertainties.
items.quote: But despite this, I can say that our internal targets, which we have kept for our team are definitely a double-digit growth. I would not like to give that as a guidance because, as I said, as a policy, we don't give guidance.

items.statement: Industry PVC plastic pipe CAGR expected at 8-10%, with internal calculations assuming slightly above 10% growth.
items.quote: See, CAGR has always been about 8% to 10%, and there is no reason for that to change drastically either lower or higher. So we expect that close to double-digit trend to continue, both on agri as well as non -agri side.

items.statement: April and May saw very strong agri and non-agri demand; channel inventory low; monsoon onset may slow agri demand temporarily.
items.quote: Right now, in fact, April and May have been very strong months for us, both agri and non-agri. In fact, till the rain started a couple of years -- I mean, a couple of days ago, we have been completely sold out on inventory.

items.statement: Focus on margin recovery via better pricing strategy, product mix, and cost initiatives; not dependent on ADD/BIS.
items.quote: Independent of ADD and BIS, we are confident of improving the margins. I would not again like to place a number on that, but margin definitely, we see a margin improvement.

items.statement: Q4 FY25 pipe segment margin expansion driven by better pricing decisions and product mix, not cost cuts.
items.quote: This is basically not so much on the costing side. The cost initiatives have started last quarter itself, but that is still to kick in. This is basically because of, one, better product mix; and two, more importantly, better pricing decisions.

items.statement: ADD stay removed; implementation expected June or July; BIS for suspension PVC also expected soon and will block Chinese imports.
items.quote: No, no, the stay has been removed. So there is nothing -- no hindrance left now. So it's a question of procedural delays. I don't think they can delay it too much now. But having said that, we are already at the end of May. So whether it will happen in June or in July, we have to wait and see.

items.statement: Pipes & fittings volume up 2% YoY in Q4 FY25 to 102,253 MT; up 4% YoY in FY25 to 347,982 MT despite weak demand.
items.quote: For Q4 FY '25, the volume in Pipes and Fittings segment increased by 2% to 102,253 metric tons against 100,171 metric tons in Q4 '24 in spite of the weak demand scenario.

items.statement: PVC resin volume grew 13% YoY to 222,708 MT in FY25.
items.quote: Volume in the PVC Resin segment grew by about 13% to 222,708 metric tons.

items.statement: Channel inventory low; company pushed out inventory to end users; not carrying excess stock.
items.quote: despite the channel not carrying too much of inventory, we pushed out everything. The channel pushed out to the -- I mean, end user. So as of now, even despite the push from our side, channel is not carrying too much of inventory.

items.statement: Net cash surplus INR2,535 crores as of March 31, 2025, up from INR1,820 crores a year ago.
items.quote: The Company continues to have a strong balance sheet with a net cash surplus of around INR2,535 crores as on 31 st March '25 compared to INR1,820 crores in the corresponding previous year.

items.statement: Management acknowledges obligation to return excess cash to shareholders if not used for business; timing at Board's discretion.
items.quote: the management is fully aware that, yes, this is a money we are holding on behalf of the investors. And if we don't use it adequately for the business, we are obliged to give it back to the investors.

items.statement: Organized market share ~30% among top players; unorganized sector data unavailable.
items.quote: So out of the largest player, we are roughly having a share of 30% around market share.

items.statement: CPVC market commoditizing with new capacities (Lubrizol, Epigral, Reliance, DCW); super margins softening but still better than PVC.
items.quote: So the super margins, which prevailed at one time have already softened a bit. They would still always be better than SPVC because of the technology angle and because of the very low leve l producers not being able to enter the market.

items.statement: PVC resin production: 55% via EDC route, 45% via VCM route in FY25.
items.quote: Out of total production, roughly -- one second. 55% came from the EDC route, rest came from the resin route.

items.statement: Monsoon timing uncertain; if prolonged rains, agri pipe demand will slow; if lull after onset, demand may rebound.
items.quote: With the rains now starting, obviously, the demand will slow down. We still have to take a call whether this is a long spell of monsoon, which has already started because we saw in the last -- almost thrice out of the last 5 years, we saw that the monsoon starts in June, then there's a long lull for about 1 month, 1.5 months and then it resumes.

items.statement: No new product launches or geographical expansion announcements expected in next 6 months; focus on brownfield efficiency gains first.
items.quote: But even in the last call, I said, at least for the next 6 months, you will not hear any announcement about that. Currently, we -- see, our philosophy, we have already spelled out in the past also is to first squeeze out every possible effic iency from the existing plants.

items.statement: Staff cost INR51.3 crores in Q4 FY25 due to year-end valuation impact; expected to revert to ~INR57 crores quarterly run rate.
items.quote: See, there are a lot of year -end valuation is required to be done. Because of that, it's more or less impact of that, cascading impact

items.statement: EBIT per kg in pipes & fittings improved from INR4 in Q3 FY25 to INR10.50 in Q4 FY25.
items.quote: EBIT per kg was about INR4 per kg in Q3 FY '25, which has now increased to INR10.50 per kg in Q4 FY '25.

items.statement: Management aims to sustain full-year gross margin around 40% and EBITDA margin at the higher end of mid-to-high teens range
items.quote: On a full financial year, we did deliver 40.4% of gross margin, and this is about 5%, 6% improvement versus the last financial year. And we believe that our endeavor i s to sustain this kind of gross margin and EBITDA going forward

items.quote: earlier this month we announced a strategic investment of INR 1,400 million. items.quote: excluding these 2 large orders as well, the momentum has been very strong and we were able to improve our order booking from various products from various customers from INR58 billion last year to INR77 billion, excluding the large orders.

items.quote: this quarter has been very strong in terms of revenue as well as profitability execution, we did deliver 42% gross margin. items.quote: So I would say that the pricing is stable as of now. Maybe we don't see much improvement coming there. If there is an increase in raw material prices, we are able to pass on. But now the incremental growth in pricing is not so much there. But it is still not going down and we are looking at a stable pricing environment.

items.statement: India targeting 35% transmission capacity increase by FY32; government plan INR 9 lakh crores investment; global energy transition driving export TAM growth
items.quote: I think, yes, of course, what we are looking at the government plan of about INR9 lakh crores up till FY '32. So that gives a lot of confidence. And also, what we see is that there's a lot of growth in terms of the energy transition story globally. So first the Europe opened and then Australia and then now even Middle East is also opening up. So yes, definitely the TAM for the export potential is

items.quote: today, on the HVDC valves and control side there is no existing capacity and whatever we are adding is going to be the new capacity.

items.statement: Strategy shifting from turnkey projects to product orders for better margins and lower risk; product revenue share growing
items.quote: as a strategy, we are moving towards product orders and -- rather than focusing on turnkey orders that leads to a better margin profile. So mix is improving.

items.quote: earlier, as we have said in various presentations earlier, we used to focus more on Africa and Southeast Asia, but slowly slowly we expanded to Latin America. So it's basically the demand which comes from some geography and then when we get engaged with the global

items.quote: in note 10 of the financial statement that we circulated, the Board has recommended a dividend of INR5 per share. Once approved by the shareholders, that will lead to an outflow of roughly INR130 crores.

items.statement: Make in India localization requirements for HVDC projects; new capacity helps meet local content criteria
items.quote: The condition is basically for the whole project, you need to meet the minimum criteria for Make in India. items.quote: our entity borrowed from the cash pool for quite a number of years when we were in debt. items.statement: No fund raise discussed; capital deployment via capex (INR 240-250 crore) and dividend (INR 130 crore)
items.quote: we are consciously reviewing and meaningfully deploying cash in terms of net capex needs and also return to the shareholders, and we'll continue to work in this direction.

items.statement: No management changes discussed; credited team dedication for performance
items.quote: As we transition into FY 2025-26, I am grateful for the unwavering dedication of our entire team. Their efforts are the foundation of our optimism for future and our commitment to consistently creating value for all our stakeholders.

items.statement: Industry capacity expanding; pricing stable; focus on risk-free sustainable business over pure profit maximization
items.quote: In our strategy, we have always compensated cash over profit and to do a business which is risk-free and a sustainable business.

items.statement: Service revenue sub-10% of total; growing in absolute terms with order book expansion
items.quote: Generally, the service revenue is sub-10% for us. But as the overall order booking has been growing, so obviously the overall volume of services is also growing.

items.statement: Data center market currently small (220kV, 300MW scale) but large potential as sizes grow to 400kV/765kV gigawatt scale
items.quote: Presently the data center market is basically 300-megawatt data centers, where the evacuation is at 220 kV. items.quote: So at least for next 5 years, this demand is going to keep on increasing. And then, of course, you have a requirement like rural connectivity where gove rnments want to connect all the villages like in India, BharatNet program is happening, those demands will be in addition

items.quote: We have a lready secured orders worth Rs.800 crore for this innovative new product. items.quote: As far as fiber optic cable and passive connectivity solution attached with that are concerned, I think I'm quite sure this year, our exports will be in 4 figures.
