items.quote: Fiber optic cable, the price which was coming to be around INR840 per fiber kilometer for cable is now around INR905 fiber kilometer. The fiber price, which was around INR266 in 31st December 2024 is around INR259 right now.

items.statement: Selective on EPC orders; refused Rs 2,400 crore order due to payment uncertainty; prefers milestone control and quick payment
items.quote: Recently, I would not name the customer, I refused an order, which could have been more than INR2,000 crores for EPC. I refused. I was not sure about payments, when would they come and when would I be able to do that cable laying, because things were under not my control. So we refused INR2,000 crores order, I refused INR2,400 crores rather. I just refused. I did not take.

items.statement: Expects ~100% revenue growth in fibre optic cable and associated business in FY26 vs Rs 1,100 crore in FY25 (not formal guidance)
items.quote: Now this year, against the revenue of INR1,100 crores last year, with all humbleness, I can say, with the kind of orders we are receiving from data centers, telcos, locally, exports, I am of the opinion that we will grow by at least 100% this year as compared to last year, 100%. And this is not a guidance. Please note, this is not a guidance. I'm giving purely this number from my present knowledge

items.statement: EPC revenue expected between Rs 1,200-1,500 crore in FY26 (not guidance)
items.quote: Not giving any guidance, To the best of my knowledge and order book which we have, it would be somewhere between INR1,200 crores to INR1,500 crores.

items.statement: Telecom products revenue estimated at Rs 1,200-1,500 crore in FY26 (not guidance)
items.quote: Again, this is no guidance. This is just based on my current orders and expectations of orders which we have. I would again say it's something like INR1,200 crores to INR1,500 crores. I'm not giving any guidance. Don't take any of the number I've given as a guidance. These are my estimation based on my current order book and expected orders.

items.quote: Yes. I think this transition phase we say, you can say quarter 1 maximum, this quarter. And quarter 2 will start showing much better results improvement. This transition phase should last in quarter 1, that's it

items.quote: Our subsidiary HTL Ltd. has ventured into the wire harness business for Defence Sector which is a high-potential, low-capex segment with good profitability prospects. items.quote: On April '24 to March '25, EBITDA decreased from Rs. 659 to Rs. 530 a ton. This was mainly due to decrease in prices on the pressure period which started from April, May and continued well till November. So there was Rs. 163 per ton dilution in prices.

items.statement: Q4 FY25 EBITDA per ton flat at Rs 722 vs Rs 721 YoY; raw material cost up Rs 41/ton due to one-time clinker purchase during kiln shutdown

items.statement: Targets AFR ~10% in FY26 (up from 8%), driven by biomass; AFR flat in FY25 due to kiln upgrade shutdown
items.quote: So we should be ending this year at about 10%.

items.quote: The amount increases in the financial year 2025 last quarter is on account of increment when we compare with the March 2024 quarter. But there is the increase as compared to December because two reasons are there . items.statement: Group investing in 2 mtpa clinker expansion at Gulbarga; evaluating merger options among Heidelberg, Zuari and Gulbarga entity; process may take 24+ months

items.statement: Management expects to drive rates higher given strong demand and believes Indian city hotels are significantly underpriced globally.
items.quote: Our objective, I've mentioned this a number of times, is to drive our rates higher and we've done that during the financial year and we'll continue to do that going forward.

items.statement: Strong demand continues domestically and internationally; June reservations show positive pace over last year after India-Pakistan conflict impact stabilized.
items.quote: We continue to see strong demand this financial year as well. There was some impact because of the conflict between India and Pakistan, but that's since stabilised. items.statement: Consolidated revenue grew 11%, EBITDA grew 13% YoY; standalone revenue grew 9%, EBITDA grew 10% for FY25.

items.statement: Foreign tourist business across owned/managed hotels had not yet reached pre-pandemic levels by end of FY25; expects to meet or exceed pre-COVID levels in current year.

items.quote: We are absolutely open to looking at other, all options for growth, which will include brownfield or acquisition.

items.statement: Industry RevPAR grew 16% in FY25; EIH owned/managed hotels grew 22% (Oberoi 24%, Trident 22%); Q4 occupancy 81-82%, ARR up 11-13%, RevPAR up 14-16%.
items.quote: Overall industry grew in the range of 16%, while Oberoi and managed hotels grew by 22% helped by Oberoi hotels, which grew by 24% and Trident was in the same range as our total hotel growth at 22%.

items.statement: Oberoi Grand Kolkata closed for renovation (18-month plan, 6 months done, partial opening in ~12 months); revenue impact ~Rs 70 cr and EBITDA impact ~Rs 43 cr for FY25.
items.quote: So, for the year, the impact is roughly, and Vineet can give you the exact number, but it's roughly 70 crore on revenue and 43 crore on EBITDA.

items.statement: Bombay Airport lounge business concluded March 31, 2025 (was Rs 122 cr of total OFS Rs 490 cr); no renewal chance; aim to offset loss via flight catering growth.
items.quote: So, Amit, no. The lounge business has been concluded. That concluded at the end of the financial year. So, the lounge business is no longer there. In fact, it was supposed to end sooner. It was supposed to end halfway through last financial year, and then there was an extension which was received for two consecutive quarters. So, as of 31st March, that business has been concluded.

items.statement: International revenue Rs 131 cr, EBITDA Rs 36 cr in FY25, up 10% YoY; Middle East impacted by Israel-Palestine conflict but now stabilizing; Marrakesh and Mauritius performed well.
items.quote: So if I look at the international category, we had a contribution to the revenue around 131 crores and 36 crores in EBITDA. We grew by 10% in terms of revenue, and seen similar growth in EBITDA from our international category.

items.statement: Mashobra deconsolidation resulted in one-time exceptional gain of Rs 115 cr in Q4 FY25; expect to recover Rs 136 cr advance plus ~Rs 141 cr book value pending court outcome.
items.quote: We have given the control back to the government. Due to that, we had a one-time exceptional gain of Rs 115 crores, which came in the books for Q4, resulting in a 109% increase over last year impact.

items.statement: No management changes or key hires discussed.
items.quote: We remain committed to providing the highest levels of service to our guests. We're extremely grateful to our colleagues who do so much every day to look after our guests.

items.statement: Management targets double-digit volume growth internally but does not provide formal guidance due to policy and uncertainties.
items.quote: But despite this, I can say that our internal targets, which we have kept for our team are definitely a double-digit growth. I would not like to give that as a guidance because, as I said, as a policy, we don't give guidance.

items.statement: Industry PVC plastic pipe CAGR expected at 8-10%, with internal calculations assuming slightly above 10% growth.
items.quote: See, CAGR has always been about 8% to 10%, and there is no reason for that to change drastically either lower or higher. So we expect that close to double-digit trend to continue, both on agri as well as non-agri side.

items.statement: April and May saw very strong demand for both agri and non-agri pipes; channel inventory remains low.
items.quote: Right now, in fact, April and May have been very strong months for us, both agri and non-agri. In fact, till the rain started a couple of years -- I mean, a couple of days ago, we have been completely sold out on inventory.

items.statement: Focus on margin recovery through better pricing strategy, product mix, and cost initiatives; not dependent on ADD/BIS.
items.quote: Independent of ADD and BIS, we are confident of improving the margins. I would not again like to place a number on that, but margin definitely, we see a margin improvement.

items.statement: Q4 FY25 pipe segment margin expansion driven by better pricing decisions and product mix, not cost cuts.
items.quote: This is basically not so much on the costing side. The cost initiatives have started last quarter itself, but that is still to kick in. This is basically because of, one, better product mix; and two, more importantly, better pricing decisions.

items.statement: ADD stay removed by High Court; implementation expected in June or July. BIS for suspension PVC also expected soon.
items.quote: No, no, the stay has been removed. So there is nothing -- no hindrance left now. So it's a question of procedural delays. I don't think they can delay it too much now. But having said that, we are already at the end of May. So whether it will happen in June or in July, we have to wait and see.

items.statement: CPVC market commoditizing with new capacities (Lubrizol, Epigral, Reliance, DCW); super margins softening but still better than SPVC.
items.quote: So the super margins, which prevailed at one time have already softened a bit. They would still always be better than SPVC because of the technology angle and because of the very low leve l producers not being able to enter the market

items.statement: Channel inventory low; company pushed out inventory despite rains starting.
items.quote: despite the channel not carrying too much of inventory, we pushed out everything. The channel pushed out to the -- I mean, end user. So as of now, even despite the push from our side, channel is not carrying too much of inventory.

items.statement: Net cash surplus INR2,535 crores as of March 31, 2025, up from INR1,820 crores previous year.
items.quote: The Company continues to have a strong balance sheet with a net cash surplus of around INR2,535 crores as on 31 st March '25 compared to INR1,820 crores in the corresponding previous

items.statement: No immediate plans for property sales or asset monetization.
items.quote: No, I don't think we plan to sell anything now.

items.statement: Excess cash to be returned to shareholders if not used for capex; Board decision, no timeline given.
items.quote: Finally, if we don't have a very large capex, then it will be returned to the shareholders. But it's a Board's decision. So I would not like to specify anything right now.

items.statement: Staff cost lower in Q4 due to year-end valuation impact; expected to return to ~INR57 crores quarterly run rate.
items.quote: No, it's not exactly a one -off. See, there are a lot of year -end valuation is required to be done. Because of that, it's more or less impact of that, cascading impact

items.statement: Monsoon timing uncertain; if prolonged rains, agri pipe demand will slow; if lull occurs, demand may rebound.
items.quote: With the rains now starting, obviously, the demand will slow down. We still have to take a call whether this is a long spell of monsoon, which has already started because we saw in the last -- almost thrice out of the last 5 years, we saw that the monsoon starts in June, then there's a long lull for about 1 month, 1.5 months and then it resumes.

items.statement: No new product launches or geographical expansion announcements expected in next 6 months; focus on existing plant efficiency.
items.quote: But even in the last call, I said, at least for the next 6 months, you will not hear any announcement about that. Currently, we -- see, our philosophy, we have already spelled out in the past also is to first squeeze out every possible effic iency from the existing plants

items.statement: OPVC, Silent pipes, Fire Pro pipes under study; no concrete launch plans.
items.quote: OPVC, Silent pipes are on the study table, but nothing concrete to be announced yet.

items.statement: No immediate plans for VCM backward integration at Ratnagiri; under study but no announcement in next 6 months.
items.quote: No, nothing immediately. We are still, as I said, still under study. We have not -- I wouldn't say that it will never happen. It does definitely make sense to push through that. But you will not -- again, I don't think -- hear any announcement in the next 6 months about that.

items.statement: Fittings capacity 50,000 tons (1:4 in-house to dedicated outsourced).
items.quote: So Ritesh, our total fitting capacity is 50,000. Roughly, it consists of 1:4, roughly. 1 is in-house, 4 is the dedicated outsourced contract manufacturers.

items.statement: Organized market share ~30% among largest players; unorganized sector data unavailable.
items.quote: So out of the largest player, we are roughly having a share of 30% around market share.

items.statement: Management expects around 20% top-line growth in FY26 with margins at similar levels to FY25 (around 15% EBITDA)
items.quote: We are expecting around 20% growth plus/minus something. See, last year also, we were expecting certain businesses to click, but our growth is a lumpy growth.

items.statement: FY25 consolidated EBITDA margin was 15% vs 17% in FY24; Q4 FY25 EBITDA margin was 11% vs 12% in Q4 FY24
items.quote: EBITDA margins for financial year '25 is at 15% compared to 17% in the previous year. For Q4, EBITDA margin is 11%, down from 12% in the corresponding quarter last year.

items.statement: Management expects FY26 margins to remain at similar levels to current 14-15% range, with potential slight improvement as one-off development expenses normalize
items.quote: At the current level, yes. Rohit: Got it, sir. Sharad Taparia: Last year, there were some extra development expenses and one-time charges. To that effect, maybe margins will be slightly better. But overall, what you say is correct

items.statement: Capex of INR 15-20 crore planned for relay manufacturing facility, with production starting H2 FY26; new furnace for alloys business ordered, to be installed by December 2025
items.quote: We plan to invest about between, let's say, INR 15 crores to INR 20 crores roughly and then scale up as the demand, whatever demand will be.

items.statement: Alloys capacity to increase 6-7x with new furnace installation by December 2025; current alloys capacity can generate ~INR 30 crore revenue at 100% utilization with virgin materials
items.quote: We have already ordered new furnace and our capacity will become almost 6-7 times of what we have today.

items.statement: Alloys business running at full capacity currently; FY26 alloys revenue expected at INR 20-30 crore with new furnace contributing from H2; relay business expects meaningful traction in FY26
items.quote: This year, we are expecting somewhere between INR 20 crores to INR 30 crores maybe for alloy. Also depends a lot on how much can we productionize and utilize capacity out of our new furnace.

items.statement: Relay business peak revenue potential estimated at INR 70-100 crore on INR 15-20 crore capex; initial focus on domestic smart meter market with production starting H2 FY26
items.quote: Maybe between INR 70 crores to INR 100 crores maybe roughly.

items.statement: EV segment demand muted in FY25 due to Western OEMs facing Chinese competition; domestic EV supply chain engagement underway with Tier 1 supplies to Indian OEMs already started
items.quote: Demand from the EV segment has remained muted throughout financial year 2025. Our exposure in the EV industry is primarily due to Western OEMs, particularly those based in the U.S. and Europe, who are currently facing intense competition from Chinese OEMs.

items.statement: Smart meter domestic orders lower in FY25 due to key customer demand weakness; only <10% of total smart meter program implemented so far, leaving large addressable market
items.quote: See, today, only about less than 10% of the total program is implemented. So balance, the 90% is yet to be implemented across India.

items.statement: Licensing agreement with REL Developments (UK) for latching relays adds higher-value product (INR 225-325 per meter) to smart meter portfolio; relay margins estimated at 10-25% depending on customization
items.quote: Latching relays generally on an average per meter ranges from about INR 225 to may be about INR 300 or maybe INR 325, depending on the customization and depending on the quality of the product.

items.statement: AS9100:2016 certification secured for alloys facility, opening aerospace, aviation and defense opportunities; Chinese export restrictions on rare earth magnets impacting Quantum Magnetics subsidiary
items.quote: A notable achievement was that we secured AS9100:2016 certification for our alloys facility, and this will open up opportunities in aerospace, aviations and defense sectors.

items.statement: Export energy meter business grew to 65% of segment revenue in FY25 from 52% in FY24; US import duties not impacting customized EV sensor business due to high switching costs
items.quote: Export energy meters last year grew. It was out of the total energy meter business, after the total, roughly 65% was export only compared to 52% in the last year.

items.statement: Quantum Magnetics subsidiary commercial scale-up constrained by Chinese export restrictions on rare earth magnets; production currently paused awaiting license approvals; exploring alternative technology partners
items.quote: It is very uncertain at the moment because there is a ban from China. Chinese they are only exporting to against specific licenses. So we have done all that work regarding the licenses, but we don't know how what the decision because that is all controlled by the Chinese government.

items.statement: New 8-acre land acquired for plant consolidation (2 more acres pending September 2025); operations to start in new facility in 2-3 years; currently operating from leased premises
items.quote: We have acquired 8 acres in total, 2 more acres is pending, which we will do in September. And after we do that, we will start developing the land and building.

items.statement: Shunt business revenue ~INR 60 crore in FY25; forward integration into relay manufacturing underway as shunt components used in relays
items.quote: Shunt business roughly will be between about INR 60 crores plus/minus something.

items.statement: Chinese component manufacturers present but existing customized EV sensor products protected by high switching costs; new standardized product line being developed at multiple price points to compete with Chinese offerings
items.quote: Chinese, yes, they have the component manufacturers are there. However, we are introducing one more product line, which I cannot comment about today to address this issue, which will have multiple pricing range, so that we can compete with the Chinese.

items.statement: Relay manufacturing cost similar to Chinese competitors when including 15% import duty; silver and copper (~70% of cost) are pass-through; conversion cost currently higher than Chinese due to less automation
items.quote: Regarding the metals, it is almost similar, but major plus the relay metals maybe about 70% plus something like that. Silver, copper are the major cost elements. And regarding conversion cost, Chinese have a lot of automation already in place. So they will be little lower than us when we start. But there is an import duty also. So we get a certain advantage there.

items.statement: Alloys business has 10-15 customers in pipeline with varying volumes; focus on higher-margin conversion business; PSU orders coming through government tender portal
items.quote: Yes, we have multiple customers, at least, I would say, 10, 15 customers with different, different volumes that they want, but we do not want to, ultimately, we want to be in a space where margins are better.

items.statement: Quantum Magnetics JV partner (Quadrant) keen on China+1 strategy but Chinese technology transfer restrictions forcing evaluation of alternative partners for rare earth magnet supply chain
items.quote: They were keen, but now due to this restriction put in by China, we have to see the legal situation, and we are looking at alternative partners also because there is a restriction from China.

items.statement: Large capex for rare earth magnet backward integration planned to be funded by debt-equity mix; pilot facilities to be set up first before scaling
items.quote: Yes, we have to the capex required is quite large, and we will be we are planning how to fund that capex by way of debt equity, maybe a mix and that we are planning.

items.statement: No management changes mentioned; focus on capability expansion and customer pitching as core strategy despite near-term roadblocks
items.quote: Long-term, overall, we must grow and we must grow fast. So I think our strategy based on the expansion related to capability, pitching our capabilities to the customer. I think, will pay us rewards.

items.statement: Management reiterates 20-25% growth guidance for FY26 across presales, revenue, EBITDA and PAT
items.quote: We'll stick to the guidance of 20%, 25% growth.

items.statement: Management expects blended average realization of INR 6,500-6,700 per sq ft for FY26
items.quote: It will be around INR6,500, INR6,700 on average so -- on a year-on-year basis.

items.statement: Management targets construction capex of INR 650 crores for FY26
items.quote: our target is to do construction of around INR650 crores for the financial year.

items.statement: World Villas sales were weak in Q4 due to equity market volatility but momentum has improved in Q1 with recovery expected in Q1-Q2
items.quote: Q1 onwards, we started gaining momentum, and Q2, we'll really be able to cover up a lot because majorly this is -- I mean, today, we see a great weather with respect to World Villa sales and clients who are going are very much attracted to the greenery and the environmental development over there.

items.statement: Q4 FY25 EBITDA margin declined to 14.55% due to higher interest costs on land acquisition debt and increased employee costs for new project teams
items.quote: The main reason for that is the interest cost increasing and also the employee cost increasing. So that has led to the decrease in the margin.

items.statement: Q4 FY25 sales bookings of 272 units (2.49 lakh sq ft) worth INR 186 crores at average price INR 7,462/sq ft; FY25 bookings of 1,568 units (14.61 lakh sq ft) worth INR 889 crores
items.quote: For the financial year, the company achieved total sales bookings of 1,568 units equivalent to 14.61 lakh square feet of area, which was totaling to a value of INR889 crores.

items.statement: FY25 collections of INR 545 crores, up 8% YoY; Q4 collections of INR 139 crores
items.quote: Total collections for the year stood at INR545 crores, which is an 8% year-on-year increase.

items.statement: New phase launches planned for FY26: Arihant Avanti Tower 3 (Shilphata), Arihant Aspire Panvel (approvals by August, launch Q2/Q3), Arihant Aloki Kharghar (last 2 towers), Arihant Anmol Badlapur (2 buildings)
items.quote: So we have phased -- new phase launches for FY '26 for the existing projects. So one of them is at Arihant Avanti in Shilphata where we'll be opening the third tower. There's also more launches planned -- lined up in Arihant Aspire Panvel, which is also one of our largest projects. So we expect approvals for that by August, and in Q3, we can plan -- Q2 or Q3 and we can plan up a

items.statement: World Villas environmental clearance expected by Q2/Q3 FY26, enabling revenue recognition from Q4 FY26
items.quote: So we expect it to be cleared by, say, Q2 or maybe October, basically, which is Q3. So once that is done, recognition can start in 1 or max 2 quarters. So we expected that recognition should happen from Q4 of FY '26.

items.statement: Premium project Advika drove Q4 average price to INR 7,462/sq ft (first time above INR 7,000); premium contribution to increase going forward
items.quote: We saw great sales happening -- or sorry, better sales happening at Arihant Advika. We sold around 23 units, which is around INR53 crores in value. So that led to the price per square foot going above INR7,000, which is for the first time it has happened for -- in the company's history.

items.statement: Current micro-market prices: Panvel INR 7,100/sq ft saleable (INR 11,500 carpet), Taloja INR 4,800-5,200/sq ft (avg INR 5,000), Kharghar INR 8,600/sq ft (INR 14,000 carpet); expects 5-7% price increase in FY26
items.quote: How the price trends could be on a blended basis for the next year, we expect at least 5% to 7% increase in the prices for these locations because these are the hot destinations today.

items.statement: Key FY26 presales drivers: Arihant Advika (Vashi), World Villas (Chowk), Arihant Aalishan (Kharghar), Arihant Aspire, Arihant Avanti; P&L contributions from Aalishan, Aspire, Advika plus affordable projects nearing completion
items.quote: With respect to presales, key projects will continue to be again Advika -- yes. So with respect to presales, Arihant Advika at Vashi, the World Villas at Ch owk, Arihant Aalishan in Kharghar, Arihant Aspire and Arihant Avanti

items.statement: No direct competition for World Villas due to unique 390-villa configuration across 63 acres with 2 lakh sq ft Gymkhana and 225-room 5-star hotel
items.quote: So at our product level, there is no direct competition. Everybody, whoever is making villas also, their villas are below par to what we are making and to what our designs are. Ours is a very unique concept where we are having almost 390 villas spread across 63 acres.

items.statement: Net debt INR 685 crores (INR 300 crores unsecured, INR 385 crores secured); comfortable with secured debt up to INR 500 crores and total net debt up to INR 750-800 crores; new debt for annuity assets (Gymkhana, hotel)
items.quote: as of now, we are at around INR685 crores of net debt and we'll be comfortable with the debt going to around INR750 crores, INR800 crores. So out of this INR685 crores, INR300 crores is unsecured loans, which is payable when and able. So balance the net debt, which is secured debt is only INR385 crores. So we'll be comfortable to sustain the secured debt to around INR500

items.statement: No major land acquisitions planned for FY26; sufficient land bank (307+ acres) for 2-3 years of execution; internal accruals and debt used for past INR 300 crores land investments
items.quote: We have not lined up many more acquisitions in this coming financial year. We feel we have enough land now to execute and implement the projects, which can give out good, positive cash flows to the company over the next 2 to 3 years.

items.statement: FY25 operating revenue INR 499 crores, EBITDA INR 104 crores (20.91% margin), PAT INR 255 crores; Q4 revenue INR 153 crores, EBITDA INR 22 crores (14.55% margin), PAT INR 11 crores
items.quote: Whereas the full financial yea r 2025, the operating revenue stood at INR499 crores. The total EBITDA stood at INR104 crores and the EBITDA margin reported at 20.91%. The profit after tax was totaling INR255 crores

items.statement: Construction halted on projects awaiting environmental clearance (Anaika, World Villas, Avanti) despite ongoing sales; revenue recognition delayed until clearance obtained
items.quote: So the construction is halted till we get the clearance, although sales is happening.

items.statement: Town Villas project in design stage, launch expected FY27 onwards
items.quote: We are in the design stage at the moment for Town Villas, and it should take another 1 year for it to start. So it's all FY '27 onwards.

items.statement: HEG expanded graphite electrode capacity to 100,000 tons and operates at 80-85% utilization vs peers at 50-60%
items.quote: HEG continues to be amongst the lowest cost producer of electrodes in the world, more so with our last expansion which brought our capacity to 100,000 tons.

items.statement: Global graphite electrode capacity reduced by 120,000 tons (18%) over past 2 years due to plant closures and downsizing
items.quote: All these closures add up to about 120,000 tons. And with these, the total graphite electrode industry today stands at a total of about 633,000 tons as against about 752,000 tons about 2 years ago, a reduction of 18%.

items.statement: ~11 million tons of new greenfield EAF capacity commissioned in last 18 months; another 25-30 million tons expected in next 18 months
items.quote: We believe over the last 18 months or so, approximately 11 million tons of new greenfield electric arc furnace capacities have already been commissioned and in the next 18 months, this figure is likely to be in the region of another 25 to 30 million tons.

items.statement: Total new EAF capacity including commissioned and planned exceeds 100 million tons globally
items.quote: So from all the various data that we collect from different sources, the total new electric arc furnace capacities including the last 12 months actual commissions of about 10, 12 million tons, it's more than 100 million tons.

items.statement: Western peers announced 15-20% electrode price hikes in last 2 quarters; some increases being absorbed but full impact pending
items.quote: You are aware that given their high cost structur e and incurring significant losses, most of our international peers had announced their intent to increase electrode prices by about 15% to 20% in last 2

items.statement: EBITDA margin improved sequentially: 16% in Q1, 21% in Q3, 27% in Q4 FY25; full year average 21%
items.quote: Our EBITDA quarter-on-quarter has been going up. It was 16% in Q1, which went up to 21% in Q3. And in last quarter, Q4, it was as high as 27%, with a full year average being 21%.

items.statement: Excluding GrafTech MTM loss, Q4 FY25 PBT would be Rs 88 crore and full year Rs 228 crore, making Q4 best quarter
items.quote: this MTM loss on GrafTech investment shares, our PBT would have been Rs. 88 crores for Q4 and Rs. 228 crores for the full year 2024- 25, which makes Q4 as the best performing quarter in the previous year

items.statement: Anode plant funding to be a mix of debt and equity
items.quote: It will be a mix of debt and equity.

items.statement: US imposed 10% import duty on graphite electrodes from all countries; impact limited due to diversified sales footprint
items.quote: The recent imposition of 10% import duties in the US, if not withdrawn, will have some impact on our business. However, given HEG's very well diversified sales, sales footprint across all major global markets, the overall impact is expected to be limited.

items.statement: 10% US tariff effective until July 9; uncertainty whether it will remain, revert to zero, or change
items.quote: No, it is 10%. For the time being, it is 10% no t only from India, but from all over the world. So we will have to see, wait and se e. I mean, the real date is the 9th of July, when this 10%..until when it is 10%, we never know whether it will come back to zero or it will remain at 10% or

items.statement: Board recommended 90% final dividend (Rs 1.80 per share of face value Rs 2) for FY25
items.quote: The board of directors have recommended a 90% of final dividend that is through Rs. 1.80 per equity share of the face value of Rs 2 each for the Financial Year 2025 subject to the approval of the shareholders at the ensuing AGM.

items.statement: Company is long-term debt-free with treasury of ~Rs 875 crore as of March 31, 2025
items.quote: The Company is long-term debt-free and had a treasury size of approximately Rs. 875 crores as on 31st March 2025.

items.statement: Global graphite electrode demand estimated at 450,000-500,000 tons for top 6 producers combined based on ~65% capacity utilization
items.quote: So I think we will come in demand of around between 450,000 to 500,000 tons for these 6 six companies combined.

items.statement: Needle coke prices stable for last 3 quarters and expected to remain stable through July-September quarter
items.quote: Needle coke prices have been stable in the last 3 quarters. Now they are also, of course, needle coke prices are tied to the electrode prices. So let's say in the next 1 or 2 quarters, we think they should be in the same range because the electrode prices are also going to be in the same range.

items.statement: Anode plant benefiting from China+1 strategy; OEMs in Europe and US see clear advantage in India-based supply vs China or Western facilities
items.quote: So right now, in case of anode, the biggest change which has happened is that almost all the customers outside China have started opting for China Plus One because of the uncertainty in US and various other geographies. So that is giving us a very clear advantage of the product being manufactured in India.

items.statement: Domestic anode demand expected to reach 100,000-140,000 tons by 2030; HEG plans to double 20,000 ton initial capacity in 4-5 years
items.quote: I think by the year 2030 you will see a demand of between 100,000 tons to 140,000 tons based on the cell battery that will be produced in India. So we are looking at not only the global market but actually the India market itself would be mature enough to consume 120,000 tons of graphite anode powder. So our first stage, of course, we are starting with 20,000, but we hope that in the same location

items.statement: Chinese electrode exports minimal competition in ultra-high-power segment; HEG competes mainly with Japanese firms and GrafTech
items.quote: China still does not have the technology and we do compete with China, but very small segment in the market which is the lower part of the segment of the let us say 500-1000 tons of electrode demand or whatever Manish was spoke about. So the impact on people like us or Graphite India or the Japanese or Americans is minimal because of Chinese production of electrode and exports.

items.statement: No concrete development on POSCO/sister company graphite electrode plant in South Korea despite 3-4 month old reports
items.quote: See, what you're mentioning, this Korea thing, POSCO, we have also heard this, but nothing beyond that, nothing concrete we have come acr oss. We did hear that they are considering putting up a plant somewhere here, there. So beyond that, nothing came over. This news is, I think, about 3 to 4 months old. So maybe, but we will check up. But so far, there is nothing concrete on that

items.statement: Demerger scheme filed with stock exchanges and authorities; NCLT approval expected by end of calendar year 2025
items.quote: Our scheme has been filed with stock exchanges and all other relevant authorities, after which it will go to NCLT. We expect to get all the required approvals by end of calendar year 2025.

items.statement: Electrode price recovery timing uncertain; may take 1-2 quarters for capacity closures to fully exit market and for price hikes to reflect in orders
items.quote: It may take a while, it may take a quarter for you to actually see it happening on the ground. But what the sense we are getting at is that yes, some price increase may be on the way, but we have to wait for a while because the orders which we have on hand, of course, they have to be executed.

items.statement: Expect to maintain ~80% capacity utilization in current year, possibly slightly higher
items.quote: Our capacity utilization for the year 2024-25 was close to 80% based on our expanded capacity of 100,000 tons and we hope to maintain this in the cu rrent year too, if not increase th is a little bit

items.statement: Exploring renewable power sourcing; have 15 MW hydro plant and 3 MW solar (adding another 3 MW); MP Discom renewable power currently 50 paise/unit costlier
items.quote: We have some 3 megawatts solar plant inside. Another three is being put up. And there is option available from the Madhya Pradesh Discom that they are ready to sell us renewable energy, but that it costs higher, more than 50 paisa higher.

items.statement: Management declined to provide specific numerical growth targets for FY26, citing regulatory constraints on forward-looking statements
items.quote: So essentially, I cannot give you numbers because it will be leading statement.

items.statement: Student segment market degrew ~16% YoY per RBI LRS data; company gained market share despite market decline
items.quote: There has been significant restrictions in Canada. You're also seeing the restrictions imposed by in the US. Multiple restrictions through countries for students which has impacted the students business and we have seen a year-on-year degrowth here.

items.statement: Leisure travel segment identified as biggest growth opportunity; India leisure travel expected to grow with GDP similar to China's historical trajectory
items.quote: We feel growth in leisure travel is the biggest opportunity as of now and it's als o validated by the LRS numbers

items.statement: PBT grew 61% YoY to Rs 6.63 crore in FY25; PAT was Rs 3.24 crore after deferred tax reversal of Rs 2.10 crore in Q4
items.quote: for the year , we closed at Rs. 6.63 crores, which is 61 % year-on-year growth over the previous year, where we closed at Rs. 4.12 crore

items.statement: Gross revenue grew at 44.07% CAGR over 5 years to Rs 86.51 crore; selling expenses grew at 21.52% CAGR to Rs 34 crore
items.quote: At this time around, we have given you a figure where we can show you the last 5 years how the company's gross revenue has grown, from Rs. 20 crores we have gone up to Rs. 86.51 crores, which is a CAGR of 44.07%.

items.statement: Gross turnover Rs 5,722 crore for FY25 (18% YoY growth); Q4 gross turnover Rs 1,415 crore (11% YoY growth)
items.quote: This year we have clocked Rs. 5722 crores against last year's Rs. 4853 crores which is 18% growth year-on-year.

items.statement: Card issuance revenue model shifts from distributor commissions to usage-based MDR fees and float income like credit/debit card model
items.quote: When you are a distributor, you work on commissions. When you are an issuer, you work on the actual usage of the card, like how a credit card model works or a debit card model works.

items.statement: Corporate client base 850+ including Accenture, Siemens, EY, Zoho, Tech Mahindra, Reliance, Mindtree, Godrej, Titan, Adani; ~50% of corporate business on platform, targeting 80%
items.quote: Today we have around 850 plus corporate customers. We have key customers like Accenture, Siemens, EY, Zoho, Tech Mahindra, Reliance, Mindtree, Godrej, Titan, Adani, etc.

items.statement: Student segment: 400+ B2B partners (agents, education loan providers, consultants); handled 35,000+ students in FY25
items.quote: Last year, we handled 35,000 plus students and as I already mentioned 400 plus consultants.

items.statement: Tour operator partnerships expanding: integrated with EaseMyTrip, Zaggle, and 200-300 agents; digital enablement for partners underway
items.quote: In fact, you will be seeing a lot of redirections. I n fact, we are there in EaseMyT rip also recently . You can get redirected for FOREX to our

items.statement: Employee costs capitalized in Q4 for card product development; IT infrastructure build required for PA-CB license (DSP or platform build)
items.quote: So with the previous quarter, actually this quarter, there was a lot of expense on employees, which was done towards building the product when we issued our ca rd. So that amount is capitalized

items.statement: Digital platforms cover ~60% of business (corporate, agent, direct); target to reach 80% digital penetration
items.quote: We have around close to 50% on the platform because bigger companies are more ready to get into the platform. There is some resistance by smaller companies. We are working on it, but our aim is to at least reach 80%.

items.statement: TCS threshold raised from Rs 7 lakh to Rs 10 lakh for personal remittances; FXC (Forex Correspondent) model for AD2s awaited from RBI
items.quote: The good news is now the limit of 7 lakhs has been raised to 10 lakhs which gives us some breathing space to do business otherwise credit cards are an unfavo rable advantage here where there was no TCS applied on credit

items.statement: PA-CB license application planned within current quarter or before next quarter ends; MTSS license also in roadmap but sequenced after PA-CB
items.quote: That is our idea. That is the idea that we will apply it within this quarter or max before the next quarter ends.

items.statement: Dividend recommended at Rs 1.5 per share (face value Rs 10) for FY25, up from Rs 1.0 in FY24; board confident on liquidity and growth funding
items.quote: We have now this year recommended Rs. 1.5 per equity share of the face value of Rs. 10 has been our recommendation. Last year we recommended Rs. 1 per share.

items.statement: Business funded through internal accruals and bank borrowing limits; corporate segment on credit terms, rest largely prepaid; net owned funds requirement met
items.quote: We have capital, we also have borrowed, we have banking limits through which we drive our business because capital requirements are always there in our business.

items.statement: ESOP pool: 17.5 lakh shares under 2018 plan; ~1 lakh shares remaining for grants; FY25 ESOP expense Rs 51 lakh; FY26 expense depends on actuarial valuation
items.quote: See, we already have some 17.5 lakhs of ESOP which was as per 2018 ESOP plan. And out of that o nly the ESOP issue and new bands are done. We are still left with around 1 lakh shares to be granted

items.statement: Student visa restrictions in US, Canada creating headwinds; credit card competition due to TCS advantage; corporate travel subdued by virtual meetings
items.quote: Obviously, Student segment is under pressure. You are all aware, even today, yesterday, we got the news that student's visas are temporarily on hold in US.

items.statement: Remittances constitute ~65% of business; 5-year CAGR 40%; FOREX cards 5-year CAGR 96.41%; retail segment 5-year CAGR 47.09%
items.quote: Next, we talk of remittances which is a big business for us because this constitutes around 65% of our business. Here we have grown at a CAGR of 40% over the last 5 years.

items.statement: Deferred tax asset ~Rs 2 crore remaining on balance sheet; reversal timing at auditor discretion, typically visible in Q4; effective tax rate 25% post utilization
items.quote: So still we have some deferred tax in the asset which is around Rs. 2 crores or so. So in the next year, when it will be utilized that time it will be reversed.

items.statement: Consolidated revenue growth guided at 18-20% for FY26
items.quote: On a consolidated basis, we will grow for 18% to 20%, and that is basically driven by a higher growth rate contribution from the standalone entity, which is at over the 25% level, whereas at the subsidiary level we would be roughly flat, I would say.

items.statement: Standalone blended revenue growth guided at 25-28% for FY26
items.quote: at a standalone level both the EMS and the BTS part of the business should grow for us at a blended rate of somewhere in the range of about 25% to 28%.

items.statement: Consolidated EBITDA margin target of 10% for FY26
items.quote: Yes. That should be definitely be possible at the consol level.

items.statement: Consolidated EBITDA margin target of around 12% in next two years
items.quote: Yes. Definitely. I think that's our goal, to improve that from 10% to probably around 12% in the next two years.

items.statement: Consolidated revenue CAGR target of 18-20% for next three years
items.quote: As we have been maintaining, we are targeting 18% to 20% CAGR for the next three years.

items.statement: Total consolidated order book at Rs 1,736 crore as of March 31, 2025
items.quote: Our total order book position stands at Rs. 1,736 crores as of 31st March 2025.

items.statement: Standalone order book increased to Rs 1,330 crore from Rs 1,118 crore
items.quote: On a standalone basis itself, the order book increased to Rs. 1,330 crores, up from Rs. 1,118 crores at the end of the previous financial year.

items.statement: Order book executable over 15-18 months on overall basis
items.quote: And maybe at an overall basis something in the range of about 15 months or so, 15 odd months I would say, 15 to 18 months is what you can look at.

items.statement: BTS order book executable over 2-2.5 years, EMS under 12 months
items.quote: Typically our BTS order book is executable over say somewhere between two to two and a half years in terms of time horizon, whereas the EMS order book is typically less than 12 months, at this stage at least.

items.statement: Targeting Rs 2,000 crore of order booking in next 3-4 years on BTS defense and aerospace
items.quote: we are roughly looking at something in the range of about Rs. 2,000 crores of booking in the next three to four years, that's what we are targeting.

items.statement: Standalone Q4 FY25 EBITDA margin at 17.37%
items.quote: With one of the best quarterly EBITDA margins , we have reported 17.37%.

items.statement: Consolidated Q4 FY25 EBITDA margin at 11.31%
items.quote: The EBITDA for the quarter was Rs. 42 crores which grew by around 115% quarter-on-quarter and 132% year-on-year, with EBITDA margin reported at 11.31%.

items.statement: Standalone FY25 EBITDA margin at 13.6%
items.quote: The EBITDA for the period was about Rs. 102 crores, which increased by around 30% year-on-year with the EBITDA margins reported at 13.6%.

items.statement: Consolidated FY25 EBITDA margin at 8.37%
items.quote: The EBITDA stood at around Rs. 97 crores which increased by 12.6% with EBITDA margin at 8.37%.

items.statement: BTS EBITDA margin typically around 20%, EMS at 10-12%
items.quote: your typical EBITDA margin for build-to-spec can be in the range of 20% or so . And whereas on the EMS side of the business, it's more build-to-print, and that is typically in the 10% to 12% level or so.

items.statement: Planning Rs 40 crore capex in FY26 for standalone to augment BTS and EMS capabilities
items.quote: We are planning to invest about Rs. 40 crores, that again only in the standalone, essentially to augment the capabilities and increase the capacities, both in the BTS segment as well as the EMS segment.

items.statement: Strong demand visibility from order intake and customer forecasts for both BTS and EMS
items.quote: on the build-to-spec side of the business, with the order intake that we have had, I think the demand side of it is relatively secure. Similarly, on the EMS side of the business as well, we have a clear plan and visibility of which specific products and customers will be driving this growth based on either firm orders or customer forecasts that we have received from them.

items.statement: Added new customers in semiconductor equipment and biometric solutions for EMS growth
items.quote: One being in semiconductor equipment where we have an important customer that we have added, and another one is in biometric solutions. So these are there . And apart from that, of course, our existing customers itself in the aerospace and defense side of it, we have continued to add new part numbers and also some increased volumes on existing part numbers.

items.statement: Consolidated working capital increased to 87 days due to higher Q4 billings
items.quote: Our working capital has increased at a consolidated level to 87 days, primarily due to higher billings in Q4.

items.statement: Raised Rs 210 crore via QIP, repaid Rs 110 crore debt, remainder for capex and corporate purposes
items.quote: we successfully raised Rs. 210 crores from our marquee investors via a QIP during the last quarter, which reflects a strong confidence in our company's future growth potential. The fund utilization has been for debt reduction Rs. 115 crores. Out of which, we have already repaid Rs. 110 crores , w hile the remaining funds are strategically allocated towards CAPEX and general corporate purposes

items.statement: French engineering services revenue declined, cost optimization underway
items.quote: Having said that, I think we also have seen some revenue decline in our French subsidiary on the engineering services side . A nd that has resulted in, I guess, degradation of the margin compared to the previous year

items.statement: Space applications 40-50% of BTS order book, rest defense across Army, Navy, Air Force
items.quote: space applications are I would say in the range of somewhere about 40% to 50% of that part. And the rest is non -space or more defense side of the business , and this cuts across different applications.

items.statement: No firm requests received for expedited SBS-3 procurement despite media reports
items.quote: we have not received any firm requests or anything of that sort right now in terms of expediting S BS3 or anything like that. So, we have no specific comment as such on that.

items.statement: EMS business largely export-oriented to global OEMs, domestic contribution rising
items.quote: And then similarly we also do in the EMS part of the business, where we are manufacturing products to customers' designs. And this part of the business is largely export oriented to global customers.

items.statement: Q4 EBITDA was 1500 million vs expected 1724 million due to one-time employee cost and other expense increases including 8 crore inventory and receivables cleanup
items.quote: Considering that sales grew by almost 15%, our EBITDA should have been about 1724 million, against that we did about 1500 million.

items.statement: One-time expenses of ~8 crore for inventory and receivables cleanup impacted Q4 and full-year EBITDA; will shift to quarterly cleanup going forward
items.quote: We cleaned up some of our books in India in other parts of the world. We cleaned up some inventory and we cleaned up some receivables, not so much as a loss, but as a prudent accounting thing. So that is to the extent of about 8 crores, we did that, but this is not just for the quarters, for the whole year.

items.statement: Five-year guidance targets $450 million revenue, 16% EBITDA margin, 30% ROCE by FY25-26; confident of achieving these numbers
items.quote: Five years ago, we gave a guidance about our top line 450 million. And the EBITDA of 16% and the return on cash capital employed of 30%. We will be able to achieve these numbers in 25-26, so that is really what I can give as a guidance now.

items.statement: Conservative outlook: minimum same growth as FY25 (~9%) if global conditions stabilize; India expected low to mid double-digit growth
items.quote: Minimum do this same growth as last year.

items.statement: India inquiries healthy but finalizations delayed due to wait-and-watch approach; textiles sector recovering; overall no concern yet but early days for tariff impact
items.quote: Inquiries are still healthy. There is no problem, but people are. There is a wait and watch approach.

items.statement: Portable compressor market down 30-40% over last couple of years; expected to remain subdued in current year
items.quote: Portables is a more a market structural thing. You know for three years there is a big growth and since the last couple of years there has been a significant almost a 30-40% drop in the market and we are feeling the effect of it and we expect this this portable to remain subdued in the current year as well.

items.statement: Motor plant investment nearing completion; 85-90% of global motors to be manufactured in-house this financial year, providing cost advantage to absorb tariff impact
items.quote: This financial year close to 85 to 90% of our motors globally will be manufactured by us and that's going to give us a significant advantage to be able to absorb the impact of the tariff without any compromise on profitability in the US market.

items.statement: Cost reduction initiatives (including motor plant) sufficient to absorb 10% tariff (base case) and up to 16% reciprocal tariff without pricing or profitability compromise in US
items.quote: Assuming that's a best case 10%. And if we look at import of compressors from the US into India and that is. At currently about 16 and 1/2 percent. And assuming they are going to make it in the worst-case reciprocal to that same percentage in this range, we are pretty much ok with all the cost reduction initiatives we can sustain our current pricing and our profitability.

items.statement: Europe recovery fragile; potential US tariffs on EU could significantly impact European business; monitoring closely and preparing structural cost changes if needed
items.quote: Europe was already fragile. And it was recovering after the Ukraine war and all those issues, and we were beginning to grow slowly. We've all broke broken even last year. Now there is going to be a challenge in Europe and we don't know how it is going to be.

items.statement: Siemens railway compressor order validated and machines deployed; expect business movement in Q3-Q4 FY26, significant improvement next year; metro rail discussions ongoing with global OEMs (5-year journey)
items.quote: We have supplied and you know our Prime Minister inaugurated the first locomotive. And if you actually see the video of that locomotive running on the tracks, you will see in the undercarriage of the locomotive. A device with a red band and that's an ELGI machine.

items.statement: Aftermarket share ~27-28% of India revenue, ~13-14% of rest of world; both expected to improve progressively with installed base growth
items.quote: In India our aftermarket would be close to, I don't have the numbers readily in front of me, but I'm making an intelligent guess. It's about 27-28% is on our revenue in India in the rest of the world, we are probably around 13 to 14% right now.

items.statement: Generating 97-98% of profit as cash; strong receivables control processes showing impact; global inventory control project expected to yield results in Q2-Q3 FY26
items.quote: We've generating close to 97 to 98% of our Profit we are generating every quarter. We have put in very strong. Processes for receivables control that is beginning to show its impact.

items.statement: Chinese imports ~25-30% of Indian market volume in low-kW segment; ELGI developed competitive range matching Chinese price-performance without quality compromise; optimistic on capturing share
items.quote: We think that the size of that market is anywhere between 25 to 30% of in volume terms. If they sell primarily on the low end of a low kilowatt machines, not in the high kilowatt.

items.statement: Motor plant capacity sufficient for 85-90% in-house production; initial supplier issues resolved, Chinese equipment installation now proceeding with visa clearance
items.quote: We're quite confident. That we have the capacity. That's not an issue.

items.statement: US business profitable on steady-state basis excluding one-time cleanup; Europe broken even in FY25; Australia recovering; Middle East and Brazil performed well
items.quote: US has from a loss in the prior year has actually become profitable on a steady state basis now.

items.statement: US tariff initially 26%, temporarily reduced to 10%; base case 10%, worst case reciprocal 16.5%; monitoring Europe impact if US imposes tariffs on EU
items.quote: We started off with 26%. Which is a pretty challenging number to manage it from a cost point of view. It's been reduced down temporarily to 10%.

items.statement: Growth path includes adjacencies via acquisitions or in-house development; dryers already launched globally; consciously avoiding refrigeration and gas segments
items.quote: We are expanding the range of our adjacencies by either looking at acquisition opportunities for specific adjacencies or in House development of these adjacencies, which is really what our growth path is going to be.

items.statement: International business investing only in revenue-producing roles; offshoring overhead processes via shared services to reduce costs structurally over next couple of years
items.quote: We are focusing on only investing in revenue producing roles and we are trying to through shared services and offshoring some of the overhead processes. We are reducing the overheads in all these locations all over the world.

items.statement: Management aims to sustain full-year gross margin around 40% and EBITDA margin at the higher end of mid-to-high teens range
items.quote: On a full financial year, we did deliver 40.4% of gross margin, and this is about 5%, 6% improvement versus the last financial year. And we believe that our endeavor i s to sustain this kind of gross margin and EBITDA going forward

items.statement: Announced INR 1,400 million capex for new HVDC Thyristor/VSC Valves line at Pallavaram and HVDC Controls facility in Noida; plus INR 800-900 million for debottlenecking existing lines, total INR 2,400-2,500 million over 1-2 years
items.quote: So overall put together, INR140 crores plus roughly INR80 crores, we have now announced overall capex in the range of INR240 crores to INR250 crores.

items.statement: No existing HVDC valve/control capacity; new lines being built from scratch; existing transformer/switchgear capacity being debottlenecked
items.quote: Today, on the HVDC valves and control side there is no existing capacity and whatever we are adding is going to be the new capacity.

items.statement: Q4 order bookings INR 29.9 billion, up 124% YoY; full-year order intake INR 107 billion (INR 77 billion excluding two large one-off orders), nearly double prior year
items.quote: Our order book remained strong in Q4 and we saw bookings of INR 29.9 billion, up by 124% YoY, compared to INR 13.3 billion in quarter ended Mar' 24.

items.statement: Order backlog doubled to INR 126.6 billion as at March 2025 vs INR 62.7 billion a year earlier
items.quote: New orders outpaced revenue, doubling the order backlog at 126.6 BINR as at Mar'25 vs 62.7 BINR as at March'24.

items.statement: Q4 gross margin 42.3%; full-year gross margin 40.4%, up 5-6 percentage points YoY driven by better pricing, product mix shift, export share, and execution
items.quote: On a full financial year, we did deliver 40.4% of gross margin, and this is about 5%, 6% improvement versus the last financial year.

items.statement: Pricing environment stable; no significant further improvement expected but able to pass on raw material increases if they occur
items.quote: So I would say that the pricing is stable as of now. Maybe we don't see much improvement coming there. If there is an increase in raw material prices, we are able to pass on.

items.statement: Strategy shifting toward product orders (transformers, switchgear, GIS, HVDC components) over turnkey projects for better margins and lower execution risk
items.quote: And as a strategy, we are moving towards product orders and -- rather than focusing on turnkey orders that leads to a better margin profile. So mix is improving.

items.statement: India targeting 35% transmission capacity increase by FY32; management sees strong domestic demand across transformers, switchgear, HVDC, and grid technologies; export TAM growing in Europe, Middle East, Southeast Asia, Africa
items.quote: India is aiming to increase its power transmission capacity by 35% by FY32, focusing on integrating renewable energy and securing 24x7 power supply.

items.statement: Order book diversified across Power Grid, Sterlite, Adani, Jindal, state utilities, EPCs, and export markets; state utility share kept small by design
items.quote: We secured orders of 765 kV power transformer and reactors from Power Grid. Similarly, we secured 765 kV power transformer and reactor from Sterlite. We also secured orders from Adani Group for 400 kV GIS.

items.statement: Export momentum maintained across Europe, Southeast Asia, Africa, Latin America; US market served from US factories due to technology difference; export mix target ~30% of revenue
items.quote: That is what is always our endeavor to maintain that kind of a ratio.

items.statement: Cash generated INR 8.3 billion in FY25; cash and equivalents INR 10.5 billion at March 2025 vs INR 2.8 billion a year earlier; surplus cash invested in GEV group cash pool
items.quote: The cash and cash equivalent balance was at 10.5 BINR as on March 31, 2025 vs 2.8 BINR as at March 31, 2024. The cash generated was 1.9 BINR in Q4 and 8.3 BINR during the FY 24-25.

items.statement: Company moved from net debt to net cash position; surplus funds deployed in group cash pool earning market-rate interest with on-demand liquidity
items.quote: We have taken shareholder approval regularly to invest surplus cash to the cash pool, which is managed by the GEV Group.

items.statement: Board recommended dividend of INR 5 per share (~INR 130 million outflow) for FY25; conscious deployment of cash between capex and shareholder returns
items.quote: the Board has recommended a dividend of INR5 per share. Once approved by the shareholders, that will lead to an outflow of roughly INR130 crores.

items.statement: HVDC project pipeline dependent on government transmission committee approvals; at least 1-2 projects expected to be decided in FY26; Khavda-South Olpad under bidding
items.quote: One of the project that had gone for the approval of the committee, there was some discussion about feasibility of batteries storage. Let the committee work out various options. But we expect at least 1 to 2 projects to get decided during this year.

items.statement: Key risks: global supply chain volatility and geopolitical uncertainty; demand outlook stable for 3-10 years driven by energy transition
items.quote: As we said that, of course, supply chain management, yes, that's a big risk because not only about the availability, but also about the political situation keep on developing globally as well.

items.statement: Revenue grew 35% YoY to INR 42.9 billion in FY25; Q4 revenue up 26% YoY to INR 11.5 billion
items.quote: On an FY basis, our FY24-25 revenue stood at 42.9 billion INR vs 31.7 billion INR in FY23-24, up by 35% YoY.

items.statement: Profit before tax and exceptional items tripled to INR 8.2 billion in FY25 from INR 2.6 billion in FY24
items.quote: From a FY24-25 perspective, profit before tax and exceptional items stood at 8,197 million INR vs. 2,631 million INR in FY23-24, which is a 3x times increase.

items.statement: No plans for backward integration into component manufacturing (e.g., CRGO); supply chain risks managed through dedicated supplier engagement teams
items.quote: As of today, we are not planning to backward integrate any of the component level manufacturing.

items.statement: Indian factories are cost-competitive strength for GE Vernova globally; localization investments enhance competitiveness for domestic and export HVDC/STATCOM opportunities
items.quote: Today for any such large opportunity, Indian factories are really the strength for GE Vernova to go and take these orders.

items.statement: No management changes or key hires discussed; credited team dedication for performance
items.quote: As we transition into FY 2025-26, I am grateful for the unwavering dedication of our entire team. Their efforts are the foundation of our optimism for future.

items.statement: Royalty payments to parent increased to INR 640 million in FY25 from INR 350 million in FY24, linked to revenue formula
items.quote: During the entire year, we have made a royalty payment of roughly INR640 million.

items.statement: Management targets overall gross margin of about 60% on a blended basis.
items.quote: But in general, about 60% overall gross margin is what the company targets. And we are normally somewhere close to that.

items.statement: COGS was 41% in Q4 FY25, improving from 43% in Q3 FY25; full-year FY25 COGS at 40%, flat year-on-year.
items.quote: The cost of goods sold on a stand-alone basis is around 41% in Q4. There is a slight improvement from the Q3 of the current financial year. It was about 43%.

items.statement: Employee cost 14% of revenue in Q4 vs 17% in Q3; full-year steady at 17%. Other expenses 14% in Q4 vs 15% in Q3; full-year 13% vs 14% prior year.
items.quote: Employee costs are 14% of total revenue in Q4. In comparison, this was 17% of the total revenue in the third quarter. That said, on an annual basis, this has remained steady at 17% for the current year and the previous year.

items.statement: EBITDA grew 10.4% in FY25.
items.quote: The EBITDA growth was 10.4%.

items.statement: Q4 revenue split: printers 14%, consumables 58%, spares 11%, services 16%.
items.quote: For this quarter, the breakup between printers, consumables, spares and service is 14%, 58%, 11%, 16%.

items.statement: Codeology UK has a good order pipeline and expects a profitable year ahead.
items.quote: And regarding the growth for the Codeology Limited performance in the U.K., there was a bit of recession for them in 1.5 years before. But now it has been ironed out and there's good order pipeline with us. And we believe that like the next year would be a good profitable business for the stand-alone Codeology U.K. operations.

items.statement: V-Shapes packaging capacity 15-40 machines/year depending on model mix; sold 3 machines last year (2 large, 1 small), none installed in FY25.
items.quote: In terms of the capacity of what we do in V-Shapes, it really depends on the types of machines we are selling. It could be as few as like 15 all the way up to 40.

items.statement: V-Shapes breakeven on materials at ~60-70 small machines installed; large machines count as 2.5-3x small.
items.quote: I think we have like about , Jaideep, I mean I think we did calculation, we hav e like 60 or 70 machines, or maybe less or more. But I think something like that of the Twin Prime, the smaller machines, we have like 60, 70 of them, I think we should be breakeven on the material business.

items.statement: Packaging subsidiary operational loss ~₹20 cr in FY25; expected to reduce in FY26 as machines installed generate recurring material revenue, but cash burn may continue due to reinvestment.
items.quote: think it was about ₹20 crores approximately, if I remember in the year gone by. Jaideep Barve: Yes. Shiva Kabra: So we definitely expect that to reduce over the course of the year, like if you look at the overall annual basis

items.statement: Track & Trace addressable market estimated at ₹400-500 cr in India (equipment + software), growing; pharma primary, also agrochemicals, explosives.
items.quote: We estimate it to be about ₹400-odd crores as of right now. Like I said, it's mainly geared towards the pharmaceutical sector and certain other regu lated sectors

items.statement: Consumables pricing: competitors more aggressive; CPL passes cost increases with lag, not used as revenue lever; rupee depreciation may prompt price hikes in FY26.
items.quote: Some of our competitors have been a bit more aggressive in terms of increasing prices than us. I think I've disclosed that in the past. And there's now, I'd say, more of a pricing gap between , a little bit of a pricing gap between our three competitors and us.

items.statement: Track & Trace: four major players (ACG, Jekson Vision, OPTEL, PharmaSecure); CPL aims for technological superiority and >30% value delta to win switch.
items.quote: So like I said, ACG, Associated Capsules Group, which is a well -known company in India, and it's a very good company, is the biggest player in this business, then Jekson Vision, OPTEL and PharmaSecure. So the four of them are in this, four good competitors.

items.statement: Track & Trace driven by government compliance mandates in pharma, agrochemicals, explosives; L1-L5 compliance required.
items.quote: The first is the compliance, which is the essential element that everyone needs to meet. So everyone has to be compliant with the new government rules and also for certain export markets these rules are in place.

items.statement: Standalone revenue: Q4 FY25 ₹114 cr (up from ₹98 cr), FY25 ₹395 cr (vs ₹347 cr FY24, ₹295 cr FY23).
items.quote: The total revenue for the entire financial year '24 -'25 is ₹395 crores. Just for information, for '23 -'24 and '22 -'23, the total income was ₹347 crores and ₹295 crores, respectively.

items.statement: Core coding & marking industry growing ~10%; CPL targets slightly above with better product mix and new digital/thermal inkjet products.
items.quote: We believe we've got a slightly better product mix. So we should do 10%, maybe a bit more. And we've done that over the last two, three, four years or something like that.

items.statement: Deferred tax asset ₹49.5 cr recognised from MAT credit (Guwahati Sec 80IE); expect zero tax for next 2-3 years as asset utilised.
items.quote: So what has happened is that in our MA T, we had a credit of about ₹49.50 some crores. And since now there's a virtual certainty that we can reali se the same out of profit stability in the next two, three years.

items.statement: No major cost increases planned across subsidiaries; may add 1-2 sales/marketing heads in Track & Trace and packaging.
items.quote: Other than that we're not going to see any major cost increases, unless there's some unforeseen issues that happen. So in that case, as we sell more, we should get some more operational leverage and the SG&A will be spread over a bigger revenue base.

items.statement: V-Shapes packaging material: aluminium-layer barrier film; piloting recyclable material to cut cost from ₹2 to ₹1 per 10ml pack and enable recyclability.
items.quote: Our core material got an aluminium layer in it for a perfect barrier. We are trying to work very aggressively to come with a sort of recyclable material. We've done pilot projects on that and it's working well, it seems.

items.statement: V-Shapes co-packing for sampling/awareness (e.g., Bombay Shaving Company); not a core focus, aim to convert to machine sales.
items.quote: We have some customers that we are doing it, including like I think some people see like Bombay Shaving, of course. Like I'm only saying this name because he himself has put it on his own X and Twitter and other handle, we never disclose a customer.

items.statement: Track & Trace success uncertain; need to prove ROI to displace incumbents; if no strong delta, business will be just another supplier.
items.quote: And if they don't see that, then ye ah, we still got a good solution, but then we're just like another supplier, and we'll still do okay, but it's not going to be like a fun business.

items.statement: Codeology acquired March 2024; synergies via holistic solutions (conveyor, print & apply) for India market.
items.quote: Now the Codeology as a company, it provides a ho listic solution. So it is much more in addition to the pure coding and marking business what we do. So it involves like the conveyor systems, the coding and marking, the end -of-line print and apply systems.
