items.quote: South is the major contributor because being a coastal world that acceptance for the good substitute solution, particularly the polymer-based product is more from the South India. So we can say around 40% revenue is coming from the South India itself. And then the major market after South India is the Eastern part that West Bengal, Odisha region.

items.statement: PVC profile: listed peer Kaka Industries plus regional players; WPC Doors: new solution for Indian market
items.quote: See competitor in the PVC profile extrusion, which is a B2B segment. That listed peer, there is only one party as currently which is from Gujarat Kaka Industries and then there are several regional players everywhere, so many regional players are there.

items.statement: Debt ~Rs. 53 crores stagnant; aims to be debt-free in 4-5 years via internal accruals
items.quote: You can see that in current financial year, we have very good cash flows with us, in fact around Rs. 25 crores plus cash profit is there in the books. So going forward , based on the increased business and all , so this should also increase. So considering the profitability and incremental business, so that CAPEX can be met out mostly with the internal accruals and at the same time, our vision to

items.statement: Average cost of debt <8.5% for both long-term and short-term
items.quote: It is lesser than 8.5%.

items.statement: Board recommended higher dividend of 7% vs 5% in past two years
items.quote: In recognition of the Company's robust financial performance and healthy balance sheet, the brand has recommended a higher dividend of 7% compared to 5% in each of the past 2 years.

items.statement: Headcount rose to 700+ from 500+; major addition at new Bangalore fluted/soffit plant
items.quote: We had started our manufacturing factory in Bangalore for the fluted and soffit. So that major addition is in that plant only.

items.statement: Added 15+ sales heads in FY25; plans more ground-level sales force hiring
items.quote: In fact, in last year also, we have added more than 15 heads in sales front.

items.statement: Marketing & sales promotion spend Rs. 3.26 crores in FY25 (+50% YoY); targets 2% of revenue
items.quote: Our marketing and sales promotion expenses stood at Rs. 3.26 crores in Financial Year '25, reflecting a 50% increase over Financial Year '24.

items.statement: Plans 2 new Studio Arezzo showrooms in FY26 (South & West); 4 showrooms currently (2 exclusive)
items.quote: Yes, for the current Financial Year '26, we have planned for two more studio, Arezzo Studio to be added.

items.statement: Fluted panel segment target Rs. 100 crores revenue in 2-3 years
items.quote: Rs. 100 crores, just our plan is to do it in within 2 years, next 2 years maybe, or you can take it 2-3 years we will achieve, take this segment to Rs. 100 crores level.

items.statement: Management guided for double-digit revenue growth in FY26 and improvement in EBITDA margins from current levels
items.quote: And as far as looking ahead in the guidance for financial '26, I think we are very confident of achieving double-digit growth going forward in next financial year. And also, we are very hopeful of improving our EBITDA from this level also.

items.statement: Management indicated they may revise guidance upwards in Q2 FY26 if performance meets expectations
items.quote: Yes, we can revise our guidance in Q2 con call. So, if we see that everything is going as per the expectation, we may revise our guidance upwards in Q2 onwards.

items.statement: Management expects EBITDA margin to reach above 20% including other income in FY26
items.quote: I'm confident that we'll be touching above 20% going forward, including other income.

items.statement: Management expects EBITDA margin excluding other income to be around 200 basis points lower than including other income
items.quote: Then it should be around 200 basis points.

items.statement: Price hikes of 6-8% taken in FY25 and 8-10% taken for FY26 across all categories
items.quote: So last year, across all categories on average, 6% to 8% price hike was taken. And this year, 8% to 10% price hike was taken.

items.statement: Trade show response was very good with over 1,500 retailers attending and strong order book giving confidence for double-digit growth
items.quote: We just concluded our 7-day winter trade show and the response was very good. We had more than 1,500 retailers coming over for the trade show and we've gotten a very good order book.

items.statement: Summer volumes growing year-on-year, summer wear now 30-35% of total garment sales vs 4-5% a decade ago
items.quote: So summer is one area where the company is continuously growing from last 4, 5 years. That is why the overall percentage of summer wear has actually increased from last 3, 4 years as compared to winter wear sales.

items.statement: Plan to open 45-50 Monte Carlo EBOs and 10-15 Clock & Decker EBOs in FY26, continuing pace for next 2 years
items.value: 45 to 50 Monte Carlo stores and 10 to 15 Clock & Decker stores
items.quote: So, this year also, we have plan to open 45 to 50 Monte Carlo stores and 10 to 15 Clock & Decker stores. And so, the speed will continue, I think, going forward for next 2 years.

items.statement: Store openings spread across Tier 1 to Tier 5 cities, 80-85% in North/East/Central, 15-20% in West/South
items.quote: So last year also, we have said that the 80% to 85% would be opening in our main regions, that is Northern and Eastern and Central region. And the 20% balance would be opened in the Western and Southern region, 15% to 20%.

items.statement: Winter wear remains dominant but summer share increasing; target 45-55% summer/winter ratio in 1-2 years
items.quote: But definitely, winter wear has been a very huge segment. So, it might take 1 or 2 more years for a company to have around 45% to 55% ratio.

items.statement: MBO channel declining; shutting ~150 low-performing MBOs in West Bengal/Northeast to open own EBOs instead
items.quote: And so, what we've taken a call is we are going to shut down these 150-odd MBO outlets and instead open our own exclusive brand outlets to service these markets.

items.statement: LFS/SOR business growing at better terms with stronger negotiating power vs 2 years ago
items.quote: Now that leaves lesser brands in the market to service the winter wear market for players like Reliance or all of these large-format stores. Saying that, we are increasing our sales and number of doors with Reliance and all the other major large-format stores, but these are at a better term than what we were doing a couple of years back.

items.statement: Expect 5-10 days reduction in debtor days through distributor advance payment arrangements
items.quote: We expect 5 to 10 days of debtor days should come down going forward.

items.statement: Creditor days reduced to 45 days due to MSME payment regulations; inventory days expected to remain at current levels +/-5%
items.quote: But creditors basically have come down because of MSME. There we have to make the payments in 45 days to our creditors. So that is basically as per the government regulations. So, 45 days payment, we have to make to all our vendors.

items.statement: Salesforce and Tableau software implemented to improve retail merchandise planning and reduce inventory in EBOs
items.quote: We have installed Salesforce software, our Tableau software. So that led us to give us the better planning as far as our retail merchandise are concerned in our EBOs even at our other stores.

items.statement: Net finance cost near zero - INR34 cr interest cost offset by INR34 cr other income from investments
items.quote: So actual finance cost is only INR34 crores. And the other income is basically from government bonds, mutual funds, and debt, that is, again, INR34 crores. So, on a net basis, we are not paying any money to the bank as far as finance cost is concerned.

items.statement: Board discussed plans to deploy INR290 cr cash reserves but details not disclosed; may share in next con call
items.quote: So, there are some plans which have been discussed in the Board meeting, but I might not be able to disclose at this point of time. But maybe we can come out with some of the points in the next con call.

items.statement: Board recommended final dividend of INR20 per equity share (200%) for FY25
items.quote: The Board of Directors, in its meeting held yesterday, has recommended a final dividend of INR20 per equity share, that is 200%, having a face value of INR10 each for financial year 2024-'25.

items.statement: Exporting Monte Carlo branded goods via Amazon to US/Canada and tied up with Landmark Group's Style for 8,000-10,000 pieces in UAE
items.quote: Also, last week, we had 2 members from our team visiting Dubai for the IATF, which is the International Trade Fair. And we've also tied up with Style, which is from the Landmark Group in the UAE, to supply around 8,000 to 10,000 pieces of Monte Carlo products in the UAE market.

items.statement: Clock & Decker EBOs achieving target of INR8,000 per sq ft annual sales across 12 stores opened in last 8 months
items.value: INR8,000 per square foot per annum
items.quote: So, we targeted around INR8,000 per square feet sales. So, I'm pleased to share that we have been achieving this kind of sales in the last 1 year where we have started. It's almost 8 months and already 12 EBOs we have opened. So, we are getting a sale of around INR8,000 per square foot per annum.

items.statement: Same-store sales growth declined ~4% in FY25
items.quote: But as far as SSG is concerned, last year, we had seen a decline of around 4% in SSG, same-store growth.

items.statement: Q4 profitability impacted by early EOSS discounting and returns; provisioning increased to target zero Q4 loss in FY26
items.quote: And the third is that more of our business is now going into SOR. So, returns are more as compared to financial '22 as we are increasing our business in LFS, we're increasing in SOR, EBOs and SIS. So that also affects the profitability. But still, the company is taking adequate provisioning to improve on the fourth quarter results.

items.statement: Tax rate elevated to 29% in FY25 due to long-term capital gains structure change; steady-state rate 25.168%
items.quote: Actually, this year, there is a change in the long-term capital gain structure. So, this year, deferred tax element has changed. The context is okay. So next year, it will not be like this. 29%, it has come because of this budget changes with respect to the long-term capital gains.

items.statement: Quick commerce partnerships with Blinkit and Swiggy piloted in Delhi NCR for pre-winter/winter clothing; exploring home furnishing with Swiggy
items.quote: So, with Blinkit and Swiggy, we are piloting in the Delhi NCR or the northern part of the country as of now. So, these are basically pre-winter and winter clothing, along with -- we are also speaking with Swiggy on an exclusive tie-up for our home furnishing category.

items.statement: Ajay Agarwal joined as President, Finance and Strategy with 24 years experience
items.quote: Before we begin, I would like to take a moment to introduce Mr. Ajay Agarwal, who has joined us as President, Finance and Strategy. Mr. Agarwal is a chartered accountant and lawyer, brings over 24 years of experience in the areas of strategy and finance.

items.statement: Indian auto industry grew ~6% YoY in Q4 FY25 driven by 2-wheeler premiumization and EV adoption
items.quote: Overall, the industry delivered about a 6% Y-o-Y growth in Q4, underpinned by increased EV traction, product premiumization and rising consumer affordability.

items.statement: Highest ever quarterly revenue INR 1,321 cr, EBITDA INR 153 cr at 11.6% margin in Q4 FY25
items.quote: The Company surpassed consensus estimates, delivering the highest-ever quarterly revenue of INR 1,321 crores, a growth of 9% on a Y-o-Y basis. The Company reported highest-ever EBITDA of INR 153 crores, along with the highest ever margin of 11.6% for the quarter

items.statement: FY25 full year revenue INR 5,056 cr, EBITDA INR 575 cr at 11.4% margin, PAT INR 255 cr
items.quote: For the full year FY25, the Company delivered highest ever annual revenue of INR 5,056 crores, registering a growth of 9% Y-o-Y basis. The Company reported highest EBITDA of INR 575 crores, a growth of 12% Y-o-Y with a margin expansion of 31 basis points

items.statement: Lifetime orders booked exceeding INR 8,000 cr in FY25 with ~25% from EV platforms
items.quote: During the year, the Company booked lifetime orders exceeding INR 8,000 crores with approximately 25% of new orders coming from electric vehicle platforms.

items.statement: Acquired 49% stake in Flash Electronics for powertrain and EV components
items.quote: In January 2025, Minda Corporation entered into a strategic partnership through the acquisition of 49% stake in Flash Electronics, a key player in powertrain and EV components in India.

items.statement: EV sales ~8% of Minda Corp revenue in Q4 FY25, ~7% for full year FY25
items.quote: In Q4, EV sales stood at about 8% of the Minda Corporation's total revenue and on a full year basis, it is approximately 7%.

items.statement: Flash Electronics EV revenue 23% of its INR 1,537 cr revenue, up 92% YoY
items.quote: Flash Electronics has its 23% of its revenue coming from EV products, which is a 92% growth over the previous year.

items.statement: Capex guidance INR 250-350 cr for standalone, INR 50-100 cr for Flash Electronics
items.quote: Going forward, we see the capex to remain in the range of about INR 250 crores to max INR 350 crores. And as regards the capex in Flash is concerned, again, that should broadly be in the range of INR 50 crores to INR 100 crores only.

items.statement: Two greenfield facilities planned in next 18 months for die casting and information & connected systems
items.quote: Well, in this, say, in the course of next 18 months, we are also talking of 2 gree nfield manufacturing facilities, of which one Akash covered in die casting and the other is in information and connected systems

items.statement: Net debt INR 1,250 cr, net debt/EBITDA 1.8x, target to reduce debt/equity from 0.5x to 0.2x in 2-3 years
items.quote: The net debt is INR 1,250 crores with the capital employed is INR 1,975 crores. The ROCE is 20% and net debt to net worth is 0.6x and net debt to EBITDA, which is including 49% of Flash EBITDA is 1.8x.

items.statement: Promoter warrant funds INR 420 cr over 18 months (25% within 2 weeks, 75% within 18 months)
items.quote: We are expecting the stock exchanges approval within this week, and 25% of the money should be received max within 2 weeks and thereafter, as per the terms, the balance 75% can be paid by the promoters within 18 months.

items.statement: Board recommended final dividend 45% of face value (INR 0.90/share), total 70% for FY25
items.quote: In view of this, the Board of Directors has recommended a final dividend of 45% on the face value, that is INR 0.90 per equity share, totaling to 70% on the overall.

items.statement: Wiring harness 28%, vehicle access 24%, die casting 16%, clusters 16%, others 16% of revenue
items.quote: Wiring harness continues to be about 28%; vehicle access 24%; die casting 16%; clusters 16%; and others, which includes our sensors, EV products, other electronics is growing to 16% now.

items.statement: Exports ~7% of revenue, Southeast Asia (Indonesia, Vietnam) ~5%, order book exports ~15%
items.quote: By geography, India continues to be majority at about 88%. Our exports are about 7% and Southeast Asia locations, which is Indonesia and Vietnam, contribute about 5%.

items.statement: Export wiring harness lifetime order book INR 700 cr secured in Q4 FY25
items.quote: We secured multiple export orders for wiring harness in particular, with lifetime order book of INR 700 crores.

items.statement: Sensors revenue INR 250-300 cr in FY25, expected to grow with localization and new SOPs
items.quote: for the current year, our sensors revenue is in the tune of about INR 250 crores to INR 300 crores. This is expected to grow further while we are localizing many sensors in India

items.statement: Flash Electronics revenue growth expected mid-to-high double-digit percentage in FY26
items.quote: So Raghu, the growth momentum in the revenue of Flash Electronics should be again in the similar range that they have been doing for the last few years. So, again, in the range of mid- to high double-digit percentage.

items.statement: Cross-selling synergies with Flash identified in 3 areas (die casting, wiring harness, electronics), targeting 3-digit crore by FY27
items.quote: we have already identified 3 important areas for cross-selling. These products such as die casting or wiring harnesses and electronic components needs end customer approval. So that is already underway and hopefully, by end of the year, we shall have these in SOP. And by FY27, we can see maybe close to a 3-digit number coming into cross-selling.

items.statement: FY25 capex INR 350 cr vs INR 200-300 cr range in prior years
items.quote: As you can see that over the last 2-3 years, our capex has been in the range of about INR 200 crores to INR 300 crores, while this year, we spent about INR 350 crores.

items.statement: Overall utilization 65-80% across segments and plants
items.quote: But overall, we, as an organization, are currently working to the tune of about 65% to 80% of utilization. So different segments, different plants will have that variation.

items.statement: Digital clusters 25-30% of Minda Instruments revenue, targeting 40% in 18-24 months
items.quote: currently about INR 800 crores plus revenue of the Minda Instruments Limited, you can say the digital clusters contribute somewhere about 25% to 30% and, of course, this is expected to grow to somewhere about 40% or so in the next, let's say, 18 months to 24 months.

items.statement: High-voltage connector localization target 20-25% in 18-24 months from current ~15%
items.quote: currently, our utilization of Minda connectors from our own Wiring Harness division is to the range of about 15%. And for the full year also, we have almost reached the same number. Now going forward, with our validations from our customers, both in high voltage or EV segment and Low-Voltage segments, this is expected to grow higher. Our target is to reach about 20% to 25% over the next 18 to 24 m

items.statement: Supplying high-voltage wiring harness to top 3 EV 2-wheeler OEMs and largest EV 3-wheeler OEMs
items.quote: we are supplying high-voltage wiring harness to the top 3 EV 2-wheeler manufacturers. We are already supplying them. In terms of the 3-wheelers also, the largest of all 3 manufacturers of the EV 3-wheelers, we are supplying our high-voltage kits to them.

items.statement: Quarterly depreciation run rate ~INR 55 cr, expected to continue
items.quote: In the range of about INR 55 crores that we have reported in this quarter.

items.statement: Flash Electronics EPS accretive from FY27, FY25 had only 75 days consolidation at PAT level
items.quote: However, we had said that this will be EPS accretive from FY27 and for the FY25, we have only 75 days of consolidation at the PAT level.

items.statement: Flash Electronics FY25 revenue INR 1,537 cr, EBITDA INR 223 cr at 14.5% margin, PAT INR 86 cr at 5.6%
items.quote: In line with our estimation, Flash Electronics has delivered INR 1,537 crores for the full year. EBITDA at about INR 223 crores with EBITDA margin of 14.5% and EV revenue stands at 23%.

items.statement: Sunroof JV plant revenues to start from FY27, not FY26, treated as associate company
items.quote: So Raghu, the revenues will not be in FY26. As we have committed before, the revenues will be starting from FY27. The plant which is next to our facility in the Pune region is in progress. and since this is a 50-50 joint venture, it will be treated as an associate Company.

items.statement: FY26 capex planned at INR 286 crores for network expansion and technology upgrades
items.quote: Looking ahead, we plan a capex of INR286 crores in FY '26 in line with our network expansion and technology upgrade plans.

items.statement: FY25 capex included INR 275 crores ROU creation, INR 400 crores fixed assets addition, and INR 250 crores net debt increase
items.value: INR 275 crores ROU, INR 400 crores fixed assets, INR 250 crores net debt
items.quote: Our expansion efforts led to ROU creation of INR275 crores, fixed assets addition of INR400 crores and an increase in net debt of about INR250 crores.

items.statement: Ahmedabad flagship center inaugurated with 189 beds, 9 OTs, 34 ICU beds, 22 day-care beds, 6 BMT units; expects 30-40% patient footfall increase
items.quote: We have started the year on a strong note with the formal inauguration of our flagship HCG Cancer Center in Ahmedabad, 189-bedded state-of-the-art facility that marks a significant milestone in our expansion journey.

items.statement: Two new Bangalore hospitals to open in H2 FY26: North Bangalore and Whitefield; targeting 900+ beds operationalized over next 3 years including 350 fully invested but not yet operational beds
items.quote: As informed earlier, we aim to expand in our existing markets by operationalizing over 900 beds across networks within next 3 years, including this year's addition and 350 beds that are fully invested but not yet operational.

items.statement: Q4 FY25 revenue grew 18% YoY to INR 585 crores; FY25 revenue grew 16% to INR 2,223 crores; core HCG centers (ex-Milann) grew 17%
items.quote: For the quarter ended 31st March 2025, we recorded a robust 18% year-on-year growth in revenue, reaching INR 585 crores. And on a full year basis, revenue grew 16% to INR 2,223 crores.

items.statement: Outpatient footfall rose 13.8%; chemotherapy sessions grew 24% YoY in Q4 FY25
items.quote: Outpatient footfall rose by 13.8%, indicating higher patient engagement. In medical oncology, we saw a 24% growth in chemotherapy sessions, a clear indicator of growing patient demand.

items.statement: Q4 FY25 adjusted EBITDA INR 106.9 crores at 18.3% margin; FY25 EBITDA INR 396.3 crores at 17.8% margin; established centers >20% margin, emerging centers ~10% margin
items.quote: Our adjusted EBITDA for the quarter was INR 106.9 crores, up 14% with margin of 18.3%, while for the full year, it stood at INR396.3 crores, a 17% increase with margin of 17.8%.

items.statement: Management targets low-20s EBITDA margin as initial goal; emerging centers scaling toward established center margins (>20%) but new greenfield centers may cause near-term dilution
items.quote: But is it good to say as the emerging centers also rack up, our margin, as we always indicated, will be in the low 20s. That is our initial goal.

items.statement: Network ARPOB increased 4% YoY to INR 44,236 in Q4 FY25; established centers ARPOB INR 42,591 (+2.5%), emerging centers ARPOB INR 66,755 (+12.4%)
items.quote: On the pricing and efficiency front, for the quarter ended 31st March '25, ARPOB across our network increased by 4%, reaching to INR 44,236.

items.statement: ARPOB growth guidance of 7-8% for FY26 driven by decreasing length of stay and high-end treatment modalities
items.quote: With continu ous decrease in length of stay in the hospital coupled with high end treatment modalities we expect 7% to 8% increase in ARPOB

items.statement: Digital revenue doubled in FY25; HCG mobile app launched for appointments, virtual consults, reports, and care journey management
items.quote: Digital revenue for FY '25 has doubled over the past year, and we are committed to scaling this further. We launched our official HCG mobile app, a platform that enables to book appointments, consult doctor virtually, access reports and manage their care journey end-to-end.

items.statement: Receivable days temporarily high at ~115 days end-March due to election-related collection delays; corrected to 105-107 days in April; new normal guided at 105-107 days
items.quote: So, I wouldn't say that the March number is the new normal. In fact, in terms of number of days, if I have to say, 105 to 107 should be the new normal, which we will maintain.

items.statement: Primary equity infusion from incoming investor KKR expected in coming months; quantum to be decided; proceeds may reduce debt and improve PAT
items.quote: We have communicated to the investors in the past that once the new investors, shareholders come, we will be looking at the possibility of primary equity coming into the system, and this will be decided in the coming few months.

items.statement: Acquired MG Hospital in Vizag (MGM) in H2 FY25; H2 revenue INR 50 crores, EBITDA INR 9.5 crores (adjusted INR 10.5 crores); targeting 25-30% EBITDA margin at steady state
items.value: INR 50 crores revenue, INR 9.5 crores EBITDA
items.quote: In terms of financial outcome, MGM had a revenue of INR50 crores in H2, with an EBITDA of INR9.5 crores.

items.statement: Planning to divest Milann fertility business this fiscal year; discussed with new investor KKR; former partner competition impacted performance
items.quote: So, we are definitely putting a proposal to divest. And hopefully, this will happen definitely this fiscal year, and we'll keep you updated.

items.statement: International patient revenue ~3-4% of total; Bangladesh visa restrictions impacted international business; domestic growth more than offset the decline
items.quote: Around 3-4% of revenue is from international.

items.statement: Maintained market leadership in all locations over last 3-4 years despite multi-specialty competition; gained largest market share in Kolkata and Mumbai within 4 years of entry
items.quote: We have not lost our market leadership in any of our locations in the last 3, 4 years in spite of competition coming in.

items.statement: Odisha government withdrew government scheme from non-Odisha states in Q4 FY25, causing ~INR 4.5 crores quarterly revenue loss at Vizag center
items.quote: quarter 4, Odisha government pull ed out its government scheme from non- Odisha states. And Vizag in Andhra Pradesh had been the largest beneficiary of treating patients from Odisha under the scheme

items.statement: LINAC utilization steady at 60% in Q4 FY25 with 2 new LINACs added via MGM acquisition over last 12 months; 5 LINACs added across centers in FY25
items.quote: Our LINAC machine utilization remained steady at 60% in quarter 4 of FY '25 with acquisition of 2 LINACs with MGM Hospital over the last 12 months.

items.statement: Medical oncology (chemotherapy) is least profitable but highly return-accretive modality; 24% chemo volume growth pressured gross margin but improves operating leverage long-term
items.quote: a financial outcome perspective, medical oncology modality is least profitable, but highly return accretive. So, the way we see it is as the medical oncology grows, it may have some pressure on our gross margin

items.statement: CVC paid transaction bonuses to some employees upon exit; approved by majority of minority shareholders; HCG not party to arrangement
items.quote: It is purely a thought process of CVC. They felt because of their exit; they should reward the bonus for some employees. And for this, there was an approval by the majority of the minority shareholders.

items.statement: International business suppressed due to India-Bangladesh geopolitical issues reducing medical visas; expected to continue for few months until relations normalize
items.quote: That is the major reason for the impact on international business across India, across players. That to some level has improved, but I think that will continue to be suppressed for the next few months till our relationship between 2 countries get completely normalized.

items.statement: Acquired Orbitrap Astral Mass Spectrometer from Thermo Fisher Scientific - first in world - to advance proteogenomics, biomarker discovery, and precision medicine capabilities
items.quote: We are pleased to share that we are acquiring the Orbitrap Astral Mass Spectrometer from Thermo Fisher Scientific, one of the most advanced platforms globally for high-resolution mass spectrometry.

items.statement: Effective tax rate expected around 30% for FY26
items.quote: I think we can expect about 30-odd percent to remain in that level during the next 1 year.

items.statement: Bangalore and Ahmedabad centers have highest ARPOB near INR 1 lakh; Mumbai and Kolkata ~INR 60,000-70,000; Tier 2 cities ~INR 30,000-35,000; overall blended ARPOB ~INR 45,000
items.quote: So, in the centre where we have full offering in terms of high-end therapies as well as being in metro, like, for example, Bangalore and Ahmedabad, the ARPOB is close to INR1 lakh.

items.statement: Welding business targets ₹25 crore annual sales within next two years
items.quote: With this momentum, we aim to achieve annual sales of ₹25 crore within the next two years.

items.statement: Expects single-digit growth in cored wire volumes due to moderate steel production
items.quote: So, if steel production is moderate and not growing, I don't see our cored wires also doing too great -like a single digit growth is still expected due to the trust and the dependence that I mentioned.

items.statement: Greater clarity on aluminium business outlook expected by end of June 2025
items.quote: We expect greater clarity on the aluminium business outlook by the end of June 2025, and we remain committed to making strategic decisions in the best interest of our long-term growth.

items.statement: Plans to add 3 flux cored wire production lines costing approximately ₹3 crore
items.quote: So, CapEx req uirement for Flux Cored Wire, I would say where we are currently hosting 3 production lines and we plan to go ramp it up with 3 more productions lines in the new near future, which will approximately cost us ₹ 3 crore

items.statement: Flux cored wire capacity currently 250 MT/month with 3 lines, infrastructure supports 9+ lines
items.quote: We have currently 3 lines with a total capacity of 250 MTs per month. Enough room for growth.

items.statement: Welding division volumes grew 39% QoQ to 201 tonnes in Q4 FY25
items.quote: In Q4 FY25, our welding division achieved revenues of ₹2.4 crore, with volumes growing an impressive 39% quarter-on-quarter to 201 tonnes.

items.statement: Cored wire revenue rose 26% YoY to ₹36.5 crore with 16% volume growth in Q4 FY25
items.quote: Specifically, in Q4FY25, our cored wire business demonstrated robust growth, with revenue rising 26% year-on-year to ₹36.5 crore and realizations increasing by 3% to ₹2.62 lakh per metric tonne.

items.statement: Aluminium flipping coil revenue declined 80% YoY to ₹6.4 crore, volumes fell 84% to 253 tonnes in Q4 FY25
items.quote: Turning to our aluminium flipping coil business, revenue declined by 80% year-on-year in Q4FY25 to ₹6.4 crore, with volumes falling 84% to 253 tonnes.

items.statement: EBITDA margin at 2.84% in Q4 FY25, down from 4.67% in preceding quarter
items.quote: Our EBITDA, excluding other income and extraordinary items, stood at ₹1.36 crore for Q4FY25, a decline of 48% year-on-year. Consequently, EBITDA margins for the quarter were at 2.84%, compared to 4.67% in the preceding quarter.

items.statement: Welding flux cored wire price realization at ₹1.18 lakh per tonne
items.quote: Our price realization stood at ₹1.18 lakh per tonne.

items.statement: Received RDSO approval in April 2025, opening opportunities with Indian Railways and major engineering companies
items.quote: A significant milestone for us was the recent approval from the Research Designs and Standards Organisation (RDSO) in April. As the technical advisor and consultant to Indian Railways, RDSO sets stringent standards and specifications for railway equipment.

items.statement: Secured IBR, IRS, Boiler Inspectorate, Thermax, and Steel Authority approvals for flux cored wire products

items.statement: FY25 EBITDA margin fell to 17% from 19% due to RM mix and one-time costs
items.quote: If we basically work on overall year margin, like in FY'25, our EBITDA margin dropped to 17% from 19%, 2%. I can give you more detail about that. So, basically, if you see the RM ratio in FY'25 versus FY'24, it increased by 0.7%, which we see is not significant. It depends a lot on the overall product mix and within that, the customer mix item level. So, I don't think going forward, we are not see

items.statement: Raw material imports 7% by volume, 18% by value in FY25, targeting reduction
items.quote: In term it is 7% and in value term, in the import value term it is 17.5%. Mayank: 18% in FY’25. Balkishan Jalan: And that we are still trying to keep on reducing by continually developing the Indian mills sources and get the customer approval for the same

items.statement: DSO rose to 105 days in FY25 from 85 days due to export credit terms and goods in transit
items.quote: the DSO was 85 days in FY'25 which increased to 105 days or so and the major reason, there are 2. One is in fastener division export started where one customer to whom we are exporting in U.S. market, the credit period compared to the domestic is high which resulted into almost 10 number of days which resulted into higher DSO. For that, again, we are seeing how we can reduce this credit period and

items.statement: Inventory days up 5-6 days to support Q1 FY26 demand, expected to stabilise
items.quote: As far as the inventory is concerned, we analyze if we go by number of days. So, the number of days increased by 5-6 days. But if we consider the reason, then we have built some inventory to cater to the Q1 demand of FY'26 and going forward, we should be able to stabilize in this inventory days as well.

items.statement: IPO raised Rs 121 cr, Rs 62 cr deployed, Rs 59 cr in FD, negligible debt ahead
items.quote: In March 2025, we raised this IPO where we got the money of 121 crores. We deployed 62 crores or something and 59 crores still lying in the FD. So, FD and working capital knockoff and still we have a good surplus fund lying and going forward, at least for current year also, we don't see any cash debt position. Debt position will be very negligible.

items.statement: Open to inorganic opportunities in domestic market, evaluation ongoing
items.quote: So, as we mentioned in our last call as well, yes, we are open for inorganic opportunity as well. And the evaluation expositions are going on, particularly in the domestic market.

items.statement: Schaeffler contributes 3-4% of sales, growth expected with their India capex
items.quote: Schaeffler has large requirements of spring, and we have been associated with Schaeffler for more than 6 years now. Based on their growth plan and also getting more opportunities to Gala, our sales have been growing consistently with Schaeffler, including in last year. So, they contribute almost 3-4% of our annual sales and considering their investments in India, particularly in powertrain segment

items.statement: New Grip Lock washer launched for construction equipment sector
items.quote: Lastly, we have developed and launched new product, the Grip Lock washer, significantly targeted at construction equipment sector, further diversifying our product offering and market reach.

items.statement: Bolt development opens US$1 bn addressable market, first US order secured
items.quote: We have also made a strategic move by initiating development of the bolt products, which open up additional addressable market of approximately US $1 billion. I am proud to share that we have already secured first order from an industrial customer based in the United States.

items.statement: Net fixed asset turnover improved to 3.65x in FY25 from 3.05x in FY24
items.quote: Operationally, we have also improved our net fixed asset turnover ratio, which grew to 3.65x in FY'25 from 3.05x in FY'24, a clear sign of better asset utilization and efficiency across all our existing plants.

items.statement: Patent legal case and consultant fees were one-time EBITDA margin drag in FY25
items.quote: Like, for example, we are fighting one legal case, patent case. For that, we are incurring some fees. The second more important case is we hired the universal consultants, UC consultants for our market study, particularly for the fastener division growth opportunity in India international market and phase 2 study where we covered which new product we can add out of this considering the margins and

items.statement: Revenue growth guidance of 23-25% over FY25 revenue of INR 5,307 crores
items.quote: Our guidance is that we will grow our revenue by 23% to 25% over what we have achieved in March '25 and this trajectory we know can be achieved through our execution and the fact that we have order book to back up.

items.statement: EBITDA margin guidance maintained at 12% to 12.25% for FY26
items.quote: Our guidance remains the same at 12 % to 12.25% EBITDA because we know the margin profile of the order book we have which is, of course, the best in the industry as we speak.

items.statement: Order book with L1 stands at INR 15,915 crores including L1 of INR 1,364 crores providing 24-month revenue visibility
items.quote: The order book and our industry outlook, what we have today is order book with L1 of INR 15,915 crores out of which L1 is INR 1,364 crores which provides us a strong revenue visibility in the next 24 months.

items.statement: FY25 order inflow of INR 9,680 crores, up 120% YoY and highest ever for Transrail
items.quote: This year we booked orders worth INR 9,680 crores which is not only a growth of 120% year -on-year but the highest order book we have booked in Transrail.

items.statement: FY25 EBITDA margin expanded 102 bps to 12.73%; Q4 FY25 EBITDA margin at 12.2%
items.quote: EBITDA margin expanded by 102 basis points to 12.73%. Profit after tax for the year stood at INR326.63 crore, delivering a strong growth of 40.07% over the previous year

items.statement: Phase 1 capex of INR 326 crores approved in January for tower and conductor capacity expansion; INR 90 crores from IPO funds
items.quote: Firstly, we are looking at capex which we got approved in the month of January. We had looked at INR 326 crores for our expansion of our factories and a new factory and some plant in equipment.

items.statement: Additional INR 50 crores capex approved in principle for Phase 2 expansion over next 15-18 months
items.quote: INR 50 odd crores more we are planning to add, so that within the existing brownfield projects so as to go to this capacity I mentioned.

items.statement: Current capacity utilization at 95% for towers and 100% for conductors
items.quote: So, currently we are at 95% on towers and 100% on conductors.

items.statement: Phase 1 expansion to reach 173,000 MT towers and 40,800 km conductors by December 2025; Phase 2 to reach 196,000 MT and 49,500 km by mid-FY27
items.quote: So with INR 326 crores what we had planned, we will reach 1 ,73,000 metric tons of towers and 40,800 kilometers of conductors. Now we have in the last board meeting, we have got further capex approved in principle and which we will utilize in the next 15-18 months which will then take us to 196,000 metric tons and 49,500 circuit kilometers.

items.statement: Strong tendering pipeline exceeding INR 1 lakh crores across domestic and international markets
items.quote: As you are aware that we bid domestic and global and the pipeline is pretty strong. As you have seen yourself, 35,000 (INR crore) itself is Power Grid and then we are talking about global players. Africa, there is a growth of expected 20% on the current opportunity. So we are talking about the global market and domestic market and the pipeline will be more than INR1 lakh crores.

items.statement: Power Grid market share target of 8-10% from their INR 35,000 crores capex plan for FY27-28
items.quote: Our current market share is around 8 % to 10% and this is what we intend to achieve this year with Power Grid which is a good number and it gives us a good base to execute in India.

items.statement: Bangladesh order book reduced from 20% (Dec) to 15% (Mar) to ~12% (May); targeting 5-6% by year-end and completion by June 2026
items.quote: As of December, Bangladesh order book was 20% of our total order book. As of March 25, it became 15%. And as we are executing well as of May, it will be approximately 12%. And by the year end, it will be 5% to 6% only. And we intend to finish the Bangladesh job by Juneof 26.

items.statement: International funding primarily through World Bank and African Development Bank; no exposure to US funding cuts
items.quote: So, for us, most of our funding is through World Bank and African Development Bank, which is an independent body and they are not through MCA, American funding. So, we have not been, you know, any way troubled with that.

items.statement: Working capital days at 74 days excluding IPO funds; expected to remain 75-85 days in FY26
items.quote: Sir, actually it is with including the IPO fund which is parked in the bank. So if we exclude the IPO fund we remain at 74 days of the working capital. It is almost in the similar line of the last year and we expect it to be remain within 75 -85 working days in the next year.

items.statement: Net debt-to-equity improved to 0.34x from 0.56x; interest cost expected at 3.5-3.6% of turnover in FY26 vs INR 197 crores in FY25
items.quote: Yes, it is going to be in the range of 3.5% to 3.6% of the total turnover.

items.statement: Fund-based limit INR 600 crores, non-fund-based limit INR 4,800 crores; both 90-95% utilized
items.value: INR 600 crores fund-based, INR 4,800 crores non-fund-based
items.quote: Our fund-based limit is around INR 600 crores and non -fund-based limit is around INR 4,800 crores and we have fully tied up almost both the limits. And utilization remains something between 90% to 95%.

items.statement: Subcontractor costs up due to higher construction execution phase but in line with project budgets; margins maintained through supply chain management
items.quote: Yes, so it's the nature of the project and when you are looking at higher degree of execution based on the timelines. So initially when the project starts up, you see the engineering, design, approval, the supplies happening. So it's a mix of project which happened in '24 and '25. FY25 has been a year where we had to do huge amount of construction and delivery in terms of on the ground and therefo

items.statement: Revenue mix: 92% T&D, 4% civil, 2% railways, 1% poles & lighting; T&D order book 51% domestic, 49% international
items.quote: So, predominantly, 92% is T&D, 4% is civil, 2% is railways and 1% is poles.

items.statement: Substation order book ~INR 1,000 crores out of INR 14,500 crores; won two international substation jobs worth INR 750 crores recently
items.quote: Substation is small. We would be out of INR 14,500, would be around INR 1,000 crores.

items.statement: HVDC pipeline ~INR 5,000 crores; won KPS 2 to Nagpur project; execution timeline 24-30 months; focused on transmission line not substation
items.quote: So, the pipeline is around INR 5,000 crores what we hear and we see the forecast. We already got one job, that is KPS 2 to Nagpur and we are now starting work there, which we got in the last quarter.

items.statement: Selective bidding using risk matrix scorecard; 5 out of 10 international jobs declined; each tender approved by CEO and Chairman
items.quote: So firstly, we work with multilateral funding agencies globally and we pick and choose our projects through a risk matrix which we look at through a scorecard, where to go, what to do, and a threshold number if we don't achieve, we do not go ahead. So basically, five out of ten jobs, we would, you know, refrain from bidding.

items.statement: Dividend policy exists but payout percentage to be finalized in first year post-listing
items.quote: So the dividend policy is there and depending on the manner in which we look at our profits, the dividend policy guidelines approved by the board will be deciding on the dividend.

items.statement: Skilled labor shortage due to infrastructure boom; managing through close coordination with teams and subcontractors
items.quote: So yes, there is skilled labor, availability which has become, you know, demand and supply situation based on the infrastructure boom. And we are working on the ground with our teams very closely with the skilled labor and subcontractors. So, yes, it's a challenge, but obviously, it is something which we have to work around and we are doing that.

items.statement: T&D market share 10-12% in India; win ratio 8-10% on pipeline
items.quote: In T&D, we would have a 10%-12% market share.

items.statement: No plans for EPC in US/Europe; only exploring product sales of towers/conductors on wait-and-watch basis
items.quote: So we are not looking at doing EPC in US and Europe for sure. We are looking at some seed marketing of product sales of towers and conductors which again we are going slow. It is a wait and watch and strategically seeing how things emerge. So, Europe and US is really not in our agenda today.

items.statement: Revenue growth guidance of 20%-25% CAGR for next 2-3 years remains intact; management more bullish on achieving stronger growth than FY25's 24%
items.quote: Absolutely. In fact, like I said, we are more bullish on achieving stronger as compared to last year which is 24%.

items.statement: Adjusted EBITDA margin ~21% in FY25; management confident of margin expansion across all businesses driven by digitization and AI
items.quote: Correct, then it's about 21%.

items.statement: Management sees definite scope for EBITDA margin expansion going forward due to digitization and automation
items.quote: I think there is definitely scope for expansion

items.statement: Domestic business grew 22% and international 26% in FY25; aligner solutions revenue grew 41% to INR77 crores
items.quote: Aligner Solutions revenue grew by 41% and contributed 32% of the revenue.

items.statement: Digital penetration increased to 64% from 49% in FY25; target is 90%-95% digitization
items.quote: During the year, our digital penetration increased to 64% from 49%.

items.statement: IDS Germany event generated strong leads across all three businesses (lab, aligners, Kids-e-Dental); expect good results within this year and momentum for next two years
items.quote: We have started processing all three different businesses. And we expect that within this year, we will see good results in all three categories.

items.statement: IPO proceeds capex plan of INR68 crores; only small amount deployed in FY25, more deployment in current year; may enhance capex based on growth visibility
items.quote: we have planned for capex, which is close to INR68 crores and we have only done very small amount in the last financial year, while we are deploying more in the current year.

items.statement: Aligner segment at 67% capacity utilization currently
items.quote: Mathematical analysis, it will be 67% capacity utilization in the aligner category. That is how, what we are currently.

items.statement: A&P expenses ~5% of sales on full year basis; IDS event cost ~INR45 lakhs in Q4 (once in 2 years); IPL costs to be booked in FY26
items.quote: Going ahead on a full year basis, our A&P can be taken at approximately 5% of the sales.

items.statement: Zirconia contributes >50% of domestic lab revenue and significant majority of export lab revenue
items.quote: On the domestic part it's more than 50% in terms of revenue. On the export part there is a significant majority of Zirconia

items.statement: Cover ~22,000 dentists in India out of 3 lakh total; aligner revenue ~50% from pay-as-you-go model
items.quote: Currently what we have mentioned our coverage of about 22,000 dentists and while we growing that coverage, India has 3 lakh dentists.

items.statement: Dentist-led B2B2C model vs D2C competitors; Illusion aligners profitable vs competitors' profitability issues; 10x revenue growth in 3.5 years from INR4 crores
items.quote: We are on our side extremely profitable aligner company while if you see of all the other people they are really having issues with their profitability.

items.statement: Received regulatory clearance for Singapore for Kids-e-Dental; confident of approvals from many other countries soon
items.quote: Recently we have got a regulatory clearance to go ahead for Singapore, and this is just the beginning and we are very confident to get green signals from many other countries soon.

items.statement: Debt-to-equity ratio at 0.06; finance cost INR1.3 crores in Q4 FY25, decreasing YoY; expect considerable reduction from Q1 FY26
items.quote: Currently, our debt-to-equity ratio stands at 0.06.

items.statement: INR100 crores cash from IPO proceeds; plan to deploy for capex (INR68 crores) and evaluate inorganic opportunities
items.quote: we have Rajat from our IPO proceed, we have planned for capex, which is close to INR68 crores

items.statement: ESOPs granted to 200+ employees across hierarchy; 4-year vesting; total ESOP cost ~INR14 crores over next 4 years
items.quote: In the next 4 years, we are looking at about INR14 crores of ESOPs. That is in the next 4 years. All put together, spread across four years, all put together.

items.statement: Kids-e-Dental revenue INR26 crores, EBITDA INR15.5 crores, PAT INR12 crores in FY25
items.quote: Our Kids-e-Dental business delivered a revenue of INR26 crores with the EBITDA of INR15.5 crores and PAT of INR12 crores during the year.

items.statement: US business performing well despite tariff concerns; seeing strong traction and positive outlook vs China
items.quote: We are now actually very positive about it, rather than negative about the tariffs.

items.statement: Digital impressions reduce logistic costs and internal processes, improving operational efficiency and turnaround time
items.quote: When it comes to us, we get instant impression, so there is no logistic cost and at the same time our internal processes are also reduced thereby improving the operational efficiency.

items.statement: Q4 FY25 was lumpy due to IDS event expenses (once in 2 years) and IPL campaign costs; scanner sales timing affected by IDS event
items.quote: Quarter 4 of FY25 was a lumpy quarter like I had mentioned in terms of our promotional expenses with approximately 45 lakhs of expenses towards the IDS Germany dental show which happens only once in two years.

items.statement: Management commits to quarter-on-quarter growth trend continuing in FY26 but declines to give specific revenue numbers
items.quote: I would still like to avoid the number right now because we would like to still stay put with the growth number that we have already pushed from Q3 to Q4. But one thing I can say is that there will be a quarterly growth like the way we did it last year.

items.statement: Payment platform revenue share expected to return to 70% in FY26 from current 65%
items.quote: we anticipate our payment platform to be going back to the same 70-odd percent revenue share this financial year, coming from 65% to 70%-odd from this particular business.

items.statement: Central Bank of India order worth INR70 crore over 5 years, live in Phase 1 with SaaS revenue starting Q1 FY26
items.quote: One of the largest deal being Central Bank of India, which is majorly because we ensured that we pivot into more areas of business and offline payment was one, which is about INR70-odd crore order in the next 5 years.

items.statement: Three orders secured for AI-based risk engine before official launch
items.quote: we declared about risk engine, AI-based risk engine last quarter. And today, we have three orders already even before launching it.

items.statement: 15+ payment aggregators and large merchants signed for payment platform
items.quote: we signed 15-plus aggregators and large merchants. This itself will give us a GMV peak, which we did last year coming in the first half yearly itself.

items.statement: Two new BBPS orders received, plus BBPS corporate payment and agent institute models added
items.quote: When it comes to BBPS, we have additional orders. I think we have got two new orders from the customers. And at the same time, it has added a very strong funnel to the company.

items.statement: EBITDA margin improved from 35% to 37% in FY25, net profit margin from 20% to 25%
items.quote: EBITDA margin, on the other hand, has gone from 35% to about 37%. Net profit again has not shrunk. In fact, it has gone up from 20% to about 25%.

items.statement: New subsidiary set up in UAE to focus on international deals
items.quote: we have set up new subsidiary in UAE to focus on the international deals.

items.statement: Talent pool grew ~20% in FY25, estimated ~30% incremental growth in FY26 with AI implementation
items.quote: Last year, there were about 20% addition in our talent pool. And this year, the estimated upward trend is going to be about 30-odd percent incremental talent along with the AI implementation.

items.statement: Four new product launches planned in Q1 FY26 including RegTech, BBPS corporate payments, ONDC buyer app, hosted solution for small banks
items.quote: there are 4 new product launches that we are doing in Q1 itself

items.statement: AI risk engine trained on 640 million data points over 1.5-2 years, predicts liability amounts, mass launch planned Q2 FY26
items.quote: we have completed our testing, and we have trained the module with about 640 million data. So that -- to bring this up, we have taken about 1.5, 2 years of effort

items.statement: Internet banking interoperability and BBPS corporate payments: NPST is a POC vendor for both RBI initiatives
items.quote: Internet banking interoperability, which was declared in last April by RBI, we are already one of the POC vendors in the country. And then at the same time, when it comes to BBPS corporate payments, which is again a new initiative, we are one of the POC vendors.

items.statement: UPI incentive budget reduced to INR500 crore, management sees positive as credit card on UPI and new players drive MDR/interchange revenue
items.quote: There is always a backup to such kind of decisions whenever happens in the sense, it's -- we need to understand that if India's digital growth has been due to this instrument, which contributes 82% as on today to the entire digital volume in the country, then this instrument will definitely have a backup if the mighty incentives have gone down.

items.statement: Africa digital payment infrastructure deal: execution started, 7-8 month implementation, milestone-based payments in USD
items.quote: the execution has already started this quarter. We are expecting this is going to be 7, 8 months execution period, but the revenue will start hitting from Q1 itself and because there are milestone-based payments.

items.statement: Global expansion strategy: partner-led channel model, NPST retains IPR/product ownership, 3-4 channel partners active
items.quote: We are in discussion with multiple partners, because we decided to go with the partner model, channel partner model. We want to play a specific role around OEM so that the IPR and those kind of quality ownership is with us.

items.statement: Declared 20% dividend on face value in FY25
items.quote: Second, we declared dividend, which is 20% on the face value.

items.statement: Q3 revenue loss due to single-bank dependency; resolved via multi-bank model but customer recovery takes time, Q4 revenue would have been larger without this
items.quote: Yes, it does. That's the reason why our Q4 number otherwise would have been much larger. We have taken that time to be -- that's why. Otherwise, it was like one side is you have banks, other side is you have to re-establish, retest, redo everything.
